entries.zh: 晉將劉裕之伐姚泓，太宗假嵩節，督山東諸軍事，傳詣平原，緣河北岸，列軍次於畔城。
entries.en: When Liu Yu of Jin marched against Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his staff and made him overseer of armies east of the mountains; he went to Pingyuan, followed the north bank of the Yellow River, and encamped at Pancheng.
entries.literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his tally of authority and made him overseer of all military affairs east of the mountains; he was sent to Pingyuan, marched along the north bank of the Yellow River, and drew up his army at Pancheng.

entries.zh: 軍頗失利。
entries.en: The campaign went badly in several clashes.
entries.literal: The army met with considerable setbacks.

entries.zh: 詔假裕道，裕於舟中望嵩麾蓋，遺以酃酒及江南食物，嵩皆送京師。
entries.en: An edict granted Liu Yu free passage; from his boat Yu looked on Song's banners and sent Ling wine and delicacies of the south — Song forwarded everything to the capital.
entries.literal: An edict granted Liu Yu passage; from his boat Yu gazed at Song's banners and canopies and sent him wine from Ling and foods of the Jiang region; Song had them all forwarded to the capital.

entries.zh: 詔嵩厚答之。
entries.en: The court ordered Song to return the courtesy in full measure.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Song to reply with generous gifts.

entries.zh: 又敕簡精兵為戰備，若裕西過者，便率精銳南出彭沛，如不時過，但引軍隨之。
entries.en: He also told him to pick crack troops for battle: if Yu crossed west, strike south into Peng and Pei with the elite; if Yu did not pass on schedule, simply follow with the host.
entries.literal: He further charged him to select elite troops for war readiness: if Yu passed westward, Song was to lead picked forces south into Peng and Pei; if Yu did not pass in season, he was only to trail the army with his own.

entries.zh: 彼至崤陝間，必與姚泓相持，一死一傷，眾力疲弊。
entries.en: By the time they reached the country between Xiao and Shan they would be locked with Yao Hong — one dead, one hurt, both armies spent.
entries.literal: When they reached the Xiao-Shan corridor they would surely grapple with Yao Hong — one side dead, one wounded, their strength spent.

entries.zh: 比及秋月，徐乃乘之，則裕首可不戰而懸。
entries.en: Wait until the autumn moon, move at ease, and Liu Yu's head might be taken without a fight.
entries.literal: Wait until autumn moon, then strike at leisure, and Liu Yu's head might hang without a battle.

entries.zh: 於是叔孫建等尋河趣洛。
entries.en: Shusun Jian and the rest then followed the river toward Luoyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luoyang.

entries.zh: 遂入關。
entries.en: They entered the passes.
entries.literal: They then entered the passes.

entries.zh: [3]嵩與建等自成皐南濟，晉諸屯戍皆望塵奔潰。
entries.en: [3] Song and Jian crossed south from Chenggao; Jin outposts everywhere broke and ran at their dust.
entries.literal: [3] Song with Jian and the rest crossed south from Chenggao; every Jin garrison they met fled at the dust of their approach.

entries.zh: 裕克長安，嵩乃班師。
entries.en: Once Liu Yu had Chang'an, Song led the army home.
entries.literal: When Yu took Chang'an, Song withdrew his army.

entries.zh: 於是叔孫建等尋河趣洛遂入關 按尋河趣洛者是叔孫建所領魏軍，入關者是劉裕所統的晉軍，這裏牽連敍述，遂似叔孫建等入關。
entries.en: "Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luo and entered the passes": the river march was Shusun Jian's Wei force; entering the passes was Liu Yu's Jin army—the linked narrative makes it seem Jian entered the passes.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luo and then entered the passes. Commentary: Those who followed the river toward Luo were the Wei army Shusun Jian led; those who entered the passes were the Jin army Liu Yu commanded—here the narrative is linked, so it seems Shusun Jian and others entered the passes.

entries.zh: 疑「遂入關」上脫「裕」字。
entries.en: Yu (Liu Yu) may have dropped before "entered the passes."
entries.literal: It is suspected the character for "Yu" has dropped above "then entered the passes."

entries.zh: 太宗寢疾，問後事於嵩，嵩曰：「立長則順，以德則人服。
entries.en: Taizong, bedridden, asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To set up the eldest is to follow order; to set up by virtue is to win hearts.
entries.literal: Taizong lay ill in bed and asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To establish the eldest is accordance with order; to establish by virtue is to win men's hearts.

entries.zh: 今長皇子賢而世嫡，天所命也，請立。」
entries.en: The eldest imperial son is able and the rightful heir — Heaven has chosen him; I beg that he be established."
entries.literal: The eldest imperial son is worthy and the hereditary heir — Heaven's mandate; I beg that he be established."

entries.zh: 乃定策禁中。
entries.en: With that the choice was settled inside the palace.
entries.literal: Thus the decision was fixed within the palace precincts.

entries.zh: 於是詔世祖臨朝監國，嵩為左輔。
entries.en: An edict then had Shizu preside at court and oversee the realm; Song was made left supporter.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict had Shizu attend court and oversee the state; Song was made left supporter.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，進爵北平王，司州中正。
entries.en: At Shizu's accession Song was raised to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.

entries.zh: 詔問公卿，赫連、蠕蠕征討何先。
entries.en: The Emperor asked the ministers whether the Helian or the Rouran should be attacked first.
entries.literal: An edict asked the ministers whether to campaign first against the Helian or the Rouran.

entries.zh: 嵩與平陽王長孫翰、司空奚斤等曰：「赫連居土，未能為患，蠕蠕世為邊害，宜先討大檀。
entries.en: Song with Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, Xi Jin, Minister of Works, and the rest said: "The Helian cling to their land and are not yet a great peril; the Rouran have long harried the border — strike Dadan first.
entries.literal: Song with Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han, Minister of Works Xi Jin, and others said: "The Helian hold to their soil and cannot yet be a grave threat; the Rouran have for generations been a frontier scourge — it is right to strike Dadan first.

entries.zh: 及則收其畜產，足以富國；
entries.en: Catch them in time and take their livestock and the realm grows rich;
entries.literal: If we reach them in time and seize their herds, that alone will enrich the state;

entries.zh: 不及則校獵陰山，多殺禽獸，皮肉筋角，以充軍實，亦愈於破一小國。」
entries.en: if not, hunt the Yin Mountains, kill game in masses, and stock the host with hide, meat, sinew, and horn — still better than breaking some small kingdom."
entries.literal: if we do not reach them, hunt the Yin Mountains, slaughter beasts in number, and fill the army's stores with hide, flesh, sinew, and horn — that too is better than crushing a petty state."

entries.zh: 太常崔浩曰：「大檀遷徙鳥逝，疾追則不足經久，大眾則不能及之。
entries.en: Cui Hao, Grand Minister of Ceremonials, said: "Dadan vanishes like migrating birds — hot pursuit cannot last, and a great army cannot catch him.
entries.literal: Grand Minister of Ceremonials Cui Hao said: "Dadan shifts like birds in flight; a swift pursuit cannot be sustained, and a great host cannot overtake him.

entries.zh: 赫連屈丐，土宇不過千里，其刑政殘虐，人神所棄，宜先討之。」
entries.en: Helian Qugai holds barely a thousand li; his laws are savage and men and gods alike have turned from him — attack him first."
entries.literal: Helian Qugai's domain is no more than a thousand li; his punishments and government are cruel — abandoned by men and spirits alike; he should be attacked first."

entries.zh: 尚書劉潔、武京侯安原請先平馮跋。
entries.en: Liu Jie of the Masters of Writing and An Yuan, Marquis of Wujing, urged that Feng Bo be subdued first.
entries.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked to pacify Feng Bo first.

entries.zh: 帝默然，遂西巡狩。
entries.en: The Emperor said nothing and went west on a hunting tour.
entries.literal: The Emperor was silent and thereafter went west on tour.

entries.zh: 後聞屈丐死，關中大亂，議欲征之。
entries.en: Later word came that Qugai was dead and Guanzhong in turmoil; the court debated marching west.
entries.literal: Later, hearing that Qugai had died and that Guanzhong was in great disorder, the court debated an expedition.

entries.zh: 嵩等曰：「彼若城守，以逸代勞，大檀聞之，乘虛而寇，危道也。」
entries.en: Song and the rest said: "If they sit behind walls and trade our strength for their rest, Dadan will hear and strike our flank — a dangerous course."
entries.literal: Song and the others said: "If they hold the walls and meet our strength with ease, Dadan will hear of it and raid while we are exposed — a perilous road."

entries.zh: 帝乃問幽微於天師寇謙之，[5]謙之勸行。
entries.en: The Emperor then asked the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi for Heaven's hidden signs; [5] Qianzhi urged him to go.
entries.literal: The Emperor then asked the subtle signs of Heaven from the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi; [5] Qianzhi urged the march.

entries.zh: 杜超之贊成之，[6]崔浩又言西伐利。
entries.en: Du Chao backed the plan; [6] Cui Hao again argued the gain of a western war.
entries.literal: Du Chao endorsed it; [6] Cui Hao again spoke of the profit in a western campaign.

entries.zh: 嵩等固諫不可。
entries.en: Song and his party remonstrated hard that the move must not be made.
entries.literal: Song and the others firmly remonstrated that it could not be done.

entries.zh: 帝大怒，責嵩在官貪污，使武士頓辱。
entries.en: The Emperor flew into rage, charged Song with graft in office, and had warriors shame him in public.
entries.literal: The Emperor was furious, accused Song of corruption in office, and had armored men publicly humiliate him.

entries.zh: 尋遷太尉。
entries.en: Before long he was moved to Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 久之，加柱國大將軍。
entries.en: Years later he received the added rank Grand General with Pillar of State.
entries.literal: After a long while he was given the added title Grand General with Pillar of State.

entries.zh: 自是，輿駕征伐，嵩以元老多留鎮京師，坐朝堂，平斷刑獄。
entries.en: Thereafter, whenever the Emperor marched out, Song — by then the senior man of the court — usually stayed to hold the capital, presiding in the hall of court to settle suits at law.
entries.literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, Song as an elder statesman mostly remained to guard the capital, sitting in the hall of court and judging criminal cases.

entries.zh: 薨，年八十。
entries.en: He passed away at eighty.
entries.literal: He died at eighty.

entries.zh: 諡曰宣王。
entries.en: He was posthumously titled King Xuan.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: King Xuan.

entries.zh: 後高祖追錄先朝功臣，以嵩配饗廟庭。
entries.en: Later Gaozu, honoring the founders, had Song given a place in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu, recalling the merit of the former court, had Song enshrined to share sacrifice in the temple hall.

entries.zh: 子冀歸，六歲襲爵，降為公。
entries.en: His son Jigui, at age six, inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.
entries.literal: His son Jigui, at age six, inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.

entries.zh: 高祖以其幼承家業，賜名稚，字承業。
entries.en: Gaozu, seeing him take up the house while still a boy, gave him the name Zhi, styled Chengye.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because he succeeded the family estate while young, bestowed the name Zhi, style Chengye.

entries.zh: 稚聰敏有才藝，虛心愛士。
entries.en: Zhi was quick-witted and skilled, humble, and devoted to men of talent.
entries.literal: Zhi was clever and talented, modest and fond of scholars.

entries.zh: 為前將軍，從高祖南討，授七兵尚書、太常卿、右將軍。
entries.en: As forward general he followed Gaozu south and received the posts of minister of the seven arms, grand minister of ceremonies, and right general.
entries.literal: As Forward General he followed Gaozu on the southern campaign and was appointed Minister of the Seven Arms, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Right General.

entries.zh: 時有詔廢鹽池稅，稚上表曰：「鹽池天資賄貨，密邇京畿，唯須寶而護之，均贍以理。
entries.en: An edict abolished the salt-pool levy; Zhi memorialized: "The pools are Heaven's wealth at the capital's door; they must be guarded and rationed fairly.
entries.literal: At that time there was an edict abolishing the salt-pool tax; Zhi submitted a memorial stating: "The salt pools are Heaven's gift of wealth, close to the capital region; they must be treasured and guarded and shared out with fair rule.

entries.zh: 今四境多虞，府藏罄竭。
entries.en: The borders are alarmed and the treasury bare.
entries.literal: Now on four sides there are many alarms and the treasury is empty.

entries.zh: 然冀定二州且亡且亂，常調之絹，不復可收。
entries.en: Ji and Ding are half lost; their regular silk dues cannot be gathered.
entries.literal: Yet the regular silk levies of Ji and Ding provinces are dying in disorder and can no longer be collected.

entries.zh: 仰惟府庫，有出無入，必須經綸，出入相補。
entries.en: The coffers spend without filling; income and outlay must be balanced.
entries.literal: Looking to the storehouses, outflow without inflow—there must be planning so expenditure and income balance.

entries.zh: 略論鹽稅，一年之中，準絹而言，猶不應減三十萬匹也，便是移冀定二州置於畿甸。
entries.en: The salt tax alone, reckoned in silk for a year, should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts—like moving Ji and Ding into the inner commanderies.
entries.literal: Roughly reckoning the salt tax for one year against silk, it should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts—this is like setting Ji and Ding within the capital belt.

entries.zh: 今若廢之，事同再失。
entries.en: To abolish it now is to lose twice over.
entries.literal: If it is now abolished, the matter is like losing twice.

entries.zh: 臣前仰違嚴旨，不先討關賊而解河東者，非是閑長安而急蒲坂。
entries.en: I earlier defied your stern order and relieved Hedong before striking the border rebels—not because I slighted Chang'an for Puban.
entries.literal: Your subject earlier disobeyed the stern order and did not first attack the border rebels but relieved Hedong—not because he was idle about Chang'an and urgent only for Puban.

entries.zh: 蒲坂一陷，沒失鹽池，三軍口命，濟贍理絕。
entries.en: Had Puban fallen, the pools would be gone, the army's ration cut, and supply ended.
entries.literal: Once Puban fell, the salt pools would be lost and the army's mouth would be cut off—relief and supply would end.

entries.zh: 天助大魏，茲計不爽。
entries.en: Heaven aided Great Wei; the plan held.
entries.literal: Heaven aided Great Wei; this plan did not miss.

entries.zh: 昔高祖昇平之年，無所乏少，猶創置鹽官而加典護，非為物而競利，恐由利而亂俗也。
entries.en: Even in Gaozu's peaceful years, without want, he set salt officers and overseers—not for profit but lest profit corrupt custom.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's years of rising peace there was no want, yet he still created salt officials and added custodians—not for goods and profit, but fearing that profit would corrupt custom.

entries.zh: 況今王公素餐，百官尸祿，租徵六年之粟，調折來歲之資，此皆出人私財，奪人膂力。
entries.en: How much more now, when nobles feast on salary and officials on empty posts, rent taking six years' grain and levies folding next year's funds—all from private purses, all seizing men's strength.
entries.literal: How much more now, when princes and dukes eat salary without work and officials hold posts without labor, rent taking six years' grain and levies folding next year's funds—these all come from private purses and seize men's strength.

entries.zh: 豈是願言，事不獲已。
entries.en: This is not what I wish to say; the matter cannot be helped.
entries.literal: It is not what I wish to say; the matter cannot be helped.

entries.zh: 臣輒符司監將尉還率所部，依常收稅，更聽後敕。」
entries.en: I have ordered the supervising office and commanders to collect the tax as usual, pending further command."
entries.literal: Your subject has already ordered the supervising office and commanders to lead their units and collect tax as usual, awaiting further edict."

entries.zh: 世宗時，侯剛子淵，稚之女壻。
entries.en: Under Shizong, Hou Gang's son Yuan became Zhi's son-in-law.
entries.literal: In Shizong's time Hou Gang's son Yuan married Zhi's daughter.

entries.zh: 剛為元叉所厚，故稚驟得轉進。
entries.en: Gang stood high with Yuan Cha, and Zhi rose in rank again and again.
entries.literal: Gang was favored by Yuan Cha, and so Zhi was repeatedly promoted.

entries.zh: 出為撫軍大將軍，領揚州刺史，假鎮南大將軍，都督淮南諸軍事。
entries.en: He was sent out as pacification-army grand general and inspector of Yangzhou, with acting rank as general who pacifies the south and command of Huainan.
entries.literal: He went out as Pacification Army Grand General, acting Inspector of Yangzhou, with acting title General Who Pacifies the South and command over all military affairs in Huainan.

entries.zh: 蕭衍將裴邃、虞鴻襲據壽春，稚諸子驍果，邃頗難之，號曰「鐵小兒」。
entries.en: Pei Sui and Yu Hong of Liang seized Shouchun's outer ramparts; Zhi's sons fought like iron, and Sui, finding them hard to beat, called them the "iron boys."
entries.literal: Xiao Yan's generals Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized the outer wall of Shouchun; Zhi's sons were fierce fighters, and Sui found them hard to face, calling them the "little men of iron."

entries.zh: 詔河間王琛總眾援之。
entries.en: An edict put Prince of Hejian Chen in overall command to relieve him.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Hejian Chen to take overall command and reinforce him.

entries.zh: 琛欲決戰，稚以雨久，更須持重。
entries.en: Chen wanted a pitched battle; Zhi, with the rains dragging on, urged restraint.
entries.literal: Chen wished to give battle; Zhi, because the rains had lasted long, said they must still be cautious.

entries.zh: 琛弗從，遂戰，為賊所乘，稚後殿。
entries.en: Chen refused; the enemy turned the fight, and Zhi covered the retreat.
entries.literal: Chen would not follow; they fought and the enemy took advantage; Zhi brought up the rear.

entries.zh: 初，稚既總強兵，久不決戰，議者疑有異圖。
entries.en: At first, with strong troops under him and no battle for a long while, some suspected another design.
entries.literal: At first, because Zhi held strong forces yet would not decide battle for a long time, critics suspected ulterior designs.

entries.zh: 朝廷重遣河間王琛及臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等三都督外聲助稚，內實防之。
entries.en: The court sent Chen of Hejian, Yu of Linhuai, and Li Xian of the Masters of Writing as three commanders—nominally to help Zhi, in truth to watch him.
entries.literal: The court again sent Prince of Hejian Chen, Prince of Linhuai Yu, and Minister of Writing Li Xian as three area commanders—outwardly to aid Zhi, inwardly in fact to guard against him.

entries.zh: 多侯弟子慶賓，善騎射，有將略。
entries.en: Duohou's nephew Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and showed commander's gifts.
entries.literal: Duohou's younger brother's son Qingbin was skilled in mounted archery and had generalship.

entries.zh: 高祖時，釋褐員外散騎侍郎，稍遷左將軍、太中大夫。
entries.en: Under Gaozu he doffed the hemp and became supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then rose by degrees to left general and grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: In Gaozu's time he doffed the hemp and was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then gradually rose to Left General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 肅宗時，議欲送蠕蠕主阿那瓌還國，慶賓上表固爭，不從。
entries.en: Under Suzong, when the court debated sending the Rouran ruler Anagui home, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the throne would not listen.
entries.literal: In Suzong's time, when there was debate on sending the Rouran ruler Anagui back to his country, Qingbin memorialized in firm opposition; the court did not follow.

entries.zh: 後蠕蠕遂執行臺元孚，大掠北境。
entries.en: The Rouran then seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern marches.
entries.literal: Later the Rouran indeed seized the touring commissioner Yuan Fu and ravaged the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 詔尚書令李崇討之，慶賓別將隸崇，出塞而返。
entries.en: An edict set the Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin served under him as detached commander, went beyond the passes, and came back.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Writing Li Chong to chastise them; Qingbin as a detached commander served under Chong, went beyond the passes, and returned.

entries.zh: 元法僧之外叛，蕭衍遣其豫章王蕭綜鎮徐州，又詔慶賓為別將隸安豐王延明討之。
entries.en: When Yuan Faseng defected, Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to hold Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin detached commander under the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, to strike him.
entries.literal: At Yuan Faseng's defection to the outside Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong to garrison Xuzhou; an edict also made Qingbin a detached commander under Prince of Anfeng Yanming to chastise him.

entries.zh: 尋除後將軍、肆州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was rear general and inspector of Sizhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Rear General and Inspector of Sizhou.

entries.zh: 時尒朱榮兵威漸盛，曾經肆州，慶賓畏惡之，據城不出。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong's military fame was then rising; passing through Sizhou once, he found Qingbin so fearful and hostile that the city gates stayed shut.
entries.literal: At that time Erzhu Rong's military prestige was gradually growing; he once passed through Sizhou, and Qingbin, fearing and loathing him, shut the city and would not come out.

entries.zh: 榮恨慶賓，舉兵襲之。
entries.en: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to take him.
entries.literal: Rong hated Qingbin and raised troops to assault him.

entries.zh: 慶賓別駕姚和內應，榮遂害慶賓僚屬，拘慶賓還秀容，呼為假父。
entries.en: Qingbin's attendant officer Yao He opened the gates from within; Rong killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin, and carried him to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."
entries.literal: Qingbin's attendant officer Yao He colluded within; Rong then killed Qingbin's staff, seized Qingbin and brought him back to Xiurong, calling him "foster father."

entries.zh: 後以母憂還都，尋起為平東將軍、光祿大夫、都督，鎮汝陰。
entries.en: Later, after mourning his mother in the capital, he was soon recalled as general who pacifies the east, grand master of splendid happiness, and commander at Ruyin.
entries.literal: Later, on returning to the capital for his mother's mourning, he was soon recalled and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and commander, garrisoning Ruyin.

entries.zh: 還朝，永安二年卒。
entries.en: He returned to court and died in Yong'an year 2.
entries.literal: He returned to court and died in the second year of Yong'an.

entries.zh: 贈車騎將軍、雍州刺史，又追加侍中、司空公。
entries.en: They posthumously made him general of chariots and cavalry and inspector of Yongzhou, then added palace attendant and duke of works.
entries.literal: Posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yongzhou; further added Palace Attendant and Duke of Works.

entries.zh: 第八子觀 北史卷二０尉古真傳「觀」作「歡」。
entries.en: "The eighth son Guan": Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen's life, has "Guan" as "Huan."
entries.literal: The eighth son Guan. Northern History juan 20, Wei Guzhen biography, reads "Guan" as "Huan."

entries.zh: 魏書當因避高歡諱改。
entries.en: Wei shu likely altered the name to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.
entries.literal: Wei shu must have changed it to avoid the taboo on Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 長孫肥 尉古真
entries.en: Biographies of Changsun Fei and Wei Guzhen
entries.literal: Changsun Fei; Wei Guzhen

entries.zh: 劉義符前東牟太守清河張幸先匿孤山 張森楷云；
entries.en: "Former Administrator of Dongmou under Liu Yifu, Zhang Xing of Qinghe, had earlier hidden on Gushan": Zhang Senkai says:
entries.literal: "Former Administrator of Dongmou under Liu Yifu, Zhang Xing of Qinghe, had earlier hidden on Gushan": Zhang Senkai says:

entries.zh: 「張彝傳
entries.en: "Biography of Zhang Yi
entries.literal: "Biography of Zhang Yi

entries.zh: 〈卷六四〉
entries.en: 〈juan 64〉
entries.literal: 〈juan 64〉

entries.zh: 及南燕錄並云幸是慕容超東牟太守，不聞仕宋。
entries.en: and the Southern Yan records all say Xing was Murong Chao's administrator of Dongmou, with no mention of service under Song.
entries.literal: and the records of Southern Yan all say Xing was Administrator of Dongmou under Murong Chao and are not heard to have served Song.

entries.zh: 此『劉義符』三字恐誤。」
entries.en: The three characters Liu Yifu are likely in error."
entries.literal: These three characters 'Liu Yifu' are likely in error."

entries.zh: 奚斤 叔孫建
entries.en: Xi Jin; Shusun Jian
entries.literal: Xi Jin; Shusun Jian

entries.zh: 王洛兒 車路頭 盧魯元 陳建 萬安國
entries.en: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, and Wan Anguo
entries.literal: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Wan Anguo

entries.zh: 弟彌娥，襲爵。
entries.en: His younger brother Mie inherited the title.
entries.literal: His younger brother Mie inherited the title.

entries.zh: 拜北鎮都將。
entries.en: He was appointed commander of the northern garrison.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of the Northern Garrison.

entries.zh: 卒，贈襄城王，諡曰恭。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously honored as Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous title Respectful.
entries.literal: He died; posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Respectful.

entries.zh: 子興仁襲爵。
entries.en: His son Xingren inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Xingren inherited the title.

entries.zh: 陳建，代人也。
entries.en: Chen Jian was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Chen Jian was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 祖渾，太祖末為右衞將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Hun, in the last years of Emperor Taizu, served as General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hun, at the end of Taizu, was General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 父陽，尚書。
entries.en: His father Yang held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Yang was Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 建以善騎射，擢為三郎。
entries.en: For his skill in horsemanship and archery, Jian was promoted to the rank of third-grade guard.
entries.literal: Jian for skill in mounted archery was promoted to Third-Rank Guard.

entries.zh: 稍遷下大夫、內行長。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to lower grand master and chief of the inner service.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master and Chief of Inner Service.

entries.zh: 世祖討山胡白龍，意甚輕之，單將數十騎登山臨嶮，每日如此。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu chieftain Bai Long, he took the enemy lightly and would ride up alone with only a few dozen horsemen to overlook the steep passes, doing so day after day.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Mountain Hu Bai Long and thought it quite light; alone he led several dozen horsemen up the mountain overlooking the defile, daily so.

entries.zh: 白龍乃伏壯士十餘處，出於不意，世祖墮馬，幾至不測。
entries.en: Bai Long had hidden stalwart warriors in more than ten places; they sprang out unexpectedly, the emperor was thrown from his horse, and he came within a hair's breadth of disaster.
entries.literal: Bai Long then hid stalwart warriors in more than ten places, emerging unexpectedly; Emperor Shizu fell from his horse and nearly reached beyond reckoning.

entries.zh: 建以身捍賊，大呼奮擊，殺賊數人，身被十餘創。
entries.en: Jian shielded the emperor with his own body, shouting as he fought fiercely, killed several of the enemy, and took more than ten wounds himself.
entries.literal: Jian with his body defended against the bandits, shouted and struck fiercely, killed several bandits, his body received more than ten wounds.

entries.zh: 世祖壯之，賜戶二十。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu admired his courage and granted him twenty tax households.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu admired him and granted twenty households.

entries.zh: 高祖初，徵為尚書右僕射，加侍中，進爵趙郡公。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was recalled as Vice Director of the Right Secretariat, appointed Palace Attendant, and raised to Duke of Zhao commandery.
entries.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat Right, added Palace Attendant, advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 建與侍中尚書、晉陽侯元仙德，殿中尚書、長樂王穆亮，比部尚書、平原王陸叡密表曰：[2]「皇天輔德，命集大魏。
entries.en: Jian joined with Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director Yuan Xiande, Marquis of Jinyang, Director of Palace Affairs Prince Changhe Mu Liang, and Director of Justice Prince Pingyuan Lu Rui in a secret memorial that read: [2] "High Heaven assists the virtuous, and the mandate has settled upon Great Wei.
entries.literal: Jian with Palace Attendant and Secretariat Director, Marquis of Jinyang Yuan Xiande, Director of Palace Affairs Changhe Prince Mu Liang, and Director of Justice Pingyuan Prince Lu Rui submitted a secret memorial saying: [2] "High Heaven assists virtue; the mandate gathers on Great Wei.

entries.zh: 臣等祖父翼贊初興，勤過蜀漢，誓固山河，享茲景福，寵辱休戚，與國均焉。
entries.en: Our grandfathers aided the dynasty at its founding, their service surpassing even the ministers of Shu-Han; they swore to hold the realm firm and have enjoyed this bright fortune, sharing honor and disgrace, weal and woe, equally with the state.
entries.literal: We subjects' grandfathers aided the founding, their diligence exceeding Shu-Han, swore to secure mountains and rivers, enjoy this bright fortune; favor and disgrace, weal and woe, are equal with the state.

entries.zh: 臣以凡近，識無遠達，階藉先寵，遂荷今任，彼己之譏，播於羣口。
entries.en: I am a man of common station and shallow understanding, yet I have climbed on my family's former favor to bear my present office; reproaches comparing me with worthier men spread among the multitude.
entries.literal: Your subject by ordinary proximity, knowledge without far sight, steps on former favor's stairs, thus bears present burden; comparison to others' reproach spreads among the multitude.

entries.zh: 仰感生成，俯自策厲，顧省駑鈍，終於無益。
entries.en: I look up, moved by the grace the throne has shown me, and bend my efforts to improve myself, yet when I examine my own dull inadequacy I find it avails nothing in the end.
entries.literal: Looking up, moved by the emperor's nurturing; bowing down, I spur myself on; reflecting on my dull incompetence, in the end of no benefit.

entries.zh: 然飲冰驚寐，實懷慚負。
entries.en: Yet I lie awake in distress as though drinking ice, truly burdened with shame and remorse.
entries.literal: Yet drinking ice and starting from sleep, truly harboring shame and debt.

entries.zh: 至於願。
entries.en: As for my wish—
entries.literal: As to my wish.

entries.zh: 天高地厚，何日忘之。
entries.en: Heaven is high and earth is deep—on what day could I ever forget such kindness?
entries.literal: Heaven high and earth thick—on what day could I forget it?

entries.zh: 自永嘉之末，封豕橫噬，馬叡南據，奄有荊楚。
entries.en: Since the end of the Yongjia era, barbarian invaders have ravaged the land unchecked, while Sima Rui seized the south and came to hold Jing and Chu.
entries.literal: From the end of Yongjia, the great boar rampaged across the land; Sima Rui seized the south and swallowed Jing and Chu.

entries.zh: 及桓劉跋扈，禍難相繼。
entries.en: When the houses of Huan and Liu grew arrogant and overbearing, disasters followed one after another.
entries.literal: When Huan and Liu grew overbearing, calamities followed one upon another.

entries.zh: 岱宗隔望秩之敬，青徐限見德之風。
entries.en: Mount Tai stood cut off from the rites of ranked sacrifice, and Qing and Xu were barred from the transforming breeze of imperial virtue.
entries.literal: Mount Tai was cut off from ranked sacrifices; Qing and Xu were barred from the wind of transforming virtue.

entries.zh: 獻文皇帝髫齓龍飛，道光率土，干戚暫舞，淮海從風，車書既同，華裔將一。
entries.en: Emperor Xianwen took the throne while still a child; his radiance shone across the realm; when arms were briefly raised, the Huai and Hai regions bowed to the wind; chariots and writing were unified, and Chinese and barbarian were on the verge of becoming one.
entries.literal: Emperor Xianwen in infancy rose like a dragon; his way illuminated the entire realm; arms briefly danced and Huai and Hai followed the wind; chariots and documents were unified, Chinese and barbarian would become one.

entries.zh: 昊天不弔，奄背萬邦。
entries.en: Bright Heaven showed no mercy, and he suddenly abandoned the myriad realms.
entries.literal: Bright Heaven did not pity; suddenly he turned his back on the myriad states.

entries.zh: 竊聞劉昱夭亡，權臣殺害，思正之民，翹想罔極。
entries.en: I have heard that Liu Yu died young, murdered by powerful ministers, and that upright people throughout the land yearn for him beyond measure.
entries.literal: I have privately heard Liu Yu died young, slaughtered by powerful ministers; people who think rightly long for him beyond measure.

entries.zh: 愚謂時不再來，機宜易失，毫分之差，致悔千里。
entries.en: I humbly believe that time will not return, that opportunity is easily lost, and that an error no wider than a hair can bring regret a thousand leagues hence.
entries.literal: I foolishly think the time will not come again, opportunity easily lost—a hairsbreadth slip leads to regret a thousand li away.

entries.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎，所謂見而不作，過在介石者也。
entries.en: He who fails to seize what Heaven offers will suffer punishment in return; as the saying goes, to see yet not act is a fault as plain as a jie stone set in the sun.
entries.literal: Heaven's gift not taken—one receives punishment in return; what is called seeing yet not acting, the fault lies in the alert jie stone.

entries.zh: 宜簡雄將，號令八方。
entries.en: We should select bold commanders and issue orders to the eight directions.
entries.literal: One should select fierce generals and command the eight directions.

entries.zh: 義陽王臣昶，深悟存亡，遠同孫氏。
entries.en: Prince Yiyang, our subject Yuan Chang, deeply understands the stakes of survival and ruin and is well suited to follow the example of Sun Quan.
entries.literal: Prince of Yiyang, our subject Chang, deeply comprehends survival and destruction, far sharing the Sun clan's example.

entries.zh: 苟歷運響從，則吳會可定，脫事有難成，則振旅而返。
entries.en: If the dynasty's fortune answers and the people respond, Wu and Kuaiji can be secured; if the enterprise proves difficult, the army can be rallied and withdrawn.
entries.literal: If the dynasty's fortune responds and follows, then Wu and Hui can be settled; if matters are hard to accomplish, then rally the army and return.

entries.zh: 進可以揚義聲於四海，退可以通德信於遐裔。
entries.en: Advancing, we can spread righteous renown to the four seas; retreating, we can extend virtue and good faith to distant lands.
entries.literal: Advancing can spread righteous fame through the four seas; retreating can extend virtue and trust to distant realms.

entries.zh: 宜乘之會，運鍾今日，如合聖聽，乞速施行。
entries.en: This is the moment to act, for fortune has struck today; if this accords with Your Majesty's judgment, I beg that it be carried out at once.
entries.literal: One should seize this opportune moment—fortune rings today; if it fits the sage's hearing, I beg swift implementation.

entries.zh: 脫忤天心，願存臣表，徐觀後驗，賞罰隨焉。」
entries.en: If it runs counter to Heaven's intent, I ask only that this memorial be kept on record so that later results may be weighed, and reward or punishment may follow accordingly."
entries.literal: If it goes against Heaven's heart, I wish to preserve this subject's memorial and slowly observe later verification; reward and punishment will follow."

entries.zh: 高祖嘉之。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen commended the proposal.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised it.

entries.zh: 遷司徒、征西大將軍，進爵魏郡王。
entries.en: Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Prince of Wei commandery.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, advanced to Duke of Wei Commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖與文明太后頻幸建第，賜建妻宴於後庭。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming often visited Jian's mansion, and the empress dowager granted banquets for Jian's wife in the rear palace.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming frequently visited Jian's residence and granted his wife banquets in the rear court.

entries.zh: 太和九年薨。
entries.en: He died in the ninth year of the Taihe era.
entries.literal: He died in the ninth year of Taihe.

entries.zh: 高宗初，賜爵阜城侯，加冠軍將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fucheng and appointed Champion General.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was granted the title Marquis of Fucheng, added Champion General.

entries.zh: 出為幽州刺史，假秦郡公。
entries.en: He was sent out as governor of You Province with the acting title Duke of Qin commandery.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Governor of You Province, acting Duke of Qin Commandery.

entries.zh: 高宗以建貪暴懦弱，遣使就州罰杖五十。
entries.en: Because Jian was greedy, cruel, and weak in character, Emperor Gaozong sent an envoy to his province to have him beaten with fifty strokes of the staff.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong because Jian was greedy, brutal and weak, sent a messenger to the prefecture to punish with fifty cane strokes.

entries.zh: 子念，襲爵。
entries.en: His son Nian inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Nian inherited the title.

entries.zh: 為中山守，坐掠良人為御史中尉王顯所彈。
entries.en: He served as administrator of Zhongshan and was impeached by Imperial Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian for seizing innocent people.
entries.literal: He was Administrator of Zhongshan; for seizing good people he was impeached by Imperial Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian.

entries.zh: 遇赦，免。
entries.en: He was pardoned when an amnesty was declared.
entries.literal: He encountered an amnesty and was pardoned.

entries.zh: 爵除。
entries.en: His noble title was revoked.
entries.literal: His title was removed.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：王洛兒、車路頭、盧魯元、陳建，咸以誠至發衷，竭節危難，苟非志烈過人，亦何能以若此！
entries.en: The historian writes: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, and Chen Jian all acted from sincere devotion of heart and gave their utmost loyalty in times of peril; had they not possessed resolution surpassing ordinary men, how could they have done as they did!
entries.literal: The historian says: Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, and Chen Jian all with utmost sincerity moved their inner hearts and exhausted their integrity in hardship; if not men of surpassing fierce resolve, how could they have done thus!

entries.zh: 宜其生受恩遇，歿盡哀榮。
entries.en: It is only fitting that in life they received imperial favor and in death the full honors of mourning.
entries.literal: It is fitting that in life they received favor and in death full mourning honor.

entries.zh: 至如安國，貴寵異於數子哉。
entries.en: As for Anguo, his exalted favor stood apart even from these others.
entries.literal: As for Anguo, his noble favor differed from these several men!

entries.zh: 太宗即位，拜散騎常侍。
entries.en: After Emperor Taizong acceded to the throne, Luoer was appointed Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「士處家必以孝敬為本，在朝則以忠節為先，不然，何以立身於當世，揚名於後代也。
entries.en: An edict declared: "A man at home must root himself in filial piety and respect, and at court must put loyalty and integrity first; without these, how could he establish himself in his own age or leave a name to posterity?
entries.literal: An edict said: "A gentleman at home must take filial piety and respect as root; in court he must take loyalty and integrity as foremost—otherwise how can he stand in his generation and spread his name to posterity?

entries.zh: 散騎常侍王洛兒、車路頭等，服勤左右，十有餘年，忠謹恭肅，久而彌至，未嘗須臾之頃，有廢替之心。
entries.en: Regular Attendant Wang Luoer, Che Lutou, and the rest have served diligently at my side for more than ten years, loyal, careful, and reverent, their devotion deepening with the years, and never for a moment have they shown any wish to leave my service.
entries.literal: Regular Attendant Wang Luoer, Che Lutou and others served diligently at his side for more than ten years, loyal, respectful and solemn, growing more so over time; never for an instant did they have a heart of abandoning their post.

entries.zh: 及在艱難，人皆易志，而洛兒等授命不移，貞操踰懇。
entries.en: When times grew hard, others readily changed their allegiance, yet Luoer and his companions held to their charge without wavering, their steadfast loyalty surpassing mere duty.
entries.literal: When in hardship, all men easily change purpose, but Luoer and the others received their mandate without shifting, their chaste conduct exceeding earnestness.

entries.zh: 雖漢之樊灌，魏之許典無以加焉。
entries.en: Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Chu and Dian Wei of Wei, could outdo them.
entries.literal: Even Han's Fan Kuai and Guan Ying, Wei's Xu Dian—none could surpass them.

entries.zh: 勤而不賞，何以奬勸將來為臣之節？
entries.en: If such service goes unrewarded, how shall we encourage future generations of ministers in their duty?
entries.literal: Diligence without reward—how can one encourage future generations in the integrity of ministers?

entries.zh: 其賜洛兒爵新息公，加直意將軍。」
entries.en: Let Luoer be enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxin and appointed General of Straight Intent."
entries.literal: Therefore grant Luoer the title Duke of Xinxin, add General of Straight Intent."

entries.zh: 又追贈其父為列侯，賜僮隸五十戶。
entries.en: His father was also posthumously enfeoffed as a ranked marquis, with a grant of fifty households of retainers.
entries.literal: Also posthumously enfeoff his father as a ranked marquis, grant fifty households of bondsmen.

entries.zh: 永興五年卒。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year of the Yongxing era.
entries.literal: He died in the fifth year of Yongxing.

entries.zh: 贈太尉、建平王，賜溫明祕器，載以轀輬車，使殿中衞士為之導從。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
entries.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Commandant, Prince of Pingping; granted warm bright secret vessels, carried in the barred funeral carriage, with palace guards as escort.

entries.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟者數四焉。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him, weeping again and again.
entries.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn, weeping several times.

entries.zh: 乃鴆其妻周氏，與洛兒合葬。
entries.en: He then had Luoer's wife, Lady Zhou, compelled to take poison and buried her with him in a joint grave.
entries.literal: He then had Luoer's wife Lady Zhou poisoned and buried with Luoer.

entries.zh: 子定州，襲爵，降為建陽侯、安遠將軍。
entries.en: His son Dingzhou inherited the title but was reduced to Marquis of Jianyang and made General Who Pacifies the Far.
entries.literal: His son Dingzhou inherited the title, demoted to Marquis of Jianyang, General Who Pacifies the Far.

entries.zh: 後定州弟升為侍御中散，有寵於顯祖，以祖父洛兒著勳先朝，詔復定州爵為公。
entries.en: Later Dingzhou's younger brother Sheng became an attendant in the imperial escort and won favor with Emperor Xianzu; because their grandfather Luoer had earned distinction under the previous reign, an edict restored Dingzhou's rank to duke.
entries.literal: Later Dingzhou's younger brother Sheng became Attendant Scattered Cavalier in the Imperial Escort, favored by Emperor Xianzu; because grandfather Luoer had merit in the previous dynasty, an edict restored Dingzhou's title to duke.

entries.zh: 高祖初，為長安鎮將。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as garrison commander of Chang'an.
entries.literal: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was General Who Guards Chang'an.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 子陵，襲升爵。
entries.en: His son Ling inherited the title that Sheng had held.
entries.literal: His son Ling inherited Sheng's title.

entries.zh: [1]承明初，遷監御長，賜爵始新子，加寧朔將軍、員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: [1] At the opening of the Chengming era he was made supervisor of the imperial guard, enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixin, and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and extraordinary Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: [1] At the beginning of Chengming, he was transferred to Supervisor of the Imperial Guard, granted the title Viscount of Shixin, added General Who Pacifies the North and Extraordinary Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 子陵襲升爵 按上不言升封何爵，疑傳有脫文。
entries.en: "Son Ling inherited Sheng's title": the text above does not say what title Sheng held; the biography appears to have lost wording here.
entries.literal: "Son Ling inherited Sheng's title" — examining above, it does not state what title Sheng received; the biography is suspected to have lost text.

entries.zh: 萬安國，代人也。
entries.en: Wan Anguo was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 祖真，世為酋帥，恒率部民從世祖征伐，以功除平西將軍、敦煌公，轉驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhen had for generations been a tribal chieftain and regularly led his people to follow Emperor Shizu on campaign; for his service he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Dunhuang, and later promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry with the privilege of the Three Departments.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhen for generations was tribal chief, constantly leading his tribesmen to follow Emperor Shizu on campaigns; for merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Dunhuang, transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Three Departments.

entries.zh: 父振，尚高陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: His father Zhen married the Elder Princess of Gaoyang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
entries.literal: His father Zhen married the Elder Princess of Gaoyang and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍、寧西將軍、長安鎮將，賜爵馮翊公。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and garrison commander of Chang'an, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fengyi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Garrison Commander of Chang'an, granted the title Duke of Fengyi.

entries.zh: 安國少明敏，有姿貌。
entries.en: Anguo was clever and quick-witted in his youth and possessed a handsome appearance.
entries.literal: Anguo in youth was clever and keen, and had good looks.

entries.zh: 以國甥，復尚河南公主，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: As a nephew of the imperial house by marriage, he also married the Princess of Henan and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
entries.literal: As the emperor's nephew by marriage, he again married the Princess of Henan and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 顯祖特親寵之，與同臥起，為立第宅，賞賜至巨萬。
entries.en: Emperor Xianzu favored him with special intimacy, sharing his bed and his daily routine, built him a mansion, and lavished rewards upon him to the sum of tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Emperor Xianzu especially cherished him, sharing bed and rising with him, built a residence for him, and rewards reached tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 超拜大司馬、大將軍，封安城王。
entries.en: He was abruptly promoted to Grand Marshal and Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.
entries.literal: He was extraordinarily appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.

entries.zh: 安國先與神部長奚買奴不平，承明初，矯詔殺買奴於苑中。
entries.en: Anguo had long been at odds with Shenbu chieftain Xi Mainu; early in the Chengming era he forged an edict and had Mainu killed in the imperial park.
entries.literal: Anguo had earlier been on bad terms with Shenbu Chief Xi Mainu; at the beginning of Chengming, he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，大怒，遂賜安國死。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowen learned of this he was furious and ordered Anguo to take his own life.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard of it, was greatly angered, and thereupon granted Anguo death.

entries.zh: 年二十三。
entries.en: He was twenty-three years old.
entries.literal: He was twenty-three years old.

entries.zh: 子翼，襲王爵。
entries.en: His son Yi inherited the princely title.
entries.literal: His son Yi inherited the princely title.

entries.zh: 太和十五年薨。
entries.en: He died in the fifteenth year of the Taihe era.
entries.literal: He died in the fifteenth year of Taihe.

entries.zh: 高祖以其父受寵先朝，特贈并州刺史。
entries.en: Because his father had enjoyed favor under the previous reign, Emperor Xiaowen specially posthumously honored him as governor of Bing province.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu because his father had received favor in the previous dynasty specially posthumously granted him Governor of Bing Province.

entries.zh: 盧魯元，昌黎徒河人也。
entries.en: Lu Luyuan came from Tuhe in Changli commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Luyuan was a man of Tuhe in Changli.

entries.zh: 曾祖副鳩，仕慕容垂為尚書令、臨澤公。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Fuchiu had served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat and been enfeoffed as Duke of Linze.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Fuchiu served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Linze.

entries.zh: 祖父並至大官。
entries.en: His grandfather and father both rose to high office.
entries.literal: His grandfather and father both reached great office.

entries.zh: 魯元敏而好學，寬和有雅度。
entries.en: Luyuan was quick-witted and fond of study, magnanimous and possessed of cultivated bearing.
entries.literal: Luyuan was clever and loved learning, generous and had refined bearing.

entries.zh: 太宗時，選為直郎。
entries.en: During Emperor Taizong's reign he was chosen as a direct attendant.
entries.literal: In Taizong's time he was selected as Direct Gentleman.

entries.zh: 以忠謹給侍東宮，恭勤盡節，世祖親愛之。
entries.en: For his loyalty and discretion he was assigned to the Eastern Palace, where he served with reverent diligence; Emperor Shizu held him in special affection.
entries.literal: For loyalty and prudence he was assigned to serve the Eastern Palace with respectful diligence in utmost integrity; Emperor Shizu cherished him.

entries.zh: 及即位，以為中書侍郎，拾遺左右，寵待彌深，而魯元益加謹肅，世祖逾親信之，內外大臣莫不敬憚焉。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, Luyuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with the duty of remonstrance at the emperor's side; his favor deepened, yet Luyuan grew only more grave and careful, and the emperor trusted him all the more, so that ministers within and without the court all regarded him with respect and awe.
entries.literal: Upon taking the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, remonstrance at left and right; favor grew deeper, while Luyuan grew more solemn; Emperor Shizu trusted him ever more; inward and outward ministers none did not respect and fear him.

entries.zh: 性多容納，善與人交，好掩人之過，揚人之美，由是公卿咸親附之。
entries.en: He was by nature forbearing and open-handed, skilled at friendship, apt to cover others' faults and praise their virtues, and for this the highest officials all sought his company.
entries.literal: His nature was much tolerant; he was good at making friends, liked covering others' faults and praising others' virtues; thereby all chief ministers drew close to him.

entries.zh: 魯元以工書，有文才，累遷中書監，領祕書事。
entries.en: For his skill in calligraphy and literary talent Luyuan was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Director of the Secretariat and overseer of the imperial library.
entries.literal: Luyuan for skill in calligraphy and literary talent was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat, overseeing Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 賜爵襄城公，加散騎常侍、右將軍。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangcheng and appointed Regular Attendant and General of the Right.
entries.literal: Granted the title Duke of Xiangcheng, added Regular Attendant and General of the Right.

entries.zh: 賜其父為信都侯。
entries.en: His father was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu.
entries.literal: His father was granted the title Marquis of Xindu.

entries.zh: 從征赫連昌。
entries.en: He accompanied the campaign against Helian Chang.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang.

entries.zh: 世祖親追擊之，入其城門，魯元隨世祖出入。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu personally pursued the enemy and entered their city gate, with Luyuan attending him in and out.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu personally pursued him, entering the city gate; Luyuan followed Emperor Shizu in and out.

entries.zh: 是日，微魯元，幾至危殆。
entries.en: That day, but for Luyuan, the emperor would have come to grievous harm.
entries.literal: That day, without Luyuan he would nearly have reached peril.

entries.zh: 從征平涼，以功拜征北大將軍，加侍中。
entries.en: On the campaign against Pingliang he was rewarded with the post of General Who Campaigns North and Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign to Pingliang; for merit he was appointed General Who Campaigns North, added Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 後遷太保、錄尚書事。
entries.en: He was later made Grand Guardian and put in charge of recording Secretariat affairs.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Guardian and recorded Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 世祖貴異之，常從征伐，出入臥內。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu prized him above others, taking him on campaign after campaign and admitting him to his private chambers.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu held him in exceptional esteem, often followed on campaigns, entering and leaving his sleeping quarters.

entries.zh: 每有平殄，輒以功賞賜僮隸，前後數百人，布帛以萬計。
entries.en: Whenever a campaign ended in victory he would reward Luyuan with household retainers for his service—several hundred in all over the years—and silk cloth by the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Whenever there was pacification he would reward with bondsmen for merit, several hundred before and after, silk cloth by tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 世祖臨幸其第，不出旬日。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu visited his mansion and stayed for nearly ten days.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu visited his residence and did not leave for ten days.

entries.zh: 欲其居近，易於往來，乃賜甲第於宮門南。
entries.en: Wishing him to live close at hand for easy visits, the emperor granted him a grand residence just south of the palace gate.
entries.literal: Wishing him to dwell nearby for easy coming and going, he granted a fine mansion south of the palace gate.

entries.zh: 衣食車馬，皆乘輿之副。
entries.en: His food, clothing, carriages, and horses were all of the same quality as the emperor's own.
entries.literal: Food, clothing, carriages and horses were all surplus of the imperial equipage.

entries.zh: 真君三年冬，車駕幸陰山，魯元以疾不從。
entries.en: In winter of the third year of Zhenjun, the emperor visited Yinshan, but Luyuan stayed behind because he was ill.
entries.literal: In winter of the third year of Zhenjun, the imperial carriage visited Yinshan, and Luyuan did not accompany it because of illness.

entries.zh: 侍臣問疾送醫藥，傳驛相屬於路。
entries.en: Attendants were sent to ask after him and deliver medicine, with relay messengers following one another along the route.
entries.literal: Attending ministers inquired after his illness and sent medicines, with relay messengers following one another along the road.

entries.zh: 及薨，世祖甚悼惜之。
entries.en: When Luyuan died, Emperor Shizu mourned him deeply.
entries.literal: When he died, Emperor Shizu greatly mourned and regretted him.

entries.zh: 還，臨其喪，哭之哀慟。
entries.en: On his return, the emperor went to the mourning rites and wept for him with great sorrow.
entries.literal: On returning, he attended the mourning and wept for him in bitter grief.

entries.zh: 東西二宮命太官日送奠，晨昏哭臨，訖則備奏鐘鼓伎樂。
entries.en: The Eastern and Western Palaces ordered the Imperial Provisioner to send offerings each day; morning and evening they came to mourn and weep, and afterward bells, drums, and music were performed in full.
entries.literal: The Eastern and Western Palaces ordered the Imperial Provisioner to send offerings daily, attended and wept morning and evening, and when this was finished fully performed bells, drums, and music.

entries.zh: 輿駕比葬三臨之。
entries.en: Before the burial, the emperor came in person to mourn him three times.
entries.literal: Before the burial, the imperial carriage came to mourn him three times.

entries.zh: 喪禮依安城王故事，而贈送有加。
entries.en: His funeral rites followed the precedent for Prince Ancheng, with still greater posthumous gifts and honors.
entries.literal: The funeral rites followed the precedent for Prince Ancheng, but the posthumous gifts and send-off were increased.

entries.zh: 贈襄城王，諡曰孝。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Xiao.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Xiao.

entries.zh: 葬於崞山，為建碑闕。
entries.en: He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
entries.literal: Buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.

entries.zh: 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比。
entries.en: Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
entries.literal: Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.

entries.zh: 子統襲爵。
entries.en: His son Tong succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Tong inherited the title.

entries.zh: 少子內，給侍東宮，恭宗深昵之，常與臥起同衣。
entries.en: His younger son Nei served in the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Gongzong was deeply attached to him and often shared his bed, rising together and even wearing the same garments.
entries.literal: His younger son Nei served the Eastern Palace; Prince Gongzong was deeply fond of him, often sharing bed, rising and clothes.

entries.zh: 父子有寵兩宮，勢傾天下。
entries.en: Father and son enjoyed favor in both palaces, and their influence overshadowed the court.
entries.literal: Father and son had favor in both palaces; their power tilted the realm.

entries.zh: 內性寬厚，有父風，而恭順不及。
entries.en: Nei was generous by nature and resembled his father in manner, yet he lacked his father's reverent obedience.
entries.literal: Nei's nature was generous, had his father's manner, but did not match his father's deference.

entries.zh: 正平初，宮臣伏誅，世祖以魯元故，唯殺內而厚撫其兄弟。
entries.en: Early in the Zhengping era, when palace officials were put to death, Emperor Shizu, for Luyuan's sake, executed only Nei and treated his brothers with generous favor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhengping, palace officials were executed; Emperor Shizu for Luyuan's sake only killed Nei and treated his brothers generously.

entries.zh: 統以父任，侍東宮。
entries.en: Tong entered service in the Eastern Palace through his father's position.
entries.literal: Tong, through his father's position, served in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 世祖以元舅陽平王杜超女，南安長公主所生妻之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu married him to a daughter of Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and imperial maternal uncle, who had been born to Grand Princess Nan'an.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu took the daughter of Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and the imperial maternal uncle, born to Grand Princess Nan'an, and married her to him.

entries.zh: 車駕親自臨送，太官設供具，賜賚以千計。
entries.en: The emperor personally attended the send-off; the Imperial Provisioner laid out the wedding provisions, and gifts were bestowed by the thousand.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage personally came to send them off; the Imperial Provisioner set out the supplies, and gifts were counted by the thousand.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，典選部、主客二曹。
entries.en: After Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, Tong oversaw the Selection and Host and Guest bureaus.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, he managed the two bureaus of Selection and Host and Guest.

entries.zh: 興安二年卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of the Xing'an era.
entries.literal: He died in the second year of Xing'an.

entries.zh: 贈襄城王，諡曰景。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Jing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously presented as Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Jing.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He had no sons.
entries.literal: He had no son.

entries.zh: 子纂，字輔興，襲，依例降為公。
entries.en: His son Zuan, whose style name was Fuxing, inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to duke.
entries.literal: His son Zuan, style name Fuxing, inherited; according to precedent was reduced to duke.

entries.zh: 世宗時，起家司徒倉曹參軍。
entries.en: During Emperor Shizong's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
entries.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he began his career as Registrar of the Granary Bureau under the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 遷南秦平西府司馬、護軍長史，加右軍將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to military adviser of the Pacify-West headquarters in Southern Qin and chief clerk to the Protector Army, with the additional title General of the Right Army.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Military Adviser of the Pacify-West Headquarters of Southern Qin and Chief Clerk of the Protector Army, added General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 正光二年卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of the Zhengguang era.
entries.literal: He died in the second year of Zhengguang.

entries.zh: 贈假節、征虜將軍、荊州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored with the provisional staff of authority, the title General Who Captures Barbarians, and the post of governor of Jing province.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted provisional staff, General Who Captures Barbarians, and Governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 有嵇拔者，[4]世為紇奚部帥。
entries.en: There was also Ji Ba, [4] who for generations had been chieftain of the Hexi tribe.
entries.literal: There was Ji Ba, [4] for generations chief of the Hexi tribe.

entries.zh: 其父根，皇始初率眾歸魏。
entries.en: His father Gen, at the beginning of the Huangshi era, led his people to submit to Wei.
entries.literal: His father Gen, at the beginning of Huangshi, led the multitude to submit to Wei.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉之。
entries.en: Emperor Taizu commended him for it.
entries.literal: Taizu praised this.

entries.zh: 尚昭成女，生子拔，卒於尚書令。
entries.en: He married a daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng and fathered Ba, who died while serving as Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He married a daughter of Zhaocheng and begot Ba, who died in the office of Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 拔尚華陰公主，生子敬。
entries.en: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and fathered Jing.
entries.literal: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot Jing.

entries.zh: 元紹之逆也，主有功，超授敬大司馬、大將軍，封長樂王。
entries.en: During Yuan Shao's revolt the princess rendered distinguished service, and Jing was abruptly promoted to Grand Marshal and Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
entries.literal: During Yuan Shao's rebellion, the princess had merit; Jing was extraordinarily appointed Grand Marshal and Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

entries.zh: 薨。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 有嵇拔者 諸本「嵇」作「奚」，北史卷二五本傳作「嵇」。
entries.en: "There was Ji Ba": various editions write "Ji" as "Xi," but the main biography in the History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 25, reads "Ji."
entries.literal: "There was Ji Ba" — in various editions "ji" is written as "xi"; the main biography in History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 25, writes "ji."

entries.zh: 按卷三太宗紀永興三年十二月甲午見「任城公嵇拔」，泰常四年甲戌，記「獻懷長公主子嵇敬封長樂王」，與此傳合。
entries.en: Juan 3 of the Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3 (day jiawu), records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba," and Taichang year 4 (day jiaxu) records "Ji Jing, son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai, enfeoffed as Prince of Changle," which agrees with this biography.
entries.literal: Examining: juan 3 Taizong Annals, twelfth month of Yongxing year 3, day jiawu, records "Duke of Rencheng Ji Ba"; Taichang year 4, day jiaxu, records "Son of the Elder Princess of Xianhuai Ji Jing enfeoffed as Prince of Changle" — matching this biography.

entries.zh: 卷一一三官氏志：「紇奚氏後改為嵇氏。」
entries.en: Juan 113, Offices and Clans: "The Hexi clan was later changed to the Ji clan."
entries.literal: Juan 113 Offices and Clans Record: "The Hexi clan later was changed to the Ji clan."

entries.zh: 這裏「奚」字乃涉下「紇奚部帥」而訛，今據北史改。
entries.en: The character "Xi" here was corrupted under the influence of "Hexi tribal chief" below; it is corrected here on the authority of the History of the Northern Dynasties.
entries.literal: Here the character "xi" was corrupted by influence from "Hexi tribal chief" below; now changed according to the History of the Northern Dynasties.

entries.zh: 又傳失書嵇拔封爵。
entries.en: The biography also fails to record Ji Ba's enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Also the biography lost recording Ji Ba's enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 子護，襲爵。
entries.en: His son Hu inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Hu inherited the title.

entries.zh: 拜外都大官。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.

entries.zh: 太和中，詔以護年邁，既未致仕，令依舊養老之例。
entries.en: During the Taihe era an edict noted that Hu was advanced in years yet had not retired, and ordered that he be treated according to the established precedent for supporting elderly officials.
entries.literal: In Taihe, an edict because Hu was aged and had not yet retired ordered him to follow the old precedent for supporting the elderly.

entries.zh: 卒，子彥嗣。
entries.en: He died, and his son Yan succeeded him.
entries.literal: He died; his son Yan succeeded.

entries.zh: 根事迹遺落，故略附云。
entries.en: Because Gen's deeds have been lost from the record, they are only briefly appended here.
entries.literal: Gen's deeds were lost and scattered; therefore they are briefly appended here.

entries.zh: 車路頭，代人也。
entries.en: Che Lutou was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Che Lutou was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 少以忠厚選給東宮，為太宗帳下帥。
entries.en: In his youth he was chosen for the Eastern Palace on account of his honesty and loyalty and became commander of Emperor Taizong's personal guard.
entries.literal: In youth, for his honesty and kindness he was selected to serve the Eastern Palace as Tent Commander under Taizong.

entries.zh: 善自修立，謹慎無過。
entries.en: He cultivated himself diligently and was careful never to give offense.
entries.literal: He was good at cultivating himself, cautious and without fault.

entries.zh: 天賜末，太宗出於外，路頭隨侍竭力。
entries.en: Near the end of the Tiansi reign, when Emperor Taizong was forced out of the palace, Lutou followed and served him with all his strength.
entries.literal: At the end of Tiansi, Taizong lived outside; Lutou followed and served with all his strength.

entries.zh: 及太宗即位，拜為散騎常侍，賜爵金鄉公，加忠意將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong acceded, Lutou was appointed Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxiang, and made General of Loyal Intent.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant, granted the title Duke of Jinxiang, added General of Loyal Intent.

entries.zh: 後改為宣城公。
entries.en: He was later reassigned as Duke of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: Later he was changed to Duke of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 太宗性明察，羣臣多以職事遇譴，至有杖罰，故路頭優遊不任事，侍宿左右，從容談笑而已。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong was keen and exacting; many officials were punished for faults in their duties, some even beaten with the staff, so Lutou held no active post and merely kept night watch at the emperor's side, passing the time in easy talk and laughter.
entries.literal: Taizong's nature was sharp in perception; many officials were punished for their duties, even to beating; therefore Lutou leisurely did not take office, staying by his side at night, merely conversing and laughing at ease.

entries.zh: 路頭性無害，每至評獄處理，常獻寬恕之議，以此見重於朝。
entries.en: Lutou was by nature gentle and harmless; whenever cases came before him for judgment he would urge leniency, and for this he was held in high regard at court.
entries.literal: Lutou's nature was harmless; whenever he reached verdicts and judgments he often offered lenient views, and thus was honored at court.

entries.zh: 太宗亦敬納之，寵待隆厚，賞賜無數，當時功臣親幸莫及。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong likewise respected and heeded him; his favor was lavish and his gifts beyond counting, and among the meritorious ministers of the day none enjoyed such intimacy.
entries.literal: Taizong also respected and accepted this; favor was thick, rewards countless; among meritorious officials of the time none matched his intimacy.

entries.zh: 泰常六年卒。
entries.en: He died in the sixth year of the Taichang era.
entries.literal: He died in the sixth year of Taichang.

entries.zh: 太宗親臨哀慟。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong came in person to mourn him.
entries.literal: Taizong in person came to mourn.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、左衞大將軍、太師、宣城王，諡曰忠貞。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Left Guard, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Xuancheng, with the posthumous title Loyal and True.
entries.literal: Posthumously conferred Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Left Guard, Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xuancheng; posthumous name Loyal and True.

entries.zh: 喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。
entries.en: The funeral rites followed entirely the precedent set for Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.
entries.literal: Mourning rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

entries.zh: 陪葬金陵。
entries.en: He was buried beside the emperor at Jinling.
entries.literal: Buried alongside at Jinling.

entries.zh: 子眷襲爵。
entries.en: His son Juan inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Juan inherited the title.

entries.zh: 子裔，字承業。
entries.en: His son Yi, whose courtesy name was Chengye.
entries.literal: His son Yi, styled Chengye.

entries.zh: 世宗時，悅等為裔理嫡，還襲祖爵。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuanwu (Shizong), Yue and others upheld Yi's claim as legitimate heir, and he recovered the ancestral title.
entries.literal: During Shizong's time, Yue and others argued Yi's case as legitimate heir, and he returned to inherit the ancestral title.

entries.zh: 位至後軍將軍。
entries.en: He rose to General of the Rear Guard.
entries.literal: He reached the post of General of the Rear Guard.

entries.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、洛州刺史。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo province.

entries.zh: 子藏，襲。
entries.en: His son Zang inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Zang inherited.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，例降。
entries.en: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced in the usual way.
entries.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent his rank was reduced.

entries.zh: 晉宣帝季弟譙王遜之後也 南本以下諸本及北史卷二九司馬休之傳「遜」作「進」。
entries.en: "A descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun": in the Southern edition and later editions, and in the Beishi biography of Sima Xiuzhi (juan 29), "Xun" is written as "Jin."
entries.literal: "A descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun": in the Southern edition and later editions, and in the Beishi biography of Sima Xiuzhi (juan 29), "Xun" is written as "Jin."

entries.zh: 百衲本作「遜」，汲、局二本注宋本作「遜」。
entries.en: The Patchwork edition reads "Xun"; the Ji and Bureau editions' notes on the Song edition also read "Xun."
entries.literal: The Patchwork edition has "Xun"; the Ji and Bureau editions' notes on the Song edition also have "Xun."

entries.zh: 錢氏考異卷二八、李慈銘魏書札記、張森楷魏書校勘記各有說。
entries.en: Qian's Textual Variants (juan 28), Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Wei, and Zhang Senkai's Collation of the Book of Wei each discuss the point.
entries.literal: Qian's Textual Variants juan 28, Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Wei, and Zhang Senkai's Collation of the Book of Wei each have explanations.

entries.zh: 按晉書卷三七譙王遜傳，遜是進子，進死於曹魏時，封譙王的是遜，不是進。
entries.en: According to the Jinshu biography of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun (juan 37), Xun was Jin's son. Jin died in the Cao-Wei period, and it was Xun who was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao, not Jin.
entries.literal: According to Jinshu juan 37 biography of Prince of Qiao Sima Xun, Xun was Jin's son; Jin died in Cao-Wei times, and the one enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao was Xun, not Jin.

entries.zh: 但進才是晉宣帝司馬懿季弟，遜是從子，作「遜」也有問題。
entries.en: Yet only Jin was the youngest brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan, Sima Yi; Xun was a nephew. Writing "Xun" is also problematic.
entries.literal: But only Jin was the youngest brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan Sima Yi; Xun was a nephew—writing "Xun" also has problems.

entries.zh: 作「進」作「遜」既都有問題，而宋本作「遜」，恐原來就錯。
entries.en: Whether one writes "Jin" or "Xun" both are problematic, yet the Song edition reads "Xun"—the original text was probably already in error.
entries.literal: Whether written "Jin" or "Xun" both have problems, yet the Song edition has "Xun"—probably the original was already wrong.

entries.zh: 此卷史實上的謬誤較多，疑有訛脫竄亂，非魏收原文。
entries.en: This chapter contains many factual errors and is suspected of corruption, omission, and interpolation—not Wei Shou's original text.
entries.literal: This juan has rather many factual errors; it is suspected there are corruptions, omissions, and interpolations—not Wei Shou's original text.

entries.zh: 司馬休之 司馬楚之 司馬景之 司馬叔璠 司馬天助
entries.en: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, and Sima Tianzhu
entries.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu

entries.zh: 李訢，字元盛，小名真奴，范陽人也。
entries.en: Li Xin, whose courtesy name was Yuansheng and childhood name Zhennu, came from Fanyang.
entries.literal: Li Xin, courtesy name Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, was a native of Fanyang.

entries.zh: 曾袓產，產子績，二世知名於慕容氏。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji had both won renown for two generations under the Murong.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji were both famed for two generations under the Murong.

entries.zh: 父崇，馮跋吏部尚書、石城太守。
entries.en: His father Chong had served Feng Ba as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Shicheng.
entries.literal: His father Chong was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.

entries.zh: 延和初，車駕至和龍，崇率十餘郡歸降。
entries.en: Early in the Yanhe era, when the emperor reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies in submitting to the Wei court.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yanhe the imperial carriage reached Helong; Chong led more than ten commanderies in surrender.

entries.zh: 世袓甚禮之，呼曰「李公」，以崇為平西將軍、北幽州刺史、固安侯。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu honored him greatly, addressing him as "Lord Li," and appointed him General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Northern Youzhou, and Marquis of Gu'an.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu treated him with great courtesy, calling him "Lord Li," and appointed Chong General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Northern Youzhou, and Marquis of Gu'an.

entries.zh: 卒，年八十一，諡曰襄侯。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty-one and was given the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
entries.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one; his posthumous title was Marquis Xiang.

entries.zh: 奭弟盛，字仲炎。
entries.en: Shi's younger brother Sheng, whose courtesy name was Zhongyan.
entries.literal: Shi's younger brother Sheng, courtesy name Zhongyan.

entries.zh: 安東將軍、開府諮議參軍。
entries.en: He served as General Who Pacifies the East and Consulting Aide on a commander's staff.
entries.literal: He was General Who Pacifies the East and Consulting Aide on the staff with the ceremonial trappings of a commander.

entries.zh: 盛弟叔樊，平西將軍、太中大夫。
entries.en: Sheng's younger brother Shufan served as General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
entries.literal: Sheng's younger brother Shufan was General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

entries.zh: 竇瑾 許彥 李訢
entries.en: Dou Jin; Xu Yan; Li Xin
entries.literal: Dou Jin; Xu Yan; Li Xin

entries.zh: 夫百王之御士也，莫不資伏羣才，以隆治道。
entries.en: In governing scholars, none of the hundred kings failed to rely on the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.
entries.literal: Of the hundred kings' governing of scholars, none did not rely on and submit to the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.

entries.zh: 故周文以多士克寧，漢武以得賢為盛。
entries.en: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility, and Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as his glory.
entries.literal: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility; Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as flourishing.

entries.zh: 此載籍之所記，由來之常義。
entries.en: Such is what the records memorialize—the constant meaning handed down from antiquity.
entries.literal: This the records memorialize—the constant meaning from antiquity.

entries.zh: 魏自神䴥已後，宇內平定，誅赫連積世之僭，掃窮髮不羇之寇，南摧江楚，西盪涼域，殊方之外，慕義而至。
entries.en: From Shenqi onward Wei pacified the realm, destroyed the Herunian usurpers across generations, and swept away unrestrained barbarians; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—and beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.
entries.literal: Wei from after Shenqi onward, within the realm was pacified; they executed the Herunian line's usurpation across generations and swept away the unrestrained barbarians of poor hair; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.

entries.zh: 於是偃兵息甲，修立文學，登延儁造，酬諮政事。
entries.en: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established literary learning, promoted outstanding men, and consulted them on government affairs.
entries.literal: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established and raised literary learning, ascended and extended outstanding makers, and rewarded and consulted on government affairs.

entries.zh: 夢想賢哲，思遇其人，訪諸有司，以求名士。
entries.en: They dreamed of the worthy and wise and sought to encounter such persons, inquiring of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.
entries.literal: Dreaming of the worthy and wise, they thought to encounter such persons; they inquired of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.

entries.zh: 咸稱范陽盧玄等四十二人，皆冠冕之冑，著問州邦，有羽儀之用。
entries.en: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all scions of eminent houses, renowned in their commanderies and states, fit to serve as exemplars.
entries.literal: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all caps and coronets' scions, renowned in their commanderies and states, with the usefulness of feathered banners.

entries.zh: 親發明詔，以徵玄等。
entries.en: He personally issued bright edicts summoning Xuan and the others.
entries.literal: The sovereign personally issued bright edicts to summon Xuan and the others.

entries.zh: 乃曠官以待之，懸爵以縻之。
entries.en: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to retain them.
entries.literal: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to tether them.

entries.zh: 其就命三十五人，自餘依例州郡所遣者不可稱記。
entries.en: Thirty-five accepted the command; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.
entries.literal: Those who accepted the command were thirty-five men; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.

entries.zh: 爾乃髦士盈朝，而濟濟之美興焉。
entries.en: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the splendor of abundance flourished.
entries.literal: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the beauty of abundance arose.

entries.zh: 昔與之俱蒙斯舉，或從容廊廟，或游集私門，上談公務，下盡忻娛，以為千載一時，始於此矣。
entries.en: Those who together received this summons—some at ease in court, some gathering in private homes—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a moment once in a thousand years, beginning from this.
entries.literal: Formerly those who together received this summons—some at ease in the hall and temple, some gathering in private gates—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a thousand-year moment, beginning from this.

entries.zh: 日月推移，吉凶代謝，同徵之人，凋殲殆盡。
entries.en: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all gone.
entries.literal: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all destroyed.

entries.zh: 在者數子，然復分張。
entries.en: Of those who remain, only a few—and they too are scattered apart.
entries.literal: Of those who remain, a few men—yet again scattered apart.

entries.zh: 往昔之忻，變為悲戚。
entries.en: Former delight has changed into present sorrow.
entries.literal: Former delight changed into present sorrow.

entries.zh: 張仲業東臨營州，遲其還返，一敍于懷，齊衿于垂歿之年，寫情於桑榆之末。
entries.en: Zhang Zhongye governed Yingzhou in the east; I longed for his return and once poured out my heart to him; together we grieved as death approached, writing our feelings at life's sunset.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhongye eastward governed Yingzhou; I delayed his return and once poured out my breast; together we grieved in the year of approaching death, writing feeling at mulberry and sunset's end.

entries.zh: 其人不幸，復至殞歿。
entries.en: That man was unfortunate and again met death.
entries.literal: That man was unfortunate and again came to perishing death.

entries.zh: 在朝者皆後進之士，居里者非疇昔之人，進涉無寄心之所，出入無解顏之地。
