entries.en: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; in advancing there is no place for the mind to rest, in going out and entering no face to unburden.
entries.literal: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; advancing and wading has no place for the mind to rest; going out and entering has no place to unknit the countenance.

entries.zh: 顧省形骸，所以永歎而不已。
entries.en: Looking back at my bodily form, I therefore sigh unceasingly.
entries.literal: Looking back at my bodily form, therefore I sigh unceasingly.

entries.zh: 夫頌者美盛德之形容，亦可以長言寄意。
entries.en: The eulogy portrays flourishing virtue's form; one may also use extended words to lodge one's intent.
entries.literal: The eulogy is the portrayal of flourishing virtue's form and appearance; one may also use long words to lodge intent.

entries.zh: 不為文二十年矣，然事切於心，豈可默乎？
entries.en: I have not written for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I remain silent?
entries.literal: I have not composed writing for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I be silent?

entries.zh: 遂為之頌，詞曰：
entries.en: Thereupon I composed this eulogy; the words say:
entries.literal: Thereupon I made this eulogy for them; the words say:

entries.zh: 郡功曹長樂杜熙
entries.en: Du Xi of Changle, Merit Officer Scribe of the Commandery
entries.literal: Merit Officer Scribe of the Commandery, Du Xi of Changle

entries.zh: 潘符摽尚，杜熙好和，清不潔流，渾不同波。
entries.en: Pan Fu held high esteem and Du Xi loved harmony; pure without defiling the current, muddy without sharing the wave.
entries.literal: Pan Fu held high esteem; Du Xi loved harmony; pure without defiling the current; muddy without sharing the wave.

entries.zh: 絕希龍津，止分常科，幽而逾顯，損而逾多。
entries.en: He utterly hoped for the dragon ford yet stopped at the common grade; obscure yet more illustrious, diminished yet more abundant.
entries.literal: He utterly hoped for the dragon ford; stopping at the common grade; obscure yet more illustrious; diminished yet more abundant.

entries.zh: 高允，字伯恭，勃海人也。
entries.en: Gao Yun, whose courtesy name was Bogong, came from Bohai.
entries.literal: Gao Yun, styled Bogong, was a man of Bohai.

entries.zh: 祖泰，在叔父湖傳。
entries.en: His grandfather Tai is discussed in the biography of his uncle Hu.
entries.literal: His grandfather Tai is treated in the biography of his uncle Hu.

entries.zh: 父韜，少以英朗知名，同郡封懿雅相敬慕。
entries.en: His father Tao won early fame for his keen intelligence and open manner; he and Feng Yi of the same commandery held each other in deep mutual esteem.
entries.literal: His father Tao was in youth renowned for brilliance and clarity; Feng Yi of the same commandery admired and respected each other in refined friendship.

entries.zh: 為慕容垂太尉從事中郎。
entries.en: He served Murong Chui as an attendant gentleman in the office of the grand commandant.
entries.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman in the office of the Grand Commandant under Murong Chui.

entries.zh: 太祖平中山，以韜為丞相參軍。
entries.en: After Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, Tao was appointed an army adviser on the chancellor's staff.
entries.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Zhongshan, Tao was made Army Advisor to the Chancellor.

entries.zh: 早卒。
entries.en: He died at an early age.
entries.literal: He died young.

entries.zh: 渾弟繪，字敬文。
entries.en: Hun's younger brother Hui, whose courtesy name was Jingwen.
entries.literal: Hun's younger brother Hui, styled Jingwen.

entries.zh: 齊王丞相府司馬。
entries.en: He served as marshal of the Prince of Qi's chancellor's office.
entries.literal: He was marshal of the Prince of Qi's chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 繪弟系，字乾經。
entries.en: Hui's younger brother Xi,[2] whose courtesy name was Ganjing.
entries.literal: Hui's younger brother Xi,[2] styled Ganjing.

entries.zh: 少聰惠，有才學，與舅子河間邢昕少相倫輩，晚不逮之。
entries.en: As a youth he was clever and well read; in his early years he was the equal of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later life he did not measure up to him.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and bright and possessed literary learning; in youth he was a peer of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later years he did not match him.

entries.zh: 初為征東法曹參軍，後除奉車都尉，加寧遠將軍。
entries.en: He began as a legal bureau staff officer on the eastern campaign staff, then was appointed commandant of the imperial carriages and additionally made general who pacifies the distance.
entries.literal: At first he was a legal bureau staff officer on the eastern campaign staff; later he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and additionally given the title General Who Pacifies the Distance.

entries.zh: 尋拜大司馬廣陵王錄事參軍。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made a recording staff officer under the grand marshal, Prince of Guangling.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed recording staff officer under the Grand Marshal, Prince of Guangling.

entries.zh: 府解，還鄉里。
entries.en: When the office was dissolved, he returned home.
entries.literal: When the office was dissolved, he returned to his home district.

entries.zh: 徵拜冠軍將軍、中散大夫。
entries.en: He was summoned and appointed general who establishes the champion and palace writer grand master.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Establishes the Champion and Palace Writer Grand Master.

entries.zh: 齊獻武王從子永樂為濟州刺史，聞而請與相見，待以賓交之禮。
entries.en: Prince Xianwu of Qi's nephew Yongle was regional inspector of Jizhou; when he heard of Xi he asked to meet him and treated him with the courtesy due an honored guest.
entries.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi's nephew Yongle was Regional Inspector of Jizhou; when he heard of this he requested a meeting and treated Xi with the courtesy due a guest and companion.

entries.zh: 及永樂薨，系送葬還都。
entries.en: When Yongle died, Xi attended the funeral and then returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When Yongle died, Xi attended the funeral and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 蕭衍遣使朝貢，侍中李神儁舉系為尚書南主客郎。
entries.en: When Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute, Palace Attendant Li Shenjun recommended Xi for the post of southern host master in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When Xiao Yan sent envoys to offer tribute, Palace Attendant Li Shenjun recommended Xi for the post of Southern Host Master in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 系前後接對凡十八人，頗為稱職。
entries.en: Xi received and entertained eighteen envoys in all and proved quite competent in the role.
entries.literal: Xi in all received and responded to eighteen envoys, and performed the duty quite competently.

entries.zh: 齊文襄王攝選，以系為司徒諮議參軍，因謂之曰：「自郎署至此，所謂不次，以卿人才，故有此舉耳。」
entries.en: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi took charge of appointments, he made Xi a consulting member on the minister of works' staff and told him, "To rise from the bureau ranks to here is what people call an exceptional promotion—it is because of your talent that you have received it."
entries.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi assumed charge of selections, he made Xi a Consulting Member of the Household of the Minister of Works, and said to him: "From the bureau offices to this post, one might call it an exceptional promotion; it is because of your talent that this appointment has been made."

entries.zh: 尋加征虜將軍。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was also made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 武定五年，兼散騎常侍使蕭衍，與其二兄前後將命，時人稱之。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary on a mission to Xiao Yan; he and his two elder brothers went on embassies in succession, and contemporaries praised them.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Xiao Yan; together with his two elder brothers he went on embassies in succession, and men of the time praised them.

entries.zh: 太尉高岳出討，以系為大都督司馬。
entries.en: When Grand Commandant Gao Yue marched out on campaign, he made Xi marshal of the area commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: When Grand Commandant Gao Yue marched out on campaign, he made Xi marshal of the area commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 師還，拜太子家令。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was appointed director of the household of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 七年八月卒，時年四十六，時人傷惜之。
entries.en: He died in the eighth month of the seventh year at the age of forty-six, and contemporaries mourned his loss.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year he died; he was then forty-six years old, and men of the time mourned and regretted it.

entries.zh: 齊初，贈平東將軍、北徐州刺史，諡曰文。
entries.en: Early in Qi he was posthumously made general who pacifies the east and regional inspector of North Xuzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of North Xuzhou; his posthumous name was Wen.

entries.zh: 李靈 崔鑒
entries.en: Li Ling and Cui Jian
entries.literal: Li Ling, Cui Jian

entries.zh: 宗欽，字景若，金城人也。
entries.en: Zong Qin, whose courtesy name was Jingruo, came from Jincheng.
entries.literal: Zong Qin, courtesy name Jingruo, was a man of Jincheng.

entries.zh: 父燮，字文友，呂光太常卿。
entries.en: His father Xie, whose courtesy name was Wenyou, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Lü Guang.
entries.literal: His father Xie, courtesy name Wenyou, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Lü Guang.

entries.zh: 欽少而好學，有儒者之風，博綜羣言，聲著河右。
entries.en: Qin from youth loved learning, had the air of a Confucian, ranged broadly through all schools of discourse, and his fame resounded west of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: Qin from youth loved learning, had the air of a Confucian, ranged broadly through all schools of discourse, and his fame resounded in the lands west of the Yellow River.

entries.zh: 仕沮渠蒙遜，為中書郎、世子洗馬。
entries.en: Indeed, He served Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He served Juqu Mengxun as Secretariat Gentleman and Groom of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 欽上東宮侍臣箴曰：「恢恢玄古，悠悠生民。
entries.en: Qin presented an Admonition for Eastern Palace Attendants, saying: "Vast, vast the dark antiquity, and long, long the living folk.
entries.literal: Qin presented an Admonition for Eastern Palace Attendants, saying: "Vast, vast the dark antiquity; long, long the living folk.

entries.zh: 五才迭用，經敍彝倫。
entries.en: The five talents rotate in use, and the classics set out constant norms.
entries.literal: The five talents rotate in use; the classics set out constant norms.

entries.zh: 匡父維子，弼君伊臣。
entries.en: To correct the father and sustain the son, to assist the ruler— ministers like Yi.
entries.literal: To correct the father and sustain the son, to assist the ruler— ministers like Yi.

entries.zh: 顛而能扶，屈而能申。
entries.en: Upright when overturned yet able to support, and bent yet able to straighten.
entries.literal: Upright when overturned yet able to support; bent yet able to straighten.

entries.zh: 昔在上聖，妙鑒厥趣。
entries.en: of old the highest sages subtly discerned this aim.
entries.literal: Of old the highest sages subtly discerned this aim.

entries.zh: 不曰我明，而乖其度。
entries.en: Indeed, Not saying "I am enlightened" yet straying from its measure.
entries.literal: Not saying "I am enlightened" yet straying from its measure.

entries.zh: 不曰我新，而忽其故。
entries.en: Indeed, Not saying "I am new" yet neglecting what is old.
entries.literal: Not saying "I am new" yet neglecting what is old.

entries.zh: 如彼在泉，臨深是懼。
entries.en: like one beside a spring, in deep places he fears.
entries.literal: Like one beside a spring, in deep places he fears.

entries.zh: 如彼覆車，望途改步。
entries.en: Indeed, [3] Like one beside an overturned cart, seeing the road he changes step.
entries.literal: Like one beside an overturned cart, seeing the road he changes step.

entries.zh: 是以令問宣流，英風遠布。
entries.en: Therefore good repute spreads abroad, and heroic wind reaches far.
entries.literal: Therefore good repute spreads abroad; heroic wind reaches far.

entries.zh: 及於三季，道喪純遷。
entries.en: Indeed, By the three degenerate ages the Way was lost and purity shifted.
entries.literal: By the three degenerate ages the Way was lost and purity shifted.

entries.zh: 桀起瓊臺，紂醊糟山。
entries.en: Jie raised the Jade Terrace, and zhou piled the Mountain of Dregs.
entries.literal: Jie raised the Jade Terrace; Zhou piled the Mountain of Dregs.

entries.zh: 周滅妖姒，羿喪以田。
entries.en: Zhou destroyed the evil Mo, and yi lost his state through fields.
entries.literal: Zhou destroyed the evil Mo; Yi lost his state through fields.

entries.zh: 險詖蔽其耳目，鄭衞陳於其前。
entries.en: Peril and deceit blocked their ears and eyes, and zheng and Wei were set before them.
entries.literal: Peril and deceit blocked their ears and eyes; Zheng and Wei were set before them.

entries.zh: 怙才肆虐，異端是纏。
entries.en: Relying on talent they acted wildly, and heterodox ways entangled them.
entries.literal: Relying on talent they acted wildly; heterodox ways entangled them.

entries.zh: 豈伊害身，厥胤殲焉。
entries.en: did they only harm themselves? Their heirs were destroyed.
entries.literal: Did they only harm themselves? Their heirs were destroyed.

entries.zh: 茫茫禹跡，畫為九區。
entries.en: Vast, vast the traces of Yu, and the land was drawn into nine regions.
entries.literal: Vast, vast the traces of Yu; the land was drawn into nine regions.

entries.zh: 昆蟲鳥獸，各有巢居。
entries.en: insects, birds, and beasts— each had its nest and dwelling.
entries.literal: Insects, birds, and beasts— each had its nest and dwelling.

entries.zh: 雲歌唐后，垂橫美虞。
entries.en: Cloud songs for the lord of Tang, and hanging banners praised Yu.
entries.literal: Cloud songs for the lord of Tang; hanging banners praised Yu.

entries.zh: 疏網改祝，殷道攸敷。
entries.en: Loose nets changed the sacrifice, and the Yin Way was broadly spread.
entries.literal: Loose nets changed the sacrifice; the Yin Way was broadly spread.

entries.zh: 龍盤應德，隨蛇銜珠。
entries.en: The dragon coiled responding to virtue, and the snake followed, holding a pearl.
entries.literal: The dragon coiled responding to virtue; the snake followed, holding a pearl.

entries.zh: 勿謂無心，識命不殊。
entries.en: Do not say they were without mind, and they knew fate was not different.
entries.literal: Do not say they were without mind; they knew fate was not different.

entries.zh: 勿謂理絕，千載同符。
entries.en: Do not say principle was cut off, and through a thousand ages the seal is the same.
entries.literal: Do not say principle was cut off; through a thousand ages the seal is the same.

entries.zh: 爰在子桓，靈數攸臻。
entries.en: It came to the age of Zihuan, and the numinous tally was at hand.
entries.literal: It came to the age of Zihuan; the numinous tally was at hand.

entries.zh: 儀形徐阮，左右劉陳。
entries.en: He took Xu and Ruan as models, and at his left and right Liu and Chen.
entries.literal: He took Xu and Ruan as models; at his left and right Liu and Chen.

entries.zh: 披文採友，叩典問津。
entries.en: He spread writing and chose friends, and knocked at the canon and asked the ford.
entries.literal: He spread writing and chose friends; knocked at the canon and asked the ford.

entries.zh: 用能重離襲曜，魏鼎維新。
entries.en: Thus he could renew the doubled radiance, and the Wei tripod was made new.
entries.literal: Thus he could renew the doubled radiance; the Wei tripod was made new.

entries.zh: 於昭儲后，運應玄籙。
entries.en: Indeed, How glorious the Heir Apparent— his fortune matched the dark tally.
entries.literal: How glorious the Heir Apparent— his fortune matched the dark tally.

entries.zh: 夕惕乾乾，虛衿遠屬。
entries.en: Evening vigil, morning diligence, and empty breast, far-reaching aim.
entries.literal: Evening vigil, morning diligence; empty breast, far-reaching aim.

entries.zh: 外撫幽荒，內懷焭獨。
entries.en: Without he soothed the dark frontier, and within he cherished the orphaned and alone.
entries.literal: Without he soothed the dark frontier; within he cherished the orphaned and alone.

entries.zh: 猶懼思不逮遠，明不遐燭。
entries.en: Still he feared his thought did not reach far, his clarity did not shine distant.
entries.literal: Still he feared his thought did not reach far, his clarity did not shine distant.

entries.zh: 君有諍臣，庭立謗木。
entries.en: The ruler has remonstrating ministers, and in the court stands the slander-wood.
entries.literal: The ruler has remonstrating ministers; in the court stands the slander-wood.

entries.zh: 本枝克昌，永符天祿。
entries.en: The root branches flourish, and forever matching heaven's blessing.
entries.literal: The root branches flourish; forever matching heaven's blessing.

entries.zh: 微臣作箴，敢告在僕。」
entries.en: This humble servant composes an admonition— I dare report it to the attendant.".
entries.literal: This humble servant composes an admonition— I dare report it to the attendant."

entries.zh: 趙逸 胡方回 胡叟 宋繇 張湛 宗欽 段承根 闞駰 劉昞 趙柔 索敞 陰仲達
entries.en: Zhao Yi, and hu Fanghui, and hu Sou, and song Yao, and zhang Zhan, and zong Qin, and duan Chenggen, and yan Yin, and liu Bing, and zhao Rou, and suo Chang, and yin Zhongda
entries.literal: Zhao Yi; Hu Fanghui; Hu Sou; Song Yao; Zhang Zhan; Zong Qin; Duan Chenggen; Yan Yin; Liu Bing; Zhao Rou; Suo Chang; Yin Zhongda

entries.zh: 二十一年，車駕南伐，顯宗為右軍府長史、征虜將軍、統軍。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year, when the emperor marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and commander of the army.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and army commander.

entries.zh: 軍次赭陽，蕭鸞戍主成公期遣其軍主胡松、高法援等并引蠻賊來擊軍營，顯宗親率拒戰，遂斬法援首。
entries.en: When the army halted at Zheyang, Cheng Gongqi, garrison commander under Xiao Luan, sent his commanders Hu Song and Gao Fayuan, among others, together with tribal allies to strike the camp; Xianzong personally led the defense and cut off Fayuan's head.
entries.literal: When the army halted at Zheyang, Xiao Luan's garrison commander Cheng Gongqi sent his army commanders Hu Song, Gao Fayuan, and others, together leading tribal raiders to attack the camp; Xianzong personally led the resistance and beheaded Fayuan.

entries.zh: 顯宗至新野，高祖詔曰：「卿破賊斬帥，殊益軍勢，朕方攻堅城，何為不作露布也？」
entries.en: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Xiaowen sent an edict: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening our army's momentum; I am pressing a hard siege — why did you not publish a victory bulletin?"
entries.literal: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening army morale; I am assaulting a fortified city — why did you not issue a battle report?"

entries.zh: 顯宗曰：「臣頃聞鎮南將軍王肅獲賊二三，驢馬數匹，皆為露布，臣在東觀，私每哂之。
entries.en: Xianzong said: "I recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and a few donkeys and horses, yet still issued victory bulletins; when I served at the Eastern Hall, I privately laughed at that every time.
entries.literal: Xianzong said: "Your subject recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and several donkeys and horses, yet issued battle reports; when I was at the Eastern Hall for observations, I privately always laughed at this.

entries.zh: 近雖仰憑威靈，得摧醜虜，兵寡力弱，擒斬不多。
entries.en: Recently, though I leaned on your august power and was able to break the foul enemy, my troops were few and my strength slight; captures and kills were not many.
entries.literal: Recently, though relying on your august power I was able to crush the foul enemy, our troops were few and strength weak; captures and kills were not many.

entries.zh: 脫復高曳長縑，虛張功捷，尤而效之，其罪彌甚。
entries.en: If I now unfurled long silk banners and falsely inflated my achievements, copying that fault and making it my own, my offense would be all the graver.
entries.literal: If I again hoisted long silk banners and falsely inflated achievements, committing the same fault and imitating that example, my guilt would be all the greater.

entries.zh: 臣所以斂毫卷帛，解上而已。」
entries.en: That is why I put away brush and silk and submitted only a plain report."
entries.literal: Therefore I folded my brush and rolled up the silk and submitted a simple report, nothing more."

entries.zh: 高祖笑曰：「如卿此勳，誠合茅社，須赭陽平定，檢審相酬。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen smiled and said: "Merit such as yours truly deserves a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review the matter and reward you properly."
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu smiled and said: "For merit such as yours, you truly deserve a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review and reward you accordingly."

entries.zh: 新野平，以顯宗為鎮南、廣陽王嘉諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was appointed consulting adjutant on the staff of Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.
entries.literal: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was made consulting adjutant to Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 顯宗後上表，頗自矜伐，訴前征勳，詔曰：「顯宗斐然成章，甚可怪責，進退無檢，虧我清風。
entries.en: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather full of self-praise, pleading his earlier campaign merit. An edict said: "Xianzong's polished prose is very much to be censured; his conduct lacks restraint in advance and retreat, and it tarnishes our pure ethos.
entries.literal: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather self-praising, pleading his prior campaign merit. An edict read: "Xianzong's polished composition is much to be blamed; his advance and retreat lack restraint and damage our pure ethos.

entries.zh: 此而不糾，或長弊俗。
entries.en: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may take deeper root.
entries.literal: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may grow.

entries.zh: 可付尚書，推列以聞。」
entries.en: Let the matter be referred to the Masters of Writing for investigation and report."
entries.literal: Let it be referred to the Masters of Writing to investigate and report."

entries.zh: 兼尚書張彝奏免顯宗官，詔曰：「顯宗雖浮矯致愆，才猶可用，豈得永棄之也！
entries.en: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity brought him to fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be cast off forever!
entries.literal: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity caused fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be abandoned forever!

entries.zh: 可以白衣守諮議，展其後效。
entries.en: He may continue as adviser in plain clothes and prove his worth hereafter.
entries.literal: He may serve as adviser in plain clothes and show his merit hereafter.

entries.zh: 但鄙很之性，不足參華，可奪見□，并禁問訊諸王。」
entries.en: But his coarse and obstinate nature makes him unfit for elegant company; his privilege of audience may be revoked, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."
entries.literal: But his boorish and obstinate nature is unfit for elegant company; his audience privilege may be revoked □, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."

entries.zh: 韓麒麟 程駿
entries.en: Han Qilin and Cheng Jun
entries.literal: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun

entries.zh: 張讜，字處言，清河東武城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Dang of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, styled Chuyan.
entries.literal: Zhang Dang, courtesy name Chuyan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

entries.zh: 六世祖名犯顯祖諱，晉長秋卿。
entries.en: A sixth-generation ancestor's name tabooed Xianzu; he was Jin Director of Palace Parks.
entries.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor's name violated Emperor Xianzu's taboo; he was Jin Director of the Palace Parks.

entries.zh: 父華，為慕容超左僕射。
entries.en: Father Hua was Chao's left vice minister.
entries.literal: His father Hua was Left Vice Minister under Murong Chao.

entries.zh: 讜仕劉駿，歷給事中、泰山太守、青冀二州輔國府長史，帶魏郡太守。
entries.en: Dang served Liu Jun as palace gentleman, Taishan and Wei governor, and Qing-Ji chief clerk.
entries.literal: Dang served Liu Jun, passing through Gentleman at the Palace Gate, Taishan governor, chief clerk of Qing-Ji auxiliary state, and concurrent Wei governor.

entries.zh: 劉彧之立，遙授冠軍將軍、東徐州刺史。
entries.en: When Yu took power, Dang was named champion general and eastern Xu governor.
entries.literal: At Liu Yu's enthronement he was remotely made General Who Champions the Army and eastern Xu governor.

entries.zh: 薛安都 畢眾敬 沈文秀 張讜 田益宗 孟表
entries.en: Xue Andou; Bi Zhongjing; Shen Wenxiu; Zhang Dang; Tian Yizong; Meng Biao
entries.literal: Xue Andou; Bi Zhongjing; Shen Wenxiu; Zhang Dang; Tian Yizong; Meng Biao

entries.zh: 紹，肅前妻謝生也，肅臨薨，謝始攜二女及紹至壽春。
entries.en: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie. When Su was dying, Lady Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.
entries.literal: Shao was the son of Su's former wife, Lady Xie; when Su was near death, Xie at last brought her two daughters and Shao to Shouchun.

entries.zh: 世宗納其女為夫人，肅宗又納紹女為嬪。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as a consort, and Emperor Suzong later took Shao's daughter as an imperial concubine.
entries.literal: The Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Lady; the Emperor Suzong also took Shao's daughter as Imperial Concubine.

entries.zh: 肅弟秉，字文政。
entries.en: Su's younger brother Bing, whose courtesy name was Wenzheng.
entries.literal: Su's younger brother Bing, styled Wenzheng.

entries.zh: 涉獵書史，微有兄風。
entries.en: He read widely in books and histories and showed something of his elder brother's manner.
entries.literal: He ranged through books and histories and had a slight trace of his elder brother's manner.

entries.zh: 世宗初，攜兄子誦、翊、衍等入國，拜中書郎，遷司徒諮議，出為輔國將軍、幽州刺史。
entries.en: Early in the Shizong reign he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into Wei territory. He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, then Adviser to the Minister of Education, and later sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizong, he brought his elder brother's sons Song, Yi, Yan, and others into the state; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, and sent out as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of You Province.

entries.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、徐州刺史。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He died; posthumously granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 誦弟衍，字文舒。
entries.en: Song's younger brother Yan, whose courtesy name was Wenshu.
entries.literal: Song's younger brother Yan, styled Wenshu.

entries.zh: 名行器藝亞於誦。
entries.en: His reputation, conduct, and abilities were second only to Song's.
entries.literal: His reputation, conduct, talent, and skill were second to Song's.

entries.zh: 自著作佐郎，稍遷尚書郎、員外常侍、司空諮議、光祿大夫、廷尉、揚州大中正、度支尚書，仍轉七兵，徙太常卿。
entries.en: Starting as Assistant Gentleman of the Academy, he rose through Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, and Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops and became Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: From Assistant Gentleman of the Academy he was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat, Acting Regular Attendant, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Justice, Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, Director of Revenue, then transferred to the Seven Troops, and moved to Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 出為散騎常侍、征東將軍、西兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Attendant at the Palace Cadet, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Western Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 衍屆治未幾，屬尒朱仲遠稱兵內向，州既路衝，為其攻逼。
entries.en: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward. The province lay on the main route and came under his attack.
entries.literal: Yan had been in office only a short time when Erzhu Zhongyuan raised troops and marched inward; the province being on the main route, he was attacked and pressed by him.

entries.zh: 衍不能守，為仲遠所擒，以其名望不害也，令其騎牛從軍，久乃見釋。
entries.en: Yan could not hold the province and was captured by Zhongyuan. Because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army. Only after a long time was he released.
entries.literal: Yan could not hold it and was captured by Zhongyuan; because of his reputation he was not harmed, but was made to ride an ox with the army; only after a long time was he released.

entries.zh: 還洛，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: On returning to Luoyang he was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 孝靜初，轉侍中，將軍如故。
entries.en: Early in the Xiaojing reign he was made Palace Attendant while retaining his general's title.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, he was transferred to Palace Attendant; his general's title as before.

entries.zh: 天平三年卒，年五十二。
entries.en: In the third year of the Tianping reign he died, at the age of fifty-two.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died, aged fifty-two.

entries.zh: 敕給東園祕器、賵物三百段，贈使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、徐州刺史，諡曰文獻。
entries.en: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods. He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
entries.literal: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and three hundred sections of funeral goods; posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenxian.

entries.zh: 衍篤於交舊，有故人竺虩，於西兗為仲遠所害，其妻子飢寒，衍置之於家，累年贍恤，世人稱其敦厚。
entries.en: Yan was devoted to old friends. An acquaintance named Zhu Xi had been killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou, leaving his wife and children hungry and cold. Yan took them into his household and supported them for years, and the world praised his generosity.
entries.literal: Yan was devoted to old friends; he had an old acquaintance Zhu Xi who was killed by Zhongyuan in Western Yanzhou; his wife and children were hungry and cold; Yan took them into his household and for years provided support; the world praised his generosity.

entries.zh: 誦，字國章，肅長兄融之子。
entries.en: Song, whose courtesy name was Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.
entries.literal: Song, styled Guozhang, was the son of Su's elder brother Rong.

entries.zh: 學涉有文才，神氣清儁，風流甚美。
entries.en: He was learned and gifted in letters, with a clear and handsome presence and an exceptionally refined bearing.
entries.literal: He studied broadly and had literary talent; his spirit was clear and handsome, and his bearing exceedingly fine.

entries.zh: 自員外郎、司徒主簿，轉司徒屬、司空諮議、通直常侍、汝南王友。
entries.en: He rose from Gentleman of the Palace and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.
entries.literal: From Gentleman of the Palace, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, he was transferred to Attendant of the Minister of Education, Adviser to the Minister of Works, Direct Regular Attendant, and Companion to the Prince of Runan.

entries.zh: 遷司徒諮議，加前軍、散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Adviser to the Minister of Education, with additional titles of Vanguard General, Attendant at the Palace Cadet, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 出為左將軍、幽州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.
entries.literal: He was sent out as General of the Left and Inspector of You Province.

entries.zh: 未幾，徵為長兼祕書監，徙給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Before long he was recalled as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Before long he was summoned as Senior Acting Director of the Palace Library, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 肅宗崩，靈太后之立幼主也，於時大赦，誦宣讀詔書，音制抑揚，風神疎秀，百僚傾屬，莫不歎美。
entries.en: When Emperor Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling installed the young emperor, a general amnesty was proclaimed. Song read the edict aloud with cadences rising and falling, his bearing open and refined. The officials all turned to him in admiration.
entries.literal: When Suzong died and Empress Dowager Ling established the young ruler, there was at the time a great amnesty; Song read the edict aloud, his tones rising and falling, his bearing open and refined; the hundred officials turned to him, and none failed to sigh in admiration.

entries.zh: 孝莊初，於河陰遇害，年三十七。
entries.en: Early in the Xiaozhuang reign he was killed at Heyin, at the age of thirty-seven.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, he met with violence at Heyin, aged thirty-seven.

entries.zh: [3]贈驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、司空公、徐州刺史，諡曰文宣。
entries.en: [3] He was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenhuan.
entries.literal: [3] Posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Xuzhou; posthumous title Wenhuan.

entries.zh: 遷中書侍郎，兼員外常侍，使於蕭賾。
entries.en: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Acting Regular Attendant and sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Acting Regular Attendant, and sent on mission to Xiao Ze.

entries.zh: 賾司徒蕭子良、祕書丞王融等皆稱美之，以為志氣謇烈不逮李彪，而體韻和雅、舉止閑邃過之。
entries.en: Xiao Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary Wang Rong, and others all praised him, finding that in resolve and boldness he did not match Li Biao, but in grace of manner and refined bearing he surpassed him.
entries.literal: Ze's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretary of the Palace Library Wang Rong, and others all praised him, considering that in resolve and spirit, forthrightness and fierceness, he did not match Li Biao, but in bodily grace and harmony, elegance of manner and leisurely depth, he surpassed him.

entries.zh: 轉散騎侍郎，時散騎位在中書之右。
entries.en: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet, whose rank at the time stood above that of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at the Palace Cadet; at the time the Palace Cadet's rank stood to the right of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 高祖曾論江左事，因問弁曰：「卿比南行，入其隅隩，彼政道云何？
entries.en: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and asked Bian: 'On your recent mission south you entered their inner circles—how is their governance?
entries.literal: The Emperor Gaozu once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and therefore asked Bian: 'On your recent journey south, you entered their inner recesses—how is their governance?

entries.zh: 興亡之數可得知不？」
entries.en: Can one discern the signs of their rise or fall?'
entries.literal: Can the numbers of rise and fall be known?'

entries.zh: 弁對曰：「蕭氏父子無大功於天下，既以逆取，不能順守。
entries.en: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have won no great merit for the realm. Having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it through proper governance.
entries.literal: Bian replied: 'The Xiao father and son have no great merit for the realm; having seized power by rebellion, they cannot preserve it by compliance.

entries.zh: 德政不理，徭役滋劇，內無股肱之助，外有怨叛之民，以臣觀之，必不能貽厥孫謀，保有南海。
entries.en: Their virtuous governance is in disorder and corvée labor grows ever heavier. Within they lack loyal ministers; without they face resentful and rebellious subjects. In my view they cannot bequeath lasting plans to their descendants or long hold the south.
entries.literal: Virtuous governance is not ordered; corvée labor grows ever heavier; within they have no helpers as arms and thighs; without they have resentful and rebellious people—in my view they surely cannot bequeath plans to their descendants or long hold the southern sea.

entries.zh: 若物憚其威，身免為幸。」
entries.en: If men fear their might, merely to escape with one's life is already fortunate.'
entries.literal: If creatures fear their might, to escape with one's person is already fortunate.'

entries.zh: 王肅 宋弁
entries.en: Wang Su; Song Bian
entries.literal: Wang Su; Song Bian

entries.zh: 郭祚 張彝
entries.en: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi
entries.literal: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi

entries.zh: 張彝，字慶賓，清河東武城人。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

entries.zh: 曾祖幸，慕容超東牟太守，後率戶歸國。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xing had been Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; later he led his household in submission to the Wei.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xing was Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; afterward he led his household to surrender to [Northern Wei].

entries.zh: 世祖嘉之，賜爵平陸侯，拜平遠將軍、青州刺史。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu praised him, granted him the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu commended him, bestowed the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 祖準之襲，又為東青州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhun inherited the title and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhun inherited [the title] and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.

entries.zh: 父靈真，早卒。
entries.en: His father Lingzhen died young.
entries.literal: His father Lingzhen died early.

entries.zh: 彝性公強，有風氣，歷覽經史。
entries.en: Yi was by nature upright and forceful, possessed of moral bearing, and had read widely in the classics and histories.
entries.literal: Yi was by nature forthright and forceful, possessed moral stature, and read widely in the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 高祖初，襲祖侯爵，與盧淵、李安民等結為親友，往來朝會，常相追隨。
entries.en: In the early years of Emperor Wen, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and became close friends with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court they were often together.
entries.literal: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and formed friendships with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court gatherings they were often in each other's company.

entries.zh: 淵為主客令，安民與彝並為散令。
entries.en: Lu Yuan was Director of Guests; Li Anmin and Zhang Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: Yuan was Director of Guests; Anmin and Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 彝少而豪放，出入殿庭，步眄高上，無所顧忌。
entries.en: From youth Zhang Yi was bold and free-spirited; entering and leaving the palace halls, he walked with his eyes lifted high, heedless of restraint.
entries.literal: Yi from youth was bold and unrestrained; entering and leaving the palace hall, he walked with his gaze lifted high, without any restraint.

entries.zh: 文明太后雅尚恭謹，因會次見其如此，遂召集百僚督責之，令其修悔，而猶無悛改。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Wenming prized reverence and restraint. Once at court she saw him behave so and summoned the hundred officials to rebuke him publicly, ordering him to repent—but he still would not change.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming greatly valued reverence and prudence; on one occasion at court she saw him behave thus, whereupon she assembled the hundred officials to supervise and rebuke him, ordering him to repent and reform—yet he still showed no change of heart.

entries.zh: 善於督察，每東西馳使有所巡檢，彝恒充其選，清慎嚴猛，所至人皆畏伏，儔類亦以此高之。
entries.en: He was skilled at inspection. Whenever envoys were sent east or west on tour, Yi was always chosen. Clear, cautious, strict, and stern, he inspired fear wherever he went, and his peers respected him for it.
entries.literal: He was skilled at supervision and inspection; whenever emissaries were dispatched east and west for inspections, Yi was invariably chosen; clear, cautious, strict, and severe—wherever he went people feared and submitted, and his peers also held him in high regard for this.

entries.zh: 遷主客令，例降侯為伯，轉太中大夫，仍行主客曹事。
entries.en: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy. He became Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the Bureau of Guests.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy; he was transferred to Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the affairs of the Bureau of Guests.

entries.zh: 尋為黃門。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he became Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 後從駕南征，母憂解任。
entries.en: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign, then left office upon his mother's death.
entries.literal: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign and resigned his post upon his mother's death.

entries.zh: 彝居喪過禮，送葬自平城達家，千里徒步，不乘車馬，顏貌毀瘠，當世稱之。
entries.en: Zhang Yi mourned beyond the prescribed rites. To escort the funeral from Pingcheng home—a thousand li—he went entirely on foot, never mounting horse or carriage. His face was wasted and gaunt, and his age praised him.
entries.literal: Yi observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites; to escort the funeral from Pingcheng to his home he walked a thousand li on foot without riding horse or carriage; his appearance was gaunt and wasted—the age praised him for this.

entries.zh: 高祖幸冀州，遣使弔慰，詔以驍騎將軍起之，還復本位。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen visited Ji Province, he sent envoys to offer condolences and ordered Zhang Yi recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry. On his return he resumed his former post.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu visited Ji Province, sent envoys to offer condolences, and ordered him recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry; upon return he resumed his former position.

entries.zh: 以參定遷都之勳，進爵為侯，轉太常少卿，遷散騎常侍，兼侍中，持節巡察陝東、河南十二州，甚有聲稱。
entries.en: For his merit in planning the move of the capital, he was raised to marquis, made Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, then Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan. His reputation soared.
entries.literal: For his merit in participating in deciding the capital relocation, he was advanced to marquis, transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan—his reputation was greatly enhanced.

entries.zh: 使還，以從征之勤，遷尚書。
entries.en: When he returned from his mission, he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works for his service on campaign.
entries.literal: Upon returning from his mission, for his diligence on the campaign he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 坐舉元昭為兼郎中，黜為守尚書。
entries.en: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for recommending Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for having recommended Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 世宗初，除正尚書、兼侍中，尋正侍中。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, and soon afterward full Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant; shortly afterward he became full Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 世宗親政，罷六輔，彝與兼尚書邢巒聞處分非常，出京奔走，為御史中尉甄琛所彈，云「非虎非兕，率彼曠野」，詔書切責之。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule and dismissed the Six Assistants, Zhang Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that extraordinary measures were afoot, fled the capital. Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen impeached them with the line "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sharply rebuked them.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally assumed government and dismissed the Six Assistants, Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that the measures were extraordinary, fled the capital; they were impeached by the Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen, citing "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sternly rebuked them.

entries.zh: 尋除安西將軍、秦州刺史。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 彝務尚典式，考訪故事。
entries.en: Zhang Yi devoted himself to proper forms and searched out precedent.
entries.literal: Yi devoted himself to institutional forms and investigated precedents.

entries.zh: 及臨隴右，彌加討習，於是出入直衞，方伯威儀，赫然可觀。
entries.en: When he took up his post in Longyou, he applied himself all the more to study and drill. Whether entering or leaving, his guard escort and the bearing of a frontier governor were visibly imposing.
entries.literal: When he arrived in Longyou [the west], he applied himself all the more to study and practice; thus whether entering or leaving, his imperial guard escort and the majesty of a regional governor were visibly imposing.

entries.zh: 羌夏畏伏，憚其威整，一方肅靜，號為良牧。
entries.en: The Qiang and Xia submitted in fear of his stern discipline. The region grew quiet, and he was hailed as an excellent governor.
entries.literal: The Qiang and Xia peoples feared and submitted, dreading his stern authority; the region was tranquil and he was hailed as an excellent governor.

entries.zh: 其年冬，太極初就，彝與郭祚等俱以勤舊被徵。
entries.en: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Zhang Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned to court for their long service.
entries.literal: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned for their long service and seniority.

entries.zh: 及還州，進號撫軍將軍，彝表解州任，詔不許。
entries.en: When he returned to his province his title was raised to General Who Pacifies the Army. Zhang Yi memorialized asking to resign the governorship, but the edict refused.
entries.literal: When he returned to his province, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army; Yi submitted a memorial requesting to relinquish his provincial post, but the edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 彝敷政隴右，多所制立，宣布新風，革其舊俗，民庶愛仰之。
entries.en: In Longyou Zhang Yi governed broadly, establishing many new rules, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old custom. The people loved and looked up to him.
entries.literal: Yi spread good governance in Longyou, establishing many new regulations, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old customs; the people loved and admired him.

entries.zh: 為國造佛寺名曰興皇，諸有罪咎者，隨其輕重，謫為土木之功，無復鞭杖之罰。
entries.en: For the state he built a Buddhist temple called Xinghuang. Offenders, according to the weight of their crimes, were assigned to construction labor instead of being flogged.
entries.literal: He built for the state a Buddhist temple named Xinghuang; all who had offenses were, according to severity, relegated to labor on construction works, with no further flogging punishments.

entries.zh: 時陳留公主寡居，彝意願尚主，主亦許之。
entries.en: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was a widow. Zhang Yi wished to marry her, and the princess agreed.
entries.literal: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was widowed; Yi wished to marry her, and the princess also agreed.

entries.zh: 僕射高肇亦望尚主，主意不可。
entries.en: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry her, but the princess would not have it.
entries.literal: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry the princess, but the princess would not agree.

entries.zh: 肇怒，譖彝於世宗，稱彝擅立刑法，勞役百姓。
entries.en: Gao Zhao was furious and slandered Zhang Yi to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he had set up punishments on his own authority and overworked the people.
entries.literal: Gao Zhao was enraged and slandered Yi to Emperor Shizong, claiming Yi had arbitrarily established penal laws and conscripted the people in labor.

entries.zh: 詔遣直後萬貳興馳驛撿察。
entries.en: An edict sent Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.
entries.literal: An edict dispatched the Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.

entries.zh: 貳興，肇所親愛，必欲致彝深罪。
entries.en: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao favored and was bent on bringing Zhang Yi to ruin.
entries.literal: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao cherished and favored; he was determined to bring deep guilt upon Yi.

entries.zh: 彝清身奉法，求其愆過，遂無所得。
entries.en: Zhang Yi had kept himself clean and upheld the law; they searched for fault and found none.
entries.literal: Yi had kept himself pure and upheld the law; they sought his faults and ultimately found nothing.

entries.zh: 見代還洛，猶停廢數年，因得偏風，手脚不便。
entries.en: When his successor arrived he returned to Luoyang, but remained idle for several years. He then suffered a stroke and his hands and feet were impaired.
entries.literal: When his replacement arrived he returned to Luoyang, yet remained idle and dismissed for several years; he thereupon contracted hemiplegia and his hands and feet were impaired.

entries.zh: 然志性不移，善自將攝，稍能朝拜。
entries.en: Yet his spirit did not change. He cared for himself well and gradually was able to attend court again.
entries.literal: Yet his will and character did not change; he was good at caring for himself and gradually was able to attend court.

entries.zh: 久之，除光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
entries.en: After a long while he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.
entries.literal: After a long time, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.

entries.zh: 景尚弟慶禮，字叔，為祚所愛。
entries.en: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was a favorite of Zuo's.
entries.literal: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was beloved by Zuo.

entries.zh: 著作佐郎、通直郎。
entries.en: He served as Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.
entries.literal: [He served as] Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.

entries.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、瀛州刺史。
entries.en: When he died he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: Upon his death, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 彝愛好知己，輕忽下流，非其意者，視之蔑爾。
entries.en: Zhang Yi cherished those he knew and looked down on those beneath him; anyone who did not suit him he treated with contempt.
entries.literal: Yi loved and favored those he knew well and slighted those of lower rank; those who did not suit his liking he regarded with contempt.

entries.zh: 雖疹疾家庭，而志氣彌亮。
entries.en: Though illness kept him at home, his resolve burned all the brighter.
entries.literal: Though afflicted with illness at home, his spirit was all the brighter.

entries.zh: 上表曰：「臣聞元天高朗，尚假列星以助明；
entries.en: He memorialized the throne: "I have heard that though primordial Heaven is high and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to help its light;
entries.literal: In a memorial he said: "Your servant has heard that though the primordial Heaven is lofty and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to aid its brilliance;

entries.zh: 洞庭淵湛，猶藉眾流以增大。
entries.en: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to swell its breadth.
entries.literal: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to enlarge it.

entries.zh: 莫不以孤照不詣其幽，獨深未盡其廣。
entries.en: Neither solitary light reaches every shadow, nor solitary depth fills every expanse.
entries.literal: None can illuminate the hidden with a solitary beam, nor exhaust the breadth with depth alone.

entries.zh: 先聖識其若此，必取物以自誡。
entries.en: The ancient sages, knowing this, always took things around them as warnings to themselves.
entries.literal: The ancient sages, knowing this to be so, invariably took material things as admonitions to themselves.

entries.zh: 故堯稱則天，設謗木以曉未明；
entries.en: Thus Yao, styled Pattern of Heaven, set up a board for criticism to reveal what was still dark;
entries.literal: Thus Yao, styled "the Pattern of Heaven," set up a wooden board for criticism to make known what was unclear;

entries.zh: 舜稱盡善，懸諫鼓以規政闕。
entries.en: Shun, styled Utmost Goodness, hung a drum for remonstrance to mark what was lacking in government.
entries.literal: Shun, styled "Utmost Goodness," hung a remonstrance drum to mark flaws in governance.

entries.zh: 虞人獻箴規之旨，盤盂著舉動之銘，庶幾見善而思齊，聞惡以自改。
entries.en: Forest keepers offered words of admonition; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that seeing good one would strive to match it, and hearing evil one would turn and reform.
entries.literal: Forest keepers offered the purpose of admonition and regulation; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that upon seeing good one might aspire to emulate it, and upon hearing evil one might reform oneself.

entries.zh: 眷眷於悔往之衢，孜孜於不逮之路，用能聲高百王，卓絕中古，經十氏而不渝，歷二千以孤鬱。
entries.en: Attentive on the road of repenting the past, tireless on the path of what they had not yet reached—they raised their fame above the hundred kings, stood alone through the middle ages, endured through ten houses without wavering, and shone across two thousand years.
entries.literal: Attentive on the path of repenting past errors, diligent on the road of what one has not yet attained—thus their fame towered above the hundred kings, transcendent through the middle antiquity, enduring through ten dynasties without change, spanning two thousand years in solitary eminence.

entries.zh: 伏惟太祖撥亂，弈代重光。
entries.en: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor quelled the chaos, and dynasty after dynasty renewed the imperial light.
entries.literal: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor [Emperor Taiwu] quelled the chaos, and generation after generation renewed the imperial splendor.

entries.zh: 世祖以不世之才，開盪函夏；
entries.en: Emperor Shizu, possessing extraordinary talent, expanded rule over the Central Plains.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu, with matchless talent, opened and swept across the Central Plains.

entries.zh: 顯祖以溫明之德，潤沃九區。
entries.en: Emperor Xianzu, with his gentle and luminous virtue, nourished all the realm.
entries.literal: Emperor Xianzu, with warm and bright virtue, moistened and enriched the nine regions.

entries.zh: [2]高祖大聖臨朝，經營云始，未明求衣，日昃忘食，開翦荊棘，徙御神縣，更新風軌，冠帶朝流。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu the great sage came to the throne and began his labors from the very start—rising before dawn and forgetting meals at dusk—cutting away brambles, moving the capital to the sacred heartland, renewing laws and customs, and drawing the civilized world to court.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu the great sage attended court, beginning his efforts at the start; rising before daylight and forgetting to eat at sunset, he cleared thorns and brambles, moved the capital to the sacred heartland, renewed customs and institutions, and drew the girdled and capped to court.

entries.zh: 海東雜種之渠，衡南異服之帥，沙西氊頭之戎，漠北辮髮之虜，重譯納貢，請吏稱藩。
entries.en: Tribal leaders from the eastern seas, southern chiefs in exotic dress, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired peoples north of the desert—all sent tribute through successive interpreters and requested imperial administrators, styling themselves as vassals.
entries.literal: Chiefs of mixed tribes east of the sea, chieftains in strange dress south of Heng, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired enemies north of the desert—all came through multiple translations to offer tribute and requested officials, styling themselves as vassals.

entries.zh: 積德懋於夏殷，富仁盛於周漢，澤教既周，武功亦匝。
entries.en: Their accumulated virtue surpassed that of the Xia and Shang, their benevolence exceeded that of the Zhou and Han; civilizing influence was complete, and military achievements likewise comprehensive.
entries.literal: Accumulated virtue surpassing Xia and Yin, abundant benevolence exceeding Zhou and Han—benevolent instruction was complete, and martial achievements likewise comprehensive.

entries.zh: 猶且發明詔，思求直士，信是蒼生薦言之秋，祝史陳辭之日。
entries.en: They even issued enlightened decrees seeking upright officials—it was truly the season when the people might offer counsel and when the ritual officials might speak their minds.
entries.literal: Moreover they issued bright edicts seeking upright men—it was truly the season for the common people to offer advice and for the prayer-officers to present their words.

entries.zh: 況臣家自奉國八十餘年，紆金鏘玉，及臣四世。
entries.en: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, honored with gold seals and jade insignia, spanning four generations down to me.
entries.literal: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, adorned with gold seals and jade insignia, extending to four generations including myself.

entries.zh: 過以小才，藉蔭出仕，學慚專門，武闕方略，早荷先帝眷仗之恩，末蒙陛下不遺之施。
entries.en: I came to office beyond my modest abilities through inherited privilege; I lacked specialized learning and military strategy. I was early favored by the late emperor and later found favor with Your Majesty despite my unworthiness.
entries.literal: I overstepped with my small talent, entered office through inherited favor; ashamed in learning for lacking specialization and in warfare for lacking strategy—I early received the previous emperor's trusting favor and finally Your Majesty's gracious consideration without abandonment.

entries.zh: [3]侍則出入兩都，[4]官歷納言常伯，忝牧秦藩，號兼安撫。
entries.en: I attended at court, moving between the two capitals; I served as Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.
entries.literal: Attending at court I moved between the two capitals; my offices included Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and I shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.

entries.zh: 實思碎首膏原，仰酬二朝之惠；
entries.en: I truly wished to give my life to repay the kindness of two emperors.
entries.literal: Truly I wished to smash my head and smear my blood on the plain, looking up to repay the grace of two reigns.

entries.zh: 輕塵碎石，遠增嵩岱之高。
entries.en: Though insignificant as dust or pebbles, I hoped from afar to add to the stature of Mount Song and Mount Tai.
entries.literal: Light as dust and broken stone, I hoped from afar to increase the height of Mount Song and Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 輒私訪舊書，竊觀圖史，其帝皇興起之元，配天隆家之業，修造益民之奇，龍麟雲鳳之瑞，卑宮愛物之仁，釋網改祝之澤，前歌後舞之應，囹圄寂寥之美，可為輝風景行者，輒謹編丹青，以標睿範。
entries.en: I privately consulted ancient texts and historical records, and for accounts of emperors' founding achievements, dynastic glory endorsed by Heaven, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious omens of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, humane governance through frugal palaces and care for creatures, merciful policies of sparing the net and reforming sacrifices, popular rejoicing, and the virtue of empty prisons—all that could inspire and instruct—I carefully compiled them in illustrated form to mark the wise standard.
entries.literal: I then privately consulted old books and secretly viewed illustrated histories; of emperors' rise to power, enterprises matching Heaven and elevating families, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious signs of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, the benevolence of humble palaces and love of creatures, the grace of releasing nets and changing prayers, the response of singing before and dancing behind, and the beauty of empty prisons—all that could illuminate and inspire—I carefully compiled in paintings to mark the wise standard.

entries.zh: 至如太康好田，遇窮后迫禍；
entries.en: Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.
entries.literal: King Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.

entries.zh: 武乙逸禽，罹震雷暴酷；
entries.en: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and was struck down by thunder in violent punishment.
entries.literal: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and suffered violent thunder in punishment.

entries.zh: 夏桀淫亂，南巢有非命之誅；
entries.en: Xia Jie was debauched and tyrannical; at Nanqiao he met an untimely death.
entries.literal: Xia Jie was licentious and disorderly; at Nanqiao there was execution not by fate.

entries.zh: 殷紂昏酣，牧野有倒戈之陳；
entries.en: King Zhou of Yin was dissolute and drunk; at Muye his troops turned their weapons against him.
entries.literal: King Zhou of Yin was muddled and drunken; at Muye there was the array of turned spears.

entries.zh: 周厲逐獸，滅不旋踵；
entries.en: King Li of Zhou obsessed over hunting; his ruin followed almost immediately.
entries.literal: King Li of Zhou chased beasts; destruction came without turning the heel.

entries.zh: 幽王遇惑，死亦相尋；
entries.en: King You was beguiled into error; death soon followed in turn.
entries.literal: King You met deception; death followed in succession.

entries.zh: 暨於漢成失御，亡新篡奪；
entries.en: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.
entries.literal: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.

entries.zh: 桓靈不綱，魏武遷鼎；
entries.en: Emperors Huan and Ling neglected governance; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.
entries.literal: Emperors Huan and Ling lacked discipline; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.

entries.zh: 晉惠闇弱，骨肉相屠，終使聰曜鴞視并州，勒虎狼據燕趙：如此之輩，罔不畢載。
entries.en: Emperor Hui of Jin was weak and muddled; his kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to covet Bingzhou like owls and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such cases are fully recorded.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin was dim and weak; kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to owl-watch Bingzhou and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such types are without exception fully recorded.

entries.zh: 起元庖犧，終於晉末，凡十六代，百二十八帝，歷三千二百七年，雜事五百八十九，合成五卷，名曰歷帝圖，亦謗木、諫鼓、虞人、盤盂之類。
entries.en: From Fuxi at the beginning to the end of Jin—sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, 3,207 years, and 589 miscellaneous records—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to the remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.
entries.literal: Beginning from Fuxi at the origin and ending at the end of Jin—in all sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, spanning 3,207 years, with 589 miscellaneous matters—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.

entries.zh: 脫蒙置御坐之側，時復披覽，冀或起予左右，上補未萌。
entries.en: If it might be placed beside Your Majesty's seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.
entries.literal: If I am fortunate enough to have it placed beside the imperial seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.

entries.zh: 伏願陛下遠惟宗廟之憂，近存黎民之念，取其賢君，棄其惡主，則微臣雖沉淪地下，無異乘雲登天矣。」
entries.en: I humbly pray Your Majesty will heed distant concerns for the ancestral temple and keep near in mind the welfare of the people, taking the worthy rulers as models and rejecting the wicked—then though I lie buried underground, it would be as if I ascended to heaven on clouds."
entries.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty would far consider the ancestors' concerns and near preserve thoughts of the people, taking the worthy rulers and discarding the evil ones—then though I sink underground, it would be no different from riding clouds to ascend heaven."

entries.zh: 世宗善之。
entries.en: Emperor Xuanwu approved it.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong approved it.

entries.zh: 彝又表曰：「竊惟皇王統天，必以窮幽為美；
entries.en: Zhang Yi submitted another memorial: "I believe that emperors who align with Heaven must regard penetrating the hidden as a virtue;
entries.literal: Zhang Yi again memorialized: "I reflect that emperors and kings who harmonize with Heaven must take penetrating the obscure as excellence;

entries.zh: 盡理作聖，亦假廣採成明。
entries.en: To perfect understanding and become sage likewise depends on broad collection to achieve enlightenment.
entries.literal: To exhaust principle and become sage likewise borrows broad collection to achieve clarity.

entries.zh: 故詢於芻蕘，著之周什，輿人獻箴，流於夏典。
entries.en: Hence inquiry was made even of grass cutters and recorded in the Zhou odes, and chariot makers offered admonitions preserved in the Xia canon.
entries.literal: Therefore inquiry was made of grass cutters, recorded in the Odes of Zhou; chariot makers presented admonitions, flowing into the canon of Xia.

entries.zh: 不然，則美刺無以得彰，善惡有時不達。
entries.en: Otherwise praise and blame could never be made clear, and good and evil would sometimes never reach the ruler.
entries.literal: Otherwise, praise and censure could not be made manifest, and good and evil would at times fail to reach [the throne].

entries.zh: 逮於兩漢、魏、晉，雖道有隆汚，而被繡傳檄，未始闕也。
entries.en: Down through the Two Han, Wei, and Jin, though governance rose and fell, officials in court dress presenting memorials never ceased.
entries.literal: Reaching the Two Han, Wei, and Jin—though the Way had ascent and defilement—embroidered robes conveying memorials never once were lacking.

entries.zh: 及惠帝失御，中夏崩離，劉苻專據秦西，燕趙獨制關左，姚夏繼起，五涼競立，致使九服搖搖，民無定主，禮儀典制，此焉堙滅。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui lost the throne, the heartland fragmented; Liu and Fu held western Qin, Yan and Zhao controlled the eastern passes, Later Yan and the Five Liang rose in turn—the nine provinces trembled, the people had no settled ruler, and ritual and institutions perished.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui lost control, the Central Plains collapsed and split apart; Liu and Fu monopolized western Qin, Yan and Zhao alone controlled the passes to the left, Yao of Xia rose in succession, and the Five Liang competed to establish themselves—causing the nine domains to sway unsteadily, the people without a fixed lord, and ritual codes and institutions to be buried and extinguished here.

entries.zh: 暨大魏應歷，撥亂登皇，翦彼鯨鯢，龕靖神縣，數紀之間，天下寧一，傳輝七帝，積聖如神。
entries.en: When Northern Wei received the mandate, quelled chaos, and took the throne, it cut down its foes and restored order to the realm; within a few reigns the empire was unified, seven emperors passed down its glory, and sagacity accumulated like that of a spirit.
entries.literal: When Great Wei received the mandate, quelling chaos and ascending the throne, cutting down those whale-demons and peacefully settling the divine counties, within a few reigns the realm was united under one rule, transmitting glory through seven emperors, accumulated sagacity like a spirit.

entries.zh: 高祖遷鼎成周，永茲八百，偃武修文，憲章斯改，實所謂加五帝、登三王，民無德而名焉。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, continuing the Zhou legacy of eight hundred years, sheathed the sword and fostered letters, and reformed law and institutions—truly surpassing the Five Emperors and equaling the Three Kings, a fame the people need not ascribe to virtue alone.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu moved the tripod to Cheng and Zhou, continuing those eight hundred years, laying down arms and cultivating culture, statutes and patterns thereby reformed—truly what is called surpassing the Five Emperors and ascending the Three Kings, the people without virtue yet naming it.

entries.zh: 猶且慮獨見之不明，欲廣訪於得失，乃命四使，觀察風謠。
entries.en: Yet he still feared that his own judgment alone might be unclear and wished to seek widely for what was right and wrong; he therefore appointed four envoys to observe folk songs and local opinion.
entries.literal: Yet he still worried that solitary insight was not clear, and wished broadly to inquire into gains and losses; therefore he ordered four envoys to observe popular songs and rumors.

entries.zh: 臣時忝常伯，充一使之列，遂得仗節揮金，宣恩東夏，周歷於齊魯之間，遍馳於梁宋之域，詢採詩頌，研撿獄情，實庶片言之不遺，美刺之俱顯。
entries.en: I then served as Regular Grandee and was one of the four envoys; bearing the imperial staff I proclaimed grace in the east, traveled through Qi and Lu and across Liang and Song, gathered folk songs, and examined legal cases—hoping that no voice would be lost and that praise and blame alike would come to light.
entries.literal: Your subject at the time held the post of Regular Grandee and filled one place among the envoys; thus I was able to bear the staff and wield gold, proclaiming grace in eastern Xia, touring between Qi and Lu, ranging widely through the lands of Liang and Song, inquiring into and collecting odes and hymns, examining and sorting prison cases—truly hoping that not a single word would be lost and that praise and censure alike would be displayed.

entries.zh: 而才輕任重，多不遂心。
entries.en: But my abilities were slight and my responsibilities heavy, and much did not go as I had hoped.
entries.literal: Yet my talent was light and my burden heavy; much did not accord with my wishes.

entries.zh: 所採之詩，並始申目，而值鑾輿南討，問罪宛鄧，臣復忝行軍，樞機是務。
entries.en: The poems collected had only just been entered on the register when the emperor marched south to punish Wan and Deng; I was again attached to the campaign staff, occupied with military affairs.
entries.literal: The odes collected had only just begun to be catalogued when the imperial carriage went south on campaign to question guilt at Wan and Deng; your subject again held a post on the campaign staff, with military keys as the task.

entries.zh: 及輦駕之返，膳御未和，續以大諱奄臻，四海崩慕，遂爾推遷，不及聞徹。
entries.en: When the emperor returned, the court was still in disarray; then came the sudden death of the emperor and universal mourning, and in the upheaval I never completed the submission.
entries.literal: When the carriage returned, the imperial meals were not yet settled; continuing with the great bereavement suddenly arriving, the four seas collapsed in mourning; thus there was deferral and transfer, and I did not reach full report.

entries.zh: 未幾，改牧秦蕃，違離闕下，繼以譴疾相纏，寧丁八歲。
entries.en: Soon I was transferred to govern the Qin region, far from court; then reproof and illness followed one upon another, and I spent eight years in mourning for my father.
entries.literal: Before long I was reassigned to govern the Qin frontier, parted from below the palace gates; continuing with reproof and illness entwined, I mourned for my father for eight years.

entries.zh: 常恐所採之詩永淪丘壑，是臣夙夜所懷，以為深憂者也。
entries.en: I constantly feared the poems I had gathered would be lost forever in obscurity—this has been my deepest worry night and day.
entries.literal: I constantly feared the odes collected would forever sink into ravines and mounds—this is what your subject has harbored day and night, taking it as a deep worry.

entries.zh: 陛下垂日月之明，行雲雨之施，察臣往罪之濫，矜臣貧病之切，既蒙崇以祿養，復得拜掃丘墳，明目友朋，無所負愧。
entries.en: Your Majesty shines like sun and moon and showers grace like rain, overlooking my past excesses and pitying my poverty and illness; honored with stipends for my support and allowed again to tend my family's graves, I can face my friends without shame.
entries.literal: Your Majesty sheds the brightness of sun and moon and exercises the bestowal of clouds and rain, examining the excess of your subject's past faults and pitying the urgency of my poverty and illness; having been honored with stipends for support, I was again able to sweep my ancestors' tombs—clear-eyed before friends, with nothing to bear as shame.

entries.zh: 且臣一二年來，所患不劇，尋省本書，粗有髣髴。
entries.en: Moreover, over the past year or two my illness has not been grave, and reviewing the original compilation I have recovered a rough draft.
entries.literal: Moreover, for the past year or two my illness has not been severe; searching through the original book, there is a rough outline.

entries.zh: 凡有七卷，今寫上呈，伏願昭覽，敕付有司，使魏代所採之詩，不堙於丘井，臣之願也。」
entries.en: There are seven volumes in all, which I now submit; I humbly pray Your Majesty will review them and order the proper offices to preserve the poems gathered in the Wei period from being lost to oblivion—this is my sole wish."
entries.literal: In all there are seven volumes; I now copy and present them above, humbly wishing Your Majesty would illuminate and view them and command the relevant offices, so that the odes collected in the Wei age may not be buried in wells and ravines—this is your subject's wish."

entries.zh: 第二子仲瑀上封事，求銓別選格，排抑武人，不使預在清品。
entries.en: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial calling for revised selection standards that would exclude military men from the pure grades.
entries.literal: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial seeking to examine and separate selection standards, suppressing military men and not allowing them to enter the pure grades.

entries.zh: 由是眾口喧喧，謗讟盈路，立榜大巷，剋期會集，屠害其家。
entries.en: Because of this public outcry and slander filled the streets; placards were posted in the main thoroughfares fixing a date for assembly to attack his household.
entries.literal: Because of this the multitude clamored, slander and abuse filled the roads; they posted placards in the great alleys, fixing a date to assemble, slaughtering and harming his household.

entries.zh: 彝殊無畏避之意，父子安然。
entries.en: Zhang Yi showed no fear or evasion; father and sons remained at ease.
entries.literal: Yi showed absolutely no fear or avoidance; father and sons remained at ease.

entries.zh: 神龜二年二月，羽林虎賁幾將千人，相率至尚書省詬罵，求其長子尚書郎始均，不獲，以瓦石擊打公門。
entries.en: In the second month of the second Shengui year, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard soldiers went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and abuse the family, seeking his eldest son Shijun, a Secretariat Gentleman; failing to find him, they pelted the ministry gates with tiles and stones.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shengui, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard troops went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and curse, seeking his eldest son, Secretariat Gentleman Shijun; not obtaining him, they struck the public gates with tiles and stones.

entries.zh: 上下畏懼，莫敢討抑。
entries.en: Officials high and low were terrified; none dared restrain them.
entries.literal: High and low were fearful; none dared suppress or restrain them.

entries.zh: 遂便持火，虜掠道中薪蒿，以杖石為兵器，直造其第，曳彝堂下，捶辱極意，唱呼嗸嗸，焚其屋宇。
entries.en: They then seized fire, looted fuel along the road, took up staffs and stones as weapons, marched straight to his residence, dragged Zhang Yi into the courtyard, beat and humiliated him without restraint, shouting wildly as they burned his houses.
entries.literal: They then took fire, plundering firewood and reeds along the road, using staffs and stones as weapons, going straight to his residence, dragging Yi beneath the hall, beating and humiliating him to the utmost, shouting and howling, burning his houses.

entries.zh: 始均、仲瑀當時踰北垣而走。
entries.en: Shijun and Zhongyu at once leaped the north wall and fled.
entries.literal: Shijun and Zhongyu at the time leaped over the north wall and fled.

entries.zh: 始均回救其父，拜伏羣小，以請父命。
entries.en: Shijun turned back to save his father, prostrating himself before the mob to beg for his life.
entries.literal: Shijun turned back to rescue his father, bowing prostrate before the mob to beg for his father's life.

entries.zh: 羽林等就加毆擊，生投之於烟火之中。
entries.en: The guards then beat him further and cast him alive into the fire and smoke.
entries.literal: The Feathered Guard and others then added beating and strikes, casting him alive into the flames and smoke.

entries.zh: 及得尸骸，不復可識，唯以髻中小釵為驗。
entries.en: When his body was recovered it could no longer be identified; only a small hairpin in the topknot served to identify him.
entries.literal: When the corpse was obtained it could no longer be recognized; only a small hairpin in the topknot served as identification.

entries.zh: 仲瑀傷重走免。
entries.en: Zhongyu, badly wounded, escaped.
entries.literal: Zhongyu, severely wounded, fled and escaped.

entries.zh: 彝僅有餘命，沙門寺與其比隣，輿致於寺。
entries.en: Zhang Yi clung to life; a Buddhist monastery stood next door, and they carried him there on a litter.
entries.literal: Yi had only a remnant of life; the Buddhist monastery neighbored him, and they carried him by litter to the monastery.

entries.zh: 遠近聞見，莫不惋駭。
entries.en: All who heard and saw it, near and far, were struck with grief and horror.
entries.literal: Those near and far who heard and saw were all struck with grief and horror.

entries.zh: 肅宗初，侍中崔光表曰：「彝及李韶，朝列之中唯此二人出身官次本在臣右，器能幹世，又並為多，近來參差，便成替後。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Zhang Yi and Li Shao are the only two men in court whose family standing and seniority originally ranked above mine, yet both are gifted administrators; recently, through uneven treatment, they have been passed over.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Yi and Li Shao—in the court ranks only these two men's origins and official seniority were originally above your subject's, yet in capacity and ability to govern the age they both excel; recently through uneven treatment they have been pushed to the rear.

entries.zh: 計其階途，雖應遷陟，然恐班秩猶未賜等。
entries.en: By the stages of their careers they ought to be promoted, yet I fear their ranks have still not been granted fairly.
entries.literal: Calculating their stages of advancement, though they ought to be promoted and elevated, I fear their ranks and grades have still not been granted in equal measure.

entries.zh: 昔衞之公叔，引下同舉；
entries.en: In antiquity Wei's Gongsun drew up his subordinates to advance together;
entries.literal: In former days the Gongsun of Wei drew up those below to advance together;

entries.zh: 晉之士丐，推長伯游。
entries.en: and Jin's Shigai promoted the senior Boyou.
entries.literal: Jin's Shigai pushed forward the elder Boyou.

entries.zh: 古人所高，當時見許。
entries.en: What the ancients honored was praised and approved in their own day.
entries.literal: What the ancients esteemed was praised and approved in their own time.

entries.zh: 敢緣斯義，乞降臣位一階，授彼汎級，齊行聖庭，帖穆選敍。」
entries.en: I venture to follow this principle and beg to lower my own rank by one step, granting them an equal grade so we may stand together at court in fair and harmonious order."
entries.literal: I dare follow this principle and beg to lower my rank by one step, granting them a general grade, walking together in the sage court, harmoniously aligned in selection and ordering."

entries.zh: 詔加征西將軍、冀州大中正。
entries.en: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 雖年向六十，加之風疾，而自強人事，孜孜無怠。
