entries.en: Though nearing sixty and afflicted with wind disorder, he still drove himself in public affairs, diligent and never slackening.
entries.literal: Though he was nearing sixty and moreover afflicted with wind illness, he still forced himself in human affairs, diligent and never slackening.

entries.zh: 公私法集，衣冠從事；
entries.en: He compiled public and private law codes and gathered officials and gentry to assist;
entries.literal: Public and private legal compilations, officials and gentry attending;

entries.zh: 延請道俗，修營齋講；
entries.en: invited Daoists and lay believers and organized fasts and lectures;
entries.literal: inviting Daoists and lay believers, repairing and conducting fasts and lectures;

entries.zh: 好善欽賢，愛獎人物。
entries.en: loved the worthy, cherished talent, and rewarded men of ability.
entries.literal: loving the good and respecting the worthy, cherishing and rewarding men of talent.

entries.zh: 南北新舊莫不多之。
entries.en: Men old and new, from north and south, all flocked to him.
entries.literal: Whether from north or south, old or new, none failed to flock to him.

entries.zh: 大起第宅，微號華侈，頗侮其疏宗舊戚，不甚存紀，時有怨憾焉。
entries.en: He built grand mansions in a somewhat lavish style, showed little regard for distant clansmen and old kin, and at times stirred resentment.
entries.literal: He greatly raised mansions and residences, slightly styled as splendid and extravagant, quite slighting his distant clansmen and old kin, not greatly preserving records of them; at times there were resentments.

entries.zh: 榮宦之間，未能止足，屢表在秦州預有開援漢中之勳，希加賞報，積年不已，朝廷患之。
entries.en: In his pursuit of rank he could not know when to stop; he repeatedly claimed credit for aiding the campaign to recover Hanzhong while governing Qinzhou and pressed for further rewards year after year until the court grew weary of it.
entries.literal: Between glory and office he could not stop at sufficiency; repeatedly he memorialized that at Qinzhou he had beforehand rendered service in opening relief for Hanzhong, hoping for added reward and recompense, year after year without end—the court was troubled by it.

entries.zh: 彝臨終，口占左右上啟曰：「臣自奉國及孫六世，尸祿素餐，負恩唯靦，徒思竭智盡誠，終然靡効。
entries.en: On his deathbed Zhang Yi dictated a final memorial: "My family has served the state for six generations, receiving salary without merit and grace I have only shamed; I thought only to exhaust my loyalty, yet in the end achieved nothing.
entries.literal: At the end of his life Yi dictated to those beside him a memorial above: "Your subject from serving the state through six generations has received salary without merit, bearing grace with only shame, merely thinking to exhaust wisdom and loyalty, yet in the end without effect.

entries.zh: 臣第二息仲瑀所上之事，益治實多，既曰有益，寧容默爾。
entries.en: The proposal my second son Zhongyu submitted would in truth benefit governance greatly; if it is beneficial, how could I keep silent?
entries.literal: The matter submitted by your subject's second son Zhongyu in governing truly has much benefit; since it is said to be beneficial, how could it be silently tolerated?

entries.zh: 通呈有日，未簡神聽，豈圖眾忿，乃至於此。
entries.en: It had been submitted for days without yet reaching the emperor's ear; who could have imagined public fury would come to this?
entries.literal: It had been presented for days without yet being sifted by the divine hearing; who would have thought popular wrath would reach this point?

entries.zh: 臣不能禍防未萌，慮絕殃兆，致令軍眾橫囂，攻焚臣宅。
entries.en: I could not forestall disaster before it sprouted or cut off the signs of calamity, and so soldiers rioted, attacked, and burned my house.
entries.literal: Your subject could not ward off disaster before it sprouted, consider and cut off the omen of calamity, causing military masses to rampage and shout, attacking and burning your subject's residence.

entries.zh: 息始均、仲瑀等叩請流血，乞代臣死，始均即陷塗炭，仲瑀經宿方蘇。
entries.en: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu begged with blood flowing to die in my place; Shijun at once perished in the flames, and Zhongyu revived only after a night.
entries.literal: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu knocked their heads and begged with flowing blood to die in my place; Shijun at once fell into ashes and charcoal, Zhongyu after a night barely revived.

entries.zh: 臣年已六十，宿被榮遇，垂暮之秋，忽見此苦，顧瞻災酷，古今無比。
entries.en: I am already sixty, long favored by the throne; in the autumn of my life I suddenly meet this agony—a cruelty without parallel in past or present.
entries.literal: Your subject is already sixty years old, long receiving honored favor; in the autumn of life's decline I suddenly see this suffering; looking back on the cruel disaster, there is no parallel in past or present.

entries.zh: 臣傷至重，殘氣假延，望景顧時，推漏就盡，頃刻待終，臣之命也，知復何言。
entries.en: My wounds are grave; on borrowed breath I watch the shadow and count the hours, the water clock nearing its end, death imminent—this is my fate, and what more can I say?
entries.literal: Your subject's wounds are extremely grave; with remnant breath borrowed for extension, looking at the shadow and counting the time, pushing the clepsydra toward its end, awaiting the final moment in an instant—your subject's fate; knowing again what to say.

entries.zh: 若所上之書，少為益國，臣便是生以理全，死與義合，不負二帝於地下，臣無餘恨矣。
entries.en: If what we submitted can even slightly benefit the state, then I have lived with integrity and die in righteousness, not failing the two emperors in the grave—I have no further regret.
entries.literal: If the book submitted can slightly benefit the state, your subject would then be living with principle intact and dying united with righteousness, not failing the two emperors underground—your subject has no remaining regret.

entries.zh: 一歸泉壤，長離紫庭，戀仰天顏，誠痛無已。
entries.en: Once I return to the grave, forever parted from the imperial court, I shall still cherish Your Majesty's countenance—my grief will know no end.
entries.literal: Once returning to the springs and mounds, long parted from the purple court, cherishing and looking up at the heavenly countenance, truly pain without end.

entries.zh: 不勝眷眷，力喘奉辭，伏願二聖加御珍膳，覆露黔首，壽保南嶽，德與日昇。
entries.en: Overcome with devotion, gasping out these words I take leave; I humbly pray the two sovereigns will guard their precious health, shelter the common people, long preserve life as the southern mountains, and let virtue rise with the sun.
entries.literal: Unable to bear the deep attachment, with strength gasping I offer this farewell; humbly wishing the two sages would add to their precious meals, cover and shelter the black-haired people, preserve life like the southern mountains, virtue rising with the sun.

entries.zh: 臣夙被芻豢，先後銜恩，欲報之期，昊天罔極，亡魂有知，不忘結草。」
entries.en: I have long been fed by the state's bounty and repeatedly received grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if my departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget to repay with knotted grass."
entries.literal: Your subject long received fodder and grain, successively bearing grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if the departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget the knotted grass."

entries.zh: 彝遂卒，時年五十九。
entries.en: Zhang Yi then died at the age of fifty-nine.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then died, aged fifty-nine at the time.

entries.zh: 官為收掩羽林凶強者八人斬之，不能窮誅羣豎，即為大赦以安眾心，有識者知國紀之將墜矣。
entries.en: The authorities buried Zhang Yi and beheaded eight of the ringleaders among the guards but could not punish the whole mob; a general amnesty was then issued to calm the people—those with insight knew the dynasty's discipline was collapsing.
entries.literal: The government for collecting and burying beheaded eight of the violent among the Feathered Guard but could not exhaustively punish the whole mob; thereupon a great amnesty was issued to settle popular hearts—those with insight knew the nation's discipline was about to fall.

entries.zh: 喪還所焚宅，與始均東西分斂於小屋。
entries.en: The funeral procession returned to the burned house; Zhang Yi and Shijun were laid out separately in a small room east and west.
entries.literal: The funeral returned to the burned residence; east and west with Shijun they were separately enshrouded in a small room.

entries.zh: 仲瑀遂以創重避居滎陽，至五月，創得漸瘳，始奔父喪，詔賜布帛千匹。
entries.en: Zhongyu, severely wounded, took refuge at Xingyang; by the fifth month his wounds had healed enough for him to attend his father's funeral, and an edict granted him a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
entries.literal: Zhongyu then because of severe wounds avoided residence at Xingyang; by the fifth month the wounds gradually healed and he first rushed to his father's funeral; an edict bestowed a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.

entries.zh: 靈太后以其累朝大臣，特垂矜惻，數月猶追言泣下，謂諸侍臣曰：「吾為張彝飲食不御，乃至首髮微有虧落。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling, because he had served many reigns, showed special compassion; for months she still spoke of him in tears, telling the attendant ministers: "For Zhang Yi I have refused my meals, even until the hair on my head has begun to thin.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he was a minister of many reigns, especially showed pity; for months she still spoke of it with tears, saying to the attendant ministers: "Because of Zhang Yi I have not taken my meals, even to the point that the hair on my head has slightly fallen out.

entries.zh: 悲痛之苦，以至於此。」
entries.en: My grief has gone as far as this."
entries.literal: The pain of grief has reached this point."

entries.zh: 初，彝曾祖幸，所招引河東民為州裁千餘家，後相依合，至於罷入冀州，積三十年，析別有數萬戶，故高祖比校天下民戶，最為大州。
entries.en: Earlier, Zhang Yi's great-grandfather Xing had settled more than a thousand households from Hedong in the province; over thirty years they grew through division and merger to tens of thousands of households—so when Emperor Gaozu compared household registers throughout the realm, Ji ranked as the largest province.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yi's great-grandfather Xing had attracted and settled over a thousand households of Hedong people as provincial settlers; later they joined together, until dismissal and entry into Ji Province, accumulating thirty years; through division and separation there were tens of thousands of households—therefore Emperor Gaozu compared and checked the realm's household registers and [Ji] was the greatest province.

entries.zh: 彝為黃門，每侍坐以為言，高祖謂之曰：「終當以卿為刺史，酬先世誠效。」
entries.en: When Zhang Yi served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate, he raised the matter whenever he attended the emperor, who told him: "In the end I shall make you inspector to reward your ancestors' loyal service."
entries.literal: When Yi was Attendant of the Yellow Gate, each time he sat in attendance he spoke of this; Emperor Gaozu said to him: "In the end I shall take you as inspector to reward your forebears' sincere service."

entries.zh: 彝追高祖往旨，累乞本州，朝議未許。
entries.en: Zhang Yi pressed the emperor's earlier promise and repeatedly begged for his home province, but court deliberation did not approve.
entries.literal: Yi pursued Emperor Gaozu's former intent and repeatedly begged for his native province; court deliberation did not permit it.

entries.zh: 彝亡後，靈太后云：「彝屢乞冀州，吾欲用之，有人違我此意。
entries.en: After Zhang Yi's death, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Zhang Yi repeatedly asked for Ji Province; I meant to grant it—someone opposed my wish.
entries.literal: After Yi died, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Yi repeatedly begged for Ji Province; I wished to use him—someone went against my intent in this.

entries.zh: 若從其請，或不至是，悔之無及。」
entries.en: Had I granted his request, perhaps things would not have come to this—my regret is boundless."
entries.literal: If I had followed his request, perhaps it would not have come to this; regret is without limit."

entries.zh: 乃贈使持節、衞將軍、冀州刺史，諡文侯。
entries.en: He was then posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

entries.zh: 始均，字子衡，端潔好學，有文才。
entries.en: Shijun, whose courtesy name was Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary gifts.
entries.literal: Shijun, courtesy name Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary talent.

entries.zh: 司徒行參軍，遷著作佐郎。
entries.en: He served as staff officer to the Grand Commandant and was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant, promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 世宗以彝先朝勤舊，不幸疹廢，特除始均長兼左民郎中。
entries.en: Emperor Xuanwu, because Zhang Yi was a meritorious minister of the previous reign who had met a tragic end, specially appointed Shijun as long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Yi was an old meritorious minister of the former court who had met misfortune and ruin, specially appointed Shijun long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.

entries.zh: 遷員外常侍，仍領郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant while retaining his gentleman post.
entries.literal: Promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant, still holding the gentleman post.

entries.zh: 始均才幹，有美於父，改陳壽魏志為編年之體，廣益異聞，為三十卷。
entries.en: Shijun's ability surpassed his father's; he reworked Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, adding much additional material, in thirty volumes.
entries.literal: Shijun's talent and ability had beauty surpassing his father; he revised Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, broadly adding divergent hearsay, making thirty volumes.

entries.zh: 又著冠帶錄及諸賦數十篇，今並亡失。
entries.en: He also wrote Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.
entries.literal: He also composed Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.

entries.zh: 初，大乘賊起於冀瀛之間，遣都督元遙討平之，多所殺戮，積尸數萬。
entries.en: Earlier, Mahayana rebels rose in the Ji and Ying region; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress them, killing many until corpses numbered in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Initially Mahayana rebels arose between Ji and Ying; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress and pacify them, killing many until corpses piled up to tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 始均以郎中為行臺，忿軍士重以首級為功，乃令檢集人首數千，一時焚爇，至於灰燼，用息僥倖，見者莫不傷心。
entries.en: As a director on the campaign staff, Shijun was angered that soldiers prized enemy heads for merit; he had thousands of heads gathered and burned to ash at once to curb opportunism, and all who saw it were heartsick.
entries.literal: Shijun served as Gentleman on the mobile secretariat; angered that the soldiers prized enemy heads for merit, he ordered thousands of human heads collected and burned at once to ashes, to quell opportunism—all who witnessed it were grieved.

entries.zh: 及始均之死也，始末在於烟炭之間，有燋爛之痛，論者或亦推咎焉。
entries.en: When Shijun died, he had been caught from start to finish in smoke and fire, burned alive—some commentators blamed his earlier act for it.
entries.literal: When Shijun died, from beginning to end he was amid smoke and embers, suffering the pain of scorching—commentators sometimes placed blame on this as well.

entries.zh: 贈樂陵太守，諡曰孝。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：郭祚才幹敏實，有世務之長，高祖經綸之始，獨在勤勞之地，居官任事，動靜稱述。
entries.en: The historian writes: Guo Zuo was talented, practical, and quick, skilled in affairs of state; at the outset of Emperor Wen's great enterprise he alone bore the heaviest burdens, and in every office his conduct won praise.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Guo Zuo was talented, capable, and diligent in substance, with strengths in worldly affairs; at the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's grand planning he alone stood in the realm of strenuous labor—in office and charged with duties, his conduct in motion and rest was praised.

entries.zh: 張彝風力謇謇，有王臣之氣，銜命擁旄，風聲猶在。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the air of a true minister of the throne; entrusted with command and banner, his reputation endures still.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the bearing of a king's minister; bearing credentials and waving banners, his renown still stands.

entries.zh: 並魏氏器能之臣乎？
entries.en: Were they not both able servants of Wei?
entries.literal: Were they not both capable ministers of Wei?

entries.zh: 遭隨有命，俱嬰世禍，悲哉！
entries.en: Subject to the turns of fate, both were struck down by the calamities of their age—how tragic!
entries.literal: Meeting fate as it followed, both suffered calamities of the age—how tragic!

entries.zh: 始均才志未申，惜也。
entries.en: Shijun's talent and ambition were never fully realized—a pity.
entries.literal: Shijun's talents and aspirations were unfulfilled—a pity.

entries.zh: 盧同 張烈
entries.en: Lu Tong; Zhang Lie
entries.literal: Lu Tong; Zhang Lie

entries.zh: 盧同，字叔倫，范陽涿人，盧玄之族孫。
entries.en: Lu Tong, whose style name was Shulun, came from Zhuo in Fanyang and was a descendant of Lu Xuan's clan.
entries.literal: Lu Tong, style name Shulun, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang, a clan grandson of Lu Xuan.

entries.zh: 父輔，字顯元，本州別駕。
entries.en: His father Fu, styled Xianyuan, served as provincial aide.
entries.literal: His father Fu, style name Xianyuan, was Separate Carriage of this province.

entries.zh: 同身長八尺，容貌魁偉，善於處世。
entries.en: Tong stood eight chi tall, with a towering presence, and was adept in worldly affairs.
entries.literal: Tong was eight chi in height, his appearance imposing and grand, and skilled in dealing with the world.

entries.zh: 太和中，起家北海王詳國常侍。
entries.en: During the Taihe reign he began his career as a household attendant in the household of Prince Xiang of Beihai.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era he first entered service as a household retainer of the state of Prince Xiang of Beihai.

entries.zh: 稍遷司空祭酒、昌黎太守。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Libationer of the Works and Grand Administrator of Changli.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Libationer of the Minister of Works and Grand Administrator of Changli.

entries.zh: 尋為營州長史，仍帶郡。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Chief Clerk of Yingzhou, retaining concurrent charge of the commandery.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he became Chief Clerk of Ying Province, still holding the commandery as well.

entries.zh: 入除河南尹丞，遷太尉屬。
entries.en: He was summoned to the capital as Assistant Intendant of Henan, then promoted to an aide under the Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Assistant to the Intendant of Henan, then transferred to an aide post under the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 靈太后反政，以同叉黨，除名。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, Tong was struck from the rolls as a member of Cha's faction.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because Tong was counted among Cha's faction, his name was struck from the rolls.

entries.zh: 孝昌三年，除左將軍、太中大夫、兼左丞，為齊兗二州行臺，節度大都督李叔仁。
entries.en: In the third year of Xiaochang he was appointed Left General, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and concurrent Left Assistant Director, and served as mobile headquarters over the two provinces of Qi and Yan directing Grand Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang, he was appointed Left General, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and concurrent Left Assistant Director; he served as mobile headquarters over Qi and the two Yanzhou provinces, directing Grand Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren.

entries.zh: 闕莊帝踐祚，詔復本秩，除都官尚書，復兼七兵。
entries.en: 〈Missing text〉 When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, an edict restored his former ranks; he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Scrutiny and again concurrently held the Seven Troops bureau.
entries.literal: 〈Missing text〉 When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, an edict restored his former ranks; he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Scrutiny and again concurrently held the Seven Troops bureau.

entries.zh: 以同前慰勞德興之功，封章武縣開國伯，邑四百戶。
entries.en: For Tong's earlier service in pacifying Jiudexing, he was enfeoffed as founding baron of Zhangwu County with a fief of four hundred households.
entries.literal: For Tong's earlier achievement in comforting Dexing, he was enfeoffed as Baron Who Founded Zhangwu County, with a fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 正除七兵，尋轉殿中，加征南將軍。
entries.en: He was formally appointed to the Seven Troops bureau; soon afterward he was transferred to the Palace Attendants and additionally named General Who Campaigns South.
entries.literal: He was formally appointed to the Seven Troops bureau; shortly afterward he was transferred to the Palace Attendants and given the additional title General Who Campaigns South.

entries.zh: 普泰初，除侍中，進號驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: At the opening of the Putai reign he was appointed Palace Attendant and advanced to General of Fast Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he was appointed Palace Attendant and advanced to General of Fast Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 同時久病，強牽從務，啟乞儀同。
entries.en: Tong had long been ill but was forcibly pressed to continue in office; he memorialized requesting the honorific rank of Yitong.
entries.literal: At the same time Tong had long been ill but was forcibly pressed into service; he memorialized requesting the honorific rank of Yitong.

entries.zh: 初同之為黃門也，與前廢帝俱在門下，同異其為人，素相款託。
entries.en: Earlier, when Tong served in the Yellow Gate, he and the Deposed Former Emperor were both in the Gate Department; Tong admired his character and they had long been on intimate terms.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Tong served in the Yellow Gate, he and the Deposed Former Emperor were both in the Gate Department; Tong was impressed by his character and they had long been on friendly terms.

entries.zh: 廢帝以恩舊許之，除儀同三司，餘官如故。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor granted it out of old friendship; Tong was given Yitong Third Rank, his other offices remaining unchanged.
entries.literal: The Deposed Emperor, out of old friendship, granted it; Tong was given Yitong Third Rank, his other offices remaining as before.

entries.zh: 永熙初薨，年五十六。
entries.en: At the opening of the Yongxi reign he died at the age of fifty-six.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he died, aged fifty-six.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、都督冀滄瀛三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、冀州刺史，開國伯如故，賜帛四百匹，諡曰孝穆。
entries.en: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant, command over the military affairs of Ji, Cang, and Ying provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Duke of the Works, and Inspector of Jizhou; his founding barony was unchanged; four hundred bolts of silk were granted; his posthumous title was Xiaomu.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ji, Cang, and Ying provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Duke of the Works, and Inspector of Jizhou; his founding barony remained as before; four hundred bolts of silk were granted; his posthumous title was Xiaomu.

entries.zh: 三年，復加贈尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Three years later he was again posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Three years later he was again posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 有四子。
entries.en: He had four sons.
entries.literal: He had four sons.

entries.zh: 會豫州城民白早生反，都督中山王英、尚書邢巒等討之，詔同為軍司。
entries.en: When the townspeople of Yuzhou under Bai Zaosheng rose in revolt, Prince Ying of Zhongshan as commander-in-chief, Minister Xing Luan, and others marched against them; Tong was ordered to serve as army aide.
entries.literal: It happened that the city people of Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, rebelled; the Commander-in-Chief Prince Ying of Zhongshan, the Minister Xing Luan, and others attacked them, and an edict appointed Tong as Army Aide.

entries.zh: 事平，除冀州鎮東府長史。
entries.en: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was made Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification headquarters in Jizhou.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification Headquarters in Jizhou.

entries.zh: 遭父憂解任。
entries.en: He resigned upon his father's death.
entries.literal: He met with his father's bereavement and left office.

entries.zh: 後除司空諮議參軍，兼司馬，為營構東宮都將。
entries.en: He was later appointed Consulting Army Aide under the Minister of Works, also serving as Major, and named chief commander for building the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Consulting Army Aide to the Minister of Works, concurrently Major, and made Chief Commander for constructing the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 延昌中，秦州民反，詔同兼通直常侍，持節慰諭之，多所降下。
entries.en: During the Yan-chang era, when the people of Qinzhou rebelled, Tong was ordered to serve concurrently as Regular Attendant and, bearing imperial credentials, to console and instruct them; many groups surrendered.
entries.literal: In the Yan-chang era the people of Qinzhou rebelled; an edict made Tong concurrently Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, bearing credentials to console and instruct them, and many submitted.

entries.zh: 還轉尚書右丞，進號輔國將軍，以父諱不拜，改授龍驤。
entries.en: After returning he became Right Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing and was advanced to General Who Assists the State; because the title conflicted with his father's name he declined it and was reassigned as Dragon Cavalry General.
entries.literal: On his return he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced in title to General Who Assists the State; because of his father's taboo name he did not accept the appointment and was instead given Dragon Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 熙平初，轉左丞，加征虜將軍。
entries.en: At the opening of the Xiping reign he was moved to Left Assistant Director and additionally named General Who Captures the Barbarians.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Xiping era he was transferred to Left Assistant Director and given the additional title General Who Captures the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 時相州刺史奚康生徵民歲調，皆七八十尺，以邀奉公之譽。
entries.en: At that time Xi Kangsheng, Inspector of Xiangzhou, collected the annual levy from the people in bolts of seventy or eighty chi each, seeking a reputation for scrupulous devotion to the state.
entries.literal: At that time the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Xi Kangsheng, levied the people's annual tribute in lengths all of seventy or eighty chi, to win a reputation for devoted public service.

entries.zh: 部內患之，同於歲祿官給長絹。
entries.en: The people under his jurisdiction resented this; Tong, from the year's official salary, had long bolts of silk issued as stipends.
entries.literal: Those within his jurisdiction were distressed by this; Tong, in the year's salary, had officials issue long bolts of silk as stipends.

entries.zh: 同乃舉按康生度外徵調。
entries.en: Tong then impeached Kangsheng for collecting levies beyond the statutory quota.
entries.literal: Tong thereupon brought charges and investigated Kangsheng's levies beyond the prescribed measure.

entries.zh: 書奏，詔科康生之罪，兼褒同在公之績。
entries.en: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict convicted Kangsheng and at the same time commended Tong's service to the public good.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict assessed Kangsheng's crime and also praised Tong's public achievements.

entries.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后也，相州刺史、中山王熙起兵於鄴。
entries.en: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Prince Xi of Zhongshan, who was Inspector of Xiangzhou, raised an army at Ye.
entries.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince Xi of Zhongshan, raised troops at Ye.

entries.zh: 熙敗，以同為持節、兼黃門侍郎、慰勞使，乃就州刑熙。
entries.en: After Xi's defeat, Tong was appointed Bearer of Credentials and concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant as a comforting envoy; he executed Xi in the province.
entries.literal: When Xi was defeated, Tong was made Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant, and Comforting Envoy; he then executed Xi in the province.

entries.zh: 還授平東將軍，正黃門，營明堂副將。
entries.en: On returning he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and deputy commander for building the Bright Hall.
entries.literal: On his return he was given General Who Pacifies the East, Regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and Deputy Commander for constructing the Bright Hall.

entries.zh: 尋加撫軍將軍、光祿大夫、本州大中正。
entries.en: He was soon additionally named Army-soothing General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Rectifier of the Pure for his native province.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the additional titles Army-soothing General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Rectifier of the Pure for his home province.

entries.zh: 同善事在位，為叉所親，戮熙之日，深窮黨與，以希叉旨，論者非之。
entries.en: Tong knew how to please those in power and was favored by Cha; on the day Xi was killed he pursued associates relentlessly to win Cha's approval, and critics condemned him for it.
entries.literal: Tong was skilled at serving those in power and was intimate with Cha; on the day Xi was executed he pursued associates to the depths, hoping to please Cha's intent, and critics condemned him.

entries.zh: 又給同羽林二十人以自防衞。
entries.en: He was also granted twenty guards of the Forest of Feathers for his protection.
entries.literal: He was also given twenty guards of the Forest of Feathers for his own protection.

entries.zh: 同兄琇，少多大言，常云「公侯可致」。
entries.en: Tong's elder brother Xiu had been boastful since youth, often saying, "Marquisates and dukedoms are within reach."
entries.literal: Tong's elder brother Xiu, from youth fond of grand talk, often said, "Marquisates and dukedoms can be attained."

entries.zh: 至此始為都水使者。
entries.en: Only then did he become Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.
entries.literal: Only at this point did he become Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.

entries.zh: 同啟求回身二階以加琇，琇遂除安州刺史。
entries.en: Tong petitioned to surrender two ranks from his own record for Xiu's benefit; Xiu was then appointed Inspector of Anzhou.
entries.literal: Tong memorialized asking to return two ranks from his own person to add to Xiu; Xiu was then appointed Inspector of Anzhou.

entries.zh: 論者稱之。
entries.en: Commentators praised him for it.
entries.literal: Critics praised this.

entries.zh: 營州城民就德興謀反，除同度支尚書，黃門如故，持節使營州慰勞，聽以便宜從事。
entries.en: When the townspeople of Yingzhou under Jiudexing plotted rebellion, Tong was appointed Minister of the Treasury while retaining his Yellow Gate post; bearing credentials he was sent to console Yingzhou with discretionary authority.
entries.literal: The city people of Yingzhou, Jiudexing, plotted rebellion; Tong was appointed Minister of the Treasury, Yellow Gate Attendant as before, bearing credentials as envoy to console Yingzhou, with authority to act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 同頻遣使人，皆為賊害，乃遣賊家口三十人并免家奴為良，齎書諭德興，德興乃降。
entries.en: Tong sent envoys repeatedly, but the rebels killed them all; he then sent thirty rebel dependents and freed household slaves to commoner status, carrying a letter to Jiudexing, who then surrendered.
entries.literal: Tong repeatedly sent envoys, all of whom were harmed by the rebels; he then sent thirty family members of the rebels and also freed household slaves to commoner status, carrying a letter to instruct Dexing, and Dexing then surrendered.

entries.zh: 安輯其民而還。
entries.en: He pacified the people and returned.
entries.literal: He settled and comforted the people and returned.

entries.zh: 德興復反，詔同以本將軍為幽州刺史，兼尚書行臺慰勞之。
entries.en: When Jiudexing rebelled again, Tong was ordered to serve as Inspector of Youzhou with his existing general's rank and concurrently as mobile headquarters of the Masters of Writing to console the region.
entries.literal: Dexing rebelled again; an edict made Tong, with his existing general's title, Inspector of Youzhou, concurrently Masters of Writing mobile headquarters to console them.

entries.zh: 同慮德興難信，勒眾而往，為德興所擊，大敗而還。
entries.en: Fearing Jiudexing could not be trusted, Tong marched in force, was attacked and routed, and retreated in defeat.
entries.literal: Tong feared Dexing could not be trusted, drove the host forward, was struck by Dexing, suffered a great defeat, and returned.

entries.zh: 長子斐，武定中，文襄王大將軍府掾。
entries.en: His eldest son Fei, during the Wuding era, served as an aide in Grand General Wen Xiang Wang's headquarters.
entries.literal: His eldest son Fei, in the Wuding era, was an aide in Grand General Wen Xiang's headquarters.

entries.zh: 斐弟筠，青州治中。
entries.en: Fei's younger brother Jun served as Administrative Aide of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Fei's younger brother Jun was Administrative Aide of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 肅宗世，朝政稍衰，人多竊冒軍功。
entries.en: During Emperor Suzong's reign, court governance weakened, and many men fraudulently claimed military merit.
entries.literal: In the age of Emperor Suzong, court governance gradually declined, and many people usurped military merit fraudulently.

entries.zh: 同閱吏部勳書，因加檢覆，覈得竊階者三百餘人。
entries.en: Tong examined the Ministry of Personnel's merit registers and, on further audit, identified more than three hundred who had stolen rank.
entries.literal: Tong reviewed the Ministry of Personnel's merit records and, adding further inspection and verification, found more than three hundred who had stolen ranks.

entries.zh: 同乃表言：
entries.en: Tong then memorialized the throne as follows:
entries.literal: Tong thereupon submitted a memorial saying:

entries.zh: 竊見吏部勳簿，多皆改換。
entries.en: I have observed that the Ministry's merit registers have largely been altered or replaced.
entries.literal: Your subject has observed that the Ministry of Personnel's merit registers have for the most part been altered and replaced.

entries.zh: 乃校中兵奏按，並復乖舛。
entries.en: When checked against the Central Army bureau's submitted investigations, they again failed to agree.
entries.literal: When they were checked against the Central Army's submitted investigations, they were again at variance.

entries.zh: 臣聊爾揀練，已得三百餘人，明知隱而未露者，動有千數。
entries.en: In a preliminary review I have already found more than three hundred cases; those still concealed must number in the thousands.
entries.literal: Your subject, in a cursory sorting and review, has already found more than three hundred; those plainly hidden and not yet exposed must number in the thousands.

entries.zh: 愚謂罪雖恩免，猶須刊定。
entries.en: I hold that even if offenses are pardoned by imperial grace, the records must still be corrected.
entries.literal: This fool believes that although the crimes may be forgiven by grace, they still must be corrected and fixed in the record.

entries.zh: 請遣一都令史與令僕省事各一人，總集吏部、中兵二局勳簿，對勾奏按。
entries.en: I ask that one chief clerk and one secretariat aide each be sent to assemble the merit registers of the Personnel and Central Army bureaus and cross-check them against the submitted investigations.
entries.literal: I request that one chief clerk and one secretariat aide from the Masters of Writing and Works be dispatched to gather together the merit registers of the Ministry of Personnel and the Central Army bureaus and cross-check them against submitted investigations.

entries.zh: 若名級相應者，即於黃素楷書大字，具件階級數，令本曹尚書以朱印印之。
entries.en: Where name and rank match, let the full rank and grade be written in large characters on yellow plain silk and sealed in vermilion by the responsible minister.
entries.literal: Where names and ranks correspond, then on yellow plain silk write in large regular script the full list of rank levels, and have the Minister of that bureau affix a vermilion seal.

entries.zh: 明造兩通，一關吏部，一留兵局，與奏按對掌。
entries.en: Two copies should be made explicitly: one filed with Personnel, one kept in the military bureau, each held against the investigation records.
entries.literal: Clearly make two copies: one to be filed with the Ministry of Personnel, one kept in the military bureau, each to be held against the submitted investigations.

entries.zh: 進則防揩洗之偽，退則無改易之理。
entries.en: Henceforth erasure and forgery will be prevented; retroactive alteration will no longer be possible.
entries.literal: Going forward this will guard against the fraud of erasure and alteration; looking back, there will be no grounds for changing records.

entries.zh: 從前以來，勳書上省，唯列姓名，不載本屬，致令竊濫之徒輕為苟且。
entries.en: Hitherto merit documents sent to the capital listed only names, not home jurisdictions, so that fraudsters treated the system casually.
entries.literal: From former times until now, when merit documents were sent up to the province, only names were listed and native jurisdictions were not recorded, causing those who stole and abused rank to treat the matter lightly and carelessly.

entries.zh: 今請征職白民，具列本州、郡、縣、三長之所；
entries.en: Hereafter, for commoners drafted to service, let their home province, commandery, county, and ward under the three-chief system be fully listed;
entries.literal: Now I request that for commoners called to service, their original province, commandery, county, and the locality of the three chiefs be fully listed;

entries.zh: 其實官正職者，亦列名貫，別錄歷階。
entries.en: and for men holding actual regular office, let name and lineage be listed and successive ranks recorded separately.
entries.literal: for those who are actual officials in regular posts, also list their name and lineage, and separately record their successive ranks.

entries.zh: 仰本軍印記其上，然後印縫各上所司，統將、都督並皆印記，然後列上行臺。
entries.en: Let the home army affix its seal first; then, with seals along the fold, copies should go to each responsible office, and the army commander and regional inspector should all seal them before the list is sent to the mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: Have the home army stamp and seal upon it, then at the seal seam submit copies to each responsible office; the commanding general and regional inspector shall all affix seals, and only then submit the list to the mobile headquarters.

entries.zh: 行臺關太尉，太尉檢練精實，乃始關刺省重究括，然後奏申。
entries.en: The mobile headquarters forwards it to the Grand Commandant; once he has verified the facts, it goes to the provincial authorities for thorough review, and only then is it memorialized to the throne.
entries.literal: The mobile headquarters forwards it to the Grand Commandant; the Grand Commandant inspects, refines, and verifies the facts, and only then forwards it to the province for thorough re-examination, after which it is memorialized and reported.

entries.zh: 奏出之日，黃素朱印，關付吏部。
entries.en: On the day the memorial is approved, a yellow register sealed in vermilion is forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: On the day the memorial is issued, yellow plain silk with vermilion seal is forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 頃來非但偷階冒名，改換勳簿而已，或一階再取，或易名受級，凡如此者，其人不少。
entries.en: Recently men have not only stolen rank and usurped names or altered merit registers; some have claimed the same rank twice, or changed names to receive grades—such cases are numerous.
entries.literal: Recently it is not only stealing ranks and usurping names and altering merit registers; some take one rank twice, or change names to receive grades—such cases are not few.

entries.zh: 良由吏部無簿，防塞失方。
entries.en: This is chiefly because Personnel keeps no proper register, so safeguards have failed.
entries.literal: This is truly because the Ministry of Personnel has no register, and the means of prevention and blocking have failed.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 吏部加階之後，簿不注記，緣此之故，易生僥倖。
entries.en: After Personnel awards a rank, the register is not annotated, and opportunism easily follows.
entries.literal: After the Ministry of Personnel adds a rank, the register is not annotated; because of this, opportunism easily arises.

entries.zh: 自今敍階之後，名簿具注加補日月，尚書印記，然後付曹。
entries.en: Henceforth, whenever a rank is conferred, the register must note the date of the award, be sealed by the minister, and only then passed to the bureau.
entries.literal: From now on, after ranks are conferred, the name register shall fully note the date of addition and supplementation, the Minister shall affix a seal, and only then hand it to the bureau.

entries.zh: 郎中別作抄目，[1]印記一如尚書，郎中自掌，遞代相付。
entries.en: The bureau director shall keep a separate copy register, stamped like the minister's copy, held in his own custody and handed on in rotation.
entries.literal: The director shall make a separate copy register, stamped like the Minister's register, which the director keeps in hand and passes on in rotation.

entries.zh: 此制一行，差止姦罔。
entries.en: Once this system is in force, fraud will largely cease.
entries.literal: Once this system is implemented, fraud and deception will largely cease.

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The emperor approved the proposal.
entries.literal: An edict approved it.

entries.zh: 同又奏曰：
entries.en: Tong submitted a further memorial:
entries.literal: Tong again memorialized, saying:

entries.zh: 臣頃奏以黃素為勳，[2]具注官名、戶屬及吏部換勳之法，事目三條，已蒙旨許。
entries.en: I recently proposed using yellow registers for merit records, with full notation of office, household affiliation, and Personnel's rules for altering registers—three measures in all—which Your Majesty has already approved.
entries.literal: Your subject recently memorialized using yellow plain silk for merit records, fully noting official names, household affiliation, and the Ministry of Personnel's method for altering merit records—three items in all—which have already received imperial approval.

entries.zh: 臣伏思黃素勳簿，政可粗止姦偽，然在軍虛詐，猶未可盡。
entries.en: I consider that yellow merit registers can curb forgery in general, yet army-side fraud cannot yet be fully eliminated.
entries.literal: Your subject reflects that yellow plain silk merit registers can roughly stop fraud and forgery, yet false claims in the army still cannot be fully ended.

entries.zh: 請自今在軍閱簿之日，行臺、軍司、監軍、都督各明立文按，處處記之。
entries.en: I ask that from now on, on the day registers are reviewed in camp, the mobile headquarters, army aide, army inspector, and regional inspector each keep explicit written records at every point.
entries.literal: I request that from now on, on the day of army muster and register review, the mobile headquarters, army aide, army inspector, and regional inspector each clearly establish written records and note every place.

entries.zh: 斬首成一階已上，即令給券。
entries.en: Whenever decapitations amount to one full rank of merit or more, a warrant should be issued at once.
entries.literal: When decapitations amount to one rank or more, issue a warrant immediately.

entries.zh: 一紙之上，當中大書起行臺、統軍位號，勳人甲乙。
entries.en: On one sheet, the mobile headquarters and army commander's titles should be written prominently at the center, with the merit-holder's name in sequence.
entries.literal: On a single sheet, write prominently in the center the mobile headquarters and army commander's titles, and the merit-holder's name in order.

entries.zh: 斬三賊及被傷成階已上，亦具書於券。
entries.en: Decapitating three enemies and wounds qualifying for one rank or more should likewise be fully recorded on the warrant.
entries.literal: Decapitating three bandits and being wounded to the level of one rank or more should also be fully written on the warrant.

entries.zh: 各盡一行，當行豎裂。
entries.en: Each entry should fill one line, with a vertical split along that line.
entries.literal: Each fills one line; along the line make a vertical split.

entries.zh: 其券前後皆起年號日月，破某處陳，某官某勳，印記為驗。
entries.en: Both ends of the warrant should bear the reign era date; breaking such-and-such enemy formation, such-and-such officer's such-and-such merit—with seals as proof.
entries.literal: At front and back of the warrant begin with reign era year, month, and day; breaking such-and-such place's formation, such-and-such official's such-and-such merit—seals as verification.

entries.zh: 一支付勳人，一支付行臺。
entries.en: One copy goes to the merit-holder, one to the mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: One copy given to the merit-holder, one given to the mobile headquarters.

entries.zh: 記至京，即送門下，別函守錄。
entries.en: When records reach the capital, they should go at once to the Gate Department, with a separate sealed copy kept on file.
entries.literal: When the record reaches the capital, send it immediately to the Gate Department and keep a separate sealed copy on file.

entries.zh: 又自遷都以來，戎車屢捷，所以征勳轉多，敍不可盡者，良由歲久生姦，積年長偽，巧吏階緣，偷增遂甚。
entries.en: Moreover, since the capital was moved, repeated military victories have multiplied battlefield merit; the backlog of unrewarded merit owes chiefly to years of fraud, long-standing falsification, and clever clerks who exploit connections until illicit claims have grown severe.
entries.literal: Moreover, since the move of the capital, war chariots have repeatedly won victories, so battlefield merit has steadily increased; those who cannot all be rewarded are truly because years breed fraud, long accumulation breeds falsehood, and clever clerks climb by connections, so illicit additions have become extreme.

entries.zh: 請自今為始，諸有勳簿已經奏賞者，即廣下遠近，云某處勳判，咸令知聞。
entries.en: I ask that henceforth, whenever merit registers have been memorialized and rewarded, notice be sent far and wide naming the place and judgment, so that all may know.
entries.literal: I request that from now on, wherever merit registers have already been memorialized and rewarded, copies be widely sent near and far, stating such-and-such place's merit judgment, so that all may know.

entries.zh: 立格酬敍，以三年為斷。
entries.en: Set a rule that rewards must be conferred within three years.
entries.literal: Establish a rule for rewarding and conferring ranks, with three years as the limit.

entries.zh: 其職人及出身，限內悉令銓除；
entries.en: Within that limit, clerical posts and entry-level appointments must all be filled;
entries.literal: For clerical personnel and initial appointments, within the limit all are to be evaluated and cleared;

entries.zh: 實官及外號，隨才加授。
entries.en: regular offices and honorary titles should be granted according to merit and ability.
entries.literal: actual offices and external titles are to be granted according to talent.

entries.zh: 庶使酬勤者速申，立功者勸，事不經久，僥倖易息。
entries.en: Thus the diligent may be rewarded promptly, men of merit encouraged, delays avoided, and opportunism easily suppressed.
entries.literal: Thus those repaying diligence may quickly report, those establishing merit may be encouraged, affairs will not drag on for long, and opportunism will easily subside.

entries.zh: 或遭窮難，州無中正者，不在此限。
entries.en: Cases where hardship prevents evaluation, or a province lacks a Rectifier of the Pure, are excepted.
entries.literal: Or if they meet hardship and the province has no Rectifier of the Pure, they are outside this limit.

entries.zh: 又勳簿之法，征還之日即應申送。
entries.en: Moreover, by merit-register law, registers should be submitted the day the army returns.
entries.literal: Moreover, by the law of merit registers, on the day the campaign returns they should be submitted.

entries.zh: 頃來行臺、督將，至京始造，或一年二歲方上勳書。
entries.en: Recently mobile headquarters and supervising generals have waited until reaching the capital to compile registers, or submitted merit documents only after one or two years.
entries.literal: Recently mobile headquarters and supervising generals have waited until reaching the capital to compile them, or only after one or two years submitted merit documents.

entries.zh: 姦偽之原，實自由此。
entries.en: The root of fraud lies precisely here.
entries.literal: The root of fraud and falsehood truly lies in this.

entries.zh: 於今以後，軍還之日便通勳簿，不聽隔月。
entries.en: Henceforth registers must be transmitted the day the army returns; delay beyond a month will not be allowed.
entries.literal: From now on, on the day the army returns the merit register must be transmitted; crossing a month is not permitted.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：盧同質器洪厚，卷舒兼濟。
entries.en: The historian writes: Lu Tong possessed a broad and weighty character, able to adapt whether advancing or withdrawing.
entries.literal: The historian says: Lu Tong's native substance was broad and deep, able both to advance and to withdraw as the times required.

entries.zh: 張烈早標名輩，氣尚見知。
entries.en: Zhang Lie early distinguished himself among notable men, and his bearing won esteem.
entries.literal: Zhang Lie early marked himself among famous men, and his spirit and bearing won recognition.

entries.zh: 趨捨深沉，俱至顯達，雅道正路，其殆病諸。
entries.en: Both pursued their ambitions with subtle calculation and reached high office—yet on the path of true refinement, this may be where they fell short.
entries.literal: Their choices in advance and retreat were deep and hidden; both reached eminence—yet on the refined path and upright road, this is perhaps where they fell ill.

entries.zh: 同兄靜，太常丞。
entries.en: Tong's elder brother Jing was Assistant Director of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
entries.literal: Tong's elder brother Jing was Assistant in the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 郎中別作抄目 諸本「目」訛「自」，不可通，今據北史卷三０盧同傳改。
entries.en: Regarding "the director shall make a separate copy register": various editions wrongly read "register" (mu) as "self" (zi), which is unintelligible; the text is corrected here according to Lu Tong's biography in juan 30 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.
entries.literal: On "the director shall make a separate copy register": in various editions "register" (mu) is wrongly written as "self" (zi), which makes no sense; the text is now corrected according to the biography of Lu Tong in juan 30 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.

entries.zh: 節度大都督李叔仁
entries.en: Grand Commander-in-Chief and Controller Li Shuren
entries.literal: Grand Commander-in-Chief and Controller Li Shuren

entries.en: 〈Missing text〉
entries.literal: 〈Missing〉

entries.zh: 諸本下旁注「闕」字。
entries.en: Various editions carry a marginal note reading "missing."
entries.literal: Various editions have a marginal note reading "missing."

entries.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀孝昌三年二月庚申稱東郡民趙顯德反，詔都督李叔仁討之；
entries.en: According to juan 9 of Emperor Suzong's annals, on gengshen day in the second month of the third year of Xiaochang, the people of Dong Commandery under Zhao Xiande rebelled, and an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to suppress them;
entries.literal: According to juan 9 of the Annals of Emperor Suzong, in the third year of Xiaochang, second month, day gengshen, it says the people of Dong Commandery under Zhao Xiande rebelled and an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack them;

entries.zh: 三月辛未又稱齊州廣川民劉鈞執清河太守邵懷聚眾反，六月稱詔都督李叔仁討劉鈞平之。
entries.en: on xinwei day in the third month it records that Liu Jun of Guangchuan in Qizhou seized Grand Administrator Shao Huai of Qinghe and raised a rebellion; in the sixth month an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack Liu Jun and pacify him.
entries.literal: third month, day xinwei, it again says the people of Guangchuan in Qizhou, Liu Jun, seized the Grand Administrator of Qinghe, Shao Huai, gathered a host and rebelled; sixth month says an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack Liu Jun and pacify him.

entries.zh: 東郡屬西兗州。
entries.en: Dong Commandery belonged to West Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Dong Commandery belonged to West Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 盧同以齊兗二州行臺節度李叔仁，所闕必即鎮壓這兩支變亂軍事，但紀不書盧同以行臺節度事。
entries.en: Lu Tong, as mobile headquarters over Qi and the two Yanzhou provinces, directed Li Shuren; the missing passage must concern the suppression of these two rebellions, though the annals do not record Tong's role as mobile headquarters commander.
entries.literal: Lu Tong, as mobile headquarters of Qi and Yanzhou, controlled Li Shuren; what is missing must be the suppression of these two rebellions, yet the annals do not record Lu Tong's role as mobile headquarters controller.

entries.zh: 張烈，字徽仙，清河東武城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Lie, whose style name was Huixian, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
entries.literal: Zhang Lie, style name Huixian, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

entries.zh: 高祖賜名曰烈，仍以本名為字焉。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu gave him the name Lie, while his original name served as his style name.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu bestowed the name Lie upon him, yet still used his original name as his style name.

entries.zh: 高祖悕，為慕容 尚書右僕射。
entries.en: His great-great-grandfather Xi served the Murong as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xi was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under the Murong.

entries.zh: 曾祖恂，散騎常侍，隨慕容德南渡，因居齊郡之臨淄。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xun was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; he followed Murong De south across the Yangzi and settled at Linzi in Qi Commandery.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xun was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, followed Murong De south across the river, and thus settled at Linzi in Qi Commandery.

entries.zh: 烈少孤貧，涉獵經史，有氣概。
entries.en: Lie was orphaned and poor in youth, read widely in the classics and histories, and possessed force of character.
entries.literal: Lie from youth was orphaned and poor, ranged through the classics and histories, and had spirit and force of character.

entries.zh: 時青州有崔徽伯、房徽叔，與烈並有令譽，時人號曰「三徽」。
entries.en: At that time Qingzhou had Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu; they and Lie all enjoyed fine reputations, and contemporaries called them "the Three Huis."
entries.literal: At that time in Qingzhou were Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu; together with Lie they all had fine reputations, and men of the time called them "the Three Huis."

entries.zh: 高祖時，入官代都，歷侍御、主文中散。
entries.en: During Gaozu's reign he entered service at the capital in Dai, serving as Attendant Censor and Regular Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time he entered office at the capital in Dai, passing through Attendant Censor and Regular Attendant of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 遷洛，除尚書儀曹郎、彭城王功曹史、太子步兵校尉。
entries.en: After the move to Luoyang he was appointed Master of Writing in the Ceremonials Bureau, Merit Officer to the Prince of Pengcheng, and Commandant of Footsoldiers to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was appointed Master of Writing in the Ceremonials Bureau, Merit Officer of the Prince of Pengcheng, and Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 蕭寶卷將陳顯達治兵漢南，謀將入寇。
entries.en: Chen Xianda, a general of Xiao Baojuan of Qi, drilled troops south of the Han and planned an invasion.
entries.literal: Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda drilled troops south of the Han, plotting to invade.

entries.zh: 時順陽太守王青石世官江南，荊州刺史、廣陽王嘉慮其有異，表請代之。
entries.en: The Grand Administrator of Shunyang, Wang Qingshi, came from a family long established south of the Yangzi; Prince Jia of Guangyang, Inspector of Jingzhou, suspected his loyalty and memorialized for his replacement.
entries.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator of Shunyang, Wang Qingshi, had for generations held office south of the Yangzi; the Inspector of Jingzhou, Prince Jia of Guangyang, feared he was disloyal and memorialized requesting a replacement.

entries.zh: 高祖詔侍臣各舉所知，互有申薦者。
entries.en: Gaozu ordered his attendant ministers each to recommend someone they knew, and several names were put forward.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the attendant ministers each to recommend men they knew, and several offered nominations.

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此郡今當必爭之地，須得堪濟之才，何容汎舉也。
entries.en: Gaozu said, "This commandery is certain to become a battleground; it requires talent equal to the task—how could one put forward names at random?
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "This commandery is now certain to become contested ground; it requires talent equal to the task—how could one put forward names at random?

entries.zh: 太子步兵張烈每論軍國之事，時有會人意處，朕欲用之，何如？」
entries.en: The Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhang Lie, whenever he discusses military and state affairs, often hits the mark; I wish to employ him—what do you think?"
entries.literal: The Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhang Lie, whenever he discusses military and state affairs, often hits the point; We wish to employ him—what do you think?"

entries.zh: 彭城王勰稱贊之，遂敕除陵江將軍、順陽太守。
entries.en: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, praised him, and an edict appointed him General Who Crosses the Jiang and Grand Administrator of Shunyang.
entries.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, praised him, and an edict thereupon appointed him General Who Crosses the Jiang and Grand Administrator of Shunyang.

entries.zh: 烈到郡二日，便為寶卷將崔慧景攻圍，七十餘日，烈撫厲將士，甚得軍人之和。
entries.en: Two days after Lie reached the commandery, he was besieged by Cui Huijing, a general of Xiao Baojuan; for more than seventy days Lie rallied his troops and won their wholehearted loyalty.
entries.literal: Lie had been in the commandery two days when he was besieged by Baojuan's general Cui Huijing; for more than seventy days Lie comforted and encouraged the troops, winning great harmony among the soldiers.

entries.zh: 會車駕南討，慧景遁走。
entries.en: When the emperor marched south in person, Huijing fled.
entries.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage marched south to attack, and Huijing fled.

entries.zh: 高祖親勞烈曰：「卿定可，遂能不負所寄。」
entries.en: Gaozu personally congratulated Lie, saying, "You have proved yourself capable and have not betrayed the trust I placed in you."
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally comforted Lie, saying, "You are certainly capable and have not failed the trust placed in you."

entries.zh: 烈拜謝曰：「若不值鑾輿親駕，臣將不免困於犬羊。
entries.en: Lie bowed and replied, "Had Your Majesty not come in person, I would surely have been overrun by the enemy like a flock of beasts.
entries.literal: Lie bowed in thanks and said, "Had I not met the imperial carriage's personal campaign, your subject would not have escaped being trapped by dogs and sheep.

entries.zh: 自是陛下不負臣，非臣能不負陛下。」
entries.en: It is Your Majesty who has not failed me—not that I could claim never to have failed Your Majesty."
entries.literal: From this it is Your Majesty who has not failed your subject, not that your subject could fail to fail Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 高祖善其對。
entries.en: Gaozu was pleased with his answer.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved his reply.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，追錄先勳，封清河縣開國子，邑二百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he recognized Lie's earlier merit and enfeoffed him as founding viscount of Qinghe County with a fief of two hundred households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he recorded former merit and enfeoffed him as Viscount Who Founded the State of Qinghe, with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋以母老歸養。
entries.en: He soon retired to care for his aged mother.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward, because his mother was old, he returned home to support her.

entries.zh: 積十餘年，頻值凶儉，烈為粥以食飢人，蒙濟者甚眾，鄉黨以此稱之。
entries.en: For more than ten years he lived through repeated famines; Lie made gruel to feed the hungry, relieving a great many people, and his neighbors praised him for it.
entries.literal: Over more than ten years he frequently met with famine and dearth; Lie made gruel to feed the hungry, and those who received relief were very many; his village and district praised him for this.

entries.zh: 肅宗初，除龍驤將軍、司徒右長史。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Dragon Cavalry General and Right Chief Clerk under the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Dragon Cavalry General and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 又轉征虜將軍、司空長史。
entries.en: He was later transferred to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Chief Clerk under the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 先是，元叉父江陽王繼曾為青州刺史，及叉當權，烈託故義之懷，遂相諂附。
entries.en: Earlier, Yuan Cha's father, Prince Ji of Jiangyang, had served as Inspector of Qingzhou; when Cha came to power, Lie invoked their old ties and attached himself to him with flattery.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yuan Cha's father Prince Ji of Jiangyang had once been Inspector of Qingzhou; when Cha held power, Lie relied on their old bond of righteousness and thus flattered and attached himself to him.

entries.zh: 除前將軍、給事黃門侍郎，尋加平南將軍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was appointed Forward General and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and soon additionally named General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: He was appointed Forward General and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and shortly given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 後靈太后反政，以烈叉黨，出為鎮東將軍、青州刺史。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Ling later regained power, Lie was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou because he was counted among Cha's faction.
entries.literal: Later, when Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because Lie was counted among Cha's faction, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 于時議者以烈家產畜殖，僮客甚多，慮其怨望，不宜出為本州，改授安北將軍、瀛州刺史。
entries.en: Critics at the time noted that Lie's household wealth and retinue had grown large and feared he might harbor resentment if sent to his home province; he was instead appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: At that time critics, because Lie's household wealth and livestock had multiplied and his retainers were many, feared he harbored resentment and that he should not be sent out to his home province; he was instead given General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 為政清靜，吏民安之。
entries.en: His administration was quiet and orderly, and officials and commoners alike were content.
entries.literal: His governance was pure and tranquil, and officials and people were at ease.

entries.zh: 綦儁 山偉 劉仁之 宇文忠之
entries.en: Qi Jun; Shan Wei; Liu Renzhi; Yuwen Zhongzhi
entries.literal: Qi Jun; Shan Wei; Liu Renzhi; Yuwen Zhongzhi

entries.zh: 劉仁之，字山靜，河南洛陽人。
entries.en: Liu Renzhi, courtesy name Shanjing, was from Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Liu Renzhi, courtesy name Shanjing, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 其先代人，徙于洛。
entries.en: His ancestors were northerners of Dai who had moved to Luoyang.
entries.literal: His forebears were men of Dai who moved to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 父爾頭，在外戚傳。
entries.en: His father Er'tou is treated in the biographies of consorts' kin.
entries.literal: His father Er'tou is in the biographies of consorts' kin.

entries.zh: 仁之少有操尚，粗涉書史，真草書迹，頗號工便。
entries.en: Renzhi in youth had moral resolve, read broadly in books and histories, and was known as skilled in both regular and cursive script.
entries.literal: Renzhi in youth had moral resolve, roughly ranged through books and histories, and in regular and cursive script his traces were famed as quite handy.

entries.zh: 御史中尉元昭引為御史。
entries.en: Chief of censors Yuan Zhao brought him in as a censor.
entries.literal: Chief of censors Yuan Zhao brought him in as censor.

entries.zh: 前廢帝時，兼黃門侍郎，深為尒朱世隆所信用。
entries.en: Under the former Deposed Emperor he served concurrently as gentleman of the yellow gate and was deeply trusted by Erzhu Shilong.
entries.literal: In the time of the Deposed Emperor of Former times he concurrently served as gentleman of the yellow gate and was deeply trusted by Erzhu Shilong.

entries.zh: 出帝初，為著作郎，兼中書令，既非其才，在史未嘗執筆。
entries.en: At the start of the fleeing emperor's reign he was made compilation gentleman and concurrently director of the secretariat; the post was beyond his ability, and in the history office he never actually wrote.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the fleeing emperor he was made compilation gentleman and concurrently director of the secretariat; it was not his talent, and in the history bureau he never took up the brush.

entries.zh: 出除衞將軍、西兗州刺史，在州有當時之譽。
entries.en: He left court to serve as general of the guard and governor of Western Yan Province, where he won a fine reputation.
entries.literal: He went out and was made general of the guard and governor of Western Yan Province; in the province he had a reputation of the day.

entries.zh: 武定二年卒，贈衞大將軍、吏部尚書、青州刺史，諡曰敬。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Wuding and was posthumously made grand general of the guard, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Jing.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wuding he died; posthumously he was given grand general of the guard, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, governor of Qing Province; his posthumous title was Jing.

entries.zh: 魏書卷八十一 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」。
entries.en: Wei shu juan 81: In the tables of contents of various editions this scroll is marked "lacunose."
entries.literal: Wei shu juan 81: In the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked "deficient."

entries.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。」
entries.en: The Palace Edition notes: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later hands supplied this."
entries.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification says: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later persons supplemented it."

entries.zh: 按此卷以北史卷五０綦儁、山偉、宇文忠之三傳及卷二０劉庫仁附劉仁之傳補。
entries.en: This scroll was patched from Beishi juan 50 (biographies of Qi Jun, Shan Wei, and Yuwen Zhongzhi) and juan 20 (Liu Kuren appendix, Liu Renzhi).
entries.literal: According to this, this juan was supplemented from Beishi juan 50 biographies of Qi Jun, Shan Wei, and Yuwen Zhongzhi and juan 20 Liu Kuren appendix Liu Renzhi biography.

entries.zh: 卷末無宋人校語，當是脫去。
entries.en: The scroll ends without Song-dynasty collation notes; they must have dropped out.
entries.literal: At the end of the juan there are no Song-dynasty collation notes; they must have been lost.

entries.zh: 仁之外示長者，內懷矯詐。
entries.en: Outwardly Renzhi played the elder; inwardly he was full of deceit.
entries.literal: Outwardly Renzhi displayed the bearing of an elder; inwardly he harbored deceit and craft.

entries.zh: 其對賓客，破牀弊席，粗飯冷菜，衣服故敗，乃過逼下。
entries.en: With guests he offered broken beds and ragged mats, coarse rice and cold dishes, and worn-out clothes—going to excess to humble himself.
entries.literal: Toward guests he broke beds and worn mats, coarse rice and cold dishes, clothes old and ruined—thus he overpressed those below.

entries.zh: 善候當途，能為詭激。
entries.en: He was skilled at watching those in power and could stage sudden dramatic gestures.
entries.literal: He was skilled at watching those in power and could perform abrupt provocations.

entries.zh: 每於稠人廣眾之中，或撾一姦吏，或縱一孤貧，大言自眩，示己高明，矜物無知。
entries.en: In crowded public gatherings he would sometimes beat a corrupt official or sometimes release a lone poor man, declaiming loudly to dazzle others, showing himself lofty and looking down on the ignorant world.
entries.literal: Whenever in a dense crowd or broad assembly he would sometimes beat a corrupt official or sometimes release a lone poor man, speaking loudly to dazzle others, showing himself lofty and bright, condescending that things were ignorant of him.

entries.zh: 淺識皆稱其美，公能之譽，動過其實。
entries.en: Shallow observers all praised him; his reputation for public virtue far outran the reality.
entries.literal: Men of shallow insight all praised his beauty; the reputation of public talent exceeded the fact.

entries.zh: 性又酷虐，在晉陽曾營城雉，仁之統監作役，以小稽緩，遂杖前殷州刺史裴瑗、并州刺史王綽，齊獻武王大加譴責。
entries.en: He was also cruel by nature. At Jinyang, when city walls were under construction, Renzhi supervised the labor; for a slight delay he had the former governor of Yin Province, Pei Yuan, and the governor of Bing Province, Wang Chuo, beaten—King Xianwu of Qi rebuked him severely.
entries.literal: His nature was also cruel and violent; at Jinyang he once oversaw city walls; Renzhi directed and supervised the labor, and for a small delay in pace he had the former Yin Province governor Pei Yuan and Bing Province governor Wang Chuo beaten—King Xianwu of Qi greatly denounced him.

entries.zh: 性好文字，吏書失體，便加鞭撻，言韻微訛，亦見捶楚，吏民苦之。
entries.en: He was exacting about written forms; if a clerk's document was improperly formatted he would flog him, and if a word's pronunciation or tone was slightly off he would beat him as well—officials and commoners alike suffered under him.
entries.literal: He loved written forms; if clerical documents lost proper form he would add the whip; if pronunciation or rhyme was slightly wrong he also saw the cudgel—clerks and people suffered.

entries.zh: 而愛好文史，敬重人流。
entries.en: Yet he loved literature and history and treated men of letters with respect.
entries.literal: Yet he loved belles-lettres and history and respected men of culture.

entries.zh: 與齋帥馮元興交款，元興死後積年，仁之營視其家，常出隆厚。
entries.en: He was close to director of auspices Feng Yuanxing; years after Yuanxing's death Renzhi still looked after his household and often gave generously.
entries.literal: He was on close terms with director of auspices Feng Yuanxing; years after Yuanxing's death Renzhi still managed and watched his household, often giving generously.

entries.zh: 時人以此尚之。
entries.en: Men of the time esteemed him for this.
entries.literal: Men of the time for this held him in esteem.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：綦儁遭逢受職；
entries.en: The historian writes: Qi Jun met with opportunity and took office;
entries.literal: The historian says: Qi Jun encountered fortune and received office;

entries.zh: 山偉位行頗爽；
entries.en: Shan Wei's rank and conduct were fairly upright;
entries.literal: Shan Wei's position and conduct were rather upright;

entries.zh: 仁之雖內懷矯詐，而交情自篤；
entries.en: Renzhi, though inwardly deceitful, was steadfast in friendship;
entries.literal: Renzhi, though inwardly harboring deceit and craft, was earnest in friendship;

entries.zh: 忠之雖文史足用，而雅道蔑聞。
entries.en: Zhongzhi, though competent in letters and history, showed no trace of refined conduct.
entries.literal: Zhongzhi, though sufficient in belles-lettres and history, showed no refinement of manner.

entries.zh: 謂全德者，其難矣哉！
entries.en: To call any of them wholly virtuous—how difficult indeed!
entries.literal: To call any of them fully virtuous—how difficult!

entries.zh: 尒朱榮之害朝士，偉時守直，故免禍。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered court officials, Wei happened to be on straight duty and so escaped harm.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Rong killed court gentlemen, Wei was then on straight duty and therefore escaped disaster.

entries.zh: 及莊帝入宮，仍除偉給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuang took the palace, Wei was made gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuang entered the palace, Wei was still made gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.

entries.zh: 先是，偉與儀曹郎袁昇、屯田郎李延孝、外兵郎李奐、三公郎王延業方駕而行，偉少居後。
entries.en: Earlier Wei had been riding with Ritual Director Yuan Sheng, Field Director Li Yanxiao, External Troops Director Li Huan, and Three Ducal Houses Director Wang Yanye; Wei, being the youngest, trailed behind.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wei had been riding abreast with Ritual Director Yuan Sheng, Field Director Li Yanxiao, External Troops Director Li Huan, and Three Ducal Houses Director Wang Yanye—Wei, being younger, lagged behind.

entries.zh: 路逢一尼，望之歎曰：「此輩緣業，同日而死。」
entries.en: On the road they met a nun who looked at them and sighed: "These men's karmic lot binds them to die on the same day."
entries.literal: On the road they met a nun, who looked at them and sighed: "This group's karmic lot is to die on the same day."

entries.zh: 謂偉曰：「君方近天子，當作好官。」
entries.en: She said to Wei: "You are about to draw near the Son of Heaven—you will hold a fine office."
entries.literal: She said to Wei: "You will soon be near the Son of Heaven—take a good office."

entries.zh: 而昇等四人，皆於河陰遇害，果如其言。
entries.en: Sheng and the other three were all killed at Heyin, exactly as she had foretold.
entries.literal: Sheng and the other four all met their end at Heyin, exactly as she had said.

entries.zh: 俄領著作郎。
entries.en: Before long he headed the Bureau of Compilation.
entries.literal: Before long he headed the Bureau of Compilation.

entries.zh: 前廢帝立，除安東將軍、祕書監，仍著作。
entries.en: When the former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, he was made general who pacifies the east and supervisor of the secretariat while still heading compilation.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor of Former times was enthroned, he was made general who pacifies the east and supervisor of the secretariat, while still compiling.

entries.zh: 初，尒朱兆之入洛，官守奔散，國史典書高法顯密埋史書，故不遺落。
entries.en: When Erzhu Zhao first entered Luoyang, officials fled in disorder; state historian and keeper of the canon Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical records, so nothing was lost.
entries.literal: At first, when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, guards of office scattered in flight; the state historian and keeper of canon Gao Faxian secretly buried the historical writings, so nothing was lost.

entries.zh: 偉自以為功，訴求爵賞。
entries.en: Wei claimed the credit for himself and petitioned for rank and reward.
entries.literal: Wei took this as his own merit and petitioned for rank and reward.

entries.zh: 偉挾附世隆，遂封東阿縣伯，而法顯止獲男爵。
entries.en: Wei relied on Shilong's patronage and was enfeoffed Baron of Dong'e, while Faxian received only a baron's rank.
entries.literal: Wei leaned on Shilong's favor and was enfeoffed Baron of Dong'e, while Faxian received only a male noble rank.

entries.zh: 偉尋進侍中。
entries.en: Wei was soon promoted to palace attendant.
entries.literal: Wei was soon advanced to palace attendant.

entries.zh: 孝靜初，除衞大將軍、中書令、監起居。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was made grand general of the guard, director of the secretariat, and overseer of the imperial diary.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing, he was made grand general of the guard, director of the secretariat, and overseer of the imperial diary.

entries.zh: 後以本官復領著作，卒官。
entries.en: Later, while still holding those posts, he again headed compilation and died in office.
entries.literal: Later, in that same office, he again headed compilation and died in office.

entries.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督、幽州刺史，諡曰文貞公。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand general of agile cavalry, bearer of the open bureau with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, and governor of You Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wenzhen.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given grand general of agile cavalry, open bureau with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, governor of You Province; his posthumous title was Duke Wenzhen.

entries.zh: 字文忠之，河南洛陽人也。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhongzhi was from Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Yuwen Zhongzhi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 其先南單于之遠屬，世據東部，後入居代都。
entries.en: His ancestors were distant kin of the southern Chanyu; for generations they held the eastern territories, later settling at the Dai capital.
entries.literal: His forebears were distant kin of the southern Chanyu; for generations they held the eastern regions, later entering to dwell at the Dai capital.

entries.zh: 祖阿生，安南將軍，巴西公。
entries.en: His grandfather Asheng was general who pacifies the south and Duke of Brazil.
entries.literal: His grandfather Asheng was general who pacifies the south and Duke of Brazil.

entries.zh: 父侃，卒於治書侍御史。
entries.en: His father Kan died while serving as editorial court attendant.
entries.literal: His father Kan died while serving as attendant at the editorial court.

entries.zh: 忠之獵涉文史，頗有筆札，釋褐太學博士。
entries.en: Zhongzhi read widely in literature and history, wrote competently, and on entering office was made erudite of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: Zhongzhi ranged through belles-lettres and history, had considerable brushwork, and on leaving the sackcloth was made erudite of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 天平初，除中書侍郎。
entries.en: At the start of the Tianping era he was made attendant of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was made attendant of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 裴伯茂與之同省，常侮忽之，以忠之色黑，呼為「黑宇」。
entries.en: Pei Bomao served in the same bureau and often slighted him; because Zhongzhi was dark-skinned, he nicknamed him "Black Yu."
entries.literal: Pei Bomao was in the same bureau with him and often treated him with contempt; because Zhong was dark in complexion, he called him "Black Yu."

entries.zh: 後敕修國史。
entries.en: Later he received orders to compile the national history.
entries.literal: Later he was ordered to revise the national history.

entries.zh: 元象初，兼通直散騎常侍，副鄭伯猷使蕭衍。
entries.en: At the start of the Yuanxiang era he served concurrently as regular attendant of direct communication at scattered cavalry and accompanied Zheng Boyou on a mission to Xiao Yan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he concurrently served as regular attendant of direct communication at scattered cavalry and accompanied Zheng Boyou on a mission to Xiao Yan.

entries.zh: 武定初，為安南將軍、尚書右丞，仍修史。
entries.en: At the start of Wuding he was made general who pacifies the south and right vice director of the Masters of Writing while still compiling history.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was made general who pacifies the south and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, while still revising history.

entries.zh: 未幾，以事除名。
entries.en: Before long he was dismissed and stripped of rank because of an offense.
entries.literal: Before long, because of an affair he was stripped of name and rank.

entries.zh: 忠之好榮利，自為中書郎，六七年矣，遇尚書省選右丞，預選者皆射策，忠之入試焉。
entries.en: Zhongzhi loved rank and profit; he had been an attendant of the secretariat for six or seven years when the Masters of Writing selected a right vice director—all candidates took the archery examination—and Zhongzhi entered the competition.
entries.literal: Zhongzhi loved glory and profit; since becoming attendant of the secretariat six or seven years had passed, when the Masters of Writing bureau selected a right vice director—all candidates shot arrows at targets in examination—and Zhongzhi entered the test.

entries.zh: 既獲丞職，大為忻滿，志氣囂然，有驕物之色，識者笑之。
entries.en: Once he won the vice director post he was elated, swaggering with arrogant airs and a look that scorned others—those who knew him laughed.
entries.literal: Having obtained the vice director post, he was greatly pleased and satisfied, his spirit arrogant, with a look that despised things—those who knew him laughed.

entries.zh: 既失官爵，怏怏發病卒。
entries.en: After losing his office and rank he fell ill with resentment and died.
entries.literal: Having lost office and rank, he died resentfully of illness.

entries.zh: 子君山。
entries.en: His son Junshan.
entries.literal: His son Junshan.

entries.zh: 景所著述數百篇，見行於世，刪正晉司空張華博物志及撰儒林、列女傳各數十篇云。
entries.en: Jing's writings numbered several hundred pieces in circulation; he revised the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Records of Broad Learning and is said to have compiled several dozen chapters each of Biographies of Confucian Scholars and Biographies of Exemplary Women.
entries.literal: Jing's compositions numbered several hundred pieces circulating in the world; he edited and corrected the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Bowuzhi and compiled several dozen chapters each of the Rulin and Lienv Zhuan, it is said.

entries.zh: 李琰之 祖瑩 常景
entries.en: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, and Chang Jing
entries.literal: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, Chang Jing

entries.zh: 子暉，字宣明，后母弟也。
entries.en: His son Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, was the empress's younger uterine brother.
entries.literal: His son Hui, styled Xuanming, was the empress's younger uterine brother.

entries.zh: 少有氣幹。
entries.en: From youth he showed force of character and ability.
entries.literal: In youth he had spirit and capacity.

entries.zh: 襲爵，位汾州刺史。
entries.en: He inherited the family title and served as Governor of Fenzhou.
entries.literal: He inherited the title and held the post of Governor of Fenzhou.

entries.zh: 暉善事人，為尒朱榮所親，以女妻其子長孺。
