entries.en: Hui was skilled at winning people over. Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter as wife for his son Changru.
entries.literal: Hui was skilled at winning people; Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter in marriage to his son Changru.

entries.zh: 歷侍中、河南尹，後兼尚書僕射、東南道行臺。
entries.en: He served in turn as Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.
entries.literal: He successively held Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan; later he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.

entries.zh: 與齊獻武王討平羊侃於兗州。
entries.en: Together with Prince of Qi Who Offered the Kingdom, he put down Yang Kan's rebellion in Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Together with the Prince of Qi Who Offered the Kingdom, he suppressed and pacified Yang Kan in Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 元顥入洛，害之。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he had Hui killed.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he killed him.

entries.zh: 長子彧，字子文，尚莊帝姊豐亭公主。
entries.en: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, married the Princess of Fengting, Emperor Zhuang's elder sister.
entries.literal: His eldest son was Yu, styled Ziwen, who married the Princess of Fengting, Emperor Zhuang's elder sister.

entries.zh: 封東平郡公，位侍中、左光祿大夫、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Rapid Cavalry General, Honored with the Three Insignia and establishment of a headquarters, and Governor of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Rapid Cavalry General, and establishment of a headquarters with the Three Insignia, and Governor of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 彧任俠交遊，輕薄無行。
entries.en: Yu was a chivalric rover who made many friends but was frivolous and dissolute.
entries.literal: Yu was chivalrous and fond of making friends, frivolous and without proper conduct.

entries.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，武毅之士皆彧所進。
entries.en: When Erzhu Rong died, the bold warriors who struck him down had all been introduced by Yu.
entries.literal: At the death of Erzhu Rong, the martial and resolute men had all been introduced by Yu.

entries.zh: 孝靜初，以罪棄市。
entries.en: Early in the Xiaojing era he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign, he was executed by public display in the marketplace for his crimes.

entries.zh: 高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延寔
entries.en: Gao Zhao; Yu Jin; Hu Guozhen; Li Yanshi
entries.literal: Gao Zhao; Yu Jin; Hu Guozhen; Li Yanshi

entries.zh: 夫文之為用，其來日久。
entries.en: Literature has served human purposes for a very long time.
entries.literal: As for the use of literature, its coming has been long.

entries.zh: 自昔聖達之作，賢哲之書，莫不統理成章，蘊氣標致，其流廣變，諸非一貫，文質推移，與時俱化。
entries.en: Since antiquity, the writings of the greatest sages and the books of the wisest minds have all been shaped into coherent form, charged with spirit and distinguished by style. Their currents spread and change in many ways rather than following a single line; elegance and plainness evolve as literature keeps pace with the times.
entries.literal: From of old the works of sages and worthies and the books of the wise have all been ordered into chapters, imbued with spirit and marked by style; their currents are broad and varied and not of one tradition; substance and ornament shift and transform with the age.

entries.zh: 淳于出齊，有雕龍之目；
entries.en: When Chunyu emerged from Qi, he possessed the discerning eye celebrated in the title Carving the Dragon;
entries.literal: Chunyu came forth from Qi and had the eyes of the Carved Dragon;

entries.zh: 靈均逐楚，著嘉禍之章。
entries.en: Qu Yuan was banished from Chu and wrote his celebrated piece on the noble orange.
entries.literal: Lingjun was banished from Chu and composed the chapter of auspicious calamity.

entries.zh: [2]漢之西京，馬揚為首稱；
entries.en: In the Western Capital of the Han, Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong were the leading names;
entries.literal: In the Western Capital of Han, Sima and Yang were foremost in renown;

entries.zh: 東都之下，班張為雄伯。
entries.en: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban Gu and Zhang Heng were the reigning masters.
entries.literal: Under the Eastern Capital, Ban and Zhang were the heroic lords.

entries.zh: 曹植信魏世之英，陸機則晉朝之秀，雖同時並列，分途爭遠。
entries.en: Cao Zhi was truly the genius of the Wei, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though contemporaries, they pursued diverging paths to ever greater distance.
entries.literal: Cao Zhi was truly the hero of Wei times, and Lu Ji the outstanding talent of the Jin; though standing at the same time, they contested along separate paths to ever greater distance.

entries.zh: 永嘉之後，天下分崩，夷狄交馳，文章殄滅。
entries.en: After the Yongjia turmoil, the empire fell apart, foreign peoples surged one after another, and literary culture was nearly extinguished.
entries.literal: After the Yongjia era, the realm fragmented, barbarians rode in succession, and belles-lettres perished.

entries.zh: 昭成、太祖之世，南收燕趙，網羅俊乂。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhaocheng and Emperor Daowu, the court recovered Yan and Zhao in the south and gathered men of outstanding talent.
entries.literal: In the reigns of Zhaocheng and Taizu, they gathered Yan and Zhao to the south and netted outstanding men.

entries.zh: 逮高祖馭天，銳情文學，蓋以頡頏漢徹，掩踔曹丕，氣韻高豔，才藻獨構。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowen came to the throne, he threw himself into literature, in spirit rivaling Emperor Wu of Han and outshining Cao Pi, with a lofty tone, brilliant style, and literary gifts all his own.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took Heaven's mandate, he was keen on literature, roughly rivaling Han Wudi, surpassing Cao Pi, with lofty spirit and brilliant ornament and literary talent uniquely formed.

entries.zh: 衣冠仰止，咸慕新風。
entries.en: Men of culture looked up to him, and all were drawn to the new literary current he set.
entries.literal: The gentry looked up and all admired the new style.

entries.zh: 肅宗歷位，文雅大盛，學者如牛毛，成者如麟角，孔子曰：「才難，不其然乎？」
entries.en: Under Emperor Suzong, literary culture flourished as never before: students were as numerous as ox hairs, but those who truly succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is that not exactly the case?"
entries.literal: When Emperor Suzong held the throne, refinement flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns. Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find—is it not so?"

entries.zh: 袁躍，字景騰，陳郡人，尚書翻弟也。
entries.en: Yuan Yue, whose style was Jingteng, came from Chen commandery and was the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.
entries.literal: Yuan Yue, style name Jingteng, was a man of Chen commandery and the younger brother of Minister Yuan Fan.

entries.zh: 博學儁才，性不矯俗，篤於交友。
entries.en: He was widely learned and exceptionally gifted, unpretentious by nature, and deeply loyal to his friends.
entries.literal: He was broadly learned and outstanding in talent, by nature not given to affectation, and devoted in friendship.

entries.zh: 翻每謂人曰：「躍可謂我家千里駒也。」
entries.en: Fan often told others, "Yue may truly be called the thousand-li steed of our clan."
entries.literal: Fan often said to people, "Yue may be called the thousand-li colt of our house."

entries.zh: 釋褐司空行參軍，歷位尚書都兵郎中，加員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He began his career as acting adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose to director of arms in the Ministry of Works, and was later given the additional title of supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: He took his first office as Acting Adjutant in the Bureau of the Minister of Works, rose through posts to Director of Arms in the Ministry of Works, and was additionally made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 將立明堂，躍乃上議，當時稱其博洽。
entries.en: When the court was preparing to build the Bright Hall, Yue submitted a memorial on the subject, and contemporaries praised his encyclopedic learning.
entries.literal: When the Bright Hall was about to be established, Yue submitted a memorial of discussion, and at the time he was praised as broadly versed.

entries.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瓌亡破來奔，朝廷矜之，送復其國。
entries.en: Anagui, ruler of the Rouran, fled to the court after his state was destroyed; the court took pity on him and helped restore his kingdom.
entries.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui, destroyed and fleeing, came to surrender; the court took pity on him and sent him back to restore his state.

entries.zh: 既而每使朝貢，辭旨頗不盡禮。
entries.en: Afterward, whenever he sent tribute missions, their language was often less than fully respectful.
entries.literal: Thereafter, whenever he sent tribute missions, their wording was rather lacking in courtesy.

entries.zh: 躍為朝臣書與瓌，陳以禍福，言辭甚美。
entries.en: Yue drafted a letter from the court ministers to Anagui, explaining the consequences of fortune and disaster in language of exceptional elegance.
entries.literal: Yue wrote on behalf of the court ministers to Gui, setting forth fortune and calamity; the language was very fine.

entries.zh: 後遷車騎將軍、太傅、清河王懌文學，雅為懌所愛賞。
entries.en: He was later appointed literary aide to Prince Yi of Qinghe, who also held the posts of general of chariots and cavalry and grand tutor, and Yi greatly favored and admired him.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to literary aide to the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Qinghe, Yuan Yi, and was greatly loved and rewarded by Yi.

entries.zh: 懌之文表多出於躍。
entries.en: Most of Yi's official documents and memorials were written by Yue.
entries.literal: Yi's literary memorials and proclamations mostly came from Yue.

entries.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、吏部郎中。
entries.en: When he died, he was posthumously honored as champion general and director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously given the titles Champion General and Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 所制文集行於世。
entries.en: His collected writings circulated widely.
entries.literal: The collected writings he composed circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 無子，兄翻以子聿脩繼。
entries.en: He left no son; his elder brother Fan had his own son Yuxiu succeed him.
entries.literal: He had no son; his elder brother Fan made his son Yuxiu the heir.

entries.zh: 邢臧，字子良，河間人，光祿少卿虬長孫也。
entries.en: Xing Cang, whose style was Ziliang, came from Hejian and was the eldest grandson of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Xing Qiu.
entries.literal: Xing Cang, style name Ziliang, was a man of Hejian and the eldest grandson of Vice Director of the Imperial Household Xing Qiu.

entries.zh: 幼孤，早立操尚，博學有藻思。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he early formed a strong moral character, was widely learned, and possessed a refined literary mind.
entries.literal: Orphaned in youth, he early established moral resolve, was broadly learned and had literary thought.

entries.zh: 年二十一，神龜中，舉秀才，問策五條，考上第，為太學博士。
entries.en: At twenty-one, during the Shengui era, he was recommended as a cultivated talent; on five policy questions he placed at the top and was appointed erudite of the Imperial Academy.
entries.literal: At twenty-one, in the Shengui era, he was recommended as a cultivated talent; on five policy questions he ranked at the top and was made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

entries.zh: 正光中，議立明堂，臧為裴頠一室之議，事雖不行，當時稱其理博。
entries.en: During the Zhenguang era, when the court debated building the Bright Hall, Cang drafted the one-room proposal associated with Pei Zhi; though the plan was not adopted, contemporaries praised the breadth of his reasoning.
entries.literal: In the Zhenguang era, when the Bright Hall was debated, Cang drafted Pei Zhi's one-room proposal; though the matter was not carried out, at the time his reasoning was praised as broad.

entries.zh: 出為本州中從事，雅為鄉情所附。
entries.en: He was sent out as central assistant of his native province and was warmly supported by local opinion.
entries.literal: He went out as Central Assistant of his native province and was gracefully attached to by local sentiment.

entries.zh: 永安初，徵為金部郎中，以疾不赴，轉除東牟太守。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was summoned as director of the gold bureau but declined because of illness; he was then transferred and appointed administrator of Dongmou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was summoned as Director of the Gold Bureau but did not go because of illness; he was transferred and made Administrator of Dongmou.

entries.zh: 時天下多事，在職少能廉白，臧獨清慎奉法，吏民愛之。
entries.en: The realm was in turmoil, and few officials could remain honest and upright; Cang alone was scrupulous and law-abiding, and both clerks and common people admired him.
entries.literal: At the time the realm had many troubles; few in office could be pure and upright, but Cang alone was clear, cautious, and observant of law, and officials and people loved him.

entries.zh: 隴西李延寔，莊帝之舅，以太傅出除青州，啟臧為屬，領樂安內史，有惠政。
entries.en: Li Yanshi of Longxi, Emperor Xiaozhuang's maternal uncle, left the capital as grand tutor to take up Qingzhou; he recommended Cang as his aide and had him serve concurrently as interior secretary of Le'an, where he governed with benevolence.
entries.literal: Li Yanshi of Longxi, the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaozhuang, went out as Grand Tutor to Qingzhou, recommended Cang as aide, and had him lead as Interior Secretary of Le'an, with benevolent administration.

entries.zh: 後除濮陽太守，尋加安東將軍。
entries.en: He was later appointed administrator of Puyang and soon given the additional title of pacifier of the east general.
entries.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Puyang and soon additionally given the title Pacifier of the East General.

entries.zh: 臧和雅信厚，有長者之風，為時人所愛敬。
entries.en: Cang was gentle, refined, trustworthy, and generous, with the bearing of a man of mature virtue, and was loved and respected by his contemporaries.
entries.literal: Cang was harmonious, refined, faithful, and generous, with the bearing of an elder, and was loved and respected by people of the age.

entries.zh: 為特進甄琛行狀，世稱其工。
entries.en: He wrote the conduct account for Zhen Chen, holder of special advancement, and contemporaries praised its craftsmanship.
entries.literal: He composed the conduct account for Special Advancement Zhen Chen, and the age praised its craftsmanship.

entries.zh: 與裴敬憲、盧觀兄弟並結交分，曾共讀回文集，臧獨先通之。
entries.en: He formed close friendships with Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan; they once read Feng Hui's collected writings together, and Cang alone mastered them first.
entries.literal: With Pei Jingxian and the brothers Lu Guan he formed bonds of friendship; they once together read Hui's collected writings, and Cang alone first mastered them.

entries.zh: 撰古來文章，并敍作者氏族，號曰文譜，未就，病卒，時賢悼惜之。
entries.en: He was compiling writings from antiquity to his own day, with notes on each author's clan and lineage, under the title Literary Genealogy; he died of illness before finishing it, and leading men of the day deeply mourned the loss.
entries.literal: He compiled writings from antiquity to the present and also narrated authors' clans and surnames, calling it the Literary Genealogy; it was unfinished when he died of illness, and worthies of the time mourned and regretted it.

entries.zh: 其文筆凡百餘篇。
entries.en: His literary pieces altogether numbered more than a hundred.
entries.literal: His literary pieces altogether numbered more than a hundred.

entries.zh: 贈鎮北將軍、定州刺史，諡曰文。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as pacifier of the north general and governor of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given Pacifier of the North General and Governor of Dingzhou, posthumous name Wen.

entries.zh: 邢昕，字子明，河間人，尚書巒弟偉之子。
entries.en: Xing Xin, styled Ziming, was a native of Hejian and the son of Wei, younger brother of Minister Luan.
entries.literal: Xing Xin, styled Ziming, a man of Hejian, was son of Wei, younger brother of Luan, Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 幼孤，見愛於祖母李氏。
entries.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was doted on by his grandmother, Lady Li.
entries.literal: Orphaned young, he was cherished by his grandmother Lady Li.

entries.zh: 好學，早有才情。
entries.en: He loved learning and displayed literary talent from an early age.
entries.literal: He loved study and showed literary talent early.

entries.zh: 蕭寶夤以車騎大將軍開府討關中，以子明為東閤祭酒，委以文翰。
entries.en: When Xiao Baoyin opened a field headquarters as Cavalry General-in-Chief to campaign in Guanzhong, he appointed Ziming Eastern Pavilion Libationer and entrusted him with official correspondence.
entries.literal: When Xiao Baoyin served as Cavalry General-in-Chief with an open headquarters to campaign against Guanzhong, he made Ziming Eastern Pavilion Libationer and entrusted him with literary documents.

entries.zh: 在軍解褐盪寇將軍，累遷太尉記室參軍。
entries.en: While on campaign he entered official service as Campaign General Who Quells Banditry and was promoted step by step to Army Aide of Record to the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: In the army he doffed his plain robe as Campaign General Who Quells Banditry; he was promoted repeatedly to Army Aide of Record to the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁奏昕修起居注。
entries.en: Li Shenjun, Minister of the Personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the imperial diary.
entries.literal: Li Shenjun, Minister of the Personnel, memorialized that Xin should compile the Veritable Records.

entries.zh: 太昌初，除中書侍郎，加平東將軍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Taichang era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat with the additional ranks of General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, with additional titles as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 時言冒竊官級，為中尉所劾，免官，乃為述躬賦。
entries.en: Rumors then claimed he had fraudulently taken another's rank; impeached by the Commandant of Justice, he was dismissed from office and wrote the "Fu on Embodying Oneself."
entries.literal: At the time it was said he had usurped others' ranks; the Commandant of Justice impeached him, he was dismissed, and he then wrote the "Fu on Embodying Oneself."

entries.zh: 未幾，受詔與祕書監常景典儀注事。
entries.en: Before long he received an edict to oversee ritual regulations together with Chang Jing, Director of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: Before long, he received an edict jointly with Chang Jing, Director of the Palace Library, to oversee ritual regulations.

entries.zh: 出帝行釋奠禮，昕與校書郎裴伯茂等俱為錄義。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor performed the Confucian temple sacrifice, Xin together with Collator Pei Bomao and others served as recorders of the rites.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor performed the Confucian sacrifice, Xin together with Collator Pei Bomao and others all served as recorders of the exposition.

entries.zh: 永熙末，昕入為侍讀，與溫子昇、魏收參掌文詔。
entries.en: At the end of the Yongxi era, Xin entered court as Reader-in-Waiting and, together with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou, shared responsibility for edicts and imperial documents.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongxi, Xin entered court as Reader-in-Waiting, and with Wen Zisheng and Wei Shou jointly managed edicts and memorials.

entries.zh: 遷鄴，乃歸河間。
entries.en: When the capital was moved to Ye, he returned to Hejian.
entries.literal: When the capital moved to Ye, he returned to Hejian.

entries.zh: 天平初，與侍中從叔子才、魏季景、魏收同徵赴都。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianping he was summoned to the capital together with Palace Attendant and paternal uncle Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was summoned to the capital together with Palace Attendant and clan uncle Zicai, Wei Jijing, and Wei Shou.

entries.zh: 尋還鄉里。
entries.en: Before long he returned home.
entries.literal: Before long he returned to his native district.

entries.zh: 既而復徵。
entries.en: He was summoned again not long after.
entries.literal: Afterward he was summoned again.

entries.zh: 時蕭衍使兼散騎常侍劉孝儀等來朝貢，詔昕兼正員郎迎於境上。
entries.en: At that time envoys from Xiao Yan, including Vice Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds Liu Xiaoyi, came bearing tribute; an edict made Xin Acting Regular Gentleman to receive them at the frontier.
entries.literal: At the time Xiao Yan's envoys, including Vice Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds Liu Xiaoyi, came to court with tribute; an edict appointed Xin Acting Regular Gentleman to welcome them at the border.

entries.zh: 司徒孫騰引為中郎。
entries.en: Minister of Education Sun Teng recommended him as Palace Gentleman.
entries.literal: Minister of Education Sun Teng recommended him as Gentleman of the Palace.

entries.zh: 尋除通直常侍，加中軍將軍。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Service with the additional rank of General of the Central Army.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Service, with the additional rank of General of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 既有才藻，兼長几案。
entries.en: He possessed both literary brilliance and administrative competence at the desk.
entries.literal: He had both literary talent and skill at desk work.

entries.zh: 自孝昌之後，天下多務，世人競以吏工取達，文學大衰。
entries.en: After the Xiaochang era the empire was overwhelmed with affairs, and men competed to rise through bureaucratic skill while literary learning sharply declined.
entries.literal: From Xiaochang onward the realm was burdened with tasks, and people in the world competed to advance through bureaucratic craft, while letters and learning greatly declined.

entries.zh: 司州中從事宋遊道以公斷見知，時與昕嘲謔。
entries.en: Song Youdao, Secretariat Aide of Sizhou, was known for fair-minded decisiveness; he and Xin often exchanged witty taunts.
entries.literal: Song Youdao, secretariat aide of the provincial inspectorate of Sizhou, was known for fair judgment; at the time he and Xin would banter and joke.

entries.zh: 昕謂之曰：「世事同知文學外。」
entries.en: Xin told him, "In worldly affairs one must know what lies beyond letters."
entries.literal: Xin said to him: "In worldly affairs one must know what lies outside literature."

entries.zh: 遊道有慚色。
entries.en: Youdao flushed with embarrassment.
entries.literal: Youdao showed an ashamed countenance.

entries.zh: 興和中，以本官副李象使於蕭衍。
entries.en: In the Xinghe era he served as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Xiao Yan, retaining his existing post.
entries.literal: In Xinghe, with his existing office he served as deputy to Li Xiang on a mission to Xiao Yan.

entries.zh: 昕好忤物，人謂之牛。
entries.en: Xin was fond of crossing others; people nicknamed him the Ox.
entries.literal: Xin loved to go against others; people called him the Ox.

entries.zh: 是行也，談者謂之牛象鬬於江南。
entries.en: On that mission, observers quipped that an ox and an elephant were fighting south of the Yangtze.
entries.literal: On this journey, gossips called it an Ox and Elephant fighting south of the Yangtze.

entries.zh: 齊文襄王攝選，擬昕為司徒右長史，未奏，遇疾卒，士友悲之。
entries.en: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi oversaw appointments, he proposed Xin as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; before the nomination reached the throne, Xin fell ill and died, to the grief of his peers.
entries.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi acted as regent in selections, he proposed Xin as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; before the memorial was submitted, Xin fell ill and died, and gentlemen mourned him.

entries.zh: 贈車騎將軍、都官尚書、冀州刺史，諡曰文。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Cavalry General-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, and Inspector of Jizhou with the posthumous title Wen.
entries.literal: Posthumously made Cavalry General-in-Chief, Minister of Justice, Inspector of Jizhou, posthumous title Wen.

entries.zh: 所著文章，自有集錄。
entries.en: His writings were gathered in a collected anthology.
entries.literal: His literary writings were collected in their own anthology.

entries.zh: 正光末，廣陽王淵為東北道行臺，召為郎中，軍國文翰皆出其手。
entries.en: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander and summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state papers came from his hand.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhengguang, Prince Yuan of Guangyang served as Northeast Circuit Commander; he summoned Zisheng as Gentleman; all military and state documents issued from his hand.

entries.zh: 於是才名轉盛。
entries.en: His fame for talent then grew still greater.
entries.literal: Thereupon his fame for talent grew still greater.

entries.zh: 黃門郎徐紇受四方表啟，答之敏速，於淵獨沉思曰：「彼有溫郎中，才藻可畏。」
entries.en: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four quarters and answered them swiftly; facing Yuan alone he mused and said, "They have Gentleman Wen on staff—his literary power inspires dread."
entries.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Hong received memorials from the four directions and answered swiftly; facing Yuan alone he pondered and said: "They have Gentleman Wen there—his literary talent is formidable."

entries.zh: 高車破走，珍實盈滿，子昇取絹四十匹。
entries.en: When the Gaoche were routed, booty filled the tents; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.
entries.literal: When the Gaoche were routed and fled, treasures filled the camp; Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 及淵為葛榮所害，子昇亦見羈執。
entries.en: When Yuan was slain by Ge Rong, Zisheng too was seized and detained.
entries.literal: When Yuan was killed by Ge Rong, Zisheng was also seized and held.

entries.zh: 榮下都督和洛興與子昇舊識，以數十騎潛送子昇，得達冀州。
entries.en: Heluo Xing, a subordinate commander under Rong and an old acquaintance of Zisheng, secretly escorted him with several dozen horsemen until he reached Jizhou.
entries.literal: Ge Rong's subordinate commander Heluo Xing was an old acquaintance of Zisheng; with several dozen horsemen he secretly sent Zisheng off, enabling him to reach Jizhou.

entries.zh: 還京，李楷執其手曰：「卿今得免，足使夷甫慚德。」
entries.en: On returning to the capital, Li Kai grasped his hand and said, "You have come through alive—enough to make Yifu blush for his character."
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, Li Kai took his hand and said: "You have now escaped—enough to make Yifu ashamed of his virtue."

entries.zh: 自是無復宦情，閉門讀書，厲精不已。
entries.en: From then on he lost all desire for office, shut his door to read, and honed his mind without cease.
entries.literal: From then on he had no further desire for office, shut his door and read books, and refined his mind without cease.

entries.zh: 及帝殺尒朱榮也，子昇預謀，當時赦詔，子昇詞也。
entries.en: When the Emperor killed Erzhu Rong, Zisheng took part in the plot; the amnesty edict of that hour was in Zisheng's words.
entries.literal: When the Emperor killed Erzhu Rong, Zisheng took part in the plot; the amnesty edict of the time was Zisheng's wording.

entries.zh: 榮入內，遇子昇，把詔書問是何文書，子昇顏色不變，曰「敕」。
entries.en: Rong entered the inner quarters, met Zisheng, seized the edict and asked what document it was; Zisheng's expression did not change as he answered, "An imperial order."
entries.literal: Rong entered within; he met Zisheng, seized the edict and asked what document it was; Zisheng's countenance did not change, saying "An imperial order."

entries.zh: 榮不視之。
entries.en: Rong did not read it.
entries.literal: Rong did not look at it.

entries.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，子昇懼禍逃匿。
entries.en: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zisheng feared calamity and hid himself.
entries.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zisheng feared disaster and went into hiding.

entries.zh: 永熙中，為侍讀兼舍人、鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，遷散騎常侍、中軍大將軍，後領本州大中正。
entries.en: In Yongxi he served as Reader-in-Waiting with concurrent duty as Drafting Officer, General Who Guards the South, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel; he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds and Great General of the Central Army, and later headed the senior clan scorer for his native province.
entries.literal: In Yongxi he was Reader-in-Waiting concurrent Drafting Officer, General Who Guards the South, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel; promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds and Great General of the Central Army; later he headed the senior clan scorer for his native province.

entries.zh: 蕭衍使張皐寫子昇文筆，傳於江外。
entries.en: Xiao Yan had Zhang Gao copy Zisheng's writings, which circulated beyond the Yangtze.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan had Zhang Gao copy out Zisheng's writings, which spread beyond the river.

entries.zh: 衍稱之曰：「曹植、陸機復生於北土。
entries.en: Yan praised him, saying, "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji are reborn in the northern lands.
entries.literal: Yan praised him, saying: "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji are reborn in the northern lands.

entries.zh: 恨我辭人，數窮百六。」
entries.en: I only regret that among my literary men fortune has been broken by repeated calamity."
entries.literal: I regret that among my men of letters the count has been exhausted by the cycle of calamity."

entries.zh: 陽夏太守傅標使吐谷渾，見其國主牀頭有書數卷，乃是子昇文也。
entries.en: Fu Biao, Administrator of Yangxia, on a mission to the Tuyuhun, saw several scrolls at the ruler's bedside—they were writings of Zisheng.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Yangxia, Fu Biao, on a mission to the Tuyuhun, saw several scrolls at the ruler's bedside—these were writings of Zisheng.

entries.zh: 濟陰王暉業嘗云：「江左文人，宋有顏延之、謝靈運，梁有沈約、任昉，我子昇足以陵顏轢謝，含任吐沈。」
entries.en: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said, "Among literati south of the Yangtze, Song had Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, Liang had Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng is enough to stride over Yan and trample Xie, encompass Ren and surpass Shen."
entries.literal: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said: "Among men of letters south of the Yangtze, in Song there were Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, in Liang there were Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng suffices to tread upon Yan and crush Xie, swallow Ren and spit out Shen."

entries.zh: 楊遵彥作文德論，以為古今辭人皆負才遺行，澆薄險忌，唯邢子才、王元景、溫子昇彬彬有德素。
entries.en: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," arguing that writers of every age bore talent yet abandoned proper conduct—shallow, base, treacherous, and jealous—yet only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed genuine virtue.
entries.literal: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," holding that men of letters ancient and modern all bore talent yet cast off conduct, shallow, thin, treacherous, and jealous—only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were refined and possessed virtue and plainness.

entries.zh: 齊文襄王引子昇為大將軍府諮議參軍。
entries.en: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as Adviser of the Grand General's Headquarters.
entries.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as Adviser of the Grand General's Headquarters.

entries.zh: 子昇前為中書郎，嘗詣蕭衍客館受國書，自以不修容止，謂人曰：「詩章易作，逋峭難為。」
entries.en: Zisheng had previously served as Secretariat Gentleman and once went to Xiao Yan's guesthouse to receive the state letter; finding his bearing inadequate, he told others, "Poems are easy to write; striking presence is hard to manage."
entries.literal: Zisheng had earlier served as Secretariat Gentleman and once went to Xiao Yan's guest lodge to receive the state letter; thinking himself negligent in deportment, he told others: "Poems are easy to compose; a striking mien is hard to achieve."

entries.zh: 文襄館客元僅曰：「諸人當賀。」
entries.en: Yuan Jin, a retainer at Wenxiang's residence, said, "Everyone ought to congratulate."
entries.literal: Yuan Jin, a client of Wenxiang's lodge, said: "Everyone should congratulate."

entries.zh: 推子昇合陳辭。
entries.en: They urged Zisheng to help draft the presentation speech.
entries.literal: They pressed Zisheng to join in composing the formal address.

entries.zh: 子昇久忸怩，乃推陸操焉。
entries.en: Zisheng hesitated for some time, then put forward Lu Cao in his stead.
entries.literal: Zisheng was bashful for a long time, then recommended Lu Cao instead.

entries.zh: 及元僅、劉思逸、荀濟等作亂，文襄疑子昇知其謀。
entries.en: When Yuan Jin, Liu Siyi, Xun Ji, and the others rose in revolt, Prince Wenxiang suspected that Zisheng had known of their conspiracy.
entries.literal: When Yuan Jin, Liu Siyi, Xun Ji, and others rebelled, Wenxiang suspected Zisheng knew their plot.

entries.zh: 方使之作獻武王碑文，既成，乃餓諸晉陽獄，食弊襦而死，棄尸路隅，沒其家口。
entries.en: He was just then having him write the inscription for King Xianwu. When it was done, he left him to starve in the Jinyang prison; he died gnawing rotten rags. His body was thrown by the road, and his entire household was seized.
entries.literal: He had just had him compose the stele text for King Xianwu; once it was finished, he starved him in the Jinyang prison; eating tattered clothes he died; his corpse was cast by the roadside; his household was confiscated.

entries.zh: 太尉長史宋遊道收葬之，又為集其文筆為三十五卷。
entries.en: Song Youdao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, recovered his body for burial and also collected his literary works into thirty-five scrolls.
entries.literal: Song Youdao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant, gathered and buried him, and also compiled his writings into thirty-five scrolls.

entries.zh: 子昇外恬靜，與物無競，言有準的，不妄毀譽，而內深險。
entries.en: Zisheng appeared outwardly serene and uncontentious; his speech was measured, and he did not praise or revile rashly—yet within he was profoundly cunning.
entries.literal: Outwardly Zisheng was calm and still, competing with nothing; his words had their mark; he did not rashly praise or blame—yet inwardly he was deeply treacherous.

entries.zh: 事故之際，好預其間，所以終致禍敗。
entries.en: When troubles arose, he liked to thrust himself into them—hence his final fall to ruin.
entries.literal: At times of incidents he liked to take part in them; and so he ultimately met calamity and ruin.

entries.zh: 又撰永安記三卷。
entries.en: He also wrote the Records of Yong'an in three scrolls.
entries.literal: He also compiled Records of Yong'an in three scrolls.

entries.zh: 無子。
entries.en: He left no sons.
entries.literal: He had no sons.

entries.zh: 文襄館客元僅曰諸人當賀按何事當賀，敍述不明，疑「文襄」下有脫文。
entries.en: "Yuan Jin, a retainer at Wenxiang's residence, said, 'Everyone ought to congratulate'"—Commentary: what there was to celebrate is nowhere made clear; the account is muddled. Text may be missing after "Wenxiang."
entries.literal: Wenxiang's lodge client Yuan Jin said everyone should congratulate—Commentary: what occasion to congratulate is unclear, narrative is obscure, suspect text missing after "Wenxiang".

entries.zh: 又「元僅」當作「元瑾」。
entries.en: Moreover, "Yuan Jin" written with the character jin (merely) should read "Yuan Jin" written with the character jin (gem).
entries.literal: Moreover, Yuan Jin written with the character jin (merely) should read Yuan Jin written with the character jin (gem).

entries.zh: 瑾謀殺高澄，事見本書卷一二孝靜紀末、卷一四華山王鷙附子大器傳，北史卷六齊文襄紀，北齊書卷四七宋遊道傳，都作「瑾」。
entries.en: Jin conspired to assassinate Gao Cheng; the episode appears in this book, volume 12 (end of the annals of Emperor Xiaojing), volume 14 (biography of Prince Huashan Zhi, with the attached biography of his son Daqi), Northern History, volume 6 (annals of Prince Wenxiang of Qi), and Northern Qi History, volume 47 (biography of Song Youdao)—all of which write the name with the character "jin" meaning gem.
entries.literal: Jin conspired to assassinate Gao Cheng; the episode appears in this book, volume 12 (end of the annals of Emperor Xiaojing), volume 14 (biography of Prince Huashan Zhi, with the attached biography of his son Daqi), Northern History, volume 6 (annals of Prince Wenxiang of Qi), and Northern Qi History, volume 47 (biography of Song Youdao)—all of which write the name with the character jin meaning gem.

entries.zh: 袁躍 裴敬憲 盧觀 封肅 邢臧 裴伯茂 邢昕 溫子昇
entries.en: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng
entries.literal: Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Cang, Pei Bomao, Xing Xin, Wen Zisheng

entries.zh: 趙琰，字叔起，天水人。
entries.en: Zhao Yan, courtesy name Shuqi, was from Tianshui.
entries.literal: Zhao Yan, styled Shuqi, was a man of Tianshui.

entries.zh: 父溫為楊難當司馬。
entries.en: His father Wen served as marshal under Yang Nanang.
entries.literal: His father Wen served as marshal to Yang Nanang.

entries.zh: 初，苻氏亂，琰為乳母攜奔壽春，年十四乃歸。
entries.en: When the Fu clan fell into chaos, Yan was carried off to Shouchun by his wet nurse and did not return until he was fourteen.
entries.literal: At first, during the Fu clan turmoil, Yan was taken in flight to Shouchun by his wet nurse and did not return until he was fourteen.

entries.zh: 孝心色養，飪熟之節，必親調之。
entries.en: He served his parents with filial devotion and attentive care for their comfort; whenever food was cooked and ready, he always seasoned it himself.
entries.literal: In filial devotion he attended to his parents' comfort and appearance; at the season when food was cooked and done, he always seasoned it himself.

entries.zh: 皇興中，京師儉，婢簡粟糶之，琰遇見切責，敕留輕粃。
entries.en: During the Huangxing period, when the capital was in want, a servant winnowed grain to sell. Yan happened upon her and rebuked her sharply, ordering her to leave only the light chaff.
entries.literal: In the Huangxing era, when the capital was straitened, a maid winnowed grain to sell; Yan chanced upon this and sternly rebuked her, ordering that only the light chaff be removed.

entries.zh: 嘗送子應冀州娉室，從者於路偶得一羊，[2]行三十里而琰知之，令送於本處。
entries.en: Once, while escorting his son Ying to Jizhou to fetch a bride, a follower on the road happened to obtain a sheep. After they had gone thirty li Yan learned of it and ordered the sheep returned to its owner.
entries.literal: Once, when escorting his son Ying to fetch a bride in Jizhou, a follower on the road happened upon a sheep; after thirty li Yan learned of it and ordered it returned to where it had been obtained.

entries.zh: 又過路傍，主人設羊羹，琰訪知盜殺，卒辭不食。
entries.en: On another occasion he passed a roadside inn whose host served mutton broth. Yan learned the sheep had been stolen and slaughtered, and at once declined to eat.
entries.literal: Again, passing a roadside host who set out mutton broth, Yan inquired and learned the animal had been stolen and killed; he thereupon declined and would not eat.

entries.zh: 遣人買耜刃，得剩六耜，即令送還刃主。
entries.en: He sent someone to buy plowshares and received six extra shares in the bargain; he immediately had them returned to the owner.
entries.literal: He sent someone to buy plowshares; receiving six extra shares, he at once had them returned to the share's owner.

entries.zh: 刃主高之，義而不受，琰命委之而去。
entries.en: The owner held him in esteem and on principle refused to take them back; Yan ordered the shares left with him and departed.
entries.literal: The owner admired this and on principle would not accept them; Yan ordered them deposited and departed.

entries.zh: 初為兗州司馬，轉團城鎮副將。
entries.en: He first served as marshal of Yanzhou, then was transferred to deputy commandant of Tuncheng garrison.
entries.literal: At first he was marshal of Yanzhou, then transferred to deputy commandant of Tuncheng garrison.

entries.zh: 還京，為淮南王他府長史。
entries.en: On returning to the capital he became chief clerk in the household of Prince Huainan Tuo.
entries.literal: Returning to the capital, he became chief clerk in the household of the Prince of Huainan, Tuo.

entries.zh: 時禁制甚嚴，不聽越關葬於舊兆。
entries.en: At that time restrictions were very strict, and burial at the old family tombs across the frontier was not permitted.
entries.literal: At that time prohibitions were very strict; crossing the frontier to bury at the old tombs was not permitted.

entries.zh: 琰積三十餘年，不得葬二親。
entries.en: For more than thirty years Yan could not bury his two parents.
entries.literal: For more than thirty years Yan could not bury his two parents.

entries.zh: 及蒸嘗拜獻，未曾不嬰慕卒事。
entries.en: At every seasonal offering and sacrifice, when the rites were finished he was never free of overwhelming grief.
entries.literal: At seasonal offerings and sacrifices he never failed, when the rites were completed, to be seized by longing and grief.

entries.zh: 每於時節，不受子孫慶賀。
entries.en: At each festival season he would not accept congratulations from his descendants.
entries.literal: At each festival he would not accept congratulations from his descendants.

entries.zh: 年餘耳順，而孝思彌篤。
entries.en: Though he was past sixty, his filial thoughts grew only more earnest.
entries.literal: Though he was past sixty, his thoughts of filial piety grew only more earnest.

entries.zh: 慨歲月推移，遷窆無期，乃絕鹽粟，斷諸滋味，食麥而已。
entries.en: Lamenting the passage of years and that reinterment had no fixed date, he gave up salt and grain, cut off all other flavors, and ate only wheat.
entries.literal: Lamenting the passage of years and that moving the coffins had no fixed date, he gave up salt and grain, cut off all flavorings, and ate only wheat.

entries.zh: 年八十卒。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: He died at eighty.

entries.zh: 遷都洛陽，遷都洛陽，子應等乃還鄉葬焉。
entries.en: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and his brothers were at last able to return home and bury their parents.
entries.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and the others were finally able to return home and bury them.

entries.zh: 應弟煦，字賓育。
entries.en: Ying's younger brother Xu, courtesy name Binyu.
entries.literal: Ying's younger brother Xu, styled Binyu.

entries.zh: 好音律，以善歌聞於世。
entries.en: He loved music and was renowned throughout the realm for his fine singing.
entries.literal: He loved music and was famed throughout the world for fine singing.

entries.zh: 位秦州刺史。
entries.en: He rose to the post of governor of Qinzhou.
entries.literal: He held the post of governor of Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 長孫慮，代人也。
entries.en: Zhangsun Lu was a man of Dai.
entries.literal: Zhangsun Lu, a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 母因飲酒，其父真呵叱之，誤以杖擊，便即致死。
entries.en: His mother had been drinking when his father Zhen scolded her; he mistakenly struck her with his staff and killed her on the spot.
entries.literal: His mother, having taken drink, was scolded by his father Zhen; he mistakenly struck her with his staff and at once caused her death.

entries.zh: 真為縣囚執，處以重坐。
entries.en: Zhen was seized as a county prisoner and sentenced to a heavy punishment.
entries.literal: Zhen was seized as a county prisoner and sentenced to a heavy penalty.

entries.zh: 慮列辭尚書云：「父母忿爭，本無餘惡。
entries.en: Lu submitted a petition to the Ministry of Works, saying: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is originally no deep malice.
entries.literal: Lu submitted a memorial to the Ministry of Works, saying: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is originally no deep malice.

entries.zh: 直以謬誤，一朝橫禍。
entries.en: It was only through a mistake that disaster struck in a single morning.
entries.literal: It was only through a blunder that calamity struck in a single morning.

entries.zh: 今母喪未殯，父命旦夕。
entries.en: Now my mother's body lies unburied, and my father's life hangs by a thread.
entries.literal: Now my mother's funeral is not yet prepared for burial, and my father's life hangs by a thread.

entries.zh: 慮兄弟五人，並各幼稚。
entries.en: We five brothers are each still young.
entries.literal: Lu and his brothers, five in all, are each still young.

entries.zh: 慮身居長，今年十五，有一女弟，始向四歲，更相鞠養，不能保全。
entries.en: I, Lu, am the eldest, fifteen this year, with one younger sister who has just turned four. If we must raise one another, we cannot keep everyone alive.
entries.literal: I, Lu, am the eldest, fifteen this year, with one younger sister just turning four; if we must rear one another, we cannot keep everyone safe.

entries.zh: 父若就刑，交墜溝壑，乞以身代老父命，使嬰弱眾孤得蒙存立。」
entries.en: If my father goes to execution, we will all fall into ditches and ravines. I beg to die in my aged father's place, so that the infants and many orphans may be allowed to live."
entries.literal: If my father goes to execution, we will all fall into ditches and gullies; I beg to take my aged father's place in death, so that the infants and the many orphans may be granted survival."

entries.zh: 尚書奏云：「慮於父為孝子，於弟為仁兄。
entries.en: The Ministry reported: "Lu is a filial son toward his father and a benevolent elder brother toward his younger brothers.
entries.literal: The Ministry reported: "Lu is a filial son toward his father and a benevolent elder brother toward his younger brothers.

entries.zh: 尋究情狀，特可矜感。」
entries.en: On examining the circumstances, he is especially deserving of pity and compassion."
entries.literal: Examining the circumstances, he is especially deserving of pity and sympathy."

entries.zh: 高祖詔特恕其父死罪，以從遠流。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu decreed that his father's capital crime be specially pardoned and commuted to exile in a distant region.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu decreed that his father's capital crime be specially pardoned and commuted to exile to a distant place.

entries.zh: 孫益德，樂安人也。
entries.en: Sun Yide was a man of Le'an.
entries.literal: Sun Yide, a man of Le'an.

entries.zh: 其母為人所害，益德童幼為母復仇。
entries.en: His mother had been murdered; while still a child Yide avenged her.
entries.literal: His mother had been killed by someone; while still a child Yide avenged his mother.

entries.zh: 還家，哭於殯以待縣官。
entries.en: He returned home and wept beside the coffin, awaiting the district authorities.
entries.literal: Returning home, he wept beside the coffin awaiting the district authorities.

entries.zh: 高祖、文明太后以其幼而孝決。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming judged him filial though young.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming judged him filial though young.

entries.zh: 又不逃罪，特免之。
entries.en: Moreover, he had not fled punishment, so they specially exempted him.
entries.literal: Moreover, he had not fled punishment, so they specially exempted him.

entries.zh: 王續生，滎陽京縣人也。
entries.en: Wang Xusheng was from Jing county in Xingyang.
entries.literal: Wang Xusheng was a man of Jing county in Xingyang.

entries.zh: 遭繼母憂，居喪杖而後起。
entries.en: When his stepmother died he observed mourning, leaning on a staff before he could rise.
entries.literal: He suffered mourning for his stepmother and dwelt in mourning, leaning on a staff before he could rise.

entries.zh: 及終禮制，鬢髮盡落。
entries.en: When the mourning rites were complete, all his hair fell out.
entries.literal: When the mourning rites were complete, his temples and hair all fell out.

entries.zh: 有司奏聞，世宗詔標旌門閭，甄其徭役。
entries.en: The relevant offices reported to the throne. Emperor Shizong decreed that his gate and hamlet be marked and his corvée obligations waived.
entries.literal: The relevant offices reported to the throne; Emperor Shizong decreed to mark his gate and hamlet and exempt him from corvée.

entries.zh: 趙琰 長孫慮 乞伏保 孫益德 董洛生 楊引 閻元明 吳悉達 王續生 李顯達 張昇 倉跋 王崇 郭文恭
entries.en: Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Zhang Sheng, Cang Ba, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong
entries.literal: Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Zhang Sheng, Cang Ba, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong

entries.zh: 于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯 朱長生 于提 馬八龍 門文愛 晁清 劉侯仁 石祖興 邵洪哲 王榮世 胡小虎 孫道登 李几 張安祖 王閭
entries.en: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.
entries.literal: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Houran, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.

entries.zh: 晁清，遼東人也。
entries.en: Chao Qing came from Liaodong.
entries.literal: Chao Qing was a man of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 祖暉，濟州刺史、潁川公。
entries.en: His grandfather Hui had served as inspector of Ji province and Duke of Yingchuan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hui was inspector of Ji province and Duke of Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 清襲祖爵，例降為伯。
entries.en: Qing inherited his grandfather's rank, which by regulation was reduced one step to marquis.
entries.literal: Qing inherited his grandfather's title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.

entries.zh: 為梁城戍將。
entries.en: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng.
entries.literal: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng.

entries.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，糧盡城陷，清抗節不屈，為賊所殺。
entries.en: When Xiao Yan besieged the city and supplies ran out, the fortress fell. Qing held to his integrity and refused to yield, and the enemy killed him.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan besieged him; when grain was exhausted the city fell. Qing upheld his integrity and would not submit, and was killed by the bandits.

entries.zh: 世宗褒美，贈樂陵太守，諡曰忠。
entries.en: Emperor Xuanwu honored him posthumously as administrator of Leling with the posthumous name Zhong.
entries.literal: Shizong praised and commended him, posthumously granting him administrator of Leling, with the posthumous name Zhong.

entries.zh: 子榮賓襲。
entries.en: His son Rongbin inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Rongbin inherited.

entries.zh: 劉侯仁，豫州人也。
entries.en: Liu Houran came from Yu province.
entries.literal: Liu Houran was a man of Yu province.

entries.zh: 城人白早生殺刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。
entries.en: A local man named Bai Zaosheng killed the provincial inspector Sima Yue, seized the southern part of the city, and rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: A townsman, Bai Zaosheng, killed the inspector Sima Yue, seized the south of the city, and rebelled.

entries.zh: 悅息朏，走投侯仁。
entries.en: Yue's son Fei fled for his life to Liu Houran.
entries.literal: Yue's son Fei fled in distress to seek Houran.

entries.zh: 賊雖重加購募，又嚴其捶撻，侯仁終無漏泄，朏遂免禍。
entries.en: Though the rebels raised the bounty on his head and tortured him severely, Houran never betrayed the boy, and Fei was spared.
entries.literal: Although the bandits repeatedly increased the reward for his capture and strictly beat and flogged him, Houran never leaked anything, and Fei thereby escaped harm.

entries.zh: 事寧，有司奏其操行，請免府籍，敍一小縣，詔可。
entries.en: When order was restored, the authorities reported his conduct and asked that he be struck from the prefectural rolls and given a minor county post; the court approved.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, the responsible offices memorialized his conduct and requested that he be removed from the prefectural register and appointed to a small county; the edict approved.

entries.zh: 于簡，字什門，代人也。
entries.en: Yu Jian, whose courtesy name was Shenmen, came from Dai.
entries.literal: Yu Jian, courtesy name Shenmen, was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 太宗時為謁者，使喻馮跋。
entries.en: Under Emperor Mingyuan he served as usher and was dispatched to deliver the court's message to Feng Ba.
entries.literal: Under Taizong he served as usher and was sent as envoy to instruct Feng Ba.

entries.zh: 及至和龍，住外舍不入，使人謂跋曰：「大魏皇帝有詔，須馮主出受，然後敢入。」
entries.en: On reaching Helong he stayed in an outer lodge and refused to go in, sending word to Feng Ba: "The emperor of Great Wei has issued an edict. Your lordship must come out to receive it; only then may I enter."
entries.literal: When he reached Helong, he lodged in an outer residence and would not enter, sending someone to tell Ba, "The Great Wei emperor has an edict; the Lord of Feng must come out to receive it—only then do I dare enter."

entries.zh: 跋使人牽逼令入，見跋不拜，跋令人按其項。
entries.en: Feng Ba's men seized and hustled him inside. When he saw Feng Ba he would not bow, and Feng Ba ordered someone to press down on his neck.
entries.literal: Ba had men drag and force him to enter. Seeing Ba, he did not bow; Ba had someone press down on his neck.

entries.zh: 什門曰：「馮主拜受詔，吾自以賓主致敬，何須苦見逼也！」
entries.en: Shenmen said, "When my lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I will offer the respect proper between host and guest. Why torment me like this?"
entries.literal: Shenmen said, "When the Lord of Feng bows to receive the edict, I myself will pay the courtesy due between host and guest—why must you torment me so!"

entries.zh: 與跋往復，聲氣厲然，初不撓屈。
entries.en: He and Feng Ba argued back and forth, his tone fierce throughout, and he never once gave way.
entries.literal: He and Ba went back and forth; his voice and bearing were fierce, and from the first he did not yield.

entries.zh: 既而跋止什門。
entries.en: In the end Feng Ba held Shenmen prisoner.
entries.literal: Presently Ba detained Shenmen.

entries.zh: 什門於羣眾之中，回身背跋，被袴後襠以辱之。
entries.en: Before the assembled crowd Shenmen turned his back on Feng Ba, pulled on his trousers with the seat to the front, and presented his backside to insult him.
entries.literal: Shenmen, in the midst of the crowd, turned his body with his back to Ba, put on trousers backward, and exposed his rear to shame him.

entries.zh: 既見拘留，隨身衣裳敗壞略盡，蟣虱被體。
entries.en: Once he was held captive, the clothes he wore were nearly destroyed, and his body was covered with lice.
entries.literal: Once detained, the clothes on his person were nearly all ruined, and lice and nits covered his body.

entries.zh: 跋遺以衣服，什門拒而不受。
entries.en: Feng Ba sent him clothing, but Shenmen refused to take it.
entries.literal: Ba sent him clothes; Shenmen refused and would not accept them.

entries.zh: 和龍人皆歎曰：「雖古烈士，無以過也！」
entries.en: The people of Helong all marveled: "Even the heroes of antiquity could not have done better!"
entries.literal: The people of Helong all sighed, "Even the martyrs of old could not surpass this!"

entries.zh: 歷二十四年，[3]後馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸。
entries.en: Twenty-four years passed. When Feng Wentong at last submitted a memorial professing vassalage, Shenmen was sent back.
entries.literal: Twenty-four years passed; later Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home.

entries.zh: 拜治書侍御史。
entries.en: He was appointed attendant imperial censor.
entries.literal: He was appointed attendant censor.

entries.zh: 世祖下詔曰：「什門奉使和龍，值狂豎肆虐，勇志壯厲，不為屈節，雖昔蘇武何以加之。」
entries.en: Emperor Taiwu issued an edict: "Shenmen served as envoy at Helong when a reckless usurper ran riot. His courage and resolve were magnificent, and he would not bend his integrity. Not even Su Wu of old could have done more."
entries.literal: Shizu issued an edict saying, "Shenmen was sent on mission to Helong and encountered a mad villain's tyranny; his courage and will were fierce and strong, and he would not compromise his integrity—even the Su Wu of old could not surpass him."

entries.zh: 賜羊千口、帛千匹，進為上大夫，策告宗廟，頒示天下，咸使聞也。
entries.en: He was given a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoted to senior grand master, and the court reported the honor to the ancestral temple and proclaimed it throughout the realm.
entries.literal: He was granted a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoted to senior grand master, and the honor was reported to the ancestral temple and proclaimed throughout the realm so that all might hear.

entries.zh: 段進，不知何許人也。
entries.en: Duan Jin was a man of unknown origin.
entries.literal: Duan Jin—of what place he was is unknown.

entries.zh: 世祖初，為白道守將。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Taiwu's reign he served as garrison commander of Baidao.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign he was garrison commander of Baidao.

entries.zh: 蠕蠕大檀入塞，圍之，力屈被執。
entries.en: The Rouran khan Datan raided across the border, besieged him, and when resistance failed took him prisoner.
entries.literal: The Rouran khan Datan entered the frontier, besieged him, and when his strength failed he was captured.

entries.zh: 進抗聲大罵，遂為賊殺。
entries.en: Jin shouted back and reviled them at the top of his voice, and the enemy killed him.
entries.literal: Jin answered with a loud voice and great curses, and was thereupon killed by the bandits.

entries.zh: 世祖愍之，追贈安北將軍，賜爵顯美侯，諡曰莊。
entries.en: Emperor Taiwu mourned him and posthumously appointed him General Who Pacifies the North, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Xianmei with the posthumous name Zhuang.
entries.literal: Shizu pitied him and posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Pacifies the North, granting the title Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

entries.zh: 歷二十四年 通鑑卷一二二
entries.en: "Twenty-four years passed": Zizhi tongjian, juan 122
entries.literal: Twenty-four years passed: Zizhi tongjian juan 122

entries.zh: 〈三八五三頁〉
記于什門還魏於元嘉十一年
entries.en: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in the eleventh year of Yuanjia
entries.literal: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in the eleventh year of Yuanjia

entries.zh: 〈魏延和三年
entries.en: 〈Northern Wei Yanhe year 3
entries.literal: 〈Northern Wei Yanhe year 3

entries.zh: (四三四)〉，
「二十四」作「二十一」。
entries.en: reading "twenty-four" as "twenty-one."
entries.literal: "twenty-four" is written as "twenty-one."

entries.zh: 考異云：「後魏本紀
entries.en: Kaoyi notes: "The Later Wei annals
entries.literal: Kaoyi states: "The Later Wei basic annals

entries.zh: 〈卷三〉
entries.en: 〈juan 3〉
entries.literal: 〈juan 3〉

entries.zh: 神瑞元年
entries.en: first year of Shenrui
entries.literal: first year of Shenrui

entries.zh: 〈四一四〉
八月遣于什門招諭馮跋，至此年二十一年矣。
entries.en: In the eighth month Yu Shenmen was sent to summon Feng Ba; by this year twenty-one years had elapsed.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Yu Shenmen was sent to summon and instruct Feng Ba; by this year twenty-one years had passed.

entries.zh: 若二十四年，乃在太延三年，而太延二年馮氏亡矣。」
entries.en: If it were twenty-four years, that would place the return in Taiyan year 3, but the Feng state fell in Taiyan year 2."
entries.literal: If it were twenty-four years, that would fall in the third year of Taiyan, yet in the second year of Taiyan the Feng clan had perished."

entries.zh: 按傳稱「馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸」，卷四上世祖紀上延和三年三月記「文通遣尚書高顒上表稱藩」，故通鑑置於是年。
entries.en: The biography says that "Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home." Shizu annals, juan 4A, Yanhe third year, third month, records that "Wentong sent Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial declaring himself a vassal"; hence the Zizhi tongjian places the return in that year.
entries.literal: According to the biography, "Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent home"; juan 4A, Annals of Shizu, upper, third month of the third year of Yanhe records "Wentong sent the Master of Writing Gao Yong to submit a memorial declaring himself a vassal," hence the Zizhi tongjian places it in that year.

entries.zh: 疑「二十四」當作「二十一」。
entries.en: "Twenty-four" is probably a mistake for "twenty-one."
entries.literal: It is suspected that "twenty-four" should read "twenty-one."

entries.zh: 時有敕勒部人蛭拔寅兄地于，坐盜食官馬，依制命死。
entries.en: At that time two men of the Chile tribe, Zhi Bayin and his elder brother Diyu, were sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses.
entries.literal: At that time a man of the Chile tribe, Zhi Bayin, and his elder brother Diyu were sentenced to death for stealing and eating government horses.

entries.zh: 拔寅自誣己殺，兄又云實非弟殺，兄弟爭死，辭不能定。
entries.en: Bayin falsely confessed to the killing himself, while his brother insisted that the younger man had not done it. The two brothers each claimed guilt, and the court could not decide between their accounts.
entries.literal: Bayin falsely confessed that he himself had killed; the elder brother also said that in truth it was not the younger who had killed. The brothers vied to die, and their statements could not be settled.

entries.zh: 高祖詔原之。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict pardoning them both.
entries.literal: Gaozu issued an edict pardoning them.

entries.zh: 劉渴侯，不知何許人也。
entries.en: Liu Kehou was a man of unknown origin.
entries.literal: Liu Kehou—of what place he was is unknown.

entries.zh: 禀性剛烈。
entries.en: By nature he was fierce and unyielding.
entries.literal: His inborn nature was fierce and unyielding.

entries.zh: 太和中，為徐州後軍，以力死戰，眾寡不敵，遂禽。
entries.en: During the Taihe period he served in the rear guard of Xuzhou, fought to the death, was overwhelmed by superior numbers, and was taken prisoner.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era he served as rear army of Xuzhou, fought to the death with all his strength, was outnumbered, and was captured.

entries.zh: 瞋目大罵，終不降屈，為賊所殺。
entries.en: He glared and reviled them without cease, would never yield, and the enemy killed him.
entries.literal: Glaring with wide eyes he cursed loudly, never submitting in defeat, and was killed by the bandits.

entries.zh: 高祖贈立忠將軍、平州刺史、上庸侯，賜絹千匹、穀千斛。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen posthumously appointed him General Who Establishes Loyalty, inspector of Ping province, and Marquis of Shangyong, and granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
entries.literal: Gaozu posthumously granted him General Who Establishes Loyalty, inspector of Ping province, and Marquis of Shangyong, with a gift of a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

entries.zh: 朱長生及于提，並代人也。
entries.en: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.
entries.literal: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.

entries.zh: 高祖時，以長生為員外散騎常侍，與提俱使高車。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xiaowen, Changsheng was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, together with Yu Ti, was sent on embassy to the Gaoche.
entries.literal: Under Gaozu, Changsheng was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, together with Ti, was sent as envoy to the Gaoche.

entries.zh: 至其庭，高車主阿伏至羅責長生等拜，長生拒之曰：「我天子使，安肯拜下土諸侯！」
entries.en: At the Gaoche court their ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that Changsheng and his party bow. Changsheng refused: "I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven. How could I bow to a petty frontier lord?"
entries.literal: When they reached the court, the Gaoche ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that Changsheng and the others bow. Changsheng refused, saying, "I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven—how could I bow to a petty lord of the lower lands!"

entries.zh: 阿伏至羅乃不以禮待。
entries.en: Avuzhiluo then refused them proper ceremonial treatment.
entries.literal: Avuzhiluo thereupon did not treat them with ritual courtesy.

entries.zh: 長生以金銀寶器奉之，至羅既受獻，長生曰：「為臣內附，宜盡臣禮，何得口云再拜而實不拜！」
entries.en: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels as tribute. Once Avuzhiluo had accepted them, Changsheng said, "As a subject who has submitted to the court, you ought to perform a subject's obeisance. How can you say you will bow twice and then not bow at all?"
entries.literal: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels to him. After Avuzhiluo had accepted the tribute, Changsheng said, "As a subject who has submitted within, you ought to fulfill a subject's rites—how can you say with your mouth that you bow twice while in fact not bowing!"

entries.zh: 呼出帳，命眾中拜。
entries.en: He summoned Avuzhiluo outside the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled company.
entries.literal: He called him out of the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembly.

entries.zh: 阿伏至羅慚其臣下，大怒曰：「帳中何不教我拜，而辱我於大眾！」
entries.en: Ashamed before his followers, Avuzhiluo flew into a rage: "Why did you not have me bow inside the tent, but humiliate me before the whole assembly?"
entries.literal: Avuzhiluo, shamed before his subjects, said in great anger, "Why did you not teach me to bow inside the tent, but instead humiliate me before the great crowd!"

entries.zh: 奪長生等獻物，囚之叢石之中，兵脅之曰：「汝能為我臣則活，如其不降，殺汝！」
entries.en: He confiscated their tribute gifts and imprisoned them among the rocks. Armed men threatened them: "Become my subjects and you shall live. Refuse, and you die."
entries.literal: He seized the tribute objects of Changsheng and the others and imprisoned them among piled stones. Soldiers threatened them, saying, "If you can become my subjects you will live; if you do not submit, you will be killed!"

entries.zh: 長生與于提瞋目厲聲責之曰：「豈有天子使人拜汝夷，我寧為魏鬼，不為汝臣！」
entries.en: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared and shouted their rebuke: "Shall an envoy of the Son of Heaven bow to you barbarians? I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"
entries.literal: Changsheng and Yu Ti glared with wide eyes and in fierce voices rebuked them, saying, "How could an envoy of the Son of Heaven bow to you barbarians! I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"

entries.zh: 至羅彌怒，絕其飲食。
entries.en: Avuzhiluo's fury only grew, and he cut off their food and drink.
entries.literal: Avuzhiluo grew still angrier and cut off their food and drink.

entries.zh: 從行者三十人皆降，至羅乃給以肉酪，惟長生與提不從，乃各分徙之。
entries.en: All thirty of their attendants submitted, and Avuzhiluo gave them meat and curds. Only Changsheng and Yu Ti refused, so he had them separated and sent to different places of exile.
entries.literal: The thirty who had accompanied them all submitted; Avuzhiluo then gave them meat and curds, but only Changsheng and Ti would not comply, and he had them separated and exiled each to a different place.

entries.zh: 積三歲，乃得還。
entries.en: Three years passed before they were able to return.
entries.literal: After three years they were at last able to return.

entries.zh: 高祖以長生等守節遠同蘇武，甚嘉之，拜長生河內太守，于提隴西太守，並賜爵五等男。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen held that in keeping their integrity Changsheng and his companions rivaled Su Wu of old, and he greatly honored them. Changsheng was appointed administrator of Henei, Yu Ti administrator of Longxi, and both were enfeoffed as fifth-rank barons.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because Changsheng and the others upheld their integrity in a manner far matching Su Wu, greatly commended them, appointing Changsheng administrator of Henei and Yu Ti administrator of Longxi, and granting both the fifth-rank baronetcy.

entries.zh: 從者皆為令長。
entries.en: Their attendants were all appointed district magistrates.
entries.literal: Those who had accompanied them were all made magistrates.

entries.zh: 石祖興，常山九門人也。
entries.en: Shi Zuxing came from Jiumen in Changshan commandery.
entries.literal: Shi Zuxing was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.

entries.zh: 太守田文彪、縣令和真等喪亡，祖興自出家絹二百餘匹，營護喪事。
entries.en: When Grand Administrator Tian Wenbiao, Magistrate He Zhen, and others died in office, Zuxing gave more than two hundred bolts of silk from his own household to see to their burials.
entries.literal: When the grand administrator Tian Wenbiao, the magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing himself contributed more than two hundred bolts of silk from his household to arrange and oversee their funerals.

entries.zh: 州郡表列，高祖嘉之，賜爵二級，為上造。
entries.en: The province and commandery reported his conduct. Emperor Xiaowen praised him, raised his noble rank by two steps, and enfeoffed him as Shangzao.
entries.literal: The province and commandery reported and listed him; Gaozu commended him and granted two ranks of nobility, making him Shangzao.

entries.zh: 後拜寧陵令，卒。
entries.en: He was later appointed magistrate of Ningling, where he died.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Ningling and died in office.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書李韶奏其節義，請加贈諡，以奬來者，靈太后令如所奏。
entries.en: Li Shao, Minister of Personnel, memorialized Zuxing's loyalty and asked that a posthumous title be granted to encourage others. Empress Dowager Ling ordered that it be done as he proposed.
entries.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shao memorialized his integrity and righteousness and requested a posthumous title to encourage those who would come after; Empress Dowager Ling ordered that it be done as memorialized.

entries.zh: 有司諡曰恭。
entries.en: The court granted him the posthumous name Gong.
entries.literal: The responsible offices gave the posthumous name Gong.

entries.zh: 王榮世，陽平館陶人也。
entries.en: Wang Rongshi came from Guantao in Yangping commandery.
entries.literal: Wang Rongshi was a man of Guantao in Yangping.

entries.zh: 為三城戍主、方城縣子。
entries.en: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and held the title Baron of Fangcheng.
entries.literal: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and Baron of Fangcheng county.

entries.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，力窮知不可全，乃先焚府庫，後殺妻妾。
entries.en: When Xiao Yan besieged the fortress and resistance failed, seeing that all could not be saved, he burned the treasury first and then killed his wife and concubines.
entries.literal: When Xiao Yan besieged him and his strength was exhausted, knowing he could not preserve all, he first burned the treasury and then killed his wife and concubines.

entries.zh: 及賊陷城，與戍副鄧元興等俱以不屈被害。
entries.en: When the city fell, he and his deputy Deng Yuanxing and others were killed for refusing to yield.
entries.literal: When the bandits took the city, he and the deputy garrison commander Deng Yuanxing and others were all killed for refusing to submit.

entries.zh: 肅宗下詔褒美忠節，進榮世爵為伯，贈齊州刺史；
entries.en: Emperor Suzong issued an edict praising their loyalty, promoted Rongshi's rank to marquis, and posthumously appointed him inspector of Qi province;
entries.literal: Suzong issued an edict praising their loyal integrity, promoted Rongshi's title to marquis, and posthumously granted him inspector of Qi province;

entries.zh: 元興開國子，贈洛州刺史。
entries.en: Yuanxing was enfeoffed as a founding viscount and posthumously appointed inspector of Luo province.
entries.literal: Yuanxing was granted the founding viscountcy and posthumously made inspector of Luo province.

entries.zh: 胡小虎，河南河陰人也。
entries.en: Hu Xiaohu came from Heyin in Henan commandery.
entries.literal: Hu Xiaohu was a man of Heyin in Henan.

entries.zh: 少有武氣。
entries.en: Even in youth he had a warrior's spirit.
entries.literal: In youth he possessed martial spirit.

entries.zh: 正光末，為統軍於晉壽。
entries.en: At the end of the Zhenguang period he commanded troops at Jinshou.
entries.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era he served as army commander at Jinshou.

entries.zh: 孝昌中，蕭衍將樊文熾等寇邊，益州刺史邴虬遣長史和安固守小劍，文熾圍之。
entries.en: During the Xiaochang period Xiao Yan's generals Fan Wenchì and others raided the border. Bing Qiu, inspector of Yi province, sent his chief clerk He An to hold Xiaojian, and Wenchì laid siege.
entries.literal: In the Xiaochang era the generals of Xiao Yan, Fan Wenchì and others, raided the frontier; the inspector of Yi province, Bing Qiu, sent his chief clerk He An to hold Xiaojian firmly, and Wenchì besieged it.

entries.zh: 虬命小虎與統軍崔珍寶同往防拒。
entries.en: Qiu ordered Xiaohu and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to march out and resist.
entries.literal: Qiu ordered Xiaohu and the army commander Cui Zhenbao to go together to defend against them.

entries.zh: 文熾掩襲小虎、珍寶，並擒之。
entries.en: Wenchì ambushed Xiaohu and Zhenbao and took them both prisoner.
entries.literal: Wenchì launched a surprise attack on Xiaohu and Zhenbao and captured them both.

entries.zh: 文熾攻小劍未陷，乃將珍寶至城下，使謂和安曰：「南軍強盛，北救不來，豈若歸款，取其富貴。」
entries.en: Before Xiaojian fell, Wenchì brought Zhenbao to the wall and had him call to He An: "The southern army is strong and northern relief will not come. Why not surrender and win wealth and rank?"
entries.literal: Wenchì had not yet taken Xiaojian, so he brought Zhenbao to the foot of the wall and had him say to He An, "The southern army is strong; northern relief will not come—would it not be better to submit and win wealth and honor?"

entries.zh: 和安命射之，乃退。
entries.en: He An ordered his men to shoot at them, and the enemy withdrew.
entries.literal: He An ordered archers to shoot at him, and they withdrew.

entries.zh: 復逼小虎與和安交言，小虎乃慷慨謂安曰：「我柵不防，為賊所虜。
entries.en: They forced Xiaohu to speak with He An again. Xiaohu cried out to him: "My camp was unprepared and the enemy took me.
entries.literal: They again forced Xiaohu to speak with He An. Xiaohu then said with fervor to An, "My palisade was not defended and I was captured by the bandits.

entries.zh: 觀其兵士，勢不足言，努力堅守。
entries.en: Their troops are nothing to fear. Hold the fortress with all your strength.
entries.literal: Looking at their soldiers, their strength is not worth mentioning—strive to hold firm.

entries.zh: 魏行臺傳梁州遣將已至。」
entries.en: The Wei field headquarters in Liang province has already dispatched reinforcements—they are here."
entries.literal: The Wei mobile headquarters in Liang province has already sent generals—they have arrived."

entries.zh: [6]賊以刀毆擊，言不得終，遂害之。
entries.en: [6] The enemy beat him with blades before he could finish, and killed him.
entries.literal: [6] The bandits struck him with blades; he could not finish his words and was thereupon killed.

entries.zh: 三軍無不歎其壯節，哀其死亡。
entries.en: The whole army marveled at his courage and mourned his death.
entries.literal: Throughout the three armies none failed to admire his stalwart integrity and mourn his death.

entries.zh: 賊尋奔敗，禽其次將蕭世澄、陳文緒等一十一人。
entries.en: The enemy soon broke and fled, and eleven of their officers, including Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu, were captured.
entries.literal: The bandits soon fled in defeat, and eleven of their subordinate generals, including Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu, were captured.

entries.zh: 行臺魏子建壯其氣概，啟以世澄購其屍柩，乃獲骸骨歸葬。
entries.en: Field commander Wei Zijian admired his spirit and petitioned to exchange the captive Shicheng for his body. The remains were recovered and buried with honor.
entries.literal: The mobile headquarters commander Wei Zijian admired his spirit; he memorialized that Shicheng be ransomed for his coffin, and the remains were obtained and returned for burial.

entries.zh: 孫道登，彭城呂縣人也。
entries.en: Sun Daodeng came from Lü county in Pengcheng commandery.
entries.literal: Sun Daodeng was a man of Lü county in Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 永安初，為蕭衍將韋休等所虜，面縛臨刃，巡遠村塢，令其招降鄉曲。
entries.en: Early in the Yong'an period he was taken prisoner by Xiao Yan's general Wei Xiu and others. Bound and marched at sword-point through distant hamlets, he was forced to urge the countryside to surrender.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was captured by the generals of Xiao Yan, Wei Xiu and others; bound facing the blade, he was led through distant villages and stockades and ordered to induce the local people to submit.

entries.zh: 道登厲聲唱呼：「但當努力，賊無所能。」
entries.en: Daodeng shouted at the top of his voice: "Stand firm! The enemy can do nothing!"
entries.literal: Daodeng shouted in a fierce voice, "Only strive with all your might—the bandits can do nothing!"

entries.zh: 賊遂屠戮之。
entries.en: The enemy killed him on the spot.
entries.literal: The bandits thereupon slaughtered him.

entries.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款以除縣令 諸本「朐」作「眴」，北史卷八五邵洪哲傳作「眗」。
entries.en: On "Magistrate Fan Daorong submitted from Qucheng": various editions read qu as shun; Beishi, juan 85, Shao Hongzhe biography, has ju.
entries.literal: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier submitted from Qucheng in allegiance and was relieved of the magistracy: various editions write "qu" as "shun"; Beishi juan 85, Shao Hongzhe biography, writes "ju."

entries.zh: 冊府卷一三八
entries.en: Cefu yuangui, juan 138
entries.literal: Cefu yuangui juan 138

entries.zh: 〈一六六六頁〉、
卷八０三
entries.en: juan 803
entries.literal: juan 803

entries.zh: 〈九五四八頁〉
並作「朐」。
entries.en: Both read "qu."
entries.literal: Both read "qu."

entries.zh: 按「朐城歸款」事見卷八世宗紀永平四年四月、卷四七盧淵附盧昶傳、卷九八蕭衍傳，「朐城」亦作「朐山」。
entries.en: The affair of "Qucheng's surrender in allegiance" appears in Shizong annals, juan 8, Yongping fourth year, fourth month; Lu Yuan with appended biography of Lu Chang, juan 47; and the biography of Xiao Yan, juan 98. The place name "Qucheng" is also written "Qushan."
entries.literal: According to this, the affair of "Qucheng's submission in allegiance" appears in juan 8, Annals of Shizong, fourth month of the fourth year of Yongping; juan 47, Lu Yuan with appended biography of Lu Chang; and juan 98, Xiao Yan biography; "Qucheng" is also written as "Qushan."

entries.zh: 「眴」「眗」都是「朐」之訛，今據改。
entries.en: Both "shun" and "ju" are corruptions of "qu"; the text is emended accordingly.
entries.literal: "Shun" and "ju" are both corruptions of "qu"; the text is now emended accordingly.

entries.zh: 于洛侯，代人也。
entries.en: Yu Luohou was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Yu Luohou was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 以勞舊為秦州刺史，而貪酷安忍。
entries.en: On account of long-standing merit he was appointed Governor of Qinzhou, but he was greedy, brutal, and pitiless.
entries.literal: Because of meritorious service in the old days he was made Governor of Qinzhou, yet he was greedy, cruel, and calmly ruthless.

entries.zh: 州人富熾奪民呂勝脛纏一具，洛侯輒鞭富熾一百，截其右腕。
entries.en: When a local man named Fu Chi seized a pair of leg wrappings from the commoner Lü Sheng, Luohou had him flogged one hundred times on the spot and cut off his right wrist.
entries.literal: A man of the province named Fu Chi seized from a commoner, Lü Sheng, one pair of leg wrappings. Luohou immediately had Fu Chi flogged one hundred strokes and cut off his right wrist.

entries.zh: 百姓王隴客刺殺民王羌奴、王愈二人，依律罪死而已，洛侯生拔隴客舌，刺其本，并刺胸腹二十餘瘡。
entries.en: The commoner Wang Longke had killed Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu—an offense that by law merited execution and nothing more. Luohou tore out Longke's tongue while he still lived, stabbed his groin, and drove more than twenty wounds into his chest and belly.
entries.literal: The commoner Wang Longke had stabbed and killed two men, Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu; by law he deserved death and nothing more. Luohou pulled out Longke's tongue while he was alive, stabbed his perineum, and stabbed his chest and belly more than twenty times.

entries.zh: 隴客不堪苦痛，隨刀戰動。
entries.en: Longke could not bear the agony; his body convulsed with every thrust of the knife.
entries.literal: Longke could not endure the pain; he quivered with each stab of the blade.

entries.zh: 乃立四柱磔其手足，命將絕，始斬其首，支解四體，分懸道路。
entries.en: He then set up four posts and impaled Longke's limbs upon them. Only when life was nearly extinguished did he behead him, quarter the body, and hang the pieces along the roads.
entries.literal: Then he erected four posts and spiked Longke's hands and feet to them. Only when life was nearly gone did he cut off his head, dismember the four limbs, and hang the pieces along the roads.

entries.zh: 見之者無不傷楚，闔州驚震，人懷怨憤。
entries.en: All who witnessed it were overcome with grief; the entire province was shaken, and the people seethed with resentment.
entries.literal: Those who saw it were all stricken with pity; the whole province was shaken, and the people nursed resentment and rage.

entries.zh: 百姓王元壽等一時反叛。
entries.en: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rose in revolt together.
entries.literal: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rebelled all at once.

entries.zh: 有司糾劾。
entries.en: The authorities impeached him.
entries.literal: The responsible offices impeached him.

entries.zh: 高祖詔使者於州刑人處宣告兵民，然後斬洛侯以謝百姓。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to announce the case to soldiers and civilians at the site of execution in the province, then had Luohou beheaded to answer the people's grievances.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered an envoy to proclaim the matter to soldiers and people at the place of punishment in the province, then executed Luohou to appease the populace.

entries.zh: 胡泥，代人也。
entries.en: Hu Ni was a native of Dai.
entries.literal: Hu Ni was a man of Dai.

entries.zh: 歷官至司衞監，賜爵永城侯。
entries.en: He rose through the ranks to Supervisor of the Palace Guards and was ennobled as Marquis of Yongcheng.
entries.literal: He rose through offices to Supervisor of the Palace Guards and was granted the title Marquis of Yongcheng.

entries.zh: 泥率勒禁中，不憚豪貴。
entries.en: Ni enforced discipline within the palace and showed no fear of the powerful and privileged.
entries.literal: Ni led and disciplined those within the forbidden precincts and did not fear the powerful and noble.

entries.zh: 殿中尚書叔孫侯頭應內直而闕於一時，泥以法繩之。
entries.en: When Palace Attendant Shusun Hutou failed to report for his shift on inner palace duty, Ni prosecuted him according to the law.
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant Shusun Hutou was on duty for inner attendance but was absent for a time; Ni bound him by law.

entries.zh: 侯頭恃寵，遂與口諍。
entries.en: Hutou, trusting in imperial favor, quarreled with him openly.
entries.literal: Hutou relied on imperial favor and thereupon argued with him face to face.
