entries.zh: 高祖聞而嘉焉，賜泥衣服一襲。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu heard of this and praised him, granting Ni a suit of robes.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard of it he commended him and bestowed on Ni one suit of clothing.

entries.zh: 出為幽州刺史，假范陽公。
entries.en: He was appointed Governor of Youzhou and given the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.
entries.literal: He went out as Governor of Youzhou, with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.

entries.zh: 以北平陽尼碩學，遂表薦之。
entries.en: Recognizing Yang Ni of Beiping as a distinguished scholar, he memorialized the throne recommending him for office.
entries.literal: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a profound scholar, he submitted a memorial recommending him.

entries.zh: 遷平東將軍、定州刺史。
entries.en: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 以暴虐，刑罰酷濫，受納貨賄，徵還戮之。
entries.en: For his brutality, his excessive and arbitrary punishments, and his acceptance of bribes, he was recalled to the capital and put to death.
entries.literal: Because of his violence and cruelty, his excessive and wanton punishments, and his acceptance of bribes, he was summoned back and executed.

entries.zh: 將就法也，高祖臨太華殿引見，遣侍臣宣詔責之，遂就家賜自盡。
entries.en: As he was about to face punishment, Emperor Gaozu received him at Taihua Hall, sent an attendant to read out an edict of rebuke, and then permitted him to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: When he was about to face the law, Emperor Gaozu received him in audience at Taihua Hall, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him suicide at his home.

entries.zh: 李洪之，本名文通，恒農人。
entries.en: Li Hongzhi, born Li Wentong, was a native of Hengnong.
entries.literal: Li Hongzhi, whose original name was Wentong, was a man of Hengnong.

entries.zh: 少為沙門，晚乃還俗。
entries.en: In his youth he was a Buddhist monk; he did not return to secular life until later years.
entries.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; only later did he return to lay life.

entries.zh: 真君中，為狄道護軍，賜爵安陽男。
entries.en: During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector of the Army at Didao and was ennobled as Baron of Anyang.
entries.literal: In the Zhenjun era he served as Protector of the Army at Didao and was granted the title Baron of Anyang.

entries.zh: 會永昌王仁隨世祖南征，得元后姊妹二人。
entries.en: When Prince Ren of Yongchang accompanied Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign, he captured two sisters of the woman who would become Empress Yuan.
entries.literal: It happened that Prince of Yongchang Ren accompanied Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign and obtained two sisters of the future Empress Yuan.

entries.zh: 洪之以宗人潛相餉遺，結為兄弟，遂便如親。
entries.en: Hongzhi, claiming kinship, secretly sent them gifts; they swore brotherhood and thereafter treated one another as family.
entries.literal: Hongzhi, as a clansman, secretly sent them gifts; they formed a bond as brothers and thereafter treated one another as kin.

entries.zh: 頗得元后在南兄弟名字，乃改名洪之。
entries.en: Having learned the names of Empress Yuan's brothers in the south, he changed his own name to Hongzhi.
entries.literal: He learned rather fully the names of the Empress Yuan's brothers in the south and thereupon changed his name to Hongzhi.

entries.zh: 及仁坐事誅，元后入宮，得幸於高宗，生顯祖。
entries.en: When Ren was executed for his crimes, Empress Yuan entered the palace, won the favor of Emperor Gaozong, and bore Emperor Xianzu.
entries.literal: When Ren was executed for his offense, the Empress Yuan entered the palace, won favor from Emperor Gaozong, and bore Emperor Xianzu.

entries.zh: 元后臨崩，昭太后問其親，因言洪之為兄。
entries.en: On her deathbed Empress Yuan told Empress Dowager Zhao, when asked about her relatives, that Hongzhi was her brother.
entries.literal: As the Empress Yuan lay dying, Empress Dowager Zhao asked about her kin, and she said that Hongzhi was her brother.

entries.zh: 與相訣經日，具條列南方諸兄珍之等，手以付洪之。
entries.en: They bade farewell over several days; she wrote out a full list of her brothers in the south, including Zhenzhi, and handed it to Hongzhi in her own writing.
entries.literal: They took leave of one another for days; she fully listed her brothers in the south, Zhenzhi and the others, and handed the list to Hongzhi in her own hand.

entries.zh: 遂號為顯祖親舅。
entries.en: He was thereafter known as Emperor Xianzu's maternal uncle.
entries.literal: He was thereafter styled the maternal uncle of Emperor Xianzu.

entries.zh: 太安中，珍之等兄弟至都，與洪之相見，敍元后平生故事，計長幼為昆季。
entries.en: During the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and his brothers came to the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the life of Empress Yuan, and arranged themselves as brothers according to age.
entries.literal: In the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and his brothers arrived at the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the Empress Yuan's life story, and reckoned seniority to establish themselves as brothers.

entries.zh: 洪之素非廉清，每多受納。
entries.en: Hongzhi had never been honest; he frequently accepted bribes.
entries.literal: Hongzhi had never been honest and clean; he frequently accepted many bribes.

entries.zh: 時高祖始建祿制，法禁嚴峻，司察所聞，無不窮糾。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu had just instituted the salary system; laws were strict, and inspectors pursued every report to its conclusion.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just established the salary system; laws and prohibitions were severe, and whatever the inspectors heard they pursued to the end.

entries.zh: 遂鎖洪之赴京。
entries.en: Hongzhi was shackled and escorted to the capital.
entries.literal: Hongzhi was therefore shackled and sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖臨太華，庭集羣官，有司奏洪之受贓狼藉，又以酷暴。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu convened the court at Taihua Hall. The authorities reported that Hongzhi's bribery was rampant and that he was also brutal.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu came to Taihua; officials were assembled in the court. The responsible offices reported that Hongzhi's acceptance of bribes was flagrant, and that he was also cruel and violent.

entries.zh: 高祖親臨數之，以其大臣，聽在家自裁。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu rebuked him in person; because he was a senior minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally came forward and rebuked him; because he was a great minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.

entries.zh: 洪之志性慷慨，多所堪忍，疹疾灸療，艾炷圍將二寸，首足十餘處，一時俱下，而言笑自若，接賓不輟。
entries.en: Hongzhi was bold and long-suffering. When treated for skin ailments by moxibustion, cones nearly two inches across were applied to more than ten points on his head and limbs all at once, yet he conversed and laughed as usual and never ceased receiving guests.
entries.literal: Hongzhi's disposition was bold and generous and he could endure much. When he was treated for rash illness by moxibustion, the moxa cones were nearly two inches around; more than ten places on head and limbs received them all at once, yet he spoke and laughed as usual and did not cease receiving guests.

entries.zh: 及臨自盡，沐浴換衣。
entries.en: When the time came to take his own life, he bathed and changed his garments.
entries.literal: When the time came for him to take his own life, he bathed and changed his clothes.

entries.zh: 防卒扶持，將出却入，遍遶家庭，如是再三，泣歎良久，乃臥而引藥。
entries.en: Supported by guards, he started to leave, then turned back, walked through his entire household three times, wept and sighed at length, then lay down and drank the poison.
entries.literal: Guards supported him as he was about to go out, then turned back in, walked all around the household—thus three times—wept and sighed for a long while, then lay down and took the poison.

entries.zh: 始洪之託為元后兄，公私自同外戚。
entries.en: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as Empress Yuan's brother and in public and private enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin.
entries.literal: At first Hongzhi had pretended to be the Empress Yuan's brother and had in public and private treated himself as equal to the imperial affines.

entries.zh: 至此罪後，高祖乃稍對百官辨其誣假，而諸李猶善相視，恩紀如親。
entries.en: After his conviction Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to the officials the fraud he had perpetrated, yet the Li clan still treated one another with affection, their bonds as close as kin.
entries.literal: After this offense Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to the officials his deception, yet the various Lis still treated one another well and their bonds of kindness remained as among kin.

entries.zh: 洪之始見元后，計年為兄。
entries.en: When Hongzhi first met Empress Yuan, he calculated by age that he was her elder brother.
entries.literal: When Hongzhi first met the Empress Yuan, he reckoned by age that he was her elder brother.

entries.zh: 及珍之等至，洪之以元后素定長幼，其呼拜坐皆如家人。
entries.en: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi—relying on the seniority Empress Yuan had long since established—greeted them with the ease of family, bowing and taking his seat as among kin.
entries.literal: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi, because the Empress Yuan had long since fixed their seniority, addressed them, bowed, and seated himself all as among family.

entries.zh: 暮年數延攜之宴飲，醉酣之後，攜之時或言及本末，洪之則起而加敬，笑語自若。
entries.en: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to feasts. When drunk, Xiezhi would sometimes recount how their relationship had begun; Hongzhi would rise and show added deference, yet converse and laugh as usual.
entries.literal: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to banquets. After deep drunkenness Xiezhi would sometimes speak of how things had begun and ended; Hongzhi would rise and show added respect, yet laugh and talk as usual.

entries.zh: 富貴赫弈，當舅戚之家，遂棄宗專附珍之等。
entries.en: His wealth and rank blazed brilliantly; as a household of imperial kin by marriage, he abandoned his own clan and attached himself exclusively to Zhenzhi and his brothers.
entries.literal: His wealth and rank blazed brilliantly; as a household of maternal imperial kin, he abandoned his own clan and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and the others.

entries.zh: 後頗存振本屬，而猶不顯然。
entries.en: Later he made some effort to restore ties with his original clan, but only discreetly.
entries.literal: Later he somewhat sought to revive his original clan affiliation, but still not openly.

entries.zh: 劉氏四子，長子神自有傳。
entries.en: Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest, Shen, has his own biography.
entries.literal: Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest son Shen has his own biography.

entries.zh: 涉歷文史，頗有筆札，進中書侍郎。
entries.en: He studied literature and history and was skilled with the pen; he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He studied literature and history and possessed considerable skill with the brush; he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 詣長安，刊燕宣王廟碑，進爵安昌子。
entries.en: He went to Chang'an to carve the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was ennobled as Viscount of Anchang.
entries.literal: He went to Chang'an and carved the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan, and was advanced to Viscount of Anchang.

entries.zh: 及新製衣冠，高祖恭薦宗廟，遵形貌莊潔，音氣雄暢，常兼太祝令，跪贊禮事，為俯仰之節，粗合儀矩。
entries.en: When new ceremonial robes were introduced and Emperor Gaozu offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and his voice resonant. He regularly served as Director of Grand Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the rituals and performing the prescribed movements of obeisance, roughly in accord with ceremonial propriety.
entries.literal: When new caps and robes were made and Emperor Gaozu reverently offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and pure, his voice strong and clear. He regularly served concurrently as Director of Grand Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the ritual proceedings and performing the movements of bowing and rising, roughly conforming to ceremonial norms.

entries.zh: 由是高祖識待之。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu thereby came to notice and favor him.
entries.literal: Hence Emperor Gaozu came to know and favor him.

entries.zh: 後與游明根、高閭、李沖入議律令，親對御坐，時有陳奏。
entries.en: Later, together with You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong, he participated in drafting laws and statutes, speaking before the emperor and occasionally offering proposals.
entries.literal: Later, together with You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong, he entered deliberation on laws and statutes, speaking face to face before the imperial seat and sometimes offering memorials.

entries.zh: 以積年之勞，賜粟帛牛馬。
entries.en: For years of accumulated service he was rewarded with grain, silk, cattle, and horses.
entries.literal: For accumulated years of service he was granted grain, silks, cattle, and horses.

entries.zh: 出為立忠將軍、齊州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Qizhou.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Qizhou.

entries.zh: 建節歷本州，宗鄉改觀，而矯等彌妬毀之。
entries.en: Bearing the staff of authority he toured his home province; clansmen and neighbors changed their opinion of him, yet Jiao and the others grew only more envious and slandered him.
entries.literal: Bearing the staff of authority he passed through his home province; clansmen and townsfolk changed their view of him, yet Jiao and the others only grew more jealous and slandered him.

entries.zh: 遵性不廉清，在中書時，每假歸山東，必借備騾馬，將從百餘。
entries.en: Zun was not honest. While serving at the Secretariat, whenever he took leave to return to Shandong he requisitioned mules and horses and traveled with more than a hundred attendants.
entries.literal: Zun's character was not honest and clean. While at the Secretariat, whenever he took leave to return to Shandong he invariably requisitioned mules and horses and had more than a hundred attendants.

entries.zh: 屯逼民家求絲縑，不滿意則詬罵不去，強相徵求。
entries.en: He billeted troops on common households and demanded silk and fine cloth; if dissatisfied he cursed them and refused to leave, forcibly extorting goods.
entries.literal: He quartered troops and pressed common households for silk and fine cloth; if not satisfied he reviled them and would not leave, forcibly extorting supplies.

entries.zh: 旬月之間，縑布千數。
entries.en: Within a month he accumulated several thousand bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Within a month or so he accumulated several thousand bolts of silk cloth.

entries.zh: 邦邑苦之。
entries.en: The towns and districts suffered grievously.
entries.literal: The towns and districts suffered from it.

entries.zh: 遵既臨州，本意未弭，選召僚吏，多所取納。
entries.en: Once Zun took up the governorship his original intent was still unquelled; in selecting and summoning subordinate officials he accepted many bribes.
entries.literal: Once Zun took up the governorship his original intent was not quelled; in selecting and summoning subordinate officials he accepted many bribes.

entries.zh: 又其妻明氏家在齊州，母弟舅甥共相憑屬，爭求貨利，嚴暴非理，殺害甚多。
entries.en: His wife Lady Ming's family lived in Qizhou; her mother, brothers, uncles, and nephews relied on one another, vied for profit, acted with brutal violence, and killed many.
entries.literal: Moreover, his wife Lady Ming's family was in Qizhou; mother, younger brothers, maternal uncles, and nephews relied on one another, vied for profit, acted with harsh violence beyond reason, and killed many.

entries.zh: 貪酷之響，帝頗聞之。
entries.en: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor.
entries.literal: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor rather fully.

entries.zh: 及車駕幸鄴，遵自州來朝，會有赦宥。
entries.en: When the emperor visited Ye, Zun came from his province to court; a general amnesty happened to be in effect.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Zun came from his province to court; it happened that there was a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 遵臨還州，請辭帝於行宮，引見誚讓之。
entries.en: As Zun prepared to return to his province he took leave of the emperor at the traveling palace; the emperor received him and rebuked him sharply.
entries.literal: As Zun was about to return to his province he requested leave of the emperor at the traveling palace; the emperor received him and rebuked him.

entries.zh: 遵自陳無負，帝厲聲曰：「若無遷都赦，必無高遵矣！
entries.en: Zun protested his innocence, but the emperor said harshly: "Were it not for the amnesty proclaimed at the capital's relocation, Gao Zun would certainly be dead!
entries.literal: Zun declared himself innocent, but the emperor said in a harsh voice: "Were it not for the amnesty on the move of the capital, there would certainly be no Gao Zun left!

entries.zh: 又卿非惟貪惏，又虐於刑法，謂何如濟陰王，猶不免於法。
entries.en: You are not only greedy but brutal in your application of the law—consider the Prince of Jiyin: even he could not escape punishment.
entries.literal: Moreover, you are not only greedy but also cruel in penal law—what do you think of the Prince of Jiyin? Even he could not escape the law.

entries.zh: 卿何人，而為此行！
entries.en: Who are you to behave in this fashion!
entries.literal: Who are you, to act in this way!

entries.zh: 自今宜自謹約。」
entries.en: Henceforth you must restrain yourself."
entries.literal: From now on you should restrain yourself."

entries.zh: 還州，仍不悛革。
entries.en: After returning to his province he still did not reform.
entries.literal: When he returned to his province he still did not repent or reform.

entries.zh: 齊州人孟僧振至洛訟遵。
entries.en: Meng Sengzhen of Qizhou traveled to Luoyang to bring suit against Zun.
entries.literal: Meng Sengzhen of Qizhou went to Luoyang to sue Zun.

entries.zh: 詔廷尉少卿劉述窮鞫，皆如所訴。
entries.en: An edict ordered Vice Director Liu Shu of the Court of Judicial Review to investigate thoroughly; every charge proved true.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Liu Shu to investigate to the end; everything was as alleged.

entries.zh: 先是，沙門道登過遵，遵以道登荷寵於高祖，多奉以貨，深託仗之。
entries.en: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun. Knowing that Daodeng enjoyed Emperor Gaozu's favor, Zun lavished gifts on him and placed great trust in him.
entries.literal: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun. Zun, because Daodeng enjoyed favor from Emperor Gaozu, presented him with many gifts and relied on him deeply.

entries.zh: 道登屢因言次申啟救遵，帝不省納，遂詔述賜遵死。
entries.en: Daodeng repeatedly interceded for Zun, but the emperor would not listen; an edict then ordered Shu to sentence Zun to death.
entries.literal: Daodeng repeatedly seized occasions of conversation to plead for Zun's life, but the emperor would not heed him; an edict then ordered Shu to grant Zun death.

entries.zh: 時遵子元榮詣洛訟冤，猶恃道登，不時還赴。
entries.en: Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead his father's case; still trusting in Daodeng, he did not return in time.
entries.literal: At that time Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead his father's innocence; still trusting in Daodeng, he did not return in time.

entries.zh: 道登知事決，方乃遣之。
entries.en: Only when Daodeng knew the outcome was settled did he send him back.
entries.literal: When Daodeng knew the matter was settled, only then did he send him back.

entries.zh: 遵恨其妻，不與訣，別處沐浴，引椒而死。
entries.en: Zun hated his wife and would not bid her farewell; he bathed in a separate room and took poison.
entries.literal: Zun hated his wife and did not bid her farewell; he bathed elsewhere and took pepper poison to die.

entries.zh: 赦提克己厲約，遂有清稱。
entries.en: Sheti disciplined himself and practiced austerity, earning a reputation for integrity.
entries.literal: Sheti restrained himself and practiced austerity, and thereby gained a reputation for integrity.

entries.zh: 後頗縱妻段氏，多有受納，令僧尼因事通請，貪虐流聞。
entries.en: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan; bribes were frequent, and he used monks and nuns as intermediaries for favors; reports of greed and cruelty spread widely.
entries.literal: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan rather fully; there were many bribes, and he had monks and nuns intercede on various matters; reports of greed and cruelty spread.

entries.zh: 中散李真香出使幽州，採訪牧守政績。
entries.en: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang was sent to Youzhou to investigate the conduct of provincial governors.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang went on mission to Youzhou to investigate the achievements of provincial governors.

entries.zh: 真香驗案其罪，赦提懼死欲逃。
entries.en: Zhenxiang verified his crimes; Sheti, fearing execution, planned to flee.
entries.literal: Zhenxiang verified and prosecuted his crimes; Sheti, fearing death, wished to flee.

entries.zh: 其妻姑為太尉、東陽王丕妻，恃丕親貴，自許詣丕申訴求助，謂赦提曰：「當為訴理，幸得申雪，願且寬憂，不為異計。」
entries.en: His wife's aunt was married to Grand Commandant Pi, Prince of Dongyang; relying on Pi's rank and connections, she promised to appeal to him on Sheti's behalf, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case; if we can clear your name, set aside your worries for now and make no other plans."
entries.literal: His wife's aunt was the wife of the Grand Commandant, Prince of Dongyang Pi; relying on Pi's kinship and rank, she promised to go to Pi to plead and seek help, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case; if we can clear your name, I hope you will set aside your worries for now and make no other plans."

entries.zh: 赦提以此差自解慰。
entries.en: Sheti was somewhat reassured by this.
entries.literal: Sheti was somewhat relieved and comforted by this.

entries.zh: 段乃陳列真香昔嘗因假而過幽州，知赦提有好牛，從索不果。
entries.en: Lady Duan then argued that Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave, knew Sheti owned a fine ox, had asked for it and been refused.
entries.literal: Lady Duan then set forth that Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave, knew Sheti had a fine ox, asked for it but failed to obtain it.

entries.zh: 今臺使心協前事，[3]故威逼部下，拷楚過極，橫以無辜，證成誣罪。
entries.en: Now the imperial envoy still harbored resentment over that earlier affair; he coerced subordinates, tortured them excessively, and fabricated charges against the innocent.
entries.literal: Now the imperial envoy bore a grudge over that earlier matter; therefore he coerced subordinates, tortured them beyond all bounds, and falsely charged the innocent to fabricate a trumped-up crime.

entries.zh: 執事恐有不盡，使駕部令趙秦州重往究訊。
entries.en: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Office Zhao of Qinzhou to reinvestigate.
entries.literal: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Office Zhao of Qinzhou to investigate again.

entries.zh: 事伏如前，處赦提大辟。
entries.en: The facts were confirmed as before; Sheti was sentenced to death.
entries.literal: The facts were as before; Sheti was sentenced to the death penalty.

entries.zh: 高祖詔賜死於第。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu ordered that he be permitted to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered that he be granted death at his residence.

entries.zh: 將就盡，召妻而責之曰：「貪濁穢吾者卿也，又安吾而不得免禍，九泉之下當為仇讎矣。」
entries.en: As death approached he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "You defiled me with your greed, yet you comforted me and could not save me from ruin; in the grave we shall be enemies."
entries.literal: As he was about to die he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "It was you who defiled me with greed and corruption, yet you also comforted me and could not save me from disaster; in the nine springs below we shall be enemies."

entries.zh: 羊祉，字靈祐，太山鉅平人，晉太僕卿琇之六世孫也。
entries.en: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was a native of Juping in Taishan and sixth-generation descendant of Xiu, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud under the Jin.
entries.literal: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was a man of Juping in Taishan, sixth-generation descendant of Xiu, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud in Jin.

entries.zh: 父規之，宋任城令。
entries.en: His father Guizhi served as Magistrate of Rencheng under the Liu Song.
entries.literal: His father Guizhi was Magistrate of Rencheng under Song.

entries.zh: 世祖南討至鄒山，規之與魯郡太守崔邪利及其屬縣徐通、愛猛之等俱降，賜爵鉅平子，拜雁門太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu campaigned south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi surrendered together with Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu, and officials of subordinate counties including Xu Tong and Ai Mengzhi; he was ennobled as Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi together with Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu Commandery, and Xu Tong, Ai Mengzhi, and others of the subordinate counties all surrendered; he was granted the title Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 祉性剛愎，好刑名，為司空令輔國長史，[4]襲爵鉅平子。
entries.en: Zhi was stubborn and obstinate, with a fondness for penal law. He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.
entries.literal: Zhi's nature was stubborn and obstinate; he favored penal law. He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.

entries.zh: 侵盜公資，私營居宅，有司案之抵死，高祖特恕遠徙。
entries.en: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the authorities prosecuted him for a capital offense, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him to a distant region.
entries.literal: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the responsible offices prosecuted him to the death penalty, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him to a distant place.

entries.zh: 後還。
entries.en: He was later permitted to return.
entries.literal: Later he returned.

entries.zh: 景明初，為將作都將，加左軍將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served as Director of Palace Construction with the additional title General of the Left Army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served as Director of Palace Construction and was given the additional title General of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 四年，持節為梁州軍司，討叛氐。
entries.en: In the fourth year he bore the staff of authority as Military Commissioner of Liangzhou to campaign against rebellious Di tribes.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he bore the staff of authority as Military Commissioner of Liangzhou to campaign against rebellious Di.

entries.zh: 正始二年，王師伐蜀，以祉假節、龍驤將軍、益州刺史，出劍閣而還。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhengshi the imperial army campaigned against Shu; Zhi was appointed provisional General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yizhou, advanced through Jian'ge Pass, and returned.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the royal army campaigned against Shu; Zhi was given provisional authority as General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yizhou, advanced through Jian'ge Pass and returned.

entries.zh: 又以本將軍為秦梁二州刺史，加征虜將軍。
entries.en: He was again appointed Governor of Qin and Liang provinces with his original rank, and given the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
entries.literal: He was again appointed with his original rank as General as Governor of the two provinces Qin and Liang, with the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 天性酷忍，又不清潔。
entries.en: By nature he was cruel and dishonest.
entries.literal: By nature he was cruel and ruthless, and also not honest.

entries.zh: 坐掠人為奴婢，為御史中尉王顯所彈免。
entries.en: He was impeached and dismissed by Palace Aide of the Censorate Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
entries.literal: He was impeached and dismissed by Palace Aide of the Censorate Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.

entries.zh: 高肇南征，祉復被起為光祿大夫、假平南將軍，持節領步騎三萬先驅趣涪。
entries.en: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was again summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, bearing the staff of authority to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard toward Fu.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was again summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, bearing the staff of authority to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard hurrying to Fu.

entries.zh: 未至，世宗崩，班師。
entries.en: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.
entries.literal: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 夜中引軍，山有二徑，軍人迷而失路。
entries.en: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths, and the soldiers lost their way.
entries.literal: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths, and the soldiers lost their way in confusion.

entries.zh: 祉便斬隊副楊明達，梟首路側。
entries.en: Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head beside the road.
entries.literal: Zhi thereupon beheaded the squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head beside the road.

entries.zh: 為中尉元昭所劾，會赦免。
entries.en: He was impeached by Director Yuan Zhao but was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: He was impeached by Director Yuan Zhao and was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 後加平北將軍，未拜而卒。
entries.en: He was later given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North but died before assuming the post.
entries.literal: Later he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North but died before assuming the post.

entries.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵 張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 酈道元 谷楷
entries.en: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai
entries.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai

entries.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。
entries.en: The paths of serving the common good and cultivating oneself in solitude, of public renown and private withdrawal—these have never been the same, and the difference is ancient.
entries.literal: For benefiting all and perfecting oneself alone, the distinction between manifest and hidden—their affairs differ; this has been so for a long time.

entries.zh: 昔夷齊獲全於周武，華矞不容於太公，何哉？
entries.en: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, yet Hua Yu found no place with Duke Tai of Qi—why was this?
entries.literal: In the past Boyi and Shuqi were preserved whole under King Wu of Zhou, while Hua Yu was not tolerated by Duke Tai of Qi—why?

entries.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；
entries.en: Those who probe their motives credit them with the power to rouse the grasping from corruption;
entries.literal: Those who seek their hearts approve them for stirring the greedy to reform;

entries.zh: 督其迹者，以為束教之風。
entries.en: Those who judge them by their deeds take them as a model for restraining custom.
entries.literal: Those who scrutinize their conduct regard them as a discipline for instruction.

entries.zh: 而肥遁不反，代有人矣。
entries.en: Yet men who withdraw far into reclusion and never return back—each generation has produced them.
entries.literal: Yet those who retire deep into seclusion and do not return—every age has had such men.

entries.zh: 夷情得喪，忘懷累有。
entries.en: Indifferent to worldly passion, heedless of gain and loss—examples are many.
entries.literal: Detached from worldly emotion, gain and loss forgotten—such cases abound.

entries.zh: 比夫邁德弘道，匡俗庇民，可得而小，不可得而忽也。
entries.en: Measured against those who advance virtue, broaden the Way, reform society, and shelter the people, such men may seem small in scale, yet they cannot be dismissed lightly.
entries.literal: Compared with advancing virtue and spreading the Way, correcting custom and sheltering the people, they may be slighted but cannot be disregarded.

entries.zh: 自叔世澆浮，淳風殆盡，錐刀之末，競入成羣，而能冥心物表，介然離俗，望古獨適，求友千齡，亦異人矣。
entries.en: From the fallen age onward, honest manners have all but vanished; men scramble over the smallest profit. Yet those who can fix their minds beyond the world of things, stand aloof from vulgar life, take antiquity alone as their measure, and seek kindred spirits across a thousand years are rare beings indeed.
entries.literal: Since the decadent age, pure custom has nearly perished; at the tip of a knife's edge men rush in crowds—yet those who can darken their minds beyond things, stand apart from the vulgar, look to antiquity alone for their path, and seek friends across a thousand years are also extraordinary men.

entries.zh: 何必御霞乘雲而追日月，窮極天地，始為超遠哉。
entries.en: Why must one ride the clouds and pursue the sun and moon, traversing heaven and earth to the limit, before being called truly remote from the world?
entries.literal: Why must one ride mist and mount clouds to chase sun and moon, exhaust heaven and earth, before being deemed transcendent?

entries.zh: 今錄眭夸等為逸士傳。
entries.en: Here Sui Kua and the others are entered in a Biography of Reclusive Scholars.
entries.literal: Now Sui Kua and the others are recorded in a Biography of Reclusive Scholars.

entries.zh: 馮亮，字靈通，南陽人，蕭衍平北將軍蔡道恭之甥也。
entries.en: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, came from Nanyang; he was nephew to Xiao Yan's General Who Pacifies the North, Cai Daogong.
entries.literal: Feng Liang, styled Lingtong, was a man of Nanyang, nephew of Cai Daogong, General Who Pacifies the North under Xiao Yan.

entries.zh: 少博覽諸書，又篤好佛理。
entries.en: As a youth he read widely and was deeply devoted to Buddhist teaching.
entries.literal: In youth he read widely among books and was also deeply devoted to Buddhist doctrine.

entries.zh: 隨道恭至義陽，會中山王英平義陽而獲焉。
entries.en: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying took the city, Liang was captured.
entries.literal: He followed Daogong to Yiyang; when Prince of Zhongshan Ying pacified Yiyang he was taken captive.

entries.zh: 英素聞其名，以禮待接。
entries.en: Ying had long known his reputation and treated him with courtesy.
entries.literal: Ying had long heard his name and received him with courtesy.

entries.zh: 亮性清淨，至洛，隱居崧高，感英之德，以時展勤。
entries.en: Liang was pure in temperament; reaching Luoyang he withdrew to Mount Song, grateful for Ying's kindness, and visited him from time to time.
entries.literal: Liang's nature was pure and still; reaching Luoyang he retired to Mount Song, moved by Ying's kindness, and from time to time paid his respects.

entries.zh: 及英亡，亮奔赴，盡其哀慟。
entries.en: When Ying died, Liang rushed to the mourning and grieved to the utmost.
entries.literal: When Ying died, Liang hurried to the funeral and gave full vent to grief.

entries.zh: 世宗嘗召以為羽林監，領中書舍人，將令侍講十地諸經，固辭不拜。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong summoned him as Captain of the Feathered Forest with concurrent duty as Palace Scribe, intending to have him expound the Ten Grounds sutras; he firmly refused the appointment.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong once summoned him as Captain of the Feathered Forest and concurrently Palace Scribe, intending to have him lecture on the Ten Grounds sutras, but he firmly declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 又欲使衣幘入見，亮苦求以幅巾就朝，遂不強逼。
entries.en: The court wished him to appear in formal cap; Liang begged to attend in a plain headcloth, and they did not press him.
entries.literal: They also wished him to enter audience wearing a kerchiefed cap; Liang begged hard to attend court in a plain headcloth, and they did not force him.

entries.zh: 還山數年，與僧徒禮誦為業，蔬食飲水，有終焉之志。
entries.en: Back in the hills for years he chanted sutras with monks, lived on vegetables and water, and meant to end his days there.
entries.literal: Returning to the mountains for several years, he made ritual chanting with monks his occupation, ate vegetables and drank water, and had the will to end his days there.

entries.zh: 會逆人王敞事發，連山中沙門，而亮被執赴尚書省，十餘日，詔特免雪。
entries.en: When the rebel Wang Chang's plot surfaced, mountain monks were swept up; Liang was seized and held at the Ministry of State, then specially pardoned after ten-odd days.
entries.literal: When the rebel Wang Chang's affair broke out, mountain monks were implicated; Liang was seized and taken to the Ministry of State, but after more than ten days an edict specially cleared him.

entries.zh: 亮不敢還山，遂寓居景明寺。
entries.en: He dared not return to the hills and lodged at Jingming Temple.
entries.literal: Liang dared not return to the mountains and therefore lodged at Jingming Temple.

entries.zh: 敕給衣食及其從者數人。
entries.en: An edict provided food, clothing, and several attendants.
entries.literal: An edict supplied food and clothing for him and several attendants.

entries.zh: 後思其舊居，復還山室。
entries.en: Later, longing for his old retreat, he went back to his mountain cell.
entries.literal: Later, thinking of his old dwelling, he returned to his mountain cell.

entries.zh: 亮既雅愛山水，又兼巧思，結架巖林，甚得栖游之適，頗以此聞。
entries.en: Liang loved landscape and had a gift for design; his cliff and forest structures suited dwelling and wandering so well that fame spread.
entries.literal: Liang both loved landscape in refined taste and was also skilled in design; he built structures among cliffs and woods with great fitness for dwelling and roaming, and became known for this.

entries.zh: 世宗給其工力，[2]令與沙門統僧暹、河南尹甄琛等，周視崧高形勝之處，遂造閑居佛寺。
entries.en: The emperor gave him workmen and ordered him, with the Buddhist overseer Sengxian, Henan Intendant Zhen Chen, and others, to tour Mount Song's finest sites and build a reclusive temple.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong gave him laborers and ordered him, with the Buddhist overseer Sengxian, Henan Intendant Zhen Chen, and others, to survey Mount Song's commanding sites and there build a reclusive Buddhist temple.

entries.zh: 林泉既奇，營製又美，曲盡山居之妙。
entries.en: Wood and spring were wondrous, the construction exquisite—mountain life at its finest.
entries.literal: The woods and springs were already marvelous, the construction also beautiful, fully expressing the subtlety of mountain dwelling.

entries.zh: 亮時出京師。
entries.en: From time to time Liang came down to the capital.
entries.literal: Liang would sometimes come out to the capital.

entries.zh: 延昌二年冬，因遇篤疾，世宗敕以馬輿送令還山，居崧高道場寺。
entries.en: In winter of Yanchang year 2, gravely ill, he was sent by imperial palanquin to Mount Song's Daochang Temple.
entries.literal: In winter of the second year of Yanchang, falling gravely ill, Emperor Shizong ordered a palanquin to convey him back to the mountains; he dwelt at the Daochang Temple on Mount Song.

entries.zh: 數日而卒。
entries.en: He died within days.
entries.literal: Within several days he died.

entries.zh: 詔贈帛二百匹，以供凶事。
entries.en: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.
entries.literal: An edict granted two hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses.

entries.zh: 遺誡兄子綜，斂以衣㡊，左手持板，右手執孝經一卷，置尸盤石上，去人數里外。
entries.en: He instructed his nephew Zong: enshroud him in hemp, left hand on a tablet, right hand holding one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety; lay the body on a stone slab miles from any dwelling.
entries.literal: He left instructions to his nephew Zong: wrap the body in hemp garments; left hand hold a tablet, right hand grasp one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety; place the corpse on a flat stone several li from men.

entries.zh: 積十餘日，乃焚於山。
entries.en: After ten-odd days they burned him on the mountain.
entries.literal: After more than ten days they burned him on the mountain.

entries.zh: 以灰燼處，起佛塔經藏。
entries.en: At the ashes they raised a stupa and sutra repository.
entries.literal: At the place of ashes they raised a stupa and sutra repository.

entries.zh: 余謂論事辨物，當取正於經典之真文；
entries.en: I hold that in discussing affairs and distinguishing things one must take one's standard from the authentic text of the classics;
entries.literal: I hold that in discussing affairs and distinguishing things one should take correctness from the authentic text of the classics;

entries.zh: 援證定疑，必有驗於周孔之遺訓。
entries.en: to settle doubt by evidence one must find confirmation in what Zhou and Confucius handed down.
entries.literal: in citing evidence to settle doubt there must be verification in the surviving teachings of Zhou and Confucius.

entries.zh: 然後可以稱準的矣。
entries.en: Only then can one claim a true standard.
entries.literal: Only then may one be said to have a true measure.

entries.zh: 今禮文殘缺，聖言靡存，明堂之制，誰使正之。
entries.en: Today the ritual texts are broken, the sage's words nearly gone—who can correct the Mingtang regulations?
entries.literal: Now the ritual texts are defective, the sage's words scarcely survive, and who can set right the Mingtang regulations?

entries.zh: 是以後人紛糾，競興異論，五九之說，各信其習。
entries.en: Hence later scholars tangle in dispute, each trusting habit, the theories of five chambers and nine chambers alike clinging to custom.
entries.literal: Hence later men are tangled in dispute, each school trusting its own habit, competing to raise strange theories—the five-nine theories each believing its custom.

entries.zh: 是非無準，得失相半。
entries.en: There is no standard for right and wrong; gain and loss divide evenly.
entries.literal: Right and wrong have no standard; gain and loss are half and half.

entries.zh: 故歷代紛紜，靡所取正。
entries.en: Through the ages confusion has ruled, with nothing to adopt as correct.
entries.literal: Therefore through the ages confusion has reigned with nothing to take as correct.

entries.zh: 乃使裴頠云：「今羣儒紛糾，互相掎摭，就令其象可得而圖，其所以居用之禮莫能通也，為設虛器耳。
entries.en: This led Pei Wei to say, "Confucians now tangle in dispute, each pulling the other down; even if their forms could be drawn, the rites of use cannot be made coherent—it is empty vessels.
entries.literal: This led Pei Wei to say: "Now the Confucians are tangled, each pulling down the other; even if one could diagram their forms, the rites by which they would be used cannot be made to cohere—it is setting up empty vessels.

entries.zh: 況漢氏所作，四維之个，復不能令各處其辰。
entries.en: What the Han dynasty built, with its four corner posts, could not even place each in its proper season.
entries.literal: Moreover what the Han made—the four corner posts—again could not be made each to occupy its season.

entries.zh: 愚以為尊祖配天，其儀明著；
entries.en: Honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—these rites are clear;
entries.literal: I deem honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—their rites are clear and plain;

entries.zh: 廟宇之制，理據未分。
entries.en: temple and hall regulations—their principles remain unsettled.
entries.literal: the regulations for temples and halls—their principles are undivided.

entries.zh: 直可為殿屋以崇嚴父之祀，其餘雜碎一皆除之。」
entries.en: Build only a hall to dignify the father's sacrifice; cut away every other miscellaneous detail."
entries.literal: One need only build a hall to exalt the father's sacrifice; all other miscellaneous details should be removed."

entries.zh: 斯豈不以羣儒舛互，並乖其實，據義求衷，莫適可從哉？
entries.en: Is it not because the Confucians contradict one another, all missing the truth, so that when one seeks the mean by principle, nothing can be adopted?
entries.literal: Is this not because the Confucians contradict one another, all departing from fact, and when one seeks the mean by principle, nothing can be followed?"

entries.zh: 但恨典文殘滅，求之靡據而已矣。
entries.en: One can only regret that the canonical texts are ruined and that no firm evidence remains.
entries.literal: One only regrets that the canonical texts are destroyed and that nothing can be found to serve as evidence.

entries.zh: 乃復遂去室牖諸制。
entries.en: He then cast aside the regulations for chambers, doors, and windows as well.
entries.literal: He then went on to remove the regulations for chambers, doors, and windows.

entries.zh: 施之於教，未知其所隆政；
entries.en: Applied to teaching, one cannot tell what government it would dignify;
entries.literal: Applied to instruction, it is unknown what government it would exalt;

entries.zh: 求之於情，未可喻其所以必須。
entries.en: weighed by human feeling, one cannot explain why it must be required.
entries.literal: sought in human feeling, one cannot explain why it must be required.

entries.zh: 惜哉言乎！
entries.en: What a pity, such words!
entries.literal: Alas for such words!

entries.zh: 仲尼有言曰：「賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。」
entries.en: Confucius said, "Ci, you care for the sheep; I care for the ritual."
entries.literal: Confucius said: "Ci, you love the sheep; I love the ritual."

entries.zh: 余以為隆政必須其禮，豈彼一羊哉！
entries.en: I hold that exalting government requires ritual--surely it is not a matter of one sheep alone!
entries.literal: I hold that exalting government must require ritual—how could it be that one sheep!"

entries.zh: 推此而論，則聖人之於禮，殷勤而重之，裴頠之於禮，任意而忽之。
entries.en: By this reasoning the sage honored ritual with earnest care, while Pei Wei treated ritual arbitrarily and lightly.
entries.literal: Pushing this to discuss it, the sage toward ritual was earnest and weighty, while Pei Wei toward ritual was arbitrary and neglectful.

entries.zh: 是則頠賢於仲尼矣。
entries.en: By that logic Pei would surpass Zhongni.
entries.literal: In that case Pei would be worthier than Zhongni.

entries.zh: 以斯觀之，裴氏之子以不達而失禮之旨也。
entries.en: Seen this way, Pei's follower missed the point of ritual through incomprehension.
entries.literal: Viewed thus, the son of the Pei clan failed the aim of ritual through lack of understanding.

entries.zh: 余竊不自量，頗有鄙意，據理尋義，以求其真，貴合雅衷，不苟偏信。
entries.en: I do not presume on my own measure, yet I have a view: I seek truth by principle, value refined intent, and will not cling to partial belief.
entries.literal: I venture without measuring myself to have a humble opinion: seeking truth by principle and meaning, valuing accord with refined intent, not crediting partial belief.

entries.zh: 乃藉之以禮傳，考之以訓注，博採先賢之言，廣搜通儒之說，量其當否，參其同異，棄其所短，收其所長，推義察圖，以折厥衷。
entries.en: I rely on the ritual tradition, test it against commentaries, gather the words of former worthies and search the theories of accomplished scholars, weigh right and wrong, compare agreements and differences, discard the weak, keep the strong, and settle the mean by reasoning and diagram.
entries.literal: I therefore rely on the ritual tradition, examine commentaries, broadly gather the words of former worthies and widely search the theories of accomplished Confucians, weigh their right and wrong, compare their agreements and differences, discard what is short, gather what is long, push meaning and inspect diagrams to settle the mean.

entries.zh: 豈敢必善，聊亦合其言志矣。
entries.en: I dare not claim perfection, yet it at least matches what I mean to say.
entries.literal: I dare not claim it must be good, yet it at least accords with the intent of my words.

entries.zh: 其年，四門小學博士孔璠等學官四十五人上書曰：「竊見故處士趙郡李謐：十歲喪父，哀號罷隣人之相；
entries.en: That year Kong Fan, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School, and forty-five academic officers memorialized: "We observe the former recluse Li Mi of Zhao: at ten he lost his father and wailed until neighbors ceased condoling one another;
entries.literal: That year, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School Kong Fan and forty-five academic officers memorialized, saying: "We have observed the former recluse of Zhao commandery, Li Mi: at ten he lost his father, wailing until neighbors ceased mutual condolence;

entries.zh: 幼事兄瑒，恭順盡友于之誠。
entries.en: in youth he served his elder brother Yang with full brotherly devotion.
entries.literal: in youth he served his elder brother Yang with respectful obedience, fully displaying the sincerity of brotherly friendship.

entries.zh: 十三通孝經、論語、毛詩、尚書，歷數之術尤盡其長，州閭鄉黨有神童之號。
entries.en: At thirteen he mastered the Filial Piety Classic, Analects, Mao Odes, and Documents; in calendrical arts he excelled—district and village called him a divine child.
entries.literal: At thirteen he mastered the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, and Documents; especially in calendrical arts he exhausted his strength—throughout district and village he had the title of divine child.

entries.zh: 年十八，詣學受業，時博士即孔璠也。
entries.en: At eighteen he came to study; the erudite then was Kong Fan himself.
entries.literal: At eighteen he went to study and receive instruction; the erudite at the time was Kong Fan himself.

entries.zh: 覽始要終，論端究緒，授者無不欣其言矣。
entries.en: From first to last he traced every thread; all who heard him were delighted.
entries.literal: From beginning to end he surveyed and pursued the thread; those who received his teaching were all delighted by his words.

entries.zh: 於是鳩集諸經，廣校同異，比三傳事例，名春秋叢林，十有二卷。
entries.en: He gathered the classics, collated agreements and differences, compared the Three Commentaries, and compiled the Thicket of the Spring and Autumn in twelve scrolls.
entries.literal: Thereupon he gathered the classics, broadly collated agreements and differences, compared the examples of the Three Commentaries, and named it Thicket of the Spring and Autumn—twelve scrolls.

entries.zh: 為璠等判析隱伏，垂盈百條。
entries.en: For Fan and others he resolved hidden difficulties—more than a hundred items.
entries.literal: For Fan and others he judged hidden points, more than a hundred items in all.

entries.zh: 滯無常滯，纖毫必舉；
entries.en: Where confusion had no fixed form, he raised the slightest point;
entries.literal: Where stagnation had no constant stagnation, the slightest thread was raised;

entries.zh: 通不長通，有枉斯屈。
entries.en: where insight faltered, if there was error he corrected it.
entries.literal: where penetration did not long penetrate, if there was wrong he bent it.

entries.zh: 不苟言以違經，弗飾辭而背理。
entries.en: He would not speak carelessly against the classics or ornament words against reason.
entries.literal: He did not speak carelessly against the classics, nor ornament words against reason.

entries.zh: 辭氣磊落，觀者忘疲。
entries.en: His manner was bold and open; listeners forgot fatigue.
entries.literal: His words were bold and open; viewers forgot fatigue.

entries.zh: 每曰：『丈夫擁書萬卷，何假南面百城。』
entries.en: He often said, "A man with ten thousand scrolls—why need a hundred cities facing south?"
entries.literal: He often said: "A man with ten thousand scrolls—why need he face south over a hundred cities?"

entries.zh: 遂絕跡下幃，杜門却掃，棄產營書，手自刪削，卷無重複者四千有餘矣。
entries.en: He withdrew behind his curtain, shut his door, sold property for books, and personally edited more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.
entries.literal: Thereupon he cut off his tracks below the curtain, shut the door and swept the courtyard, abandoned property to build books, personally edited and pruned—more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.

entries.zh: 猶括次專家，搜比讜議，隆冬達曙，盛暑通宵。
entries.en: He still indexed specialists and compared commentaries—working from deep winter to dawn and through midsummer nights.
entries.literal: Still he indexed specialists and searched comparative commentaries—deep winter until dawn, midsummer through the night.

entries.zh: 雖仲舒不闚園，君伯之閉戶，高氏之遺漂，張生之忘食，方之斯人，未足為喻。
entries.en: Though Dong Zhongshu never glanced into his garden, Junbo shut his door, Gao let the grain drift, and Master Zhang forgot to eat—none equals this man.
entries.literal: Though Dong Zhongshu did not peep into the garden, Junbo shut his door, Gao's grain was left to drift, and Master Zhang forgot food—compared with this man, they are not enough for a likeness.

entries.zh: 謐嘗詣故太常卿劉芳推問音義，語及中代興廢之由，芳乃歎曰：『君若遇高祖，侍中、太常非僕有也。』
entries.en: Mi once visited former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang on sounds and meanings; speaking of dynastic rise and fall, Fang sighed: "Had you met Gaozu, Secretariat Director and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine."
entries.literal: Mi once visited the former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang to inquire about sounds and meanings; speaking of the rise and fall of the middle age, Fang sighed and said: "If you had met Emperor Gaozu, Secretariat Director and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine."

entries.zh: 前河南尹、黃門侍郎甄琛內贊近機，朝野傾目，于時親識求官者，答云：『趙郡李謐，耽學守道，不悶于時，常欲致言，但未有次耳。
entries.en: Former Henan Intendant and Palace Attendant Zhen Chen held power at court; when friends sought office he answered: "Li Mi of Zhao is absorbed in learning and keeps the Way, untroubled by the age—I have long meant to speak for him but lacked the chance.
entries.literal: The former Henan Intendant and Palace Attendant Zhen Chen inwardly assisted near policy; court and countryside turned their eyes. When acquaintances then sought office, he answered: "Li Mi of Zhao commandery is absorbed in learning and keeps the Way, not troubled by the age—I have often wished to speak for him but have not yet had the chance.

entries.zh: 諸君何為輕自媒衒？』
entries.en: Why do you lightly peddle yourselves?"
entries.literal: Why do you gentlemen lightly advertise yourselves?"

entries.zh: 謂其子曰：『昔鄭玄、盧植不遠數千里詣扶風馬融，今汝明師甚邇，何不就業也？』
entries.en: He told his son, "Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi once traveled thousands of li to study with Ma Rong in Fufeng; your teacher is near—why not study?"
entries.literal: He told his son: "In the past Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi traveled thousands of li to Fufeng to study with Ma Rong; now your bright teacher is very near—why not take instruction?"

entries.zh: 又謂朝士曰：『甄琛行不媿時，但未薦李謐，以此負朝廷耳。』
entries.en: He told court gentlemen, "Zhen Chen's conduct does not shame the age, but he failed the court by not recommending Li Mi."
entries.literal: He also told court gentlemen: "Zhen Chen's conduct does not shame the age, but only that he did not recommend Li Mi—by this he failed the court."

entries.zh: 又結宇依巖，憑崖鑿室，方欲訓彼青衿，宣揚墳典，冀西河之教重興、北海之風不墜。
entries.en: He built cliff dwellings and carved rock rooms, intending to teach young scholars and spread the classics, hoping to revive Xihe's teaching and keep Beihai's wind alive.
entries.literal: He also built a dwelling against the cliff, carved rooms in the rock, intending to instruct the blue-collared youths, spread the classics of the tombs, hoping to revive the teaching of Xihe and keep the wind of Beihai from falling.

entries.zh: 而祐善空聞，暴疾而卒。
entries.en: Yet Heaven's favor rang hollow; he died suddenly.
entries.literal: Yet Heaven's favor was heard only in vain; he died suddenly of a violent illness.

entries.zh: 邦國銜殄悴之哀，儒生結摧梁之慕。
entries.en: The realm mourned a broken pillar; scholars mourned a fallen beam.
entries.literal: The state bore the grief of ruin and withering; Confucian students bound the sorrow of a broken beam.

entries.zh: 況璠等或服議下風，或親承音旨，師儒之義，其可默乎！」
entries.en: How much more Fan and others, some submitting to his teaching, some hearing him in person—how could teacher and student stay silent!"
entries.literal: How much more Fan and others, some submitting to his arguments, some personally receiving his instruction—the duty of teacher and student—how could they be silent!"

entries.zh: 事奏，詔曰：「謐屢辭徵辟，志守沖素，儒隱之操，深可嘉美。
entries.en: The memorial reached the throne; the edict said, "Mi repeatedly declined summons; his will guards pure simplicity—recluse conduct deeply praiseworthy.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict said: "Mi repeatedly declined summons and commissions, his will guarding pure simplicity—recluse-Confucian conduct deeply praiseworthy.

entries.zh: 可遠傍惠、康，近準玄晏，諡曰貞靜處士，并表其門閭，以旌高節。」
entries.en: Compare him from afar to Hui and Kang, near at hand to Xuan Yan; grant the posthumous title Recluse of Upright Stillness and mark his gate and lane to honor his integrity."
entries.literal: He may be compared at a distance to Hui and Kang, at hand to Xuan Yan; posthumous title Recluse of Upright Stillness, and his gate and lane are to be marked to honor his lofty integrity."

entries.zh: 遣謁者奉冊，於是表其門曰文德，里曰孝義云。
entries.en: A messenger bore the patent; his gate was marked Literary Virtue and his lane Filial Duty.
entries.literal: A messenger was sent with the patent; thereupon his gate was marked Literary Virtue and his lane Filial Duty."

entries.zh: 世宗給其工力 諸本「世宗」作「世祖」，北史卷八八作「宣武」。
entries.en: "The emperor gave him laborers": editions read "ancestral emperor"; Northern History scroll 88 reads "Xuanwu."
entries.literal: The emperor gave him laborers: in various editions "emperor" reads "ancestral emperor"; Northern History scroll 88 reads "Xuanwu."

entries.zh: 按上已見「世宗」，「祖」是「宗」之訛，今據改。
entries.en: "Emperor" already appears above; "ancestral" is a corruption of "emperor"—corrected here.
entries.literal: Since "emperor" already appears above, "ancestral" is an error for "emperor"—now corrected accordingly.

entries.zh: 眭夸 馮亮 李謐 鄭脩
entries.en: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, and Zheng Xiu
entries.literal: Sui Kua, Feng Liang, Li Mi, Zheng Xiu

entries.zh: 漁陽太守陽尼妻高氏，勃海人。
entries.en: Lady Gao, consort of Yang Ni, Administrator of Yuyang, was a native of Bohai.
entries.literal: Lady Gao, wife of Yang Ni, Administrator of Yuyang, was a native of Bohai.

entries.zh: 學識有文才，高祖敕令入侍後宮。
entries.en: Learned and gifted with literary talent, Emperor Gaozu ordered her to serve in the inner palace.
entries.literal: Learned and accomplished, with literary talent, Emperor Gaozu ordered her to attend in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 幽后表啟，悉其辭也。
entries.en: The memorials and reports of Empress You were entirely composed by her.
entries.literal: The memorials and reports of Empress You were entirely in her wording.

entries.zh: 任城國太妃孟氏，鉅鹿人，尚書令、任城王澄之母。
entries.en: Grand Consort Meng of Rencheng was a native of Julu and mother of Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.
entries.literal: Grand Consort Meng of the State of Rencheng was a native of Julu and mother of Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.

entries.zh: 澄為揚州之日，率眾出討。
entries.en: When Cheng served in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.
entries.literal: When Cheng was in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.

entries.zh: 於後賊帥姜慶真陰結逆黨，襲陷羅城。
entries.en: Afterward the rebel leader Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined traitors and seized Luocheng in a surprise attack.
entries.literal: Afterward the bandit chief Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined rebellious factions and in a surprise attack seized Luocheng.

entries.zh: 長史韋纘倉卒失圖，計無所出。
entries.en: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was caught unprepared and could think of no plan.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan in the emergency lost his plan and had no course to take.

entries.zh: 孟乃勒兵登陴，先守要便。
entries.en: Meng then rallied the troops onto the battlements and secured the strategic points.
entries.literal: Meng then marshaled troops onto the battlements and first secured the strategic points.

entries.zh: 激厲文武，安慰新舊，勸以賞罰，喻之逆順，於是咸有奮志。
entries.en: She roused the civil and military officers, comforted old and new alike, urged them with rewards and punishments, and taught them the difference between loyalty and treason; all were stirred to fight.
entries.literal: She roused civil and military officers, comforted old and new alike, urged them with rewards and punishments, and instructed them in loyalty and rebellion; thereby all were stirred to resolve.

entries.zh: 親自巡守，不避矢石。
entries.en: She personally made the rounds on the walls, heedless of arrows and stones.
entries.literal: She personally made the rounds on guard, not avoiding arrows and stones.

entries.zh: 賊不能克，卒以全城。
entries.en: The rebels could not take the city, and the whole fortress was preserved.
entries.literal: The rebels could not overcome them and in the end the whole city was preserved.

entries.zh: 澄以狀表聞，屬世宗崩，[8]事寢。
entries.en: Cheng reported the matter to the throne, but Emperor Shizong died [8] and the matter was set aside.
entries.literal: Cheng memorialized the circumstances; as it happened Emperor Shizong died, [8] and the matter was set aside.

entries.zh: 靈太后後令曰：「鴻功盛美，實宜垂之永年。」
entries.en: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered: "Such great merit and splendid virtue ought to be handed down through the ages."
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered: "Great merit and splendid virtue truly ought to be handed down through the ages."

entries.zh: 乃敕有司樹碑旌美。
entries.en: She then ordered the authorities to erect a stele in her honor.
entries.literal: She then ordered the authorities to erect a stele proclaiming her excellence.

entries.zh: 屬世宗崩 諸本「宗」作「祖」。
entries.en: "As it happened Emperor Shizong died": various editions read "Ancestor" instead of "Shizong."
entries.literal: "As it happened Emperor Shizong died": in various editions "Shizong" is written as "Ancestor."

entries.zh: 按卷八世宗紀事在正始元年二月，「祖」字訛，今改正。
entries.en: Note: juan 8's annals of Emperor Shizong date the event to the second month of the first year of Zhengshi; "Ancestor" is a corrupt reading and is corrected here.
entries.literal: Note: the annals of Emperor Shizong in juan 8 place the event in the second month of the first year of Zhengshi; "Ancestor" is a corrupt character and is corrected here.

entries.zh: 苟金龍妻劉氏，平原人也。
entries.en: Lady Liu, consort of Gou Jinlong, was a native of Pingyuan.
entries.literal: Lady Liu, wife of Gou Jinlong, was a native of Pingyuan.

entries.zh: 廷尉少卿劉叔宗之姊。
entries.en: She was the elder sister of Vice Director of Justice Liu Shuzong.
entries.literal: She was the elder sister of Vice Director of Justice Liu Shuzong.

entries.zh: 世宗時，金龍為梓潼太守，郡帶關城戍主。
entries.en: During Emperor Shizong's reign, Jinlong served as Administrator of Zitong and commander of the garrison at Guancheng.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong, Jinlong was Administrator of Zitong; the commandery included Guancheng, where he was garrison commander.

entries.zh: [9]蕭衍遣眾攻圍，值金龍疾病，不堪部分，眾甚危懼。
entries.en: [9] Xiao Yan sent troops to besiege the city; Jinlong fell ill and could not command—the garrison was gripped with fear.
entries.literal: [9] Xiao Yan sent troops to attack and besiege them; as it happened Jinlong was ill and unable to deploy forces—the troops were greatly fearful.

entries.zh: 劉遂率厲城民，修理戰具，一夜悉成。
entries.en: Liu rallied the townspeople, repaired the weapons of war, and finished everything in a single night.
entries.literal: Liu then led and encouraged the city folk, repaired war equipment, and in one night all was completed.

entries.zh: 拒戰百有餘日，兵士死傷過半。
entries.en: They held out for more than a hundred days; more than half the soldiers were killed or wounded.
entries.literal: They resisted battle for more than a hundred days; soldiers killed and wounded exceeded half.

entries.zh: 戍副高景陰圖叛逆，劉斬之，及其黨與數十人。
entries.en: Deputy commander Gao Jing secretly plotted treason; Liu beheaded him and several dozen of his followers.
entries.literal: Deputy garrison commander Gao Jing secretly plotted rebellion; Liu beheaded him along with several tens of his associates.

entries.zh: 自餘將士，分衣減食，勞逸必同，莫不畏而懷之。
entries.en: She shared clothing and reduced rations among the remaining troops, sharing hardship and ease alike; all revered and embraced her.
entries.literal: As for the remaining officers and soldiers, she divided clothing and reduced rations, sharing hardship and ease alike; none failed to revere and embrace her.

entries.zh: 井在外城，尋為賊陷，城中絕水，渴死者多。
entries.en: The wells lay outside the outer wall and soon fell to the enemy; water inside the city ran out and many died of thirst.
entries.literal: The wells lay outside the outer wall and soon fell to the rebels; within the city water was cut off and many died of thirst.

entries.zh: 劉乃集諸長幼，喻以忠節，遂相率告訴於天，俱時號叫，俄而澍雨。
entries.en: Liu gathered young and old, taught them loyalty and integrity, and led them in crying out to Heaven together; shortly afterward a soaking rain fell.
entries.literal: Liu then gathered elders and young, instructed them in loyalty and integrity, and they together appealed to Heaven, all crying out at once; shortly afterward a soaking rain fell.

entries.zh: 劉命出公私布絹及至衣服，懸之城中，絞而取水，所有雜器悉儲之。
entries.en: Liu ordered cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, and wrung for water; every vessel was put to use.
entries.literal: Liu ordered public and private cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, wrung to draw water, and all miscellaneous vessels stored for the purpose.

entries.zh: 於是人心益固。
entries.en: The people's resolve grew firmer still.
entries.literal: Thereupon the people's hearts grew firmer still.

entries.zh: 會益州刺史傅豎眼將至，賊乃退散。
entries.en: Just then Inspector of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was approaching, and the enemy dispersed.
entries.literal: It happened that Inspector of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was about to arrive, and the rebels then dispersed and withdrew.

entries.zh: 豎眼歎異，具狀奏聞，世宗嘉之。
entries.en: Shuyan marveled at her deeds and reported them to the throne; Emperor Shizong praised her.
entries.literal: Shuyan marveled and reported the full circumstances; Emperor Shizong commended her.

entries.zh: 正光中，賞平昌縣開國子，邑二百戶，授子慶珍，又得二子出身。
entries.en: In the Zhengguang era, her son Qingzhen was granted the title Viscount of Pingchang with a fief of two hundred households, and two other sons received entry into office.
entries.literal: In the Zhengguang era, she was rewarded with the title Viscount of Pingchang County, fief of two hundred households, granted to her son Qingzhen, and two sons additionally received entry into office.

entries.zh: 慶珍卒，子純陀襲。
entries.en: When Qingzhen died, his son Chuntuo inherited the title.
entries.literal: Qingzhen died; his son Chuntuo inherited.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。
entries.en: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced accordingly.
entries.literal: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced by precedent.

entries.zh: 崔覽妻封氏 封卓妻劉氏 魏溥妻房氏 胡長命妻張氏 平原女子孫氏 房愛親妻崔氏 涇州貞女兕先氏[1] 姚氏婦楊氏 張洪初妻劉氏[2] 董景起妻張氏 陽尼妻高氏 史映周妻耿氏 任城國太妃孟氏 苟金龍妻劉氏 盧元禮妻李氏 河東孝女姚氏 刁思遵妻魯氏
entries.en: Lady Feng, consort of Cui Lan; Lady Liu, consort of Feng Zhuo; Lady Fang, consort of Wei Pu; Lady Zhang, consort of Hu Changming; Sun Nanyu of Pingyuan; Lady Cui, consort of Fang Aiqin; the chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture; Lady Yang of the Yao household; Lady Liu, consort of Zhang Hongchu; Lady Zhang, consort of Dong Jingqi; Lady Gao, consort of Yang Ni; Lady Geng, consort of Shi Yingzhou; Grand Consort Meng of Rencheng; Lady Liu, consort of Gou Jinlong; Lady Li, consort of Lu Yuanli; the filial daughter Yao of Hedong; Lady Lu, consort of Diao Sizun.
entries.literal: Cui Lan's wife Lady Feng; Feng Zhuo's wife Lady Liu; Wei Pu's wife Lady Fang; Hu Changming's wife Lady Zhang; the woman Sun of Pingyuan; Fang Aiqin's wife Lady Cui; the chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture; Lady Yang, daughter-in-law of the Yao clan; Zhang Hongchu's wife Lady Liu; Dong Jingqi's wife Lady Zhang; Yang Ni's wife Lady Gao; Shi Yingzhou's wife Lady Geng; Grand Consort Meng of the State of Rencheng; Gou Jinlong's wife Lady Liu; Lu Yuanli's wife Lady Li; the filial daughter Yao of Hedong; Diao Sizun's wife Lady Lu.

entries.zh: 悅子子建，字敬忠。
entries.en: Yue's son Zijian, styled Jingzhong.
entries.literal: Yue's son Zijian, courtesy name Jingzhong.

entries.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，累遷太尉從事中郎。
entries.en: After beginning his career as Attending Counselor at Court, he was promoted repeatedly until he became Attendant to the Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he became Attending Counselor at Court; through successive promotions he rose to Attendant of the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 初，世宗時平氐，[4]遂於武興立鎮，尋改為東益州。
entries.en: Earlier, during Emperor Shizong's reign the Di were subdued, [4] and a military post was set up at Wuxing, which before long became the province of Eastern Yizhou.
entries.literal: Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified, [4] and a garrison was established at Wuxing, soon changed to Eastern Yizhou.

entries.zh: 其後鎮將、刺史乖失人和，羣氐作梗，遂為邊患，乃除子建為東益州刺史。
entries.en: Later the garrison commanders and provincial inspectors failed to maintain good relations with the people. The Di rose in obstruction and the region became a border trouble spot, so Zijian was appointed governor of Eastern Yizhou.
entries.literal: Thereafter the garrison commander and regional inspector lost harmony with the people; the Di tribes caused obstruction and it became a border affliction, so Zijian was appointed Regional Inspector of Eastern Yizhou.

entries.zh: 子建布以恩信，風化大行，遠近清靜。
entries.en: Zijian governed with kindness and integrity. His influence spread widely, and peace returned to the region near and far.
entries.literal: Zijian spread favor and trust; moral transformation was greatly practiced, and far and near were quiet and clear.

entries.zh: 正光五年，南、北二秦城人莫折念生、韓祖香、張長命相繼構逆，僉以州城之人莫不勁勇，同類悉反，宜先收其器械。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, Mo She Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming led successive rebellions among the townspeople of the two Qin provinces. Officials agreed that the capital's inhabitants were fierce fighters and that their clansmen had already risen in revolt, so their arms should be seized first.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, city people of Southern and Northern Er Qin—Mo She Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming—in succession raised rebellion; all agreed that the people of the provincial capital were without exception stalwart and brave, their kindred all having turned rebel, and that their weapons ought first be confiscated.

entries.zh: 子建以為城人數當行陳，盡皆驍果，安之足以為用，急之腹背為憂，乃悉召居城老壯曉示之；
entries.en: Zijian reasoned that these city dwellers were men slated for military service—every one of them tough and battle-ready. Treat them well and they could be enlisted; push them hard and they would become a danger on every side. So he called together all the elderly and able-bodied residents and explained his thinking to them.
entries.literal: Zijian held that the city people were those who were due to serve in the ranks, all of them fierce and resolute; if pacified they would suffice for use, but if pressed, trouble front and rear would be the concern; he therefore summoned all old and young dwelling in the city and explained this to them;

entries.zh: 并上言諸城人本非罪坐而來者悉求聽免。
entries.en: He also petitioned the throne to exempt and release all those city dwellers who had been sent there for reasons other than criminal punishment.
entries.literal: And in a memorial he requested that all city people who had come not because of criminal conviction be granted exemption and released.

entries.zh: 肅宗優詔從之。
entries.en: Emperor Suzong graciously approved the request by imperial edict.
entries.literal: Emperor Suzong graciously issued an edict acceding.

entries.zh: 子建漸分其父兄子弟外居郡戍，內外相顧，終獲保全。
entries.en: Zijian gradually posted the fathers, brothers, and sons of local families to garrisons outside the city, so that those inside and out could keep watch on one another, and in this way the community was preserved.
entries.literal: Zijian gradually dispersed the fathers, elder and younger brothers, and sons of families to dwell outside at district garrisons; inside and outside watched over one another, and in the end preservation was achieved.

entries.zh: 及秦賊乘勝，屯營黑水，子建乃潛使掩襲，前後斬獲甚眾，威名赫然，先反者及此悉降。
entries.en: When the Qin rebels pressed their advantage and made camp at Black Water, Zijian sent troops in a secret raid. They killed and captured large numbers of enemy fighters, his prestige soared, and those who had rebelled earlier submitted one after another.
entries.literal: When the Qin rebels seized victory and encamped at Black Water, Zijian then secretly sent men to launch a surprise attack; before and after many were beheaded and captured, his awesomeness was brilliant, and those who had first rebelled and those here all submitted.

entries.zh: 乃間使上聞，肅宗甚嘉之，詔子建兼尚書為行臺，刺史如故。
entries.en: He sent word through a special messenger. Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed Zijian Director of the Secretariat with authority as a mobile imperial commission, while retaining his post as provincial governor.
entries.literal: Then through an intermediary he reported upward; Suzong greatly praised this, and ordered Zijian additionally as Director of the Secretariat to serve as Mobile Office, regional inspector as before.

entries.zh: 於是威震蜀土，其梁、巴、二益、兩秦之事，皆所節度。
entries.en: His authority now extended across the Shu region, and he had supervisory power over affairs in Liang, Ba, the two Yizhou provinces, and the two Qin provinces.
entries.literal: Thereupon his prestige shook the lands of Shu; matters of Liang, Ba, the two Yis, and the two Qins were all under his coordination.

entries.zh: 梁州刺史傅豎眼子敬和中心以為愧，在洛大行貨賄，以圖行臺。
entries.en: Fu Jinghe, son of Liangzhou governor Fu Shuyan, felt deeply aggrieved. In Luoyang he spent lavishly on bribes, angling for the mobile commission post.
entries.literal: Jinghe, son of Fu Shuyan, Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, felt shame at heart; in Luoyang he extensively engaged in bribery, seeking the mobile office position.

entries.zh: 先是，子建亦屢求歸京師，至此，乃遣刺史唐永代焉，[5]豎眼因為行臺。
entries.en: Zijian had already been asking repeatedly to return to the capital. At this juncture Tang Yong was sent as provincial governor to replace him, [5] and Fu Shuyan took over the mobile commission.
entries.literal: Before this, Zijian also had repeatedly sought return to the capital; at this point, Regional Inspector Tang Yong was sent to replace him, [5] and Shuyan thereby became mobile office.

entries.zh: 子建將還，羣氐慕戀，相率斷道。
entries.en: When Zijian prepared to leave, the Di people, who cherished him, gathered in groups and blocked the road.
entries.literal: As Zijian was about to return, the Di tribes, cherishing attachment, one after another blocked the road.

entries.zh: 主簿楊僧覆先行曉喻，諸氐忿曰：「我留刺史，爾送出也！」
entries.en: Chief Clerk Yang Sengfu went ahead to reason with them. The Di shouted angrily: "We kept our governor here—you're the ones trying to escort him away!"
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Yang Sengfu went ahead first to explain and persuade; the Di angrily said: "We kept the regional inspector—you are the ones to see him off!"

entries.zh: 斫之數創，幾死。
entries.en: They hacked him repeatedly and nearly killed him.
entries.literal: They hacked him with many wounds, and he nearly died.

entries.zh: 子建徐加慰譬，旬日方得前行，吏人贈遺，一無所受。
entries.en: Zijian gently soothed and reassured them, and only after ten days could he continue on his way. He accepted none of the gifts the officials and commoners pressed upon him.
entries.literal: Zijian gradually added consolation and instruction; only after ten days could he proceed forward; gifts from officials and people he accepted not one.

entries.zh: 而東益氐、蜀尋反，攻逼唐永，永棄城而走，乃喪一藩矣。
entries.en: Before long the Di and Shu peoples of Eastern Yizhou rebelled, attacked Tang Yong, and drove him to abandon the city and flee—the province was lost.
entries.literal: But the Di and Shu of Eastern Yizhou soon rebelled, pressing Tang Yong in attack; Yong abandoned the city and fled—thus a frontier defense was lost.

entries.zh: 初永之走，子建客有沙門曇璨及鉅鹿人耿顯皆沒落氐手，及知子建之客，垂泣追衣物還之，送出白馬。
entries.en: When Yong fled, two of Zijian's companions—the monk Tancan and Geng Xian of Julu—were seized by the Di. Learning they were Zijian's men, the Di wept, restored their stolen possessions, and saw them safely out at White Horse Pass.
entries.literal: When Yong fled, among Zijian's retainers the monk Tancan and Julu native Geng Xian both fell into Di hands; when they learned they were Zijian's guests, weeping they pursued to return their clothing and goods, escorting them out at White Horse.

entries.zh: 遺愛所被如此。
entries.en: Such was the depth of affection he had inspired.
entries.literal: The legacy love he left was such as this.

entries.zh: 自國家開華陽等郡，梁州邢巒、益州傅豎眼及子建為最。
entries.en: From the time the empire established Huayang and other districts, Xing Luan in Liangzhou, Fu Shuyan in Yizhou, and Zijian were ranked the finest governors.
entries.literal: Since the state opened Huayang and other commanderies, Xing Luan of Liangzhou, Fu Shuyan of Yizhou, and Zijian were foremost.

entries.zh: 初，子建為前軍將軍，十年不徙，在洛閑暇，與吏部尚書李韶、韶從弟延寔頗為弈棊，時人謂為耽好。
entries.en: When Zijian served as General of the Vanguard he remained in that post for ten years without transfer. During his idle days in Luoyang he often played go with Li Shao, Director of Personnel, and Shao's cousin Yanbao—pastimes that contemporaries dismissed as frivolous indulgence.
entries.literal: Initially Zijian was General of the Vanguard; for ten years he was not transferred; in Luoyang in leisure, with Director of Personnel Li Shao and Shao's cousin Yanbao he fairly often played weiqi; people of the time called it a distracting passion.

entries.zh: 子建每曰：「棊於機權廉勇之際，得之深矣。
entries.en: Zijian often remarked: "In the game of go one learns deeply about timing, authority, integrity, and courage at decisive moments.
entries.literal: Zijian often said: "In weiqi, at the junctures of stratagem, authority, integrity, and courage, one gains profound insight.

entries.zh: 且吾未為時用，博弈可也。」
entries.en: Besides, I have not yet been put to use by the age—a game or two is harmless enough."
entries.literal: Moreover, I am not yet employed by the times—gaming and gambling are permissible."

entries.zh: 及一臨邊事，凡經五年，未曾對局。
entries.en: Once he took up frontier duties, he went five full years without playing a single match.
entries.literal: Once he took charge of border affairs, for fully five years he never faced a board.

entries.zh: 初世宗時平氐 諸本「世宗」作「世祖」，北史卷五六作「宣武」
entries.en: On "Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified"—various editions read "Shizu" for "Shizong," and scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "Xuanwu"
entries.literal: "Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified"—in various editions "Shizong" reads "Shizu"; scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "Xuanwu"

entries.zh: 〈即世宗元恪〉。
entries.en: 〈that is, Emperor Shizong Yuan Ke〉
entries.literal: 〈that is, Emperor Shizong Yuan Ke〉

entries.zh: 按事見卷八世宗紀正始三年正月壬申、卷七０傅豎眼傳、卷一０一氐傳補，「祖」乃「宗」之訛，今據改。
entries.en: The event appears in the Annals of Emperor Shizong (Zhengshi 3, first month, renshen day), the biography of Fu Shuyan in scroll 70, and the supplementary biography of the Di in scroll 101. "Zu" is a corruption of "zong," and the text is emended accordingly.
entries.literal: According to examination, the event appears in the Annals of Emperor Shizong for the third year of Zhengshi, first month, renshen; the biography of Fu Shuyan in scroll 70; and the supplementary biography of the Di in scroll 101—"zu" is a corruption of "zong," and the text is emended accordingly.

entries.zh: 二年，受詔撰魏史，除魏尹，故優以祿力，專在史閣，不知郡事。
entries.en: In the second year he received an edict to compile the History of Wei and was appointed administrator of the Wei capital. Given generous salary and support, he worked exclusively in the historiography office and paid no attention to local administration.
entries.literal: In the second year, he received an edict to compile the History of Wei, was appointed Administrator of Wei Capital, and therefore given generous salary and support, devoted entirely to the historiography office, unaware of commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 初，帝令羣臣各言志，收曰：「臣願得直筆東觀，早出魏書。」
entries.en: When the emperor first asked his ministers to declare their ambitions, Shou said: "I wish to write history with an honest brush at the Eastern Pavilion and complete the History of Wei without delay."
entries.literal: Initially the emperor ordered the ministers each to state their ambitions; Shou said: "Your servant wishes to wield the straight brush at the Eastern Pavilion and bring forth the History of Wei early."

entries.zh: 故帝使收專其任。
entries.en: The emperor therefore entrusted the entire project to Shou.
entries.literal: Therefore the emperor had Shou take sole charge of the task.

entries.zh: 又詔平原王高隆之總監之，隆之署名而已。
entries.en: An edict also named Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi as general supervisor, but Longzhi did nothing more than sign his name.
entries.literal: An edict also appointed Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi as general supervisor; Longzhi merely affixed his signature.

entries.zh: 帝敕收曰：「好直筆，我終不作魏太武誅史官。」
entries.en: The emperor told Shou: "Write honestly—I will never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei did and kill the historiographers."
entries.literal: The emperor admonished Shou: "Write with a straight brush—I will never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei and execute historiographers."

entries.zh: 始魏初鄧淵撰代記十餘卷，其後崔浩典史，游雅、高允、程駿、李彪、崔光、李琰之世修其業。
entries.en: At the founding of Wei, Deng Yuan compiled the Annals of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls. Later Cui Hao directed the historiography, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, and Li Yanzhi carried on the tradition through successive generations.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Deng Yuan compiled the Annals of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; thereafter Cui Hao took charge of the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, and Li Yanzhi successively continued the work.

entries.zh: 浩為編年體，彪始分作紀表志傳，書猶未出。
