entries.en: Hao wrote in annalistic form; Biao first organized the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the history had still not been published.
entries.literal: Hao used the annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the book had still not been published.

entries.zh: 世宗時，命邢巒追撰高祖起居注，書至太和十四年，又命崔鴻、王遵業補續焉。
entries.en: During Emperor Shizong's reign Xing Luan was ordered to compile the Daily Records of Emperor Gaozu, bringing the account down to the fourteenth year of Taihe; Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were also ordered to continue the work.
entries.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time, Xing Luan was ordered to compile the Daily Records of Emperor Gaozu, the text reaching to the fourteenth year of Taihe; Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were also ordered to continue it.

entries.zh: 下訖肅宗，事甚委悉。
entries.en: The record extended through Emperor Suzong and was exceedingly detailed.
entries.literal: It extended down to Emperor Suzong, and the events were very detailed.

entries.zh: 濟陰王暉業撰辨宗室錄三十卷。
entries.en: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.
entries.literal: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.

entries.zh: 收於是與通直常侍房延祐，司空司馬辛元植，國子博士刁柔、裴昂之，尚書郎高孝幹博總斟酌，[8]以成魏書。
entries.en: Shou then worked with Direct Attendant Fang Yanyou, Secretary to the Minister of Works Xin Yuanzhi, Erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Xiaogan to gather and evaluate sources broadly, [8] and complete the History of Wei.
entries.literal: Shou thereupon, together with Direct Attendant Fang Yanyou, Secretary to the Minister of Works Xin Yuanzhi, Erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Xiaogan, broadly gathered and weighed materials, [8] to complete the History of Wei.

entries.zh: 辨定名稱，隨條甄舉，又搜採亡遺，綴續後事，備一代史籍，表而上聞。
entries.en: He standardized names and titles, selected material category by category, recovered lost records, and continued the account of later events, completing the historical record of an entire dynasty, which he submitted to the throne.
entries.literal: He fixed names and titles, selected entries according to each category, also searched out what was lost and missing, patched and continued later events, completing the historical records of an entire dynasty, and submitted the tables in memorial to the throne.

entries.zh: 勒成一代大典，凡十二紀、九十二列傳，合一百一十卷，五年三月奏上之。
entries.en: He produced the great historical canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographies, one hundred and ten scrolls in all, submitted in the third month of the fifth year.
entries.literal: He carved out the great canon of a generation: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical accounts in all, totaling one hundred and ten scrolls, memorialized and submitted in the third month of the fifth year.

entries.zh: 秋，除梁州刺史，收以志未成，奏請終業，許之。
entries.en: That autumn he was appointed governor of Liangzhou, but Shou petitioned to remain until the treatises were finished, and his request was granted.
entries.literal: In autumn he was appointed Regional Inspector of Liangzhou; Shou, because the treatises were not yet complete, memorialized requesting to finish the work, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 十一月，復奏十志：天象四卷，地形三卷，律歷二卷，禮、樂四卷，食貨一卷，刑罰一卷，靈徵二卷，官氏二卷，釋老一卷，凡二十卷，續於紀傳，合一百三十卷，分為十二帙。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena (4 scrolls), Geography (3), Calendars and Chronology (2), Rites and Music (4), Food and Goods (1), Punishments (1), Spiritual Signs (2), Offices and Clans (2), and Buddhism and Daoism (1)—twenty scrolls in all, appended to the annals and biographies for a total of one hundred and thirty scrolls in twelve fascicles.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he again memorialized the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena, four scrolls; Geography, three scrolls; Calendars and Chronology, two scrolls; Rites and Music, four scrolls; Food and Goods, one scroll; Punishments, one scroll; Spiritual Signs, two scrolls; Offices and Clans, two scrolls; Buddhism and Daoism, one scroll—twenty scrolls in all, continuing the annals and biographies, one hundred and thirty scrolls in total, divided into twelve fascicles.

entries.zh: 其史三十五例，二十五序，九十四論，前後二表一啟焉。
entries.en: The history also included thirty-five precedents, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and two tables plus one memorial.
entries.literal: The history included thirty-five precedents, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and in all two tables and one memorial.

entries.zh: 還洛後，俄拜常侍、衞尉卿。
entries.en: After returning to Luoyang he was soon made Regular Attendant and Commandant of the Guard.
entries.literal: After returning to Luoyang, he was soon appointed Regular Attendant and Commandant of Guards.

entries.zh: 初，元顥內逼，莊帝北幸，子建謂所親盧義僖曰：「北海自絕社稷，稱藩蕭衍，吾老矣，豈能為陪臣？」
entries.en: When Yuan Hao advanced on the capital and Emperor Zhuang fled north, Zijian told his confidant Lu Yixi: "Beihai has abandoned the imperial altars and declared himself a vassal of Xiao Yan. I am too old to serve as anyone's subordinate minister."
entries.literal: Initially, when Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang fled north; Zijian said to his close associate Lu Yixi: "Beihai has severed himself from the state altars and declared himself vassal to Xiao Yan—I am old; how could I become a subordinate minister?"

entries.zh: 遂攜家口居洛南，顥平乃歸。
entries.en: He moved his family south of the Luo River, and only returned after Yuan Hao's defeat.
entries.literal: Thereupon taking family and dependents he dwelt south of the Luo River; when Hao was pacified he then returned.

entries.zh: 先苦風痺，及此遂甚，以卿任有務，屢上書乞身，特除右光祿大夫。
entries.en: He had long suffered from rheumatism, which now worsened considerably. Burdened by official responsibilities despite his illness, he repeatedly petitioned to retire and was specially appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right.
entries.literal: Previously he suffered painful rheumatism; at this time it grew severe; because of his court duties, he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire; specially appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 邢杲之平，太傅李延寔子侍中彧為大使，撫慰東土，時外戚貴盛，送客填門，子建亦往候別。
entries.en: After the suppression of Xing Gao's rebellion, Li Yu—son of Grand Tutor Li Yanbao and Attendant-in-Ordinary—was sent as imperial envoy to pacify the eastern provinces. The emperor's powerful in-laws saw such envoys off in great numbers, and Zijian went to bid Yu farewell as well.
entries.literal: When Xing Gao was pacified, Grand Tutor Li Yanbao's son, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu, was grand envoy to console the eastern lands; at that time the emperor's maternal relatives were noble and flourishing, farewell guests filled the gates, and Zijian also went to bid farewell.

entries.zh: 延寔曰：「小兒今行，何以相勗？」
entries.en: Yanbao asked: "My son is setting out today—what advice would you give him?"
entries.literal: Yanbao said: "My young son departs today—what counsel have you to offer?"

entries.zh: 子建曰：「益以盈滿為誡。」
entries.en: Zijian replied: "Warn him against the dangers of excess and overreach."
entries.literal: Zijian said: "Admonish him that fullness and excess are to be taken as warning."

entries.zh: 延寔悵然久之。
entries.en: Yanbao stood in gloomy silence for a long while.
entries.literal: Yanbao was long wistful and sorrowful.

entries.zh: 及莊帝殺尒朱榮，遇禍於河陰者其家率相弔賀。
entries.en: After Emperor Zhuang had Erzhu Rong killed, families whose relatives had been killed at Heyin exchanged ostensible condolences that were really celebrations.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuang killed Erzhu Rong, families of those who met calamity at Heyin mostly congratulated one another in condolence.

entries.zh: 太尉李虔第二子仁曜，子建之女壻，往亦見害。
entries.en: Li Renyao, second son of Grand Commandant Li Qian and Zijian's son-in-law, was among the dead.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Li Qian's second son Renyao, Zijian's son-in-law, also went and was killed.

entries.zh: 子建謂姨弟盧道虔曰：「朝廷誅翦權強，凶徒尚梗，未聞有奇謀異略，恐不可濟。
entries.en: Zijian told his cousin Lu Daoxian: "The court has struck down a powerful faction, but dangerous men still hold out, and I hear nothing of any bold strategy. I doubt this will end well.
entries.literal: Zijian said to his cousin-in-law Lu Daoxian: "The court has executed and cut down the powerful; wicked ruffians still obstruct; I have not heard of any extraordinary schemes or different strategies—I fear success may be impossible.

entries.zh: 此乃李門禍始，弔賀無乃怱怱？」
entries.en: This looks like the start of calamity for the Li family. Surely their celebrations are premature?"
entries.literal: This is the beginning of disaster for the Li clan—is congratulatory condolence not too hasty?

entries.zh: 及永安之後，李氏宗族流離，或遇誅夷，如其所慮。
entries.en: After the Yong'an period the Li clan was uprooted and destroyed, just as he had predicted.
entries.literal: After the Yong'an era, the Li clan was scattered and displaced, some meeting execution and extermination, as he had foreseen.

entries.zh: 後歷左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍。
entries.en: He later served as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and was further appointed Gentleman-in-Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: Later he served as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, additionally Grand Master for Gentlemen of the Palace and General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 收兼通直散騎常侍副王昕聘蕭衍，昕風流文辯，收辭藻富逸，衍及其羣臣咸加敬異。
entries.en: Shou served as envoy deputy to Wang Xin on a mission to Xiao Yan. Xin was polished and articulate; Shou's prose was rich and fluent. Yan and his entire court treated them with marked respect.
entries.literal: Shou additionally served as Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary and Deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Xiao Yan; Xin was refined in manner and eloquent in argument, Shou's diction rich and unrestrained; Yan and all his ministers greatly showed respect and wonder.

entries.zh: 先是，南北初和，李諧、盧元明首通使命，二人才器，並為鄰國所重。
entries.en: When north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming were the pioneering envoys, and both were held in high regard across the border.
entries.literal: Before this, when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming first carried missions; the two men's talents and capacity were both held in esteem by the neighboring state.

entries.zh: 至此，衍稱曰：「盧、李命世，王、魏中興，未知後來復何如耳？」
entries.en: On this occasion Yan said: "Lu and Li were geniuses of their generation; Wang and Wei renew that glory—but who knows whether those who follow will measure up?"
entries.literal: At this point Yan declared: "Lu and Li were men of their age; Wang and Wei revive the tradition—who knows what those to come will be like?"

entries.zh: 文襄啟收兼散騎常侍，修國史。
entries.en: Wen Xiang recommended Shou for appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary with responsibility for compiling the national history.
entries.literal: Wen Xiang memorialized Shou as additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary, compiling national history.

entries.zh: 武定二年，除正常侍，領兼中書侍郎，仍修史。
entries.en: In Wuding 2 he was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat, continuing his work on the histories.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wuding, appointed Regular Attendant, concurrently leading and additionally as Vice Director of the Secretariat, still compiling history.

entries.zh: 帝宴百僚，問何故名人日，皆莫能知。
entries.en: At a banquet for the hundred officials the emperor asked why the seventh day of the New Year was called Human Day. No one knew.
entries.literal: The emperor feasted the hundred officials and asked why the day is called Human Day; none could know.

entries.zh: 收對曰：「晉議郎董勛答問，稱俗云正月一日為鷄，二日為狗，三日為猪，四日為羊，五日為牛，六日為馬，七日為人。」
entries.en: Shou answered: "According to Dong Xun, Discussion Officer of the Jin dynasty, folk tradition holds that the first day of the first month is the day of the rooster, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, and the seventh the day of humanity."
entries.literal: Shou answered: "Jin Discussion Officer Dong Xun in reply to questions said the common saying is: first day of first month is the cock, second day the dog, third the pig, fourth the sheep, fifth the ox, sixth the horse, seventh the person."

entries.zh: 時邢卲亦在側，甚恧焉。
entries.en: Xing Shao, standing nearby, flushed with embarrassment.
entries.literal: At that time Xing Shao was also at the side, and was greatly ashamed.

entries.zh: 自南北和好，書下紙每云「想彼境內寧靜，此率土安和」。
entries.en: After the northern and southern courts made peace, their diplomatic letters routinely opened with the phrase: "We trust your realm is at peace, and all is well throughout our land."
entries.literal: Since north and south made peace, every letter sent down on paper always said, "We trust that within your borders all is tranquil, and here throughout the land all is at peace."

entries.zh: 蕭衍後使，其書乃去「彼」字，自稱猶著「此」，欲示無外之意。
entries.en: Later, envoys from Xiao Yan dropped the word "your" from their letters while still using "our," intending to imply that no foreign realm existed beyond their own.
entries.literal: Later envoys from Xiao Yan removed the character "your" from their letters, while still using "our" for themselves, wishing to show the meaning of having no outside realm.

entries.zh: 收定報書云：「想境內清晏，今萬國安和。」
entries.en: Shou drafted the reply to read: "We trust the realm is peaceful; now all nations under heaven enjoy harmony."
entries.literal: Shou fixed the reply letter to say: "We trust the realm is clear and tranquil; now the myriad states are at peace."

entries.zh: 南人復書，依以為體。
entries.en: The southern court adopted this phrasing as the standard in their return correspondence.
entries.literal: The southerners in their reply letters followed this as the standard form.

entries.zh: 後獻武入朝，靜帝授相國，固讓，令收為啟。
entries.en: When Xianwu later came to court, Emperor Jing invested him as Chancellor of State. He steadfastly declined, and had Shou draft the memorial of refusal.
entries.literal: Later when Xianwu entered court, Emperor Jingdi invested him as Chancellor of State; he firmly declined, and ordered Shou to draft the memorial of refusal.

entries.zh: 啟成呈上，文襄時侍側，獻武指收曰：「此人當復為崔光。」
entries.en: When the memorial was finished and submitted, Wen Xiang stood nearby. Xianwu pointed at Shou and said: "This man will become another Cui Guang."
entries.literal: When the memorial was completed and presented, Wen Xiang was attending at the side; Xianwu pointed to Shou and said: "This man will again become another Cui Guang."

entries.zh: 四年，獻武於西門豹祠宴集，謂司馬子如曰：「魏收為史官，書吾善惡。
entries.en: In the fourth year Xianwu hosted a banquet at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou, as historiographer, will record my virtues and faults.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Xianwu held a banquet at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou as historiographer writes my good and ill.

entries.zh: 聞北伐時，諸貴常餉史官飲食，司馬僕射頗曾餉不？」
entries.en: I hear that during the northern campaign the nobles often treated the historiographers to meals—Vice Director Sima, did you ever send any gifts?"
entries.literal: I hear that during the northern campaign the nobles often supplied food and drink to the historiographers—Vice Director Sima, did you ever supply any?"

entries.zh: 因共大笑。
entries.en: They all burst out laughing together.
entries.literal: Thereupon they all laughed heartily together.

entries.zh: 仍謂收曰：「卿勿見元康等在吾目下趨走，謂吾以為勤勞，我後世身名在卿手，勿謂我不知。」
entries.en: Then he told Shou: "Do not see Yuan Kang and the others scurrying about before me and think I mistake it for true diligence. My legacy rests in your hands—do not imagine I do not know it."
entries.literal: He then said to Shou: "Do not see Yuan Kang and the rest bustling before my eyes and think I consider it labor; my posthumous name and reputation are in your hands—do not suppose I am unaware."

entries.zh: 尋加兼著作郎。
entries.en: Shou was soon additionally appointed Compiler.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Compiler.

entries.zh: 靜帝曾季秋大射，普令賦詩，收詩末云：「尺書徵建鄴，折簡召長安。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing once held a grand autumn archery ceremony and ordered all officials to compose poems. Shou's poem ended with the lines: "A written summons will summon Jiankang; a folded letter will summon Chang'an."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing once held a grand autumn archery ceremony and universally ordered poems composed; the closing lines of Shou's poem read: "A written summons will summon Jiankang; a folded letter will summon Chang'an."

entries.zh: 文襄壯之，顧謂人曰：「在朝今有魏收，便是國之光采。
entries.en: Wen Xiang was impressed and said to those present: "With Wei Shou in court today, the state itself shines brighter.
entries.literal: Wen Xiang was impressed and, turning to those present, said: "In court today there is Wei Shou—that itself is the nation's glory.

entries.zh: 雅俗文墨，通達縱橫，我亦使子才、子昇時有所作，至於詞氣並不及之。
entries.en: Whether in refined or plain writing, in prose or statecraft, he is masterful and versatile. I have Zicai and Zisheng write on occasion, but neither matches his force of expression.
entries.literal: In refined and common letters, in prose and policy, he is thoroughly versed and resourceful; I also have Zicai and Zisheng compose pieces from time to time, yet in tone and spirit they cannot match him.

entries.zh: 吾或意有所懷，忘而不語，語而不盡，意有未及。
entries.en: Sometimes I have thoughts I keep to myself, or words I leave unfinished, or ideas I have not yet fully formed.
entries.literal: Sometimes I have thoughts I hold and forget to speak, or speak yet do not fully express, or have intentions not yet reached.

entries.zh: 及收呈草，皆以周悉。
entries.en: When Shou submitted his drafts, they captured everything completely.
entries.literal: When Shou presented his draft, all were complete and thorough.

entries.zh: 此亦難有。」
entries.en: That kind of talent is rare indeed."
entries.literal: This too is hard to match."

entries.zh: 又敕兼主客郎，接蕭衍使謝珽徐陵。
entries.en: He also appointed Shou chief of receiving guests to host the envoys from Xiao Yan, Xie Yan and Xu Ling.
entries.literal: He also ordered Shou additionally to serve as Chief of Receiving Guests, receiving the envoys of Xiao Yan, Xie Yan and Xu Ling.

entries.zh: 侯景既陷臺城，衍鄱陽王範時為合州刺史，文襄敕收以書喻之。
entries.en: After Hou Jing captured Taicheng, Fan, Prince of Poyang under Xiao Yan, was serving as governor of Hezhou. Wen Xiang ordered Shou to write a letter urging him to defect.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing had taken Taicheng, Fan, Prince of Poyang under Xiao Yan, was then Regional Inspector of Hezhou; Wen Xiang ordered Shou to write a letter to persuade him.

entries.zh: 範得書，乃率部伍西上，□州刺史崔聖念入據其城。
entries.en: Fan received the letter and marched west with his troops, whereupon Governor Cui Shengnian of □ Province entered and seized his city.
entries.literal: Fan received the letter and thereupon led his troops westward; Regional Inspector Cui Shengian of □zhou entered and occupied his city.

entries.zh: 文襄謂收曰：「今定一州，卿有其力，猶恨『尺書徵建鄴』未效耳。」
entries.en: Wen Xiang told Shou: "We have secured a province today, and you played a part—but I still regret that your line about summoning Jiankang with a letter has not yet come true."
entries.literal: Wen Xiang said to Shou: "Now one province is secured—you had a hand in it; I still regret that 'A written summons will summon Jiankang' has not yet taken effect."

entries.zh: 收字伯起，小字佛助。
entries.en: Shou, styled Boqi, childhood name Fozhu.
entries.literal: Shou, courtesy name Boqi, childhood name Fozhu.

entries.zh: 年十五，頗已屬文。
entries.en: By fifteen he was already writing capably.
entries.literal: At age fifteen, he could already compose literary pieces.

entries.zh: 及隨父赴邊，值四方多難，好習騎射，欲以武藝自達。
entries.en: When he accompanied his father to the frontier during widespread turmoil, he took up riding and archery, hoping to make his way through military skill.
entries.literal: When he followed his father to the frontier, encountering many difficulties in all quarters, he loved to practice riding and archery, wishing to advance through martial arts.

entries.zh: 滎陽鄭伯調之曰：「魏郎弄戟多少？」
entries.en: Zheng Bo of Xingyang mocked him: "Young Wei, how much do you really know about handling a spear?"
entries.literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him: "Young Wei, how much do you know about wielding a halberd?"

entries.zh: 收慚，遂折節讀書。
entries.en: Deeply embarrassed, Shou turned to serious study.
entries.literal: Shou was ashamed, and thereupon reined in his will to read books.

entries.zh: 夏月坐板牀，隨樹陰諷誦，積年，牀板為之銳減，而精力不輟。
entries.en: In summer he sat on a wooden couch in the shifting shade of a tree, reciting his texts. Year after year he wore the boards thin, yet his dedication never flagged.
entries.literal: In summer months sitting on a plank bed, following the tree shade to recite and chant, over accumulated years the bed planks were sharply worn down by this, yet his vigor did not slacken.

entries.zh: 以文華顯。
entries.en: He rose to prominence through his literary talent.
entries.literal: Through literary brilliance he became distinguished.

entries.zh: 初以父功除太學博士，及尒朱榮於河陰濫害朝士，收亦在圍中，以日晏獲免。
entries.en: He first received appointment as Erudite of the Imperial Academy through his father's service. When Erzhu Rong massacred court officials at Heyin, Shou was caught in the roundup but spared because nightfall had come.
entries.literal: Initially through his father's merit he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy; when Erzhu Rong at Heyin indiscriminately slaughtered court officials, Shou was also within the encirclement, and because the day was late he was spared.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁重收才學，奏授司徒記室參軍。
entries.en: Li Shenjun, Director of Personnel, admired Shou's talents and recommended him for appointment as secretary in the Office of the Minister over the Masses.
entries.literal: Director of Personnel Li Shenjun valued Shou's talent and learning, memorialized to grant him Secretary in the Office of the Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 永安三年，除北主客郎中。
entries.en: In Yongan 3 he was appointed chief of the northern office for receiving foreign guests.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, appointed Chief of the Northern Bureau of Receiving Guests.

entries.zh: 前廢帝立，妙簡近侍，詔試收為封禪書，收下筆便就，不立草稿，文將千言，所改無幾。
entries.en: When the former deposed emperor took the throne, he selected close attendants carefully and tested Shou by ordering him to compose a fengshan proclamation. Shou wrote it straight off without a draft—nearly a thousand characters, with hardly a correction.
entries.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended, finely selecting close attendants, he ordered Shou tested with a fengshan document; Shou took brush and immediately completed it, not drafting preliminary notes—the text nearly a thousand words, with scarcely any revisions.

entries.zh: 時黃門郎賈思同侍立，深奇之。
entries.en: Attendant of the Yellow Gates Jia Sitong, standing nearby, was deeply impressed.
entries.literal: At that time Attendant of the Yellow Gates Jia Sitong stood attending and was deeply amazed.

entries.zh: 帝曰：[7]「雖七步之才，無以過此。」
entries.en: The emperor remarked: [7]"Not even Cao Zhi's seven-pace talent could surpass this."
entries.literal: The emperor said: [7]"Even talent for seven paces could not surpass this."

entries.zh: 遷散騎侍郎，尋敕典起居注，并修國史。
entries.en: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary and soon put in charge of the imperial diary while also compiling the national history.
entries.literal: Promoted to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary, soon ordered to take charge of the Daily Records and also compile the national history.

entries.zh: 俄兼中書侍郎，年二十六。
entries.en: Before long he was also named Vice Director of the Secretariat—at only twenty-six.
entries.literal: Soon additionally Vice Director of the Secretariat, age twenty-six.

entries.zh: 出帝初，又詔收攝本職，文誥填積，事咸稱旨。
entries.en: When the Departure Emperor came to the throne, Shou was recalled to his former duties. Official documents piled up, and everything he wrote met with approval.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Departure Emperor's reign, again ordered Shou to resume his original post; documents and decrees piled up, and affairs all matched his intent.

entries.zh: 黃門郎崔㥄從齊獻武王入朝，熏灼於世，收初不詣門。
entries.en: Cui Lin, Attendant of the Yellow Gates, rode into court in the train of Duke Xianwu of Qi and wielded enormous influence. Shou never went near his gate.
entries.literal: Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Lin followed Duke Xianwu of Qi into court, blazing hot in the world; Shou at first did not visit his door.

entries.zh: 㥄為帝登祚赦，云「朕託體孝文」，收嗤其率直。
entries.en: When Lin drafted the emperor's accession amnesty with the phrase "I take my form from Emperor Xiaowen," Shou laughed at its blunt literalism.
entries.literal: Lin composed the amnesty for the emperor's accession, saying "I take my body from Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou scoffed at its bluntness.

entries.zh: 正員郎李慎以告之，㥄深忿忌。
entries.en: Regular Gentleman Li Shen reported Shou's mockery, and Lin nursed a deep grudge.
entries.literal: Regular Gentleman Li Shen told him of this; Lin deeply resented and bore jealousy.

entries.zh: 時前廢帝殂，令收為詔，㥄乃宣言：「收普泰世出入幃幄，一日造詔，優為詞旨，然則義旗之士，盡為逆人；
entries.en: When the former deposed emperor died and Shou was ordered to draft the mourning edict, Lin publicly accused him: "During the Putai reign Shou moved freely in the inner court. He can turn out a polished edict in a day—so by that logic every man who raised the righteous banner becomes a rebel.
entries.literal: At that time when the Former Deposed Emperor died, Shou was ordered to draft the edict; Lin then proclaimed: "Shou during the Putai era went in and out of the curtain chambers; in one day he drafted an edict with words finely tuned—in that case the men who raised the righteous banners are all made rebels;

entries.zh: 又收父老合解官歸侍。」
entries.en: And Shou's elderly father should by rights resign and return home so his son can care for him."
entries.literal: Moreover, Shou's father is old and ought properly to resign office and return home to attend him."

entries.zh: 南臺將加彈劾，賴尚書辛雄為言於中尉綦儁，乃解。
entries.en: The southern censorate prepared to impeach him, but Director Xin Xiong interceded with Chief Commandant Qi Jun, and the case was dropped.
entries.literal: The Southern Censorate was about to impeach; thanks to Director Xin Xiong speaking on his behalf to Chief Commandant Qi Jun, the matter was resolved.

entries.zh: 收有賤生弟仲同先未齒錄，因此怖懼，上籍，遣還鄉扶侍。
entries.en: Shou had a younger half-brother, Zhongtong, who had never been officially registered. Frightened by Lin's attack, Shou entered him in the family register and sent him home to care for their father.
entries.literal: Shou had a younger half-brother Zhongtong who had not before been entered in the register; from this fear he submitted his name to the register and sent him home to the village to attend and support.

entries.zh: 出帝嘗大發士卒，狩於嵩少之南，旬有六日，時既寒苦，朝野嗟怨。
entries.en: The Departure Emperor once mobilized a large force and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days. The weather was bitterly cold, and people throughout the court and countryside complained bitterly.
entries.literal: The Departure Emperor once greatly mobilized troops and hunted south of Song and Shao for sixteen days; the season was already bitter cold, and court and countryside lamented in complaint.

entries.zh: 帝與從官皆胡服而騎，宮人及諸妃主雜其間，奇伎異飾，多非禮度。
entries.en: The emperor and his attendants rode in nomadic dress, with palace women and imperial consorts mingled among them, performing outlandish stunts and wearing bizarre costumes—most of it well outside proper ceremonial bounds.
entries.literal: The emperor and attendant officials all wore nomadic dress and rode; palace women and various consorts and princesses were mixed among them; strange skills and exotic adornments mostly departed from ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 收欲言則畏懼，欲默不能已，乃上南狩賦以諷焉，年二十七，雖富言淫麗，而終歸雅正。
entries.en: Shou wanted to speak out but feared retribution, yet could not keep silent. At twenty-seven he submitted his "Rhapsody on the Southern Hunt" as a veiled remonstrance. Though lushly ornate, it ultimately upheld moral propriety.
entries.literal: Shou wished to speak yet feared; wished to be silent yet could not stop himself, and so submitted an "Ode on the Southern Hunt" to admonish thereby; age twenty-seven—though the words were rich and luxuriant, in the end they returned to the elegant and upright.

entries.zh: 帝手詔報焉，甚見褒美。
entries.en: The emperor responded with a handwritten note lavishing praise on the piece.
entries.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict in reply, greatly praising and commending it.

entries.zh: 鄭伯謂曰：「卿不遇老夫，猶應逐兔。」
entries.en: Zheng Bo told him: "If you had never met me, you'd still be out hunting rabbits."
entries.literal: Zheng Bo said to him: "Had you not met this old man, you would still be chasing rabbits."

entries.zh: 初，齊獻武王固讓天柱大將軍，帝敕收為詔，令遂所請，欲加相國，問收相國品秩，收以實對，帝遂止。
entries.en: When Duke Xianwu of Qi steadfastly declined the title General of the Heavenly Pillar, the emperor had Shou draft the edict granting his wish. The emperor then considered adding the title Chancellor of State, asked Shou about its rank in the official hierarchy, and when Shou answered honestly, abandoned the idea.
entries.literal: Initially, Duke Xianwu of Qi firmly declined the title General of the Heavenly Pillar; the emperor ordered Shou to draft the edict, directing acceptance of his request; wishing to add the title Chancellor of State, he asked Shou about the rank and grade of Chancellor; Shou answered according to fact, and the emperor thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 收既未測主相之意，以前事不安，求解，詔許焉。
entries.en: Unable to read the intentions of the emperor and the duke, and unsettled by earlier troubles, Shou asked to resign—and was allowed to do so.
entries.literal: Shou had not yet fathomed the lord and chancellor's intent; uneasy over earlier affairs, he sought release; an edict granted it.

entries.zh: 久之，除帝兄子廣平王贊開府從事中郎，收不敢辭，乃為庭竹賦以致己意。
entries.en: Some time later he was appointed attendant in the prince of Guangping's household—the prince was the emperor's nephew. Shou could not refuse, but wrote his "Rhapsody on the Court Bamboo" to express his true feelings.
entries.literal: After some time, appointed Attendant of the Staff for the Prince of Guangping, the emperor's brother's son Zan, with an open office; Shou dared not decline, and so composed an "Ode on the Bamboo in the Courtyard" to convey his intent.

entries.zh: 尋兼中書舍人，與濟陰溫子昇、河間邢子才齊譽，世號三才。
entries.en: He soon became a secretariat aide and, together with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian, earned equal renown as the Three Talents of the age.
entries.literal: Soon additionally Secretariat Aide; together with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian equally renowned—the age called them the Three Talents.

entries.zh: 時出帝猜忌獻武，內有間隙，收遂以疾固辭而免。
entries.en: When the Departure Emperor grew suspicious of Xianwu and court factions split, Shou pleaded illness and managed to get himself relieved of duty.
entries.literal: At that time the Departure Emperor suspected Xianwu; internally there were rifts; Shou thereupon pleaded illness, firmly declined, and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 其舅崔孝芬怪而問之，收曰：「懼有晉陽之甲。」
entries.en: His uncle Cui Xiaofen asked why. Shou answered: "I fear troops will march from Jinyang."
entries.literal: His uncle Cui Xiaofen, puzzled, asked him; Shou said: "I fear there will be armor from Jinyang."

entries.zh: 尋而獻武南上，帝西入關。
entries.en: Before long Xianwu advanced south and the emperor fled west into the pass.
entries.literal: Soon after Xianwu marched south, the emperor entered the Pass to the west.

entries.zh: 文襄崩，文宣如晉陽，令與黃門郎崔季舒、高德正、吏部郎中尉瑾於北第參掌機密。
entries.en: When Wen Xiang died, Wen Xuan went to Jinyang and ordered Shou, together with Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Jishu, Gao Dezheng, and Director in the Ministry of Personnel Wei Jin, to handle confidential affairs at the northern residence.
entries.literal: When Wen Xiang died, Wen Xuan went to Jinyang and ordered Shou, together with Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Jishu, Gao Dezheng, and Director in the Ministry of Personnel Wei Jin, to manage confidential affairs at the northern residence.

entries.zh: 轉祕書監，兼著作郎，又除定州大中正。
entries.en: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Compiler, and also appointed Chief Rectifier of Ding Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Compiler, and also appointed Chief Rectifier of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 時齊將受禪，楊愔奏收置之別館，令撰禪代詔冊諸文，遣徐之才守門不聽出。
entries.en: As Qi prepared to receive the abdication, Yang Yin memorialized to confine Shou in a separate lodge, ordering him to draft the abdication proclamations and related documents, and sent Xu Zhicai to guard the door and keep him from leaving.
entries.literal: When Qi was about to receive the abdication, Yang Yin memorialized to place Shou in a separate lodge, ordering him to draft the abdication proclamations and related documents, and sent Xu Zhicai to guard the door and forbid him to leave.

entries.zh: 天保元年，除中書令，仍兼著作郎，封富平縣子。
entries.en: In Tianbao 1 he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, still concurrently Compiler, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuping.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, still concurrently Compiler, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuping.

entries.zh: 成帝世位終鉅鹿太守 錢氏考異卷二八云：「此成帝謂漢成帝也。
entries.en: Regarding "In the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended as Administrator of Julu"—Qian's Textual Variants, scroll 28, states: "This Emperor Cheng refers to Emperor Cheng of Han.
entries.literal: "In the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended as Administrator of Julu"—Qian's Textual Variants, scroll 28, says: "This Emperor Cheng refers to Emperor Cheng of Han.

entries.zh: 魏歆仕於漢成帝朝，而其子悅乃仕於元魏太武之世，此理之所必無者。
entries.en: Wei Xin served under Emperor Cheng of Han, yet his son Yue served under Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei—something that reason flatly cannot accept.
entries.literal: Wei Xin served in the court of Emperor Cheng of Han, yet his son Yue served in the era of Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei—this is something reason absolutely cannot allow.

entries.zh: 伯起亦通人，何至憒憒乃爾。
entries.en: Boqi was himself a learned man—how could he have been so confused?
entries.literal: Boqi too was a man of broad learning—how could he have been so muddled as this?

entries.zh: 良由魏史自序久亡，後人節取北史補之，而北史又有脫簡，後人無從校正爾。」
entries.en: The explanation is surely that Wei Shou's original authorial preface to the History of Wei had long been lost; later editors patched it with excerpts from the Northern Dynasties, which itself contained lacunae that could no longer be corrected."
entries.literal: Surely because Wei Shou's original authorial preface to the History of Wei had long been lost, later men excerpted the Northern Dynasties to fill the gap, and the Northern Dynasties itself had lacunae that later men had no means to correct."

entries.zh: 按「成帝世」三字，北史卷五六魏收傳無，當取他書增，據元和姓纂輯本卷八魏氏稱「漢鉅鹿太守歆，居鉅鹿」，錢氏謂成帝謂漢成帝，是。
entries.en: Examination shows that the phrase "in the reign of Emperor Cheng" does not appear in scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties; it was likely added from another source. The reconstructed Yuanhe Xingzuan, scroll 8, records under the Wei clan that "Xin, Administrator of Julu under the Han, dwelt in Julu." Qian's identification of Emperor Cheng as Emperor Cheng of Han is correct.
entries.literal: According to examination, the three characters "in the reign of Emperor Cheng" are absent from the biography of Wei Shou in scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties; they must have been added from another book. The reconstructed Yuanhe Xingzuan, scroll 8, under the Wei clan states "Xin, Administrator of Julu of Han, dwelt in Julu"; Qian's view that Emperor Cheng means Emperor Cheng of Han is correct.

entries.zh: 漢初，魏無知封高良侯，子均，均子恢，恢子彥。
entries.en: In the early Han dynasty, Wei Wuzhi was made Marquis of Gaoliang; from him came Jun, from Jun came Hui, and from Hui came Yan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han, Wei Wuzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoliang; his son was Jun, Jun's son Hui, and Hui's son Yan.

entries.zh: 彥子歆，字子胡，幼孤有志操，博洽經史，成帝世，位終鉅鹿太守，[2]仍家焉。
entries.en: Yan's son Xin, styled Zihu, lost his father early but possessed strong character. Well read in the classics and histories, he served during Emperor Cheng's reign and ultimately became Administrator of Julu, [2] where the family established its home.
entries.literal: Yan's son Xin, courtesy name Zihu, orphaned young yet resolute in will and conduct, thoroughly versed in the classics and histories; in the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended his career as Administrator of Julu, [2] and the family settled there.

entries.zh: 歆子悅，[3]字處德，性沉厚有度量，宣城公趙國李孝伯見而重之，以女妻焉。
entries.en: Xin's son Yue, [3] styled Chude, was grave, steady, and broad-minded. Li Xiaobo, Duke of Xuan Cheng in Zhao, took a liking to him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Xin's son Yue, [3] courtesy name Chude, of deep and steady nature with great forbearance; Xuan Cheng Gong Li Xiaobo of Zhao State saw him and held him in esteem, giving him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 位濟陰太守，以善政稱。
entries.en: He served as Administrator of Jiyin and won renown for his effective administration.
entries.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Jiyin, famed for good governance.

entries.zh: 夫在天成象，聖人是觀，日月五星，象之著者，變常舛度，徵咎隨焉。
entries.en: Heaven sets signs in the sky, and the sage is the one who reads them; the sun, moon, and five planets are the clearest of those signs—when the usual order shifts and celestial measures go wrong, omens of calamity follow in their wake.
entries.literal: As for Heaven forming signs on high, the sage is one who observes them; the sun, moon, and five stars are the prominent among such signs—when constancy changes and degrees go awry, tokens of blame and misfortune follow.

entries.zh: 然則明晦暈蝕，疾餘犯守，飛流欻起，彗孛不恒，或皇靈降臨，示譴以戒下，或王化有虧，感達於天路。
entries.en: Whether in brightness or dimness, halos or eclipses, swift planetary crossings or prolonged station-keeping, sudden meteors or unpredictable comets—sometimes the imperial spirit descends to warn the realm below, and sometimes defects in royal governance reach heaven's road.
entries.literal: Thus whether bright or dark, halos or eclipses, swift trespass and lingering occupancy, meteor flashes suddenly rising, or comets and broom-stars not constant—sometimes the imperial numen descends, displaying reprimand to warn those below, or sometimes royal transformation is impaired and the response reaches the road of Heaven.

entries.zh: 易稱「天垂象，見吉凶」，「觀乎天文，以察時變」；
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, "Heaven displays signs revealing fortune and misfortune," and "Look to the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the times";
entries.literal: The Changes says, "Heaven displays signs by which fortune and misfortune may be seen," and "Observe the patterns of heaven to discern the changes of the times";

entries.zh: 書曰「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時」。
entries.en: The Book of Documents says, "Mark out the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently give the people their seasons."
entries.literal: The Documents says, "Calculate and image the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and reverently bestow the seasons upon the people."

entries.zh: 是故有國有家者之所祗畏也。
entries.en: This is why rulers of states and clans treat it with reverent awe.
entries.literal: Therefore this is what those who possess a state or a clan hold in reverent awe.

entries.zh: 百王興廢之驗，萬國禍福之來，兆勤雖微，罔不必至，著於前載，不可得而備舉也。
entries.en: The rise and fall of dynasties and the fortune or ruin of nations—even the faintest omen is never empty; the former records are full of them, and no complete list could be given.
entries.literal: The proofs of the rise and fall of the hundred kings, the coming of fortune and misfortune to the myriad states—though the portents be slight and subtle, none fail to arrive; recorded in former annals, they cannot all be enumerated.

entries.zh: 班史以日暈五星之屬列天文志，薄蝕彗孛之比入五行說。
entries.en: Ban Gu's History put solar halos and the five planets in the Astronomical Treatise, but eclipses, comets, and similar phenomena in the discourse on the Five Phases.
entries.literal: Ban's History placed solar halos and the five stars and their kind in the Treatise on Astronomy, while thin eclipses, comets, and broom-stars and the like were entered into the discourse on the Five Phases.

entries.zh: 七曜一也，而分為二志，故陸機云學者所疑也。
entries.en: The seven luminaries are one class of phenomena, yet Ban split them across two treatises—hence Lu Ji's remark that scholars have long found this puzzling.
entries.literal: The seven luminaries are one category, yet they were divided into two treatises; hence Lu Ji said that scholars have doubts about this.

entries.zh: 今以在天諸異咸入天象，其應徵符合，隨而條載，無所顯驗則闕之云。
entries.en: Here all heavenly anomalies are gathered in this Celestial Phenomena treatise; when earthly events confirm the omen, they are recorded in sequence, and where no verification appears, the entry is left blank.
entries.literal: Now all celestial anomalies in the heavens are gathered into Celestial Phenomena; where there are corresponding proofs, they are entered item by item as they occur, and where there is no manifest verification, that is omitted.

entries.zh: 世祖始光四年六月癸卯朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Shiguang 4, during the reign of Emperor Taiwu, on the guimao new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Shiguang under Emperor Shizu, on the first day guimao, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 占曰「諸侯非其人」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "The wrong men hold power among the feudatories."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The feudal lords are not the right men."

entries.zh: 神䴥元年二月，司空奚斤、監軍侍御史安頡討赫連昌，擒之於安定。
entries.en: In the second month of Shenlu 1, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Xie campaigned against Helian Chang and took him prisoner at Anding.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shenlu, Minister of Works Xi Jin and Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Xie attacked Helian Chang and captured him at Anding.

entries.zh: 其餘眾立昌弟定為主，走還平涼，斤追之，為定所擒。
entries.en: The survivors set up Chang's brother Ding as their leader and withdrew to Pingliang; Xi Jin pursued them but was captured by Ding.
entries.literal: The remaining host installed Chang's younger brother Ding as ruler, fled back to Pingliang, and Jin pursued them but was captured by Ding.

entries.zh: 將軍丘堆棄甲與守將高涼王禮東走蒲坂，世祖怒，斬堆。
entries.en: General Qiu Dui abandoned his armor and fled east to Puban with the garrison commander, Prince Li of Gaoliang; Emperor Taiwu was furious and had Dui executed.
entries.literal: General Qiu Dui cast off his armor and, with the defending commander Prince of Gaoliang Li, fled east to Puban; Emperor Shizu was enraged and executed Dui.

entries.zh: 六年六月戊子朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the sixth month of year 6, on the wuzi new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, on the first day wuzi, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 占曰「有九族夷滅」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "An entire clan will be wiped out."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The nine degrees of kin will be exterminated to the roots."

entries.zh: 七年正月戊辰，世祖車駕次東雍州。
entries.en: In the first month of year 7, on wuchen day, Emperor Taiwu's entourage encamped in Eastern Yong Province.
entries.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day wuchen, Emperor Shizu's imperial carriage halted at Eastern Yong Province.

entries.zh: 庚午，圍薛永宗營壘。
entries.en: On gengwu day he besieged Xue Yongzong's camp.
entries.literal: On gengwu he besieged Xue Yongzong's fortified camp.

entries.zh: 永宗出戰，大敗，六軍乘之，永宗眾潰，斬永宗，男女無少長皆赴汾水而死。
entries.en: Yongzong gave battle and was routed; the Six Armies pressed the attack, his forces broke, and he was beheaded; men and women of every age threw themselves into the Fen River and drowned.
entries.literal: Yongzong came out to fight, suffered a great defeat, the Six Armies pressed the pursuit, his host collapsed, Yongzong was beheaded, and men and women, young and old alike, all threw themselves into the Fen River and died.

entries.zh: 高祖延興元年十二月癸卯，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Yanxing 1, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, on guimao day, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yanxing under Emperor Gaozu, on the day guimao, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 占曰「有兵」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "War will break out."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "There will be warfare."

entries.zh: 二年正月乙卯，統萬鎮胡民相率北叛，遣寧南將軍、交阯公韓拔等滅之。
entries.en: In the first month of year 2, on yimao day, the Hu people of Tongwan garrison rebelled en masse and fled north; General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba and others were dispatched to crush them.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year, on the day yimao, the Hu people of Tongwan garrison rose in rebellion together and fled north; Ningnan General, Duke of Jiaozhi Han Ba and others were sent to destroy them.

entries.zh: 十五年正月癸亥晦，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the first month of year 15, on guihai day, the last day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, on the day guihai, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 占曰「王者將兵，天下擾動」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "The sovereign will take the field and the realm will be thrown into turmoil."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The king will lead troops; the realm under heaven will be disturbed."

entries.zh: 十七年六月丙戌，高祖南伐。
entries.en: In the sixth month of year 17, on bingxu day, Emperor Xiaowen launched his southern campaign.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, on the day bingxu, Emperor Gaozu marched south on campaign.

entries.zh: 世宗景明元年正月辛丑朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the first month of Jingming 1, during the reign of Emperor Xuanwu, on the xinchou new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jingming under Emperor Shizong, on the first day xinchou, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 四年十一月癸卯，日中有黑氣二，大如桃。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of year 4, on guimao day, two black spots within the sun grew as large as peaches.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, on the day guimao, there were two black vapors within the sun, as large as peaches.

entries.zh: 占曰「天子崩」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "The emperor will die."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven will die."

entries.zh: 延昌四年正月丁巳，世宗昇遐。
entries.en: In the first month of Yanchang 4, on dingsi day, Emperor Xuanwu passed away.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Yanchang, on the day dingsi, Emperor Shizong ascended to the remote.

entries.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，日有蝕之，在牛四度。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the renxu new moon, the sun was eclipsed at four degrees in the Ox asterism.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day renxu, there was a solar eclipse, at four degrees in the Ox asterism.

entries.zh: 占曰「其國叛兵發」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "Rebel armies will rise in the realm."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "In that state rebel armies will rise."

entries.zh: 延昌二年二月庚辰，[4]蕭衍郁洲民徐玄明等斬送衍鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史張稷首，以州內附。
entries.en: In the second month of Yanchang 2, on gengchen day, [4] Xu Xuanming and others of Yuzhou under Liang emperor Xiao Yan beheaded Zhang Ji, Liang's General Who Guards the North and governor of Qing and Ji, and surrendered the province to Wei.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yanchang, on the day gengchen, [4] Xu Xuanming and others, commoners of Yuzhou under Xiao Yan, beheaded and sent the head of Yan's General Who Guards the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces Zhang Ji, and submitted the province to allegiance.

entries.zh: 永熙二年四月己未朔，日有蝕之，在丙，虧從正南起。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Yongxi 2, on the jiwei new moon, the sun was eclipsed at bing; the bite began due south.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxi, on the first day jiwei, there was a solar eclipse at bing; the bite began due south.

entries.zh: 占曰「君陰謀」。
entries.en: The omen reads: "The sovereign plots in secret."
entries.literal: The prognostication says: "The ruler plots in secret."

entries.zh: 三年五月辛卯，出帝為斛斯椿等諸佞關構，猜於齊獻武王，託討蕭衍，盛暑徵發河南諸州之兵，天下怪惡之。
entries.en: In the fifth month of year 3, on xinmao day, Emperor Xiaowu, swayed by flatterers such as Husu Chun, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of campaigning against Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in midsummer, and the realm regarded it with horror.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, on the day xinmao, Emperor Xiaowu, because flatterers such as Husu Chun sowed discord between them, grew suspicious of Prince Xian of Qi; under the pretext of attacking Xiao Yan he conscripted troops from the Henan commanderies in the height of summer, and all under heaven regarded it with revulsion.

entries.zh: 語在斛斯椿傳。
entries.en: The full account appears in the biography of Husu Chun.
entries.literal: The account is given in the biography of Husu Chun.

entries.zh: 高祖延興元年十二月癸卯日有蝕之 按是年十二月乙酋朔，癸卯是十九日，不應有日蝕。
entries.en: The entry "In the twelfth month of Yanxing 1, on guimao day, the sun was eclipsed" is erroneous: that year's twelfth month began on yiyou, and guimao is the nineteenth day—no eclipse should occur then.
entries.literal: "In the twelfth month of the first year of Yanxing under Emperor Gaozu, on the day guimao, there was a solar eclipse." Examining that year: the twelfth month began on yiyou; guimao is the nineteenth day, and there should not have been a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 延昌二年二月庚辰 諸本「二月」作「正月」。
entries.en: For Yanchang 2, second month, gengchen: all editions read "first month" instead of "second month."
entries.literal: Yanchang 2, second month, gengchen: in all editions "second month" reads "first month."

entries.zh: 按卷八世宗紀，事在是年二月庚辰。
entries.en: Fascicle 8, Basic Annals of Emperor Xuanwu, places the event on gengchen in the second month of that year.
entries.literal: Examining fascicle 8, Basic Annals of Shizong, the event is on gengchen in the second month of that year.

entries.zh: 是年正月丙戊朔，無庚辰，二月丙辰朔，庚辰乃二十五日。
entries.en: That year the first month began on bingxu, so there is no gengchen in the first month; the second month began on bingchen, and gengchen is the twenty-fifth day.
entries.literal: That year the first month began on bingxu; there is no gengchen. The second month began on bingchen; gengchen is the twenty-fifth day.

entries.zh: 這裏「正月」乃「二月」之訛。
entries.en: Here "first month" is a scribal error for "second month."
entries.literal: Here "first month" is a corruption for "second month."

entries.zh: 今據紀改。
entries.en: The text is corrected here according to the annals.
entries.literal: Now corrected according to the annals.

entries.zh: 三年九月己卯 諸本「三年」作「二年」。
entries.en: Third year, ninth month, jimao: all editions read "second year" instead of "third year."
entries.literal: Third year, ninth month, jimao: in all editions "third year" reads "second year."

entries.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀，事在孝昌三年九月辛卯，梁書卷五武帝紀三，在梁大通元年
entries.en: Fascicle 9, Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaoming, places the event in the ninth month of Xiaochang 3, on xinmao day; the Book of Liang, fascicle 5, Basic Annals of Emperor Wu 3, places it in Liang Datong 1
entries.literal: Examining fascicle 9, Basic Annals of Suzong, the event is in the ninth month of Xiaochang 3, on xinmao; Liang shu, fascicle 5, Basic Annals of Emperor Wu 3, places it in the first year of Datong of Liang

entries.zh: 〈即魏孝昌三年〉
entries.en: 〈that is, Wei Xiaochang 3〉
entries.literal: 〈that is, the third year of Xiaochang of Wei〉

entries.zh: 十月。
entries.en: the tenth month.
entries.literal: the tenth month.

entries.zh: 記月不同，當是各據奏報，至元慶和降梁，必在孝昌三年無疑。
entries.en: The months differ because each source followed its own report; Yuan Qinghe's surrender to Liang certainly occurred in Xiaochang 3.
entries.literal: The months recorded differ; each source must have followed its own memorial report. As for Yuan Qinghe's surrender to Liang, it was certainly in the third year of Xiaochang without doubt.

entries.zh: 這裏「二」字乃「三」之訛。
entries.en: Here "two" is a scribal error for "three."
entries.literal: Here the character "two" is a corruption for "three."

entries.zh: 今據紀改。
entries.en: The text is corrected here according to the annals.
entries.literal: Now corrected according to the annals.

entries.zh: 是年九月有「己卯」，無「辛卯」，則是紀誤。
entries.en: That year's ninth month has "jimao" but no "xinmao" day, so the annals are wrong.
entries.literal: That year in the ninth month there is "jimao" but not "xinmao"; thus the annals are in error.

entries.zh: 二月甲子，赦王廷湊。
entries.en: In the second month on jiazi Wang Tingcou was pardoned.
entries.literal: Second month, day jiazi, Wang Tingcou was pardoned.

entries.zh: 辛巳，崔植罷。
entries.en: On xinsi Cui Zhi was dismissed.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi Cui Zhi was dismissed.

entries.zh: 工部侍郎元稹同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Yuan Zhen, vice minister of works, was appointed chancellor de facto.
entries.literal: The vice minister of works Yuan Zhen was made chancellor de facto.

entries.zh: 戊子，昭義軍節度使劉悟囚其監軍使劉承偕。
entries.en: On wuzi Liu Wu of Zhaoyi imprisoned his army supervisory commissioner Liu Chengxie.
entries.literal: On the day wuzi the Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Wu imprisoned his army supervisory commissioner Liu Chengxie.

entries.zh: 九月壬午，昭義軍節度使劉悟卒，其子從諫自稱留後。
entries.en: In the ninth month on renwu Liu Wu of Zhaoyi died; his son Congjian declared himself acting commissioner.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day renwu, the Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Wu died; his son Congjian styled himself acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 五月甲午，震，東都廣運樓災。
entries.en: In the fifth month on jiawu there was an earthquake and the Eastern Capital Broad Transport Tower burned.
entries.literal: Fifth month, day jiawu, earthquake; the Eastern Capital Broad Transport Tower burned.

entries.zh: 辛丑，成德軍節度使王元逵為北面招討澤潞使，魏博節度使何弘敬為東面招討澤潞使，及河中節度使陳夷行、河陽節度使王茂元、劉沔以討劉稹。
entries.en: On xinchou Wang Yuankui of Chengde was made northern Ze-Lu campaign commissioner; He Hongjing of Weibo eastern commissioner; and Chen Yixing of Zhonghe, Wang Maoyuan of Heyang, and Liu Mian marched against Liu Zhen.
entries.literal: On the day xinchou the Chengde military commissioner Wang Yuankui was made northern campaign commissioner against Ze and Lu; the Weibo military commissioner He Hongjing eastern campaign commissioner; together with the Zhonghe military commissioner Chen Yixing, Heyang military commissioner Wang Maoyuan, and Liu Mian to campaign against Liu Zhen.

entries.zh: 戊申，翰林學士承旨、中書舍人崔鉉為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On wushen Cui Xuan, Hanlin academician-in-chief and drafting officer, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor de facto.
entries.literal: On the day wushen the Hanlin academician-in-chief and Secretariat drafting officer Cui Xuan was made vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor de facto.

entries.zh: 武寧軍節度使李彥佐為晉絳行營諸軍節度招討使。
entries.en: Li Yanzhuo of Wuning was made Jin-He campaign military commissioner and commander.
entries.literal: The Wuning military commissioner Li Yanzhuo was made Jin-He campaign military commissioner and campaign commander.

entries.zh: 十月己巳，晉絳行營節度使石雄及劉稹戰于烏嶺，敗之。
entries.en: In the tenth month on jisi Shi Xiong of the Jin-He campaign fought Liu Zhen at Black Ridge and defeated him.
entries.literal: Tenth month, day jisi, the Jin-He campaign military commissioner Shi Xiong fought Liu Zhen at Black Ridge and defeated him.

entries.zh: 壬午，日中月食太白。
entries.en: On renwu at midday the moon eclipsed Venus.
entries.literal: On the day renwu at midday the moon eclipsed Venus.

entries.zh: 是月，党項羌寇鹽州。
entries.en: That month the Tangut raided Yan prefecture.
entries.literal: In that month the Tangut raided Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 八月乙未，昭義軍將郭誼殺劉稹以降。
entries.en: In the eighth month on yiwei Zhaoyi officer Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and surrendered.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day yiwei, the Zhaoyi army officer Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and surrendered.

entries.zh: 戊戌，給復澤、潞、邢、洺、磁五州一歲，免太原、河陽及懷、陝、晉、絳四州秋稅。
entries.en: On wushen Ze, Lu, Xing, Luo, and Ci received one year's tax remission; autumn tax was remitted in Taiyuan, Heyang, Huai, Shan, Jin, and Jiang.
entries.literal: On the day wushen Ze, Lu, Xing, Luo, and Ci prefectures were granted tax remission for one year; autumn tax in Taiyuan, Heyang, and Huai, Shan, Jin, and Jiang prefectures was remitted.

entries.zh: 戊申，李德裕為太尉。
entries.en: On wushen Li Deyu was appointed grand preceptor.
entries.literal: On the day wushen Li Deyu was made grand preceptor.

entries.zh: 四月乙丑，昭義軍節度使劉從諫卒，其子稹自稱留後。
entries.en: In the fourth month on yichou Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died; his son Zhen declared himself acting commissioner.
entries.literal: Fourth month, day yichou, the Zhaoyi military commissioner Liu Congjian died; his son Zhen styled himself acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝諱恆，憲宗第三子也。
entries.en: Emperor Muzong, posthumously honored as the Sagely Civil and Gracious Filial, bore the taboo name Heng and was the third son of Xianzong.
entries.literal: Emperor Muzong, the Sagely Civil and Gracious Filial, taboo name Heng, was the third son of Xianzong.

entries.zh: 母曰懿安皇太后郭氏。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Dowager Yi'an, née Guo.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Yi'an of the Guo clan.

entries.zh: 始封建安郡王，進封遂王，遙領彰義軍節度使。
entries.en: He was first made Prince of Jian'an, then Prince of Sui, and served as Zhangyi military commissioner in absentia.
entries.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an, then advanced to Prince of Sui, and held the post of Zhangyi army military commissioner in absentia.

entries.zh: 元和七年，惠昭太子薨，左神策軍中尉吐突承璀欲立澧王惲，而惲母賤不當立，乃立遂王為皇太子。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yuanhe the heir apparent died; Tufa Chenghuan of the Left Divine Strategy Army sought to install Prince of Li Yun, but because Yun's mother was of humble status he could not be established, and the Prince of Sui was made heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe the Brightly Filial Heir Apparent died; the Left Divine Strategy Army eunuch-commander Tufa Chenghuan wished to install Prince of Li Yun, but Yun's mother was lowly and unfit to be established, so the Prince of Sui was established as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 高宗又詔太尉長孫无忌、中書令杜正倫李義府、中書侍郎李友益、黃門侍郎劉祥道許圉師、太子賓客許敬宗、太常卿韋琨等增之為一百三十卷，是為顯慶禮。
entries.en: Gaozong further ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Chief Ministers Du Zhenglun and Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi, Vice Directors of the Yellow Gate Liu Xiangdao and Xu Yushi, Guest of the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong, Director of Court Music Wei Kun, and others to expand it to one hundred thirty scrolls: the Xianqing Ritual.
entries.literal: Gaozong further ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Chief Ministers Du Zhenglun and Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi, Vice Directors of the Yellow Gate Liu Xiangdao and Xu Yushi, Guest of the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong, Director of Court Music Wei Kun, and others to expand it to one hundred thirty scrolls: this was the Xianqing Ritual.

entries.zh: 其文雜以式令，而義府、敬宗方得幸，多希旨傅會。
entries.en: Its text was mixed with statutes and orders. Yifu and Jingzong were then in favor and largely bent their work to please imperial intent.
entries.literal: Its text was mixed with statutes and orders; Yifu and Jingzong were then in favor and largely bent their work to please imperial intent.

entries.zh: 事既施行，議者皆以為非，上元三年，詔復用貞觀禮。
entries.en: Once implemented, critics deemed it wrong; in the third year of Shangyuan, an edict restored the Zhenguan Ritual.
entries.literal: Once it was put into practice, critics all deemed it wrong; in the third year of Shangyuan, an edict restored use of the Zhenguan Ritual.

entries.zh: 由是終高宗世，貞觀、顯慶二禮兼行。
entries.en: Thus through the end of Gaozong's reign, the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals were practiced together.
entries.literal: Thus through the end of Gaozong's reign, the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals were practiced together.

entries.zh: 而有司臨事，遠引古義，與二禮參考增損之，無復定制。
entries.en: Yet when offices faced affairs, they cited distant ancient principles and consulted both rituals for additions and subtractions, with no fixed standard thereafter.
entries.literal: Yet when offices faced affairs, they cited distant ancient principles and consulted both rituals for additions and subtractions, with no fixed standard thereafter.

entries.zh: 武氏、中宗繼以亂敗，無可言者，博士掌禮，備官而已。
entries.en: The Wu clan and Zhongzong followed with turmoil and ruin—nothing worth speaking of; doctors of ritual held ritual in name only, filling posts and nothing more.
entries.literal: The Wu clan and Zhongzong followed with turmoil and ruin—nothing worth speaking of; doctors of ritual held ritual in name only, filling posts and nothing more.

entries.zh: 玄宗開元十年，以國子司業韋縚為禮儀使，以掌五禮。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, Wei Zong of the Directorate of Education was made Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to oversee the Five Rites.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, Wei Zong of the Directorate of Education was made Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to oversee the Five Rites.

entries.zh: 十四年，通事舍人王喦上疏，請刪去禮記舊文而益以今事，詔付集賢院議。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year, Remonstrance Clerk Wang Yan memorialized, asking to delete old text from the Book of Rites and add present affairs; an edict referred it to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies for deliberation.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, Remonstrance Clerk Wang Yan memorialized, asking to delete old text from the Book of Rites and add present affairs; an edict referred it to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies for deliberation.

entries.zh: 學士張說以為禮記不刊之書，去聖久遠，不可改易，而唐貞觀顯慶禮，儀注前後不同，宜加折衷，以為唐禮。
entries.en: Academician Zhang Yue held that the Book of Rites was an unalterable book, far from the sages and not to be changed, while Tang's Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals had ritual directions that differed before and after and should be harmonized into Tang ritual.
entries.literal: Academician Zhang Yue held that the Book of Rites was an unalterable book, far from the sages and not to be changed, while Tang's Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals had ritual directions that differed before and after and should be harmonized into Tang ritual.

entries.zh: 乃詔集賢院學士右散騎常侍徐堅、左拾遺李銳及太常博士施敬本撰述，歷年未就而銳卒，蕭嵩代銳為學士，奏起居舍人王仲丘撰定，為一百五十卷，是為大唐開元禮。
entries.en: An edict then ordered Academy academicians Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Xu Jian, Left Reminder Li Rui, and Court Music Doctor Shi Jingben to compile; years passed without completion and Rui died; Xiao Song replaced Rui as academician and memorialized that Diarist Wang Zhongqiu complete the work—in one hundred fifty scrolls: the Great Tang Kaiyuan Ritual.
entries.literal: An edict then ordered Academy academicians Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Xu Jian, Left Reminder Li Rui, and Court Music Doctor Shi Jingben to compile; years passed without completion and Rui died; Xiao Song replaced Rui as academician and memorialized that Diarist Wang Zhongqiu complete the work—in one hundred fifty scrolls: this was the Great Tang Kaiyuan Ritual.

entries.zh: 由是，唐之五禮之文始備，而後世用之，雖時小有損益，不能過也。
entries.en: Henceforth Tang's texts for the Five Rites were first complete; later ages used them, and though at times there were slight additions and subtractions, they could not surpass them.
entries.literal: Henceforth Tang's texts for the Five Rites were first complete; later ages used them, and though at times there were slight additions and subtractions, they could not surpass them.

entries.zh: 前祀一日，晡後，太史令、郊社令各常服，帥其屬升，設昊天上帝神座於壇上北方，南向，席以槀秸。
entries.en: One day before the sacrifice, after the afternoon, the Astronomical Director and Suburban Altar Director each in regular dress lead their subordinates up and set the spirit seat of the August Supreme Lord of Heaven on the altar in the north, facing south, with straw mat seating.
entries.literal: One day before the sacrifice, after the afternoon, the Astronomical Director and Suburban Altar Director each in regular dress lead their subordinates up and set the spirit seat of the August Supreme Lord of Heaven on the altar in the north, facing south, with straw mat seating.

entries.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝神座於東方，西向，席以莞。
entries.en: The spirit seat of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao in the east, facing west, with rush mat seating.
entries.literal: The spirit seat of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao in the east, facing west, with rush mat seating.

entries.zh: 五方帝、日、月於壇第一等，青帝於東陛之北，赤帝於南陛之東，黃帝於南陛之西，白帝於西陛之南，黑帝於北陛之西，大明於東陛之南，夜明於西陛之北，席皆以槀秸。
entries.en: The Five Directional Emperors. sun, and moon on the altar's first tier—the Green Emperor north of the eastern steps, Red Emperor east of the southern steps, Yellow Emperor west of the southern steps, White Emperor south of the western steps, Black Emperor west of the northern steps, Great Brightness south of the eastern steps, Night Brightness north of the western steps—all with straw mat seating.
entries.literal: The Five Directional Emperors, sun, and moon on the altar's first tier—the Green Emperor north of the eastern steps, Red Emperor east of the southern steps, Yellow Emperor west of the southern steps, White Emperor south of the western steps, Black Emperor west of the northern steps, Great Brightness south of the eastern steps, Night Brightness north of the western steps—all with straw mat seating.

entries.zh: 五星、十二辰、河漢及內官五十有五於第二等十有二陛之間，各依其方，席皆內向。
entries.en: The Five Stars, twelve chronograms, the River Han, and fifty-five inner officials on the second tier among the twelve flights of steps, each according to its direction, seats facing inward.
entries.literal: The Five Stars, twelve chronograms, the River Han, and fifty-five inner officials on the second tier among the twelve flights of steps, each according to its direction, seats all facing inward.

entries.zh: 其內官有北辰座於東陛之北，曜魄寶於北陛之西，北斗於南陛之東，天一、太一皆在北斗之東，五帝內座於曜魄寶之東，皆差在前。
entries.en: Among inner officials there is the North Star seat north of the eastern steps; Shining Soul Treasure west of the northern steps; Northern Dipper east of the southern steps; Celestial One and Supreme One both east of the Northern Dipper; and the Five Emperors' inner seats east of Shining Soul Treasure, all slightly forward.
entries.literal: Among inner officials there is the North Star seat north of the eastern steps, Shining Soul Treasure west of the northern steps, Northern Dipper east of the southern steps, Celestial One and Supreme One both east of the Northern Dipper, the Five Emperors' inner seats east of Shining Soul Treasure—all slightly forward.

entries.zh: 二十八宿及中官一百五十有九於第三等，其二十八宿及帝座、七公、日星、帝席、大角、攝提、太微、太子、明堂、軒轅、三台、五車、諸王、月星、織女、建星、天紀等一十有七皆差在前。
entries.en: The twenty-eight lunar mansions and one hundred fifty-nine middle officials occupy the third tier. Among them, the twenty-eight mansions, Imperial Seat, Seven Elders, Sun Star, Emperor's Seat, Great Horn, Triumphant Arch, Supreme Palace, Heir Apparent, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record, and seventeen others are all slightly forward.
entries.literal: The twenty-eight lunar mansions and one hundred fifty-nine middle officials on the third tier; of the twenty-eight mansions and Imperial Seat, Seven Elders, Sun Star, Emperor's Seat, Great Horn, Triumphant Arch, Supreme Palace, Heir Apparent, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record, and seventeen others—all slightly forward.

entries.zh: 外官一百有五於內壝之內，眾星三百六十於內壝之外，各依方次十有二道之間，席皆以莞。
entries.en: One hundred five outer officials stand inside the inner enclosure, and three hundred sixty multitude stars stand outside it, each according to directional order among the twelve paths; the seats are all rush mats.
entries.literal: One hundred five outer officials inside the inner enclosure; three hundred sixty multitude stars outside the inner enclosure, each according to directional order among the twelve paths—seating all rush mats.

entries.zh: 又設酒尊之位。
entries.en: Again wine-vessel positions stand.
entries.literal: Again wine-vessel positions are set.

entries.zh: 上帝，太尊、著尊、犧尊、山罍各二，在壇上東南隅，北向；
entries.en: For the August Lord. two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the southeast corner of the altar, facing north;
entries.literal: For the August Lord, two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the southeast corner of the altar, facing north;

entries.zh: 象尊、壺尊、山罍各二，在壇下南陛之東，北向，俱西上。
entries.en: two Elephant Vessels. two Pot Vessels, and two Mountain Urns east of the southern steps below the altar, facing north—all west ascending.
entries.literal: two Elephant Vessels, two Pot Vessels, and two Mountain Urns east of the southern steps below the altar, facing north—all west ascending.

entries.zh: 配帝，著尊、犧尊、象尊、山罍各二，在壇上，於上帝酒尊之東，北向西上。
entries.en: For the accompanying emperor. two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the altar east of the August Lord's wine vessels—north-facing, west ascending.
entries.literal: For the accompanying emperor, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the altar east of the August Lord's wine vessels—north-facing, west ascending.

entries.zh: 五帝、日、月各太尊二，在第一等。
entries.en: For the Five Emperors, sun, and moon, each two Grand Vessels At the first tier.
entries.literal: For the Five Emperors, sun, and moon, each two Grand Vessels in the first tier.

entries.zh: 內官每陛間各象尊二，在第二等。
entries.en: For inner officials, two Elephant Vessels between every flight of steps in the second tier.
entries.literal: For inner officials, two Elephant Vessels between each flight of steps in the second tier.

entries.zh: 中官每陛間各壺尊二，在第三等。
entries.en: For middle officials, two Pot Vessels between every flight of steps in the third tier.
entries.literal: For middle officials, two Pot Vessels between each flight of steps in the third tier.

entries.zh: 外官每道間各概尊二，於下壇下。
entries.en: For outer officials, two Pouring Vessels between every path below the lower altar.
entries.literal: For outer officials, two Pouring Vessels between each path below the lower altar.

entries.zh: 眾星每道間各散尊二，於內壝之外。
entries.en: For the multitude of stars, two Scattered Vessels between every path outside the inner enclosure.
entries.literal: For the multitude of stars, two Scattered Vessels between each path outside the inner enclosure.

entries.zh: 凡尊，設於神座之左而右向。
entries.en: For all vessels, they stand to the left of the spirit seat and face right.
entries.literal: For all vessels, they are set to the left of the spirit seat and face right.

entries.zh: 尊皆加勺冪，五帝、日、月以上，皆有坫，以置爵也。
entries.en: All vessels have ladles and covers added. for the Five Emperors, sun, moon, and above, all have stands for placing cups.
entries.literal: All vessels have ladles and covers added; for the Five Emperors, sun, moon, and above, all have stands for placing cups.

entries.zh: 設御洗於午陛東南，亞獻、終獻同洗於卯陛之南，皆北向。
entries.en: The imperial washing place southeast of the wu steps. secondary and final offerings share a wash south of the mao steps—facing north.
entries.literal: The imperial washing place southeast of the wu steps; secondary and final offerings share a wash south of the mao steps—all facing north.

entries.zh: 罍水在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆。
entries.en: Water urns east of the wash. baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.
entries.literal: Water urns east of the wash; baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.

entries.zh: 篚，實以巾爵也。
entries.en: The baskets hold cloth-wrapped cups.
entries.literal: The baskets hold cloth-wrapped cups.

entries.zh: 分獻，罍、洗、篚、冪各於其方陛道之左，內向。
entries.en: For separate offerings. urns, wash, baskets, and covers each on the left of their side's steps and path, facing inward.
entries.literal: For separate offerings, urns, wash, baskets, and covers each on the left of their side's steps and path, facing inward.

entries.zh: 執尊、罍、篚、冪者，各立於其後。
entries.en: Those holding vessels. urns, baskets, and covers each stand behind them.
entries.literal: Those holding vessels, urns, baskets, and covers each stand behind them.

entries.zh: 玉幣之篚於壇上下尊坫之所。
entries.en: Baskets for jade and silks at the stands of vessels on and below the altar.
entries.literal: Baskets for jade and silks at the stands of vessels on and below the altar.

entries.zh: 若在宗廟，則前享三日，尚舍直長施大次於廟東門之外道北，南向。
entries.en: If at the ancestral temple. then three days before the offering, the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy north of the road outside the temple's east gate, facing south.
entries.literal: If at the ancestral temple, then three days before the offering, the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy north of the road outside the temple's east gate, facing south.

entries.zh: 守宮設文武侍臣次於其後，文左武右，俱南向。
entries.en: The Palace Keeper sets civil and military attendant ministers' canopies behind it—civil left, military right, facing south.
entries.literal: The Palace Keeper sets civil and military attendant ministers' canopies behind it—civil left, military right, all facing south.

entries.zh: 設諸享官、九廟子孫於齋坊內道東近南，西向北上。
entries.en: All offering officers and descendants of the nine temples east inside the purification quarters near the south—west-facing, north ascending.
entries.literal: All offering officers and descendants of the nine temples east inside the purification quarters near the south—west-facing, north ascending.

entries.zh: 文官九品又於其南，東方、南方蕃客又於其南，西向北上。
entries.en: Civil officials of the ninth rank further south. eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.
entries.literal: Civil officials of the ninth rank further south; eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.

entries.zh: 介公、酅公於廟西門之外，近南。
entries.en: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi outside the temple's west gate, near the south.
entries.literal: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi outside the temple's west gate, near the south.

entries.zh: 武官九品於其南，西方、北方蕃客又於其南，東向北上。
entries.en: Military officials of the ninth rank south of them. western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.
entries.literal: Military officials of the ninth rank south of them; western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.

entries.zh: 前享一日，奉禮郎設御位於廟東南，西向。
entries.en: One day before the offering; the Master of Ceremonies sets the imperial position southeast of the temple, facing west.
entries.literal: One day before the offering, the Master of Ceremonies sets the imperial position southeast of the temple, facing west.

entries.zh: 設享官公卿位於東門之內道南，執事者位於其後，西向北上。
entries.en: Sets the positions of the offering officers and grandees south of the road inside the east gate, with the attendants positioned behind them—facing west, north ascending.
entries.literal: Sets the positions of the offering officers and grandees south of the road inside the east gate, with the attendants positioned behind them—facing west, north ascending.

entries.zh: 御史位於廟堂之下，一在東南，西向；
entries.en: Censor positions below the temple hall: one in the southeast, facing west;
entries.literal: Censor positions below the temple hall: one in the southeast, facing west;

entries.zh: 一在西南，東向。
entries.en: One southwest, facing east.
entries.literal: One southwest, facing east.

entries.zh: 令史各陪其後。
entries.en: Clerks each attend behind them.
entries.literal: Clerks each attend behind them.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎位於樂縣東北，贊者二人，在南差退，俱西向。
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand. two presenters south, slightly back—facing west.
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand; two presenters south, slightly back—all facing west.

entries.zh: 協律郎位於廟堂上前楹之間，近西，東向。
entries.en: The Pitch-Pipe Master between the front pillars of the temple hall. near the west, facing east.
entries.literal: The Pitch-Pipe Master between the front pillars of the temple hall, near the west, facing east.

entries.zh: 太樂令位於北縣之間，北向。
entries.en: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing north.
entries.literal: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing north.

entries.zh: 設從享之官位，九廟子孫於享官公卿之南，昭、穆異位。
entries.en: Positions for accompanying officers: descendants of the nine temples south of offering officers and grandees, zhao and mu in separate positions.
entries.literal: Positions for accompanying officers: descendants of the nine temples south of offering officers and grandees, zhao and mu in separate positions.

entries.zh: 文官九品以上，又於其南，東方、南方蕃客又於其南，西向北上。
entries.en: Civil officials of the ninth rank and above further south. eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.
entries.literal: Civil officials of the ninth rank and above further south; eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.

entries.zh: 介公、酅公位於西門之內道南，武官九品於其南，少西，西方、北方蕃客又於其南，東向北上。
entries.en: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road inside the west gate. military officials of the ninth rank south of them, slightly west. western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.
entries.literal: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road inside the west gate; military officials of the ninth rank south of them, slightly west; western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.

entries.zh: 設牲牓於東門之外，如郊之位。
entries.en: The victim placard outside the east gate, as at the suburban altar.
entries.literal: The victim placard outside the east gate, as at the suburban altar.

entries.zh: 設尊彝之位於廟堂之上下，每座斝彝一，黃彝一，犧尊、象尊、著尊、山罍各二，在堂上，皆於神座之左。
entries.en: Vessel positions above and below the temple hall: for each seat one Jia vessel. one Yellow vessel, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Mountain Urns on the hall—all to the left of the spirit seat.
entries.literal: Vessel positions above and below the temple hall: for each seat one Jia vessel, one Yellow vessel, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Mountain Urns on the hall—all to the left of the spirit seat.

entries.zh: 獻祖、太祖、高祖、高宗尊彝在前楹間，北向；
entries.en: The ritual vessels of Xianzu, Taizu, Gaozu, and Gaozong stood in the front intercolumnar space, facing north;
entries.literal: The honored vessels of the Founding Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and Gaozong were in the front bays between pillars, facing north;

entries.zh: 懿祖、代祖、太宗、中宗、睿宗尊彝在戶外，南向。
entries.en: The ritual vessels of Yizu, Daizu, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong stood outside the hall doors, facing south.
entries.literal: The honored vessels of Yizu, Daizu, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong were outside the doors, facing south.

entries.zh: 各有坫焉。
entries.en: Each has a stand.
entries.literal: Each has a stand.

entries.zh: 其壺尊二、太尊二、山罍四，皆在堂下階間，北向西上；
entries.en: Two Pot Vessels. two Grand Vessels, four Mountain Urns all between the steps below the hall, north-facing, west ascending;
entries.literal: Two Pot Vessels, two Grand Vessels, four Mountain Urns all between the steps below the hall, north-facing, west ascending;

entries.zh: 簋、鈃、籩、豆在堂上，俱東側階之北。
entries.en: gui. xing, bian, and dou vessels on the hall, all north of the eastern side steps.
entries.literal: gui, xing, bian, and dou vessels on the hall, all north of the eastern side steps.
