entries.zh: 每座四簋居前，四簠次之，六豋次之，六鈃次之，籩、豆為後，皆以南為上，屈陳而下。
entries.en: For each seat four gui in front. four fu next, six deng next, six xing next, bian and dou last—all with south as upper, bending down in rows.
entries.literal: For each seat four gui in front, four fu next, six deng next, six xing next, bian and dou last—all with south as upper, bending down in rows.

entries.zh: 御洗在東階東南，亞獻又於東南，俱北向。
entries.en: The imperial wash southeast of the eastern steps. secondary offering again southeast—facing north.
entries.literal: The imperial wash southeast of the eastern steps; secondary offering again southeast—all facing north.

entries.zh: 罍水在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆。
entries.en: Water urns east of the wash. baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.
entries.literal: Water urns east of the wash; baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.

entries.zh: 享日，未明五刻，太廟令服其服，布昭、穆之座於戶外，自西序以東：獻祖、太祖、高祖、高宗皆北廂南向，懿祖、代祖、太宗、中宗、睿宗南廂北向。
entries.en: On the offering day, at the fifth quarter before dawn, the Temple Director dons his robes and arranges zhao and mu seats outside the doors, from the western wing eastward: Offering Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and Gaozong all in the north wing facing south; Esteemed Ancestor, Substitute Ancestor, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong in the south wing facing north.
entries.literal: On the offering day, at the fifth quarter before dawn, the Temple Director dons his robes and arranges zhao and mu seats outside the doors, from the western wing eastward: Offering Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and High Zong all in the north wing facing south; Esteemed Ancestor, Substitute Ancestor, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong in the south wing facing north.

entries.zh: 每座黼扆，莞席紛純，藻席畫純，次席黼純，左右几。
entries.en: For each seat black-lacquered screen. rush mat with red border, painted rush mat with patterned border, secondary mat with patterned border, left and right tables.
entries.literal: For each seat black-lacquered screen, rush mat with red border, painted rush mat with patterned border, secondary mat with patterned border, left and right tables.

entries.zh: 由三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達于天下；
entries.en: Before the Three Dynasties ended, government and ritual issued from a single source, and rites and music permeated the realm;
entries.literal: From the Three Dynasties upward, governance issued from one source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm;

entries.zh: 由三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂為虛名。
entries.en: After the Three Dynasties, government split in two, and rites and music became mere names.
entries.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward, governance issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty names.

entries.zh: 古者，宮室車輿以為居，衣裳冕弁以為服，尊爵俎豆以為器，金石絲竹以為樂，以適郊廟，以臨朝廷，以事神而治民。
entries.en: In antiquity, palaces and carriages were one's home, garments and ceremonial caps one's dress, goblets and sacrificial stands one's vessels, and metal, stone, silk, and bamboo one's music—used at suburban altars and temples, at court, to serve the spirits and govern the people.
entries.literal: In antiquity, palaces and carriages served as dwelling; robes, caps, and coronets served as dress; goblets, bells, and stands served as vessels; metal, stone, silk, and bamboo served as music—to attend suburban altars and ancestral temples, to preside at court, to serve the spirits and govern the people.

entries.zh: 其歲時聚會以為朝覲、聘問，懽欣交接以為射鄉、食饗，合眾興事以為師田、學校，下至里閭田畝，吉凶哀樂，凡民之事，莫不一出於禮。
entries.en: Seasonal gatherings became court audiences and embassies; festive gatherings became archery meets and banquets; mass assemblies became military hunts and schools. Down to village lanes and fields, through joy and grief and music in ordinary life—nothing in the people's affairs fell outside ritual.
entries.literal: Their seasonal gatherings served as court audiences and diplomatic missions; joyful social exchanges served as archery fêtes and feasts; assembling the multitude for undertakings served as military hunts and schools—from village lanes and fields down to joy, sorrow, and music in the lives of common people, nothing among the people's affairs did not wholly issue from ritual.

entries.zh: 由之以教其民為孝慈、友悌、忠信、仁義者，常不出於居處、動作、衣服、飲食之間。
entries.en: Through these the people were taught filial piety, kindness, fraternity, loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness—almost always within the bounds of daily dwelling, movement, dress, and food.
entries.literal: Through these to teach the people filial piety, kindness, fraternity, loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness—such teaching rarely departed from dwelling, movement, clothing, and food.

entries.zh: 蓋其朝夕從事者，無非乎此也。
entries.en: Morning and evening they pursued nothing but this.
entries.literal: For what they pursued morning and evening was nothing but this.

entries.zh: 此所謂治出於一，而禮樂達天下，使天下安習而行之，不知所以遷善遠罪而成俗也。
entries.en: This is governance from a single source, with rites and music reaching the world—so that all under Heaven practiced them securely, unaware how they turned toward goodness, shunned wrongdoing, and formed custom.
entries.literal: This is what is called governance issuing from one source, with rites and music reaching all under Heaven, causing all under Heaven to practice them securely and habitually, unaware how they turned toward goodness, shunned wrongdoing, and formed custom.

entries.zh: 六曰進熟。
entries.en: Sixth: presenting the cooked offering.
entries.literal: Sixth, presenting the cooked offering.

entries.zh: 皇帝既升，奠玉、幣。
entries.en: Once the emperor has ascended, he presents jade and silks.
entries.literal: After the emperor has ascended, he presents jade and silks.

entries.zh: 太官令帥進饌者奉饌，各陳於內壝門外。
entries.en: The Imperial Kitchen Director leads food-bearers with the offerings, each placing them outside the inner enclosure gate.
entries.literal: The Imperial Kitchen Director leads food-bearers bearing offerings; each arrays them outside the inner enclosure gate.

entries.zh: 謁者引司徒出詣饌所，司徒奉昊天上帝之俎，太官令引饌入門，各至其陛。
entries.en: An usher leads the Minister over Masses to the offering station, where he bears the tray for the August Supreme Lord of Heaven; the Imperial Kitchen Director leads the offerings through the gate, each to its proper steps.
entries.literal: The usher leads the Minister over Masses out to the offering station; the Minister over Masses bears the tray for the August Supreme Lord of Heaven; the Imperial Kitchen Director leads the offerings through the gate, each to its steps.

entries.zh: 祝史俱進，跪，徹毛血之豆，降自東陛以出。
entries.en: The invokers advance together, kneel, remove the hair-and-blood beans, and descend the eastern steps to exit.
entries.literal: Invokers all advance together, kneel, remove the hair-and-blood beans, and descend the eastern steps to exit.

entries.zh: 諸太祝迎饌於壇上，司徒、太官令俱降自東陛以出。
entries.en: The Chief Invokers receive the offerings on the altar; the Minister over Masses and Imperial Kitchen Director both descend the eastern steps and exit.
entries.literal: The various Chief Invokers receive the offerings on the altar; the Minister over Masses and Imperial Kitchen Director both descend the eastern steps to exit.

entries.zh: 又進設外官、眾星之饌。
entries.en: Offerings for the outer officials and the host of stars are set out next.
entries.literal: Offerings for outer officials and the host of stars are presented next.

entries.zh: 皇帝詣罍洗，盥手，洗爵，升壇自南陛。
entries.en: The emperor goes to the washing urn, washes his hands, rinses the goblet, and ascends the altar by the southern steps.
entries.literal: The emperor proceeds to the urn for washing, washes his hands, rinses the goblet, and ascends the altar by the southern steps.

entries.zh: 司徒升自東陛，立於尊所。
entries.en: The Minister over Masses ascends the eastern steps and stands at the vessel position.
entries.literal: The Minister over Masses ascends the eastern steps and stands at the vessel position.

entries.zh: 齋郎奉俎從升，立於司徒後。
entries.en: Purification youths bearing trays follow him up and stand behind the Minister over Masses.
entries.literal: Purification youths bearing trays follow up and stand behind the Minister over Masses.

entries.zh: 皇帝詣上帝尊所，執尊者舉冪，侍中贊酌汎齊，進昊天上帝前，北向跪，奠爵，興，少退，立。
entries.en: The emperor goes to the Supreme Lord's vessel position; the attendant raises the cover; the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation. He advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, rises, steps back slightly, and stands.
entries.literal: The emperor proceeds to the vessel position for the Supreme Lord, the vessel attendant raises the cover, the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation; he advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, rises, steps back slightly, and stands.

entries.zh: 太祝持版進於神右，東向跪，讀祝文曰：「維某年歲次月朔日，嗣天子臣某，敢昭告于昊天上帝。」
entries.en: The Chief Invoker advances with the prayer board to the spirit's right, kneels facing east, and reads: "In the year ___, on the ___ day of the first month, the heir Son of Heaven, your subject ___, ventures to announce to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven."
entries.literal: The Chief Invoker advances with the prayer board to the right of the spirit, kneels facing east, and reads the prayer text: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the heir Son of Heaven, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven."

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice.

entries.zh: 詣配帝酒尊所，執尊者舉冪，侍中取爵於坫以進，皇帝受爵，侍中贊酌汎齊，進高祖神堯皇帝前，東向跪，奠，興，少退，立。
entries.en: He goes to the associated deity's wine vessel; the attendant raises the cover; the Palace Attendant takes a goblet from the stand and presents it. The emperor receives it; the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation and advances before Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor. He kneels facing east, presents the offering, rises, steps back slightly, and stands.
entries.literal: He proceeds to the wine vessel position for the associated deity; the vessel attendant raises the cover; the Palace Attendant takes a goblet from the stand and advances it; the emperor receives the goblet; the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation and advances before Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor; he kneels facing east, presents the offering, rises, steps back slightly, and stands.

entries.zh: 太祝持版進於左，北向跪，讀祝文曰：「維某年歲次月朔日，曾孫開元神武皇帝臣某，敢昭告于高祖神堯皇帝。」
entries.en: The Chief Invoker advances with the board to the left, kneels facing north, and reads: "In the year ___, on the ___ day of the first month, the great-grandson, the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor, your subject ___, ventures to announce to Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor."
entries.literal: The Chief Invoker advances with the board to the left, kneels facing north, and reads the prayer text: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the great-grandson, the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor, your subject so-and-so, ventures to announce to Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor."

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice again.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice.

entries.zh: 進昊天上帝前，北向立。
entries.en: He advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven and stands facing north.
entries.literal: He advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven and stands facing north.

entries.zh: 太祝各以爵酌上尊福酒，合置一爵，太祝持爵授侍中以進，皇帝再拜，受爵，跪，祭酒，啐酒，奠爵，俛伏，興。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine from the upper vessel; they combine it in one goblet; the Chief Invoker gives it to the Palace Attendant to present. The emperor bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, sips the wine, sets down the goblet, prostrates, and rises.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine from the upper vessel with a goblet; they combine it in one goblet; the Chief Invoker presents the goblet to the Palace Attendant to advance; the emperor bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, sips the wine, sets down the goblet, prostrates, and rises.

entries.zh: 太祝各帥齋郎進俎。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker leads purification youths forward with the trays.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker leads purification youths to advance the trays.

entries.zh: 太祝減神前胙肉，共置一俎，授司徒以進，皇帝受以授左右。
entries.en: The Chief Invokers cut the sacrificial flesh before the spirits, place it on one tray, and present it through the Minister over Masses; the emperor receives it and hands it to his attendants.
entries.literal: The Chief Invokers cut the sacrificial flesh before the spirits, place it together on one tray, and present it through the Minister over Masses; the emperor receives it and hands it to attendants at his sides.

entries.zh: 皇帝跪，取爵，遂飲，卒爵。
entries.en: The emperor kneels, takes the goblet, drinks, and finishes it.
entries.literal: The emperor kneels, takes the goblet, then drinks and finishes the goblet.

entries.zh: 侍中進受虛爵，復於坫。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant receives the empty goblet and returns it to the stand.
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant advances to receive the empty goblet and returns it to the stand.

entries.zh: 皇帝俛伏，興，再拜，降自南陛，復于位。
entries.en: The emperor prostrates, rises, bows twice, descends the southern steps, and returns to his place.
entries.literal: The emperor prostrates, rises, bows twice, descends the southern steps, and returns to his position.

entries.zh: 文舞出，武舞入。
entries.en: The civil dance exits and the military dance enters.
entries.literal: The civil dance exits; the military dance enters.

entries.zh: 初，皇帝將復位，謁者引太尉詣罍洗，盥手，洗瓠爵，自東陛升壇，詣昊天上帝著尊所，執尊者舉冪，太尉酌醴齊，進昊天上帝前，北向跪，奠爵，興，再拜。
entries.en: When the emperor is about to return to his position, an usher leads the Grand Commandant to the washing urn. He washes his hands, rinses the gourd goblet, ascends by the eastern steps, and goes to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven's sacrificial vessel. The attendant raises the cover; the Grand Commandant pours the second libation, advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, rises, and bows twice.
entries.literal: At first, as the emperor is about to return to his position, the usher leads the Grand Commandant to the washing urn; he washes his hands and rinses the gourd goblet, ascends the altar by the eastern steps, proceeds to the sacrificial vessel position for the August Supreme Lord of Heaven; the vessel attendant raises the cover; the Grand Commandant pours the second libation, advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, rises, and bows twice.

entries.zh: 詣配帝犧尊所，取爵於坫，酌醴齊，進高祖神堯皇帝前，東向跪，奠爵，興，再拜。
entries.en: He goes to the associated deity's sacrificial vessel, takes a goblet from the stand, pours the second libation, advances before Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor, kneels facing east, sets down the goblet, rises, and bows twice.
entries.literal: He proceeds to the sacrificial vessel position for the associated deity, takes a goblet from the stand, pours the second libation, advances before Emperor Gaozu the Divine Progenitor, kneels facing east, sets down the goblet, rises, and bows twice.

entries.zh: 進昊天上帝前，北向立。
entries.en: He again advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven and stands facing north.
entries.literal: He advances before the August Supreme Lord of Heaven and stands facing north.

entries.zh: 諸太祝各以爵酌福酒，合置一爵，進于右，西向立。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine into one goblet, advances it to the right, and stands facing west.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine with a goblet; they combine it in one goblet and advance it to the right; they stand facing west.

entries.zh: 太尉再拜，受爵，跪，祭酒，遂飲，卒爵。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, drinks, and finishes it.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, then drinks and finishes the goblet.

entries.zh: 太祝進受虛爵，復於坫。
entries.en: The Chief Invoker receives the empty goblet and returns it to the stand.
entries.literal: The Chief Invoker advances to receive the empty goblet and returns it to the stand.

entries.zh: 太尉再拜，降，復位。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant bows twice, descends, and returns to his station.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant bows twice, descends, and returns to his position.

entries.zh: 初，太尉獻將畢，謁者引光祿卿詣罍洗，盥手，洗瓠爵，升，酌盎齊。
entries.en: When the Grand Commandant's offering is nearly complete, an usher leads the Director of the Imperial Household to the washing urn. He washes his hands, rinses the gourd goblet, ascends, and pours the third libation.
entries.literal: At first, when the Grand Commandant's offering is nearly complete, the usher leads the Director of the Imperial Household to the washing urn; he washes his hands, rinses the gourd goblet, ascends, and pours the third libation.

entries.zh: 終獻如亞獻。
entries.en: The final offering follows the same procedure as the secondary offering.
entries.literal: The final offering follows the secondary offering.

entries.zh: 太尉將升獻，謁者七人分引五方帝及大明、夜明等獻官，詣罍洗，盥手，洗瓠爵，各由其陛升，酌汎齊，進，跪奠於神前。
entries.en: When the Grand Commandant is about to offer, seven ushers lead the offering officers for the Five Directional Emperors, the Bright Luminary, the Night Luminary, and the like to the washing urn. They wash their hands, rinse gourd goblets, ascend by their respective steps, pour the first libation, advance, kneel, and set offerings before the spirits.
entries.literal: When the Grand Commandant is about to ascend to offer, seven ushers in turn lead the offering officers for the Five Directional Emperors, the Bright Luminary, the Night Luminary, and the like to the washing urn; they wash their hands, rinse gourd goblets, each ascend by his steps, pour the first libation, advance, kneel, and set offerings before the spirits.

entries.zh: 初，第一等獻官將升，謁者五人次引獻官各詣罍洗，盥、洗，各由其陛升壇，詣第二等內官酒尊所，酌汎齊以獻。
entries.en: When first-rank offering officers are about to ascend, five ushers in succession lead each to the washing urn. Each ascends by his steps to the second-rank inner officials' wine vessels and pours the first libation as an offering.
entries.literal: At first, when first-rank offering officers are about to ascend, five ushers in succession lead each offering officer to the washing urn to wash; each ascends the altar by his steps to the wine vessel positions for second-rank inner officials and pours the first libation to offer.

entries.zh: 贊者四人次引獻官詣罍洗，盥、洗，詣外官酒尊所，酌清酒以獻。
entries.en: Four presenters in succession lead offering officers to wash, then to the outer officials' wine vessels to pour clear wine as offerings.
entries.literal: Four presenters in succession lead offering officers to the washing urn to wash, then to the wine vessel positions for outer officials and pour clear wine to offer.

entries.zh: 贊者四人，次引獻官詣罍洗，盥、洗，詣眾星酒尊所，酌昔酒以獻。
entries.en: Four presenters next lead offering officers to wash, then to the host of stars' wine vessels to pour aged wine as offerings.
entries.literal: Four presenters next lead offering officers to the washing urn to wash, then to the wine vessel positions for the host of stars and pour aged wine to offer.

entries.zh: 其祝史、齋郎酌酒助奠，皆如內官。
entries.en: Invokers and purification youths who pour wine to assist in presentation follow the same procedure as the inner officials.
entries.literal: Invokers and purification youths who pour wine to assist in presentation all follow the inner officials.

entries.zh: 上下諸祝各進，跪徹豆，還尊所。
entries.en: Invokers above and below advance, kneel, remove the beans, and return to the vessel positions.
entries.literal: Invokers above and below each advance, kneel, remove the beans, and return to the vessel positions.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「賜胙。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies announces: "Bestow the sacrificial flesh."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bestow the sacrificial flesh."

entries.zh: 贊者曰：「眾官再拜。」
entries.en: The presenter announces: "All officials bow twice."
entries.literal: The presenter says: "All officials bow twice."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: Everyone in position bows twice.
entries.literal: All those in position bow twice.

entries.zh: 太常卿前奏：「請再拜。」
entries.en: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please bow twice."
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please bow twice."

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「眾官再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies announces: "All officials bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "All officials bow twice."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: Everyone in position bows twice.
entries.literal: All those in position bow twice.

entries.zh: 樂作一成。
entries.en: One movement of music is performed.
entries.literal: Music performs one movement.

entries.zh: 太常卿前奏：「請就望燎位。」
entries.en: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please take the position for gazing at the fire-offering."
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please take the position for gazing at the fire-offering."

entries.zh: 皇帝就位，南向立。
entries.en: The emperor takes position and stands facing south.
entries.literal: The emperor takes his position and stands facing south.

entries.zh: 上下諸祝各執篚，取玉、幣、祝版、禮物以上。
entries.en: Invokers above and below each take baskets, gather jade, silks, prayer boards, and ritual gifts, and ascend.
entries.literal: Invokers above and below each hold baskets, take up jade, silks, prayer boards, and ritual gifts, and ascend.

entries.zh: 齋郎以俎載牲體、稷、黍飯及爵酒，各由其陛降壇，詣柴壇，自南陛登，以幣、祝版、饌物置於柴上。
entries.en: Purification youths load trays with victim portions, millet and glutinous rice, and goblets of wine. Each descends by his steps, goes to the firewood altar, ascends the southern steps, and places silks, prayer boards, and offerings on the firewood.
entries.literal: Purification youths load trays with victim portions, millet and glutinous millet rice, and goblets of wine; each descends the altar by his steps, proceeds to the firewood altar, ascends the southern steps, and places silks, prayer boards, and offerings on the firewood.

entries.zh: 戶內諸祝又以內官以下禮幣皆從燎。
entries.en: Inner-chamber invokers also send ritual silks for inner officials and below to be burned together.
entries.literal: Inner-chamber invokers also send ritual silks for inner officials and below to the fire together.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「可燎。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies announces: "The fire may be lit."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "The fire may be lit."

entries.zh: 東。
entries.en: On the east and
entries.literal: On the east and

entries.zh: 西面各六人，以炬燎火。
entries.en: west sides, six people on each side light the fire with torches.
entries.literal: west sides, six persons on each side light the fire with torches.

entries.zh: 半柴，太常卿前曰：「禮畢。」
entries.en: When half the firewood is consumed, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices advances and says: "The rite is complete."
entries.literal: When half the firewood is consumed, the Director of the Imperial Sacrifices advances and says: "The rite is complete."

entries.zh: 皇帝還大次，出中壝門，殿中監前受鎮珪，以授尚衣奉御，殿中監又前受大珪。
entries.en: The emperor returns to the great tent and exits the middle enclosure gate. The Palace Director receives the securing tablet and hands it to the Imperial Wardrobe Attendant, then receives the great tablet.
entries.literal: The emperor returns to the great tent, exits the middle enclosure gate; the Palace Director advances to receive the securing tablet and hands it to the Imperial Wardrobe Attendant; the Palace Director again advances to receive the great tablet.

entries.zh: 皇帝入次，謁者、贊引各引祀官，通事舍人分引從祀羣官、諸方客使以次出。
entries.en: The emperor enters the tent. Ushers and presenters lead the sacrifice officers; the Communications Officer leads attending officials, those accompanying the sacrifice, and regional envoys out in order.
entries.literal: The emperor enters the tent; ushers and presenters each lead sacrifice officers; the Communications Officer leads attending officials, officials accompanying the sacrifice, and envoys from the regions to exit in order.

entries.zh: 贊者引御史、太祝以下俱復執事位。
entries.en: The presenter leads censors, Chief Invokers, and those below back to their service positions.
entries.literal: The presenter leads censors, Chief Invokers, and those below back together to their service positions.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies announces: "Bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bow twice."

entries.zh: 御史以下皆再拜，出。
entries.en: Censors and below all bow twice and exit.
entries.literal: Censors and below all bow twice and exit.

entries.zh: 工人、二舞以次出。
entries.en: Craftsmen and the two dances leave in order.
entries.literal: Craftsmen and the two dances exit in order.

entries.zh: 若宗廟，曰饋食。
entries.en: At the ancestral temple, this stage is called presenting food.
entries.literal: At the ancestral temple, it is called presenting food.

entries.zh: 皇帝既升，祼，太官令出，帥進饌者奉饌，陳於東門之外，西向南上。
entries.en: After the emperor has ascended and performed the libation, the Imperial Kitchen Director leads food-bearers with offerings, arrayed outside the eastern gate, facing west with south ascending priority.
entries.literal: After the emperor has ascended and performed the libation, the Imperial Kitchen Director goes out and leads food-bearers bearing offerings, arrayed outside the eastern gate, west-facing, south ascending.

entries.zh: 謁者引司徒出，詣饌所，司徒奉獻祖之俎。
entries.en: An usher leads the Minister over Masses to the offering station, where he bears the tray for the Offering Ancestor.
entries.literal: The usher leads the Minister over Masses out to the offering station; the Minister over Masses bears the tray for the Offering Ancestor.

entries.zh: 太官引饌入自正門，至於太階。
entries.en: The Imperial Kitchen Director leads the offerings in through the main gate to the great steps.
entries.literal: The Imperial Kitchen Director leads the offerings in through the main gate to the great steps.

entries.zh: 祝史俱進，徹毛血之豆，降自阼階以出。
entries.en: The invokers advance together, remove the hair-and-blood beans, and descend the eastern steps to exit.
entries.literal: Invokers all advance together and remove the hair-and-blood beans, descending the eastern steps to exit.

entries.zh: 諸太祝迎饌於階上設之，乃取蕭、稷、黍擩於脂，燔於爐。
entries.en: The Chief Invokers receive the offerings on the steps and set them out, then take artemisia, millet, and glutinous millet, knead them in fat, and burn them on the furnace.
entries.literal: The various Chief Invokers receive the offerings on the steps and set them out; they then take artemisia, millet, and glutinous millet, knead them in fat, and burn them on the furnace.

entries.zh: 太常卿引皇帝詣罍洗，盥手，洗爵，升自阼階，詣獻祖尊彝所，執尊者舉冪，侍中贊酌汎齊，進獻祖前，北向跪，奠爵。
entries.en: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices leads the emperor to the washing urn. He washes his hands, rinses the goblet, ascends the eastern steps, and goes to the Offering Ancestor's ritual vessel. The attendant raises the cover; the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation and advances before the Offering Ancestor. He kneels facing north and sets down the goblet.
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices leads the emperor to the washing urn; he washes his hands, rinses the goblet, ascends the eastern steps, proceeds to the ritual vessel position for the Offering Ancestor; the vessel attendant raises the cover; the Palace Attendant intones as he pours the first libation and advances before the Offering Ancestor; he kneels facing north and sets down the goblet.

entries.zh: 又詣尊所，侍中取爵於坫以進，酌汎齊，進神前，北向跪，奠爵，退立。
entries.en: He again goes to the vessel position; the Palace Attendant takes a goblet from the stand, pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, and withdraws to stand.
entries.literal: He again proceeds to the vessel position; the Palace Attendant takes a goblet from the stand and advances it, pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, sets down the goblet, and withdraws to stand.

entries.zh: 太祝持版進於神右，東面跪，讀祝文曰：「維某年歲次月朔日，孝曾孫開元神武皇帝某，敢昭告于獻祖宣皇帝、祖妣宣莊皇后張氏。」
entries.en: The Chief Invoker advances with the board to the spirit's right, kneels facing east, and reads: "In the year ___, on the ___ day of the first month, the filial great-grandson, the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor ___, ventures to announce to the Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan and the ancestress Empress Xuanzhuang of the Zhang clan."
entries.literal: The Chief Invoker advances with the board to the right of the spirit, kneels facing east, and reads the prayer text: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the filial great-grandson, the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor so-and-so, ventures to announce to the Offering Ancestor Emperor Xuan and the ancestress Empress Xuanzhuang of the Zhang clan."

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜，又再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice, then twice again.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice, and again twice.

entries.zh: 奠，詣懿祖尊彝，酌汎齊，進神前，南向跪，奠爵，少西，俛伏，興。
entries.en: Having presented the offering, he goes to the Accomplished Ancestor's ritual vessel, pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing south, sets down the goblet slightly to the west, prostrates, and rises.
entries.literal: Having presented the offering, he proceeds to the ritual vessel position for the Accomplished Ancestor, pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing south, sets down the goblet, slightly to the west, prostrates, and rises.

entries.zh: 又酌汎齊，進神前，南向跪，爵，少東，退立。
entries.en: He again pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing south, sets down the goblet slightly to the east, and withdraws to stand.
entries.literal: He again pours the first libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing south, sets down the goblet, slightly to the east, and withdraws to stand.

entries.zh: 祝史西面跪，讀祝文。
entries.en: The invoker kneels facing west and reads the prayer.
entries.literal: The invoker kneels facing west and reads the prayer text.

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜，又再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice, then twice again.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice, and again twice.

entries.zh: 次奠太祖、代祖、高祖、太宗、高宗、中宗、睿宗，皆如懿祖。
entries.en: Next he presents offerings to the Great Ancestor, Replaced Ancestor, High Ancestor, Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong, all following the Accomplished Ancestor's procedure.
entries.literal: Next he presents offerings to the Great Ancestor, the Replaced Ancestor, the High Ancestor, Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong, all as at the Accomplished Ancestor.

entries.zh: 乃詣東序，西向立。
entries.en: He then goes to the eastern sequence and stands facing west.
entries.literal: He then proceeds to the eastern sequence and stands facing west.

entries.zh: 司徒升自阼階，立於前楹間，北面東上。
entries.en: The Minister over Masses ascends the eastern steps and stands between the front pillars, facing north with east ascending priority.
entries.literal: The Minister over Masses ascends the eastern steps and stands between the front pillars, facing north with east ascending priority.

entries.zh: 諸太祝各以爵酌上尊福酒，合置一爵，太祝持爵授侍中以進。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine from the upper vessel into one goblet; the Chief Invoker gives it to the Palace Attendant to present.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine from the upper vessel with a goblet; they combine it in one goblet; the Chief Invoker presents the goblet to the Palace Attendant to advance.

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜，受爵，跪，祭酒，啐酒，奠爵，俛伏，興。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, sips the wine, sets down the goblet, prostrates, and rises.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, sips the wine, sets down the goblet, prostrates, and rises.

entries.zh: 諸太祝各帥齋郎進俎，太祝減神前三牲胙肉，共置一俎上，以黍、稷飯共置一籩，授司徒以進；
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker leads purification youths to advance the trays. The Chief Invokers cut the three-sacrifice flesh before the spirits, place it on one tray, place millet and glutinous rice together on one bian, and present them through the Minister over Masses;
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker leads purification youths to advance the trays; the Chief Invokers cut the three-sacrifice flesh before the spirits, place it together on one tray, place millet and glutinous millet rice together on one bian, and present them through the Minister over Masses;

entries.zh: 太祝又以胙肉授司徒以進。
entries.en: the Chief Invoker again presents sacrificial flesh through the Minister over Masses.
entries.literal: the Chief Invoker again presents sacrificial flesh through the Minister over Masses to advance.

entries.zh: 皇帝每受，以授左右，乃跪取爵，飲，卒爵。
entries.en: Each time the emperor receives an offering he hands it to his attendants, then kneels, takes the goblet, drinks, and finishes it.
entries.literal: Each time the emperor receives an offering he hands it to attendants at his sides, then kneels, takes the goblet, drinks, and finishes the goblet.

entries.zh: 侍中進受虛爵，以授太祝，復於坫。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant receives the empty goblet and hands it to the Chief Invoker, who returns it to the stand.
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant advances to receive the empty goblet and hands it to the Chief Invoker, who returns it to the stand.

entries.zh: 皇帝降自阼階，復于版位。
entries.en: The emperor descends the eastern steps and returns to his designated ceremonial station.
entries.literal: The emperor descends the eastern steps and returns to the position marked by his ceremonial tablet.

entries.zh: 文舞出，武舞入。
entries.en: The civil dance exits and the military dance enters.
entries.literal: The civil dance exits; the military dance enters.

entries.zh: 初，皇帝將復位，太尉詣罍洗，盥手，洗爵，升自阼階，詣獻祖尊彝所，酌醴齊進神前，北向跪，奠爵；
entries.en: When the emperor is about to return to his position, the Grand Commandant goes to the washing urn, washes his hands, rinses the goblet, ascends the eastern steps, and goes to the Offering Ancestor's ritual vessel. He pours the second libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, and sets down the goblet;
entries.literal: At first, as the emperor is about to return to his position, the Grand Commandant proceeds to the washing urn, washes his hands, rinses the goblet, ascends the eastern steps, proceeds to the ritual vessel position for the Offering Ancestor, pours the second libation and advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, and sets down the goblet;

entries.zh: 少東，興，再拜。
entries.en: slightly to the east, rises, and bows twice.
entries.literal: slightly to the east, he rises and bows twice.

entries.zh: 又取爵於坫，酌醴齊進神前，北向跪，奠爵；
entries.en: He again takes a goblet from the stand, pours the second libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, and sets down the goblet;
entries.literal: He again takes a goblet from the stand, pours the second libation, advances before the spirit, kneels facing north, and sets down the goblet;

entries.zh: 少西，北向再拜。
entries.en: slightly to the west, and bows twice facing north.
entries.literal: slightly to the west, he bows twice facing north.

entries.zh: 次奠懿祖、太祖、代祖、高祖、太宗、高宗、中宗、睿宗如獻祖。
entries.en: Next he presents offerings to the Accomplished Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Replaced Ancestor, High Ancestor, Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong as at the Offering Ancestor.
entries.literal: Next he presents offerings to the Accomplished Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Replaced Ancestor, High Ancestor, Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong as at the Offering Ancestor.

entries.zh: 乃詣東序，西向立。
entries.en: He then goes to the eastern sequence and stands facing west.
entries.literal: He then proceeds to the eastern sequence and stands facing west.

entries.zh: 諸太祝各以爵酌福酒，合置一爵，太祝持爵進於左，北向立。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine into one goblet; the Chief Invoker advances with it to the left and stands facing north.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker pours blessed wine with a goblet; they combine it in one goblet; the Chief Invoker advances with the goblet to the left and stands facing north.

entries.zh: 太尉再拜受爵，跪，祭酒，遂飲，卒爵。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, drinks, and finishes it.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant bows twice, receives the goblet, kneels, offers a libation, then drinks and finishes the goblet.

entries.zh: 太祝進受爵，復於坫。
entries.en: The Chief Invoker receives the goblet and returns it to the stand.
entries.literal: The Chief Invoker advances to receive the goblet and returns it to the stand.

entries.zh: 太尉興，再拜，復于位。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant rises, bows twice, and returns to his station.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant rises, bows twice, and returns to his position.

entries.zh: 初，太尉獻將畢，謁者引光祿卿詣罍洗，盥、洗，升，酌盎齊。
entries.en: When the Grand Commandant's offering is nearly complete, an usher leads the Director of the Imperial Household to wash, ascend, and pour the third libation.
entries.literal: At first, when the Grand Commandant's offering is nearly complete, the usher leads the Director of the Imperial Household to the washing urn to wash, ascends, and pours the third libation.

entries.zh: 終獻如亞獻。
entries.en: The final offering follows the same procedure as the secondary offering.
entries.literal: The final offering follows the secondary offering.

entries.zh: 諸太祝各進，徹豆，還尊所。
entries.en: Each Chief Invoker advances, removes the beans, and returns to the vessel position.
entries.literal: Each Chief Invoker advances, removes the beans, and returns to the vessel position.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「賜胙。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bestow the sacrificial flesh."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bestow the sacrificial flesh."

entries.zh: 贊者曰：「眾官再拜。」
entries.en: The presenter says: "All officials bow twice."
entries.literal: The presenter says: "All officials bow twice."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: All those in position bow twice.
entries.literal: All those in position bow twice.

entries.zh: 太常卿前奏：「請再拜。」
entries.en: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please bow twice."
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices advances and announces: "Please bow twice."

entries.zh: 皇帝再拜。
entries.en: The emperor bows twice.
entries.literal: The emperor bows twice.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「眾官再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies says: "All officials bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "All officials bow twice."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: All those in position bow twice.
entries.literal: All those in position bow twice.

entries.zh: 樂一成止。
entries.en: When one movement of music is complete, it stops.
entries.literal: When one movement of music is complete, it stops.

entries.zh: 太常卿前曰：「禮畢。」
entries.en: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices advances and says: "The rite is complete."
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Sacrifices advances and says: "The rite is complete."

entries.zh: 皇帝出門，殿中監前受鎮珪。
entries.en: The emperor exits the gate; the Palace Director receives the securing tablet.
entries.literal: The emperor exits the gate; the Palace Director advances to receive the securing tablet.

entries.zh: 通事舍人、謁者、贊引各引享官、九廟子孫及從享羣官、諸方客使以次出。
entries.en: The Communications Officer, ushers, and presenters lead sacrifice officers, descendants of the nine temples, those accompanying the sacrifice, and regional envoys out in order.
entries.literal: The Communications Officer, ushers, and presenters each lead sacrifice officers, descendants of the nine temples, officials accompanying the sacrifice, and envoys from the regions to exit in order.

entries.zh: 贊引引御史、太祝以下俱復執事位。
entries.en: The presenter leads censors, Chief Invokers, and those below back to their service positions.
entries.literal: The presenter leads censors, Chief Invokers, and those below back together to their service positions.

entries.zh: 奉禮郎曰：「再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies says: "Bow twice."

entries.zh: 御史以下皆再拜以出。
entries.en: Censors and below all bow twice as they exit.
entries.literal: Censors and below all bow twice as they exit.

entries.zh: 工人、二舞以次出。
entries.en: Craftsmen and the two dances leave in order.
entries.literal: Craftsmen and the two dances exit in order.

entries.zh: 太廟令與太祝、宮闈令帥腰輿升，納神主。
entries.en: The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with Chief Invokers and the Director of the Palace Inner Gates, lead the litter up and return the spirit tablets.
entries.literal: The Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, together with Chief Invokers and the Director of the Palace Inner Gates, lead the litter up and return the spirit tablets.

entries.zh: 其祝版燔於齋坊。
entries.en: The prayer boards are burned in the purification lodge.
entries.literal: The prayer boards are burned in the purification lodge.

entries.zh: 冬至祀昊天上帝於圓丘，以高祖神堯皇帝配。
entries.en: At the winter solstice, sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Round Mound, with Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao Emperor, as associated recipient.
entries.literal: At the winter solstice, sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Round Mound, with Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao Emperor, as associated recipient.

entries.zh: 東方青帝靈威仰、南方赤帝赤熛怒、中央黃帝含樞紐、西方白帝白招拒、北方黑帝汁光紀及大明、夜明在壇之第一等。
entries.en: The Green Emperor of the East, Spiritual Might and Regard; the Red Emperor of the South, Red Blaze and Wrath; the Yellow Emperor of the Center, Holding the Pivot; the White Emperor of the West, White Summons and Rejection; the Black Emperor of the North, Juice of Light and Record; together with the Bright Luminary and Night Luminary on the altar's first tier.
entries.literal: The Green Emperor of the East, Spiritual Might and Regard; the Red Emperor of the South, Red Blaze and Wrath; the Yellow Emperor of the Center, Holding the Pivot; the White Emperor of the West, White Summons and Rejection; the Black Emperor of the North, Juice of Light and Record; together with the Bright Luminary and Night Luminary on the first tier of the altar.

entries.zh: 天皇大帝、北辰、北斗、天一、太一、紫微五帝座，並差在行位前。
entries.en: The Celestial Emperor, North Star, Big Dipper, Celestial One, Supreme One, and the Five Emperors' seats of Purple Tenuity are all placed in front of the regular rows.
entries.literal: The Celestial Emperor, North Star, Big Dipper, Celestial One, Supreme One, and the Five Emperors' seats of Purple Tenuity are all placed in front of the regular rows.

entries.zh: 餘內官諸坐及五星、十二辰、河漢四十九坐，在第二等十有二陛之間。
entries.en: The remaining inner-official seats, the Five Stars, twelve chronograms, and forty-nine seats of the River Han are on the second tier among the twelve steps.
entries.literal: The remaining inner-official seats, the Five Stars, twelve chronograms, and forty-nine seats of the River Han are on the second tier among the twelve steps.

entries.zh: 中官、市垣、帝座、七公、日星、帝席、大角、攝提、太微、五帝、太子、明堂、軒轅、三台、五車、諸王、月星、織女、建星、天紀十七座及二十八宿，差在前列。
entries.en: Central Palace, Market Enclosure, Imperial Seat, Seven Dukes, Sun Star, Imperial Couch, Great Horn, Sombre Establishment, Supreme Palace, Five Emperors, Crown Prince, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record—seventeen seats and the twenty-eight lodges—are ranked in the front row.
entries.literal: Central Palace, Market Enclosure, Imperial Seat, Seven Dukes, Sun Star, Imperial Couch, Great Horn, Sombre Establishment, Supreme Palace, Five Emperors, Crown Prince, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record—seventeen seats and the twenty-eight lodges—are ranked in the front row.

entries.zh: 其餘中官一百四十二座皆在第三等十二陛之間。
entries.en: The remaining one hundred forty-two central-official seats are all on the third tier among the twelve steps.
entries.literal: The remaining one hundred forty-two central-official seats are all on the third tier among the twelve steps.

entries.zh: 外官一百五在內壝之內，眾星三百六十在內壝之外。
entries.en: One hundred five outer officials are within the inner enclosure; three hundred sixty host stars are outside it.
entries.literal: One hundred five outer officials are within the inner enclosure; three hundred sixty host stars are outside the inner enclosure.

entries.zh: 正月上辛祈穀祀昊天上帝，以高祖神堯皇帝配，五帝在四方之陛。
entries.en: On the first xin day of the first month, at the prayer-for-grain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao Emperor, serves as associated recipient; the Five Emperors occupy the steps in the four directions.
entries.literal: On the first xin day of the first month, at the prayer-for-grain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao Emperor, serves as associated recipient; the Five Emperors occupy the steps in the four directions.

entries.zh: 孟夏雩祀昊天上帝，以太宗文武聖皇帝配，五方帝在第一等，五帝在第二等，五官在壇下之東南。
entries.en: In the first month of summer, rain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, with Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor as associated deity; the Five Directional Emperors on the first tier, the Five Emperors on the second, the Five Officials southeast below the altar.
entries.literal: In the first month of summer, rain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, with Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor as associated deity; the Five Directional Emperors on the first tier, the Five Emperors on the second, the Five Officials southeast below the altar.

entries.zh: 季秋祀昊天上帝，以睿宗大聖真皇帝配，五方帝在五室，五帝各在其左，五官在庭，各依其方。
entries.en: In the last month of autumn, sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, with Ruizong the Great Sagely True Emperor as associated deity; the Five Directional Emperors in the five chambers, each Five Emperor to his left, the Five Officials in the courtyard each according to his direction.
entries.literal: In the last month of autumn, sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven, with Ruizong the Great Sagely True Emperor as associated deity; the Five Directional Emperors in the five chambers, each Five Emperor to his left, the Five Officials in the courtyard each according to his direction.

entries.zh: 立春祀青帝，以太皥氏配，歲星、三辰在壇下之東北，七宿在西北，句芒在東南。
entries.en: At the beginning of spring, sacrifice to the Green Emperor, with the Great Bright One as associated deity; the Year Star and three chronograms below the altar in the northeast, seven lodges in the northwest, Goumang in the southeast.
entries.literal: At the beginning of spring, sacrifice to the Green Emperor, with the Great Bright One as associated deity; the Year Star and three chronograms below the altar in the northeast, seven lodges in the northwest, Goumang in the southeast.

entries.zh: 立夏祀赤帝，以神農氏配，熒惑、三辰、七宿、祝融氏之位如青帝。
entries.en: At the beginning of summer, sacrifice to the Red Emperor, with the Divine Farmer as associated deity; Sparkling Deluder, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Zhurong are positioned as for the Green Emperor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of summer, sacrifice to the Red Emperor, with the Divine Farmer as associated deity; the positions of Sparkling Deluder, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Zhurong are as for the Green Emperor.

entries.zh: 季夏土王之日祀黃帝，以軒轅氏配，鎮星、后土氏之位如赤帝。
entries.en: On the day when Earth is king in late summer, sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, with Xuanyuan as associated deity; the Queller Star and Queen Earth are positioned as for the Red Emperor.
entries.literal: On the day when Earth is king in the last month of summer, sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, with Xuanyuan as associated deity; the positions of the Queller Star and Queen Earth are as for the Red Emperor.

entries.zh: 立秋祀白帝，以少昊氏配，太白、三辰、七宿、蓐收之位如赤帝。
entries.en: At the beginning of autumn, sacrifice to the White Emperor, with the Lesser Bright One as associated deity; Great White, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Rushou are positioned as for the Red Emperor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of autumn, sacrifice to the White Emperor, with the Lesser Bright One as associated deity; Great White, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Rushou are as for the Red Emperor.

entries.zh: 立冬祀黑帝，以顓頊氏配，辰星、三辰、七宿、玄冥氏之位如白帝。
entries.en: At the beginning of winter, sacrifice to the Black Emperor, with Zhuanxu as associated deity; Chronogram Star, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Dark Ming are positioned as for the White Emperor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of winter, sacrifice to the Black Emperor, with Zhuanxu as associated deity; Chronogram Star, three chronograms, seven lodges, and Dark Ming are as for the White Emperor.

entries.zh: 蜡祭百神，大明、夜明在壇上，神農、伊耆各在其壇上，后稷在壇東，五官、田畯各在其方，五星、十二次、二十八宿、五方之岳鎮、海瀆、山林、川澤、丘陵、墳衍、原隰、井泉各在其方之壇，龍、麟、朱鳥、騶虞、玄武、鱗、羽、臝、毛、介、水墉、坊、郵表畷、於菟、貓各在其方壇之後。
entries.en: At the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits, the Bright Luminary and Night Luminary are on the altar; the Divine Farmer and Yiyi each on his altar; Houji east of the altar; the Five Officials and field directors each in his direction; the Five Stars, twelve chronograms, twenty-eight lodges, directional mountains and garrisons, seas and rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, wetlands, and wells and springs each on altars in his direction; dragon, unicorn, vermilion bird, zouyu, dark warrior, scaled, feathered, naked, furred, shelled, water embankments, wards, postal markers, watch huts, yutu (tiger), and cat each behind altars in his direction.
entries.literal: At the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits, the Bright Luminary and Night Luminary are on the altar; the Divine Farmer and Yiyi each on his altar; Houji east of the altar; the Five Officials and field directors each in his direction; the Five Stars, twelve chronograms, twenty-eight lodges, directional mountains and garrisons, seas and rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, wetlands, wells and springs each on altars in his direction; dragon, unicorn, vermilion bird, zouyu, dark warrior, scaled, feathered, naked, furred, shelled, water embankments, wards, postal markers, watch huts, yutu (tiger), and cat each behind altars in his direction.

entries.zh: 夏至祭皇地祇，以高祖配，五方之岳鎮、海瀆、原隰、丘陵、墳衍在內壝之內，各居其方，而中岳以下在西南。
entries.en: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to the August Earth Lord, with the High Ancestor as associated deity; directional mountains and garrisons, seas and rivers, plains, wetlands, hills, mounds, and plains and marshes are within the inner enclosure each in his direction, while below the central mountain they are in the southwest.
entries.literal: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to the August Earth Lord, with the High Ancestor as associated deity; directional mountains and garrisons, seas and rivers, plains, wetlands, hills, mounds, and plains and marshes are within the inner enclosure, each in his direction, while below the central mountain they are in the southwest.

entries.zh: 孟冬祭神州地祇，以太宗配。
entries.en: In the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Realm, with Taizong as associated deity.
entries.literal: In the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Spirit Land of the Realm, with Taizong as associated deity.

entries.zh: 社以后土，稷以后稷配。
entries.en: The altar of soil is associated with Queen Earth; the altar of grain with Houji.
entries.literal: The altar of soil with Queen Earth; the altar of grain with Houji as associated deity.

entries.zh: 吉亥祭神農，以后稷配，而朝日、夕月無配。
entries.en: On the auspicious hai day, sacrifice to the Divine Farmer, with Houji as associated deity; the morning sun and evening moon have no associated deity.
entries.literal: On the auspicious hai day, sacrifice to the Divine Farmer, with Houji as associated deity; the morning sun and evening moon have no associated deity.

entries.zh: 席，尊者以槀秸，卑者以莞。
entries.en: For seating, the honored use straw mats; the humble use sedge.
entries.literal: For seating, the honored use straw mats; the humble use sedge.

entries.zh: 此神位之序也。
entries.en: This is how spirit positions are ordered.
entries.literal: This is the order of spirit positions.

entries.zh: 皇帝元正、冬至受群臣朝賀而會
entries.en: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice the emperor receives the ministers' congratulations and holds a court feast.
entries.literal: The emperor on New Year's Day and the winter solstice receives the court's congratulatory audience and holds a feast.

entries.zh: 皇帝元正、冬至受群臣朝賀而會。
entries.en: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice the emperor receives the ministers' congratulations and holds a court feast.
entries.literal: The emperor on New Year's Day and the winter solstice receives the court's congratulatory audience and holds a feast.

entries.zh: 其日，將士填諸街，勒所部列黃麾大仗屯門及陳於殿庭，群官就次。
entries.en: That day troops lined the streets; commanders formed their detachments, posted yellow-banner great halberds at gates and in the hall court, and officials took station.
entries.literal: On that day soldiers filled the streets; commanders arrayed their units, posted yellow-banner great halberds at the gates and in the hall court, and officials took their ranks.

entries.zh: 侍中版奏「請中嚴」。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant submitted on the board: "Request inner vigilance."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "Request inner vigilance."

entries.zh: 諸侍衛之官詣閣奉迎，吏部兵部主客戶部贊群官、客使俱出次，通事舍人各引就朝堂前位，引四品以下及諸親、客等應先置者入就位。
entries.en: Guard officers went to the pavilion to receive the emperor; Personnel, War, Receptions, and Revenue directors ushered officials and envoys from their stations; Protocol Aides led each group to the audience-hall positions and brought in fourth rank and below, kin, guests, and others who were to enter first.
entries.literal: Guards went to the pavilion to welcome; the Ministries of Personnel, War, Receptions, and Revenue ushered officials and envoys from their ranks; Protocol Aides each led them to positions before the audience hall, and led fourth rank and below, kinsmen, guests, and others who should enter first to their places.

entries.zh: 侍中版奏「外辦」。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant reported on the board: "Outer preparations complete."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized on the board: "The outer rites are ready."

entries.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，冬至則服通天冠、絳紗袍，御輿出自西房，即御座南向坐。
entries.en: The emperor wore full ceremonial dress; on the winter solstice he wore the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, came out from the west chamber by imperial carriage, and took the throne facing south.
entries.literal: The emperor wore the coronation robe and cap; on the winter solstice he wore the open-heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, rode the imperial carriage out from the western chamber, and took the throne facing south.

entries.zh: 符寶郎奉寶置於前，公、王以下及諸客使等以次入就位。
entries.en: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer set the seals before him; dukes, princes, and below, with all envoys and guests, entered in sequence to their stations.
entries.literal: The Talisman-and-Seal Officer presented the seals before him; dukes, princes, and below and all envoys and guests entered in order to their places.

entries.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice."

entries.zh: 贊者承傳，在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: The announcers passed the word; all present bowed twice.
entries.literal: The announcers relayed it; all in attendance bowed twice.

entries.zh: 上公一人詣西階席，脫舄，跪，解劍置於席，升，當御座前，北面跪賀，稱：「某官臣某言：元正首祚，景福惟新，伏惟開元神武皇帝陛下與天同休。」
entries.en: A senior duke went to the western-step mat, removed his shoes, knelt, laid his sword on the mat, ascended, and knelt north of the throne to congratulate the emperor: "Official So-and-so, your servant So-and-so, says: At the year's first fortune, blessings renew; may Your Majesty the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor share Heaven's repose."
entries.literal: One senior duke went to the mat on the western steps, removed his shoes, knelt, removed his sword and set it on the mat, ascended, and before the throne knelt northward to offer congratulations, saying: "Such-and-such an official, your servant So-and-so, says: On the first day of the year, the year's fortune begins anew; may Your Majesty the Kaiyuan Divine Martial Emperor enjoy the same repose as Heaven."

entries.zh: 冬至云：「天正長至，伏惟陛下如日之升。」
entries.en: On the winter solstice he said: "The celestial new year has reached its height; may Your Majesty ascend like the sun."
entries.literal: On the winter solstice he said: "The celestial first day reaches its fullness; may Your Majesty rise like the sun."

entries.zh: 乃降階詣席，跪，佩劍，俯伏，興，納舄，復位。
entries.en: He then went down to the mat, knelt, girded his sword, prostrated, rose, put on his shoes, and returned to station.
entries.literal: He then descended the steps to the mat, knelt, girded his sword, prostrated himself, rose, put on his shoes, and returned to his place.

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: All present bowed twice.
entries.literal: All in attendance bowed twice.

entries.zh: 侍中前承詔，降，詣群官東北，西面，稱「有制」。
entries.en: The Palace Attendant advanced to take the edict, went down to the officials' northeast, faced west, and announced: "By edict."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, descended, went to the northeast of the officials, faced west, and said "There is an edict."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜。
entries.en: All present bowed twice.
entries.literal: All in attendance bowed twice.

entries.zh: 宣制曰：「履新之慶，與公等同之。」
entries.en: The edict read: "The joy of the new year—share it equally with you."
entries.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "The joy of treading the new—share it with you all alike."

entries.zh: 冬至云：「履長。」
entries.en: On the winter solstice it read: "Treading the year's height."
entries.literal: On the winter solstice it said: "Treading the fullness."

entries.zh: 在位者皆再拜，舞蹈，三稱萬歲，又再拜。
entries.en: All present bowed twice, danced, shouted "Long live the emperor" three times, and bowed twice again.
entries.literal: All in attendance bowed twice, performed the dance, thrice shouted "Ten thousand years," and bowed twice again.

entries.zh: 初，侍中已宣制，朝集使及蕃客皆再拜。
entries.en: After the Palace Attendant had proclaimed the edict, assembly envoys and foreign guests bowed twice.
entries.literal: Earlier, after the Palace Attendant had proclaimed the edict, assembly envoys and foreign guests all bowed twice.

entries.zh: 戶部尚書進詣階間跪奏，稱：「戶部尚書臣某言：諸州貢物請付所司。」
entries.en: The Revenue Minister advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Revenue Minister, your servant So-and-so, requests that provincial tribute be delivered to the proper offices."
entries.literal: The Minister of Revenue advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "The Minister of Revenue, your servant So-and-so, says: The provincial tribute—may it be handed to the relevant offices."

entries.zh: 侍中前承制，退，稱：「制曰可。」
entries.en: The Palace Attendant took the edict, withdrew, and announced: "The edict says: Approved."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, withdrew, and said: "The edict says: Approved."

entries.zh: 禮部尚書以次進詣階間，跪奏，稱「禮部尚書臣某言：諸蕃貢物請付所司。」
entries.en: The Rites Minister advanced in turn to the steps, knelt, and said: "Rites Minister, your servant So-and-so, requests that foreign tribute be delivered to the proper offices."
entries.literal: The Minister of Rites next advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "The Minister of Rites, your servant So-and-so, says: The foreign tribute—may it be handed to the relevant offices."

entries.zh: 侍中前承制，退，稱：「制曰可。」
entries.en: The Palace Attendant took the edict, withdrew, and announced: "The edict says: Approved."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant came forward to receive the edict, withdrew, and said: "The edict says: Approved."

entries.zh: 太府帥其屬受諸州及諸蕃貢物出歸仁、納義門，執物者隨之。
entries.en: The Grand Storehouse led its staff to take provincial and foreign tribute out through the Guiren and Nayi Gates, carriers following.
entries.literal: The Grand Storehouse led its subordinates to receive the provincial and foreign tribute and exit through the Guiren and Nayi Gates; those carrying items followed.

entries.zh: 典儀曰：「再拜。」
entries.en: The Master of Ceremonies called: "Bow twice."
entries.literal: The Master of Ceremonies said: "Bow twice."

entries.zh: 通事舍人以次引北面位者出。
entries.en: Protocol Aides led out those in north-facing stations in sequence.
entries.literal: Protocol Aides led out those in north-facing positions in order.

entries.zh: 侍中前，跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言：禮畢。」
entries.en: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and reported: "Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete."
entries.literal: The Palace Attendant advanced, knelt, and memorialized: "The Palace Attendant, your servant So-and-so, says: The rites are complete."

entries.zh: 皇帝降座，御輿入自東房，侍臣從至閤。
entries.en: The emperor left the throne; the imperial carriage returned through the east chamber, with the attendant ministers following as far as the side chamber.
entries.literal: The emperor left the throne; the imperial carriage entered from the eastern chamber; attendant ministers followed as far as the side chamber.

entries.zh: 引東、西面位者以次出，蕃客先出。
entries.en: East- and west-facing groups were led out in order; foreign guests left first.
entries.literal: Those in east- and west-facing positions were led out in order; foreign guests exited first.

entries.zh: 前一日，尚舍設禦幄於太極殿，有司設群官客使等次於東西朝堂，展縣，置桉，陳車輿，又設解劍席於縣西北橫街之南。
entries.en: The day before, the Imperial Household Service erected the imperial enclosure in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; officials arranged seating in the east and west audience halls, hung bells, set tables, lined up carriages, and placed sword-removal mats south of the transverse street northwest of the bell frame.
entries.literal: On the previous day the Imperial Household Service set the imperial canopy in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; the relevant offices set ranks for officials, envoys, and guests in the eastern and western audience halls, suspended the bells, set tables, arrayed carriages, and also set sword-removal mats south of the transverse street northwest of the bells.

entries.zh: 文官三品以上位於橫街之南，道東；
entries.en: Third-rank civil officials and above stood south of the transverse street, east of the lane;
entries.literal: Civil officials of the third rank and above stood south of the transverse street, east of the roadway;

entries.zh: 褒聖侯位於三品之下，介公、酅公位於道西；
entries.en: the Marquis Who Honors the Sage stood below third rank; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi stood west of the lane;
entries.literal: the Marquis Who Honors the Sage stood below the third rank; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi stood west of the roadway;

entries.zh: 武官三品以上位於介公之西，少南；
entries.en: third-rank military officials and above stood west of the Duke of Jie, slightly south;
entries.literal: military officials of the third rank and above stood west of the Duke of Jie, slightly to the south;

entries.zh: 文官四品、五品位於縣東，六品以下位於橫街之南。
entries.en: fourth- and fifth-rank civil officials stood east of the bells; sixth rank and below stood south of the transverse street.
entries.literal: civil officials of the fourth and fifth ranks stood east of the bells; those of the sixth rank and below stood south of the transverse street.

entries.zh: 又設諸州朝集使位：都督、刺史三品以上位於文、武官三品之東、西，四品以下分方位于文、武官當品之下。
entries.en: Provincial assembly envoys were placed likewise: third-rank governors and prefects flanked the third-rank civil and military lines; fourth rank and below were arrayed by region under peers of their grade.
entries.literal: Ranks were also set for provincial assembly envoys: governors and prefects of the third rank and above stood east and west of the third-rank civil and military officials; those of the fourth rank and below were placed by direction below officials of the corresponding rank.

entries.zh: 諸州使人又於朝集使之下，諸親於四品、五品之南。
entries.en: Provincial delegates stood below the assembly envoys; imperial relatives south of the fourth- and fifth-rank ranks.
entries.literal: Provincial envoys stood again below the assembly envoys; imperial kinsmen stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank officials.

entries.zh: 設諸蕃方客位：三等以上，東方、南方在東方朝集使之東，西方、北方在西方朝集使之西，每國異位重行，北面；
entries.en: Foreign guests were placed by grade: third rank and above from the east and south stood east of the eastern envoys, those from the west and north west of the western envoys, each state in its own row facing north;
entries.literal: Ranks for foreign guests were set: those of the third grade and above—eastern and southern realms east of the eastern assembly envoys, western and northern realms west of the western assembly envoys, each state in a separate row facing north;

entries.zh: 四等以下，分方位於朝集使六品之下。
entries.en: fourth rank and below were positioned by region below sixth-rank assembly envoys.
entries.literal: those of the fourth grade and below were placed by direction below the sixth-rank assembly envoys.

entries.zh: 又設門外位：文官于東朝堂，介公、酅公在西朝堂之前，武官在介公之南，少退，每等異位重行；
entries.en: Outside the gate, civil officials stood in the eastern hall; the Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi before the western hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly back, each grade in its own row;
entries.literal: Ranks outside the gate were also set: civil officials in the eastern audience hall; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi before the western audience hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly withdrawn, each grade in a separate row;

entries.zh: 諸親位於文、武官四品、五品之南；
entries.en: imperial kin stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank civil and military lines;
entries.literal: imperial kinsmen stood south of the fourth- and fifth-rank civil and military officials;

entries.zh: 諸州朝集使，東方、南方在宗親之南，使人分方於朝集使之下；
entries.en: eastern and southern assembly envoys stood south of the clansmen, with provincial delegates below them by region;
entries.literal: provincial assembly envoys from the east and south stood south of the imperial clansmen, envoys placed by direction below the assembly envoys;

entries.zh: 諸方客，東方、南方在東方朝集使之南，西方、北方在西方朝集使之南，每國異位重行。
entries.en: eastern and southern guests stood south of the eastern envoys, western and northern guests south of the western envoys, each state in its own row.
entries.literal: foreign guests from the east and south stood south of the eastern assembly envoys, those from the west and north south of the western assembly envoys, each state in a separate row.

entries.zh: 嘉禮三
entries.en: Auspicious Rites III
entries.literal: Auspicious Rites Three

entries.zh: 記曰：「功成作樂。」
entries.en: The Record states: "When achievement is complete, music is composed."
entries.literal: The Record says: "When merit is accomplished, music is made."

entries.zh: 蓋王者未作樂之時，必因其舊而用之。
entries.en: Before a sovereign fashions new music, he necessarily continues the former repertoire.
entries.literal: For before a king has made music he must use the old and employ it.

entries.zh: 唐興即用隋樂。
entries.en: Tang at its founding adopted Sui music outright.
entries.literal: When Tang rose it at once used Sui music.

entries.zh: 武德九年，始詔太常少卿祖孝孫、協律郎竇璡等定樂。
entries.en: In Wude year 9 the throne ordered Vice Director Zu Xiaosun, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Dou Jin, and colleagues to standardize the music.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Wude an edict first ordered Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Dou Jin, and others to fix the music.

entries.zh: 初，隋用黃鍾一宮，惟擊七鍾，其五鍾設而不擊，謂之啞鍾。
entries.en: Initially Sui kept to Yellow Bell palace mode and struck only seven bells; five bells stood silent—"mute bells."
entries.literal: At first Sui used the Yellow Bell palace mode alone, striking only seven bells; five bells were set up but not struck, called mute bells.

entries.zh: 唐協律郎張文收乃依古斷竹為十二律，高祖命與孝孫吹調五鍾，叩之而應，由是十二鍾皆用。
entries.en: Zhang Wenshou, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman, cut bamboo into twelve pipes by ancient rule; Gaozu had him and Xiaosun tune the five mute bells—they answered when struck, and all twelve bells came into use.
entries.literal: Tang's Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Zhang Wenshou then followed the ancient method of cutting bamboo for twelve pitch pipes; Gaozu ordered him with Xiaosun to blow and tune the five bells; struck, they responded, and thereafter all twelve bells were used.

entries.zh: 孝孫又以十二月旋相為六十聲、八十四調。
entries.en: Xiaosun further derived sixty sounds and eighty-four modes by cyclically permuting the twelve months.
entries.literal: Xiaosun further took the twelve months in rotating succession to make sixty sounds and eighty-four modes.

entries.zh: 其法，因五音生二變，因變徵為正徵，因變宮為清宮。
entries.en: The method generated two "altered" tones from the five; altered zhi became proper zhi, altered gong became clear gong.
entries.literal: The method: from the five tones generate two alterations; from altered zhi derive proper zhi, from altered gong derive clear gong.

entries.zh: 七音起黃鍾，終南呂，迭為綱紀。
entries.en: Seven tones ran from Yellow Bell to Nanlü, alternating as structural threads.
entries.literal: The seven tones begin at Yellow Bell and end at Nanlü, each in turn the warp and woof.

entries.zh: 黃鍾之律，管長九寸，王於中宮土。
entries.en: The Yellow Bell pipe measures nine cun and rules as earth at the central palace.
entries.literal: The Yellow Bell pipe is nine cun long and reigns as central palace earth.

entries.zh: 半之，四寸五分，與清宮合，五音之首也。
entries.en: Halved to four cun five fen, it aligns with clear gong—the leading tone of the five.
entries.literal: Halved, four cun five fen, it matches clear gong—the head of the five tones.

entries.zh: 加以二變，循環無間。
entries.en: With the two alterations added, the cycle closes without break.
entries.literal: Adding the two alterations, the cycle is without gap.

entries.zh: 故一宮、二商、三角、四變徵、五徵、六羽、七變宮，其聲繇濁至清為一均。
entries.en: Thus: gong, shang, jue, altered zhi, zhi, yu, altered gong—pitch ascending from muddy to clear within one jun.
entries.literal: Thus one gong, two shang, three jue, four altered zhi, five zhi, six yu, seven altered gong—from muddy to clear sound forms one jun.

entries.zh: 凡十二宮調，皆正宮也。
entries.en: All twelve gong modes count as proper gong.
entries.literal: All twelve gong modes are proper gong modes.

entries.zh: 正宮聲之下，無復濁音，故五音以宮為尊。
entries.en: Proper gong admits no tone below it in pitch; hence gong ranks first among the five.
entries.literal: Below the proper gong tone there is no further muddy sound; therefore among the five tones gong is honored.

entries.zh: 十二商調，調有下聲一，謂宮也。
entries.en: Each of the twelve shang modes carries one underpinning tone—gong.
entries.literal: The twelve shang modes each have one lower tone, called gong.

entries.zh: 十二角調，調有下聲二，宮、商也。
entries.en: Each jue mode carries two underpinning tones—gong and shang.
entries.literal: The twelve jue modes each have two lower tones, gong and shang.

entries.zh: 十二徵調，調有下聲三，宮、商、角也。
entries.en: Each zhi mode carries three underpinning tones—gong, shang, and jue.
entries.literal: The twelve zhi modes each have three lower tones, gong, shang, and jue.

entries.zh: 十二羽調，調有下聲四，宮、商、角、徵也。
entries.en: Each yu mode carries four underpinning tones—gong through zhi.
entries.literal: The twelve yu modes each have four lower tones, gong, shang, jue, and zhi.

entries.zh: 十二變徵調，居角音之後，正徵之前。
entries.en: Twelve altered-zhi modes sit after jue and before proper zhi.
entries.literal: The twelve altered-zhi modes stand after jue and before proper zhi.

entries.zh: 十二變宮調，在羽音之後，清宮之前。
entries.en: Twelve altered-gong modes sit after yu and before clear gong.
entries.literal: The twelve altered-gong modes stand after yu and before clear gong.

entries.zh: 雅樂成調，無出七聲，本宮遞相用。
entries.en: Court music forms its modes within seven tones, the home gong passing from one to the next.
entries.literal: Elegant music in forming modes does not exceed seven tones; the root gong is used in succession.

entries.zh: 唯樂章則隨律定均，合以笙、磬，節以鍾、鼓。
entries.en: For actual pieces the jun follows the pipes, joined with mouth-organ and stone chimes, paced by bells and drums.
entries.literal: Only for musical sections are jun fixed according to the pipes, joined with sheng and qing, regulated by bells and drums.

entries.zh: 樂既成，奏之。
entries.en: Once the music stood complete, it was performed.
entries.literal: When the music was complete, it was performed.

entries.zh: 文收既定樂，復鑄銅律三百六十、銅斛二、銅秤二、銅甌十四、秤尺一。
entries.en: Once Wenshou had settled the music, he cast three hundred sixty copper pitch pipes, two copper hu, two steelyards, fourteen copper ou, and one measuring rod for the steelyard.
entries.literal: After Wenshou had fixed the music, he further cast three hundred sixty copper pitch pipes, two copper hu, two copper steelyards, fourteen copper ou, and one steelyard-measure rod.

entries.zh: 斛左右耳與臀皆方，積十而登，以至於斛，與古玉尺、玉斗同。
entries.en: The hu's ears and base were square; capacities stacked by tens to the hu, matching ancient jade measure and dipper.
entries.literal: The hu's left and right ears and base were all square; tenfold accumulation ascended to the hu, matching the ancient jade foot-rule and jade dipper.

entries.zh: 皆藏於太樂署。
entries.en: All were kept in the Office of Great Music.
entries.literal: All were stored in the Office of Great Music.

entries.zh: 武后時，太常卿武延秀以為奇玩，乃獻之。
entries.en: Under Empress Wu, Director Wu Yanxiu treated them as marvels and presented them to the throne.
entries.literal: In Empress Wu's time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Yanxiu took them for curios and presented them.

entries.zh: 及將考中宗廟樂，有司奏請出之，而秤尺已亡，其跡猶存，以常用度量校之，尺當六之五，量、衡皆三之一。
entries.en: For Zhongzong's temple music the offices requested them; the measuring rod was gone though its marks remained—against present measures the foot was five-sixths, capacity and weight one-third each.
entries.literal: When they were to examine Zhongzong's temple music the authorities memorialized to bring them out, but the steelyard rod was already lost; its traces remained; comparing with current measures, the foot was five-sixths, capacity and weight each one-third.

entries.zh: 至肅宗時，山東人魏延陵得律一，因中官李輔國獻之，云：「太常諸樂調皆下，不合黃鍾，請悉更制諸鍾磬。」
entries.en: Under Suzong, Wei Yanling of Shandong found a pipe and presented it through Li Fuguo, claiming: "Court tunes all ran low against Yellow Bell and all bells and stones should be remade."
entries.literal: By Suzong's time Shandong man Wei Yanling obtained one pitch pipe and through eunuch Li Fuguo presented it, saying: "All tunes of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are too low and do not match Yellow Bell; please entirely remake all bells and chime-stones."

entries.zh: 帝以為然，乃悉取太常諸樂器入于禁中，更加磨剡，凡二十五日而成。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, brought every Court instrument within the palace, filed and polished them, and finished in twenty-five days.
entries.literal: The emperor thought it right and took all Court instruments into the inner palace, further grinding and filing them; in twenty-five days it was done.

entries.zh: 御三殿觀之，以還太常，然以漢律考之，黃鍾乃太簇也，當時議者以為非是。
entries.en: He inspected them in the Three Halls and returned them; tested against Han standards, Yellow Bell matched Taicu—critics deemed this mistaken.
entries.literal: He viewed them in the Three Halls and returned them to the Court; yet tested against Han pipes, Yellow Bell proved to be Taicu; contemporaries held this wrong.

entries.zh: 唐為國而作樂之制尤簡，高祖、太宗即用隋樂與孝孫、文收所定而已。
entries.en: Tang's state-music regulations were notably spare: Gaozu and Taizong kept Sui music plus Xiaosun's and Wenshou's revisions.
entries.literal: Tang's system for making state music was especially simple: Gaozu and Taizong used only Sui music and what Xiaosun and Wenshou had fixed.

entries.zh: 其後世所更者，樂章舞曲。
entries.en: Later changes touched chiefly lyrics and dances.
entries.literal: What later ages changed were musical sections and dance pieces.

entries.zh: 至于昭宗，始得盈孫焉，故其議論罕所發明。
entries.en: Not until Zhaozong and Yin Yingsun did theory find voice again; earlier discourse seldom innovated.
entries.literal: Only by Zhaozong did Yin Yingsun appear; hence their discussions rarely advanced new doctrine.

entries.zh: 若其樂歌廟舞，用於當世者，可以考也。
entries.en: Their temple hymns, dances, and contemporary usage can still be traced.
entries.literal: As for their hymns, temple dances, and what was used in their own time, these may be examined.

entries.zh: 初，太宗時，詔祕書監顏師古等撰定弘農府君至高祖太武皇帝六廟樂曲舞名，其後變更不一，而自獻祖而下廟舞，略可見也。
entries.en: Taizong ordered Yan Shigu and others to name dances for six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; later names shifted, but from Offered Ancestor downward the temple dances can be traced.
entries.literal: At first in Taizong's time an edict ordered Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others to compile dance names for the six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; afterward changes were many, yet from Offered Ancestor down the temple dances can be seen in outline.

entries.zh: 獻祖曰光大之舞，懿祖曰長發之舞，太祖曰大政之舞，世祖曰大成之舞，高祖曰大明之舞，太宗曰崇德之舞，高宗曰鈞天之舞，中宗曰太和之舞，睿宗曰景雲之舞，玄宗曰大運之舞，肅宗曰惟新之舞，代宗曰保大之舞，德宗曰文明之舞，順宗曰大順之舞，憲宗曰象德之舞，穆宗曰和寧之舞，敬宗曰大鈞之舞，文宗曰文成之舞，武宗曰大定之舞，昭宗曰咸寧之舞。
entries.en: Offered Ancestor: Guangda; Respected Ancestor: Changfa; Great Ancestor: Dazheng; World Ancestor: Dacheng; High Ancestor: Daming; Taizong: Chongde; Gaozong: Juntian; Zhongzong: Taihe; Ruizong: Jingyun; Xuanzong: Dayun; Suzong: Weixin; Daizong: Baoda; Dezong: Wenming; Shunzong: Dashun; Xianzong: Xiangde; Muzong: Hening; Jingzong: Dajun; Wenzong: Wencheng; Wuzong: Dading; Zhaozong: Xianning.
entries.literal: Offered Ancestor: Guangda; Respected Ancestor: Changfa; Great Ancestor: Dazheng; World Ancestor: Dacheng; High Ancestor: Daming; Taizong: Chongde; Gaozong: Juntian; Zhongzong: Taihe; Ruizong: Jingyun; Xuanzong: Dayun; Suzong: Weixin; Daizong: Baoda; Dezong: Wenming; Shunzong: Dashun; Xianzong: Xiangde; Muzong: Hening; Jingzong: Dajun; Wenzong: Wencheng; Wuzong: Dading; Zhaozong: Xianning.

entries.zh: 其餘闕而不著。
entries.en: Others are lost from the record.
entries.literal: The rest are missing and not recorded.

entries.zh: 燕樂。
entries.en: Banquet music (yan yue).
entries.literal: Banquet music.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，仍隋制設九部樂：燕樂伎，樂工舞人無變者。
entries.en: Gaozu kept Sui's Nine Department Music; Yan Music performers unchanged.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he still followed Sui in establishing the Nine Department Music: Yan Music performers, musicians and dancers unchanged.

entries.zh: 清商伎者，隋清樂也。
entries.en: Pure Shang was Sui court music.
entries.literal: Pure Shang performers were Sui's pure music.

entries.zh: 有編鍾、編磬、獨絃琴、擊琴、瑟、秦琵琶、臥箜篌、筑、箏、節鼓，皆一；
entries.en: One each: serial bells and chimes, solo-string qin, struck qin, se, Qin pipa, horizontal konghou, zhu, zheng, marking drum.
entries.literal: Serial bells, serial chimes, solo-string qin, struck qin, se, Qin pipa, horizontal konghou, zhu, zheng, marking drum—each one.

entries.zh: 笙、笛、簫、篪、方響、跋膝，皆二。
entries.en: Two each: sheng, di, xiao, chi, fangxiang, baxi.
entries.literal: Sheng, di, xiao, chi, fangxiang, baxi—each two.

entries.zh: 歌二人，吹葉一人，舞者四人，幷習巴渝舞。
entries.en: Two singers, one leaf-blower, four dancers—all trained in Ba-Yu dance.
entries.literal: Two singers, one leaf-blower, four dancers, all practicing Ba-Yu dance.

entries.zh: 西涼伎，有編鍾、編磬，皆一；
entries.en: Western Liang: one each serial bells and chimes.
entries.literal: Western Liang performers: serial bells and chimes each one.

entries.zh: 彈箏、搊箏、臥箜篌、豎箜篌、琵琶、五絃、笙、簫、觱篥、小觱篥、笛、橫笛、腰鼓、齊鼓、檐鼓，皆一；
entries.en: One each: plucked and strummed zheng, konghou, pipa, five-string, sheng, xiao, bili large and small, di, transverse di, waist, Qi, and eaves drums.
