entries.literal: Annual revenue empire-wide: zu cash over two million strings, grain over nineteen million eight hundred thousand hu, yong and diao silk over seven million four hundred thousand bolts, cotton over one million eight hundred thousand tun, cloth over ten million thirty-five thousand duan.

entries.zh: 天子驕於佚樂而用不知節，大抵用物之數，常過其所入。
entries.en: The emperor indulged in luxury and spent without restraint; expenditures routinely exceeded revenue.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven grew proud in ease and pleasure and did not restrain spending; generally what was used exceeded what came in.

entries.zh: 於是錢谷之臣，始事朘刻。
entries.en: Revenue officials then turned to squeezing the people.
entries.literal: Then ministers of revenue began to practice exaction.

entries.zh: 太府卿楊崇禮句剝分銖，有欠折漬損者，州縣督送，歷年不止。
entries.en: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli wrung out every penny; counties were hounded year after year for shortages and spoilage.
entries.literal: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli parsed and stripped every fen and zhu; for shortages, spoilage, or damage, prefectures and counties were pressed to deliver, year after year without end.

entries.zh: 其子慎矜專知太府，次子慎名知京倉，亦以苛刻結主恩。
entries.en: His son Shenjin ran the Grand Treasury and Shenming the capital granaries; both curried favor through harsh exaction.
entries.literal: His son Shenjin managed the Grand Treasury; his second son Shenming managed the capital granaries; both also won favor through harshness.

entries.zh: 王鉷為戶口色役使，歲進錢百億萬緡，非租庸正額者，積百寶大盈庫，以供天子燕私。
entries.en: Wang Hong as household levy commissioner presented ten billion strings yearly; extralegal revenue filled the Great Abundance Vault for the emperor's private use.
entries.literal: Wang Hong as Commissioner for Households and Miscellaneous Levies yearly presented ten billion strings; sums outside regular zu-yong quotas were stored in the Hundred Treasures Great Abundance Vault for the Son of Heaven's private pleasures.

entries.zh: 及安祿山反，司空楊國忠以為正庫物不可以給士，遣侍御史崔眾至太原納錢度僧尼道士，旬日得百萬緡而已。
entries.en: When An Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong, finding the regular treasury inadequate for troops, sent Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to sell ordinations—and raised only a million strings in ten days.
entries.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong held that regular vault goods could not pay the troops; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to collect cash by ordaining monks and Daoist priests, gaining only a million strings in ten days.

entries.zh: 自兩京陷沒，民物耗弊，天下蕭然。
entries.en: After both capitals fell, people and wealth were ruined and the empire lay in ruin.
entries.literal: From the fall of the two capitals, people and goods were exhausted; the realm was desolate.

entries.zh: 十六年，乃詔每三歲以九等定籍。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, the court ordered household registers revised by nine grades every three years.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict ordered household registers fixed by nine grades every three years.

entries.zh: 而庸調折租所取華好，州縣長宮勸織，中書門下察濫惡以貶官吏，精者褒賞之。
entries.en: Yong, diao, and grain substitutes had to be of fine quality; local chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat punished officials for shoddy goods and rewarded excellence.
entries.literal: Yong and diao and grain-tax substitutes were required in fine quality; prefectural and county chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat inspected shoddy goods to demote officials and rewarded the finest.

entries.zh: 二十二年，詔男十五、女十三以上得嫁娶。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 22, males of fifteen and females of thirteen were permitted to marry.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict allowed males fifteen and females thirteen and above to marry.

entries.zh: 州縣歲上戶口登耗，采訪使覆實之，刺史、縣令以為課最。
entries.en: Each year counties reported household growth; investigating commissioners verified the figures; governors and magistrates were rated on the results.
entries.literal: Prefectures and counties yearly reported household increases and decreases; investigating commissioners verified them; governors and magistrates were judged by this in performance reviews.

entries.zh: 凡庸、調、租、資課，皆任土所宜，州縣長官涖定粗良，具上中下三物之樣輸京都。
entries.en: Yong, diao, zu, and resource levies followed local products; local chiefs set quality grades and sent upper, middle, and lower samples to the capital.
entries.literal: All yong, diao, zu, and resource levies followed local products; prefectural and county chiefs set coarse and fine grades and sent samples of upper, middle, and lower goods to the capital.

entries.zh: 有濫惡，督中物之直。
entries.en: Shoddy goods were priced at the middle grade.
entries.literal: If goods were shoddy, the middle grade's price was enforced.

entries.zh: 二十五年，以江、淮輸運有河、洛之艱，而關中蠶桑少，菽粟常賤，乃命庸、調、資課皆以米，兇年樂輸布絹者亦從之。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 25, because Jiang-Huai grain faced transport bottlenecks at the Yellow and Luo while Guanzhong lacked silk and grain was cheap, yong, diao, and resource levies were paid in rice; in famine years cloth and silk were accepted.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because Jiang-Huai transport faced difficulties at the Yellow and Luo rivers, while Guanzhong had little sericulture and beans and grain were cheap, yong, diao, and resource levies were ordered paid in rice; in famine years those willing to pay in cloth and silk were also allowed.

entries.zh: 河南、北不通運州，租皆為絹，代關中庸、課，詔度支減轉運。
entries.en: In north and south Henan, unreachable by transport routes, grain tax was paid in silk to supply Guanzhong corvée and levies, and transport was reduced.
entries.literal: In Henan north and south, where transport prefectures were unreachable, zu was all paid in silk to substitute for Guanzhong yong and levies; the Department of Public Works was ordered to reduce transport.

entries.zh: 初，轉運使掌外，度支使掌內。
entries.en: Transport commissioners managed external revenue; expenditure commissioners managed internal funds.
entries.literal: Initially, transport commissioners managed external revenue and expenditure commissioners managed internal.

entries.zh: 永泰二年，分天下財賦、鑄錢、常平、轉運、鹽鐵，置二使。
entries.en: In Yongtai 2, fiscal authority—revenue, minting, granaries, transport, and salt—was split between two commissioners.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, empire-wide revenue, coinage, ever-normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were divided between two commissioners.

entries.zh: 東都畿內、河南、淮南、江東西、湖南、荊南、山南東道，以轉運使劉晏領之；
entries.en: The eastern circuits—including the capital region, Henan, Huainan, and the lower Yangzi—fell to Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;
entries.literal: Eastern capital metropolitan area, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong west, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan east circuit were led by Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;

entries.zh: 京畿、關內、河東、劍南、山南西道，以京兆尹、判度支第五琦領之。
entries.en: The western circuits—the capital, Guanzhong, Hedong, and Sichuan—went to Metropolitan Governor Diwu Qi.
entries.literal: Capital metropolitan area, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan west circuit were led by Metropolitan Governor and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Diwu Qi.

entries.zh: 及琦貶，以戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉與晏分治。
entries.en: After Qi's demotion, Han Huang as vice minister of revenue shared fiscal duties with Yan.
entries.literal: When Qi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Han Huang shared administration with Yan.

entries.zh: 食貨一
entries.en: Finance and Economics 1
entries.literal: Finance and Economics 1

entries.zh: 自代宗時，始以畝定稅，而斂以夏秋。
entries.en: Under Daizong, taxes were first assessed by acre and collected in summer and autumn installments.
entries.literal: From the time of Emperor Daizong, taxation began to be fixed by the mu, and collection was divided between summer and autumn.

entries.zh: 至德宗相楊炎，遂作兩稅法，夏輸無過六月，秋輸無過十一月。
entries.en: When Dezong elevated Yang Yan to chief minister, he enacted the Two-Tax Law, setting a summer deadline in the sixth month and an autumn deadline in the eleventh.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong made Yang Yan his chief minister, the Two-Tax Law was instituted: summer payments were due no later than the sixth month, autumn payments no later than the eleventh.

entries.zh: 置兩稅使以總之，量出制入。
entries.en: He appointed Two-Tax commissioners to administer the system, fixing revenue by estimating expenditures first.
entries.literal: Commissioners for the two taxes were appointed to oversee it; revenue was set by measuring outlays and fixing intake.

entries.zh: 戶無主、客，以居者為簿；
entries.en: Registers no longer distinguished "resident" from "guest" households; whoever actually lived in a district was recorded there.
entries.literal: Households were no longer divided into resident and guest registers; those who dwelt in a place were entered on its rolls.

entries.zh: 人無丁、中，以貧富為差。
entries.en: Adult and youth categories were dropped; liability was graded by wealth instead.
entries.literal: Persons were no longer classified as adult or youth; gradations were made according to wealth and poverty.

entries.zh: 商賈稅三十之一，與居者均役。
entries.en: Merchants paid a thirty-to-one levy and bore corvée obligations on the same basis as residents.
entries.literal: Merchants were taxed one-thirtieth and shared corvée duties equally with residents.

entries.zh: 田稅視大曆十四年墾田之數為定。
entries.en: Land tax was pegged to the acreage under cultivation as recorded in Dali year 14.
entries.literal: Field tax was fixed according to the number of cultivated mu recorded in the fourteenth year of the Dali era.

entries.zh: 遣黜陟使按比諸道丁產等級，免鰥寡惸獨不濟者。
entries.en: The throne dispatched inspection commissioners to verify registers, rank productive capacity by circuit, and exempt widowers, widows, orphans, and others too poor to pay.
entries.literal: Inspection commissioners were sent to compare household registers and grade productive capacity in each circuit, exempting widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute who could not pay.

entries.zh: 敢有加斂，以枉法論。
entries.en: Any official who imposed surcharges was liable for prosecution as a law-breaker.
entries.literal: Anyone who added extra levies was to be punished under the statute on perversion of law.

entries.zh: 議者以租、庸、調，高祖、太宗之法也，不可輕改。
entries.en: Opponents argued that zu, yong, and diao were the fiscal foundations laid by Gaozu and Taizong and must not be lightly discarded.
entries.literal: Critics held that zu, yong, and diao were the laws of Gaozu and Taizong and ought not be lightly altered.

entries.zh: 而德宗方信用炎，不疑也。
entries.en: Dezong, however, was wholly convinced by Yang Yan and would not be swayed.
entries.literal: But Dezong was then placing full trust in Yan and had no doubts.

entries.zh: 舊戶三百八十萬五千，使者按比得主戶三百八十萬，客戶三十萬。
entries.en: The old registers listed 3,805,000 households; after review, resident households totaled 3,800,000 and guest households 300,000.
entries.literal: Former households numbered 3,805,000; after the commissioners compared registers, resident households came to 3,800,000 and guest households to 300,000.

entries.zh: 天下之民，不土斷而地著，不更版籍而得其虛實。
entries.en: The people were tied to where they actually lived without redrawing territorial boundaries, and the government learned the real situation without overhauling the registers.
entries.literal: The people of the realm were bound to the land without territorial reassignment, and the true state of affairs was obtained without revising the household registers.

entries.zh: 歲斂錢二千五十餘萬緡，米四百萬斛，以供外；
entries.en: Annual collections yielded more than 20.5 million strings of cash and four million bushels of grain for provincial circuits.
entries.literal: Each year there were collected more than 20,500,000 strings of cash and 4,000,000 bushels of grain for external supply.

entries.zh: 錢九百五十餘萬緡，米千六百餘萬斛，以供京師。
entries.en: The capital received more than 9.5 million strings of cash and over sixteen million bushels of grain.
entries.literal: More than 9,500,000 strings of cash and more than 16,000,000 bushels of grain were supplied to the capital.

entries.zh: 自太宗時置義倉及常平倉以備凶荒，高宗以後，稍假義倉以給他費，至神龍中略盡。
entries.en: Taizong had established charity granaries and ever-normal granaries against famine. After Gaozong they were repeatedly diverted to other expenses, and by the Shenlong era the reserves were nearly gone.
entries.literal: From Taizong's time charity granaries and ever-normal granaries were established to guard against famine; after Gaozong they were gradually lent for other expenses, and by the Shenlong era they were nearly exhausted.

entries.zh: 玄宗即位，復置之。
entries.en: Xuanzong restored them on his accession.
entries.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, they were restored.

entries.zh: 其後第五琦請天下常平倉皆置庫，以畜本錢。
entries.en: Later Diwu Qi proposed that every ever-normal granary in the empire maintain storehouses holding operating capital.
entries.literal: Later Diwu Qi requested that every ever-normal granary in the realm have storehouses built to hold capital funds.

entries.zh: 至是趙贊又言：「自軍興，常平倉廢垂三十年，凶荒潰散，餧死相食，不可勝紀。
entries.en: Zhao Zan now argued: "Since the wars began, ever-normal granaries have been neglected for nearly thirty years. Famine drove people apart; they starved in such numbers that corpses fed the living beyond counting.
entries.literal: At this time Zhao Zan again said: "Since the outbreak of war the ever-normal granaries have lain abandoned for nearly thirty years; amid famine people scattered and starved, feeding on one another in numbers beyond counting.

entries.zh: 陛下即位，京城兩市置常平官，雖頻年少雨，米不騰貴，可推而廣之，宜兼儲布帛。
entries.en: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers in the capital's two markets have kept grain prices steady despite poor rains. The system should be expanded, and cloth and silk stockpiled as well.
entries.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, ever-normal officers have been placed in the two markets of the capital; though rain was scant in successive years, grain did not soar in price. This may be extended broadly; cloth and silk should also be stored.

entries.zh: 請於兩都、江陵、成都、揚、汴、蘇、洪置常平輕重本錢，上至百萬緡，下至十萬，積米、粟、布、帛、絲、麻，貴則下價而出之，賤則加估而收之。
entries.en: He proposed ever-normal funds from one million strings down to one hundred thousand at the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Bian, Suzhou, and Hongzhou, stockpiling grain, cloth, silk, and hemp to sell cheap when prices rose and buy dear when they fell.
entries.literal: He requested that in the two capitals, Jiangling, Chengdu, Yang, Bian, Su, and Hong, ever-normal capital be set in light and heavy amounts from one million strings down to one hundred thousand, storing rice, millet, cloth, silk, thread, and hemp; when prices were high they would sell at reduced price, when low they would buy at added valuation.

entries.zh: 諸道津會置吏，閱商賈錢，每緡稅二十，竹、木、茶、漆稅十之一，以贍常平本錢。」
entries.en: Tax agents at circuit crossings were to inspect merchant funds, levy twenty cash per string, and take one-tenth on bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer to fund the ever-normal reserves."
entries.literal: At ferry crossings in each circuit officers were to be placed to inspect merchants' cash, taxing twenty cash per string, and bamboo, timber, tea, and lacquer one-tenth, to support ever-normal capital."

entries.zh: 德宗納其策。
entries.en: Dezong accepted the plan.
entries.literal: Dezong adopted the plan.

entries.zh: 屬軍用迫蹵，亦隨而耗竭，不能備常平之積。
entries.en: Military demand soon consumed the reserves, and ever-normal stockpiles could not be maintained.
entries.literal: But as military needs pressed urgently, the stores were consumed in turn and could not maintain ever-normal accumulations.

entries.zh: 自會昌末，置備邊庫，收度支、戶部、鹽鐵錢物。
entries.en: From late Huichang a frontier reserve treasury absorbed revenue, salt-iron, and ministry funds.
entries.literal: From late Huichang, a frontier-reserve treasury was established, receiving funds and goods from the Directorate of Revenue, Ministry of Revenue, and salt-iron.

entries.zh: 宣宗更號延資庫。
entries.en: Xuanzong renamed it the Extended-Funds Treasury.
entries.literal: Xuanzong renamed it the Extended-Funds Treasury.

entries.zh: 初以度支郎中判之，至是以屬宰相，其任益重。
entries.en: Initially a revenue bureau director managed it; later it fell under the chief minister with greater weight.
entries.literal: At first a directorate-of-revenue bureau director judged it; from this time it was placed under the chief minister and its responsibility grew heavier.

entries.zh: 戶部歲送錢帛二十萬，度支鹽鐵送者三十萬，諸道進奉助軍錢皆輸焉。
entries.en: The Ministry of Revenue sent 200,000 yearly, revenue and salt-iron 300,000, and circuit aid-the-army gifts—all to this treasury.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Revenue yearly sent 200,000 in cash and cloth, the directorate of revenue and salt-iron 300,000, and circuits' presented aid-the-army funds were all delivered there.

entries.zh: 及討淮西，判度支楊於陵坐饋餫不繼貶，以司農卿皇甫鎛代之，由是益為刻剝。
entries.en: Campaigning against Huai-Xi, Yang Yuling was demoted for supply failures; Huangfu Bo replaced him and extraction grew crueler.
entries.literal: When the Huai-Xi campaign began, Yang Yuling, acting director of revenue, was demoted for failure to keep supplies flowing; the Minister of Agriculture Huangfu Bo replaced him, and from this extraction grew harsher.

entries.zh: 司農卿王遂、京兆尹李翛號能聚斂，乃以為宣歙、浙西觀察使，予之富饒之地，以辦財賦。
entries.en: Wang Sui and Li Xiao, famed extortionists, were sent to rich Xuan-She and Zhexi to raise revenue.
entries.literal: The Minister of Agriculture Wang Sui and the Prefect of Jingzhao Li Xiao were famed for gathering wealth and were made observation commissioners of Xuan-She and Zhexi, given rich territories to handle fiscal levies.

entries.zh: 鹽鐵使王播言：「劉晏領使時，自按租庸，然後知州縣錢穀利病虛實。」
entries.en: Wang Bo said: "When Liu Yan headed the commission, he audited zu and yong himself to learn each prefecture's true fiscal condition."
entries.literal: The salt-iron commissioner Wang Bo said: "When Liu Yan headed the commission, he himself examined zu and yong, and only then knew the profit, harm, emptiness, and fullness of prefectural cash and grain."

entries.zh: 乃以副使程异巡江、淮，覈州府上供錢穀。
entries.en: He sent vice commissioner Cheng Yi to tour Jiang-Huai and audit tribute funds.
entries.literal: Thereupon the vice commissioner Cheng Yi toured the Jiang and Huai, auditing prefectural tribute cash and grain.

entries.zh: 异至江、淮，得錢百八十五萬貫。
entries.en: Yi recovered 1.85 million strings from Jiang-Huai.
entries.literal: When Yi reached the Jiang and Huai, he obtained 1,850,000 strings of cash.

entries.zh: 其年，遂代播為鹽鐵使。
entries.en: That year Yi replaced Wang Bo as salt-iron commissioner.
entries.literal: That year he replaced Bo as salt-iron commissioner.

entries.zh: 是時，河北兵討王承宗，於是募人入粟河北、淮西者，自千斛以上皆授以官。
entries.en: While Hebei forces fought Wang Chengzong, the court recruited grain donors of a thousand bushels or more to Hebei and Huai-Xi with official posts.
entries.literal: At this time the Hebei army campaigned against Wang Chengzong; thereupon those who contributed grain to Hebei and Huai-Xi were recruited, and from one thousand bushels upward all were granted office.

entries.zh: 度支鹽鐵與諸道貢獻尤甚，號「助軍錢」。
entries.en: Revenue, salt-iron, and circuit gifts surged under the name "aid-the-army funds."
entries.literal: The Directorate of Revenue and salt-iron and the circuits' presentations were especially heavy, called "aid-the-army funds."

entries.zh: 及賊平，則有賀禮及助賞設物。
entries.en: After victories came congratulatory gifts and victory banquets.
entries.literal: When rebels were pacified, there were congratulatory gifts and aid-reward provisions.

entries.zh: 羣臣上尊號，又有獻賀物。
entries.en: Honorific ceremonies brought further congratulatory gifts.
entries.literal: When the ministers offered a honorific title, there were again congratulatory gifts presented.

entries.zh: 租庸調之法，以人丁為本。
entries.en: The zu-yong-diao tax system was founded on the registered male population.
entries.literal: The law of zu, yong, and diao took registered males as its basis.

entries.zh: 自開元以後，天下戶籍久不更造，丁口轉死，田畝賣易，貧富升降不實。
entries.en: After the Kaiyuan period, national household registers went unrevised for years. Deaths and transfers went unrecorded, land changed hands, and the real distribution of wealth no longer matched the books.
entries.literal: From after the Kaiyuan era onward, household registers throughout the realm were long left unrevised; as persons died or were transferred, fields were sold or exchanged, and the rise and fall of wealth and poverty were not truthfully recorded.

entries.zh: 其後國家侈費無節，而大盜起，兵興，財用益屈，而租庸調法弊壞。
entries.en: State expenditure then ran without limit, major rebellions broke out, and war drained the treasury until the zu-yong-diao system collapsed.
entries.literal: Thereafter the state spent without restraint, great bandits arose, warfare flared, resources grew ever tighter, and the zu-yong-diao system broke down.

entries.zh: 唐都長安，而關中號稱沃野，然其土地狹，所出不足以給京師，備水旱，故常轉漕東南之粟。
entries.en: The Tang made Chang'an its capital, and although Guanzhong was renowned as rich farmland, the region was too small to feed the court and buffer against famine and flood. The state therefore relied on regular canal shipments of grain from the southeast.
entries.literal: The Tang capital was at Chang'an, and Guanzhong was famed as fertile land, yet its territory was narrow and what it produced was insufficient to supply the capital, guard against flood and drought, and therefore grain was regularly transported by canal from the southeast.

entries.zh: 高祖、太宗之時，用物有節而易贍，水陸漕運，歲不過二十萬石，故漕事簡。
entries.en: Under Gaozu and Taizong, the court spent sparingly and provisions were ample. Combined water and land transport never exceeded two hundred thousand shi a year, so grain logistics remained straightforward.
entries.literal: In the times of Gaozu and Taizong, expenditures were restrained and supplies were easy to meet; water and land canal transport did not exceed two hundred thousand shi per year, and therefore transport affairs were simple.

entries.zh: 自高宗已後，歲益增多，而功利繁興，民亦罹其弊矣。
entries.en: After Gaozong's reign the annual haul kept growing, while schemes for profit multiplied, and the people bore the cost.
entries.literal: From after Emperor Gaozong onward, the annual amount increased ever more, while profit-seeking enterprises flourished in great number, and the people also suffered their harms.

entries.zh: 開元十八年，宣州刺史裴耀卿朝集京師，玄宗訪以漕事，耀卿條上便宜曰：「江南戶口多，而無征防之役。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 18 (730), Xuancheng prefect Pei Yaoqing came to court for the annual assembly. Xuanzong asked his views on grain transport, and Yaoqing submitted a detailed plan: 'Jiangnan is densely populated yet exempt from frontier garrison duty.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan, Xuancheng prefect Pei Yaoqing came to the capital for the annual assembly; Emperor Xuanzong inquired of him about canal affairs, and Yaoqing itemized and submitted conveniences, saying: 'The Jiangnan region has many registered households yet bears no garrison or frontier service.

entries.zh: 然送租、庸、調物，以歲二月至揚州入斗門，四月已後，始渡淮入汴，常苦水淺，六七月乃至河口，而河水方漲，須八九月水落始得上河入洛，而漕路多梗，船檣阻隘。
entries.en: Yet rent, corvée cloth, and diao goods had to reach Yangzhou's sluice by the second month, cross the Huai into the Bian only after the fourth, and often struggle through shallows until the sixth or seventh month to reach the Yellow River mouth—by which time the flood was rising. Not until the eighth or ninth month, when the water fell, could they move upriver into the Luo. The route was chronically blocked and convoys jammed the channel.
entries.literal: Yet in delivering rent, yong, and diao goods, from the second month of the year they entered the sluice gate at Yangzhou; only after the fourth month did they cross the Huai and enter the Bian Canal, often suffering from shallow water; only in the sixth or seventh month did they reach the river mouth, while the river water was just rising; they had to wait until the eighth or ninth month when the water fell before they could ascend the river and enter the Luo, and the canal route was often blocked and ships and masts obstructed and cramped.

entries.zh: 江南之人，不習河事，轉雇河師水手，重為勞費。
entries.en: Jiangnan crews were unused to river work and had to hire skilled pilots and sailors at great extra cost.
entries.literal: The people of Jiangnan were not practiced in river affairs and had to hire river masters and sailors in turn, which again became heavy labor and expense.

entries.zh: 其得行日少，阻滯日多。
entries.en: Days under way were few; days stuck in port were many.
entries.literal: The days on which they could travel were few, and the days of obstruction and delay were many.

entries.zh: 今漢、隋漕路，瀕河倉廩，遺迹可尋。
entries.en: The Han and Sui canal systems left riverside granaries whose sites can still be found.
entries.literal: Now the Han and Sui canal routes had granaries along the riverbanks, and their traces can still be traced.

entries.zh: 可於河口置武牢倉，鞏縣置洛口倉，使江南之舟不入黃河，黃河之舟不入洛口。
entries.en: Build the Wulao Granary at the river mouth and the Luokou Granary in Gong County, so Jiangnan vessels stop at the mouth and Yellow River craft never push into the Luo junction.
entries.literal: One could place the Wulao Granary at the river mouth and the Luokou Granary at Gong County, so that boats from Jiangnan would not enter the Yellow River and Yellow River boats would not enter Luokou.

entries.zh: 而河陽、柏崖、太原、永豐、渭南諸倉，節級轉運，水通則舟行，水淺則寓於倉以待，則舟無停留，而物不耗失。
entries.en: Relay through granaries at Heyang, Baiya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan: sail when the channel is full, store when it is low. Convoys would never idle long and spoilage would drop sharply.
entries.literal: Then the granaries at Heyang, Baiya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan would relay transport by stages; when water was open boats would sail, when water was shallow they would lodge in granaries and wait—then boats would have no long stops and goods would not be wasted or lost.

entries.zh: 此甚利也。」
entries.en: The savings would be enormous.'
entries.literal: This would be greatly advantageous.'

entries.zh: 玄宗初不省。
entries.en: Xuanzong at first paid little attention.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuanzong at first did not take it to heart.

entries.zh: 二十一年，耀卿為京兆尹，京師雨水，穀踊貴，玄宗將幸東都，復問耀卿漕事，耀卿因請「罷陝陸運，而置倉河口，使江南漕舟至河口者，輸粟於倉而去，縣官雇舟以分入河、洛。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 21 (733), now metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, Yaoqing faced floods in the capital and soaring grain prices as Xuanzong prepared to move to Luoyang. Asked again about transport, he urged: 'End the Shan overland haul, build river-mouth granaries where Jiangnan convoys would unload and leave, and have the state hire boats to move grain into the Yellow River and Luo systems.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, Yaoqing became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao; the capital had rain and floods, grain prices soared, and Emperor Xuanzong was about to visit the Eastern Capital; he again asked Yaoqing about canal affairs, and Yaoqing therefore requested: 'Abolish the Shan overland route and establish granaries at the river mouth, so that canal boats from Jiangnan reaching the mouth would unload grain into the granaries and depart, and the government would hire boats to distribute loads into the Yellow River and Luo.

entries.zh: 置倉三門東西，漕舟輸其東倉，而陸運以輸西倉，復以舟漕，以避三門之水險。」
entries.en: Place granaries on both sides of Sanmen Gorge: boats unload at the east warehouse, porters carry overland to the west warehouse, then boats resume the river leg—bypassing Sanmen's rapids.'
entries.literal: Establish granaries east and west of Sanmen; canal boats would deliver to the eastern granary, overland transport would carry to the western granary, and then boats would transport again by water to avoid the water dangers of Sanmen.'

entries.zh: 玄宗以為然。
entries.en: Xuanzong agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor thought it right.

entries.zh: 乃於河陰置河陰倉，河清置柏崖倉；
entries.en: The Heyin Granary was built at Heyin and the Baiya Granary at Heqing;
entries.literal: Thereupon the Heyin Granary was established at Heyin, and the Baiya Granary at Heqing;

entries.zh: 三門東置集津倉，西置鹽倉；
entries.en: east of Sanmen the Jijin Granary and west of it the Yan Granary;
entries.literal: east of Sanmen the Jijin Granary was placed, west of it the Yan Granary;

entries.zh: 鑿山十八里以陸運。
entries.en: and an eighteen-li mountain road was cut for the overland relay.
entries.literal: and the mountain was cut for eighteen li for overland transport.

entries.zh: 自江、淮漕者，皆輸河陰倉，自河陰西至太原倉，謂之北運，自太原倉浮渭以實關中。
entries.en: Jiang-Huai grain all went to Heyin; the leg from Heyin west to Taiyuan was called the Northern Route, and from Taiyuan boats sailed the Wei to supply Guanzhong.
entries.literal: All grain transported from the Jiang and Huai was delivered to the Heyin Granary; from Heyin west to the Taiyuan Granary was called the northern transport route, and from the Taiyuan Granary they floated on the Wei to fill Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 玄宗大悅，拜耀卿為黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，兼江淮都轉運使，以鄭州刺史崔希逸、河南少尹蕭炅為副使，益漕晉、絳、魏、濮、邢、貝、濟、博之租輸諸倉，轉而入渭。
entries.en: Delighted, Xuanzong made Yaoqing vice director of the Huangmen and chief minister, with overall charge of Jiang-Huai transport; Cui Xiyi and Xiao Jiong served as deputies. Rent from eight more prefectures was added to the relay into the Wei.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was greatly pleased and appointed Yaoqing as vice director of the Huangmen and associate chief minister under the Secretariat-Chancellery, concurrently chief transport commissioner for the Jiang and Huai, with Zhengzhou prefect Cui Xiyi and Henan vice governor Xiao Jiong as deputies; he increased canal transport of rent from Jin, Jiang, Wei, Pu, Xing, Bei, Ji, and Bo into the various granaries, then relayed it into the Wei.

entries.zh: 凡三歲，漕七百萬石，省陸運傭錢三十萬緡。
entries.en: Within three years seven million shi moved by water, saving three hundred thousand strings in overland hire.
entries.literal: In all, over three years, seven million shi were transported by canal, saving three hundred thousand strings in overland hire money.

entries.zh: 二十九年，陝郡太守李齊物鑿砥柱為門以通漕，開其山顛為輓路，燒石沃醯而鑿之。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 29 (741), Shan prefect Li Qiwu cut a gate through the Dizhu rocks for grain boats, blasted a haul road along the ridge by heating stone and dousing it with vinegar.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Shan prefect Li Qiwu cut the Dizhu rocks into a gate to open canal passage, opened the mountain crest as a hauling road, and cut the rock by heating it and pouring vinegar over it.

entries.zh: 然棄石入河，激水益湍怒，舟不能入新門，候其水漲，以人輓舟而上。
entries.en: Rubble dumped in the channel only made the current fiercer. Boats could not use the new gate until the flood rose, when teams hauled them through.
entries.literal: Yet discarded stone thrown into the river made the current more turbulent and furious; boats could not enter the new gate and had to wait for the water to rise, then men hauled the boats up.

entries.zh: 天子疑之，遣宦者按視，齊物厚賂使者，還言便。
entries.en: The emperor had doubts and sent eunuch inspectors; Qiwu bribed them heavily, and they reported the project sound.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven doubted it and sent eunuchs to inspect; Qiwu bribed the envoys heavily, and they returned saying it was convenient.

entries.zh: 齊物入為鴻臚卿，以長安令韋堅代之，兼水陸運使。
entries.en: Qiwu was promoted to minister of ceremonial; Wei Jian, magistrate of Chang'an, replaced him as combined water-and-land transport commissioner.
entries.literal: Qiwu entered court as minister of ceremonial and was replaced by Chang'an magistrate Wei Jian, who also held the post of water-and-land transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 堅治漢、隋運渠，起關門，抵長安，通山東租賦。
entries.en: Wei Jian restored the Han and Sui canals from Tong Pass to Chang'an to bring Shandong grain and taxes to the capital.
entries.literal: Jian repaired the Han and Sui transport canals, starting from Tong Pass and reaching Chang'an, to open passage for Shandong rent and levies.

entries.zh: 乃絕灞、滻，並渭而東，至永豐倉與渭合。
entries.en: He diverted the Ba and Chan, ran the channel east along the Wei to the Yongfeng Granary, and rejoined the main Wei.
entries.literal: He then cut off the Ba and Chan rivers, joined the Wei and went east, reaching the Yongfeng Granary where it met the Wei.

entries.zh: 又於長樂坡瀕苑牆鑿潭於望春樓下，以聚漕舟。
entries.en: Below Wangchun Tower on Changle Slope he excavated a basin beside the imperial park wall to berth the grain fleet.
entries.literal: He also cut a pond at Wangchun Tower below on Changle Slope along the park wall to gather canal boats.

entries.zh: 堅因使諸舟各揭其郡名，陳其土地所產寶貨諸奇物於栿上。
entries.en: Each vessel flew its home commandery's name and displayed local treasures and curios on deck beams.
entries.literal: Jian therefore had each boat display its commandery name and array the precious goods and curiosities produced in its territory on the beams.

entries.zh: 先時民間唱俚歌曰「得体紇那邪」。
entries.en: Earlier folk had sung a ditty: 'Deti he na ye.'
entries.literal: Earlier the people had sung a vulgar song saying 'Deti he na ye.'

entries.zh: 其後得寶符於桃林，於是陝縣尉崔成甫更得体歌為得寶弘農野。
entries.en: When a treasure talisman was found at Taolin, Shan county aide Cui Chengfu rewrote the refrain as 'Treasure found in the Hongnong wilds.'
entries.literal: Later a treasure talisman was obtained at Taolin, and thereupon Shan county aide Cui Chengfu changed the 'deti' song to 'Treasure found in the wilds of Hongnong.'

entries.zh: 堅命舟人為吳、楚服，大笠、廣袖、芒屩以歌之。
entries.en: Jian dressed the boatmen in Wu-Chu costume—wide hats, flowing sleeves, straw sandals—to perform the song.
entries.literal: Jian ordered the boatmen to wear Wu and Chu dress—large hats, broad sleeves, and straw sandals—to sing it.

entries.zh: 成甫又廣之為歌辭十闋，自衣缺後綠衣、錦半臂、紅抹額，立第一船為號頭以唱，集兩縣婦女百餘人，鮮服靚粧，鳴鼓吹笛以和之。
entries.en: Chengfu expanded it to ten stanzas, stood on the lead boat in green robe, brocade half-sleeves, and red forehead cloth to lead the chorus, and assembled over a hundred women from two counties in bright dress with drums, pipes, and flutes.
entries.literal: Chengfu further expanded it into ten stanzas of song lyrics; he himself wore a green robe under a quehou jacket, brocade half-sleeves, and a red forehead band, stood on the lead boat as caller to sing, gathered more than a hundred women from two counties in bright dress and fine makeup, and had drums, pipes, and flutes sound in accompaniment.

entries.zh: 眾艘以次輳樓下，天子望見大悅，賜其潭名曰廣運潭。
entries.en: The flotilla moored in turn below the tower. The emperor was delighted and named the basin Guangyun, 'Broad Transport.'
entries.literal: The fleet of boats in turn gathered below the tower; the Son of Heaven looked out and was greatly pleased, and bestowed on the pond the name Guangyun Pond.

entries.zh: 是歲，漕山東粟四百萬石。
entries.en: That year four million shi of Shandong grain reached the capital by water.
entries.literal: That year, four million shi of Shandong grain were transported by canal.

entries.zh: 自裴耀卿言漕事，進用者常兼轉運之職，而韋堅為最。
entries.en: After Pei Yaoqing's reforms, favored officials usually held transport portfolios as well; Wei Jian stood at the peak.
entries.literal: From the time Pei Yaoqing spoke on canal affairs, those advanced to office often concurrently held transport posts, and Wei Jian was foremost among them.

entries.zh: 貞觀、開元後，邊土西舉高昌、龜茲、焉耆、小勃律，北抵薛延陀故地，緣邊數十州戍重兵，營田及地租不足以供軍，於是初有和糴。
entries.en: After Zhenguan and Kaiyuan the frontier stretched west to Gaochang, Kucha, Yanqi, and Little Bolü and north to the Xueyantuo lands. Dozens of border prefectures held large garrisons. When farms and land tax could not feed the troops, the state began hedi grain purchases.
entries.literal: After Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, the frontier west took Gaochang, Kucha, Yanqi, and Little Bolü; north it reached the old lands of the Xueyantuo; dozens of border prefectures garrisoned heavy troops; garrison fields and land tax were insufficient to supply the armies, and therefore hedi purchase first arose.

entries.zh: 牛仙客為相，有彭果者獻策廣關輔之糴，京師糧稟益羨，自是玄宗不復幸東都。
entries.en: Under Chancellor Niu Xianke, Peng Guo proposed expanding Guanfu grain purchases. Capital stores overflowed, and Xuanzong never again visited Luoyang.
entries.literal: When Niu Xianke was chancellor, a Peng Guo offered a plan to expand Guanfu purchases; the capital's grain stores grew ever fuller, and from then on Emperor Xuanzong no longer visited the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 天寶中，歲以錢六十萬緡賦諸道和糴，斗增三錢，每歲短遞輸京倉者百餘萬斛。
entries.en: In the Tianbao era (742–756) circuits paid six hundred thousand strings yearly for hedi purchases with a three-cash premium per dou; over a million hu reached capital granaries each year.
entries.literal: In the Tianbao era, each year six hundred thousand strings were assessed on circuits for hedi purchase, three cash added per dou, and each year more than a million hu were delivered by short relay to the capital granaries.

entries.zh: 米賤則少府加估而糴，貴則賤價而糶。
entries.en: When rice was cheap the Court of the Imperial Treasury bought at a premium; when dear it sold at reduced prices.
entries.literal: When rice was cheap the Court of the Imperial Treasury added to the valuation and purchased; when dear, it sold at low price.

entries.zh: 肅宗末年，史朝義兵分出宋州，淮運於是阻絕，租庸鹽鐵泝漢江而上。
entries.en: Late in Suzong's reign Shi Chaoyi's forces swept out of Songzhou and severed the Huai route; rent, corvée goods, salt, and iron had to go up the Han instead.
entries.literal: In the last years of Emperor Suzong, Shi Chaoyi's troops issued from Songzhou, and Huai transport was thereby cut off; rent, yong, salt, and iron went up the Han River instead.

entries.zh: 河南尹劉晏為戶部侍郎，兼句當度支、轉運、鹽鐵、鑄錢使，江淮粟帛，繇襄、漢越商於以輸京師。
entries.en: Henan governor Liu Yan, as vice minister of revenue, also ran finance, transport, salt and iron, and minting. Jiang-Huai grain and cloth reached the capital via the Xiang-Han corridor and the Shangyu road.
entries.literal: Henan governor Liu Yan was vice minister of revenue and concurrently handled the posts of revenue administration, transport, salt and iron, and coinage; Jiang-Huai grain and cloth were sent to the capital by way of Xiang, Han, and over Shangyu.

entries.zh: 及代宗出陝州，關中空窘，於是盛轉輸以給用。
entries.en: When Daizong escaped through Shanzhou, Guanzhong was destitute and transport was massively expanded to feed the court.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daizong came out of Shanzhou, Guanzhong was empty and straitened, and therefore transport was greatly expanded to supply needs.

entries.zh: 廣德二年，廢句當度支使，以劉晏顓領東都、河南、淮西、江南東西轉運、租庸、鑄錢、鹽鐵，轉輸至上都，度支所領諸道租庸觀察使，凡漕事亦皆決於晏。
entries.en: In Guangde 2 (764) the revenue-handler post was abolished and Liu Yan took sole charge of transport, rent and yong, minting, and salt and iron from Luoyang through Henan, Huaixi, and both Jiangnans to the capital. Every circuit tax commissioner answered to him on grain logistics.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangde, the post of handler of revenue administration was abolished, and Liu Yan was placed in sole charge of Eastern Capital, Henan, Huaixi, and Jiangnan east and west transport, rent and yong, coinage, and salt and iron, with transport to the upper capital; the circuit rent-and-yong observation commissioners under revenue administration—all canal affairs were also decided by Yan.

entries.zh: 晏即鹽利顧傭分吏督之，隨江、汴、河、渭所宜。
entries.en: He funded hired crews from salt profits and posted officers along the Yangtze, Bian, Yellow River, and Wei as each stretch required.
entries.literal: Yan then used salt profits to hire labor and assign officials to supervise by sections, adapting to what suited the Yangtze, Bian, Yellow River, and Wei.

entries.zh: 故時轉運船繇潤州陸運至揚子，斗米費錢十九，晏命囊米而載以舟，減錢十五；
entries.en: Previously grain went overland from Runzhou to Yangzi at nineteen cash per dou; Yan switched to bagged rice by boat and cut fifteen cash;
entries.literal: Formerly transport boats went by land from Runzhou to Yangzi, costing nineteen cash per dou of rice; Yan ordered grain bagged and carried by boat, reducing the cost by fifteen cash;

entries.zh: 繇揚州距河陰，斗米費錢百二十，晏為歇艎支江船二千艘，每船受千斛，十船為綱，每綱三百人，篙工五十，自揚州遣將部送至河陰，上三門，號「上門填闕船」，米斗減錢九十。
entries.en: from Yangzhou to Heyin the cost had been 120 cash per dou. Yan fielded two thousand river barges of a thousand hu each, grouped in convoys of ten with three hundred men and fifty polemen, escorted by officers to Heyin and through Sanmen as 'gap-filling upper-gate ships,' cutting ninety cash per dou.
entries.literal: from Yangzhou to Heyin it cost 120 cash per dou; Yan provided 2,000 river boats of the xiehang type, each holding 1,000 hu, ten boats forming a gang, each gang with 300 men and fifty polemen; from Yangzhou he sent generals to escort deliveries to Heyin and up through Sanmen, calling them 'upper-gate gap-filling boats,' and the cost per dou of rice was reduced by ninety cash.

entries.zh: 調巴、蜀、襄、漢麻枲竹篠為綯挽舟，以朽索腐材代薪，物無棄者。
entries.en: Hemp, bamboo, and rushes from the southwest became tow ropes; rotten cord and scrap wood replaced fuel—nothing was wasted.
entries.literal: He requisitioned hemp, bamboo, and rushes from Ba, Shu, Xiang, and Han to make towing ropes for boats, used rotten cord and decayed timber in place of fuel, and nothing was wasted.

entries.zh: 未十年，人人習河險。
entries.en: Within a decade crews mastered the river hazards.
entries.literal: In less than ten years, everyone became practiced in river perils.

entries.zh: 江船不入汴，汴船不入河，河船不入渭；
entries.en: Yangtze craft stopped at the Bian junction, Bian craft at the Yellow River, Yellow River craft at the Wei;
entries.literal: Yangtze boats did not enter the Bian, Bian boats did not enter the Yellow River, and Yellow River boats did not enter the Wei;

entries.zh: 江南之運積揚州，汴河之運積河陰，河船之運積渭口，渭船之運入太倉。
entries.en: Jiangnan freight piled up at Yangzhou, Bian freight at Heyin, Yellow River freight at the Wei mouth, and Wei boats fed the Great Granary.
entries.literal: Jiangnan transport accumulated at Yangzhou, Bian Canal transport at Heyin, Yellow River transport at the Wei mouth, and Wei boats delivered into the Great Granary.

entries.zh: 歲轉粟百一十萬石，無升斗溺者。
entries.en: Annual deliveries reached 1.1 million shi without a single bushel lost to the river.
entries.literal: Each year 1.1 million shi of grain were relayed, without a sheng or dou lost by drowning.

entries.zh: 輕貨自揚子至汴州，每馱費錢二千二百，減九百，歲省十餘萬緡。
entries.en: Light cargo from Yangzi to Bianzhou had cost 2,200 cash per pack; Yan cut 900 and saved over 100,000 strings a year.
entries.literal: Light goods from Yangzi to Bianzhou cost 2,200 cash per pack load; this was reduced by 900, saving more than 100,000 strings per year.

entries.zh: 又分官吏主丹楊湖，禁引溉，自是河漕不涸。
entries.en: Officials guarded Danyang Lake and banned irrigation diversions, keeping the canal full thereafter.
entries.literal: He also assigned officials to oversee Danyang Lake, forbidding diversion for irrigation, and from then on the canal route did not run dry.

entries.zh: 大曆八年，以關內豐穰，減漕十萬石，度支和糴以優農。
entries.en: In Dali 8 (773), with Guanzhong harvests rich, the quota was cut by 100,000 shi and the treasury bought grain at fair rates to aid farmers.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, because Guanzhong was abundant and ripe, canal transport was reduced by 100,000 shi, and revenue administration made hedi purchases to benefit farmers.

entries.zh: 晏自天寶末掌出納，監歲運，知左右藏，主財穀三十餘年矣。
entries.en: Since the late Tianbao era Yan had run receipts, annual transport, and both treasuries—more than thirty years at the fiscal helm.
entries.literal: Yan from the end of Tianbao had managed receipts and disbursements, overseen annual transport, and known the left and right treasuries, directing finances and grain for more than thirty years.

entries.zh: 及楊炎為相，以舊惡罷晏，轉運使復歸度支，凡江淮漕米，以庫部郎中崔河圖主之。
entries.en: When Yang Yan became chancellor he removed Yan over old grudges. Transport reverted to the revenue office, and Jiang-Huai grain fell to Cui Hetu of the storehouse bureau.
entries.literal: When Yang Yan became chancellor, because of old enmity he dismissed Yan; transport commissioners returned to revenue administration, and all Jiang-Huai canal rice was placed under Cui Hetu, director of the storehouse bureau.

entries.zh: 是時，汴宋節度使春夏遣官監汴水，察盜灌溉者。
entries.en: Each spring and summer the Bian-Song commissioner posted officers on the Bian Canal to catch illegal irrigation diversions.
entries.literal: At this time the Bian-Song military commissioner in spring and summer sent officials to supervise the Bian Canal and investigate those who stole water for irrigation.

entries.zh: 歲漕經底柱，覆者幾半。
entries.en: Each year's convoys through the Dizhu rocks lost nearly half their boats.
entries.literal: Annual canal transport passing Dizhu saw nearly half capsized.

entries.zh: 河中有山號「米堆」，運舟入三門，雇平陸人為門匠，執標指麾，一舟百日乃能上。
entries.en: A mid-river peak was called 'Rice Mound.' Boats entering Sanmen hired Pinglu pilots called 'gate craftsmen' to signal the way; a single vessel might need a hundred days to get through.
entries.literal: In the river was a hill called 'Rice Mound'; transport boats entering Sanmen hired men from Pinglu as gate craftsmen to hold markers and direct; one boat might take a hundred days before it could ascend.

entries.zh: 諺曰：「古無門匠墓。」
entries.en: A proverb ran: "Since antiquity there have been no gate craftsmen's graves."
entries.literal: A proverb says: 'In antiquity there were no tombs for gate craftsmen.'

entries.zh: 謂皆溺死也。
entries.en: —because they all drowned.
entries.literal: —meaning they all drowned.

entries.zh: 陝虢觀察使李泌益鑿集津倉山西逕為運道，屬于三門倉，治上路以回空車，費錢五萬緡，下路減半；
entries.en: Shan-Guo commissioner Li Bi cut a haul road west of Jijin Granary linked to Sanmen, rebuilt the upper track for empty carts at fifty thousand strings and the lower at half that;
entries.literal: Shan-Guo observation commissioner Li Bi further cut a transport road west of the Jijin Granary mountain, connecting to the Sanmen granary; he repaired the upper route for returning empty carts, costing fifty thousand strings, and the lower route cost half as much;

entries.zh: 又為入渭船，方五板，輸東渭橋太倉米至凡百三十萬石，遂罷南路陸運。
entries.en: and built five-plank Wei barges that moved 1.3 million shi from the Eastern Wei Bridge granary, ending the southern overland haul.
entries.literal: he also made Wei-entry boats of five planks square, delivering grain from the Eastern Wei Bridge Great Granary totaling 1.3 million shi, and then abolished the southern overland route.

entries.zh: 其後諸道鹽鐵、轉運使張滂復置江淮巡院。
entries.en: Later circuit transport commissioner Zhang Pang restored the Jiang-Huai patrol office.
entries.literal: Afterward circuit salt-and-iron and transport commissioner Zhang Pang restored the Jiang-Huai patrol office.

entries.zh: 及浙西觀察使李錡領使，江淮堰埭隸浙西者，增私路小堰之稅，以副使潘孟陽主上都留後。
entries.en: When Zhexi commissioner Li Qi took charge, he taxed private roads and small weirs on Jiang-Huai works under Zhexi; deputy Pan Mengyang ran the capital liaison office.
entries.literal: When Zhexi observation commissioner Li Qi headed the office, on Jiang-Huai dams and weirs subordinate to Zhexi he increased taxes on private roads and small weirs, and deputy commissioner Pan Mengyang managed the capital's rear office.

entries.zh: 李巽為諸道轉運、鹽鐵使，以堰埭歸鹽鐵使，罷其增置者。
entries.en: Li Xun as circuit transport and salt-and-iron commissioner returned the dams to salt-and-iron control and abolished Li Qi's extra taxes.
entries.literal: Li Xun served as circuit transport and salt-and-iron commissioner, returned dams and weirs to the salt-and-iron office, and abolished the added levies.

entries.zh: 自劉晏後，江淮米至渭橋寖減矣，至巽乃復如晏之多。
entries.en: After Liu Yan, Jiang-Huai grain to Wei Bridge had steadily fallen; under Li Xun it recovered to Yan's levels.
entries.literal: After Liu Yan, Jiang-Huai rice reaching Wei Bridge had gradually diminished; only with Xun did it again reach Yan's volume.

entries.zh: 自兵起，流庸未復，稅賦不足供費，鹽鐵使劉晏以為因民所急而稅之，則國足用。
entries.en: After the rebellion began, refugees had not returned and tax income could not cover expenses. Salt Commissioner Liu Yan argued that levying taxes on what people could not do without would keep the state solvent.
entries.literal: Since the armies rose, displaced persons had not returned and tax revenues were insufficient for expenses. The Salt and Iron Commissioner Liu Yan held that taxing what the people urgently need would suffice for state use.

entries.zh: 於是上鹽法輕重之宜，以鹽吏多則州縣擾，出鹽鄉因舊監置吏，亭戶糶商人，縱其所之。
entries.en: He then proposed a balanced salt policy: too many salt officials harassed local government. In producing districts he restored officers at existing posts, let saltern households sell to merchants, and allowed merchants to trade freely.
entries.literal: Thereupon he presented what was fitting in the weight of the salt law: many salt officials disturbed prefectures and counties; in salt-producing districts he placed officers according to old supervisory posts; saltern households sold to merchants, who were allowed to go where they would.

entries.zh: 江、嶺去鹽遠者，有常平鹽，每商人不至，則減價以糶民，官收厚利而人不知貴。
entries.en: In the Yangzi and Ling regions far from salt sources he maintained Ever-Normal reserves: when merchants failed to arrive, officials cut prices to sell to the public. The state still took a large margin, yet consumers scarcely felt the burden.
entries.literal: Where the Yangzi and Ling regions were far from salt, there was Ever-Normal salt; whenever merchants did not arrive, prices were reduced to sell to the people; the government took thick profit yet people did not feel it dear.

entries.zh: 晏又以鹽生霖潦則鹵薄，暵旱則土溜墳，乃隨時為令，遣吏曉導，倍於勸農。
entries.en: Yan also knew that heavy rains thinned the brine and droughts washed soil over the beds, so he issued seasonal orders and sent officers to guide production—more diligently than any agricultural campaign.
entries.literal: Yan also held that when rain and flood came, brine grew thin, and when drought came, earth washed and mounded; he therefore issued timely orders and sent officers to instruct, with effort twice that of encouraging agriculture.

entries.zh: 吳、越、揚、楚鹽廩至數千，積鹽二萬餘石。
entries.en: Salt granaries in Wu, Yue, Yang, and Chu numbered in the thousands and held more than twenty thousand shi in reserve.
entries.literal: Wu, Yue, Yang, and Chu salt granaries reached several thousand, storing more than twenty thousand shi of salt.

entries.zh: 有漣水、湖州、越州、杭州四場，嘉興、海陵、鹽城、新亭、臨平、蘭亭、永嘉、大昌、候官、富都十監，歲得錢百餘萬緡，以當百餘州之賦。
entries.en: Four production fields operated at Lianshui, Huzhou, Yuezhou, and Hangzhou, and ten supervisory posts at Jiaxing, Hailing, Yancheng, Xinting, Linping, Lanting, Yongjia, Dachang, Houguan, and Fudu. Annual revenue exceeded one million strings—equivalent to taxes from more than a hundred prefectures.
entries.literal: There were four fields at Lianshui, Huzhou, Yuezhou, and Hangzhou, and ten supervisory posts at Jiaxing, Hailing, Yancheng, Xinting, Linping, Lanting, Yongjia, Dachang, Houguan, and Fudu; yearly receipts exceeded one million strings, equaling the tax of more than one hundred prefectures.

entries.zh: 自淮北置巡院十三，曰揚州、陳許、汴州、廬壽、白沙、淮西、甬橋、浙西、宋州、泗州、嶺南、兗鄆、鄭滑，捕私鹽者，姦盜為之衰息。
entries.en: North of the Huai he established thirteen patrol offices—from Yangzhou to Zheng-Hua—to suppress smuggling, and illicit salt trade sharply declined.
entries.literal: North of the Huai he set up thirteen patrol offices—Yangzhou, Chenxu, Bianzhou, Lushou, Baisha, Huaixi, Yongqiao, Zhexi, Songzhou, Sizhou, Lingnan, Yan-Yun, and Zheng-Hua—to seize private salt; illicit trade thereby declined.

entries.zh: 然諸道加榷鹽錢，商人舟所過有稅。
entries.en: Yet circuits still added monopoly surcharges, and merchants were taxed at every port their boats touched.
entries.literal: Yet the various circuits added monopoly salt surcharges, and wherever merchants' boats passed there were taxes.

entries.zh: 晏奏罷州縣率稅，禁堰埭邀以利者。
entries.en: Yan petitioned to end ad hoc local levies and to forbid dam keepers from extorting travelers for passage fees.
entries.literal: Yan memorialized to abolish prefectural and county levies in kind and to forbid dams and weirs from intercepting travelers for profit.

entries.zh: 晏之始至也，鹽利歲纔四十萬緡，至大曆末，六百餘萬緡。
entries.en: When Yan took office annual salt revenue was only four hundred thousand strings; by the end of the Dali era it exceeded six million.
entries.literal: When Yan first arrived, salt profit was only four hundred thousand strings yearly; by the end of Dali it was more than six million.

entries.zh: 天下之賦，鹽利居半，宮闈服御、軍饟、百官祿俸皆仰給焉。
entries.en: Salt profits accounted for half of national revenue, funding palace supplies, army rations, and official salaries alike.
entries.literal: Of all revenue under Heaven, salt profit comprised half; palace apparel, army provisions, and officials' salaries all depended on it.

entries.zh: 明年而晏罷。
entries.en: The following year Yan was removed from office.
entries.literal: The next year Yan was dismissed.

entries.zh: 劉晏鹽法既成，商人納絹以代鹽利者，每緡加錢二百，以備將士春服。
entries.en: After Liu Yan's salt reforms, merchants paying silk in lieu of salt dues paid an extra two hundred cash per string to fund spring uniforms for the troops.
entries.literal: Once Liu Yan's salt law was established, merchants who paid silk in lieu of salt profit had two hundred cash added per string, to prepare spring uniforms for officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 包佶為汴東水陸運、兩稅、鹽鐵使，許以漆器、瑇瑁、綾綺代鹽價，雖不可用者亦高估而售之，廣虛數以罔上。
entries.en: As transport, tax, and salt commissioner Bao Ji let merchants pay salt dues in lacquer, tortoiseshell, and brocade—even worthless goods at inflated prices—padding accounts to deceive the court.
entries.literal: Bao Ji was Commissioner for Bian-East Water and Land Transport, the Two Taxes, and Salt and Iron; he allowed lacquerware, tortoiseshell, and fine silks to substitute for salt price; even unusable goods were overvalued and sold, inflating false figures to deceive the throne.

entries.zh: 亭戶冒法，私鬻不絕，巡捕之卒，遍于州縣。
entries.en: Saltern households broke the law and illicit sales continued unabated, while patrol troops spread through every prefecture and county.
entries.literal: Saltern households violated the law; private sale did not cease; patrol soldiers were everywhere in prefectures and counties.

entries.zh: 鹽估益貴，商人乘時射利，遠鄉貧民困高估，至有淡食者。
entries.en: Salt prices kept rising as merchants profiteered. Poor villagers in remote districts, crushed by inflated valuations, were reduced to eating food without salt.
entries.literal: Salt valuations grew ever dearer; merchants seized the moment for profit; poor people in distant districts were strained by high valuations, until some ate food without salt.

entries.zh: 巡吏既多，官冗傷財，當時病之。
entries.en: With so many patrol officers, bureaucratic bloat drained the treasury—a grievance widely noted at the time.
entries.literal: Patrol officers being numerous, redundant officials harmed the treasury; contemporaries regarded this as a malady.

entries.zh: 其後軍費日增，鹽價寖貴，有以穀數斗易鹽一升。
entries.en: As military costs mounted, salt prices kept climbing until some people traded several dou of grain for a single sheng of salt.
entries.literal: Afterward military expenses daily increased and salt prices gradually grew dear; some exchanged several dou of grain for one sheng of salt.

entries.zh: 私糴犯法，未嘗少息。
entries.en: Illegal private trade never let up.
entries.literal: Private purchase in violation of law never for a moment ceased.

entries.zh: 順宗時始減江淮鹽價，每斗為錢二百五十，河中兩池鹽，斗錢三百。
entries.en: Under Emperor Shunzong Jiang-Huai salt was cut to two hundred fifty cash a dou, and the Two Ponds salt in Hezhong to three hundred.
entries.literal: In the time of Shunzong Jiang-Huai salt prices were first reduced to two hundred fifty cash per dou; the Two Ponds salt in Hezhong was three hundred cash per dou.

entries.zh: 增雲安、渙陽、塗𣉯三監。
entries.en: Three new salt supervisory posts were established at Yun'an, Huanyang, and Tuwei.
entries.literal: Three supervisory posts were added at Yun'an, Huanyang, and Tuwei.

entries.zh: 其後鹽鐵使李錡奏江淮鹽斗減錢十以便民，未幾復舊。
entries.en: Later Salt Commissioner Li Qi petitioned to cut Jiang-Huai salt by ten cash a dou to ease the burden on the people, but the reduction was soon reversed.
entries.literal: Afterward the Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Qi memorialized to reduce Jiang-Huai salt by ten cash per dou for the people's convenience; before long the old price returned.

entries.zh: 方是時，錡盛貢獻以固寵，朝廷大臣，皆餌以厚貨，鹽鐵之利，積于私室，而國用耗屈，榷鹽法大壞，多為虛估，率千錢不滿百三十而已。
entries.en: Li Qi lavished tribute to secure favor and bribed senior ministers with rich gifts, hoarding salt profits privately while the treasury emptied. The monopoly system collapsed into sham valuations—of every thousand cash collected, barely one hundred thirty was real revenue.
entries.literal: At that time Qi made lavish tribute to secure favor; court great ministers were all baited with rich goods; salt and iron profit accumulated in private chambers while state use was exhausted; the monopoly salt law was greatly ruined, mostly false valuations, so that per thousand cash not even one hundred thirty were real.

entries.zh: 兵部侍郎李巽為使，以鹽利皆歸度支，物無虛估，天下糶鹽稅茶，其贏六百六十五萬緡。
entries.en: When Vice Minister Li Xun took charge, salt revenue returned fully to the Department of Expenditure with no inflated valuations. Nationwide salt sales and tea taxes yielded a surplus of 6.65 million strings.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of War Li Xun became commissioner; salt profit all returned to the Department of Expenditure; goods had no false valuation; selling salt and taxing tea under Heaven yielded a surplus of six million six hundred fifty thousand strings.

entries.zh: 初歲之利，如劉晏之季年，其後則三倍晏時矣。
entries.en: The first year's yield matched Liu Yan's final year; within a few years revenue tripled Yan's peak.
entries.literal: The first year's profit matched Liu Yan's final years; afterward it was three times Yan's time.

entries.zh: 兩池鹽利，歲收百五十餘萬緡。
entries.en: The Two Ponds alone brought in more than 1.5 million strings a year.
entries.literal: Profit from the Two Ponds yearly collected more than one million five hundred thousand strings.

entries.zh: 四方豪商猾賈，雜處解縣，主以郎官，其佐貳皆御史。
entries.en: Wealthy and unscrupulous merchants from every region gathered at Jie County, headed by a court gentleman with censors as deputies.
entries.literal: Great merchants and crafty traders from the four directions mingled at Jie County; the chief was a court gentleman, and his assistants were all censors.

entries.zh: 鹽民田園籍於縣，而令不得以縣民治之。
entries.en: Although salt workers' land was registered locally, magistrates could not treat them as ordinary county subjects.
entries.literal: Salt workers' fields and gardens were registered in the county, yet the magistrate could not govern them as county people.

entries.zh: 當時議者以為「自天寶至今，戶九百餘萬。
entries.en: Contemporary analysts argued: "From the Tianbao era to the present there are more than nine million households.
entries.literal: Debaters at the time held that "from Tianbao to now, households are more than nine million.

entries.zh: 王制：上農夫食九人，中農夫七人。
entries.en: Royal regulations held that a superior farmer supported nine people and a middling farmer seven.
entries.literal: The royal regulations: a superior farmer feeds nine people, a middling farmer seven.

entries.zh: 以中農夫計之，為六千三百萬人。
entries.en: By middling-farmer reckoning, the population came to sixty-three million.
entries.literal: Calculated by middling farmers, this was sixty-three million people.

entries.zh: 少壯相均，人食米二升，日費米百二十六萬斛，歲費四萬五千三百六十萬斛，而衣倍之，吉凶之禮再倍，餘三年之儲以備水旱凶災，當米十三萬六千八十萬斛，以貴賤豐儉相當，則米之直與錢鈞也。
entries.en: With young and old evenly distributed and two sheng of rice per person daily, daily consumption was 1.26 million hu and annual consumption 453.6 million hu; clothing doubled that, ritual expenses doubled again, and three years' reserves for disaster required 1.3608 billion hu—at which rice and coin would balance in value.
entries.literal: Young and strong evenly distributed, each person ate two sheng of rice daily—one million two hundred sixty thousand hu per day, four hundred fifty-three million six hundred thousand hu yearly; clothing doubled this, auspicious and inauspicious rites doubled again; leaving three years' storage against flood, drought, and disaster required one billion three hundred sixty million eight hundred thousand hu of rice; with noble and base, plenty and want balanced, then rice's value and coin would be equal.

entries.zh: 田以高下肥瘠豐耗為率，一頃出米五十餘斛，當田二千七百二十一萬六千頃。
entries.en: By field quality, one qing yielded fifty-odd hu of rice, requiring 27.216 million qing of farmland.
entries.literal: Fields were rated by elevation, fertility, and yield; one qing yielded fifty-odd hu of rice—requiring twenty-seven million two hundred sixteen thousand qing of fields.

entries.zh: 而錢亦歲毀於棺瓶埋藏焚溺，其間銅貴錢賤，有鑄以為器者，不出十年錢幾盡，不足周當世之用」。
entries.en: Coin was also lost yearly to coffins, burial, burning, and drowning; as copper grew dear and coin cheap, melting coin for vessels would exhaust the supply within a decade—insufficient for contemporary needs."
entries.literal: Yet coin was also yearly destroyed in coffins, vessels, burial, burning, and drowning; meanwhile copper was dear and coin cheap; those who cast it into vessels—within ten years coin was nearly exhausted, insufficient to meet the age's use."

entries.zh: 諸道鹽鐵轉運使劉晏以江、嶺諸州，任土所出，皆重粗賤弱之貨，輸京師不足以供道路之直。
entries.en: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan noted that Jiang and Ling prefectures produced only bulky, low-value goods whose transport to the capital could not cover shipping costs.
entries.literal: Circuit Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Liu Yan held that in Jiang and Ling prefectures, what the land produced were all heavy, crude, cheap, weak goods; delivering them to the capital was insufficient to cover transport costs.

entries.zh: 於是積之江淮，易銅鉛薪炭，廣鑄錢，歲得十餘萬緡，輸京師及荊、揚二州，自是錢日增矣。
entries.en: He stockpiled goods in Jiang-Huai, traded for copper, lead, and fuel, expanded minting, and sent over one hundred thousand strings yearly to the capital and Jing and Yang—after which the money supply steadily grew.
entries.literal: Thereupon he stockpiled in Jiang-Huai, exchanged for copper, lead, fuel, and charcoal, broadly cast coin, yearly gaining one hundred thousand-plus strings, delivered to the capital and Jing and Yang prefectures; from this coin daily increased.

entries.zh: 隋末行五銖白錢，天下盜起，私鑄錢行。
entries.en: At the end of the Sui the five-zhu white coin circulated; rebellion spread and private coinage proliferated.
entries.literal: At the end of Sui the five-zhu white coin circulated; bandits rose under Heaven and privately cast coins circulated.

entries.zh: 千錢初重二斤，其後愈輕，不及一斤，鐵葉、皮紙皆以為錢。
entries.en: A thousand coins initially weighed two jin, then grew lighter until they weighed less than one jin; iron sheets and leather tokens passed as currency.
entries.literal: One thousand coins at first weighed two jin; afterward they grew ever lighter, not reaching one jin; iron leaves and leather paper were all used as money.

entries.zh: 高祖入長安，民間行綫環錢，其製輕小，凡八九萬纔滿半斛。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, thread-ring coins circulated—so light and small that eighty or ninety thousand barely filled half a hu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, the people used thread-ring coins; they were made light and small—eighty or ninety thousand barely filled half a hu.

entries.zh: 武德四年，鑄「開元通寶」，徑八分，重二銖四參，積十錢重一兩，得輕重大小之中，其文以八分、篆、隸三體。
entries.en: In 621 the "Kaiyuan tongbao" was introduced: eight fen in diameter, two zhu four can in weight, ten coins to the liang—a balanced standard inscribed in three scripts.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, "Kaiyuan tongbao" was cast: diameter eight fen, weight two zhu four can; ten coins piled weighed one liang, attaining the mean of weight and size; the inscription used three scripts—eight-divisions, seal, and clerical.

entries.zh: 洛、幷、幽、益、桂等州皆置監。
entries.en: Mints were established at Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, Gui, and other prefectures.
entries.literal: Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, Gui, and other prefectures all set up mints.

entries.zh: 賜秦王、齊王三鑪，右僕射裴寂一鑪以鑄。
entries.en: Three furnaces were granted to the Princes of Qin and Qi, and one to Vice Director Pei Ji for minting.
entries.literal: Three furnaces were granted to the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi, and one furnace to Right Vice Director Pei Ji for casting.

entries.zh: 盜鑄者論死，沒其家屬。
entries.en: Illicit coiners faced death, and their families were confiscated into government servitude.
entries.literal: Those who minted illicitly were sentenced to death, and their family members were confiscated into servitude.

entries.zh: 其後盜鑄漸起。
entries.en: Counterfeiting gradually spread thereafter.
entries.literal: Afterward illicit casting gradually arose.

entries.zh: 先天之際，兩京錢益濫，郴、衡錢纔有輪郭，鐵錫五銖之屬皆可用之。
entries.en: Around Xiantian debasement worsened in both capitals; Chen and Heng coin barely had rims, and iron, tin, and five-zhu types all circulated.
entries.literal: At the Xiantian transition, the two capitals' coin grew ever more debased; Chen and Heng coins barely had rims; iron, tin, and five-zhu types were all usable.

entries.zh: 或鎔錫摸錢，須臾百十。
entries.en: Some melted tin and cast molds, producing dozens of coins in moments.
entries.literal: Some melted tin and molded coins—a hundred or ten in an instant.

entries.zh: 開元初，宰相宋璟請禁惡錢，行二銖四參錢，毀舊錢不可用者。
entries.en: Early in Kaiyuan Chancellor Song Jing petitioned to ban debased coin, enforce the two-zhu four-can standard, and destroy unusable old coin.
entries.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Chancellor Song Jing requested banning bad coins, circulating two-zhu four-can coin, and destroying old unusable coin.

entries.zh: 江淮有官鑪錢、偏鑪錢、稜錢、時錢，遣監察御史蕭隱之使江淮，率戶出惡錢，捕責甚峻，上青錢皆輸官，小惡者沈江湖，市井不通，物價益貴，隱之坐貶官。
entries.en: Jiang-Huai had official, private, ridged, and seasonal coin types. Censor Xiao Yinzhi was sent to compel households to surrender bad coin with harsh penalties—good coin to the state, inferior coin sunk in rivers. Markets seized up, prices rose, and Yinzhi was demoted.
entries.literal: In Jiang-Huai there were official-furnace coins, side-furnace coins, ridged coins, and seasonal coins; Censor Xiao Yinzhi was sent to Jiang-Huai to lead households in surrendering bad coins; seizure and punishment were very severe; superior green coins were all delivered to government, lesser bad ones sunk in rivers and lakes; markets did not circulate and prices grew dearer; Yinzhi was demoted for it.

entries.zh: 宋璟又請出米十萬斛收惡錢，少府毀之。
entries.en: Song Jing also proposed releasing one hundred thousand hu of grain to buy up debased coin for destruction.
entries.literal: Song Jing again requested issuing one hundred thousand hu of grain to buy bad coins; the Court Provisioner destroyed them.

entries.zh: 十一年，詔所在加鑄，禁賣銅錫及造銅器者。
entries.en: In the eleventh year an edict ordered increased minting and banned sale of copper and tin and manufacture of copper vessels.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered everywhere to increase casting and forbade selling copper and tin and making copper vessels.

entries.zh: 二十年，千錢以重六斤四兩為率，每錢重二銖四參，禁缺頓、沙澀、盪染、白彊、黑彊之錢。
entries.en: In the twentieth year one thousand coins were fixed at six jin four liang, each coin at two zhu four can, with chipped, gritty, washed, and rim-defective coins banned.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year one thousand coins were set at six jin four liang; each coin weighed two zhu four can; chipped, gritty, washed, white-rimmed, and black-rimmed coins were forbidden.

entries.zh: 首者，官為市之。
entries.en: Surrendered coin was bought by the government.
entries.literal: Those who surrendered them, the government bought them.

entries.zh: 銅一斤為錢八十。
entries.en: One jin of copper yielded eighty coins.
entries.literal: One jin of copper made eighty coins.

entries.zh: 大曆七年，禁天下鑄銅器。
entries.en: In 772 the empire banned casting copper vessels.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, casting copper vessels was forbidden under Heaven.

entries.zh: 建中初，戶部侍郎韓洄以商州紅崖冶銅多，請復洛源廢監，起十鑪，歲鑄錢七萬二千緡，每千錢費九百。
entries.en: Early in Jianzhong Vice Minister Han Hui, citing abundant copper at Shangzhou's Hongya, petitioned to reopen the abandoned Luoyuan mint with ten furnaces producing 72,000 strings a year at nine hundred cash per thousand.
entries.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Vice Minister Han Hui, because Shangzhou's Hongya smelted much copper, requested restoring the abandoned Luoyuan mint, raising ten furnaces, yearly casting seventy-two thousand strings, each thousand coins costing nine hundred to produce.

entries.zh: 德宗從之。
entries.en: Dezong approved.
entries.literal: Dezong followed it.

entries.zh: 唐有鹽池十八，井六百四十，皆隸度支。
entries.en: Under the Tang there were eighteen salt ponds and six hundred forty salt wells, all administered by the Department of Expenditure.
entries.literal: The Tang had eighteen salt ponds and six hundred forty wells; all were subordinate to the Department of Expenditure.

entries.zh: 蒲州安邑、解縣有池五，總曰「兩池」，歲得鹽萬斛，以供京師。
entries.en: In Puzhou, Anyi and Jie counties together had five ponds known as the "Two Ponds," which produced ten thousand hu of salt a year for the capital.
entries.literal: At Anyi and Jie counties in Puzhou there were five ponds, together called the "Two Ponds"; each year they yielded ten thousand hu of salt to supply the capital.

entries.zh: 鹽州五原有烏池、白池、瓦池、細項池，靈州有溫泉池、兩井池、長尾池、五泉池、紅桃池、回樂池、弘靜池、會州有河池，三州皆輸米以代鹽。
entries.en: Yanzhou's Wuyuan had the Wu, Bai, Wa, and Xixiang ponds; Lingzhou had the Wenquan, Liangjing, Changwei, Wuquan, Hongtao, Huile, and Hongjing ponds; Huizhou had the He pond. These three prefectures all paid grain in place of salt tribute.
entries.literal: At Wuyuan in Yanzhou were the Wu, Bai, Wa, and Xixiang ponds; at Lingzhou were the Wenquan, Liangjing, Changwei, Wuquan, Hongtao, Huile, and Hongjing ponds; at Huizhou was the He pond. All three prefectures paid grain in lieu of salt.

entries.zh: 安北都護府有胡落池，歲得鹽萬四千斛，以給振武、天德。
entries.en: The Anbei Protectorate had the Huluo salt pond, which yielded fourteen thousand hu a year to supply the Zhenwu and Tiande garrisons.
entries.literal: The Protectorate General of the Pacified North had the Huluo pond, yielding fourteen thousand hu of salt yearly to supply Zhenwu and Tiande.

entries.zh: 黔州有井四十一，成州、巂州井各一，果、閬、開、通井百二十三，山南西院領之。
entries.en: Qianzhou had forty-one salt wells, Chengzhou and Xizhou one each, and Guo, Lang, Kai, and Tong one hundred twenty-three together—all under the Shannan West salt office.
entries.literal: Qianzhou had forty-one wells; Chengzhou and Xizhou each had one; Guo, Lang, Kai, and Tong had one hundred twenty-three wells together, overseen by the Shannan West Circuit office.

entries.zh: 邛、眉、嘉有井十三，劍南西川院領之。
entries.en: Qiong, Mei, and Jia together had thirteen wells, administered by the Jiannan West salt office.
entries.literal: Qiong, Mei, and Jia had thirteen wells, overseen by the Jiannan West Circuit office.

entries.zh: 梓、遂、緜、合、昌、渝、瀘、資、榮、陵、簡有井四百六十，劍南東川院領之。
entries.en: Zi, Sui, Mian, He, Chang, Yu, Lu, Zi, Rong, Ling, and Jian had four hundred sixty wells between them, under the Jiannan East salt office.
entries.literal: Zi, Sui, Mian, He, Chang, Yu, Lu, Zi, Rong, Ling, and Jian had four hundred sixty wells, overseen by the Jiannan East Circuit office.

entries.zh: 皆隨月督課。
entries.en: Production at all of these sites was assessed and collected on a monthly schedule.
entries.literal: All were supervised for production quotas month by month.

entries.zh: 幽州、大同橫野軍有鹽屯，每屯有丁有兵，歲得鹽二千八百斛，下者千五百斛。
entries.en: Youzhou and the Datong Hengye Army maintained salt colonies staffed by laborers and soldiers, with annual yields ranging from fifteen hundred to twenty-eight hundred hu.
entries.literal: Youzhou and the Datong Hengye Army had salt colonies; each colony had laborers and troops, yielding twenty-eight hundred hu yearly at the top and fifteen hundred at the bottom.

entries.zh: 負海州歲免租為鹽二萬斛以輸司農。
entries.en: Coastal prefectures delivered twenty thousand hu of salt a year to the Court of Imperial Granaries in lieu of land tax.
entries.literal: Coastal prefectures had their annual land tax remitted in return for delivering twenty thousand hu of salt to the Court of Imperial Granaries.

entries.zh: 青、楚、海、滄、棣、杭、蘇等州，以鹽價市輕貨，亦輸司農。
entries.en: Qing, Chu, Hai, Cang, Di, Hang, Su, and other prefectures used salt proceeds to buy light goods, which they also delivered to the Court of Imperial Granaries.
entries.literal: Qing, Chu, Hai, Cang, Di, Hang, Su, and other prefectures used salt revenues to purchase light goods, which were also delivered to the Court of Imperial Granaries.

entries.zh: 唐興，高祖入京師，約法十二條，惟殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛逆者死。
entries.en: When the Tang rose, Gaozu entered the capital and proclaimed a twelve-article compact: only murder, robbery, desertion, and treason were capital crimes.
entries.literal: When the Tang arose, Gaozu entered the capital and made a compact law of twelve articles; only for murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion was death imposed.

entries.zh: 及受禪，命納言劉文靜等損益律令。
entries.en: After he accepted the abdication, he ordered Palace Counselor Liu Wenjing and others to revise the code and ordinances.
entries.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered the Palace Counselor Liu Wenjing and others to revise the code and ordinances.

entries.zh: 武德二年，頒新格五十三條，唯吏受賕、犯盜、詐冒府庫物，赦不原。
entries.en: In Wude 2, fifty-three new administrative rules were issued; only bribery by officials, theft, and fraud involving government storehouses were excluded from amnesty.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wude, fifty-three new administrative rules were promulgated; only for officials receiving bribes, committing theft, and fraudulently taking goods from government storehouses was amnesty not granted.

entries.zh: 凡斷屠日及正月、五月、九月不行刑。
entries.en: Executions were suspended on meat-abstention days and in the first, fifth, and ninth months.
entries.literal: On all days when slaughter was forbidden, and in the first, fifth, and ninth months, punishments were not carried out.

entries.zh: 四年，高祖躬錄囚徒，以人因亂冒法者眾，盜非劫傷其主及征人逃亡、官吏枉法，皆原之。
entries.en: In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned theft that was not robbery injuring the owner, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted the law.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners; because many people in the chaos had violated the law, for theft that was not robbery injuring the owner, and for conscripts who fled and officials who perverted the law, all were pardoned.

entries.zh: 已而又詔僕射裴寂等十五人更撰律令，凡律五百，麗以五十三條。
entries.en: He then ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and fourteen others to draft a new code and ordinances: five hundred articles of code, supplemented by fifty-three additional provisions.
entries.literal: Afterward he again ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and others, fifteen persons in all, to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.

entries.zh: 流罪三，皆加千里；
entries.en: All three grades of exile were increased by one thousand li.
entries.literal: The three grades of exile were all increased by one thousand li.

entries.zh: 居作三歲至二歲半者悉為一歲。
entries.en: Terms of compulsory labor from three years down to two and a half were all reduced to one year.
entries.literal: Terms of labor service from three years down to two and a half years were all made one year.

entries.zh: 餘無改焉。
entries.en: Otherwise nothing was changed.
entries.literal: The rest was unchanged.

entries.zh: 廣州都督瓽仁弘嘗率鄉兵二千助高祖起，封長沙郡公。
entries.en: Tan Renhong, area commander of Guangzhou, had once raised two thousand local troops to aid Gaozu in his founding struggle and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha.
entries.literal: The Area Commander of Guangzhou, Tan Renhong, had once led two thousand local troops to help Gaozu rise, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha Commandery.

entries.zh: 仁弘交通豪酋，納金寶，沒降獠為奴婢，又擅賦夷人。
entries.en: Ren Hong colluded with tribal chieftains, accepted bribes of gold and jewels, enslaved surrendered Lao people, and unlawfully imposed levies on frontier tribes.
entries.literal: Ren Hong colluded with powerful chieftains, accepted gold and treasures, seized surrendered Lao as slaves, and also levied taxes on his own authority from the barbarian peoples.

entries.zh: 既還，有舟七十。
entries.en: On his return, he sailed home with seventy boatloads.
entries.literal: When he returned, he had seventy boats.

entries.zh: 或告其贓，法當死。
entries.en: When someone reported his graft, the law called for execution.
entries.literal: Someone reported his corruption; by law he deserved death.

entries.zh: 帝哀其老且有功，因貸為庶人，乃召五品以上，謂曰：「賞罰所以代天行法，今朕寬仁弘死，是自弄法以負天也。
entries.en: The emperor, pitying his age and past service, commuted his sentence to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Rewards and punishments are how the throne carries out Heaven's law. By sparing Ren Hong from death I am twisting the law and failing Heaven.
entries.literal: The emperor, pitying his age and merit, commuted his sentence to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Rewards and punishments are how one executes the law on Heaven's behalf. Now in sparing Ren Hong from death I am manipulating the law and failing Heaven.

entries.zh: 人臣有過，請罪於君，君有過，宜請罪於天。
entries.en: When a minister errs, he confesses to his sovereign; when the sovereign errs, he ought to confess to Heaven.
entries.literal: When ministers err, they beg forgiveness from their lord; when the lord errs, he ought to beg forgiveness from Heaven.

entries.zh: 其令有司設藳席于南郊三日，朕將請罪。」
entries.en: Have the officials lay out a straw mat in the southern suburbs for three days—I shall go there to confess."
entries.literal: Let the officials set out a straw mat in the southern suburbs for three days—I shall beg forgiveness."

entries.zh: 房玄齡等曰：「寬仁弘不以私而以功，何罪之請？」
entries.en: Fang Xuanling and others said: "You spared Ren Hong not from private favor but for his merit—what offense requires confession?"
entries.literal: Fang Xuanling and others said: "In sparing Ren Hong you acted not from private favor but from his merit—what crime is there to confess?"

entries.zh: 百僚頓首三請，乃止。
entries.en: The assembled officials kowtowed three times in entreaty, and he relented.
entries.literal: The hundred officials bowed their heads three times in entreaty, and he desisted.

entries.zh: 高宗既昏懦，而繼以武氏之亂，毒流天下，幾至於亡。
entries.en: Gaozong was weak and indecisive, and the Wu clan's turmoil followed; cruelty spread through the realm and the dynasty nearly perished.
entries.literal: Gaozong was both muddled and weak, and the Wu clan's turmoil followed; poison spread through the realm and the dynasty nearly perished.

entries.zh: 自永徽以後，武氏已得志，而刑濫矣。
entries.en: From the Yonghui era onward the Wu clan had already seized power, and punishments grew excessive.
entries.literal: From the Yonghui era onward, the Wu clan had already realized its ambitions, and punishments grew excessive.

entries.zh: 當時大獄，以尚書刑部、御史臺、大理寺雜按，謂之「三司」，而法吏以慘酷為能，至不釋枷而笞棰以死者，皆不禁。
entries.en: Major cases were jointly tried by the Ministry of Justice, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review—a procedure called the "Three Offices." Magistrates competed in brutality; even beating prisoners to death without removing their cangues went unpunished.
entries.literal: At the time major cases were jointly investigated by the Ministry of Justice within the Ministry of State Affairs, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review—called the "Three Offices." Legal clerks took brutal cruelty as merit; even those beaten to death without removing the cangue went unchecked.

entries.zh: 律有杖百，凡五十九條，犯者或至死而杖未畢，乃詔除其四十九條，然無益也。
entries.en: The Code prescribed one hundred blows in fifty-nine articles; offenders sometimes died before the beating was finished. An edict then struck forty-nine of those articles, yet it did no good.
entries.literal: The Code provided for one hundred blows in fifty-nine articles all told; offenders sometimes died before the full count was delivered. An edict then abolished forty-nine of those articles, yet to no avail.

entries.zh: 武后已稱制，懼天下不服，欲制以威，乃修後周告密之法，詔官司受訊，有言密事者，馳驛奏之。
entries.en: Empress Wu had already assumed regency, feared the realm would not submit, and sought to rule through terror.
