She revived the Later Zhou system of secret denunciation, decreeing that when offices received interrogations and anyone reported confidential matters, they were to dispatch fast relay to the throne.
entries.literal: Empress Wu had already assumed regency, feared the realm would not submit, and wished to control it through terror. She restored the Later Zhou system of informing on secrets, decreeing that when offices received interrogations and anyone spoke of confidential matters, they were to dispatch fast relay to report it.

entries.zh: 自徐敬業、越王貞、琅邪王沖等起兵討亂，武氏益恐。
entries.en: After Xu Jingye, Zhen the Prince of Yue, Chong the Prince of Langye, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
entries.literal: After Xu Jingye, the Prince of Yue Zhen, the Prince of Langye Chong, and others raised armies to suppress the turmoil, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.

entries.zh: 乃引酷吏周興、來俊臣輩典大獄，與侯思止、王弘義、郭弘霸、李敬仁、康暐、衞遂忠等集告事數百人，共為羅織，構陷無辜。
entries.en: She then put cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen in charge of major cases. With Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others, they assembled several hundred informants to weave false charges and frame the innocent.
entries.literal: She then brought in cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their like to handle major cases, and together with Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others gathered several hundred informants to entrap and frame the innocent through fabricated charges.

entries.zh: 自唐之宗室與朝廷之士，日被告捕，不可勝數，天下之人，為之仄足，如狄仁傑、魏元忠等皆幾不免。
entries.en: From imperial clansmen to court officials, denunciations and arrests came daily beyond counting. People everywhere lived in dread; even men like Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong barely escaped ruin.
entries.literal: From Tang imperial clansmen to court officials, daily denunciations and arrests were more than could be counted. People throughout the realm walked on tiptoe in fear; even men like Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong barely escaped harm.

entries.zh: 左臺御史周矩上疏曰：「比姦憸告訐，習以為常。
entries.en: Left Platform Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Lately treacherous accusations and denunciations have become routine.
entries.literal: Left Platform Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Recently treacherous accusations and denunciations have become habitual.

entries.zh: 推劾之吏，以深刻為功，鑿空爭能，相矜以虐。
entries.en: Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each vaunting cruelty.
entries.literal: Interrogating officers take harsh severity as merit, contriving charges from nothing to compete in ability, each praising the other's cruelty.

entries.zh: 泥耳囊頭，摺脅籤爪，縣髮燻耳，臥鄰穢溺，刻害支體，糜爛獄中，號曰『獄持』；
entries.en: They pack the ears and bag the head, fold the armpits and prick the fingernails, suspend the hair and smoke the ears, force prisoners to lie beside filth and urine, and mutilate the limbs until flesh rots in the cell—they call this "prison holding."
entries.literal: Packing the ears and bagging the head, folding the armpits and pricking the fingernails, suspending the hair and smoking the ears, making prisoners lie beside filth and urine, carving and maiming the limbs until they putrefy in prison—they call this 'prison holding.'

entries.zh: 閉絕食飲，晝夜使不得眠，號曰『宿囚』。
entries.en: They cut off food and drink and keep prisoners from sleep day and night—they call this "overnight detention."
entries.literal: Cutting off food and drink, keeping prisoners from sleep day and night—they call this 'overnight detention.'

entries.zh: 殘賊威暴，取快目前。
entries.en: They mutilate, brutalize, and terrorize for immediate gratification.
entries.literal: They mutilate, savage, and terrorize for immediate gratification.

entries.zh: 被誣者苟求得死，何所不至？
entries.en: Those falsely accused, if only to obtain death—what would they not confess?
entries.literal: Those falsely accused, if only to obtain death—what would they not do?

entries.zh: 為國者以仁為宗，以刑為助，周用仁而昌，秦用刑而亡。
entries.en: Those who govern a state take benevolence as their foundation and punishment as their support. Zhou relied on benevolence and flourished; Qin relied on punishment and perished.
entries.literal: Those who govern a state take benevolence as their foundation and punishment as their aid. Zhou employed benevolence and flourished; Qin employed punishment and perished.

entries.zh: 願陛下緩刑用仁，天下幸甚！」
entries.en: I pray Your Majesty will ease punishments and govern with benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!"
entries.literal: I pray Your Majesty will relax punishments and employ benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!"

entries.zh: 武后不納。
entries.en: Empress Wu did not accept it.
entries.literal: Empress Wu did not accept it.

entries.zh: 麟臺正字陳子昂亦上書切諫，不省。
entries.en: Palace Library corrector Chen Zi'ang also submitted a forceful remonstrance, which went unheeded.
entries.literal: Palace Library Corrector Chen Zi'ang also submitted a forceful remonstrance, which went unheeded.

entries.zh: 及周興、來俊臣等誅死，后亦老，其意少衰，而狄仁傑、姚崇、宋璟、王及善相與論垂拱以來酷濫之冤，太后感寤，由是不復殺戮。
entries.en: After Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were executed, the Empress had also grown old and her zeal somewhat faded. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together discussed the cruel excesses and wrongful convictions since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved, and from then on she no longer carried out mass killings.
entries.literal: After Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were executed, the Empress had also grown old and her intent somewhat waned. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together discussed the cruel excesses and injustices since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved to understanding, and from then on she no longer carried out slaughter.

entries.zh: 然其毒虐所被，自古未之有也。
entries.en: Yet the poison and cruelty that had spread were unmatched since antiquity.
entries.literal: Yet the poison and cruelty that had spread were unmatched since antiquity.

entries.zh: 大足元年，乃詔法司及推事使敢多作辯狀而加語者，以故入論。
entries.en: In Dazu 1, an edict declared that legal offices and special investigatory commissioners who dared to compose lengthy written defenses and add fabricated language would be prosecuted for deliberate misjudgment.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dazu, an edict declared that legal offices and special investigatory commissioners who dared to compose lengthy written defenses and add fabricated language would be prosecuted for deliberate misjudgment.

entries.zh: 中宗、韋后繼以亂敗。
entries.en: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed with disorder and ruin.
entries.literal: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed with disorder and ruin.

entries.zh: 穆宗童昏，然頗知慎刑法，每有司斷大獄，令中書舍人一人參酌而輕重之，號「參酌院」。
entries.en: Muzong was immature and dull-witted, yet he was fairly conscientious about penal law. Whenever responsible offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to review and adjust the severity of sentences—an office called the "Review and Deliberation Office."
entries.literal: Muzong was childish and dull-witted, yet he was fairly mindful in applying penal law. Whenever the responsible offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to review and adjust severity, called the "Review and Deliberation Office."

entries.zh: 大理少卿崔𣏌奏曰：「國家法度，高祖、太宗定制二百餘年矣。
entries.en: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Yuan memorialized: "The state's laws and institutions were established by Gaozu and Taizong more than two hundred years ago.
entries.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Yuan memorialized: "The state's laws and institutions were established by Gaozu and Taizong more than two hundred years ago.

entries.zh: 周禮正月布刑，張之門閭及都鄙邦國，所以屢丁寧，使四方謹行之。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe that in the first month punishments are promulgated and posted at gates and lanes, in districts and prefectures, and throughout the realm—all to repeat admonitions and ensure the four quarters carefully observe them.
entries.literal: The Rites of Zhou state that in the first month punishments are promulgated and posted at gates and lanes, in districts and prefectures, and in the states—all to repeat admonitions and make the four quarters carefully observe them.

entries.zh: 大理寺，陛下守法之司也。
entries.en: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.
entries.literal: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.

entries.zh: 今別設參酌之官，有司定罪，乃議其出入，是與奪繫於人情，而法官不得守其職。
entries.en: Now a separate office of review and deliberation has been established: after the responsible offices determine guilt, it revises the sentence up or down—so that life and death depend on personal sentiment and judicial officers cannot perform their duties.
entries.literal: Now a separate Review and Deliberation office has been established; after the responsible offices fix guilt, it deliberates increase or decrease—life and death depend on personal sentiment, and judicial officers cannot perform their duties.

entries.zh: 昔子路問政，孔子曰：『必也正名乎。』
entries.en: Formerly Zilu asked about governance, and Confucius said, 'What is necessary is to rectify names.'
entries.literal: Formerly Zilu asked about governance, and Confucius said: 'What is necessary is to rectify names.'

entries.zh: 臣以為參酌之名不正，宜廢。」
entries.en: Your subject holds that the name 'Review and Deliberation' is improper and should be abolished."
entries.literal: Your subject holds that the name 'Review and Deliberation' is not correct and should be abolished."

entries.zh: 乃罷之。
entries.en: The office was then abolished.
entries.literal: The office was then abolished.

entries.zh: 蓋自高祖、太宗除隋虐亂，治以寬平，民樂其安，重於犯法，致治之美，幾乎三代之盛時。
entries.en: From Gaozu and Taizong's removal of Sui cruelty and disorder, their lenient and moderate governance made the people secure and wary of breaking the law—their achievement in good governance nearly matched the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.
entries.literal: From Gaozu and Taizong's removal of Sui cruelty and disorder, governing with leniency and moderation, the people rejoiced in their security and feared to break the law—the beauty of good governance nearly matched the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.

entries.zh: 考其推心惻物，其可謂仁矣！
entries.en: Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for others, they may truly be called benevolent!
entries.literal: Considering their putting heart into things and compassion for others, they may be called benevolent!

entries.zh: 自高宗、武后以來，毒流邦家，唐祚絕而復續。
entries.en: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the realm; the Tang mandate was severed and then renewed.
entries.literal: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the realm; Tang's mandate was severed and then renewed.

entries.zh: 玄宗初勵精為政，二十年間，刑獄減省，歲斷死罪纔五十八人。
entries.en: At first Xuanzong exerted himself in governance; within twenty years criminal cases were reduced, and yearly death sentences amounted to only fifty-eight.
entries.literal: At first Xuanzong exerted himself in governance; within twenty years criminal cases were reduced, and death sentences adjudicated yearly amounted to only fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 以此見致治雖難，勉之則易，未有為而不至者。
entries.en: From this one sees that achieving good governance, though difficult, becomes easy with effort—nothing attempted with diligence fails to succeed.
entries.literal: From this one sees that achieving good governance, though difficult, becomes easy with effort—nothing attempted fails to succeed.

entries.zh: 自此以後，兵革遂興，國家多故，而人主規規，無復太宗之志。
entries.en: From this time onward warfare arose and the state faced many troubles; sovereigns grew petty-minded and no longer possessed Taizong's aspiration.
entries.literal: From this time onward warfare arose, the state faced many troubles, and sovereigns were petty-minded, no longer possessing Taizong's aspiration.

entries.zh: 其雖有心於治者，亦不能講考大法，而性有寬猛，凡所更革，一切臨時苟且，或重或輕，徒為繁文，不足以示後世。
entries.en: Even those with some desire to govern well could not examine and apply the great law; with natures ranging from lenient to severe, all their reforms were temporary expedients—sometimes harsh, sometimes lenient—empty formalities that could not instruct posterity.
entries.literal: Even those with some mind for governance could not examine and apply the great law; their natures had leniency and severity; all reforms were mere temporary expedients, sometimes heavy, sometimes light—empty formalities insufficient to instruct posterity.

entries.zh: 而高祖、太宗之法，僅守而存。
entries.en: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were barely preserved.
entries.literal: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were barely preserved and kept in existence.

entries.zh: 故自肅宗以來，所可書者幾希矣；
entries.en: Thus from Suzong onward, almost nothing worth recording remained;
entries.literal: Thus from Suzong onward, what could be recorded was almost nothing;

entries.zh: 懿宗以後，無所稱焉。
entries.en: After Yizong, there was nothing worth praising.
entries.literal: After Yizong, there was nothing to praise.

entries.zh: 武宗用李德裕誅劉稹等，大刑舉矣，而性嚴刻。
entries.en: Wuzong, relying on Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; harsh punishments were fully applied, and his nature was stern and harsh.
entries.literal: Wuzong, using Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; great punishments were carried out, and his nature was stern and harsh.

entries.zh: 故時，竊盜無死，所以原民情迫於飢寒也，至是贓滿千錢者死，至宣宗乃罷之。
entries.en: Formerly petty theft did not incur the death penalty, forgiving the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of goods worth a thousand cash brought death—a policy not abolished until Xuanzong's reign.
entries.literal: Formerly petty theft incurred no death penalty—this was to forgive the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of goods worth a thousand cash incurred death; this was not abolished until Xuanzong.

entries.zh: 而宣宗亦自喜刑名，常曰：「犯我法，雖子弟不宥也。」
entries.en: Xuanzong also delighted in penal law and often said, "Whoever violates my law shall not be pardoned, even if he is my own kin."
entries.literal: Xuanzong also delighted in penal law and often said: "Whoever violates my law, even if kin, shall not be pardoned."

entries.zh: 然少仁恩，唐德自是衰矣。
entries.en: Yet he lacked benevolence and grace, and from this Tang virtue declined.
entries.literal: Yet he lacked benevolence and grace; from this Tang virtue declined.

entries.zh: 古之為國者，議事以制，不為刑辟，懼民之知爭端也。
entries.en: In ancient times, rulers governed by deliberating on affairs to set policy, not by drafting penal codes—they feared teaching the people where disputes might arise.
entries.literal: In antiquity those who governed states deliberated on affairs to establish regulation, and did not create penal statutes, fearing that the people would learn the points of contention.

entries.zh: 後世作為刑書，惟恐不備，俾民之知所避也。
entries.en: Later generations wrote penal statutes and worried only that they might be incomplete, so that the people would know what to shun.
entries.literal: Later ages composed penal books, fearing only that they might be incomplete, so as to enable the people to know what to avoid.

entries.zh: 其為法雖殊，而用心則一，蓋皆欲民之無犯也。
entries.en: Though their legal methods differed, their aim was the same: to keep the people from breaking the law.
entries.literal: Although their methods of law differed, their intent was one: all wished that the people would not offend.

entries.zh: 然未知夫導之以德、齊之以禮，而可使民遷善遠罪而不自知也。
entries.en: They did not yet understand that guiding the people with virtue and harmonizing them through ritual could move them toward goodness and away from crime almost without their noticing.
entries.literal: Yet they did not know that guiding them with virtue and regulating them with ritual could cause the people to turn toward goodness and keep away from crime without their knowing it.

entries.zh: 886 二年 義成軍節度使改為宣義軍節度使，朱全忠請改，以避其父名。
entries.en: In 886, the second year of Guangqi, the Yicheng Army military commissioner was redesignated the Xuanyi Army military commissioner at Zhu Quanzhong's request, to avoid his father's name.
entries.literal: 886, second year. The Yicheng Army military commissioner was changed to the Xuanyi Army military commissioner; Zhu Quanzhong requested the change to avoid his father's name.

entries.zh: 表第五 方鎮表二
entries.en: Table 5: Military Commanderies, Part Two.
entries.literal: Table 5, Military Commanderies Table 2.

entries.zh: 昔者周有天下，封國七十，而同姓居五十三焉，後世不以為私也，蓋所以隆本支，崇屏衞。
entries.en: In ancient times, when the Zhou held the realm, they enfeoffed seventy states, fifty-three of them bearing the royal surname. Later ages did not see this as mere favoritism; it was meant to exalt the trunk line and strengthen the shielding branches.
entries.literal: In antiquity Zhou possessed All-under-Heaven, enfeoffed seventy states, and those of the same surname numbered fifty-three; later generations did not regard this as selfishness—rather it was to elevate the root branches and honor the protective screens.

entries.zh: 雖其弊也，以侵凌王室，有末大之患，然亦崇奬扶持，猶四百餘年而後亡，蓋其德與力皆不足矣，而其勢或然也。
entries.en: The system had its flaw: the enfeoffed kin could encroach on the throne and bring the peril of branches outgrowing the trunk. Yet they were still honored and sustained, and the dynasty endured more than four centuries before collapse—perhaps because virtue and power alike were wanting, or because circumstances simply ran that course.
entries.literal: Although its defect was encroaching upon and oppressing the royal house, with the calamity of the branch outweighing the root, yet they were also honored, encouraged, and supported, and still did not perish until more than four hundred years later—presumably their virtue and strength were both insufficient, and their circumstances may have been so.

entries.zh: 至漢鑒秦，務廣宗室，世其國地，不幸世絕若罪除，輒復續以存其祭祀，與為長久之計，故自三代以來，獨漢為長世。
entries.en: Learning from Qin's fall, Han worked to enlarge the imperial clan and make their domains hereditary. When a line died out, once any guilt was cleared the fief was promptly restored so sacrifices could continue—a policy aimed at longevity. Since the Three Dynasties, only Han has enjoyed such enduring rule.
entries.literal: When Han took Qin as its mirror, it strove to expand the imperial clan, making their fiefs hereditary; if a line unfortunately died out, once guilt was cleared it was promptly revived to preserve their sacrifices—a plan for long endurance—so since the Three Dynasties, Han alone has been long-lived.

entries.zh: 唐有天下三百年，子孫蕃衍，可謂盛矣！
entries.en: Tang ruled the realm for three hundred years, and its descendants multiplied prodigiously—a flourishing house indeed!
entries.literal: Tang held All-under-Heaven for three hundred years; its descendants multiplied—one may call this flourishing!

entries.zh: 其初皆有封爵，至其世遠親盡，則各隨其人賢愚，遂與異姓之臣雜而仕宦，至或流落於民間，甚可歎也！
entries.en: At first they all held titles and fiefs, but as generations passed and kinship thinned, each rose or fell on personal merit or folly. They mingled with officials of other surnames in office, and some even sank into common life—a cause for deep regret!
entries.literal: At first all had enfeoffments and ranks; when generations grew distant and kinship ties were exhausted, each followed the worth or folly of the individual, and thus mixed with officials of other surnames in government service—even sinking to life among the common people, which is deeply lamentable!

entries.zh: 然其疏戚遠近，源流所來，可以考見，作宗室世系表。
entries.en: Still, the degrees of kinship and the lines of descent can be traced, and so the Genealogical Tables of the Imperial Clan are presented here.
entries.literal: Yet the degrees of kinship, near and far, and the sources from which they flowed can be examined and seen; therefore the Genealogical Tables of the Imperial Clan are compiled.

entries.zh: 序李氏出自嬴姓。
entries.en: Preface: The Li clan traces its origin to the Ying surname.
entries.literal: Preface: The Li clan issued from the Ying surname.

entries.zh: 帝顓頊高陽氏生大業，大業生女華，女華生皐陶，字庭堅，為堯大理。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang line had Daye; Daye had Nühua; and Nühua had Gao Yao, styled Tingjian, who served Emperor Yao as Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuanxu of the Gaoyang clan begot Daye; Daye begot Nühua; Nühua begot Gao Yao, styled Tingjian, who served Yao as Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 生益，益生恩成，歷虞、夏、商，世為大理，以官命族為理氏。
entries.en: Gao Yao's line continued through Yi and Encheng. Under Yu, Xia, and Shang they held the post of Minister of Justice for generations, and the clan took the name Li ('minister of justice') from that office.
entries.literal: He begot Yi; Yi begot Encheng; through Yu, Xia, and Shang they generation after generation served as Ministers of Justice, and taking the office as their clan name they became the Li clan.

entries.zh: 至紂之時，理徵字德靈，為翼隸中吳伯，以直道不容於紂，得罪而死。
entries.en: Under King Zhou of Shang, Li Zheng, styled Deling, was Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou. His upright conduct won no favor with Zhou, and he was put to death for his offense.
entries.literal: At the time of Zhou, Li Zheng, styled Deling, was Earl of Zhongwu in Yizhou; because his upright conduct was not tolerated by Zhou, he offended and died.

entries.zh: 其妻陳國契和氏與子利貞逃難於伊侯之墟，食木子得全，遂改理為李氏。
entries.en: His wife Lady Qihe of Chen and their son Lizhen fled to the ruins of the Marquis of Yi. They survived by eating the fruit of a tree and changed the clan name from Li (minister of justice) to Li (plum tree).
entries.literal: His wife, Lady Qihe of Chen, and his son Lizhen fled in distress to the ruins of the Marquis of Yi; eating the fruit of a tree they were preserved whole, and thus changed Li to the Li clan.

entries.zh: 利貞亦娶契和氏女，生昌祖，為陳大夫，家于苦縣。
entries.en: Lizhen married a daughter of the Qihe clan as well and had Changzu, who became a grandee of Chen and settled the family in Ku County.
entries.literal: Lizhen also married a daughter of the Qihe clan and begot Changzu, who became a grandee of Chen and made his home in Ku County.

entries.zh: 生彤德，彤德曾孫碩宗，周康王賜采邑於苦縣。
entries.en: Changzu's line ran through Tongde to Shuozong, a great-grandson of Tongde, to whom King Kang of Zhou granted a fief in Ku County.
entries.literal: He begot Tongde; Tongde's great-grandson Shuozong received from King Kang of Zhou a fief in Ku County.

entries.zh: 五世孫乾，字元果，為周上御史大夫，娶益壽氏女嬰敷，生耳，字伯陽，一字聃，周平王時為太史。
entries.en: Five generations later came Qian, styled Yuanguo, Senior Censor-in-Chief of Zhou. He married Yingfu of the Yishou clan and had Er, styled Boyang, also called Dan, who served as Grand Astrologer under King Ping of Zhou.
entries.literal: The fifth-generation descendant Qian, styled Yuanguo, was Senior Censor-in-Chief of Zhou; he married Yingfu, daughter of the Yishou clan, and begot Er, styled Boyang, also known as Dan, who in the time of King Ping of Zhou was Grand Astrologer.

entries.zh: 其後有李宗，字尊祖，魏封於段，為干木大夫。
entries.en: Later in the line came Li Zong, styled Zunzu, enfeoffed at Duan by Wei and made Grandee of Ganmu.
entries.literal: Later there was Li Zong, styled Zunzu, enfeoffed in Duan by Wei and made Grandee of Ganmu.

entries.zh: 生同，為趙大將軍。
entries.en: He had a son Tong, who became Grand General of Zhao.
entries.literal: He begot Tong, who became Grand General of Zhao.

entries.zh: 生兌，為趙相。
entries.en: He had a son Dui, who became Chancellor of Zhao.
entries.literal: He begot Dui, who became Chancellor of Zhao.

entries.zh: 生躋，趙陽安君。
entries.en: He had a son Ji, Lord of Yang'an in Zhao.
entries.literal: He begot Ji, Lord of Yang'an in Zhao.

entries.zh: 二子：曰雲，曰恪。
entries.en: He had two sons: Yun and Ke.
entries.literal: Two sons: named Yun and named Ke.

entries.zh: 恪生洪，字道弘，秦太子太傅。
entries.en: Ke's son Hong, styled Daohong, was Tutor to the Crown Prince of Qin.
entries.literal: Ke begot Hong, styled Daohong, Tutor to the Crown Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 生興族，字育神，一名汪，秦將軍。
entries.en: He had Xingzu, styled Yushen, also known as Wang, a general of Qin.
entries.literal: He begot Xingzu, styled Yushen, also called Wang, a general of Qin.

entries.zh: 生曇，字貴遠，趙柏人侯，入秦為御史大夫，葬柏人西。
entries.en: He had Tan, styled Guiyuan, Marquis of Bairen in Zhao. After entering Qin service he became Censor-in-Chief and was buried west of Bairen.
entries.literal: He begot Tan, styled Guiyuan, Marquis of Bairen in Zhao; entering Qin he became Censor-in-Chief and was buried west of Bairen.

entries.zh: 生四子：崇、辨、昭、璣。
entries.en: He had four sons: Chong, Bian, Zhao, and Ji.
entries.literal: He begot four sons: Chong, Bian, Zhao, and Ji.

entries.zh: 崇為隴西房，璣為趙郡房。
entries.en: Chong founded the Longxi branch of the clan; Ji founded the Zhao commandery branch.
entries.literal: Chong was the founder of the Longxi branch; Ji was the founder of the Zhao commandery branch.

entries.zh: 崇字伯祐，隴西守、南鄭公。
entries.en: Chong, styled Boyou, served as Administrator of Longxi and was made Duke of Nanzheng.
entries.literal: Chong, styled Boyou, was Administrator of Longxi and Duke of Nanzheng.

entries.zh: 生二子：長曰平燕；
entries.en: He had two sons: the elder, Pingyan;
entries.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Pingyan;

entries.zh: 次曰瑤，字內德，南郡守、狄道侯。
entries.en: and the younger, Yao, styled Neide, Administrator of Nan commandery and Marquis of Didao.
entries.literal: the younger named Yao, styled Neide, Administrator of Nan commandery and Marquis of Didao.

entries.zh: 生信，字有成，大將軍、隴西侯。
entries.en: Yao's son Xin, styled Youcheng, was Grand General and Marquis of Longxi.
entries.literal: He begot Xin, styled Youcheng, Grand General and Marquis of Longxi.

entries.zh: 生超，一名伉，字仁高，漢大將軍、漁陽太守。
entries.en: He had Chao, also called Kang, styled Rengao, a Han Grand General and Administrator of Yuyang.
entries.literal: He begot Chao, also called Kang, styled Rengao, Grand General of Han and Administrator of Yuyang.

entries.zh: 生二子：長曰元曠，侍中；
entries.en: He had two sons: the elder, Yuankuang, Attendant-in-Ordinary;
entries.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Yuankuang, Attendant-in-Ordinary;

entries.zh: 次曰仲翔，河東太守、征西將軍，討叛羌于素昌，戰沒，贈太尉，葬隴西狄道東川，因家焉。
entries.en: and the younger, Zhongxiang, Administrator of Hedong and General Who Pacifies the West. He campaigned against rebellious Qiang at Suchang, fell in battle, and was posthumously made Grand Commandant. He was buried in the eastern ravine of Didao in Longxi, where the family then settled.
entries.literal: the younger named Zhongxiang, Administrator of Hedong and General Who Pacifies the West; campaigning against rebellious Qiang at Suchang he died in battle; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant; buried in the eastern ravine of Didao in Longxi, and the family settled there.

entries.zh: 生伯考，隴西、河東二郡太守。
entries.en: He had Bokao, who served as Administrator of both Longxi and Hedong.
entries.literal: He begot Bokao, Administrator of both Longxi and Hedong commanderies.

entries.zh: 生尚，成紀令，因居成紀。
entries.en: He had Shang, Magistrate of Chengji, and the family came to reside there.
entries.literal: He begot Shang, Magistrate of Chengji, and thus dwelt in Chengji.

entries.zh: 弟向，范陽房始祖也。
entries.en: His younger brother Xiang founded the Fanyang branch.
entries.literal: His younger brother Xiang was the founder of the Fanyang branch.

entries.zh: 尚生廣，前將軍。
entries.en: Shang's son Guang was Forward General.
entries.literal: Shang begot Guang, Forward General.

entries.zh: 二子：長曰當戶，生陵，字少卿，騎都尉；
entries.en: He had two sons: the elder, Danghu, whose son Ling, styled Shaoqing, was Commandant of Cavalry;
entries.literal: Two sons: the elder named Danghu, who begot Ling, styled Shaoqing, Commandant of Cavalry;

entries.zh: 次曰敢，字幼卿，郎中令、關內侯。
entries.en: and the younger, Gan, styled Youqing, Director of the Palace Secretariat and Marquis within the Passes.
entries.literal: the younger named Gan, styled Youqing, Director of the Palace Secretariat and Marquis within the Passes.

entries.zh: 生禹，字子通。
entries.en: He had Yu, styled Zitong.
entries.literal: He begot Yu, styled Zitong.

entries.zh: 弟忠，頓丘房始祖也。
entries.en: His younger brother Zhong founded the Dunqiu branch.
entries.literal: His younger brother Zhong was the founder of the Dunqiu branch.

entries.zh: 禹生丞公，字丞公，河南太守。
entries.en: Yu's son Chenggong, styled Chenggong, was Administrator of Henan.
entries.literal: Yu begot Chenggong, styled Chenggong, Administrator of Henan.

entries.zh: 生先，字敬宗，蜀郡、北平太守。
entries.en: He had Xian, styled Jingzong, who served as Administrator of Shu and of Beiping.
entries.literal: He begot Xian, styled Jingzong, Administrator of Shu commandery and of Beiping.

entries.zh: 生長宗，字伯禮，漁陽丞。
entries.en: He had Changzong, styled Boli, Assistant Magistrate of Yuyang.
entries.literal: He begot Changzong, styled Boli, Assistant Magistrate of Yuyang.

entries.zh: 生君況，字叔干，一字子期，博士、議郎、太中大夫。
entries.en: He had Junkuang, styled Shugan, also known as Ziqi, who served as Erudite, Gentleman Consultant, and Grand Master of the Palace.
entries.literal: He begot Junkuang, styled Shugan, also called Ziqi, Erudite, Gentleman Consultant, and Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 生本，字上明，郎中、侍御史。
entries.en: He had Ben, styled Shangming, Gentleman-of-the-Palace and Attendant Censor.
entries.literal: He begot Ben, styled Shangming, Gentleman-of-the-Palace and Attendant Censor.

entries.zh: 生次公，字仲君，巴郡太守、西夷校尉。
entries.en: He had Cigong, styled Zhongjun, Administrator of Ba and Colonel of the Western Yi.
entries.literal: He begot Cigong, styled Zhongjun, Administrator of Ba commandery and Colonel of the Western Yi.

entries.zh: 弟恬，渤海房始祖也。
entries.en: His younger brother Tian founded the Bohai branch.
entries.literal: His younger brother Tian was the founder of the Bohai branch.

entries.zh: 次公生軌，字文逸，魏臨淮太守、司農卿。
entries.en: Cigong's son Gui, styled Wenyi, was Administrator of Linhuai under Wei and Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: Cigong begot Gui, styled Wenyi, Administrator of Linhuai in Wei and Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 弟潛，申公房始祖也。
entries.en: His younger brother Qian founded the Duke of Shen branch.
entries.literal: His younger brother Qian was the founder of the Duke of Shen branch.

entries.zh: 軌生隆，字彥緒，長安令、積弩將軍。
entries.en: Gui's son Long, styled Yanxu, was Magistrate of Chang'an and General of Stacked Crossbows.
entries.literal: Gui begot Long, styled Yanxu, Magistrate of Chang'an and General of Stacked Crossbows.

entries.zh: 生艾，字世績，晉驍騎將軍、魏郡太守。
entries.en: He had Ai, styled Shiji, Valiant Cavalry General under Jin and Administrator of Wei commandery.
entries.literal: He begot Ai, styled Shiji, Valiant Cavalry General of Jin and Administrator of Wei commandery.

entries.zh: 生雍，字儁熙，濟北、東莞二郡太守。
entries.en: He had Yong, styled Junxi, who served as Administrator of Jibei and Dongguan.
entries.literal: He begot Yong, styled Junxi, Administrator of both Jibei and Dongguan commanderies.

entries.zh: 生二子：長曰倫，丹楊房始祖也；
entries.en: He had two sons: the elder, Lun, who founded the Danyang branch;
entries.literal: He begot two sons: the elder named Lun, founder of the Danyang branch;

entries.zh: 次曰柔，字德遠，北地太守。
entries.en: and the younger, Rou, styled Deyuan, Administrator of Beidi.
entries.literal: the younger named Rou, styled Deyuan, Administrator of Beidi.

entries.zh: 雍孫蓋，安邑房始祖也。
entries.en: Yong's grandson Gai founded the Anyi branch.
entries.literal: Yong's grandson Gai was the founder of the Anyi branch.

entries.zh: 柔生弇，字季子，前涼張駿天水太守、武衞將軍、安西亭侯。
entries.en: Rou's son Yan, styled Jizi, served Zhang Jun of Former Liang as Administrator of Tianshui and General of Martial Guards and was made Marquis of Anxi.
entries.literal: Rou begot Yan, styled Jizi, Administrator of Tianshui under Zhang Jun of Former Liang, General of Martial Guards, and Marquis of Anxi.

entries.zh: 生昶，字仲堅，涼太子侍講。
entries.en: He had Chang, styled Zhongjian, Lecturer to the Crown Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: He begot Chang, styled Zhongjian, Lecturer to the Crown Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 生暠，字玄盛，西涼武昭王、興聖皇帝。
entries.en: He had Gao, styled Xuansheng, Martial and Illustrious King of Western Liang and posthumously honored as the Emperor Who Raised the Sage.
entries.literal: He begot Gao, styled Xuansheng, Martial and Illustrious King of Western Liang and Emperor Who Raised the Sage.

entries.zh: 十子：譚、歆、讓、愔、恂、翻、豫、宏、眺、亮。
entries.en: He had ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.
entries.literal: Ten sons: Tan, Xin, Rang, Yin, Xun, Fan, Yu, Hong, Tiao, and Liang.

entries.zh: 愔，鎮遠將軍房始祖也。
entries.en: Yin founded the General Who Pacifies the Distance branch.
entries.literal: Yin was the founder of the General Who Pacifies the Distance branch.

entries.zh: 其曾孫系，平涼房始祖也。
entries.en: His great-grandson Xi founded the Pingliang branch.
entries.literal: His great-grandson Xi was the founder of the Pingliang branch.

entries.zh: 翻孫三人：曰丞，姑臧房始祖也；
entries.en: Fan had three grandsons: Cheng, who founded the Guzang branch;
entries.literal: Fan's grandsons, three in number: named Cheng, founder of the Guzang branch;

entries.zh: 曰茂，燉煌房始祖也；
entries.en: Mao, who founded the Dunhuang branch;
entries.literal: named Mao, founder of the Dunhuang branch;

entries.zh: 曰沖，僕射房始祖也。
entries.en: and Chong, who founded the Vice Director branch.
entries.literal: and named Chong, founder of the Vice Director branch.

entries.zh: 曾孫曰成禮，絳郡房始祖也。
entries.en: A great-grandson, Chenli, founded the Jiang commandery branch.
entries.literal: A great-grandson named Chenli was the founder of the Jiang commandery branch.

entries.zh: 豫玄孫曰剛，武陵房始祖也。
entries.en: Yu's great-great-grandson Gang founded the Wuling branch.
entries.literal: Yu's great-great-grandson named Gang was the founder of the Wuling branch.

entries.zh: 歆字士業，西涼後主。
entries.en: Xin, styled Shiye, was the last ruler of Western Liang.
entries.literal: Xin, styled Shiye, was the last ruler of Western Liang.

entries.zh: 八子：勗、紹、重耳、弘之、崇明、崇產、崇庸、崇祐。
entries.en: He had eight sons: Xu, Shao, Chong'er, Hongzhi, Chongming, Chongchan, Chongyong, and Chongyou.
entries.literal: Eight sons: Xu, Shao, Chong'er, Hongzhi, Chongming, Chongchan, Chongyong, and Chongyou.

entries.zh: 重耳字景順，以國亡奔宋，為汝南太守。
entries.en: Chong'er, styled Jingshun, fled to Song after the kingdom fell and became Administrator of Runan.
entries.literal: Chong'er, styled Jingshun, when the state perished fled to Song and became Administrator of Runan.

entries.zh: 後魏克豫州，以地歸之，拜恒農太守，復為宋將薛安都所陷，後魏安南將軍、豫州刺史。
entries.en: When Northern Wei seized Yuzhou it restored his lands and made him Administrator of Hengnong. He was later captured by the Song general Xue Andu, then served Northern Wei as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Later Wei captured Yuzhou and returned the territory to him; he was appointed Administrator of Hengnong; again he was taken by Song general Xue Andu; he became General Who Pacifies the South of Later Wei and Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 生獻祖宣皇帝熙，字孟良，後魏金門鎮將。
entries.en: He had Xi, styled Mengliang, posthumously the Founding Ancestor Emperor Xuan, who served Later Wei as Garrison Commander of Jinmen.
entries.literal: He begot the Founding Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, Xi, styled Mengliang, Garrison Commander of Jinmen under Later Wei.

entries.zh: 生懿祖光皇帝，諱天賜，字德真。
entries.en: He had Tianci, styled Dezhen, posthumously the Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Guang.
entries.literal: He begot the Illustrious Ancestor, Emperor Guang, taboo name Tianci, styled Dezhen.

entries.zh: 三子：長曰起頭，長安侯，生達摩，後周羽林監、太子洗馬、長安縣伯，其後無聞；
entries.en: He had three sons: the elder, Qitou, Marquis of Chang'an, whose son Damo served Later Zhou as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Baron of Chang'an county—his line is not recorded further;
entries.literal: Three sons: the elder named Qitou, Marquis of Chang'an, who begot Damo, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest under Later Zhou, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Baron of Chang'an county—afterward no report;

entries.zh: 次曰太祖；
entries.en: the second, the Grand Ancestor;
entries.literal: the second named the Grand Ancestor;

entries.zh: 次乞豆。
entries.en: and the third, Qidou.
entries.literal: the third Qidou.

entries.zh: 代祖代祖元皇帝諱昺，周安州總管、柱國大將軍、唐國仁公。
entries.en: Bing, posthumously Emperor Yuan with the temple name Shizu, served Zhou as General-in-Chief of Anzhou and Pillar-of-the-State Grand General and was Duke Ren of Tang.
entries.literal: Shizu, Emperor Yuan, taboo name Bing, was General-in-Chief of Anzhou under Zhou, Pillar-of-the-State Grand General, and Duke Ren of Tang.

entries.zh: 四子：長曰高祖，次曰梁王澄，次曰蜀王湛，次曰漢王洪。
entries.en: He had four sons: the eldest became the High Ancestor; the second was Prince of Liang, Cheng; the third Prince of Shu, Zhan; and the fourth Prince of Han, Hong.
entries.literal: Four sons: the eldest was the High Ancestor; the second was Prince of Liang, Cheng; the third was Prince of Shu, Zhan; the fourth was Prince of Han, Hong.

entries.zh: 高祖高祖神堯大聖大光孝皇帝二十二子，分十五房：曰楚王智雲，曰荊王元景，曰徐王元禮，曰韓王元嘉，曰彭王元則，曰鄭王元懿，曰霍王元軌，曰虢王鳳，曰道王元慶，曰鄧王元裕，曰舒王元名，曰魯王靈夔，曰江王元祥，曰密王元曉，曰滕王元嬰。
entries.en: The High Ancestor, Emperor Gaozu, had twenty-two sons grouped into fifteen houses: the Princes of Chu (Zhiyun), Jing (Yuanjing), Xu (Yuanli), Han (Yuanjia), Peng (Yuanze), Zheng (Yuanyi), Huo (Yuangui), Guo (Feng), Dao (Yuanqing), Deng (Yuanyu), Shu (Yuanming), Lu (Lingkui), Jiang (Yuanxiang), Mi (Yuanxiao), and Teng (Yuanying).
entries.literal: The High Ancestor, the Divine Yao, Great Sage, Greatly Illuminated, Filial Emperor, had twenty-two sons, divided into fifteen branches: namely Prince of Chu, Zhiyun; Prince of Jing, Yuanjing; Prince of Xu, Yuanli; Prince of Han, Yuanjia; Prince of Peng, Yuanze; Prince of Zheng, Yuanyi; Prince of Huo, Yuangui; Prince of Guo, Feng; Prince of Dao, Yuanqing; Prince of Deng, Yuanyu; Prince of Shu, Yuanming; Prince of Lu, Lingkui; Prince of Jiang, Yuanxiang; Prince of Mi, Yuanxiao; and Prince of Teng, Yuanying.

entries.zh: 智雲、元景皆無後。
entries.en: Zhiyun and Yuanjing left no descendants.
entries.literal: Zhiyun and Yuanjing both had no descendants.

entries.zh: 中宗中宗大和大聖大昭孝皇帝四子。
entries.en: Emperor Zhongzong had four sons.
entries.literal: Zhongzong, the Greatly Harmonious, Great Sage, Greatly Illuminated, Filial Emperor, had four sons.

entries.zh: 湖陽郡王房
entries.en: House of the Prince of Huyang commandery.
entries.literal: Branch of the Prince of Huyang commandery.

entries.zh: 始，唐興，疏屬畢王，至太宗，稍稍降封。
entries.en: When Tang first rose, every distant clansman was enfeoffed as king; by Taizong's reign those titles were gradually reduced.
entries.literal: At first, when Tang rose, distant clansmen were all enfeoffed as kings; by Taizong's time enfeoffments were gradually reduced.

entries.zh: 時天下已定，帝與名臣蕭瑀等喟然講封建事，欲與三代比隆，而魏征、李百藥皆謂不然。
entries.en: Once the realm was settled, the Emperor discussed enfeoffment with eminent ministers such as Xiao Yu, wishing to rival the Three Dynasties—but Wei Zheng and Li Baiyao opposed it.
entries.literal: By then the realm was already settled; the Emperor with eminent ministers such as Xiao Yu sighed and discussed enfeoffment, wishing to rival the Three Dynasties in glory, but Wei Zheng and Li Baiyao all said it should not be done.

entries.zh: 征意以唐承大亂，民人雕喪，始復生業，遽起而瓜分之，故有五不可之說。
entries.en: Zheng argued that Tang had inherited devastation, the people were only just recovering their livelihoods, and to divide the realm anew would be impossible on five grounds.
entries.literal: Zheng's view was that Tang inherited great disorder, the people were devastated, and livelihoods had only just revived—suddenly to divide them again was therefore his argument of five impossibilities.

entries.zh: 百藥稱帝王自有命，歷祚之短長不緣封建。
entries.en: Baiyao held that emperors receive their own mandate and a dynasty's span does not depend on enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Baiyao said emperors have their own mandate, and the length of a dynasty's fortune does not depend on enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 又舉春秋二百四十二年之禍，亟於哀、平、桓、靈，而詆曹元首、陸士衡之言以為繆悠。
entries.en: He also cited the calamities of the Spring and Autumn's 242 years, especially under Ai, Ping, Huan, and Ling, and dismissed the arguments of Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji as absurd.
entries.literal: He also cited the calamities of the Spring and Autumn's 242 years, pressing hardest in the reigns of Ai, Ping, Huan, and Ling, and condemned the words of Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji as absurd.

entries.zh: 而顏師古獨議建諸侯，當少其力，與州縣雜治，以相維持。
entries.en: Yan Shigu alone argued for establishing feudal lords, but with reduced power, governing alongside prefectures and counties to keep one another in check.
entries.literal: Yan Shigu alone argued for establishing feudal lords, saying their power should be reduced and they should be mixed in governance with prefectures and counties to hold one another in check.

entries.zh: 然天子由是罷不復議。
entries.en: Thereupon the Son of Heaven dropped the matter and never raised it again.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven on this account ceased and did not discuss it again.

entries.zh: 至名儒劉秩目武氏之禍，則建論以為設爵無土，署官不職，非古之道，故權移外家，宗廟絕而更存。
entries.en: Later the scholar Liu Zhi, surveying the Wu clan's seizure of power, argued that granting titles without fiefs and appointing officials without duties was not the ancient way—so power passed to the maternal kin, and though the ancestral line was severed, the dynasty endured.
entries.literal: Down to the eminent scholar Liu Zhi, who looked on the calamity of the Wu clan, he set forth the theory that granting titles without fiefs and appointing officials without duties was not the way of antiquity—therefore power shifted to the maternal kin, and though the ancestral temple was cut off, the dynasty yet survived.

entries.zh: 存之之理，在取順而難逆；
entries.en: Survival, Liu Zhi held, depends on winning compliance and making resistance hard;
entries.literal: The principle of survival lies in taking compliance and making opposition difficult;

entries.zh: 絕之之原，在單弱而無所憚。
entries.en: extinction comes from standing alone, weak, and without anything to restrain challengers.
entries.literal: the root of extinction lies in standing alone, weak, and with nothing to fear.

entries.zh: 至謂郡縣可以小寧，不可以久安。
entries.en: He even argued that the prefectural system might secure brief peace but never lasting stability.
entries.literal: He even said that commanderies and counties could bring brief peace but not lasting stability.

entries.zh: 大抵與曹、陸相上下。
entries.en: Broadly speaking, his argument stood on the same level as Cao Tongshu and Lu Ji.
entries.literal: On the whole his view ranked with those of Cao and Lu.

entries.zh: 而杜佑、柳宗元深探其本，據古驗今，而反復焉。
entries.en: Du You and Liu Zongyuan, however, dug deeper, tested present practice against antiquity, and argued the question through.
entries.literal: But Du You and Liu Zongyuan probed the root deeply, tested the present against antiquity, and argued back and forth.

entries.zh: 江夏王道宗廣寧縣公道興永安王孝基涵淮陽王道玄漢長平王叔良郇國公孝協彭國公思訓新興郡王晉長樂王幼良襄武王琛河間王孝恭晦漢陽王廬江王瑗淮安王神通膠東王道彥梁郡公孝逸國貞暠說齊物復襄邑王神符從晦隴西公博義渤海王奉慈戡
entries.en: Biographies of Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong, Duke of Guangning County Li Daoxing, Prince Yong'an Li Xiaoji, Han, Prince Huaiyang Li Daoxuan, Prince of Changping in Han Li Shuliang, Duke of Xun State Li Xiaoxie, Duke of Peng State Si Xun, Prince of Xinxing Commandery Li Jin, Prince Changle Li Youliang, Prince Xiangwu Li Chen, Prince Hejian Li Xiaogong Hui, the Prince of Hanyang, Prince Lujiang Li Yuan, Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, Prince of Jiaodong Li Daoyan, Duke of Liang Commandery Li Xiaoyi, Guo Zhen, Hao, Shuo, Qiwu, Fu, Prince Xiangyi Li Shenfu Cong Hui, Duke of Longxi Li Boyi, and Prince Bohai Li Fengci Kan.
entries.literal: Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong; Duke of Guangning County Li Daoxing; Prince Yong'an Li Xiaoji; Han; Prince Huaiyang Li Daoxuan; Prince of Changping in Han Li Shuliang; Duke of Xun State Li Xiaoxie; Duke of Peng State Si Xun; Prince of Xinxing Commandery Li Jin; Prince Changle Li Youliang; Prince Xiangwu Li Chen; Prince Hejian Li Xiaogong Hui; Prince of Hanyang; Prince Lujiang Li Yuan; Prince Huai'an Li Shentong; Prince of Jiaodong Li Daoyan; Duke of Liang Commandery Li Xiaoyi; Guo Zhen; Hao; Shuo; Qiwu; Fu; Prince Xiangyi Li Shenfu Cong Hui; Duke of Longxi Li Boyi; Prince Bohai Li Fengci Kan.

entries.zh: 時東郡賊翟讓聚黨萬人，密因介其徒王伯當以策幹讓曰：「今主昏於上，人怨於下，銳兵盡之遼海，和親絕於突厥，南巡流連，空棄關輔，此實劉、項挺興之會。
entries.en: At that time Zhai Rang of Dongjun had gathered a band of ten thousand men. Mi sent his follower Wang Bodang with a plan to approach Rang. "The ruler is benighted above and the people resentful below," he said. "Sharp troops are exhausted at the Liao coast, peace with the Turks is broken, the southern tour drags on, and the capital region is abandoned—this is truly the moment for a Liu Bang or Xiang Yu to rise.
entries.literal: At that time Zhai Rang of Dongjun had gathered a band of ten thousand men. Mi sent his follower Wang Bodang with a plan to approach Rang, saying: "Now the ruler is benighted above and the people resentful below; sharp troops are exhausted at the Liao coast, peace alliances with the Turks are broken, the southern tour drags on, and the capital region is abandoned—this is truly the moment for Liu Bang and Xiang Yu to rise.

entries.zh: 足下資豪桀，士馬精勇，指罪誅暴，為天下先，楊氏不足亡也。」
entries.en: You possess the resources of a great hero, with elite soldiers and horses. Point out crimes and punish tyranny, take the lead for the realm—the house of Yang is not beyond destruction."
entries.literal: You possess the resources of a great hero, with elite soldiers and horses; point out crimes and punish tyranny, take the lead for the realm—the Yang house is not beyond destruction."

entries.zh: 讓由是加禮，遣說諸賊，至輒下。
entries.en: Rang therefore treated him with greater respect and sent him to persuade other bandits. Wherever he went, they submitted.
entries.literal: Rang therefore treated him with greater respect and sent him to persuade other bandits; wherever he went they submitted.

entries.zh: 因為讓計曰：「今稟無見糧，難以持久，卒遇敵，其亡無時。
entries.en: He then devised a plan for Rang. "Our stores have no visible grain," he said, "and it is hard to endure long. If we suddenly meet the enemy, destruction will come at any moment.
entries.literal: He then devised a plan for Rang, saying: "Now our stores have no visible grain; it is hard to endure long. If we suddenly meet the enemy, destruction will come at any moment.

entries.zh: 不如取滎陽，休兵館谷，待士逸馬肥，乃可與人爭利。」
entries.en: Better to take Xingyang, rest the army and live off the grain stores, wait until the men are rested and the horses fat, and then contend for advantage."
entries.literal: Better to take Xingyang, rest the army and live off the grain stores, wait until the men are rested and the horses fat, and then contend for advantage."

entries.zh: 讓聽之，遂破金堤關，徇滎陽諸縣，皆下。
entries.en: Rang listened. He broke through the Jindi Pass, swept the counties of Xingyang, and all submitted.
entries.literal: Rang listened and thereupon broke through the Jindi Pass, swept the counties of Xingyang, and all submitted.

entries.zh: 滎陽太守楊慶、河南討捕大使張須陀合兵討讓，讓素憚須陀，欲引去。
entries.en: Xingyang Prefect Yang Qing and Henan Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner Zhang Xituo combined forces to attack Rang. Rang had always feared Xituo and wished to withdraw.
entries.literal: Xingyang Prefect Yang Qing and Henan Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner Zhang Xituo combined forces to attack Rang. Rang had always feared Xituo and wished to withdraw.

entries.zh: 密曰：「須陀健而無謀，且驟勝易驕，吾為公破之。」
entries.en: Mi said, "Xituo is strong but lacks strategy, and repeated victories make him arrogant. I will break him for you."
entries.literal: Mi said: "Xituo is strong but lacks strategy, and repeated victories make him arrogant. I will break him for you."

entries.zh: 讓不得已，陣而待。
entries.en: Rang had no choice but to form battle lines and wait.
entries.literal: Rang had no choice but to form battle lines and wait.

entries.zh: 密率驍勇常何等二十人為遊騎，伏千兵莽間。
entries.en: Mi led twenty picked horsemen including Chang He as skirmish cavalry and hid a thousand soldiers in the brush.
entries.literal: Mi led twenty picked horsemen including Chang He as skirmish cavalry and hid a thousand soldiers in the brush.

entries.zh: 須陀素輕讓，引兵搏之，讓少卻，伏發，與遊軍乘之，遂殺須陀。
entries.en: Xituo had always looked down on Rang and led his troops to grapple with him. Rang retreated slightly; the ambush struck, and together with the skirmishers they pressed the attack and killed Xituo.
entries.literal: Xituo had always looked down on Rang and led his troops to grapple with him. Rang retreated slightly; the ambush struck, and together with the skirmishers they pressed the attack and killed Xituo.

entries.zh: 高祖起師太原，密自謂主盟，遣將軍張仁則致書於帝，呼為兄，請以步騎會河內。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu raised his army at Taiyuan, Mi considered himself the chief ally and sent General Zhang Renze with a letter to the emperor, addressing him as elder brother and asking to meet with infantry and cavalry at Henei.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu raised his army at Taiyuan. Mi considered himself the chief ally and sent General Zhang Renze with a letter to the emperor, addressing him as elder brother and asking to meet with infantry and cavalry at Henei.

entries.zh: 帝覽書，笑曰：「密陸梁，不可折簡致之。
entries.en: The emperor read the letter and laughed. "Mi is unruly," he said. "One cannot summon him with a brief note.
entries.literal: The emperor read the letter and laughed, saying: "Mi is unruly; one cannot summon him with a brief note.

entries.zh: 吾方定京師，未能東略，若不與，是生一隋。
entries.en: I am just now securing the capital and cannot yet advance east. If I do not respond, that creates another Sui.
entries.literal: I am just now securing the capital and cannot yet advance east. If I do not respond, that creates another Sui.

entries.zh: 密適為吾守成臯，拒東都兵，使不得西，更遣剽將莫如密。
entries.en: Mi happens to guard Chenggao for me, blocking the Eastern Capital troops so they cannot go west. To send a raiding general, none is better than Mi.
entries.literal: Mi happens to guard Chenggao for me, blocking the Eastern Capital troops so they cannot go west. To send a raiding general, none is better than Mi.

entries.zh: 吾寧推順，使驕其誌，我得留撫關中，大事濟矣。」
entries.en: I would rather defer to him and let his ambition swell. I can remain to pacify Guanzhong, and the great affair will succeed."
entries.literal: I would rather defer to him and let his ambition swell; I can remain to pacify Guanzhong, and the great affair will succeed."

entries.zh: 令記室溫大雅作報書，厚禮尊讓。
entries.en: He ordered Recorder Wen Daya to compose a reply with generous gifts and deferential respect.
entries.literal: He ordered Recorder Wen Daya to compose a reply with generous gifts and deferential respect.

entries.zh: 密大喜，示其下，曰：「唐公見推，顧天下無可慮者。」
entries.en: Mi was greatly pleased and showed the letter to his subordinates. "The Duke of Tang shows me deference," he said. "Surely there is nothing left to worry about in the realm."
entries.literal: Mi was greatly pleased and showed it to his subordinates, saying: "The Duke of Tang shows me deference—surely there is nothing left to worry about in the realm."

entries.zh: 遂專事隋。
entries.en: He thereupon devoted himself solely to fighting the Sui.
entries.literal: He thereupon devoted himself solely to fighting the Sui.

entries.zh: 及入關，兵尚二萬。
entries.en: When he entered the passes, his army still numbered twenty thousand.
entries.literal: When he entered the passes, his army still numbered twenty thousand.

entries.zh: 高祖使迎勞，冠蓋相望，密大喜，謂其徒曰：「吾所舉雖不就，而恩結百姓，山東連城數百，以吾故，當盡歸國。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sent men to welcome and comfort him. Officials in caps and carriages lined the road one after another. Mi was greatly pleased and told his followers, "Though what I raised did not succeed, I bound the common people in gratitude. Several hundred walled cities in Shandong, for my sake, should all return to the state.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent men to welcome and comfort him; officials in caps and carriages lined the road one after another. Mi was greatly pleased and said to his followers: "Though what I raised did not succeed, I bound the common people in gratitude. Several hundred walled cities in Shandong, for my sake, should all return to the state.

entries.zh: 功不減竇融，豈不以臺司處我？」
entries.en: My merit is no less than Dou Rong's—surely they will not place me below the rank of a minister of the court?"
entries.literal: My merit is no less than Dou Rong's—surely they will not place me below the rank of a minister of the court?"

entries.zh: 及至，拜光祿卿，封邢國公，殊怨望。
entries.en: When he arrived he was appointed Director of the Imperial Household and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing, and he was deeply resentful.
entries.literal: When he arrived he was appointed Director of the Imperial Household and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing, and he was deeply resentful.

entries.zh: 帝嘗呼之弟，妻以表妹獨孤氏。
entries.en: The emperor sometimes addressed him as younger brother and gave him his cousin of the Dugu clan in marriage.
entries.literal: The emperor sometimes addressed him as younger brother and gave him his cousin of the Dugu clan in marriage.

entries.zh: 後禮寢薄，執政者又求賄，滋不平。
entries.en: Afterward his treatment grew thin, and those in power also sought bribes, so his discontent increased.
entries.literal: Afterward his treatment grew thin, and those in power also sought bribes, so his discontent increased.

entries.zh: 因朝會進食，謂王伯當曰：「往在洛口，嘗欲以崔君賢為光祿，不意身自為此。」
entries.en: At a court assembly when presenting food, he said to Wang Bodang, "Back at Luokou I once wished to make Cui Junxian Director of the Imperial Household. I never imagined I would hold the post myself."
entries.literal: At a court assembly when presenting food, he said to Wang Bodang: "Back at Luokou I once wished to make Cui Junxian Director of the Imperial Household—I never imagined I would hold the post myself."

entries.zh: 未幾，聞故所部將多不附世充者，高祖詔密以本兵就黎陽招撫故部曲，經略東都，伯當以左武衛將軍為密副。
entries.en: Before long, hearing that many of his former officers did not attach themselves to Shichong, Emperor Gaozu ordered Mi to take his original troops to Liyang to summon and pacify his former followers and plan strategy toward the Eastern Capital, with Bodang as Left Martial Guard General as Mi's deputy.
entries.literal: Before long, hearing that many of his former officers did not attach themselves to Shichong, Emperor Gaozu ordered Mi to take his original troops to Liyang to summon and pacify his former followers and plan strategy toward the Eastern Capital, with Bodang as Left Martial Guard General as Mi's deputy.

entries.zh: 馳驛東至稠桑驛，有詔復召密，密大懼，謀叛。
entries.en: He galloped east to Chousang Post Station when an edict recalled Mi again. Mi was greatly afraid and plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: He galloped east to Chousang Post Station when an edict recalled Mi again. Mi was greatly afraid and plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 伯當止之，不從，乃曰：「士立義，不以存亡易慮。
entries.en: Bodang stopped him, but he would not listen, and then said, "A man who stands on principle does not change his resolve because of survival or destruction.
entries.literal: Bodang stopped him, but he would not listen, and then said: "A man who stands on principle does not change his resolve because of survival or destruction.

entries.zh: 公顧伯當厚，願畢命以報。
entries.en: You have always treated Bodang generously. I wish to give my life to repay you.
entries.literal: You have always treated Bodang generously; I wish to give my life to repay you.

entries.zh: 今可同往，死生以之，然無益也。」
entries.en: We can go together, life or death as one—but it will do no good."
entries.literal: We can go together, life or death as one—but it will do no good."

entries.zh: 乃簡驍勇數十人，衣婦人服，戴幕釭，藏刀裙下，詐為家婢妾者，入桃林傳舍，須臾變服出，據其城。
entries.en: He thereupon selected several dozen fierce warriors, dressed them in women's clothing, had them wear veiled hats, hid knives beneath their skirts, and feigned to be household maids and concubines entering Taolin relay station. In a moment they changed clothes, came out, and seized the city.
entries.literal: He thereupon selected several dozen fierce warriors, dressed them in women's clothing, had them wear veiled hats, hid knives beneath their skirts, and feigned to be household maids and concubines entering Taolin relay station. In a moment they changed clothes and came out and seized the city.

entries.zh: 掠畜產，趣南山而東，馳告張善相以兵應己。
entries.en: They plundered livestock and hurried east toward the southern mountains, galloping to notify Zhang Shanxiang to bring troops to support them.
entries.literal: They plundered livestock and hurried east toward the southern mountains, galloping to notify Zhang Shanxiang to bring troops to support them.

entries.zh: 密將如黎陽，或曰：「向殺翟讓，世勣傷幾死，瘡猶未平，今可保乎？」
entries.en: Mi was about to go to Liyang when someone said, "You killed Zhai Rang before. Xu Shiji was nearly killed and his wound is not yet healed—can you be safe there now?"
entries.literal: Mi was about to go to Liyang when someone said: "You killed Zhai Rang before; Xu Shiji was nearly killed and his wound is not yet healed—can you be safe there now?"

entries.zh: 時王伯當棄金墉屯河陽，密輕騎歸之，謂曰：「敗矣，久苦諸君，我今自刎以謝眾！」
entries.en: At that time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and garrisoned Heyang. Mi rode lightly to join him and said, "I am defeated. I have long troubled you all. Today I shall cut my own throat to apologize to the company!"
entries.literal: At that time Wang Bodang had abandoned Jinyong and garrisoned Heyang. Mi rode lightly to join him and said: "I am defeated. I have long troubled you all; today I shall cut my own throat to apologize to the company!"

entries.zh: 伯當抱密慟絕，眾皆泣，莫能仰視。
entries.en: Bodang embraced Mi and wept until he lost consciousness. All wept, and none could look up.
entries.literal: Bodang embraced Mi and wept until he lost consciousness; all wept, and none could look up.

entries.zh: 密復曰：「幸不相棄，當共歸關中，密雖無功，諸君必富貴。」
entries.en: Mi again said, "If you are willing not to abandon me, let us together return to Guanzhong. Though I have no merit, you will surely be enriched and honored."
entries.literal: Mi again said: "If you are willing not to abandon me, let us together return to Guanzhong. Though I have no merit, you will surely be enriched and honored."

entries.zh: 掾柳燮曰：「昔盆子歸漢，尚食均輸。
entries.en: Clerk Liu Xie said, "In the past when Liu Penzi returned to the Han, he still received equal distribution from the state granaries.
entries.literal: Clerk Liu Xie said: "In the past when Liu Penzi returned to the Han, he still received equal distribution from the state granaries.

entries.zh: 公與唐同族，雖不共起，然遏隋歸路，使無西，故唐不戰而據京師，亦公功也。」
entries.en: You share the same clan as Tang. Though you did not rise together, you blocked the Sui return route so they could not go west, and thus Tang took the capital without fighting—that too is your merit."
entries.literal: You share the same clan as Tang. Though you did not rise together, you blocked the Sui return route so they could not go west, and thus Tang took the capital without fighting—that too is your merit."

entries.zh: 密又謂伯當曰：「將軍族重，豈復與孤俱行哉？」
entries.en: Mi again said to Bodang, "General, your clan is weighty. How could you again travel with me alone?"
entries.literal: Mi again said to Bodang: "General, your clan is weighty—how could you again travel with me alone?"

entries.zh: 伯當曰：「昔蕭何舉宗從漢，今不昆季盡行，以為愧。
entries.en: Bodang said, "In the past Xiao He brought his whole clan to follow the Han. If I do not bring all my brothers now, I would be ashamed.
entries.literal: Bodang said: "In the past Xiao He brought his whole clan to follow the Han; if I do not bring all my brothers now, I would be ashamed.

entries.zh: 豈公一失利，輕去就哉？
entries.en: Would I lightly leave or stay because you suffered one defeat?
entries.literal: Would I lightly leave or stay because you suffered one defeat?

entries.zh: 雖隕首穴胸，所甘已。」
entries.en: Even if my head were smashed and my breast pierced, I would accept it gladly."
entries.literal: Even if my head were smashed and my breast pierced, I would accept it gladly."

entries.zh: 左右感動，遂來歸。
entries.en: Those beside him were moved and thereupon came to submit.
entries.literal: Those beside him were moved and thereupon came to submit.

entries.zh: 李密，字玄邃，一字法主，其先遼東襄平人。
entries.en: Li Mi, styled Xuansui and also known as Fazhu, traced his ancestry to Xiangping in Liaodong.
entries.literal: Li Mi, styled Xuansui and also known by the style name Fazhu, had ancestors from Xiangping in Liaodong.

entries.zh: 曾祖弼，魏司徒，賜姓徒何氏，入周為太師、魏國公。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Bi had served as Minister over the Masses of Wei, was granted the surname of the Tuhe clan, and after entering Zhou rose to Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Bi was Minister over the Masses of Wei, was granted the surname of the Tuhe clan, and upon entering Zhou became Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.

entries.zh: 祖曜，邢國公。
entries.en: His grandfather Yao held the title Duke of Xing.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yao was Duke of Xing.

entries.zh: 父寬，隋上柱國、蒲山郡公。
entries.en: His father Kuan was a Sui Grand Illustrious Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan Commandery.
entries.literal: His father Kuan was a Sui Grand Illustrious Pillar of State and Duke of Pushan Commandery.

entries.zh: 遂家長安。
entries.en: The family then made its home in Chang'an.
entries.literal: Thereupon the family settled in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 三年，高祖詔夔州總管趙郡王孝恭討之，拔通、開二州，斬偽東平王阇提。
entries.en: In the third year Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Zhao, General-in-Chief of Kuizhou Li Xiaogong, to attack him. Xiaogong took Tong and Kai prefectures and beheaded the false Prince of Dongping, Zheti.
entries.literal: In the third year, Emperor Gaozu ordered the Commandery Prince of Zhao, General-in-Chief of Kuizhou Xiaogong, to campaign against him; he took the two prefectures Tong and Kai and beheaded the false Prince of Dongping Zheti.

entries.zh: 諸將擅兵橫恣，銑恐浸不制，乃陽議休兵營農，以黜其權。
entries.en: His generals abused their armies and acted as they pleased. Xian feared he would lose control of them, so he openly proposed standing the troops down for farming in order to curb their power.
entries.literal: The generals arrogantly wielded troops and acted willfully; Xian feared they would gradually be uncontrollable, and thus openly discussed resting troops and farming to strip their power.

entries.zh: 大司馬董景珍之弟為將軍，怨之，謀作亂，事泄，被誅。
entries.en: The younger brother of Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen, who was himself a general, resented this and plotted a revolt. When the plot was exposed, he was executed.
entries.literal: The younger brother of the Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen was a general, resentful of this, and plotted rebellion; when the affair leaked he was executed.

entries.zh: 景珍方鎮長沙，銑下書赦之，召還江陵。
entries.en: Jingzhen was then holding Changsha. Xian issued a pardon and summoned him back to Jiangling.
entries.literal: Jingzhen was then garrisoning Changsha; Xian sent an edict pardoning him and summoned him back to Jiangling.

entries.zh: 景珍懼，遣使詣孝恭，舉地降。
entries.en: Jingzhen was afraid, sent envoys to Xiaogong, and surrendered his territory.
entries.literal: Jingzhen feared, sent envoys to Xiaogong, and surrendered his territory.

entries.zh: 銑遣張繡攻景珍，景珍曰：「前年醢彭越，往年殺韓信，獨不見乎！
entries.en: Xian sent Zhang Xiu to attack Jingzhen. Jingzhen said, "Years ago Peng Yue was boiled alive; not long ago Han Xin was killed—have you alone never heard of it?
entries.literal: Xian sent Zhang Xiu to attack Jingzhen. Jingzhen said: "In former years Peng Yue was minced, in past years Han Xin was killed—have you alone not seen it!

entries.zh: 奈何相攻？」
entries.en: Why turn on each other now?"
entries.literal: Why attack each other?"

entries.zh: 繡不答，圍之。
entries.en: Xiu made no reply and laid siege to him.
entries.literal: Xiu did not answer and besieged him.

entries.zh: 景珍潰而走，麾下殺之。
entries.en: Jingzhen was broken and fled, but his own men killed him.
entries.literal: Jingzhen was routed and fled; his subordinates killed him.

entries.zh: 銑進繡為尚書令。
entries.en: Xian promoted Zhang Xiu to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: Xian advanced Xiu to Imperial Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 繡恃功，亦驕蹇，銑又誅之。
entries.en: Xiu, trusting in his achievements, grew insolent as well, and Xian had him executed too.
entries.literal: Xiu relying on merit was also arrogant; Xian again executed him.

entries.zh: 銑性外寬內忌，疾勝己者，於是大臣舊將皆疑間，多叛去，銑不能禁，由此愈弱。
entries.en: Xian was mild in manner but jealous at heart and could not bear rivals. Soon his senior ministers and veteran generals were estranged; many rebelled and left, and he could not stop them. His power dwindled from that point on.
entries.literal: Xian by nature was outwardly lenient and inwardly jealous, hating those who surpassed himself; thereupon great ministers and old generals were all suspicious, many rebelled and left, and Xian could not restrain it—thereby growing weaker.

entries.zh: 顯州首領楊士林、田瓚起兵攻粲，旁郡響赴，戰淮源，粲大敗，挈殘士奔菊潭，遣使乞降。
entries.en: Yang Shilin and Tian Zan of Xianzhou rose against him; neighboring districts joined in; defeated at Huaiyuan, Can fled with his survivors to Jutan and sued for peace.
entries.literal: Xianzhou leaders Yang Shilin and Tian Zan raised troops against Can; neighboring commanderies responded; at Huaiyuan Can was greatly defeated, fled with his remnants to Jutan, and sent envoys to surrender.

entries.zh: 高祖以前御史大夫段確假散騎常侍勞之。
entries.en: Gaozu sent the former Censor-in-chief Duan Que, acting as Regular Attendant, to accept his submission.
entries.literal: Gaozu appointed the former Censor-in-chief Duan Que acting Regular Attendant to console him.

entries.zh: 確醉，戲粲曰：「君膾人多矣，若為味？」
entries.en: Drunk, Duan joked, "You have butchered so many—how do they taste?"
entries.literal: Que was drunk and jested with Can: "You have minced many people — how does the taste compare?"

entries.zh: 粲曰：「啖嗜酒人，正似糟豚。」
entries.en: Can replied, "A drunkard is rather like pickled pork."
entries.literal: Can said: "Eating a wine-lover is just like pickled pork."

entries.zh: 確悸，罵曰：「狂賊，歸朝乃一奴耳，復得噬人乎？」
entries.en: Duan, shaken, cursed him: "Mad rebel! In the capital you are only a bondsman—would you dare eat men again?"
entries.literal: Que was alarmed and cursed: "Mad bandit — once you submit to the court you are but a slave; can you still devour men?"

entries.zh: 粲懼，收確於坐，並從者數十悉饔之，以饗左右。
entries.en: Terrified, Can seized Duan at the feast and, with several dozen of his escort, cooked them all to regale his officers.
entries.literal: Can was afraid; he seized Que at the banquet and with several dozen attendants fed them all to his men to feast his followers.

entries.zh: 遂屠菊潭，奔王世充，署龍驤大將軍。
entries.en: He massacred Jutan, fled to Wang Shichong, and was named Dragon-Flying Grand General.
entries.literal: He then slaughtered Jutan, fled to Wang Shichong, and was appointed Dragon-Flying Grand General.

entries.zh: 東都平，斬洛水上。
entries.en: When the eastern capital fell, he was executed on the banks of the Luo.
entries.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was beheaded on the Luo River.

entries.zh: 士庶競擲瓦礫擊其屍，須臾若冢。
entries.en: Citizens pelted his body with brick and stone until it rose like a barrow.
entries.literal: Officials and commoners vied to hurl stones and tiles at his corpse until in a moment it was like a mound.

entries.zh: 林士弘，饒州鄱陽人。
entries.en: Lin Shihong came from Poyang in Raozhou.
entries.literal: Lin Shihong was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.

entries.zh: 隋季與鄉人操師乞起為盜。
entries.en: Near the end of the Sui he and a townsman, Cao Shiji, turned bandit.
entries.literal: At the end of Sui he and a fellow townsman Cao Shiji rose as bandits.

entries.zh: 師乞自號元興王，建元天成，大業十二年據豫章，以士弘為大將軍。
entries.en: Shiji called himself King Yuanxing with the era Tiancheng; in the twelfth year of Daye he seized Yuzhang and made Shihong his Grand General.
entries.literal: Shiji styled himself King Yuanxing, era Tiancheng; in the twelfth year of Daye he held Yuzhang and made Shihong Grand General.

entries.zh: 隋遣治書侍御史劉子翊討賊，射殺師乞，而士弘收其眾，復戰彭蠡，子翊敗，死之。
entries.en: The court sent Investigative Censor Liu Ziyi, who killed Shiji in battle; Shihong rallied the remnant, met Liu again on Poyang Lake, and slew him.
entries.literal: The Sui sent Investigative Censor Liu Ziyi to suppress the bandits; he shot and killed Shiji, but Shihong gathered his forces, fought again at Poyang Lake, and Ziyi was defeated and killed.

entries.zh: 遂大振，眾十余萬，據虔州，自號南越王。
entries.en: His power surged past a hundred thousand; he held Qianzhou and styled himself King of Southern Yue.
entries.literal: He flourished greatly with more than one hundred thousand men, held Qianzhou, and styled himself King of Southern Yue.

entries.zh: 俄僭號楚：稱皇帝，建元為太平。
entries.en: He soon declared the Chu dynasty, took the imperial title, and adopted the era Taiping.
entries.literal: Soon he usurped the state of Chu, proclaimed himself emperor, and adopted the reign era Taiping.

entries.zh: 侍御史鄭大節以九江郡下之。
entries.en: Censor Attendant Zheng Dajie delivered Jiujiang to him.
entries.literal: Censor Attendant Zheng Dajie surrendered Jiujiang commandery to him.

entries.zh: 士弘任其黨王戎為司空。
entries.en: Shihong named his partisan Wang Rong Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Shihong appointed his follower Wang Rong Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 臨川、廬陵、南康、宜春豪傑皆殺隋守令以附，北盡九江，南番禺，悉有之。
entries.en: Local strongmen in Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun killed Sui officials to join him; his realm stretched from Jiujiang north to Panyu south.
entries.literal: Notables of Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun all killed Sui prefects and magistrates to join him; north to Jiujiang, south to Panyu — he held them all.

entries.zh: 後蕭銑以舟師破豫章，士弘獨有南昌、虔、循、潮之地。
entries.en: When Xiao Xian's fleet seized Yuzhang, Shihong kept only Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao.
entries.literal: Later Xiao Xian's fleet took Yuzhang; Shihong alone retained Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao.

entries.zh: 銑敗，其亡卒稍歸之，復振。
entries.en: After Xiao Xian's fall his fugitives drifted back, and Shihong revived.
entries.literal: When Xian was defeated, his scattered soldiers gradually returned to Shihong, and he revived.

entries.zh: 趙郡王孝恭招慰，降循、潮二州。
entries.en: Prince Xiaogong of Zhao offered terms and won Xun and Chao.
entries.literal: Prince of Zhao-jun Xiaogong offered pacification and received the surrender of Xun and Chao commanderies.

entries.zh: 武德五年，士弘弟鄱陽王藥師以兵二萬圍循州，總管楊世略破斬之，士弘請降。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Wude his brother Yaoshi, Prince of Poyang, invested Xunzhou with twenty thousand men; Yang Shilue destroyed the force and killed him, and Shihong sued for peace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Wude, Shihong's brother the Prince of Poyang Yaoshi besieged Xunzhou with twenty thousand men; regional commander Yang Shilue defeated and killed him, and Shihong requested surrender.

entries.zh: 王戎亦獻南昌地，詔戎為南昌州總管。
entries.en: Wang Rong yielded Nanchang as well; the court made him regional commander of Nanchang.
entries.literal: Wang Rong also offered Nanchang territory; an edict made Rong regional commander of Nanchang prefecture.

entries.zh: 士弘復遁保安城山，誘潰亡，謀復亂，袁人相聚應之，為張善安所察，以兵赴討。
entries.en: Shihong slipped to Bao'ancheng Mountain, gathered deserters, and plotted a comeback; Yuanzhou men answered his call, but Zhang Shian uncovered the scheme and marched against him.
entries.literal: Shihong again fled to Bao'ancheng Mountain, rallied stragglers, plotted renewed rebellion; Yuan men gathered in response; Zhang Shian detected it and marched troops to suppress him.

entries.zh: 會士弘死，其黨乃解。
entries.en: Shihong died before the plot matured, and his party dissolved.
entries.literal: When Shihong died, his faction dispersed.

entries.zh: 張善安，兗州方與人。
entries.en: Zhang Shian was from Fangyu in Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Shian was a native of Fangyu in Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 年十七，亡命為盜，轉掠淮南。
entries.en: At seventeen he became an outlaw and roamed Huainan as a bandit.
entries.literal: At seventeen he fled as outlaw and became a bandit, raiding through Huainan.

entries.zh: 會孟讓敗，得其散卒八百，襲破廬江郡。
entries.en: After Meng Rang's defeat he picked up eight hundred survivors and stormed Lujiang.
entries.literal: When Meng Rang was defeated he got eight hundred of his scattered troops and raided and took Lujiang commandery.

entries.zh: 依林士弘，不見信，憾之，反襲士弘，焚其郛，去保南康。
entries.en: Serving under Lin Shihong without trust, he turned on him, burned his outer ramparts, and withdrew to Nankang.
entries.literal: He attached to Lin Shihong but was not trusted, resented it, turned and raided Shihong, burned his outer walls, and withdrew to hold Nankang.

entries.zh: 蕭銑取豫章，遣將蘇胡兒守之，善安奪其地，據以歸國，授洪州總管。
entries.en: When Xiao Xian seized Yuzhang he left Su Hu'er to guard it; Shian drove him out, submitted to Tang, and was made regional commander of Hongzhou.
entries.literal: Xiao Xian took Yuzhang and sent Su Hu'er to hold it; Shian seized the territory, submitted to the state, and was appointed regional commander of Hongzhou.

entries.zh: 武德六年反，輔公祏以為西南道大行臺。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Wude he rebelled; Fu Gongshi named him Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Wude he rebelled; Fu Gongshi made him Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit.

entries.zh: 善安掠孫州，執總管王戎，襲殺黃州總管周法明。
entries.en: He plundered Sunzhou, seized Wang Rong, and killed Huangzhou commander Zhou Faming in an ambush.
entries.literal: Shian raided Sun prefecture, seized regional commander Wang Rong, and ambushed and killed Huangzhou commander Zhou Faming.

entries.zh: 會李大亮兵至，為開曉禍福，答曰：「善安初不反，為部下詿誤。
entries.en: Li Daliang arrived and explained the stakes; Shian said, "I never meant to rebel—my officers misled me.
entries.literal: When Li Daliang's troops arrived, he explained the consequences of fortune and misfortune; Shian answered: "Shian did not rebel at first; my subordinates misled me.

entries.zh: 降，今易耳，恐不免，奈何？」
entries.en: Surrender is easy now, yet I fear I may not be spared—what am I to do?"
entries.literal: To surrender now is easy, but I fear I cannot escape — what can be done?"

entries.zh: 大亮曰：「總管定降，吾固不疑。」
entries.en: Daliang said, "If you mean to submit, I never doubted you."
entries.literal: Daliang said: "Commander, you have decided to surrender; I never doubted it."

entries.zh: 因獨入其陣，與善安握手語，乃大喜，將數十騎詣大亮營。
entries.en: He rode alone into Shian's ranks, clasped his hand in talk, and Shian, delighted, followed with a few dozen horsemen to Daliang's camp.
entries.literal: He then entered Shian's lines alone, spoke hand in hand with him; Shian was greatly pleased and came with several dozen riders to Daliang's camp.

entries.zh: 大亮引入，命壯士執之。
entries.en: Daliang ushered him inside and had braves seize him.
entries.literal: Daliang led him in and ordered stalwarts to seize him.

entries.zh: 騎皆驚，引去，悉兵來戰。
entries.en: His escort fled in alarm and returned with the whole army to fight.
entries.literal: The riders were alarmed, withdrew, and brought their full force to battle.

entries.zh: 大亮諭以善安自歸，無庸鬥。
entries.en: Daliang proclaimed that Shian had come over willingly and that battle was needless.
entries.literal: Daliang announced that Shian had surrendered of his own accord and there was no need to fight.

entries.zh: 其黨罵曰：「總管賣我！」
entries.en: His men shouted, "Our commander has sold us!"
entries.literal: His followers cursed: "The commander has sold us out!"

entries.zh: 遂潰。
entries.en: They broke and ran.
entries.literal: They then scattered.

entries.zh: 送善安京師，稱不與公祏謀，高祖赦之。
entries.en: Shian was sent to the capital, swore he had not conspired with Fu Gongshi, and Gaozu pardoned him.
entries.literal: Shian was sent to the capital; he claimed he had not plotted with Gongshi; Gaozu pardoned him.

entries.zh: 公祏破，得其書，遂伏誅。
entries.en: When Gongshi fell, letters implicating Shian surfaced, and he was executed.
entries.literal: When Gongshi was defeated, his correspondence was found and Shian was executed.

entries.zh: 梁師都，夏州朔方人。
entries.en: Liang Shidu was a man of Shuofang in Xiazhou.
entries.literal: Liang Shidu was a native of Shuofang in Xiazhou.

entries.zh: 為郡豪姓。
entries.en: His family was a leading house of the district.
entries.literal: He was of a great clan of the commandery.

entries.zh: 仕隋鷹揚府郎將。
entries.en: Under the Sui he held a captaincy in the Hawk-raiser Guard.
entries.literal: He served Sui as a commandant of the Hawk-raiser Guard.

entries.zh: 大業末罷歸，結徒起為盜，殺郡丞唐世宗，據郡稱大丞相，聯兵突厥。
entries.en: Dismissed late in Daye, he returned home, raised a band, killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, seized the commandery as Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks.
entries.literal: At the end of Daye he was dismissed and returned home, gathered followers and rose as bandits, killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, held the commandery and styled himself Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks.

entries.zh: 與隋將張世隆戰，敗之，因略定雕陰、弘化、延安。
entries.en: He defeated the Sui general Zhang Shilong and overran Diaoyin, Honghua, and Yan'an.
entries.literal: He fought the Sui general Zhang Shilong, defeated him, and thereby overran Diaoyin, Honghua, and Yan'an.

entries.zh: 自為梁國，僭皇帝位，祭天於城南，坎地瘞玉得印，以為瑞，建元永隆。
entries.en: He declared the Liang state, took the imperial title, and sacrificed to Heaven south of the city; burying jade in a pit he unearthed a seal and hailed it as a portent, adopting the era Yonglong.
entries.literal: He made himself the state of Liang, usurped the imperial title, sacrificed to Heaven south of the city; digging the earth to bury jade he obtained a seal and took it as an omen; reign era Yonglong.

entries.zh: 始畢可汗遺以狼頭纛，號大度毘伽可汗、解事天子，遂導突厥兵居河南地，拔鹽川郡。
entries.en: Shibi Qaghan gave him a wolf-head standard and named him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan, "Capable Son of Heaven"; he led Turk forces into the Ordos and seized Yanchuan.
entries.literal: Shibi Qaghan sent him a wolf-head banner, titled him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan and "Capable Son of Heaven"; he then guided Turk troops to settle south of the Yellow River and took Yanchuan commandery.

entries.zh: 蕭銑，後梁宣帝曾孫也。
entries.en: Xiao Xian was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of the Later Liang.
entries.literal: Xiao Xian was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of the Later Liang.

entries.zh: 祖巖，開皇初叛隋降陳，陳亡，文帝誅之。
entries.en: His grandfather Yan, in the early Kaihuang reign, rebelled against Sui and went over to Chen; when Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui had him put to death.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yan, in the early Kaihuang era rebelled against Sui and submitted to Chen; when Chen perished, Emperor Wen executed him.

entries.zh: 銑少貧，傭書，事母孝。
entries.en: In his youth Xian was poor and made his living copying books; he was devoted in caring for his mother.
entries.literal: Xian in youth was poor, hired out as a copyist, and served his mother filially.

entries.zh: 煬帝以外戚擢為羅川令。
entries.en: Emperor Yang promoted him to magistrate of Luochuan because of his connection as an imperial in-law.
entries.literal: Emperor Yang, on account of maternal kinship, promoted him to magistrate of Luochuan.

entries.zh: 彥博裔孫廷筠，少敏悟，工為辭章，與李商隱皆有名，號「溫李」。
entries.en: Yanbo's descendant Wen Tingyun was clever as a youth and skilled at verse; he and Li Shangyin were famed together as "Wen and Li."
entries.literal: Yanbo's descendant Tingyun, quick and perceptive in youth, was skilled at literary composition; he and Li Shangyin were both famous, styled "Wen and Li."

entries.zh: 然薄於行，無檢幅。
entries.en: But his conduct was loose and unrestrained.
entries.literal: Yet he was shallow in conduct and without restraint.

entries.zh: 又多作側辭艷曲，與貴胄裴諴、令狐滈等蒲飲狎昵。
entries.en: He wrote many sensual songs and caroused intimately with young nobles such as Pei Xian and Linghu Hao.
entries.literal: He also wrote many licentious lyrics and sensual songs, and with noble scions such as Pei Xian and Linghu Hao he drank on rush mats in intimate familiarity.

entries.zh: 數舉進士不中第。
entries.en: He took the jinshi examination many times without success.
entries.literal: He repeatedly presented himself for the jinshi examination but never passed.

entries.zh: 思神速，多為人作文。
entries.en: His mind was extraordinarily quick, and he often ghost-wrote for others.
entries.literal: His thoughts were swift as a spirit; he often wrote compositions for others.

entries.zh: 大中末，試有司，廉視尤謹，廷筠不樂，上書千余言，然私占授者已八人，執政鄙其為，授方山尉。
