entries.en: Near the end of Dazhong the examination bureau screened candidates with unusual strictness; Tingyun was offended and submitted a thousand-word memorial, but eight candidates had already been privately promised posts, and the chief ministers, disgusted with him, made him marshal of Fangshan.
entries.literal: At the end of Dazhong, when the examination bureau tested candidates with especially strict integrity screening, Tingyun was displeased and submitted a memorial of more than a thousand words; yet those privately promised appointments already numbered eight, and the chief ministers despised his conduct and appointed him marshal of Fangshan.

entries.zh: 徐商鎮襄陽，署巡官，不得志，去歸江東。
entries.en: Xu Shang, governing Xiangyang, made him a touring officer, but frustrated, he left for the lower Yangtze.
entries.literal: When Xu Shang governed Xiangyang he appointed him touring officer; frustrated in his ambitions, he left and returned to the Jiangdong region.

entries.zh: 令狐綯方鎮淮南，廷筠怨居中時不為助力，過府不肯謁。
entries.en: Linghu Tao was then governing Huainan; Tingyun resented that Tao had not helped him when at court, and when passing his headquarters refused to call on him.
entries.literal: Linghu Tao was then governing Huainan; Tingyun resented that when Tao was at court he had not helped him, and passing his headquarters refused to pay a visit.

entries.zh: 丐錢揚子院，夜醉，為邏卒擊折其齒，訴於綯。
entries.en: While begging money at the Yangzi depot he got drunk one night and patrol guards broke his teeth; he appealed to Tao.
entries.literal: Begging money at the Yangzi compound, he was drunk at night and patrol soldiers broke his teeth; he complained to Tao.

entries.zh: 綯為劾吏，吏具道其汙行，綯兩置之。
entries.en: Tao had the guards prosecuted; they detailed Tingyun's misconduct, but Tao let the matter drop both times.
entries.literal: Tao had the officers impeached; the officers fully reported his filthy conduct, and Tao set the matter aside both times.

entries.zh: 事聞京師，廷筠遍見公卿，言為吏誣染。
entries.en: When word reached the capital, Tingyun visited every senior official claiming the guards had framed him.
entries.literal: When the affair reached the capital, Tingyun visited all the chief ministers and nobles, saying he had been slandered and smeared by the officers.

entries.zh: 俄而徐商執政，頗右之，欲白用。
entries.en: Soon Xu Shang came to power, favored him, and meant to recommend him for office.
entries.literal: Soon Xu Shang took power and favored him considerably, wishing to report and employ him.

entries.zh: 會商罷，楊收疾之，遂廢卒。
entries.en: But Shang fell from power, Yang Shou loathed him, and he died in obscurity.
entries.literal: When Shang was dismissed, Yang Shou detested him, and he died in obscurity.

entries.zh: 本名岐，字飛卿。
entries.en: His original name was Qi; his courtesy name was Feiqing.
entries.literal: His original name was Qi; his courtesy name was Feiqing.

entries.zh: 為人嚴愨，以威肅聞。
entries.en: He was stern and disciplined, renowned for his formidable bearing.
entries.literal: As a man he was stern and cautious, and was known for awe-inspiring severity.

entries.zh: 居家儉，厚於宗親，祿稟隨多少散之。
entries.en: He lived frugally at home but was generous to his kin, sharing his salary and grain allowances with them as soon as he received them.
entries.literal: At home he was frugal, yet generous toward kinsmen, dispersing his salary and grain allowance according to whatever amount he had.

entries.zh: 以余資寫書，罷揚州，書遂數事載。
entries.en: He used his spare income to copy books; by the time he left Yangzhou, his library filled several cartloads.
entries.literal: With surplus funds he copied books; when he left Yangzhou, his books finally filled several transport carts.

entries.zh: 嘗謂子孫曰：「吾性不喜財，遂至窶乏。
entries.en: He once told his descendants, "I have never cared for money, and so I have ended up poor.
entries.literal: He once told his sons and grandsons: "By nature I do not delight in wealth, and thus have come to destitution.

entries.zh: 然負京有賜田十頃，能耕之，足以食；
entries.en: Yet near the capital I own ten qing of granted land. If you farm it diligently, you will have enough to eat.
entries.literal: Yet near the capital I have ten qing of granted fields; if you can till them, they will suffice for food.

entries.zh: 河內千樹桑，事之可以衣；
entries.en: In Henei there are a thousand mulberry trees; work them and you will have clothes.
entries.literal: In Henei are a thousand mulberry trees; tending them can clothe you.

entries.zh: 江都書，力讀可進求宦。
entries.en: The books I left at Jiangdu—study them hard and you can make your way in official life.
entries.literal: The books at Jiangdu—if you read them with effort you may advance and seek office.

entries.zh: 吾歿後，能勤此，無資於人矣。」
entries.en: After I am gone, if you work at these three things, you will never need to depend on anyone."
entries.literal: After my death, if you can be diligent in these matters, you will need no support from others."

entries.zh: 遷涼州都督，改同州刺史。
entries.en: He was made protector-general of Liangzhou and later governor of Tong Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Protector-General of Liangzhou, then changed to Governor of Tong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 坐在涼州以私憾杖殺番禾丞劉武，當死，廢為民，流泉州，卒。
entries.en: He was found guilty of beating to death Fanhe Assistant Magistrate Liu Wu over a private grievance while serving in Liangzhou. Sentenced to death, he was instead stripped of rank, exiled to Quanzhou, and died there.
entries.literal: He was convicted for in Liangzhou beating to death Fanhe Assistant Magistrate Liu Wu by staff over a personal grudge; he should have died, but was demoted to commoner status, exiled to Quanzhou, and died there.

entries.zh: 溫皇甫二李姜崔
entries.en: Biographies of the Wen, Huangfu, two Li, Jiang, and Cui families.
entries.literal: Wen, Huangfu, the two Lis, Jiang, and Cui.

entries.zh: 是時，秦王方討王世充，遣使招懷，伏威乃獻款。
entries.en: At that time the Prince of Qin was campaigning against Wang Shichong and sent envoys to win him over. Fuwei thereupon pledged his allegiance.
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin was attacking Wang Shichong and sent envoys to win him over; Fuwei thereupon submitted allegiance.

entries.zh: 高祖授以東南道行臺尚書令、江淮安撫大使、上柱國、吳王，賜姓，豫屬籍，以其子德俊為山陽公，賜帛五千段，馬三百匹。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Secretariat, Grand Ambassador for the Pacification of Jianghuai, Upper Pillar of State, and King of Wu; granted him the imperial surname and enrolled him in the imperial clan register. His son Dejun was made Duke of Shanyang, and he received five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed him Southeastern Circuit Executive Secretariat Director, Grand Ambassador for Pacification of Jianghuai, Upper Pillar of State, King of Wu, granted the imperial surname, entered the register of imperial clan; his son Dejun was made Duke of Shanyang; five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses were bestowed.

entries.zh: 伏威遣其將陳正通、徐紹宗以兵會，取世充之梁郡。
entries.en: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with troops to join the campaign and captured Liang Prefecture from Wang Shichong.
entries.literal: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with troops to join up and took Shichong's Liang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 又遣將王雄誕討李子通於杭州，禽以獻。
entries.en: He also sent his general Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong at Hangzhou and took him prisoner for presentation at court.
entries.literal: He also sent General Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong at Hangzhou and captured him for presentation.

entries.zh: 破汪華於歙州。
entries.en: He defeated Wang Hua at She Prefecture.
entries.literal: He defeated Wang Hua at Shezhou.

entries.zh: 盡有江東、淮南地，南屬嶺，東至於海。
entries.en: He came to hold all of Jiangdong and the Huai region, his domain reaching south to the mountain ranges and east to the sea.
entries.literal: He fully possessed the lands of Jiangdong and Huainan, south to the ranges, east to the sea.

entries.zh: 秦王已平劉黑闥，師次曹、兗，伏威懼，乃入朝。
entries.en: The Prince of Qin had already pacified Liu Heidan and halted his army in Cao and Yan. Fuwei grew fearful and came to court in person.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qin had pacified Liu Heidan; his army halted at Cao and Yan; Fuwei was afraid and entered court.

entries.zh: 詔拜太子太保兼行臺尚書令，留京師，位在齊王元吉上，以寵之。
entries.en: An edict appointed him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with concurrent duties as Director of the Executive Secretariat and kept him at the capital. His precedence was set above Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, a mark of special favor.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent concurrently Executive Secretariat Director, kept at the capital; his rank was above Prince Qi Li Yuanji, as a mark of favor.

entries.zh: 伏威好神仙長年術，餌雲母被毒，武德七年二月，暴卒。
entries.en: Fuwei was devoted to the arts of immortality and long life. He ingested mica and was poisoned by it. In the second month of the seventh year of Wude he died suddenly.
entries.literal: Fuwei loved the arts of immortals and longevity, swallowed mica and was poisoned; in the second month of the seventh year of Wude he died suddenly.

entries.zh: 初，公祏反，矯伏威令以紿眾，趙郡王孝恭既平公祏，得反書以聞。
entries.en: Earlier, when Fu Gongshi rebelled, he forged orders in Fuwei's name to deceive the troops. After Li Xiaogong, Prince of Zhao Commandery, had pacified Gongshi, he obtained the rebel correspondence and reported it to the throne.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gongshi rebelled he forged Fuwei's order to deceive the masses; Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong after pacifying Gongshi obtained the rebel letters and reported.

entries.zh: 高祖追其官，削屬籍，沒入家產。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu stripped him of his offices, removed his name from the imperial clan register, and confiscated his family property.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu stripped his offices, removed him from the clan register, and confiscated family property.

entries.zh: 貞觀元年，太宗知其冤，詔復官爵，以公禮葬，仍還其子封。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong, recognizing that he had been wronged, ordered his offices and titles restored, gave him burial with full honors, and returned his son's fief.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong knew he had been wronged, ordered restoration of office and titles, burial with due rites, and return of his son's fief.

entries.zh: 雄誕愛人，善撫士，能致下死力，每破城邑，整眾山立，無絲毫犯。
entries.en: Wang Xiongdan cared for his men and knew how to win their loyalty so that they would die for him. Whenever he captured a city he held his troops in strict formation, and not the least disorder was permitted.
entries.literal: Xiongdan loved people and well comforted troops, could make subordinates die for him; whenever he took a city he arrayed troops standing like a mountain with not the slightest violation.

entries.zh: 死之日，江南士庶為流涕。
entries.en: On the day of his death, scholars and commoners throughout the Jiangnan region wept for him.
entries.literal: On the day of his death gentry and commoners of Jiangnan wept for him.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉其節，以子世果襲宜春郡封。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu honored his loyalty. His son Shiguo inherited the fief of Yichun.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised his integrity; his son Shiguo inherited the Yichun fief.

entries.zh: 太宗立，優詔贈左驍衛大將軍、越州都督，謚曰忠。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, an edict of special favor posthumously appointed him Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General and Governor of Yuezhou, with the posthumous title Loyal.
entries.literal: When Taizong ascended an excellent edict posthumously granted Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General, Governor of Yuezhou, posthumous name Zhong (Loyal).

entries.zh: 世果，垂拱初至廣州都督、安西大都護。
entries.en: Shiguo, at the beginning of the Chuigong era, rose to Governor of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of Anxi.
entries.literal: Shiguo, at the beginning of Chuigong reached Governor of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of Anxi.

entries.zh: 張士貴，虢州盧氏人，本名忽峍。
entries.en: Zhang Shigui was a native of Lushi in Guozhou. His original name was Hula.
entries.literal: Zhang Shigui was a native of Lushi in Guozhou; his original name was Hula.

entries.zh: 彎弓百五十斤，左右射無空發。
entries.en: He could draw a bow of one hundred fifty jin and shoot to left or right without ever missing.
entries.literal: He bent a bow of one hundred fifty jin; shooting left and right none missed.

entries.zh: 隋大業末，起為盜，攻剽城邑，當時患之，號「忽峍賊」。
entries.en: At the end of the Sui, in the Daye era, he took to banditry and raided cities. The people feared him and called him the "Hula Bandit."
entries.literal: At the end of Sui Daye he rose as bandit attacking cities; people then feared him and called him "Hula Bandit."

entries.zh: 高祖移檄招之，士貴即降，拜右光祿大夫。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu issued a proclamation summoning him to submit. Zhang Shigui surrendered at once and was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendor.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu moved a proclamation to summon him; Shigui at once submitted, was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendor.

entries.zh: 從征伐有功，賜爵新野縣公。
entries.en: He followed the armies on campaign and won distinction, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.
entries.literal: Following campaigns he had merit, was enfeoffed Duke of Xinye county.

entries.zh: 又從平洛，授虢州刺史。
entries.en: He again followed the campaign to pacify Luoyang and was appointed Governor of Guozhou.
entries.literal: Again following pacification of Luoyang he was made Governor of Guozhou.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「顧令卿衣錦晝遊耳。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "I meant for you to return home in glory, clad in brocade by daylight."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Intended to let you, sir, return home in brocade by day."

entries.zh: 進封虢國公、右屯衛大將軍。
entries.en: He was further enfeoffed as Duke of Guo and appointed Right Defender of the Encampment Grand General.
entries.literal: Advanced enfeoffment as Duke of Guo state, Right Defender of the Encampment Grand General.

entries.zh: 貞觀七年，為龔州道行軍總管，破反獠還，太宗聞其冒矢石先登，勞之曰：「嘗聞以忠報國者不顧身，於公見之。」
entries.en: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he served as commander of the Gongzhou circuit campaign, crushed the rebellious Lao tribes, and returned. Emperor Taizong heard that he had charged ahead through flying arrows and stones and comforted him, saying, "I have heard that those who repay the state with loyalty do not spare their own lives—and in you I see it."
entries.literal: Seventh year Zhenguan, was Gongzhou circuit campaigning commander, broke rebellious Lao and returned; Taizong heard he braved arrows and stones first up, comforted him: "I have heard that those who repay the state with loyalty disregard their bodies—on you I see it."

entries.zh: 累遷左領軍大將軍。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching the post of Left Defender Grand General.
entries.literal: Repeated promotion to Left Defender Grand General.

entries.zh: 顯慶初，卒，贈荊州都督，陪葬昭陵。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Xianqing era he died. He was posthumously appointed Governor of Jingzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
entries.literal: Beginning of Xianqing he died; posthumously made Governor of Jingzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling.

entries.zh: 高祖遣雁門人元普賜金券，會頡利亦召之，意猶豫。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sent Yuan Pu of Yanmen to present a gold bond of safe conduct. At the same time Khan Jieli summoned him as well, and Yuan Junzhang wavered between the two.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent Yuan Pu of Yanmen to bestow a gold certificate; at the same time Jieli also summoned him; he was still hesitant.

entries.zh: 子孝政諫曰：「大人許唐降，又貳頡利，自取亡也。
entries.en: His son Yuan Xiaozheng admonished him, saying, "Father, you pledged yourself to Tang, yet now you hedge toward Jieli. You are courting your own ruin.
entries.literal: His son Xiaozheng remonstrated: "Father, you promised Tang you would submit, yet you waver toward Jieli—you invite your own destruction.

entries.zh: 今糧盡眾攜，不即決，恐衿肘變生，孝政不忍見禍之酷也！」
entries.en: Our provisions are gone and the men are falling away. If you do not act now, I fear disaster will strike at any moment. I cannot bear to watch such ruin overtake us!"
entries.literal: Now grain is exhausted and the masses are divided; if you do not decide at once, I fear trouble will arise at the elbow; Xiaozheng cannot bear to see such cruel disaster!"

entries.zh: 即單騎南奔，君璋喻返之，召眾與議。
entries.en: He spurred his horse south alone to defect. Yuan Junzhang sent after him and called the leaders together for counsel.
entries.literal: He alone rode south to flee; Junzhang sent word for him to return and summoned the assembly to deliberate.

entries.zh: 恒安人郭子威曰：「恒安故王者都，山川足以自固，突厥方強，我援之，可觀天下變，何遽降？」
entries.en: Guo Ziwei of Heng'an said, "This was once a royal capital. The terrain is strong enough to hold. The Turks are at their height—we need only stand with them and watch how the empire turns. Why rush to surrender?"
entries.literal: Guo Ziwei of Heng'an said: "Heng'an was the capital of former kings; mountains and rivers suffice for self-defense; the Turks are just strong—we aid them and can watch changes in the realm—why submit in haste?"

entries.zh: 君璋然之，執元普送突厥，頡利德之，遣以錦裘羊馬。
entries.en: Yuan Junzhang agreed, seized Yuan Pu, and handed him over to the Turks. Jieli was pleased and sent him brocade robes, sheep, and horses in reward.
entries.literal: Junzhang agreed, seized Yuan Pu and sent him to the Turks; Jieli was pleased and sent brocade robes, sheep, and horses.

entries.zh: 其下怨，投書於門曰：「不早附唐，父子誅。」
entries.en: His men grew resentful and nailed a placard to the gate: "Because you would not submit to Tang in time, father and son will be put to death."
entries.literal: His subordinates were resentful and posted a letter at the gate saying: "By not submitting to Tang early, father and son will be executed."

entries.zh: 孝政懼，欲自歸，為君璋所拘。
entries.en: Yuan Xiaozheng, in fear, tried to defect on his own but Yuan Junzhang had him detained.
entries.literal: Xiaozheng was afraid and wished to surrender himself but was detained by Junzhang.

entries.zh: 與突厥寇馬邑，犯太原，邊人苦之。
entries.en: He joined the Turks in raiding Mayi and striking at Taiyuan, and the frontier people groaned under the devastation.
entries.literal: With the Turks he raided Mayi and invaded Taiyuan; the border people suffered.

entries.zh: 見頡利政亂，知將亡，遂率所部降，頡利追，擊走其兵。
entries.en: When he saw that Jieli's rule was collapsing and knew the Turks were finished, he led his followers in surrender. Jieli pursued and routed his rear guard.
entries.literal: Seeing Jieli's government in disorder and knowing he would perish, he then led his division to submit; Jieli pursued and struck away his troops.

entries.zh: 宇文化及至山東，遣使招藝，藝曰：「我隋舊臣，今大行顛覆，義不辱於賊。」
entries.en: When Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to win Luo Yi over. Luo Yi replied, "I am a loyal servant of the Sui. The dynasty lies in ruins—I will not endure insult from a rebel."
entries.literal: When Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong he sent envoys to recruit Yi; Yi said: "I am an old minister of Sui; now the Great Line is overturned—I will not suffer disgrace from bandits."

entries.zh: 斬使者，為煬帝發喪三日。
entries.en: He executed the envoys and observed three days of mourning for Emperor Yang.
entries.literal: He beheaded the envoys and held mourning for Emperor Yang for three days.

entries.zh: 時竇建德、高開道亦遣使於藝，藝謂官屬曰：「建德等皆劇賊，不足共功名，唐公起兵據關中，民望所系，王業必成，吾決歸之。
entries.en: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys. Luo Yi told his staff, "Jiande and his ilk are nothing but fierce bandits, unfit to share in great deeds. The Duke of Tang has raised his banner in Guanzhong, where the people's hopes rest. His cause is certain to triumph. I have decided to join him.
entries.literal: At that time Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys to Yi; Yi told his officials: "Jiande and the rest are fierce bandits, unworthy to share glory with; the Duke of Tang has risen holding Guanzhong, where the people's hopes lie—his royal enterprise is sure to succeed—I am resolved to join him.

entries.zh: 敢異議者戮！」
entries.en: Whoever disagrees—off with his head!"
entries.literal: Who dares dissent—execute!"

entries.zh: 會張道源撫輯山東，亦諭藝降，武德二年，乃奉表以地歸。
entries.en: Zhang Daoyuan was then pacifying Shandong and likewise urged him to submit. In the second year of Wude, Luo Yi presented a memorial offering his territory to Tang.
entries.literal: At that time Zhang Daoyuan was pacifying Shandong and also urged Yi to submit; in the second year of Wude he then presented a memorial returning the land.

entries.zh: 詔封燕王，賜姓，豫屬籍。
entries.en: An edict enfeoffed him as King of Yan, granted him the imperial surname, and enrolled him in the clan register.
entries.literal: An edict enfeoffed him King of Yan, granted surname, entered imperial clan register.

entries.zh: 數與建德戰，多所禽馘。
entries.en: He fought Dou Jiande repeatedly and took many prisoners and heads.
entries.literal: He repeatedly fought Jiande and captured and beheaded many.

entries.zh: 秦王擊劉黑闥，高祖詔藝弟監門將軍壽以兵從，藝自率眾數萬破劉什善、張君立於徐河。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qin campaigned against Liu Heidan, Emperor Gaozu ordered Luo Yi's younger brother, gate guard general Luo Shou, to join the army. Luo Yi himself led tens of thousands of men and at the Xu River defeated Liu Shishan and Zhang Junli.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qin attacked Liu Heidan; Emperor Gaozu ordered Yi's younger brother, Gate Guard General Shou, to follow with troops; Yi himself led tens of thousands and at Xu River defeated Liu Shishan and Zhang Junli.

entries.zh: 黑闥引突厥入寇，藝復以兵與皇太子建成會洺州，遂請入朝。
entries.en: When Liu Heidan brought the Turks in to raid, Luo Yi again marched with Crown Prince Li Jiancheng to Mingzhou. He then asked permission to come to court.
entries.literal: Heidan led Turks to invade; Yi again joined Crown Prince Li Jiancheng at Mingzhou with troops, then requested to enter court.

entries.zh: 帝厚禮之，拜左翊衛大將軍。
entries.en: The emperor received him with great honor and appointed him Left Wing Guard Grand General.
entries.literal: The Emperor treated him generously and appointed Left Wing Guard Grand General.

entries.zh: 藝負其功，且貴重不少屈，秦王左右嘗至其營，藝{疻}辱之。
entries.en: Luo Yi swaggered over his achievements and, proud of his rank, rarely humbled himself. When attendants of the Prince of Qin visited his camp, Luo Yi publicly humiliated them.
entries.literal: Yi relied on his merit and was noble and important, seldom bending; the Prince of Qin's attendants once came to his camp and Yi insulted them.

entries.zh: 高祖怒，以屬吏，久乃釋。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was furious and turned him over to the judicial authorities. Only after a long interval was he released.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu was angry and handed him to the law officers; after a long time released him.

entries.zh: 時突厥放橫，藉藝威名欲憚虜，詔以本官領天節軍將，鎮涇州。
entries.en: The Turks were then running wild on the frontier. The court hoped to use Luo Yi's name to intimidate them and ordered him, in his former rank, to command the Tianjie Army and garrison Jingzhou.
entries.literal: At that time the Turks ran rampant; borrowing Yi's prestige to awe the barbarians, an edict had him in his former office lead the Tianjie Army General, garrisoning Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖兵起，召之，不從。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu raised his army, he summoned Wang Junguo, who refused to come.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's army rose he summoned him; he did not follow.

entries.zh: 歸李密，密不甚禮，乃歸國。
entries.en: He went over to Li Mi, who treated him coldly, and then submitted to Tang.
entries.literal: He returned to Li Mi; Mi did not greatly honor him; he then returned to the state.

entries.zh: 授上柱國、假河內太守、常山郡公，遷遼州刺史，徙封上谷，從戰東都有功，為右武衛將軍。
entries.en: He was appointed Upper Pillar of State, acting governor of Henei, and Duke of Changshan, then transferred to Governor of Liaozhou and re-enfeoffed in Shanggu. He followed the eastern capital campaign with distinction and was made Right Martial Guard General.
entries.literal: Appointed Upper Pillar of State, Acting Governor of Henei, Duke of Changshan, moved to Governor of Liaozhou, transferred enfeoffment to Shanggu, followed campaign at eastern capital with merit, made Right Martial Guard General.

entries.zh: 詔勞之曰：「爾以十三人破賊萬，自古以少制眾，無有也！」
entries.en: An edict praised him: "You routed ten thousand rebels with thirteen men. Never in history has so small a force overcome so large."
entries.literal: An edict comforted him saying: "You with thirteen men broke ten thousand bandits—from antiquity using few to control many, there has been nothing like it!"

entries.zh: 賜雜彩百段。
entries.en: He was granted one hundred bolts of patterned silk.
entries.literal: Granted one hundred bolts of mixed silks.

entries.zh: 別下軒轅、羅川二縣，破世充將魏隱，擊糧道緱氏，沈米艘三十柁。
entries.en: He separately reduced Xuanyuan and Luochuan counties, defeated Wang Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Goushi, and sank thirty supply barges.
entries.literal: Separately he descended Xuanyuan and Luochuan two counties, defeated Shichong's general Wei Yin, struck the grain route at Gongshi, sank thirty grain boats.

entries.zh: 進爵彭國公，鎮幽州。
entries.en: He was advanced to Duke of Peng and stationed at Youzhou.
entries.literal: Advanced enfeoffment Duke of Peng, garrisoned Youzhou.

entries.zh: 擊突厥，俘斬二千，獲馬五千匹。
entries.en: He campaigned against the Turks, capturing and killing two thousand men and seizing five thousand horses.
entries.literal: He attacked the Turks, captured and beheaded two thousand, obtained five thousand horses.

entries.zh: 入朝，帝賜所乘馬，令自廷中乘以出，謂侍臣曰：「昔藺相如叱秦王，目眥皆烈。
entries.en: He came to court. The emperor gave him the horse he himself had been riding and told him to mount in the hall and ride out before the court. He said to his ministers, "Long ago Lin Xiangru faced down the King of Qin until his eyes blazed with fury.
entries.literal: He entered court; the Emperor bestowed the horse he himself rode, ordered him to mount from within the hall and ride out, telling attendants: "Formerly Lin Xiangru berated the King of Qin until his eyes bulged with rage.

entries.zh: 君廓往擊建德，李勣遏之，至發憤大呼，鼻耳皆流血，其勇何特古人哉！
entries.en: When Wang Junguo fought Dou Jiande, Li Ji had to hold him back. He raged and shouted until blood ran from his nose and ears. What ancient hero matched such fury?
entries.literal: When Junguo went to strike Jiande, Li Ji restrained him; he even vented fury with a great shout, nose and ears all bleeding—how does his courage differ from men of old?

entries.zh: 朕當不以例賞。」
entries.en: I will not reward him by the ordinary standard."
entries.literal: I shall not reward him by the usual measure."

entries.zh: 乃賜錦袍金帶，還幽州。
entries.en: He granted him a brocade robe and gold belt and sent him back to Youzhou.
entries.literal: He then granted brocade robe and gold belt and returned him to Youzhou.

entries.zh: 武周死，突厥以君璋為大行臺，統武周部曲，使郁射設監兵，與舊將高滿政夜襲代州，不克。
entries.en: After Liu Wuzhou died, the Turks appointed Yuan Junzhang Grand Executive and placed him in command of Wuzhou's former troops. They sent Yushe Shad to oversee the army; together with the veteran general Gao Manzheng, he launched a night attack on Dai Prefecture but failed to take it.
entries.literal: Wuzhou died; the Turks made Junzhang Grand Executive, commanding Wuzhou's former troops, and sent Yushe Shad to supervise the army. Together with the veteran general Gao Manzheng, he launched a night attack on Dai Prefecture but did not succeed.

entries.zh: 高祖遣使招之，賜鐵券，約不死。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to summon him, granted him an iron certificate guaranteeing he would not be put to death, and pledged him immunity.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to summon him, granted iron certificate, covenant of no death.

entries.zh: 君璋拒命，進寇代州，刺史王孝德拒卻之。
entries.en: Yuan Junzhang refused to obey and marched against Dai Prefecture. The prefect Wang Xiaode drove him back.
entries.literal: Junzhang refused the command and advanced to raid Dai Prefecture; Prefect Wang Xiaode repelled him.

entries.zh: 滿政勸君璋曰：「夷狄無禮，豈可北面臣之？
entries.en: Gao Manzheng urged Yuan Junzhang, saying, "The barbarians know no propriety. How can we bow north and serve them as subjects?
entries.literal: Manzheng urged Junzhang: "The barbarians are without propriety—how can one face north and serve them as subject?

entries.zh: 請盡殺其眾以歸唐。」
entries.en: Let us slaughter their entire force and return to Tang."
entries.literal: Please kill all their followers and return to Tang."

entries.zh: 君璋不從。
entries.en: Yuan Junzhang would not agree.
entries.literal: Junzhang did not follow.

entries.zh: 而馬邑困於兵，人厭亂，滿政因眾不忍，夜脅君璋，君璋奔突厥。
entries.en: Mayi was ravaged by warfare and the people were sick of chaos. Gao Manzheng played on their discontent and by night forced Yuan Junzhang's hand. Junzhang fled to the Turks.
entries.literal: Mayi was weary of war; the people hated disorder; Manzheng used the masses' impatience, by night coerced Junzhang; Junzhang fled to the Turks.

entries.zh: 滿政以城歸，詔拜朔州總管，封榮國公。
entries.en: Gao Manzheng handed the city over to Tang. An edict appointed him Governor of Shuozhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Rong.
entries.literal: Manzheng surrendered the city and returned; an edict appointed him Governor of Shuozhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Rong.

entries.zh: 君璋引突厥攻陷馬邑，殺滿政，夷其黨，乃去，退保恒安。
entries.en: Yuan Junzhang led the Turks to storm Mayi, killed Gao Manzheng, and wiped out his followers. He then withdrew to hold Heng'an.
entries.literal: Junzhang led Turks to attack and take Mayi, killed Manzheng, exterminated his faction, then left and withdrew to guard Heng'an.

entries.zh: 其部皆中國人，多叛去，君璋窮，乃降，自請鄣虜贖罪。
entries.en: Most of his followers were Chinese subjects, and many deserted him. Reduced to desperation, Yuan Junzhang surrendered and asked to be posted on the frontier to redeem his crimes.
entries.literal: His troops were mostly Chinese; many rebelled and left; Junzhang was destitute and then submitted, himself requesting to guard the frontier and atone for guilt.

entries.zh: 會大都督廬江王瑗反，欲奪君廓兵以委王詵。
entries.en: When the Grand Commander, Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan, rebelled, he tried to strip Wang Junguo of his command and hand the troops to Wang Shen.
entries.literal: At that time the Grand Commander Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan rebelled and wished to seize Junguo's troops to entrust to Wang Shen.

entries.zh: 君廓本紿瑗使亂為己功，乃從數騎候詵，留騎於外，曰：「聞呼聲則入。」
entries.en: Wang Junguo had originally tricked Li Yuan into rebellion so that he might claim the credit for putting it down. He rode with a few followers to visit Wang Shen, leaving his men outside with orders: "At the sound of a cry, rush in."
entries.literal: Junguo had originally deceived Yuan to make disorder his own merit; he then followed with several horsemen to wait on Shen, leaving horsemen outside, saying: "If you hear a shout, enter."

entries.zh: 乃獨款詵，詐曰：「有急變，當白！」
entries.en: He then went in alone to see Wang Shen and lied: "There is an emergency—you must be told at once!"
entries.literal: He then alone paid a cordial visit to Shen, falsely saying: "There is an urgent change—you must report it!"

entries.zh: 詵方沐，握發出，即斬之，因執瑗。
entries.en: Wang Shen was bathing. He came out holding up his hair; Wang Junguo beheaded him at once and then seized Li Yuan.
entries.literal: Shen was bathing; he came out holding up his hair, whereupon Junguo beheaded him and seized Yuan.

entries.zh: 以功授幽州都督，瑗家口悉賜之，進左光祿大夫，賜帛千段。
entries.en: For this feat he was appointed Governor of Youzhou. Li Yuan's entire household was given to him as slaves. He was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendor and granted one thousand bolts of silk.
entries.literal: For merit appointed Governor of Youzhou; Yuan's household all bestowed on him; advanced Left Grand Master of Splendor, granted one thousand bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，進開府儀同三司。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Luo Yi was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
entries.literal: When Taizong ascended he was advanced to Kaifu Yitong Sansi.

entries.zh: 藝內懼，乃圖反，詭言閱武。
entries.en: Luo Yi was inwardly terrified and plotted rebellion, announcing under false pretenses that he would hold a military review.
entries.literal: Yi was inwardly afraid and then plotted rebellion, falsely announcing a review of troops.

entries.zh: 兵既集，稱被密詔入朝，軍至豳，治中趙慈皓出謁，遂據州。
entries.en: Once the troops were assembled, he claimed he had received a secret edict summoning him to court and marched to Bin Prefecture. When Assistant Governor Zhao Cihao came out to greet him, Luo Yi seized the city.
entries.literal: When troops were gathered he claimed to have a secret edict to enter court; the army reached Bin; Assistant Governor Zhao Cihao came out to greet; he then seized the prefecture.

entries.zh: 帝命長孫無忌、尉遲敬德擊之，未至，慈皓與統軍楊岌謀誅藝，藝覺，執慈皓。
entries.en: The emperor dispatched Zhangsun Wuji and Yuchi Jingde against him. Before they arrived, Zhao Cihao and the army commander Yang Ji plotted to assassinate Luo Yi. Luo Yi discovered the plot and seized Zhao Cihao.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji and Yuchi Jingde to attack; before they arrived, Cihao with Commander Yang Ji plotted to kill Yi; Yi perceived it and seized Cihao.

entries.zh: 岌居外，即攻之，藝敗，棄妻子，從數百騎奔突厥。
entries.en: Yang Ji, stationed outside the city, attacked at once. Luo Yi was defeated. He abandoned his wife and children and fled to the Turks with only a few hundred horsemen.
entries.literal: Ji was outside and at once attacked; Yi was defeated, abandoned wife and children, followed by several hundred horsemen fled to the Turks.

entries.zh: 抵寧州，騎稍亡，左右斬之，傳首，梟於都市。
entries.en: At Ningzhou his followers dwindled away. His own men cut off his head and sent it in. It was displayed on the execution ground in the capital.
entries.literal: Reaching Ningzhou, horsemen gradually deserted; his attendants beheaded him and sent the head; it was displayed in the capital market.

entries.zh: 壽時為利州都督，亦及誅。
entries.en: His brother Luo Shou, who was then Governor of Lizhou, was executed as well.
entries.literal: Shou was then Governor of Lizhou and was also executed.

entries.zh: 杜闞王李苑羅王
entries.en: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, and Wang
entries.literal: Du, Kan, Wang, Li, Yuan, Luo, Wang

entries.zh: 時茂州俚童張仲文自稱天子，有司論斥乘輿有罪當死，攝刑部尚書韋挺奏：「童乃妖言，無死坐。」
entries.en: At that time a Li youth of Mao Prefecture, Zhang Zhongwen, proclaimed himself emperor; the responsible offices held that insulting the imperial carriage warranted death; Acting Minister of Justice Wei Ting argued, "A child's wild talk does not carry the death penalty."
entries.literal: At the time a Li boy of Mao Prefecture, Zhang Zhongwen, styled himself Son of Heaven; the responsible offices judged that denouncing the imperial carriage was a capital crime; Acting Minister of Justice Wei Ting memorialized: "The boy spoke demonic words — there is no capital offense."

entries.zh: 帝怒曰：「爾作威福於下，而歸虐朕耶！」
entries.en: The emperor flared up: "You play the tyrant below and then make me out the cruel one!"
entries.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "You wield authority below and then lay cruelty on me!"

entries.zh: 挺失據趨出。
entries.en: Ting lost his composure and fled the hall.
entries.literal: Ting lost his composure and hurried out.

entries.zh: 亮為挺直之，帝曰：「公欲取剛正名乎？」
entries.en: Liang spoke up for Ting; the emperor said, "Are you trying to win a name for righteous remonstrance?"
entries.literal: Liang spoke up for Ting; the Emperor said: "Do you wish to win a reputation for stern integrity?"

entries.zh: 亮不謝，帝寤曰：「甯屈我，以申公之請。」
entries.en: Liang did not back down; the emperor recovered and said, "I would rather yield than refuse your plea."
entries.literal: Liang did not apologize; the Emperor came to his senses and said: "I would rather bend myself to grant your request."

entries.zh: 童免死。
entries.en: The boy was spared.
entries.literal: The boy was spared death.

entries.zh: 房玄齡以亮沈果有謀，白秦王，引為車騎將軍。
entries.en: Fang Xuanling, seeing Liang's depth, resolve, and cunning, recommended him to the Prince of Qin, who made him Cavalry General.
entries.literal: Fang Xuanling, because Liang was deep, resolute, and resourceful, informed the Prince of Qin and had him brought in as Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 隱太子將作難，命亮統左右千人之洛陽，陰結山東豪傑以備變。
entries.en: When the Hidden Crown Prince plotted rebellion, he ordered Liang to command a thousand guardsmen at Luoyang and secretly rally powerful men of the east against any turn of events.
entries.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince was about to raise trouble; he ordered Liang to command a thousand men of the Left and Right Guards at Luoyang and secretly rally Shandong magnates against contingencies.

entries.zh: 齊王告亮反，高祖以屬吏詰訊，終無所言，乃得釋。
entries.en: The Prince of Qi accused Liang of rebellion; Gaozu had him interrogated by the responsible offices, but Liang said nothing throughout and was released.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qi reported Liang's rebellion; Gaozu handed him to officials for interrogation, but he finally said nothing and was released.

entries.zh: 王即位，除右衛將軍，封長平郡公。
entries.en: When the prince became emperor, he was made Right Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.
entries.literal: When the Prince acceded, Liang was made Right Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.

entries.zh: 累遷御史大夫，進封鄅國公，食益州戶五百。
entries.en: He rose to Censor-in-Chief, was advanced to Duke of Yu, and drew income from five hundred households in Yi Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was promoted through Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Duke of Yu state with an income of five hundred households in Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 歷豳夏汭鄜三州都督、相州長史，徙鄖國。
entries.en: He served as military governor of Bin, Xia, Rui, and Fu and as chief administrator of Xiang, then was transferred to the title Duke of Yun.
entries.literal: He served as military governor of Bin, Xia, Rui, and Fu prefectures and as chief administrator of Xiang, then was transferred to Duke of Yun.

entries.zh: 召拜工部尚書。
entries.en: He was recalled and appointed Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 亮為政多伺察，發擿隱微，示神明，抑強恤弱，所至有績。
entries.en: In office he relied heavily on surveillance, ferreting out hidden wrongdoing and projecting an air of omniscience, curbing the powerful and aiding the weak; wherever he served he left a record of success.
entries.literal: In governing Liang much surveilled and exposed hidden matters, displaying sagacity, restraining the strong and succoring the weak — wherever he went he had achievement.

entries.zh: 拜太子詹事，出為洛州都督。
entries.en: He was appointed Chief Steward of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo.
entries.literal: He was appointed Chief Steward of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo Prefecture.

entries.zh: 侯君集已誅，以刑部尚書參預朝政。
entries.en: After Hou Junji's execution he was made Minister of Justice and joined in deliberations on state affairs.
entries.literal: After Hou Junji was executed, he was made Minister of Justice and took part in court deliberations.

entries.zh: 侯君集，豳州三水人。
entries.en: Hou Junji was a native of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.
entries.literal: Hou Junji, a native of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以材雄稱。
entries.en: He was renowned for his martial prowess.
entries.literal: He was famed for martial prowess.

entries.zh: 少事秦王幕府，從征討有功，擢累左虞候、車騎將軍，封全椒縣子。
entries.en: In his youth he served on the staff of the Prince of Qin; he followed him on campaigns and distinguished himself, rising through the posts of Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General and receiving the title viscount of Quanjiao County.
entries.literal: In youth he served in the Prince of Qin's staff; following campaigns and punitive expeditions he had merit, was promoted through Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General, and enfeoffed as viscount of Quanjiao County.

entries.zh: 預誅隱太子尤力。
entries.en: He played an outstanding part in the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince.
entries.literal: He took exceptional part in executing the Hidden Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 王即位，拜左衛將軍，進封潞國公，邑千戶。
entries.en: When the prince became emperor, he was appointed Left Guard General and advanced to Duke of Lu with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: When the Prince acceded, Junji was appointed Left Guard General, advanced to Duke of Lu with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 貞觀四年，遷兵部尚書，俄檢校吏部尚書，參議朝政。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhenguan (630) he was made Minister of War, and shortly thereafter acting Minister of Personnel, joining in deliberations on state policy.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of War; soon he was made acting Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court affairs.

entries.zh: 初，太宗嘗以山東士人尚閥閱，後雖衰，子孫猶負世望，嫁娶必多取貲，故人謂之賣昏。
entries.en: Taizong had long noted that eastern gentry families prized pedigree. Though their power had waned, their descendants still traded on old prestige and demanded lavish bride-prices — what people called "selling a marriage."
entries.literal: Earlier Taizong had observed that the gentry east of the mountains prized pedigree; though later in decline, their descendants still bore the prestige of old families and demanded heavy bride-price at marriage, so people called it "selling a wedding."

entries.zh: 由是詔士廉與韋挺、岑文本、令狐德棻責天下譜諜，參考史傳，檢正真偽，進忠賢，退悖惡，先宗室，後外戚，退新門，進舊望，右膏粱，左寒畯，合二百九十三姓，千六百五十一家，為九等，號曰《氏族志》，而崔幹仍居第一。
entries.en: He therefore charged Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, and Linghu Defen to compile the empire's genealogies, cross-check them against history, promote the worthy and demote the corrupt, rank the imperial clan before affinal kin, favor old houses over parvenus, and place the wellborn above the humble. The result listed 293 surnames in 1,651 households across nine grades, published as Records of Clans — yet Cui Gan still headed the list.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shilian, together with Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, and Linghu Defen, to compile the empire's genealogies, consult historical records, verify truth and falsehood, advance the loyal and worthy and demote the perverse and wicked, put the imperial clan first and affinal kin after, demote new families and advance old prestige, favor the wellborn on the right and the humble on the left — in all two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one households in nine grades, titled Records of Clans — yet Cui Gan still ranked first.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「我于崔、盧、李、鄭無嫌，顧其世衰，不復冠冕，猶恃舊地以取貲，不肖子偃然自高，販鬻松檟，不解人間何為貴之？
entries.en: The emperor said: "I have nothing against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng families, but their day is past. They no longer produce ministers, yet still milk their old prestige for money. Their worthless sons strut as if noble and peddle funeral timber for profit — why does anyone still honor them?
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "I bear no grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans, but their age has declined and they no longer fill high office, yet still rely on old standing to extract wealth; unworthy sons hold themselves aloft and trade in pine and cypress for profit — I do not understand why the world still esteems them.

entries.zh: 齊據河北，梁、陳在江南，雖有人物，偏方下國，無可貴者，故以崔、盧、王、謝為重。
entries.en: Qi held the north, Liang and Chen the south — talented men they had, but as marginal states they counted for little. That is why the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were once so prized.
entries.literal: Qi held Hebei, Liang and Chen were in the south — though they had men of talent, they were peripheral lesser states with nothing to esteem, so the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were held in weight.

entries.zh: 今謀士勞臣以忠孝學藝從我定天下者，何容納貨舊門，向聲背實，買昏為榮耶？
entries.en: The counselors and warriors who followed me in loyalty, learning, and merit to win the empire — how can they pay bride-price to decayed old clans, chase empty reputation over real worth, and treat a bought marriage as an honor?
entries.literal: Now the strategists and toiling ministers who followed me in loyalty, filial piety, learning, and arts to settle the realm — how can they accept goods from old houses, heed reputation over substance, and take buying a marriage as glory?

entries.zh: 太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，其次有爵為公、卿、大夫，世世不絕，此謂之門戶。
entries.en: First comes establishing virtue, then merit, then literary legacy, then hereditary rank as duke, minister, or grandee — that is what makes a true house.
entries.literal: Supreme is establishing virtue, next establishing merit, next establishing words, next enfeoffment as duke, minister, or grandee passing from generation to generation without end — this is what is called a house.

entries.zh: 今皆反是，豈不惑邪？
entries.en: Today everything is reversed — is that not madness?
entries.literal: Now all is the reverse — is this not delusion?

entries.zh: 朕以今日冠冕為等級高下。」
entries.en: I will rank families by the offices they hold today."
entries.literal: I take today's caps and sashes as the measure of rank high and low."

entries.zh: 遂以崔幹為第三姓，班其書天下。
entries.en: He then placed Cui Gan as the third surname and had the register published empire-wide.
entries.literal: He then placed Cui Gan as the third surname and promulgated the book throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 高祖入關，召補大丞相府司錄參軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered the passes, Wei was summoned to serve as registrar on the grand chancellor's staff.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes, Wei was summoned to serve as Registrar on the Grand Chancellor's staff.

entries.zh: 方天下亂，禮典湮缺，威多識朝廷故事，乃裁定制度。
entries.en: With the realm in disorder and ritual codes lost, Wei knew many court precedents and thereupon fixed institutions and regulations.
entries.literal: With the realm in turmoil and ritual codes lost, Wei knew many court precedents and thereupon fixed institutions and regulations.

entries.zh: 帝語裴寂曰：「威，今之叔孫通也。」
entries.en: The emperor told Pei Ji, "Wei is today's Shusun Tong."
entries.literal: The emperor said to Pei Ji, "Wei is today's Shusun Tong."

entries.zh: 武德元年，授內史令。
entries.en: In the first year of Wude he was appointed director of the palace secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 每論政事得失，必陳古為諭，帝益親矚，嘗引入臥內，謂曰：「昔周有八柱國，吾與公家是也。
entries.en: Whenever policy was debated he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor grew still closer, once brought him into his private quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.
entries.literal: Whenever political gains and losses were discussed he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor drew closer to him, once brought him into the inner sleeping quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.

entries.zh: 今我為天子，而公為內史令，事固有不等耶？」
entries.en: Now I am emperor and you are director of the palace secretariat — surely our stations cannot be equal?"
entries.literal: Now I am Son of Heaven and you are Director of the Palace Secretariat — are our positions not bound to differ?"

entries.zh: 威懼，頓首謝曰：「臣家在漢，再為外戚。
entries.en: Wei was frightened and kowtowed, saying, "My house in Han was twice an imperial affinal clan.
entries.literal: Wei was afraid and kowtowed in apology, saying, "My family in Han was twice imperial affines.

entries.zh: 至元魏，有三皇后。
entries.en: Under Northern Wei our house produced three empresses.
entries.literal: Under Northern Wei we had three empresses from our house.

entries.zh: 今陛下龍興，臣復以姻戚進，夙夜懼不克任。」
entries.en: Now Your Majesty has risen, and I have again advanced through marriage ties — morning and night I fear I am not equal to the charge."
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty's rise has again advanced me through marriage ties, and morning and night I fear I cannot bear the burden."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「公以三後族誇我邪！
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, "Are you boasting to me with your three empresses' kin!
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Are you boasting to me with your three empresses' kin!

entries.zh: 關東人與崔、盧婚者，猶自矜大，公世為帝戚，不亦貴乎。」
entries.en: Men east of the Pass who marry the Cui and Lu still pride themselves — is your house, imperial affines generation after generation, not nobler?"
entries.literal: Men east of the Pass who marry the Cui and Lu still pride themselves — is your house, imperial affines generation after generation, not nobler?"

entries.zh: 高檢子:履行 審行 真行 五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄
entries.en: Gao Jian — sons Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant Chong; Dou Wei's nephews Gui, Cong, and Kang; grandnephews Jing and Dan; nephew Jin; great-grandnephew Dexuan.
entries.literal: Gao Jian's sons: Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant: Chong; Dou Wei's nephews: Gui, Cong, and Kang; grandnephews: Jing and Dan; nephew: Jin; great-grandnephew: Dexuan.

entries.zh: 淹，字執禮，材辯多聞，有美名。
entries.en: Yan, styled Zhili, was gifted in argument and widely learned, and enjoyed an excellent reputation.
entries.literal: Yan, styled Zhili, was talented in debate and widely learned, with a fine reputation.

entries.zh: 隋開皇中，與其友韋福嗣謀曰：「上好用隱民，蘇威以隱者召，得美官。」
entries.en: During the Kaihuang reign, he schemed with his friend Wei Fusi, saying, "The emperor favors men in retirement — Su Wei was recruited as a recluse and won a fine appointment."
entries.literal: During Kaihuang of Sui, he plotted with his friend Wei Fusi, saying: "The emperor likes recluses. Su Wei was summoned as a hermit and obtained a fine office.

entries.zh: 乃共入太白山，為不仕者。
entries.en: So the two withdrew together to Mount Taibai and lived as recluses.
entries.literal: Thereupon they together entered Mount Taibai and lived as men who did not serve.

entries.zh: 文帝惡之，謫戍江表。
entries.en: Emperor Wen took offense and banished them for frontier service in the south.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen disapproved and banished them to guard duty in Jiangbiao.

entries.zh: 赦還，高孝基為雍州司馬，薦授承奉郎，擢累御史中丞。
entries.en: After they were pardoned and returned, Gao Xiaoji, as Yongzhou secretary, recommended him for appointment as Gentlemen for Reception, and he rose through successive promotions to Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: After amnesty and return, Gao Xiaoji was Prefectural Secretary of Yongzhou; he recommended Yan, who was appointed Gentlemen for Reception, then repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 王世充僭號，署少吏部，頗親近用事。
entries.en: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, Yan was made vice minister of the civil office and grew close to those who wielded power.
entries.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, Yan was appointed Vice Minister of the Civil Office and became quite close to those in power.

entries.zh: 洛陽平，不得調，欲往事隱太子。
entries.en: When Luoyang fell, he could find no post and wished to enter the service of the Hidden Crown Prince.
entries.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, he could not obtain an appointment and wished to go serve the Hidden Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 時封倫領選，以諗房玄齡，玄齡恐失之，白秦王，引為天策府兵曹參軍、文學館學士。
entries.en: Feng Lun then held the appointment portfolio and tipped off Fang Xuanling, who feared losing so able a man, reported to the Prince of Qin, and secured Yan as military affairs officer of the Heavenly Strategies Office and a scholar of the Literary Institute.
entries.literal: At that time Feng Lun oversaw selection; he informed Fang Xuanling. Xuanling feared losing him, reported to the Prince of Qin, and brought Yan in as Military Affairs Officer of the Heavenly Strategies Office and a Literary Institute scholar.

entries.zh: 嘗侍宴，賦詩尤工，賜銀鐘。
entries.en: On one banquet occasion his verse was especially fine, and the prince rewarded him with a silver bell.
entries.literal: Once while attending a banquet, his composed verse was especially fine, and he was granted a silver bell.

entries.zh: 慶州總管楊文幹反，辭連太子，歸罪淹及王珪、韋挺，並流越巂，王知其誣，餉黃金三百兩。
entries.en: When Yang Wengan, military commissioner of Qingzhou, rebelled, testimony implicated the crown prince. Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting were blamed and exiled to Yuexi. The Prince of Qin knew they had been falsely implicated and sent them three hundred taels of gold.
entries.literal: When Yang Wengan, regional commander of Qingzhou, rebelled, testimony implicated the crown prince. Blame was assigned to Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting, who were all exiled to Yuexi. The prince knew this was a frame-up and sent them three hundred taels of gold.

entries.zh: 及踐阼，召為御史大夫，封安吉郡公，食四百戶。
entries.en: When Taizong ascended the throne, he recalled Yan as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed him as Duke of Anji, and granted him an income of four hundred households.
entries.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Anji Commandery, with an income of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 淹建言諸司文桉稽期，請以御史檢促。
entries.en: Yan proposed that censors be assigned to inspect each office's files for tardiness and enforce deadlines.
entries.literal: Yan proposed that each office's paperwork be checked for deadlines, requesting that censors supervise and press them.

entries.zh: 太宗以問僕射封倫，倫曰：「設官各以其事治，御史劾不法，而索桉求疵，是太苛，且侵官。」
entries.en: Taizong consulted Vice Premier Feng Lun, who replied, "Every office has its own sphere — censors should punish violations, not hunt through files for pretexts. That would be excessively harsh and an invasion of others' jurisdiction."
entries.literal: Taizong asked the Vice Premier Feng Lun. Lun said: "Offices are established so each may govern its own affairs. Censors impeach unlawfulness; to search files for flaws is too harsh and moreover an encroachment on other officials' duties.

entries.zh: 淹嘿然。
entries.en: Yan fell silent.
entries.literal: Yan was silent.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「何不申執？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Why did you not press your point?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Why not argue your case?

entries.zh: 對曰：「倫所引國大體，臣伏其議，又何言？」
entries.en: He replied, "Lord Feng spoke to the state's larger principles; I accept his view. What further case could I make?"
entries.literal: He replied: "What Lun cited concerns the great principles of the state; I submit to his argument — what more can I say?"

entries.zh: 帝悅，以資博練，帝敕東宮儀典簿最悉聽淹裁訂。
entries.en: Pleased, the emperor judged him broadly seasoned in affairs and ordered Yan to revise all ceremonial regulations and ledgers of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and considered his learning broad and practiced. The emperor ordered that the Eastern Palace's ceremonial regulations and ledgers be entirely entrusted to Yan for revision.

entries.zh: 俄檢校吏部尚書，參豫朝政。
entries.en: Soon he was made acting Minister of the Civil Office and took part in governing.
entries.literal: Shortly he was appointed Acting Minister of the Civil Office and participated in deliberating state affairs.

entries.zh: 所薦贏四十人，後皆知名。
entries.en: More than forty of those he recommended later rose to prominence.
entries.literal: Of those he recommended, more than forty later became well known.

entries.zh: 嘗白郅懷道可用，帝問狀。
entries.en: He once recommended Chi Huaidao as worthy of appointment, and the emperor asked for particulars.
entries.literal: He once reported that Chi Huaidao was usable; the emperor asked for particulars.

entries.zh: 淹曰：「懷道及隋時位吏部主事，方煬帝幸江都，群臣迎阿，獨懷道執不可。」
entries.en: Yan said, "When Huaidao was chief clerk in the Ministry of Civil Appointments under the Sui, as Emperor Yang moved to Jiangdu the courtiers all rushed to flatter him — Huaidao alone stood firm in opposition."
entries.literal: Yan said: "When Huaidao served in Sui as chief clerk in the Ministry of Civil Office, just as Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, the officials all flattered and agreed — only Huaidao steadfastly objected.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿時何云？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "What did you say at the time?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "What did you say at the time?"

entries.zh: 曰：「臣與眾。」
entries.en: He said, "I sided with the majority."
entries.literal: He said: "I went with the crowd."

entries.zh: 帝折曰：「事君有犯無隱，卿直懷道者，何不讜言？」
entries.en: The emperor reproved him: "Serving a ruler means remonstrating without hiding anything — if you truly thought Huaidao right, why did you not speak out boldly?"
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him: "Serving a ruler requires remonstrance without concealment — you approve of Huaidao, so why not speak forthrightly?"

entries.zh: 謝曰：「臣位下，又顧諫不從，徒死無益。」
entries.en: He apologized, "My rank was too low, and I feared remonstrance would go unheeded and my death would serve no purpose."
entries.literal: He apologized: "My rank was low, and I feared that if remonstrance went unheeded, death would be in vain."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「內以君不足諫，尚何仕？
entries.en: The emperor said, "If you inwardly thought the ruler beyond remonstrance, why remain in office at all?
entries.literal: The emperor said: "If inwardly you thought the ruler unworthy of remonstrance, why still serve?

entries.zh: 食隋粟忘隋事，忠乎？」
entries.en: To eat the Sui state's grain yet forget the Sui state's affairs — is that loyalty?"
entries.literal: Eating Sui grain yet forgetting Sui affairs — is that loyalty?"

entries.zh: 因顧群臣：「公等謂何？」
entries.en: He turned to the assembled ministers: "What do you say?"
entries.literal: He then turned to the officials: "What do you gentlemen say?"

entries.zh: 王珪曰：「比干諫而死，孔子稱仁，泄冶諫亦死，則曰：'民之多僻，無自立辟。
entries.en: Wang Gui said, "Confucius praised Bi Gan's humanity when he remonstrated and died. Yet when Xie Zhi remonstrated and was killed, Confucius said, 'When the people have many crooked ways, do not set yourself up as upright.
entries.literal: Wang Gui said: "Bi Gan remonstrated and died; Confucius praised his humanity. Xie Zhi remonstrated and also died, yet Confucius said: 'When the people have many crooked ways, do not erect a standard of your own.

entries.zh: '祿重責深，從古則然。」
entries.en: Great salary carries heavy responsibility — that has been true since antiquity.'"
entries.literal: Heavy salary brings deep responsibility — it has been so since antiquity.'

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿在隋不諫，宜置。
entries.en: The emperor smiled and said, "Your failure to remonstrate under the Sui may be forgiven.
entries.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "You did not remonstrate under the Sui — that may be excused.

entries.zh: 世充親任，胡不言？」
entries.en: Yet Shichong trusted you closely — why did you say nothing then?"
entries.literal: Shichong favored and trusted you — why did you not speak up?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「固嘗言，不見用。」
entries.en: Yan replied, "I did speak, but was not heeded."
entries.literal: He replied: "I did speak, but was not heeded."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「世充愎諫飾非，卿若何而免？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Shichong was obstinate, rejected counsel, and covered his errors — if so, how did you survive?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Shichong was obstinate in rejecting remonstrance and glossed over faults — if so, how did you escape?"

entries.zh: 淹辭窮不得對。
entries.en: Yan had no answer left.
entries.literal: Yan's arguments were exhausted and he could not reply.

entries.zh: 帝勉曰：「今任卿已，可有諫未？」
entries.en: The emperor then pressed him: "Now that you serve in office, do you have any remonstrance to offer?"
entries.literal: The emperor encouraged him: "Now that I have employed you, have you any remonstrance to offer?

entries.zh: 答曰：「顧死無隱。」
entries.en: He answered, "I intend to remonstrate without concealment even at the cost of my life."
entries.literal: He answered: "I shall look to death without concealment."

entries.zh: 貞觀二年疾，帝為臨問。
entries.en: In Zhenguan 2 he fell ill, and the emperor visited him in person.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he fell ill; the emperor personally visited to inquire.

entries.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰襄。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously made Right Vice Premier, with the posthumous name Xiang.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Premier; his posthumous name was Xiang.

entries.zh: 始，淹典二職，貴重於朝矣，而亡清白名，獲譏當世。
entries.en: Though Yan held two major posts and stood high at court, he never earned a name for integrity and was criticized in his own day.
entries.literal: At first Yan held two posts and was greatly honored at court, yet he left no reputation for integrity and was ridiculed in his own time.

entries.zh: 子敬同襲爵，官至鴻臚卿。
entries.en: His son Jingtong inherited the title and rose to Chamberlain for Dependencies.
entries.literal: His son Jingtong inherited the title and reached the post of Chamberlain for Dependencies.

entries.zh: 房玄齡子:遺愛 杜如晦弟:楚客 叔父:淹 五世孫:元穎 六世孫:審權 七世孫:讓能
entries.en: Fang Xuanling's son, Yiai; Du Ruhui's younger brother, Chuke; their paternal uncle, Yan; fifth-generation descendant, Yuanying; sixth-generation descendant, Shenquan; seventh-generation descendant, Rangneng.
entries.literal: Fang Xuanling's son: Yiai. Du Ruhui's younger brother: Chuke. Paternal uncle: Yan. Fifth-generation descendant: Yuanying. Sixth-generation descendant: Shenquan. Seventh-generation descendant: Rangneng.

entries.zh: 秦王討王世充，命倫參謀軍事。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qin marched against Wang Shichong, he put Feng Lun on his staff as military adviser.
entries.literal: When Prince Qin campaigned against Wang Shichong, he ordered Lun to advise on military affairs.

entries.zh: 時兵久不決，帝欲班師，王遣倫西見帝曰：「賊地雖多，羈縻不相使，所用命者洛陽爾，計窮力屈，死在旦暮。
entries.en: The campaign had dragged on without decision, and the emperor wished to withdraw. The prince sent Feng Lun west to tell him, "The rebels hold much land, but their ties are loose and they cannot truly command one another; only Luoyang takes orders. Their schemes are spent and their strength broken—they are living from hour to hour.
entries.literal: At the time the army had long been unable to achieve victory, and the Emperor wished to withdraw. The Prince sent Lun west to see the Emperor and say, "Though the rebels' territory is vast, they are loosely bound and cannot command one another; the one who receives their orders is Luoyang alone. Their plans are exhausted and their strength spent—death is imminent.

entries.zh: 今解而西，則賊勢磐結，後難以圖。」
entries.en: If we pull back now, the enemy will knit their power together, and we shall never overcome them later."
entries.literal: If we disengage now and march west, the rebels' strength will become firmly knit, and later it will be hard to overcome them."

entries.zh: 帝納之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his counsel.
entries.literal: The Emperor accepted this.

entries.zh: 賊平，帝謂侍臣曰：「始議東討，時多沮解者，唯秦王謂必克，倫贊其行，雖張華葉策晉武，亦何以加於是！」
entries.en: After the rebels were crushed, the emperor told his ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, most men tried to dissuade me; only the Prince of Qin insisted we would prevail, and Feng Lun backed him. Not even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could outshine that!"
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the Emperor said to his attending ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, many discouraged it, but only Prince Qin said victory was certain, and Lun endorsed his plan—even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could not surpass this!"

entries.zh: 封平原縣公，判天策府司馬。
entries.en: Feng Lun was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan County and appointed acting chief administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan County and made Acting Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.

entries.zh: 初，竇建德援洛，王將趣虎牢，倫與蕭瑀諫不可，至是入賀。
entries.en: Earlier, when Dou Jiande marched to relieve Luoyang, the prince had meant to rush to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu had urged against it. Now they came to offer their congratulations.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Dou Jiande came to aid Luoyang, the Prince was about to hurry to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu remonstrated that it should not be done. At this point they came in to offer congratulations.

entries.zh: 王笑曰：「不用公言，今日幸而捷，豈智者千慮或有失乎？」
entries.en: The prince smiled and said, "Had I listened to you, I might never have won today. Even the wisest man, planning a thousand times, can still miss once, can he not?"
entries.literal: The Prince smiled and said, "Had I not taken your advice, today I would fortunately have won—can even the wise, in a thousand considerations, sometimes err?"

entries.zh: 倫謝素不及。
entries.en: Feng Lun apologized that he could not measure up to Yang Su.
entries.literal: Lun apologized that he was not the equal of Su.

entries.zh: 頃之，突厥寇太原，且遣使和親。
entries.en: Soon afterward the Turks raided Taiyuan and at the same time sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance.
entries.literal: Before long, the Turks raided Taiyuan and also sent envoys proposing a marriage alliance.

entries.zh: 帝問計，群臣咸請許之可紓戰。
entries.en: The emperor asked his ministers for counsel, and all urged him to accept the offer and ease the fighting.
entries.literal: The Emperor asked for counsel; the ministers all urged accepting it to relieve the war pressure.

entries.zh: 倫曰：「不然。
entries.en: Feng Lun said, "That would be a mistake.
entries.literal: Lun said, "Not so.

entries.zh: 彼有輕中國心，謂我不能戰，若乘其怠擊之，勢必勝，勝而後和，威德兩全。
entries.en: They look down on the Middle Kingdom and think we dare not fight. Strike while they are careless and we are sure to win; make peace only after victory, and both authority and virtue will be intact.
entries.literal: They harbor contempt for China, thinking we cannot fight. If we strike while they are slack, we are sure to win. After victory, then make peace—prestige and virtue both complete.

entries.zh: 今雖不戰，後必復來。
entries.en: Even if we do not fight now, they will come again.
entries.literal: Even if we do not fight now, they will surely come again later.

entries.zh: 臣以為擊之便。」
entries.en: Your servant believes it is better to attack them."
entries.literal: Your subject holds that striking them is advantageous."

entries.zh: 詔可。
entries.en: An edict approved his proposal.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 尋檢校吏部尚書，進封趙國公，徙密國。
entries.en: Before long he was made acting Minister of Personnel, raised to Duke of Zhao, and his fief was moved to the state of Mi.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and transferred to the state of Mi.

entries.zh: 陳叔達，字子聰，陳宣帝子也。
entries.en: Chen Shuda, whose courtesy name was Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
entries.literal: Chen Shuda—Chen Shuda, courtesy name Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

entries.zh: 少封義陽王，歷丹楊尹、都官尚書。
entries.en: While still young he was made Prince of Yiyang and later held the posts of intendant of Danyang and minister of justice.
entries.literal: In his youth he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang and served successively as Intendant of Danyang and Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 入隋，久不試。
entries.en: When the Chen fell to the Sui he went for a long time without receiving an appointment.
entries.literal: After Chen fell to the Sui, he long went without being given office.

entries.zh: 大業中，授內史舍人，出為絳郡通守。
entries.en: During the Daye reign he was made a secretariat gentleman and then dispatched as prefect of Jiang Commandery.
entries.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and sent out as Administrator-General of Jiang Commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖西師，以郡聽命，授丞相府主簿，封漢東郡公。
entries.en: When Gaozu advanced west, the commandery submitted to him; Chen was named chief clerk in the chancellor's office and created Duke of Handong.
entries.literal: When Gaozu marched west with his army, the commandery submitted on his orders; he was appointed Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong Commandery.

entries.zh: 與溫大雅同管機秘，方禪代時，書冊誥詔，皆其筆也。
entries.en: He and Wen Daya jointly managed confidential records, and as the dynastic transition drew near he drafted the books, registers, and proclamations.
entries.literal: Together with Wen Daya he oversaw the secret archives; when the transfer of the mandate was imminent, all books, registers, and proclamations were in his hand.

entries.zh: 武德初，授黃門侍郎，判納言，封江國公。
entries.en: Early in Wude he became vice minister of the palace secretariat, served concurrently as head censor, and was created Duke of Jiang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, with concurrent duty as Head Censor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang.

entries.zh: 普王為襄漢元帥，進復戶部尚書、統軍長史。
entries.en: When the Prince of Pu was made grand marshal of Xiang-Han, Fu was promoted to Minister of Revenue and chief of staff for the unified command.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Pu was grand marshal of Xiang and Han, Fu was advanced to Minister of Revenue and Chief of Staff for the unified army.

entries.zh: 舊制謂「行軍長史」，德宗以復父諱更之。
entries.en: The old title had been "campaign chief of staff"; Dezong changed it to avoid Fu's father's name (Heng).
entries.literal: The old regulation called the post "campaign chief of staff"; Emperor Dezong, because of Fu's father's taboo name, changed the title.

entries.zh: 未行，扈狩奉天。
entries.en: Before he could depart, the court fled to Fengtian.
entries.literal: Before he set out, he accompanied the hunt at Fengtian.

entries.zh: 帝惡庳隘，欲西如鳳翔依張鎰。
entries.en: The emperor found Fengtian cramped and wished to move west to Fengxiang and Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: The emperor disliked the low and narrow place and wished to go west to Fengxiang to rely on Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 復曰：「鳳翔乃泚舊兵，今泚悖亂，當有同惡者。
entries.en: Fu said, "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old command. Now that Zhu Ci has rebelled, there will be men who share his cause.
entries.literal: Fu said: "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old troops; now Zhu Ci rebels against order—there should be those of like wicked intent.

entries.zh: 雖鎰，臣畏不免。」
entries.en: Even with Zhang Yi, I fear we would not be safe."
entries.literal: Even Zhang Yi—your servant fears we would not escape harm."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕業行，留一日以驗爾言！」
entries.en: The emperor said, "We are already on the march—stay one day and we shall see if you are right."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "We are already on the road—stay one day to verify your words!"

entries.zh: 俄而鎰為李楚琳所害，於是拜吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Within a day Zhang Yi was murdered by Li Chulin, and Fu was made Minister of Personnel and participant in policy deliberation.
entries.literal: Soon Zhang Yi was killed by Li Chulin; thereupon Fu was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent participation in Council deliberation.

entries.zh: 興元初，進門下侍郎。
entries.en: In early Xingyuan (784) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 初，淮南陳少游左附李希烈，而張鎰判官韋皋殺邠、隴叛卒，不應楚琳。
entries.en: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan had sided with Li Xilie, while Wei Gao, aide to Zhang Yi, executed the Bin-Long mutineers and refused to follow Li Chulin.
entries.literal: At first Chen Shaoyou of Huainan leaned in support of Li Xilie, while Zhang Yi's aide Wei Gao killed the mutinous troops of Bin and Long and did not respond to Chu Lin.

entries.zh: 復還執政，建言：「陛下反正，功臣已貴矣，唯甄善汰惡為未明。
entries.en: Back in power, Fu said, "Your Majesty has restored order and rewarded the loyal, but you have not yet distinguished the worthy from the wicked.
entries.literal: When Fu returned to hold power, he offered counsel: "Your Majesty has returned to the right path; meritorious servants are already honored—only sorting the good and culling the wicked is not yet clear.

entries.zh: 少遊位將相，首臣賊，皋名淺官下，獨挺挺抗忠。
entries.en: Shaoyou holds high rank yet led the way in serving the rebel; Gao is obscure in rank yet stood alone in loyalty.
entries.literal: Shaoyou holds the rank of general and chief minister, yet was foremost in serving the rebel; Gao's name is shallow and his office low, yet alone he stands tall in loyal resistance.

entries.zh: 如以皋代少遊，則天下嘹然知逆順之理。」
entries.en: If Gao replaced Shaoyou, all the realm would clearly see the difference between loyal and traitor."
entries.literal: If Gao were used to replace Shaoyou, then the empire would ringingly know the principle of rebellion and submission."

entries.zh: 帝許之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 復出，中官馬欽緒揖宰相劉從一，附耳語，既而從一密諗復曰：「有詔與公議向所奏，不欲李勉、盧翰聞知。」
entries.en: As Fu left, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to Chief Minister Liu Congyi and whispered. Congyi then told Fu privately, "The emperor wishes to discuss your proposal with you alone; Li Mian and Lu Han are not to know."
entries.literal: When Fu went out, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to the chief minister Liu Congyi and spoke in his ear; presently Congyi secretly informed Fu: "There is an edict to discuss with you what was just memorialized; we do not wish Li Mian and Lu Han to hear of it."

entries.zh: 復曰：「堯、舜有'僉曰'之言，朝廷大事尚當謀及公卿。
entries.en: Fu replied, "Even Yao and Shun said 'the multitude proposes.' Great matters of state should be discussed with the chief ministers.
entries.literal: Fu said: "Yao and Shun had the saying 'the multitude said'; great affairs of court ought still to be deliberated with the chief ministers and grandees.

entries.zh: 如勉等非其人，當罷去。
entries.en: If Li Mian and the others are unfit, dismiss them.
entries.literal: If Mian and the rest are not the right men, they ought to be dismissed and removed.

entries.zh: 既曰宰相，而謀議可獨避之乎？
entries.en: But if they are chief ministers, how can state business be kept from them?
entries.literal: Since they are called chief ministers, how can counsel and deliberation be deliberately kept from them alone?

entries.zh: 今與公行此或可，第恐浸以生常，政由是敝。」
entries.en: I might yield to you this once, but I fear it will become habit—and government will suffer for it."
entries.literal: I might yield to you this once, but I fear it will become habit—and government will suffer for it."

entries.zh: 從一以聞，帝不悅。
entries.en: Congyi reported Fu's words; the emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: Congyi reported this; the emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 復辭疾上政事，許之。
entries.en: Fu pleaded illness and resigned from office; the request was granted.
entries.literal: Fu pleaded illness and submitted his governmental affairs; it was granted.

entries.zh: 子廩，字富侯。
entries.en: His son Lin, styled Fuhou.
entries.literal: His son Lin, style name Fuhou.

entries.zh: 第進士，遷尚書郎。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi and was appointed a Secretariat official.
entries.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was transferred to a Secretariat official.

entries.zh: 仿領南海，解官往侍。
entries.en: When Fang took the post in the far south, Lin resigned his own office to accompany and care for him.
entries.literal: When Fang took charge of the Southern Sea, he resigned office to go and attend him.

entries.zh: 為人退約少合。
entries.en: By nature he was modest and reserved, and made few close friends.
entries.literal: As a man he was retiring and restrained, seldom in accord with others.

entries.zh: 南海多穀紙，仿敕諸子繕補殘書。
entries.en: Paper was plentiful in the south, and Fang had his sons repair damaged books from his library.
entries.literal: The Southern Sea had much grain-straw paper; Fang ordered his sons to mend and repair damaged books.

entries.zh: 廩諫曰：「州距京師且萬里，書成不可露齎，必貯以囊笥，貪者伺望，得無薏苡嫌乎？」
entries.en: Lin objected: "This post is ten thousand li from the capital. Finished books cannot be carried openly—they must be packed in chests, and the greedy will take notice. Will you not invite the suspicion Ma Yuan suffered over his Job's-tears?"
entries.literal: Lin remonstrated: "The prefecture is nearly ten thousand li from the capital; when books are finished they cannot be carried openly—they must be stored in bags and cases, and the greedy will watch and wait. Will there not be the suspicion of the Job's-tears incident?"

entries.zh: 仿曰：「善，吾思不及此。」
entries.en: Fang said, "You are right; I had not thought of that."
entries.literal: Fang said: "Good—I did not think as far as this."

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: He dropped the plan.
entries.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

entries.zh: 廣明初，以諫議大夫知制誥，請厲止夜行以備賊諜，出太倉粟賤估以濟貧民。
entries.en: Early in the Guangming era, as Remonstrating Grandee and edict drafter, he urged a strict curfew against rebel spies and the sale of imperial grain at low prices to aid the poor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangming, as Remonstrating Grandee he drafted edicts; he requested stern prohibition of night travel to guard against rebel spies, and release of Great Granary grain at low valuation to relieve the poor.

entries.zh: 俄遷京兆尹。
entries.en: He was soon made metropolitan governor of the capital district.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 田令孜養子有罪亡，擊捕吏，系獄，請救踵門，廩不納，杖殺之，內外畏讋。
entries.en: An adopted son of Tian Lingzi committed a crime and fled; he assaulted the arresting officer and was jailed. Supplicants thronged Lin's gate, but he refused them and had the man flogged to death; court and capital alike stood in awe.
entries.literal: Tian Lingzi's adopted son committed a crime and fled; he struck the arresting officer and was imprisoned. Pleas for rescue came in succession at the gate; Lin would not accept them and had him beaten to death. Within and without, all feared and submitted.

entries.zh: 令孜拒黃巢，以廩為糧料使，辭疾，貶賀州司戶參軍事。
entries.en: When Lingzi resisted Huang Chao he named Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to registrar at Hezhou.
entries.literal: Lingzi resisted Huang Chao and appointed Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to Registrar of He Prefecture.

entries.zh: 會襄王竊據，挈族逃河朔，鎮冀節度使王鎔厚禮之。
entries.en: When the Prince of Xiang seized power, Lin fled north with his family; Wang Rong, governor of Zhenji, received him with great honor.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Xiang seized territory by force, he took his clan and fled to the Hebei region; Wang Rong, military governor of Zhenji, treated him with generous courtesy.

entries.zh: 光化中，以給事中召，不至，卒。
entries.en: In the Guanghua era he was recalled as Supervising Censor but did not come; he died.
entries.literal: During Guanghua he was summoned as Supervising Censor but did not arrive; he died.

entries.zh: 定，字梅臣，瑀曾孫。
entries.en: Ding, styled Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.
entries.literal: Ding, style name Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.

entries.zh: 以廕起家陝州參軍事、金城丞。
entries.en: He entered service through hereditary privilege as adjutant at Shanzhou and magistrate of Jincheng.
entries.literal: By yin privilege he began his career as military adjutant of Shan Prefecture and magistrate of Jincheng.

entries.zh: 蒞事清挺。
entries.en: In office he was incorruptible and stern.
entries.literal: In conducting affairs he was pure and upright.

entries.zh: 選補黜陟使裴遵慶表為判官，還調萬年主簿。
entries.en: Pei Zunqing, commissioner for personnel review, recommended him as aide; he was later posted as chief clerk of Wannian County.
entries.literal: Personnel selection and promotion-and-demotion commissioner Pei Zunqing recommended him as case officer; on return he was transferred to chief clerk of Wannian.

entries.zh: 歷左右司郎中。
entries.en: He rose to director in the Left and Right Secretariats.
entries.literal: He successively served as director in the Left and Right Departments of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 為元載所惡，外遷袁、潤等六州刺史。
entries.en: Yuan Zai disliked him and had him sent out to serve as prefect of six prefectures, including Yuan and Run.
entries.literal: Hated by Yuan Zai, he was transferred outward as prefect of six prefectures including Yuan and Run.

entries.zh: 大曆中，有司差天下刺史治最，定與常州蕭復、豪州張鎰為第一，而劭桑稼，均賦稅，業徠遊口，在鎰、復右。
entries.en: In the Dali era, when the ministry ranked governors for outstanding administration, Ding stood first alongside Xiao Fu of Changzhou and Zhang Yi of Haozhou. Yet in promoting agriculture, equalizing taxes, and settling displaced people, he outranked both.
entries.literal: In the Dali era, the relevant office ranked governors nationwide for best administration; Ding together with Xiao Fu of Chang Prefecture and Zhang Yi of Hao Prefecture were first—but in encouraging mulberry and grain, equalizing taxes and levies, and building up the wandering population, he stood above Yi and Fu.

entries.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、太常卿。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonies.
