entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 硃泚泚反，詭姓名為張誕，匿裏中，與蔣沇不浼於賊。
entries.en: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Ding assumed the false name Zhang Yan, hid among the people, and—along with Jiang Yan—kept himself unstained by the rebels.
entries.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, [Ding] disguised his name as Zhang Yan, hid in the countryside, and together with Jiang Yan did not defile themselves before the rebels.

entries.zh: 事平，擢太子少師。
entries.en: After order was restored, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十七，贈太子太師。
entries.en: He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He died at age seventy-seven; posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 蕭瑀瑀從子:鈞 鈞兄子:嗣業 瓘子:嵩 嵩子:華 嵩孫:復 華孫:俛 華孫:倣 倣子:廩 復曾孫:遘 瑀曾孫:定
entries.en: Xiao Yu; his nephew's son Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.
entries.literal: Xiao Yu; Yu's nephew's son: Jun; Jun's elder brother's son: Siye; Guan's son: Song; Song's son: Hua; Song's grandson: Fu; Hua's grandson: Mian; Hua's grandson: Fang; Fang's son: Lin; Fu's great-grandson: Gou; Yu's great-grandson: Ding.

entries.zh: 初，武德四年，太宗為天策上將軍，寇亂稍平，乃鄉儒，宮城西作文學館，收聘賢才，於是下教，以大行臺司勳郎中杜如晦、記室考功郎中房玄齡及于志寧、軍諮祭酒蘇世長、天策府記室薛收、文學褚亮姚思廉、太學博士陸德明孔穎達、主簿李玄道、天策倉曹參軍事李守素、王府記室參軍事虞世南、參軍事蔡允恭顏相時、著作郎攝記室許敬宗薛元敬、太學助教蓋文達、軍諮典簽蘇勖，並以本官為學士。
entries.en: Early on, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin held the title Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as rebellion was partly subdued, he gathered Confucian scholars, built a Literature Hall west of the palace city, and recruited worthy men. He then issued an order naming Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the literary scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Imperial Academy erudites Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; chief clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, storage clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, recording secretary of the princely establishment; staff members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as recorder; Gai Wenda, assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, military advisory registrar -- all as academicians while keeping their original posts.
entries.literal: Early, in the fourth year of Wude, the Prince of Qin was Grand General of Heavenly Strategy; as bandit chaos was somewhat pacified, he gathered Confucian scholars and built the Literature Hall west of the palace city to recruit worthy talent. Thereupon he issued an order appointing, while retaining their original offices, Du Ruhui, Director of Meritorious Service in the Grand Secretariat; Fang Xuanling, Evaluation Director in the Secretariat; Yu Zhining; Su Shichang, Military Advisory Inspector; Xue Shou, Recorder of the Heavenly Strategy Office; the Literary Scholars Chu Liang and Yao Silian; the Erudites of the Imperial Academy Lu Deming and Kong Yingda; Chief Clerk Li Xuandao; Li Shousu, Storage Clerk of the Heavenly Strategy Office; Yu Shinan, Recording Secretary of the Princely Establishment; the Staff Members Cai Yungong and Yan Xiangshi; Xu Chongzong and Xue Yuanjing, Director of the Office of Compilation acting as Recorder; Gai Wenda, Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy; and Su Xu, Military Advisory Registrar -- all as academicians in their existing posts.

entries.zh: 七年，收卒，復召東虞州錄事參軍劉孝孫補之。
entries.en: In the seventh year, after Shou died, Liu Xiaosun, recording officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was recalled to replace him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year Shou died; Liu Xiaosun, Recording Officer of Dongyu Prefecture, was summoned again to fill the vacancy.

entries.zh: 凡分三番遞宿於閤下，悉給珍膳。
entries.en: They were divided into three shifts to lodge in rotation beneath the pavilion, and all were given fine meals.
entries.literal: They were divided into three watches and took turns lodging beneath the pavilion; all were supplied with fine fare.

entries.zh: 每暇日，訪以政事，討論墳籍，榷略前載，無常禮之間。
entries.en: On free days he questioned them about government, debated the classics, and sifted former records, without the stiffness of ordinary court ritual.
entries.literal: On each free day he consulted them on government affairs, discussed the classics, weighed and surveyed former records, without the constraints of ordinary ceremony.

entries.zh: 命閻立本圖像，使亮為之贊，題名字爵裏，號「十八學士」，藏之書府，以章禮賢之重。
entries.en: He had Yan Liben paint their portraits, Liang write the encomia, and their names, titles, and residences inscribed; the group was called the "Eighteen Academicians," kept in the library to show how highly he valued honoring talent.
entries.literal: He ordered Yan Liben to paint their portraits, had Liang compose encomia for them, inscribed their names, titles, and residences, called them the "Eighteen Academicians," and stored the set in the library to display the weight he placed on honoring worthies.

entries.zh: 方是時，在選中者，天下所慕問，謂之「登瀛洲」。
entries.en: At that time those selected were the envy of the empire, and the post was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."
entries.literal: At that time those chosen for it were admired and sought after throughout the realm, and the appointment was called "Ascending to Yingzhou."

entries.zh: 附 劉孝孫劉孝孫者，荊州人。
entries.en: Appended biography: Liu Xiaosun was a native of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: Appended: Liu Xiaosun -- Liu Xiaosun was a man of Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 祖貞，周石臺太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhen served as administrator of Shitai under Northern Zhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Shitai under Zhou.

entries.zh: 孝孫少知名。
entries.en: Xiaosun was known even in youth.
entries.literal: Xiaosun was known from youth.

entries.zh: 大業末，為王世充弟杞王辯行臺郎中。
entries.en: Near the end of Daye he served as director of the field secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi, Wang Shichong's younger brother.
entries.literal: At the end of Daye he served as Director of the Field Secretariat for Bian, Prince of Qi and younger brother of Wang Shichong.

entries.zh: 辯降，眾引去，獨孝孫攀援號慟，送於郊。
entries.en: When Bian surrendered, the others pulled away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him, wailing, and saw him off to the suburbs.
entries.literal: When Bian surrendered, the crowd drew him away, but Xiaosun alone clung to him wailing in grief and escorted him to the outskirts.

entries.zh: 貞觀六年，遷著作佐郎、吳王友。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he became assistant director of the Office of Compilation and companion to the Prince of Wu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation and Companion to the Prince of Wu.

entries.zh: 歷諮議參軍。
entries.en: He later served as advisory staff member.
entries.literal: He served as Advisory Staff Member.

entries.zh: 遷太子洗馬，未拜，卒。
entries.en: He was appointed groom of the heir apparent but died before taking up the post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent but died before assuming the post.

entries.zh: 附 李玄道李玄道者，本隴西人。
entries.en: Appended biography: Li Xuandao was originally from Longxi.
entries.literal: Appended: Li Xuandao -- Li Xuandao was originally a man of Longxi.

entries.zh: 世居鄭州。
entries.en: His family had long lived in Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: His family had long resided in Zhengzhou.

entries.zh: 仕隋為齊王府屬。
entries.en: Under Sui he served as an aide in the household of the Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: He served Sui as an aide in the Princely Establishment of Qi.

entries.zh: 李密據洛口，署記室。
entries.en: When Li Mi held Luokou, Xuandao was made his recorder.
entries.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, [Xuandao] was appointed Recorder.

entries.zh: 密敗，為王世充所執，眾懼不能寐，獨玄道曰：「死生有命，憂能了乎？」
entries.en: When Mi fell, Xuandao was taken by Wang Shichong; the others were too afraid to sleep, but Xuandao alone said, "Life and death are fated -- can worry settle anything?"
entries.literal: When Mi was defeated, [Xuandao] was seized by Wang Shichong; the crowd feared and could not sleep, but Xuandao alone said: "Life and death are ordained -- can worry finish the matter?"

entries.zh: 寢甚安。
entries.en: He slept soundly.
entries.literal: He slept very peacefully.

entries.zh: 及見世充，辭色不撓，釋縛，為著作佐郎。
entries.en: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and bearing did not falter; Shichong freed him and made him assistant director of the Office of Compilation.
entries.literal: When he was brought before Shichong, his words and demeanor did not waver; [Shichong] released his bonds and made him Assistant Director of the Office of Compilation.

entries.zh: 東都平，為秦王府主簿。
entries.en: After the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became chief clerk of the Prince of Qin's household.
entries.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he became Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qin's establishment.

entries.zh: 貞觀初，累遷給事中，姑臧縣男。
entries.en: Early in Zhenguan he rose to supervising censor and was enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.
entries.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang County.

entries.zh: 出為幽州長史，佐都督王君廓，專持府事。
entries.en: He was sent out as chief administrator of You Prefecture, assisting Area Commander Wang Junkuo and running the command's affairs himself.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Chief Administrator of Youzhou, assisting the Area Commander Wang Junkuo and holding sole charge of the command's affairs.

entries.zh: 君廓不法，每以義裁糾之。
entries.en: Junkuo broke the law, and Xuandao repeatedly corrected him on grounds of principle.
entries.literal: Junkuo acted unlawfully, and [Xuandao] repeatedly checked him by right principle.

entries.zh: 嘗遺玄道婢，乃良家子為所掠，遣去不納，由是始隙。
entries.en: Once Junkuo sent Xuandao a maidservant who turned out to be a good family's daughter he had seized; Xuandao sent her back and refused the gift, and from that their breach began.
entries.literal: Once [Junkuo] sent Xuandao a maidservant who was in fact a respectable family's daughter whom he had seized; Xuandao sent her away and would not accept her, and from this their rift began.

entries.zh: 君廓入朝，玄道寓書房玄齡，玄齡本甥也。
entries.en: When Junkuo went to court, Xuandao was staying with Fang Xuanling, who was his nephew.
entries.literal: Junkuo went to court; Xuandao was lodging at the house of Fang Xuanling -- Xuanling was his nephew by birth.

entries.zh: 君廓發其書，不識草字，疑以謀己，遂反。
entries.en: Junkuo opened the letter, could not decipher the cursive hand, suspected a plot against him, and rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Junkuo opened the letter, could not read cursive script, suspected a plot against himself, and rebelled.

entries.zh: 坐是流巂州，未幾，擢常州刺史，風績清簡，下詔褒美，賜繒帛。
entries.en: For this Xuandao was banished to Juan Prefecture; soon after he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou, where his rule was clear and spare; the throne issued a decree of praise and granted him silk.
entries.literal: For this [Xuandao] was exiled to Juan Prefecture; before long he was promoted to prefect of Changzhou; his governance was clear and plain; an edict praised him and granted silk.

entries.zh: 久之，致仕，加銀青光祿大夫，以祿歸第，卒。
entries.en: In time he retired, was made Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, went home on his stipend, and died.
entries.literal: After a long time he retired; was given the title Silver Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; returned home on his salary; and died.

entries.zh: 附 李守素李守素者，趙州人。
entries.en: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu came from Zhao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Appendix: Li Shousu. Li Shousu was a man of Zhao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 王世充平，召署天策府倉曹參軍，通氏姓學，世號「肉譜」。
entries.en: After Wang Shichong was subdued, Li was summoned and made warehouse clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; expert in clan and surname lore, his age called him the "Meat Genealogy."
entries.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, [Li] was summoned and appointed Warehouse Clerk in the Celestial Stratagem Office; versed in the study of surnames and clans, the age styled him the "Meat Genealogy."

entries.zh: 虞世南與論人物，始言江左、山東，尚相酬對；
entries.en: Yu Shinan debated men of talent with him; when they began with the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they could still hold their own in exchange;
entries.literal: Yu Shinan discussed with him the evaluation of men; at first speaking of the Jiangzuo and Shandong regions, they still matched wits in reply;

entries.zh: 至北地，則笑而不答，歎曰：「肉譜定可畏。」
entries.en: but when the talk turned to the north, Shousu only laughed and kept silent; Shinan sighed and said, "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable."
entries.literal: when it came to the northern regions, [Shousu] merely laughed and did not answer; [Shinan] sighed and said: "The Meat Genealogy is truly formidable."

entries.zh: 許敬宗曰：「倉曹此名，豈雅目邪？
entries.en: Xu Jingzong said, "This nickname for the warehouse clerk -- is it a refined one?
entries.literal: Xu Jingzong said: "This name for the warehouse clerk -- is it an elegant title?

entries.zh: 宜有以更之。」
entries.en: Surely something better ought to replace it."
entries.literal: There ought to be something to replace it."

entries.zh: 世南曰：「昔任彥升通經，時稱'五經笥'，今以倉曹為'人物志'，可乎？」
entries.en: Shinan said, "In olden days Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was called the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we call the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that serve?"
entries.literal: Shinan said: "In former times Ren Yansheng mastered the classics and was styled the 'Casket of the Five Classics'; might we style the warehouse clerk the 'Record of Persons' -- would that do?"

entries.zh: 時渭州刺史李淹亦明譜學，守素所論，惟淹能抗之。
entries.en: At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also learned in genealogy; of Shousu's arguments, only Yan could stand against him.
entries.literal: At that time Li Yan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was also versed in genealogical studies; of Shousu's disquisitions, only Yan could contend with him.

entries.zh: 姚思廉，本名簡，以字行，陳吏部尚書察之子。
entries.en: Yao Silian, whose original name was Jian, went by his courtesy name; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.
entries.literal: Yao Silian, original name Jian, used his courtesy name in public; he was the son of Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel under Chen.

entries.zh: 陳亡，察自吳興遷京兆，遂為萬年人。
entries.en: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to the capital district and became a man of Wannian.
entries.literal: When Chen fell, Cha moved from Wuxing to Jingzhao and thus became a man of Wannian.

entries.zh: 思廉少受《漢書》於察，盡傳其業。
entries.en: Silian studied the 《Book of Han》 under Cha in his youth and wholly inherited his father's craft.
entries.literal: Silian in youth received the 《Book of Han》 from Cha and fully inherited his work.

entries.zh: 寡嗜欲，惟一於學，未嘗問家人生貲。
entries.en: He cared little for pleasure, gave himself wholly to study, and never once asked after his family's means.
entries.literal: He had few desires, devoted himself solely to learning, and never inquired after his household's livelihood or property.

entries.zh: 岑文本，字景仁，鄧州棘陽人。
entries.en: Cen Wenben, whose courtesy name was Jingren, came from Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.
entries.literal: Cen Wenben, courtesy name Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Deng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖善方，後梁吏部尚書，更家江陵。
entries.en: His grandfather Shanfang had been Minister of Personnel under the Later Liang and resettled the family at Jiangling.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shanfang was Minister of Personnel under Later Liang and moved the family to Jiangling.

entries.zh: 父之象，仕隋為邯鄲令，坐為人訟，不得申。
entries.en: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan but was sued by another party and could not vindicate himself.
entries.literal: His father Zhixiang served the Sui as magistrate of Handan; he was implicated in a lawsuit brought against him and could not clear himself.

entries.zh: 文本年十四，詣司隸理冤，辨對哀暢無所詘。
entries.en: At fourteen Wenben went to the Censorate to plead his father's case and argued with such moving eloquence that no one could refute him.
entries.literal: When Wenben was fourteen, he went to the Censorate to seek redress for the wrong; in debate he spoke movingly and fluently and was never worsted.

entries.zh: 眾屬目，命作《蓮華賦》，文成，合臺嗟賞，遂得直。
entries.en: All eyes were on him when he was told to write a "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when he finished, the whole censorate marveled, and his father was cleared.
entries.literal: The crowd fixed their eyes on him; he was ordered to compose the "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; when the text was finished, the whole bureau sighed in admiration, and he thereby obtained justice.

entries.zh: 再遷侍御史。
entries.en: He was promoted again to Attending Censor.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Attending Censor.

entries.zh: 大夫韋挺責著位不肅，明日，挺越次與江夏王道宗語，臨進曰：「王亂班。」
entries.en: Grand Master Wei Ting had scolded an official for failing to stand in proper order. The next day Ting himself stepped out of rank to speak with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia, and Lin stepped forward: "Your Highness has disturbed the court order."
entries.literal: Grand Master Wei Ting rebuked someone for not standing in rank with proper dignity; the next day Ting stepped out of order to speak with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia; Lin advanced and said: "The prince has disturbed the ranks."

entries.zh: 道宗曰：「與大夫語，何至爾！」
entries.en: Daozong said, "I was only speaking with the grand master—must it come to this!"
entries.literal: Daozong said: "Speaking with the grand master—how does it come to this!"

entries.zh: 臨曰：「大夫亦亂班。」
entries.en: Lin replied, "The grand master has disturbed the order as well."
entries.literal: Lin said: "The grand master also has disturbed the ranks."

entries.zh: 挺失色，眾皆悚伏。
entries.en: Ting turned pale, and everyone present shrank in silence.
entries.literal: Ting changed color; the assembly all shrank in awe.

entries.zh: 俄持節按獄交州，出冤系三千人。
entries.en: Soon afterward he went to Jiao Prefecture with imperial credentials to review legal cases and secured the release of three thousand prisoners held on false charges.
entries.literal: Soon, bearing credentials, he investigated cases in Jiao Prefecture and released three thousand persons wrongfully imprisoned.

entries.zh: 累遷大理卿。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 高宗嘗錄囚，臨占對無不盡，帝喜曰：「為國之要在用法，刻則人殘，寬則失有罪，惟是折中，以稱朕意。」
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong once held a prison review. Lin answered every case without omission, and the emperor was pleased: "Governing a state depends on how the law is applied. Harshness maims the people; excessive leniency lets the guilty go free. Only a balanced middle course can satisfy my intent."
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong once reviewed prisoners; Lin's replies left nothing unspoken; the Emperor rejoiced and said: "The key to governing the state lies in using the law: if severe, people are maimed; if lenient, the guilty escape—only by striking the mean can it match Our intent."

entries.zh: 它日復訊，余司斷者輒紛訴不已，獨臨所訊無一言。
entries.en: On another review day, prisoners judged by the other officials all pleaded and protested endlessly, but not one of those Lin had tried said a word.
entries.literal: On another day when questioning was resumed, the other officials who decided cases all at once pleaded and complained without end; only those Lin had questioned had not a single word.

entries.zh: 帝問故，答曰：「唐卿斷囚不冤，所以絕意。」
entries.en: The emperor asked why. He answered, "Minister Tang's rulings are never unjust, so they have nothing left to say."
entries.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Minister Tang's judgments of prisoners are not unjust, and therefore they have no further intent."

entries.zh: 帝嘆曰：「為獄者固當若是。」
entries.en: The emperor sighed and said, "This is how a judge ought to be."
entries.literal: The Emperor sighed and said: "One who conducts prisons ought indeed to be like this."

entries.zh: 乃自述其考曰「形如死灰，心若鐵石」雲。
entries.en: He then wrote his own appraisal of Lin: "His form was like dead ashes, and his heart like iron and stone."
entries.literal: He then himself set forth his appraisal, saying "form like dead ashes, heart like iron and stone," and so on.

entries.zh: 永徽元年，拜御史大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Yonghui he was appointed censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 蕭齡之嘗任廣州都督，受賕當死，詔群臣議，請論如法，詔戮於朝堂。
entries.en: Xiao Lingzhi had once served as military governor of Guangzhou. Having accepted bribes, he was liable to death. The emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate and directed that he be judged according to law; an edict then ordered execution in the court hall.
entries.literal: Xiao Lingzhi had once served as military governor of Guangzhou; having accepted bribes he was liable to death. An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate and directed judgment according to law; an edict ordered execution in the court hall.

entries.zh: 臨建言：「群臣不知天子所以議之之意。
entries.en: Lin memorialized: "The ministers do not understand the Son of Heaven's purpose in ordering deliberation.
entries.literal: Lin memorialized: "The ministers do not understand the Son of Heaven's purpose in ordering deliberation.

entries.zh: 在律有八。
entries.en: The law provides for eight mitigating considerations.
entries.literal: In the law there are eight.

entries.zh: 王族戮於隱，議親也；
entries.en: Royal kin are executed in seclusion out of consideration for kinship;
entries.literal: Royal kin are executed in seclusion—consideration for kin;

entries.zh: 刑不上大夫，議貴也。
entries.en: punishment does not reach great officers out of consideration for noble rank.
entries.literal: punishment does not reach great officers—consideration for nobility.

entries.zh: 今齡之貪贓狼扈，死有餘咎。
entries.en: Lingzhi's greed and corruption were wanton, and death would not have been excessive punishment.
entries.literal: Now Lingzhi's greed and corruption were wanton; death would not have been excessive punishment.

entries.zh: 陛下以異於它囚，故議之有司，又令入死，非堯、舜所以用刑者，不可為後世法。」
entries.en: Yet Your Majesty treated him differently from other prisoners, had the responsible officials deliberate, and then ordered death—this is not how Yao and Shun applied punishment, and it must not become a precedent for later generations."
entries.literal: Your Majesty treated him differently from other prisoners, had the responsible officials deliberate, and then ordered death—this is not how Yao and Shun applied punishment and must not become a precedent for later generations."

entries.zh: 帝然之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved.

entries.zh: 齡之，齊高帝五世孫，由是免死。
entries.en: Lingzhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Gao of Qi and thus escaped death.
entries.literal: Lingzhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Gao of Qi, and thus escaped death.

entries.zh: 中宗始郊，國子祭酒祝欽明等知韋後能制天子，欲迎諂之，即奏以皇后亞獻，安樂公主終獻，又四時及列帝誕日，遣使者詣陵如事生。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice, National University Libationer Zhu Qinming and others, knowing Empress Wei could dominate the emperor, sought to flatter her. They memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering, and that envoys be sent to the imperial tombs in all four seasons and on successive emperors' birth anniversaries as though the dead were still living.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice, the National University Libationer Zhu Qinming and others, knowing that Empress Wei could control the Son of Heaven, wished to court and flatter her; they at once memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering; moreover, in all four seasons and on the birth days of successive emperors, they sent envoys to the tombs as if serving the living.

entries.zh: 紹以為非禮，引正誼固爭。
entries.en: Shao held these measures contrary to ritual and argued against them on principle without yielding.
entries.literal: Shao regarded this as contrary to ritual and, citing orthodox principle, firmly contended.

entries.zh: 帝又詔武氏陵及諸武墓皆置守戶，紹謂：「昊、順二陵守戶五百，與昭陵同。
entries.en: The emperor also ordered guard households placed at the Wu clan tombs and all Wu family graves. Shao protested: "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households—the same as Taizong's Zhaoling.
entries.literal: The Emperor also ordered guard households set at the Wu clan tombs and all Wu family graves; Shao said: "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households, the same as Zhaoling.

entries.zh: 在令，先世帝王陵戶二十，今雖崇奉外家，宜準附常典。
entries.en: The statutes prescribe only twenty guard households for the tombs of former emperors. Though the empress's kin are now honored, they should still follow the regular precedent.
entries.literal: In the statutes, tombs of emperors of former ages have twenty guard households; though the maternal kin are now honored, they ought to follow and attach to the regular canon.

entries.zh: 又親王墓戶十，梁、魯乃追贈，不可逾真王。
entries.en: Princely tombs receive ten guard households. Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and cannot exceed true princes.
entries.literal: Moreover, princely tombs have ten guard households; Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and cannot exceed true princes.

entries.zh: 褒德衛卒，至逾宗廟，不可明甚，請罷之。」
entries.en: To honor the Wu clan with guard troops that exceed even the imperial ancestral temple is plainly excessive. I ask that these orders be revoked."
entries.literal: Honoring virtue with guard soldiers, yet reaching beyond the ancestral temple—this cannot be made clear enough; I request that it be abolished."

entries.zh: 又言：「比群臣務厚葬，以俑人象驂眩耀相矜，下逮眾庶，流宕成俗。
entries.en: He also said, "Lately officials compete in lavish funerals, displaying figurines and carved teams of horses in dazzling show, and the fashion has spread even among commoners.
entries.literal: He also said: "Recently ministers have devoted themselves to lavish burial, using figurines and images of paired horses in dazzling display to vie with one another, reaching down to the common people until it has become a drifting custom.

entries.zh: 願按令切敕裁損，凡明器不許列衢路，惟陳墓所。
entries.en: I ask that the statutes be strictly enforced to curb this excess. Spirit goods should not be displayed on public roads but only at the burial site.
entries.literal: I wish that according to the statutes a stern edict cut and reduce this; all spirit objects are not permitted to be arrayed on public roads, but only displayed at the tomb site.

entries.zh: 昏家盛設障車，擁道為戲樂，邀貨捐貲動萬計，甚傷化紊禮，不可示天下。」
entries.en: Wedding processions now fill the roads with barrier carts and public entertainments, extorting contributions that run to tens of thousands. This deeply corrupts morals and disrupts ritual. Such practices must not be displayed before the empire."
entries.literal: Wedding families lavishly set out barrier carts, blocking the road for sport and amusement, soliciting goods and contributing wealth by the tens of thousands—greatly injuring transformation and disordering ritual; this cannot be shown to all under Heaven."

entries.zh: 事雖不從，議者美嘆。
entries.en: Though his proposals were not adopted, commentators praised him with admiration.
entries.literal: Though the matters were not followed, those who discussed them praised and sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「大理，人命所系，不可阿旨詭辭，以求茍免。」
entries.en: He once told his intimates, "The Ministry of Punishments holds human lives in its hands. One cannot twist words to flatter superiors and escape responsibility."
entries.literal: Once he told those close to him: "The Ministry of Punishments is what human lives depend on; one cannot flatter intent with deceitful words to seek careless escape."

entries.zh: 故有功為獄，常持平守正，以執據冤罔，凡三坐大辟，將死，泰然不憂，赦之，亦不喜，後以此重之。
entries.en: In every case he judged, he held to the middle way and relied on evidence against wrongful imprisonment. Three times he faced execution and met death calmly; when pardoned he showed no joy. For this the court esteemed him all the more.
entries.literal: Therefore when Yougong conducted prisons he always held the mean and guarded rectitude, relying on evidence against wrongful imprisonment; altogether three times he faced great execution, about to die yet calm without worry; when pardoned he was not pleased either—later for this he was highly regarded.

entries.zh: 所全活甚眾，酷吏為少衰，然疾之如仇矣。
entries.en: He saved a great many lives, and the cruel officials somewhat relented, though they hated him as an enemy.
entries.literal: Those he preserved alive were very many; cruel officials somewhat declined, yet they hated him as an enemy.

entries.zh: 改司仆少卿。
entries.en: He was made vice minister of the Court of Equine Administration.
entries.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Court of Equine Administration.

entries.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈司刑卿。
entries.en: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously honored as Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: He died at age sixty-eight and was posthumously given Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 中宗即位，加贈越州都督，遣使就第吊祭，賜物百段，授一子官。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne he was posthumously made governor of Yuezhou; envoys mourned at his home, bestowed a hundred lengths of goods, and granted office to one son.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne he was further given Governor of Yuezhou; envoys were sent to his residence for mourning sacrifice, a hundred lengths of goods bestowed, and one son granted office.

entries.zh: 開元初，竇希瑊等請以己官讓有功子惀，以報舊德，由是自大理司直遷恭陵令。
entries.en: Early in Kaiyuan, Dou Xi Huang and others asked to yield their offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of his kindness, and Lun rose from straightener in the Ministry of Punishments to magistrate of Gongling.
entries.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Dou Xi Huang and others requested to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of old grace; thereby from Straightener of the Ministry of Punishments he was moved to Magistrate of Gongling.

entries.zh: 會昌中，追謚忠正。
entries.en: In the Huichang era he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright.
entries.literal: In the Huichang era he was posthumously given the title Loyal and Upright.

entries.zh: 子錫，久視初，為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，代其甥李嶠為宰相。
entries.en: His son Xi, early in the Jiushi era, became vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and chancellor, succeeding his nephew Li Qiao.
entries.literal: His son Xi, early in the Jiushi era, was Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Tower, replacing his nephew Li Qiao as chancellor.

entries.zh: 請還廬陵王，不為張易之所右。
entries.en: He petitioned for the return of the Prince of Luling and earned the disfavor of Zhang Yizhi.
entries.literal: He requested the return of the Prince of Luling and was not favored by Zhang Yizhi.

entries.zh: 與鄭杲俱知選，坐泄禁中語，又賕謝鉅萬，時蘇味道亦坐事，同被訊，系鳳閣，俄徙司刑三品院。
entries.en: He and Zheng Gao oversaw civil-service selection. For leaking palace secrets and accepting bribes of tens of thousands, he was investigated together with Su Weidao, detained in the Phoenix Pavilion, and soon moved to the Court of Punishments compound.
entries.literal: Together with Zheng Gao he managed selection; for leaking palace speech and again bribing with tens of thousands, at the time Su Weidao was also implicated; together they were interrogated and held in the Phoenix Pavilion, soon moved to the Court of Punishments third-rank compound.

entries.zh: 錫按轡專道，神氣不懾，日膳豐鮮，無損貶。
entries.en: Xi rode the dedicated lane to detention unafraid, ate rich meals every day, and showed no sign of distress.
entries.literal: Xi held the reins on the dedicated road, his spirit unafraid; daily meals were abundant and fresh, without reduction or demotion.

entries.zh: 味道徒步赴逮，席地菜食。
entries.en: Weidao walked to his arrest and sat on the ground eating plain vegetables.
entries.literal: Weidao went on foot to be seized and sat on the ground eating plain vegetables.

entries.zh: 武後聞之，釋味道，將斬錫，既而流循州。
entries.en: Empress Wu released Weidao but was about to execute Xi; she then exiled him to Xunzhou instead.
entries.literal: When Empress Wu heard this, she released Weidao and was about to execute Xi; presently she exiled him to Xunzhou.

entries.zh: 神龍中，累遷工部尚書，兼修國史，東都留守。
entries.en: During the Shenlong era he rose to Minister of Works, helped revise the national history, and served as defender of the eastern capital.
entries.literal: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently revised the national history, and served as defender of the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 韋後臨朝，詔同中書門下三品，旬日，出為絳州刺史。
entries.en: When Empress Wei held court she made him chancellor of the third rank, but within ten days he was posted as prefect of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: When Empress Wei held court, an edict made him Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery; within ten days he was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 累封平原郡公，卒。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan and eventually died.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan and died.

entries.zh: 睿宗即位，數言政損益，再遷給事中，兼太常少卿。
entries.en: After Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly offered advice on government policy and was twice promoted, becoming Supervising Secretary and concurrently Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly spoke on what would benefit or harm government; he was transferred again to Supervising Secretary and concurrently Vice Minister of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 先天二年，玄宗講武驪山，紹以典儀坐失軍容，當斬。
entries.en: In the second year of Xiantian, when Emperor Xuanzong held martial exercises at Mount Li, Shao was charged with a breach of ceremonial protocol in military display and sentenced to death.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Xuanzong held martial exercises at Mount Li; Shao, for ritual management, sat in failure of military bearing and was liable to execution.

entries.zh: 帝怒甚，執纛下，左右猶冀少貸，金吾將軍李邈遽傳詔斬之。
entries.en: The emperor was furious. Shao was seized below the banner, and those nearby still hoped for some leniency, but Golden Crow General Li Miao immediately transmitted the execution order and had him beheaded.
entries.literal: The Emperor was extremely angry; he seized the banner and came down; those at his side still hoped he might spare him somewhat, but the Golden Crow General Li Miao hastily transmitted the edict and executed him.

entries.zh: 時深咎邈，帝亦悔，俄詔罷邈官，擯於家。
entries.en: Many blamed Li Miao severely. The emperor himself soon regretted the affair and shortly dismissed Miao from office, banishing him to his home.
entries.literal: At the time they deeply blamed Miao; the Emperor also repented, and soon an edict dismissed Miao from office and banished him to his home.

entries.zh: 張文瓘，字稚圭，貝州武城人。
entries.en: Zhang Wenqian, whose style was Zhigui, came from Wucheng in Beizhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenqian, style name Zhigui, was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

entries.zh: 隋大業末，徙家魏州之昌樂。
entries.en: At the end of the Sui Daye era his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.
entries.literal: At the end of Sui Daye, his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 幼孤，事母、兄以孝友聞。
entries.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for the filial devotion and brotherly affection with which he cared for his mother and elder brother.
entries.literal: Orphaned young, he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

entries.zh: 貞觀初，第明經，補并州參軍。
entries.en: Early in the Zhenguan reign he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed military aide in Bingzhou.
entries.literal: Early in Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Military Aide of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 時李勣為長史，嘗嘆曰：「稚圭，今之管、蕭，吾所不及。」
entries.en: Li Ji was then chief administrator of the prefecture. He once sighed and said, "Zhigui is a Guan Zhong or Xiao He for our age—he surpasses what I can do."
entries.literal: At the time Li Ji was Chief Administrator; he once sighed and said: "Zhigui is the Guan and Xiao of today—what I cannot match."

entries.zh: 勣入朝，文瓘與屬僚二人皆餞，勣贈二人以佩刀、玉帶，而不及文瓘。
entries.en: When Li Ji went to court, Wenqian and two subordinate officials all saw him off. Ji gave the two men girdle knives and jade belts but gave Wenqian nothing.
entries.literal: When Ji entered court, Wenqian together with two subordinate officials all saw him off; Ji presented the two with girdle knives and jade belts, but did not include Wenqian.

entries.zh: 文瓘以疑請，勣曰：「子無為嫌。
entries.en: Wenqian asked about the omission. Ji said, "Do not take offense.
entries.literal: Wenqian, puzzled, asked; Ji said: "Sir, do not take it as a slight.

entries.zh: 若某，豫少決，故贈以刀，欲其果於斷；
entries.en: One of them is hesitant by nature, so I gave him a knife to encourage firm decisions.
entries.literal: As for so-and-so, he is by nature lacking in decisiveness, and therefore I gave him a knife, wishing him to be firm in judgment;

entries.zh: 某放誕少檢，故贈以帶，俾其守約束。
entries.en: The other is undisciplined and unrestrained, so I gave him a belt to keep him within bounds.
entries.literal: so-and-so is unrestrained and lacking in restraint, and therefore I gave him a belt to make him keep to discipline.

entries.zh: 若子才，無施不可，焉用贈？」
entries.en: Your talent needs no such aid—why should I give you a gift?"
entries.literal: As for your talent, there is nothing it cannot be applied to—why use a gift?"

entries.zh: 因極推引。
entries.en: He then strongly recommended Wenqian for advancement.
entries.literal: He thereupon strongly recommended him.

entries.zh: 再遷水部員外郎。
entries.en: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Water Section.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Vice Director of the Water Section.

entries.zh: 時兄文琮為戶部侍郎，於制，兄弟不並臺閣，出為雲陽令。
entries.en: His elder brother Wencong was then Vice Minister of Revenue. Regulations forbade brothers from serving together at court, so Wenqian was posted out as magistrate of Yunyang.
entries.literal: At the time his elder brother Wencong was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue; by regulation brothers did not serve together in the central offices, and he was sent out as Magistrate of Yunyang.

entries.zh: 累授東西臺舍人，參知政事。
entries.en: He was repeatedly appointed drafter of the Eastern and Western Terraces and joined in governing affairs.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Drafter of the Eastern and Western Terraces and participated in knowing government affairs.

entries.zh: 乾封二年，遷東臺侍郎、同東西臺三品，遂與勣同為宰相。
entries.en: In the second year of Qianfeng he was made Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace with third rank and became chief minister alongside Li Ji.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Eastern and Western Terraces, and thus together with Ji became chief ministers.

entries.zh: 俄知左史事。
entries.en: He soon took charge of the Left Historian's office as well.
entries.literal: Soon he was charged with the affairs of the Left Historian.

entries.zh: 時高宗造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，復征討四夷，京師養廄馬萬匹，帑瓘浸虛。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong was building the Penglai, Shangyang, and Hebi palaces, campaigning again on all frontiers, and maintaining ten thousand horses in the capital stables. The treasury was steadily drained.
entries.literal: At the time Gaozong built the Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi, and other palaces, again campaigned against the four barbarians, and in the capital stabled ten thousand horses in the stables; the treasury stores were gradually emptied.

entries.zh: 文瓘諫曰：「王者養民，逸則富以康，勞則怨以叛。
entries.en: Wenqian remonstrated: "A ruler nourishes his people. When they are at ease they grow prosperous and secure; when overworked they resent and rebel.
entries.literal: Wenqian remonstrated, saying: "A king nourishes the people: if at ease, they grow wealthy and secure; if labored, they resent and rebel.

entries.zh: 秦、漢廣事四夷，造宮室，至二世土崩，武帝末年戶口減半。
entries.en: Qin and Han both campaigned widely and built palaces on a vast scale—Qin collapsed under the Second Emperor, and by the end of Emperor Wu's reign the registered population had been cut in half.
entries.literal: Qin and Han broadly undertook affairs on the four sides and built palaces, until the Second Emperor's collapse; in the late years of Emperor Wu the registered population was halved.

entries.zh: 夫制治於未亂，保邦於未危。
entries.en: Good government means ordering affairs before chaos arises and securing the state before danger appears.
entries.literal: To establish order before disorder, to preserve the state before peril.

entries.zh: 人罔常懷，懷於有仁。
entries.en: The people have no fixed loyalty except to those who show them benevolence.
entries.literal: The people have no constant resting place; they rest in one who has benevolence.

entries.zh: 臣願撫之，無使勞而生怨。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to cherish them and not drive them to labor until resentment arises.
entries.literal: Your servant wishes to comfort them and not let labor give rise to resentment.

entries.zh: 隋監未遠，不可不察。」
entries.en: The fall of the Sui is still recent history. This warning cannot be ignored."
entries.literal: Sui's mirror is not far off; this cannot but be examined."

entries.zh: 帝善其言，賜繒錦百段，為減廄馬數千。
entries.en: The emperor approved his advice, rewarded him with a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced the imperial stables by several thousand horses.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved his words, bestowed a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced the stabled horses by several thousand.

entries.zh: 唐張徐
entries.en: Tang, Zhang, and Xu.
entries.literal: Tang, Zhang, Xu.

entries.zh: 崔融，字安成，齊州全節人。
entries.en: Cui Rong, whose style name was Ancheng, was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.
entries.literal: Cui Rong, style name Ancheng, was a man of Quanjie in Qizhou.

entries.zh: 擢八科高第。
entries.en: He passed the Eight Subjects examination with top honors.
entries.literal: He was selected with high marks in the Eight Subjects examination.

entries.zh: 累補宮門丞、崇文館學士。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts as vice-director of the palace gates and scholar of the Chongwen Hall.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Palace Gate Vice-Director and Scholar of the Chongwen Hall.

entries.zh: 中宗為太子時，選侍讀，典東朝章疏。
entries.en: While Zhongzong was still crown prince, Rong was selected as a lecturing attendant and oversaw memorials for the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Rong was chosen as lecturing attendant and managed memorials of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 武后幸嵩高，見融銘《啟母碣》，歎美之。
entries.en: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she read Rong's inscription on the Qi Mother stele and praised it warmly.
entries.literal: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she saw Rong's inscription on the Qi Mother stele and sighed in praise.

entries.zh: 及已封，即命銘《朝覲碑》。
entries.en: Once her enfeoffment was complete, she at once commissioned him to compose the Court Audience stele.
entries.literal: When she had already been enfeoffed, she immediately ordered him to inscribe the Court Audience stele.

entries.zh: 授著作佐郎，遷右史，進鳳閣舍人。
entries.en: He was made assistant compiler, then promoted to right historiographer and advanced to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
entries.literal: He was appointed Assistant Compiler, promoted to Right Historian, and advanced to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

entries.zh: 時有司議關市，行人盡征之，融上疏謂：「《周官》九賦，其七曰關市。
entries.en: When officials proposed levying market tolls at the passes on all travelers without exception, Rong submitted a memorial arguing: "The Offices of Zhou lists nine levies; the seventh is the pass-market levy.
entries.literal: At the time the relevant offices debated market tolls at passes, taxing all travelers in full. Rong submitted a memorial saying: "In the Offices of Zhou, among the nine levies, the seventh is called market tolls at passes.

entries.zh: 以市多淫巧，而關通末遊，欲止抑之，故加稅耳。
entries.en: That levy was meant to curb extravagant goods in the markets and the petty traffic that passed through the passes—not to tax ordinary travelers as well.
entries.literal: Because markets had many extravagant crafts and passes connected with marginal pursuits, they wished to stop and restrain them, hence the added tax only.

entries.zh: 然唯斂工商，而不及往來。
entries.en: It was imposed only on artisans and merchants, not on people merely passing through.
entries.literal: Yet it only collected from artisans and merchants, and did not extend to those coming and going.

entries.zh: 今一切通取，則事不師古。
entries.en: To levy it on everyone indiscriminately would abandon the precedent of antiquity.
entries.literal: Now to take from all without distinction is a matter that does not follow antiquity.

entries.zh: 且四人異業舊矣，復動而搖之。
entries.en: Moreover, the four classes of society have long had their separate callings; to disturb them again would unsettle the whole order.
entries.literal: Moreover, the four classes with their different occupations is an old arrangement; to stir them again is to shake them.

entries.zh: 市者，兼受善惡也。
entries.en: Markets accommodate both the worthy and the base alike.
entries.literal: Markets receive both good and bad together.

entries.zh: 若甚，則細人無所容，細人無所容，久必為亂。
entries.en: If the burden is too heavy, the humble will have no room to survive; and when the humble have no room to survive, disorder will follow before long.
entries.literal: If it is excessive, then petty men have nowhere to lodge; if petty men have nowhere to lodge, in time there will surely be disorder.

entries.zh: 天下之關必險道，市必要津，豪宗、惡少在焉，聞一旦變法，或致騷動，恐南走蠻，北走狄。
entries.en: The empire's passes lie on dangerous roads and its markets at vital crossings, where powerful clans and rowdy youths gather. News of a sudden change in the law could spark unrest, driving people south toward the barbarians or north toward the Di.
entries.literal: Passes throughout the realm lie on perilous routes, and markets stand at essential fords. Powerful clans and vicious youths dwell there. Hearing that the law changes overnight, they may cause disturbances; I fear they will flee south to the barbarians or north to the Di.

entries.zh: 今江津、河滸列鋪率稅，檢覆稽留，加主司僦略邀丐，則商人廢業。
entries.en: Already at river crossings and along the banks, tax stations levy fixed rates, inspections cause long delays, and supervising officials extort and beg for bribes until merchants abandon their livelihoods.
entries.literal: Now at river crossings and river banks stations are set up to levy taxes at a fixed rate; inspection and review cause delays, and when chief officials extort and beg, merchants abandon their trades.

entries.zh: 魏、晉、齊、隋所不行，況陛下乎？
entries.en: Even Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui did not adopt such measures—how much less should Your Majesty?
entries.literal: What Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui did not carry out—how much less should Your Majesty?

entries.zh: 有如師興費廣，雖倍算商旅、加斂齊人可也。」
entries.en: If armies must be raised and costs mount, then even doubling the levy on traveling merchants and imposing extra taxes on the common people would be justified."
entries.literal: If troops are raised and expenses are vast, then even doubling the levy on traveling merchants and adding collections from the common people would be acceptable."

entries.zh: 後納之。
entries.en: The court later accepted his advice.
entries.literal: Later it was adopted.

entries.zh: 有許鐸者，罷武城令，客于徐，勳脅以官，不從。
entries.en: A former magistrate of Wucheng named Xu Duo was staying in Xuzhou when Xun tried to force an office on him; he refused.
entries.literal: There was a Xu Duo who, dismissed as magistrate of Wucheng, sojourned in Xu; Xun coerced him with office, but he would not comply.

entries.zh: 彥曾官屬被囚，鐸潛饋資糧，及死，為收瘞，匿免其子弟，賊平，乃皆歸其喪。
entries.en: While Yanzeng's staff lay imprisoned, Duo secretly supplied them; after Yanzeng's death he buried the body, sheltered his sons and brothers, and when the rebellion ended restored their remains to the family.
entries.literal: When Yanzeng's staff were imprisoned, Duo secretly supplied provisions; when Yanzeng died, he gathered and buried him, hid and spared his sons and younger brothers, and after the bandits were pacified returned all their coffins.

entries.zh: 詔拜石首令，賜銀緋。
entries.en: The court appointed him magistrate of Shishou and awarded him silver seals and scarlet robes.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him magistrate of Shishou and bestowed silver seals and scarlet robes.

entries.zh: 僚官焦璐、溫廷皓、李棁、崔蘊、柳秦、盧崇嗣、韋廷範贈官有差，錄其子官之。
entries.en: Staff members Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhi, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices in varying ranks, and their sons were granted official appointments.
entries.literal: Staff officials Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhi, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices in varying degrees, and their sons were entered on the rolls for office.

entries.zh: 徐彥伯，兗州瑕丘人，名洪，以字顯。
entries.en: Xu Yanbo was a native of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou; his personal name was Hong, but he was known by his style name.
entries.literal: Xu Yanbo, a man of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou; his name was Hong, but he was known by his style name.

entries.zh: 七歲能為文。
entries.en: At the age of seven he could already write essays.
entries.literal: At seven he could compose writing.

entries.zh: 結廬太行山下。
entries.en: He built a hut at the foot of Mount Taihang.
entries.literal: He built a hut beneath Mount Taihang.

entries.zh: 薛元超安撫河北，表其賢，對策高第。
entries.en: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei he recommended Yanbo's talent, and Yanbo took top honors in the policy examination.
entries.literal: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei, he memorialized Yanbo's worth; in the policy examination he ranked at the top.

entries.zh: 調永壽尉、蒲州司兵參軍。
entries.en: He was appointed magistrate of Yongshou and military staff officer in Puzhou.
entries.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Yongshou and military staff officer of Puzhou.

entries.zh: 時司戶韋皓善判，司士李亙工書，而彥伯屬辭，時稱「河東三絕」。
entries.en: Wei Hao, revenue registrar, excelled at legal judgments; Li Gen, records clerk, at calligraphy; and Yanbo at literary composition—they were known as the "Three Unsurpassed of Hedong."
entries.literal: At the time Revenue Registrar Wei Hao was skilled in judgments, Records Clerk Li Gen excelled at calligraphy, and Yanbo composed literary pieces; they were called at the time "the Three Unsurpassed of Hedong."

entries.zh: 遷職方員外郎，奉迎中宗房州，進給事中。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice-director of the Bureau of Appointments, welcomed Zhongzong at Fangzhou, and advanced to drafting attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Bureau of Appointments, welcomed Zhongzong at Fangzhou, and advanced to Drafting Attendant.

entries.zh: 武后撰《三教珠英》，取文辭士，皆天下選，而彥伯、李嶠居首。
entries.en: When Empress Wu compiled the 《Pearls of the Three Teachings》, she chose literary men from across the empire; Yanbo and Li Jiao ranked first.
entries.literal: When Empress Wu compiled the Pearls of the Three Teachings, she selected men of literary talent from throughout the realm; Yanbo and Li Jiao stood at the head.

entries.zh: 遷宗正卿，出為齊州刺史。
entries.en: He was promoted to director of the imperial clan and then sent out as prefect of Qizhou.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan and sent out as Prefect of Qizhou.

entries.zh: 帝復位，改太常少卿。
entries.en: When the emperor was restored to the throne, Yanbo was made vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, Yanbo was changed to Vice-Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 以脩《武后實錄》勞，封高平縣子。
entries.en: For compiling the 《Veritable Records of Empress Wu》, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping.
entries.literal: For labor in compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping.

entries.zh: 為衛州刺史，政善狀，璽書嘉勞。
entries.en: As prefect of Weizhou he earned excellent evaluations, and the emperor sent a letter of praise and reward.
entries.literal: As Prefect of Weizhou his governance earned excellent reports, and an imperial letter praised and rewarded him.

entries.zh: 移蒲州，以近畿，會郊祭，上《南郊賦》一篇，辭致黃縟。
entries.en: Transferred to Puzhou near the capital, he submitted his "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb" for the suburban sacrifice—its diction sumptuous and ornate.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Puzhou; because it was near the capital, when the suburban sacrifice occurred he submitted one piece, "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb," with diction ornate and lavish.

entries.zh: 擢脩文館學士、工部侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to scholar of the Xiūwen Hall and vice-director of the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: He was elevated to Scholar of the Xiūwen Hall and Vice-Director of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 曆太子賓客。
entries.en: He later served as guest of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He successively served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 以疾乞骸骨，許之。
entries.en: Illness led him to request retirement, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: On account of illness he begged to retire with his bones; it was granted.

entries.zh: 開元二年卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan he died.

entries.zh: 味道練台閣故事，善占奏。
entries.en: Weidao mastered Secretariat precedents and excelled at memorials and reports.
entries.literal: Weidao was versed in Secretariat precedents and skilled at memorials and reports.

entries.zh: 然其為相，特具位，未嘗有所發明，脂韋自營而已。
entries.en: Yet as chief minister he merely occupied the seat, advanced no notable policies, and devoted himself only to self-preservation and flattery.
entries.literal: Yet as chief minister he merely filled the seat and never advanced anything of note, only greasing and currying favor for himself.

entries.zh: 常謂人曰：「決事不欲明白，誤則有悔，摸棱持兩端可也。」
entries.en: He often said: "Do not decide matters too clearly; mistakes bring regret. It is best to stay equivocal and keep both sides open."
entries.literal: He often told people: "In deciding affairs one should not wish for clarity; if one errs there is regret—holding the edges and keeping both sides open will do."

entries.zh: 故世號「摸棱手」。
entries.en: For this the age called him "the equivocator."
entries.literal: Therefore the age called him "the equivocator."

entries.zh: 性友愛。
entries.en: He was affectionate by nature.
entries.literal: By nature he was affectionate toward kin.

entries.zh: 其弟味元，味元嘗請托不遂，因慢折之，味道怡然不屑。
entries.en: His younger brother Weiyuan, when a request went unfulfilled, treated him with contempt; Weidao remained calm and unperturbed.
entries.literal: His younger brother Weiyuan—Weiyuan once made a request that was not granted and therefore treated him with contempt; Weidao remained calm and unconcerned.

entries.zh: 所論著行于時。
entries.en: His writings circulated widely in his day.
entries.literal: His writings circulated in his time.

entries.zh: 豆盧欽望，雍州萬年人。
entries.en: Doulu Qinwang was a native of Wannian in Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Doulu Qinwang, a man of Wannian in Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 祖寬，隋文帝外孫，為梁泉令。
entries.en: His grandfather Kuan, a maternal grandson of Emperor Wen of Sui, served as magistrate of Liangquan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Kuan was a maternal grandson of Emperor Wen of Sui and served as magistrate of Liangquan.

entries.zh: 高祖定關中，與郡守蕭瑀率豪姓進款。
entries.en: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, Kuan and the prefect Xiao Yu led the local magnates in submitting allegiance.
entries.literal: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, Kuan with the prefect Xiao Yu led powerful clans in submitting allegiance.

entries.zh: 擢累殿中監。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to director of the palace.
entries.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Director of the Palace.

entries.zh: 子懷讓，尚萬春公主。
entries.en: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.
entries.literal: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.

entries.zh: 詔寬用魏太和詔，去「豆」姓，著「盧」。
entries.en: An edict ordered Kuan, following the Northern Wei Taihe precedent, to drop the character "Dou" from the surname and bear "Lu" instead.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Kuan to follow the Northern Wei Taihe edict, drop the character "Dou" from the surname, and bear "Lu."

entries.zh: 貞觀中，遷禮部尚書、左衛大將軍，芮國公。
entries.en: Under Zhenguan he became minister of rites and great general of the Left Guard, with the title Duke of Rui.
entries.literal: During Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of Rites and Great General of the Left Guard, Duke of Rui.

entries.zh: 卒，贈特進、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰定。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously made special advance and protector-general of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, with the posthumous name Ding.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously made Special Advance and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, with posthumous title Ding.

entries.zh: 復其舊姓。
entries.en: His original surname was restored.
entries.literal: His original surname was restored.

entries.zh: 欽望累官越州都督、司賓卿。
entries.en: Qinwang successively served as protector-general of Yuezhou and director of guests.
entries.literal: Qinwang successively held the posts of Protector-General of Yuezhou and Director of Guests.

entries.zh: 長壽二年，拜內史，封芮國公。
entries.en: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed inner scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.
entries.literal: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed Inner Scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.

entries.zh: 李昭德被罪，有司劾奏欽望阿順昭德不執正，附臣罔君，貶趙州刺史。
entries.en: When Li Zhaode was condemned, officials impeached Qinwang for flattering Zhaode instead of upholding justice and for deceiving the ruler; he was demoted to prefect of Zhaozhou.
entries.literal: When Li Zhaode was charged with crimes, the relevant offices impeached Qinwang for fawning on Zhaode and failing to uphold rectitude, for a subject deceiving his ruler, and he was demoted to Prefect of Zhaozhou.

entries.zh: 入為司府卿，遷秋官尚書。
entries.en: He entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to minister of autumn.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and was transferred to Minister of Autumn.

entries.zh: 中宗還東宮，拜太子宮尹。
entries.en: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed director of the heir apparent's household.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

entries.zh: 進文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。
entries.en: He was promoted to right chancellor of the Secretariat and third-rank associate chief minister.
entries.literal: He advanced to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

entries.zh: 罷為太子賓客。
entries.en: He was dismissed and made guest of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was dismissed and made Guest of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 帝復位，擢尚書左僕射、平章軍國重事。
entries.en: When the emperor was restored to the throne, Qinwang was promoted to left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs with charge of weighty military and state affairs.
entries.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, Qinwang was elevated to Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs and given charge of weighty military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 欽望居宰相積十餘年，方易之、三思等怙勢宣烝，窺間王室，戮忠戚，觖冀非常，不能有所裁抑，獨謹身諄諄自全。
entries.en: Qinwang served as chief minister for more than ten years while Yizhi, Sansi, and their faction abused power, eyed the throne, killed loyal princes and ministers, and pursued extravagant ambitions; he could not restrain them and devoted himself only to cautious self-preservation.
entries.literal: Qinwang served as chief minister for more than ten years while Yizhi, Sansi, and others relied on power to flaunt debauchery, watched for openings against the royal house, slaughtered loyal kin, and coveted extraordinary gains; he could not restrain them in any way and only guarded himself carefully, admonishing himself to survive.

entries.zh: 進開府儀同三司，檢校安國相王府長史。
entries.en: He was promoted to grandee of the state with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and made acting chief administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's household.
entries.literal: He advanced to Grandee of the State with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies and acting Chief Administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's household.

entries.zh: 卒，年八十，贈司空、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，諡曰元。
entries.en: He died at eighty and was posthumously made minister of works and grand protector-general of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Qianling, with the posthumous name Yuan.
entries.literal: He died, aged eighty, and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Grand Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Qianling, with posthumous title Yuan.

entries.zh: 居易被遇憲宗時，事無不言，湔剔抉摩，多見聽可，然為當路所忌，遂擯斥，所蘊不能施，乃放意文酒。
entries.en: In the days when Bai Juyi enjoyed Emperor Xianzong's trust, he held nothing back—scrubbing and probing every fault he found, and much of what he said was heeded. Yet those in power resented him, and he was driven out. Unable to put his talents to use, he surrendered himself to literature and wine.
entries.literal: When Bai Juyi enjoyed Emperor Xianzong's favor, nothing went unsaid—he scrubbed and probed every issue, and much was heeded; yet those in power envied him, and he was cast aside. What he held within could not be applied, so he gave himself over to letters and wine.

entries.zh: 既復用，又皆幼君，偃蹇益不合，居官輒病去，遂無立功名意。
entries.en: When he was recalled to service, the emperors were all young men, and his stubborn integrity suited them less and less. Each time he took office he soon pleaded illness and withdrew, until at last he abandoned all thought of establishing a lasting name.
entries.literal: When brought back to office, the emperors were all young; his unyielding manner fit less and less. Each time he took office he soon pleaded illness and left—eventually he lost all ambition for lasting achievement.

entries.zh: 與弟行簡、從祖弟敏中友愛。
entries.en: He was devoted to his younger brother Xingjian and his cousin Minzhong.
entries.literal: He was deeply affectionate with his younger brother Xingjian and his paternal cousin Minzhong.

entries.zh: 東都所居履道裏，疏詔種樹，構石樓香山，鑿八節灘，自號醉吟先生，為之傳。
entries.en: At his home in Luadao Lane in the Eastern Capital, he cleared land and planted trees, built a stone pavilion on Mount Xiangshan, and cut the Eight-Rapids channel. He styled himself the Master of Drunken Chanting and wrote an account of that life.
entries.literal: At his residence in Luadao Lane in the Eastern Capital, he cleared ground and planted trees, built a stone pavilion on Mount Xiangshan, excavated the Eight-Rapids shoal, styled himself the Master of Drunken Chanting, and wrote a biography of that life.

entries.zh: 暮節惑浮屠道尤甚，至經月不食葷，稱香山居士。
entries.en: In his later years he was drawn ever more deeply to Buddhism, abstaining from meat for months at a time, and styled himself Lay Buddhist of Mount Xiangshan.
entries.literal: In his later years he was especially drawn to Buddhism, going whole months without eating meat, and styled himself Lay Buddhist of Mount Xiangshan.

entries.zh: 嘗與胡杲、吉旼、鄭據、劉真、盧真、張渾、狄兼謨、盧貞燕集，皆高年不事者，人慕之，繪為《九老圖》。
entries.en: He once held festive gatherings with Hu Gao, Ji Min, Zheng Ju, Liu Zhen, Lu Zhen, Zhang Hun, Di Jianmo, and Lu Zhen—all elderly men who had withdrawn from office. Admiring them, people painted The Picture of the Nine Elders.
entries.literal: He once gathered for banquets with Hu Gao, Ji Min, Zheng Ju, Liu Zhen, Lu Zhen, Zhang Hun, Di Jianmo, and Lu Zhen—all advanced in years and retired from office. People admired them, and painted The Picture of the Nine Elders.

entries.zh: 武平一，名甄，以字行，潁川郡王載德子也。
entries.en: Wu Pingyi, whose personal name was Zhen but who went by his courtesy name, was the son of Prince Zaidel of Yingchuan.
entries.literal: Wu Pingyi—Wu Pingyi's given name was Zhen; he was known by his style name; he was a son of Prince Zaidel of Yingchuan Commandery.

entries.zh: 博學，通《春秋》，工文辭。
entries.en: He was erudite, thoroughly versed in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, and skilled in literary writing.
entries.literal: He was broadly learned, mastered the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》, and excelled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 武后時，畏禍不敢與事，隱嵩山修浮圖法，屢詔不應。
entries.en: During Empress Wu's reign, fearing trouble he avoided public office, withdrew to Mount Song to study Buddhist teachings, and declined repeated imperial calls.
entries.literal: In Empress Wu's time, fearing calamity he dared not take part in affairs; he retired to Mount Song to practice Buddhist dharma, and repeatedly ignored imperial summons.

entries.zh: 中宗復位，平一居母喪，迫召為起居舍人，丐終制，不見聽。
entries.en: After Zhongzong's restoration, Pingyi was observing mourning for his mother when he was pressed to serve as Attendant of the Imperial Diary; he pleaded to finish his mourning obligations, but the court would not grant it.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong was restored, Pingyi was in mourning for his mother; he was urgently summoned as Attendant of the Imperial Diary, begged to complete the mourning period, and was not heeded.

entries.zh: 景龍二年，兼修文館直學士。
entries.en: In Jinglong year 2 he was also appointed a direct academician of the Palace Library Institute.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, he was concurrently made a direct academician of the Xiūwén Guan.

entries.zh: 時天子暗柔不君，韋後蒸亂，外戚盛。
entries.en: The emperor had grown dim and pliant, no longer truly ruling; Empress Wei stirred scandal and disorder, and the power of the imperial in-laws swelled unchecked.
entries.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was dim and yielding and did not rule as sovereign; Empress Wei brought chaos through illicit relations, and the maternal kin flourished.

entries.zh: 平一重斥語，即自請抑母黨，上言：「去歲熒惑入羽林，太白再經天，太陽虧，月犯大角。
entries.en: Ping Yi had already spoken blunt rebukes; he now volunteered to curb his mother's faction and memorialized the throne: "Last year Mars entered the Feathered Guard, Venus crossed the sky twice, the sun suffered eclipse, and the moon struck Great Horn.
entries.literal: Ping Yi repeatedly spoke words of harsh rebuke, and immediately requested of himself to restrain his mother's faction, submitting a memorial: "Last year Mars entered the Forest of Feathers, the Great White Star twice crossed the heavens, the sun was eclipsed, and the moon encroached upon Great Horn.

entries.zh: 臣聞災不妄生，上見下應，信如景響。
entries.en: I have heard that disasters do not arise without reason: heaven shows a sign, and earth answers below, as surely as an echo follows a sound.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that calamities do not arise without cause; what appears above, responds below — as surely as shadow follows form.

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：'唯此文王，小心翼翼，昭事上帝，聿懷多福。
entries.en: The Book of Odes says: 'Only this King Wen — careful and reverent, serving Heaven with clear devotion — thereby gathered many blessings.'
entries.literal: The Book of Odes says: 'Only this King Wen, with meticulous care, clearly served God on high, and thereby harbored many blessings.'

entries.zh: '陛下天性孝愛，戚屬外家，恩洽澤濡。
entries.en: Your Majesty is filial and loving by nature; toward your maternal kin you have poured out favor until it runs deep.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's nature is filial and loving; toward relatives of the outer family, grace has penetrated and blessings have soaked them through.

entries.zh: 臣一宗，階三等，家數侯，硃輪華轂，過許、史、梁、鄧遠甚。
entries.en: My clan alone holds third-rank posts; several of us are enfeoffed as marquises, riding in vermillion-wheeled carriages with gilded hubs — honors surpassing by far those once granted the Xu, Shi, Liang, and Deng clans.
entries.literal: Your servant's one clan holds rank of the third grade; several in the family are marquises, with vermillion wheels and decorated hubs — far exceeding the Xu, Shi, Liang, and Deng families of old.

entries.zh: 恩崇者議積，位厚者釁速，故月滿必虧，日中則移，時不再來，榮難久藉。
entries.en: Where favor runs high, resentment gathers; where rank sits heavy, ruin comes fast. The full moon must wane, the noon sun must move — time does not return, and splendor cannot be held forever.
entries.literal: Those who receive great favor accumulate blame; those who hold weighty rank invite disaster quickly. Thus when the moon is full it must wane, when the sun stands at noon it shifts — time does not return, and glory cannot long be borrowed.

entries.zh: 昔永淳之後，王室多難，先聖從權，故臣家以宗子竊祿疏封。
entries.en: After the Yongchun reign the house of Tang knew many trials; the late emperor, acting from necessity, allowed our collateral line to hold stipends and distant fiefs we had no true right to claim.
entries.literal: In the past after the Yongchun era the royal house suffered many troubles; the former sage exercised expedient measures, so my family, as collateral descendants, improperly received salaries and distant enfeoffments.

entries.zh: 今上聖復辟，宜退守園廬，乃再假光寵，爵封如初，高班厚位，遂超涯極。
entries.en: Now that Your Majesty has restored order to the realm, we should have retired to our country estates — yet once more we were showered with honors, titles and fiefs restored as before, until rank and reward passed every proper limit.
entries.literal: Now that the sagely sovereign has restored the throne, we ought to withdraw and keep to our estates — yet again radiant favor was granted, titles and enfeoffments as before, high ranks and thick positions exceeding all bounds.

entries.zh: 故陰氣僭陽，河、洛泛溢。
entries.en: Yin overstepped yang; the Yellow and Luo rivers burst their banks.
entries.literal: Hence yin energy usurped yang; the Yellow and Luo Rivers overflowed their banks.

entries.zh: 昔王族驕盈，梅福上書；
entries.en: In former times, when the imperial clan grew proud and overbearing, Mei Fu submitted a memorial;
entries.literal: In antiquity when the royal clan grew arrogant and full, Mei Fu submitted a memorial;

entries.zh: 竇氏專縱，丁鴻進諫。
entries.en: when the Dou clan ruled without restraint, Ding Hong dared to remonstrate.
entries.literal: when the Dou clan acted with unchecked license, Ding Hong offered remonstrance.

entries.zh: 且後妃之家，恩過寵深，一朝覆沒，遂無噍類。
entries.en: And the households of empresses and consorts, though once drowned in favor, have in a single day been overturned and destroyed, until not one soul remained.
entries.literal: Moreover the families of empresses and consorts — when favor exceeded all bounds and indulgence ran deep — in a single morning were overthrown and wiped out, leaving not one survivor.

entries.zh: 願思仰損之宜、長遠之策，推遠時權，以全親親。」
entries.en: I beg you to weigh the wisdom of humble restraint and far-sighted policy — to set aside present advantage for the sake of kinship itself."
entries.literal: I pray Your Majesty will consider the fitness of upward self-diminishment and long-term strategy, push away temporary power, and thereby preserve the closeness of kin."

entries.zh: 帝慰勉，不許。
entries.en: The emperor comforted and praised him, but would not agree.
entries.literal: The Emperor comforted and encouraged him, but did not consent.

entries.zh: 遷考功員外郎。
entries.en: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 幽求自謂有勞於國，在諸臣右，意望未滿，而竇懷貞為左仆射，崔湜為中書令，殊不平，見於言面。
entries.en: Youqiu believed his service outranked every other minister and resented that Dou Huaizhen held the left vice-directorship and Cui Shi the directorship of the Secretariat; his discontent showed plainly in word and face.
entries.literal: Youqiu considered that he had labored for the state and stood above the other ministers; his ambitions were not satisfied, yet Dou Huaizhen was Left Vice Director and Cui Shi was Director of the Secretariat—he was deeply displeased, and it showed in his speech and countenance.

entries.zh: 已而湜等附太平公主，有逆計。
entries.en: Soon Shi and his circle aligned with Princess Taiping and plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: Before long Shi and the others attached themselves to Princess Taiping and had a treasonous design.

entries.zh: 幽求與右羽林將軍張暐定計，使暐說玄宗曰：「湜等皆太平黨與，日夜陰計，若不早圖，且產大害，太上不得高枕矣。
entries.en: Youqiu and Zhang Wei of the Right Imperial Insignia Army laid a plan whereby Wei urged Xuanzong: "Shi and his allies are Princess Taiping's faction, scheming night and day; unless you strike first, grave harm will follow and your father will never sleep in peace.
entries.literal: Youqiu with the Right General of the Imperial Insignia Army Zhang Wei formed a plan and had Wei persuade Emperor Xuanzong, saying, "Shi and the rest are all partisans of Taiping, plotting day and night in secret; if we do not act early, great harm will soon arise, and the Retired Emperor will not be able to rest easy.

entries.zh: 臣請督羽林兵除之。」
entries.en: I beg leave to command the palace guard and destroy them."
entries.literal: Your subject asks to lead the Imperial Insignia troops to eliminate them."

entries.zh: 帝許之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor consented.

entries.zh: 未發也，而暐漏言於侍御史鄧光賓，帝懼，即列其狀。
entries.en: Before they could act, Wei let the plan slip to Censor Deng Guangbin; alarmed, the emperor reported the whole affair himself.
entries.literal: Before it was launched, Wei leaked word to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin; the Emperor feared exposure and at once set forth the facts.

entries.zh: 睿宗以幽求等屬吏，劾奏以疏間親，罪應死。
entries.en: Ruizong turned Youqiu and his associates over for trial; they were charged with driving a wedge between father and son, a crime punishable by death.
entries.literal: Ruizong handed Youqiu and the others over to the officials, who memorialized that by estranging kin they had committed a capital offense.

entries.zh: 帝密申右之，乃流幽求於封州、暐於峰州、光賓於繡州。
entries.en: The emperor intervened in secret, and the sentences were commuted to exile: Youqiu to Feng, Wei to Peak, and Guangbin to Xiu.
entries.literal: The Emperor secretly pleaded on their behalf, and they were banished—Youqiu to Fengzhou, Wei to Peak Prefecture (Fengzhou), and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.

entries.zh: 明年，太平公主誅，即日召復舊官，知軍國事，還封戶，賜錦衣一襲。
entries.en: The following year, after Princess Taiping was killed, he was recalled the same day to his old post, entrusted with military and civil affairs, had his fief restored, and received a brocade robe.
entries.literal: The next year, when Princess Taiping was executed, he was summoned the same day to his former office, placed in charge of military and state affairs, had his fief households restored, and was given one suit of brocade robes.

entries.zh: 臨淄王入誅韋庶人，預參大策，是夜號令詔敕一出其手。
entries.en: When the Prince of Linzi marched in to destroy Consort Wei, Youqiu helped shape the coup; that night every command and proclamation bore his hand.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Linzi entered the capital to execute the Deposed Consort Wei, Youqiu took part in the great plan; that night every order and edict issued from his hand alone.

entries.zh: 以功授中書舍人，參知機務，爵中山縣男，實封二百戶，授二子五品官，二代俱贈刺史。
entries.en: Rewarded with the post of Secretariat Drafter and a share in governing, he was created Baron of Zhongshan with two hundred taxable households, his two sons were granted fifth-rank posts, and his forebears for two generations were posthumously made prefects.
entries.literal: For his merit he was made Secretariat Drafter, with a role in state affairs; he was ennobled as Baron of Zhongshan with a substantive fief of two hundred households; his two sons were given fifth-rank offices, and both generations of forebears were posthumously honored as prefects.

entries.zh: 睿宗立，進尚書右丞、徐國公，增封戶至五百，賜物千段、奴婢二十人、第一區、良田千畝、金銀雜物稱是。
entries.en: After Ruizong's accession he rose to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Xu, his fief was raised to five hundred households, and he received a thousand lengths of silk, twenty servants, a mansion, a thousand mu of fertile land, and commensurate gold and silver.
entries.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Youqiu was promoted to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Duke of Xu, with his fief increased to five hundred households; he was given a thousand lengths of goods, twenty slaves, one fine residence, a thousand mu of good land, and gold, silver, and other valuables in proportion.

entries.zh: 王琚，懷州河內人。
entries.en: Wang Ju came from Henei in Huaizhou.
entries.literal: Wang Ju was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 少孤，敏悟有才略，明天文象緯。
entries.en: Orphaned in youth, he was quick-witted and strategically gifted, and versed in astronomy.
entries.literal: Orphaned young, he was keen and perceptive with talent and stratagem, and understood astronomy and the celestial patterns.

entries.zh: 以從父隱客嘗為鳳閣侍郎，故數與貴近交。
entries.en: His father's cousin Yin Ke had once been vice director of Phoenix Pavilion, so he moved among the powerful.
entries.literal: Because his father's younger cousin Yin Ke had once been Vice Director of Phoenix Pavilion, he often associated with the noble and powerful.

entries.zh: 時年甫冠，見駙馬都尉王同皎，同皎器之。
entries.en: Still in his teens, he met Commandant-escort Wang Tongjiao, who took a liking to him.
entries.literal: At the time he had just reached manhood and met the Commandant-escort Wang Tongjiao, who valued him.

entries.zh: 會謀刺武三思，琚義其為，即與周璟、張仲之等共計。
entries.en: When a plot formed to kill Wu Sansi, Ju embraced the cause and joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in planning it.
entries.literal: When they plotted to assassinate Wu Sansi, Ju approved their cause and joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in the plan.

entries.zh: 事泄亡命，自傭於揚州富商家，識非庸人，以女嫁之，厚給以貲，琚亦賴以濟。
entries.en: After the plot leaked he fled and hired himself to a rich Yangzhou merchant, who saw his quality, married him to his daughter, and supported him handsomely.
entries.literal: When the affair was exposed he fled, hiring himself out to a wealthy merchant in Yangzhou; seeing he was no ordinary man, the merchant gave him his daughter in marriage and supplied him generously, and Ju relied on this to get by.

entries.zh: 睿宗立，琚自言本末，主人厚賫使還長安。
entries.en: At Ruizong's accession he told his full story; his patron sent him back to Chang'an with generous gifts.
entries.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Ju explained his whole story, and his patron richly rewarded him to return to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 玄宗為太子，閑遊獵韋、杜間，怠休樹下，琚以儒服見，且請過家，太子許之。
entries.en: As crown prince, Xuanzong hunted between Wei and Du; resting under a tree, he met Ju in scholar's robes, who invited him home, and the prince agreed.
entries.literal: When Xuanzong was heir apparent he would hunt leisurely between Wei and Du; resting weary under a tree, Ju appeared in scholar's dress, asked to have the prince visit his home, and the prince consented.

entries.zh: 至所廬，乃蕭然窶陋。
entries.en: At his house the prince found only poverty and squalor.
entries.literal: When they reached his dwelling, it was bleak and mean.

entries.zh: 坐久，殺牛進酒殊豐厚，太子駭異。
entries.en: They sat a long while, then slaughtered an ox and served lavish wine; the prince was astonished.
entries.literal: After sitting long, they slaughtered an ox and served wine in unusual abundance; the prince was startled.

entries.zh: 自是每到韋、杜，輒止其廬。
entries.en: After that, whenever he hunted in Wei and Du, he stopped at Ju's house.
entries.literal: From then on, whenever he came to Wei and Du, he would stop at Ju's lodge.

entries.zh: 玄宗即位，復拜戶部尚書，增實封，改太子詹事。
