entries.en: At Xuanzong's accession he was again made Minister of Revenue, his fief was enlarged, and he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Shaojing was again appointed Minister of Revenue, his substantive fief was increased, and he was changed to Steward of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 不為姚祟所喜，與幽求並以怨望得罪，貶果州刺史，賜封邑百戶。
entries.en: Disliked by Yao Chong, he and Youqiu were alike punished for discontent and demoted; Shaojing became prefect of Guo with a nominal fief of one hundred households.
entries.literal: Not favored by Yao Chong, he and Youqiu alike were punished for resentful longing and demoted—Shaojing to prefect of Guozhou, with a fief district of one hundred households granted.

entries.zh: 後坐它事，貶懷恩尉，悉奪階封，再遷溫州別駕。
entries.en: Later, implicated in another case, he was reduced to assistant magistrate of Huai'en, stripped of rank and fief, and eventually made vice-prefect of Wen.
entries.literal: Later, convicted on another matter, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Huai'en; all ranks and fiefs were stripped, and he was transferred again to vice-prefect of Wenzhou.

entries.zh: 十五年入朝，見帝泣曰：「陛下忘疇日事邪，忍使棄死草莽！
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he appeared at court, wept before the emperor, and said, "Have you forgotten what we did together, that you would leave me to die forgotten in the weeds?
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he came to court, saw the Emperor, and weeping said, "Has Your Majesty forgotten affairs of former days, that you would bear to leave me to die abandoned in the wilds!

entries.zh: 且同時立功者，今骨已朽，而獨臣在，陛下不垂湣乎？」
entries.en: Of all who earned merit that day, only I still live while the rest are dust—will you not show me mercy?"
entries.literal: Moreover, of those who achieved merit at the same time, their bones are now decayed, yet I alone remain—will Your Majesty not show pity?

entries.zh: 帝惻然，即日授太子右諭德。
entries.en: Moved, the emperor named him Right Admonisher to the Heir Apparent that very day.
entries.literal: The Emperor was moved and that same day appointed him Right Admonisher of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 久之，遷少詹事。
entries.en: Some time later he was made Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 年逾八十，以官壽卒。
entries.en: He died in office past eighty, having completed his span in service.
entries.literal: Past eighty years of age, he died in office of natural causes.

entries.zh: 紹京嗜書畫，如王義之、獻之、褚遂良真跡，藏家者至數十百卷。
entries.en: Shaojing loved calligraphy and painting; households that owned authentic pieces by Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, or Chu Suiliang might hold dozens or even hundreds of scrolls.
entries.literal: Shaojing was fond of calligraphy and painting; authentic works of Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, and Chu Suiliang in collectors' homes might reach scores or hundreds of scrolls.

entries.zh: 建中中，追贈太子太傅。
entries.en: Under Jianzhong he was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: During Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 初，太子在潞州，襄城張暐為銅鞮令，性豪殖，喜賓客弋獵事，厚奉太子，數集其家。
entries.en: Earlier, while the prince was in Luzhou, Zhang Wei of Xiangcheng, magistrate of Tongdi, was wealthy and loved hunting and guests; he entertained the prince often at his home.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the prince was in Luzhou, Zhang Wei of Xiangcheng was magistrate of Tongdi, extravagant and fond of entertaining guests in hunting; he lavishly supported the prince and often gathered at his home.

entries.zh: 山東倡人趙元禮有女，善歌舞，得幸太子，止暐第，其後生子瑛者也。
entries.en: A Shandong performer named Zhao Yuanli had a daughter who danced and sang; favored by the prince, she stayed at Zhang Wei's house and later bore his son Ying.
entries.literal: A Shandong entertainer Zhao Yuanli had a daughter skilled in song and dance who won the prince's favor and lodged at Wei's house; later she bore the son Ying.

entries.zh: 太子已平內難，召暐，拜宮門郎，與姜交、崔滌、李令問、王守一、薛伯陽等並侍左右。
entries.en: After the internal crisis he recalled Zhang Wei as palace gate officer, with Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others in attendance.
entries.literal: After the prince had settled the inner turmoil, he summoned Wei and appointed him Gate Officer of the Palace, with Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others all attending at his side.

entries.zh: 令問累擢殿中少監，守一太仆少卿。
entries.en: Li Lingwen rose to junior palace supervisor; Wang Shouyi became vice director of the imperial stud.
entries.literal: Lingwen was repeatedly promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Palace; Shouyi became Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

entries.zh: 此數人以東宮皆勢重天下。
entries.en: Through their ties to the heir apparent, these men all wielded enormous influence.
entries.literal: These several men, through the Eastern Palace, all held power weighty under Heaven.

entries.zh: 琚是時方補諸暨縣主簿，過謝東宮，至廷中，徐行高視，侍衛何止曰：「太子在！」
entries.en: Ju had just become chief clerk of Zhuji and came to thank the heir apparent; in the courtyard he walked slowly, looking about boldly, until an attendant cried, "The crown prince is here!"
entries.literal: Ju at this time had just been appointed chief clerk of Zhuji county and came to thank the Eastern Palace; in the courtyard he walked slowly with a high gaze, and an attendant cried, "The crown prince is here!

entries.zh: 琚怒曰：「在外惟聞太平公主，不聞有太子。
entries.en: Ju snapped, "Out there people talk only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.
entries.literal: Ju angrily said, "Outside one hears only of Princess Taiping, not of a crown prince.

entries.zh: 太子本有功於社稷，孝於君親，安得此聲？」
entries.en: The prince has served the realm and honored his father—how did he come by such a reputation?"
entries.literal: The crown prince himself has merit for the altars of state and filial piety toward his sovereign parent—how can such a reputation arise?

entries.zh: 太子遽召見，琚曰：「韋氏躬行弒逆，天下動搖，人思李氏，故殿下取之易也。
entries.en: The prince summoned him at once; Ju said, "The Wei clan murdered the emperor and shook the realm; men longed for the Li, so you seized power easily.
entries.literal: The prince hastily summoned him to audience; Ju said, "The Wei clan personally carried out regicide; the realm was shaken and men yearned for the Li house, so Your Highness took it easily.

entries.zh: 今天下已定，太平專思立功，左右大臣多為其用，天子以元妹，能忍其過，臣竊為殿下寒心。」
entries.en: Today the realm is settled, but Taiping still schemes for power, many ministers serve her, and the emperor indulges her as his sister—I fear for you."
entries.literal: Now the realm is already settled, yet Taiping single-mindedly seeks to build merit; many great ministers at left and right serve her use; the Son of Heaven, as her younger brother by the same mother, can bear her faults—I privately feel cold at heart for Your Highness.

entries.zh: 太子命坐，且泣曰：「計將安便？」
entries.en: The prince bade him sit and wept, "What is to be done?"
entries.literal: The prince ordered him to sit and, weeping, said, "What plan will serve?"

entries.zh: 琚曰：「昔漢蓋主供養昭帝，其後與上官桀謀殺霍光，不及天子，而帝猶以大義去之。
entries.en: Ju said, "Under Han, Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao, then plotted with Shangguan Jie against Huo Guang; though she never touched the throne, the emperor removed her on principle.
entries.literal: Ju said, "Formerly in Han, Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao and later joined Shangguan Jie in plotting to kill Huo Guang; she did not reach the Son of Heaven, yet the emperor still removed her on great principle.

entries.zh: 今太子功定天下，公主乃敢妄圖，大臣樹黨，有廢立意。
entries.en: Your merit has settled the realm, yet the princess plots openly and ministers form factions to replace you.
entries.literal: Now the crown prince's merit has settled the realm, yet the princess dares to scheme wantonly; great ministers form factions and there is intent to depose and establish.

entries.zh: 太子誠召張說、劉幽求、郭元振等計之，憂可紓也。」
entries.en: Summon Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and others to counsel you, and your fear may ease."
entries.literal: If the crown prince truly summons Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and others to plan, the worry can be eased.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「先生何以自隱而日與寡人遊？」
entries.en: The prince asked, "How can you stay hidden yet visit me every day?"
entries.literal: The prince said, "How can you, sir, hide yourself yet day after day keep company with me?"

entries.zh: 琚曰：「臣善丹沙，且工諧隱，願比優人。」
entries.en: Ju answered, "I know alchemy and merry disguise; let me pass as a court entertainer."
entries.literal: Ju said, "Your subject is skilled in cinnabar and also adept at jest and concealment; I wish to be like a performer."

entries.zh: 太子喜，恨相知晚。
entries.en: The prince was delighted and wished they had met sooner.
entries.literal: The prince was pleased and regretted that they had met so late.

entries.zh: 翌日授詹事府司直、內供奉，兼崇文學士。
entries.en: The next day Ju was made rectifier of the heir's household, inner attendant, and scholar of the Chongwen Institute.
entries.literal: The next day he was appointed Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household, inner attendant, and concurrently Scholar of the Chongwen Institute.

entries.zh: 日以諸王及姜皎等入侍，獨琚常豫秘謀。
entries.en: Princes and Jiang Jiao attended daily, but only Ju shared the secret counsel.
entries.literal: Day by day the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others entered attendance, but Ju alone was regularly privy to secret plans.

entries.zh: 不逾月，遷太子舍人，兼諫議大夫。
entries.en: Within a month he became secretary to the heir apparent and remonstrating grandee.
entries.literal: Within less than a month he was moved to Secretary of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Remonstrating Grandee.

entries.zh: 太子受內禪，擢中書侍郎。
entries.en: When the prince took the inner abdication, Ju was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the prince received the inner abdication, Ju was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 公主謀益甚，幽求、暐謀先事誅之，侍御史鄧光賓漏謀，不克，皆得罪。
entries.en: As the princess's plots deepened, Youqiu and Zhang Wei planned to strike first, but Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plot; it failed and all were punished.
entries.literal: The princess's plotting grew worse; Youqiu and Wei plotted to act first and execute her, but Attending Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plan, it did not succeed, and all were punished.

entries.zh: 久之，琚見事迫，請帝決策。
entries.en: As danger mounted, Ju urged the emperor to act.
entries.literal: After a long while, seeing affairs pressing, Ju asked the Emperor to decide.

entries.zh: 先天二年七月，乃與岐王、薛王、姜皎、李令問、王毛仲、王守一以鐵騎至承天門。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Xiantian 2 he rode with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi at the head of armored cavalry to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, together with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi, he led iron cavalry to the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

entries.zh: 太上皇聞外嘩噪，召郭元振升承天樓，閉關以拒，俄而侍御史任知古召募數百人於朝堂，不得入。
entries.en: The retired emperor heard the uproar and sent Guo Yuanzhen to the tower to shut the gates; Censor Ren Zhigu raised hundreds at the court but could not enter.
entries.literal: The Retired Emperor heard the outer clamor, summoned Guo Yuanzhen to ascend the Tower of Accepting Heaven, closed the gates to resist; soon Attending Censor Ren Zhigu recruited several hundred men in the court hall but could not enter.

entries.zh: 少選，琚從帝至樓下，誅蕭至忠、岑義、竇懷貞，斬常元楷李慈北闕下、賈膺福李猷於內客省。
entries.en: Soon Ju followed the emperor below the tower; Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen were killed, Chang Yuankai and Li Ci beheaded at the northern gate, Jia Yingfu and Li You in the inner service office.
entries.literal: Shortly after, Ju followed the Emperor to below the tower; Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen were executed, Chang Yuankai and Li Ci were beheaded below the northern gate, and Jia Yingfu and Li You at the Inner Service Office.

entries.zh: 事平，琚進戶部尚書、封趙國公，皎工部尚書、楚國公，毛仲輔國大將軍、霍國公，守一太常卿、晉國公，各食實戶五百；
entries.en: After victory Ju became minister of revenue and Duke of Zhao; Jiang Jiao minister of works and Duke of Chu; Wang Maozhong general who assists the state and Duke of Huo; Wang Shouyi minister of sacrifices and Duke of Jin—each with five hundred fief households;
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, Ju was advanced to Minister of Revenue and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao; Jiao to Minister of Works and Duke of Chu; Maozhong to General Who Assists the State and Duke of Huo; Shouyi to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Jin—each with five hundred substantive households;

entries.zh: 令問殿中監、宋國公，實戶三百。
entries.en: Li Lingwen became palace supervisor and Duke of Song with three hundred households.
entries.literal: Lingwen to Supervisor of the Palace and Duke of Song, with three hundred substantive households.

entries.zh: 琚、皎、令問辭不就，以舊官增戶二百。
entries.en: Ju, Jiang Jiao, and Li Lingwen declined the new posts and kept their old ranks with two hundred added households.
entries.literal: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen declined and did not accept, keeping their former offices with two hundred additional households.

entries.zh: 於是帝召燕內殿，賜金銀雜皿皆一床、帛二千、第一區。
entries.en: The emperor feasted them in the inner palace and gave each a couch piled with gold and silver vessels, two thousand lengths of silk, and a mansion.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor summoned them to feast in the inner hall and granted gold, silver, and mixed vessels each filling one couch, two thousand lengths of silk, and one fine residence.

entries.zh: 帝崩，韋後專制，畏禍及，更因僧普潤、道士王曄私謁臨淄王以自托，且密贊大計。
entries.en: After the emperor's death, when Empress Wei seized power, he feared for his life and, through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye, secretly sought out the Prince of Linzi, pledging support for the coup.
entries.literal: When the emperor died and Empress Wei monopolized power, fearing calamity would reach him, he further through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye paid a private visit to the Prince of Linzi to attach himself, and secretly supported the great plan.

entries.zh: 王曰：「謀非計身，直紓親難爾。」
entries.en: The prince replied, "This is not scheming for myself, only to save my father."
entries.literal: The prince said, "The plan is not calculated for one's person; it is simply to relieve a parent's distress.

entries.zh: 日用曰：「至孝動天，舉無不克。
entries.en: Riyong said, "Filial devotion so great moves Heaven itself—you cannot fail.
entries.literal: Riyong said, "Supreme filial piety moves Heaven; in action nothing fails.

entries.zh: 然利先發，不則有後憂。」
entries.en: But you must strike first, or regret will follow."
entries.literal: Yet it profits to strike first; otherwise there will be later worry."

entries.zh: 及韋氏平，夜詔權雍州長史，以功授黃門侍郎，參知機務，封齊國公，賜實戶二百。
entries.en: After the Wei faction fell, he was named acting chief administrator of Yongzhou the same night; rewarded with the vice-directorship of the Yellow Gate and a share in government, he was created Duke of Qi with two hundred fief households.
entries.literal: When the Wei faction was pacified, that night he was ordered to act as chief administrator of Yongzhou; for merit he was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate with a role in state affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and granted two hundred substantive households.

entries.zh: 坐與薛稷相忿競，罷政事，為婺州長史。
entries.en: A feud with Xue Ji cost him his place at court, and he was sent out as chief administrator of Wu.
entries.literal: Because of mutual resentment and rivalry with Xue Ji, he left the government and became chief administrator of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 歷揚、汴、允三州刺史。
entries.en: He later served as prefect of Yang, Bian, and Yun in succession.
entries.literal: He served in turn as prefect of Yang, Bian, and Yun prefectures.

entries.zh: 由荊州長史入奏計，因言：「太平公主逆節有萌，陛下往以宮府討有罪，臣、子勢須謀與力，今據大位，一下制書定矣。」
entries.en: Coming in from Jingzhou to report revenues, he said, "Princess Taiping's treason is already showing. You once relied on the palace guard to punish criminals; as prince you needed allies. Now that you sit on the throne, a single edict can finish her."
entries.literal: Entering court from chief administrator of Jingzhou to present the annual accounts, he said, "Princess Taiping's rebellious conduct is already sprouting. Your Majesty formerly used the palace offices to punish the guilty; as prince and son, you had to scheme with others for strength. Now that you hold the great position, one imperial decree will settle it.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「畏驚太上皇，奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "But I fear frightening my father—what then?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "I fear alarming the Retired Emperor—what is to be done?"

entries.zh: 日用曰：「庶人之孝，承順顏色；
entries.en: Riyong answered, "For a common man, filial piety means pleasing a parent's face;
entries.literal: Riyong said, "The commoner's filial piety is to comply with his parent's countenance;

entries.zh: 天子之孝，惟安國家，定社稷。
entries.en: for a Son of Heaven it means securing the realm and fixing the altars of state.
entries.literal: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is solely to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 若令奸宄竊發，以亡大業，可為孝乎？
entries.en: If traitors strike and the dynasty falls, is that filial piety?
entries.literal: If you allow traitors to steal forth and thereby lose the great enterprise, can that be called filial piety?

entries.zh: 請先安北軍而後捕逆黨，於太上皇固無所驚。」
entries.en: Secure the Northern Army first, then arrest the rebels—the Retired Emperor need never be troubled."
entries.literal: I ask that you first secure the Northern Army and afterward seize the rebel faction; the Retired Emperor will certainly not be alarmed.

entries.zh: 帝納之。
entries.en: The emperor took his advice.
entries.literal: The Emperor accepted this.

entries.zh: 及討逆，詔權檢校雍州長史，以功益封二百戶，進吏部尚書。
entries.en: During the purge he was again made acting chief administrator of Yongzhou; rewarded with two hundred additional fief households, he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, he was ordered to act as inspecting chief administrator of Yongzhou; for merit his fief was increased by two hundred households and he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 王毛仲，高麗人。
entries.en: Wang Maozhong was from Goguryeo.
entries.literal: Wang Maozhong was a man of Goguryeo.

entries.zh: 父坐事，沒為官奴，生毛仲，故長事臨淄王。
entries.en: His father was punished and made a government slave; Maozhong was born in bondage and grew up serving the Prince of Linzi.
entries.literal: His father was convicted and enslaved to government service; Maozhong was born thereby and so from childhood attended the Prince of Linzi.

entries.zh: 王出潞州，有李守德者，為人奴，善騎射，王市得之，並侍左右，而毛仲為明悟。
entries.en: Leaving Luzhou, the prince bought Li Shoude, a slave skilled in horsemanship and archery; both attended him, though Maozhong was the sharper.
entries.literal: When the prince left Luzhou there was one Li Shoude, a man's slave skilled in riding and archery; the prince purchased him and both attended at his side, while Maozhong was the more perceptive.

entries.zh: 景龍中，王還長安，二人常負房箙以從。
entries.en: During Jinglong the prince returned to Chang'an; the two often carried his gear.
entries.literal: In the Jinglong era the prince returned to Chang'an; the two often carried quivers and followed.

entries.zh: 王數引萬騎帥長及豪俊，賜飲食金帛，得其歡心。
entries.en: The prince often entertained commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold men with food, drink, gold, and silk.
entries.literal: The prince repeatedly summoned commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold men, bestowing food, drink, gold, and silk to win their hearts.

entries.zh: 毛仲曉旨，亦布誠結納，王嘉之。
entries.en: Maozhong read his mind, won the soldiers over, and won the prince's praise.
entries.literal: Maozhong understood his intent and also spread sincerity and formed ties; the prince praised him.

entries.zh: 韋後稱制，令韋播、高嵩為羽林將軍，押萬騎，以苛峭樹威。
entries.en: When Empress Wei ruled, she put Wei Bo and Gao Song in command of the Ten Thousand Riders and ruled them harshly.
entries.literal: When Empress Wei assumed regency she appointed Wei Bo and Gao Song as generals of the Imperial Insignia Army to command the Ten Thousand Riders, establishing authority through harsh severity.

entries.zh: 果毅葛福順、陳玄禮訴於王，王方與劉幽求、薛宗簡及利仁府折沖麻嗣宗謀舉大計，幽求諷之，皆願效死，遂入討韋氏。
entries.en: Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince, who was plotting with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and Ma Sizong; all pledged their lives, and they marched against the Wei clan.
entries.literal: Company commanders Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince; the prince was then planning the great undertaking with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and Ma Sizong, adjutant of the Liren Circuit—Youqiu admonished them, and all wished to die in service; they then entered to suppress the Wei faction.

entries.zh: 守德從帝止苑中，而毛仲匿不出，事定數日，乃還，不之責，例擢將軍。
entries.en: Shoude stayed with the prince in the park; Maozhong hid until days after the coup, yet was not blamed and was promoted to general.
entries.literal: Shoude followed the emperor and stopped in the park, while Maozhong hid and did not come out; several days after the affair was settled he returned, was not blamed, and by precedent was promoted to general.

entries.zh: 王為皇太子，以毛仲知東宮馬駝鷹狗等坊。
entries.en: As crown prince, the prince put Maozhong in charge of the heir's stables, hawks, and hounds.
entries.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Maozhong was put in charge of the Eastern Palace's horses, camels, falcons, dogs, and other yards.

entries.zh: 不旬歲，至大將軍，階三品。
entries.en: In less than a year he reached grand general, third rank.
entries.literal: Within less than ten months he reached Grand General, third rank.

entries.zh: 與誅蕭至忠等，以功進輔國大將軍，檢校內外閑廄，知監牧使，進封霍國公，實封戶五百。
entries.en: For helping kill Xiao Zhizhong and others, he was promoted for merit to General Who Assists the State, oversaw the inner and outer imperial stud parks, supervised the commissioner of herds, and was made Duke of Huo with five hundred substantive households.
entries.literal: Joining in the execution of Xiao Zhizhong and others, for merit he was advanced to General Who Assists the State, inspecting the inner and outer stud parks, knowing the supervisory commissioner of herds, promoted to Duke of Huo with five hundred substantive households.

entries.zh: 與諸王及姜皎等侍禁中，至連榻而坐。
entries.en: He attended in the inner palace with the princes and Jiang Jiao, even sharing couches.
entries.literal: With the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others he attended within the forbidden quarters, even sitting on connected couches.

entries.zh: 帝暫不見，惘惘若有失，見則釋然。
entries.en: If the emperor missed him briefly he grew uneasy; when Maozhong appeared he was comforted.
entries.literal: When the Emperor briefly did not see him, he was restless as if lost; when he saw him, he was relieved.

entries.zh: 開元九年，詔持節為朔方道防禦討擊大使，與左領軍大總管王晙、天兵軍節度使張說、幽州節度使裴伷先等數計事。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 9 he was sent with staff authority to Shuofang and met with Wang Jun, Zhang Yue, and Pei Youxian to plan campaigns.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan an edict ordered him to bear the staff of authority as defense and campaign commissioner of the Shuofang circuit, and with Left Army General-in-Chief Wang Jun, Tianbing military commissioner Zhang Yue, and Youzhou military commissioner Pei Youxian and others he repeatedly planned affairs.

entries.zh: 毛仲始見飾擢，頗持法，不避權貴為可喜事。
entries.en: At first, newly honored, he enforced the law fearlessly and pleased the emperor.
entries.literal: At first, seeing fine promotion, he quite upheld the law and did not avoid the powerful in matters that could please.

entries.zh: 兩營萬騎及閑廄官吏憚之無敢犯，雖官田草萊，樵斂不敢欺。
entries.en: Riders and stud officials feared him; even on government land none dared steal fodder.
entries.literal: The two camps of Ten Thousand Riders and the stud-yard officials all feared him and none dared offend; even official fields and overgrown wastes—woodcutters dared not cheat.

entries.zh: 於牧事尤力，娩息不訾。
entries.en: He excelled at herd management; foals and calves multiplied beyond count.
entries.literal: In herd affairs he was especially forceful; births and increases were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 初監馬二十四萬，後乃至四十三萬，牛羊皆數倍。
entries.en: Horses under his charge rose from 240,000 to 430,000; cattle and sheep multiplied likewise.
entries.literal: At first supervised horses were two hundred forty thousand; later they reached four hundred thirty thousand, and cattle and sheep were several times more.

entries.zh: 蒔茼麥、苜蓿千九百頃以禦冬。
entries.en: He planted artemisia and alfalfa on 1,900 qing for winter fodder.
entries.literal: He planted artemisia and alfalfa on one thousand nine hundred qing to guard against winter.

entries.zh: 市死畜，售絹八萬。
entries.en: Dead stock was sold for eighty thousand strings' worth of silk.
entries.literal: He purchased dead livestock and sold silk worth eighty thousand.

entries.zh: 募嚴道僰僮千口為牧圉。
entries.en: He recruited a thousand Yi herders from Yandao.
entries.literal: He recruited a thousand Yi boys from Yandao to serve as herdsmen.

entries.zh: 檢勒芻菽無漏隱，歲贏數萬石。
entries.en: He audited fodder so tightly that yearly surpluses reached tens of thousands of piculs.
entries.literal: He inspected fodder and grain without leakage or concealment; each year the surplus reached tens of thousands of piculs.

entries.zh: 從帝東封，取牧馬數萬匹，每色一隊，相間如錦繡，天子才之。
entries.en: At the eastern Feng rites he paraded tens of thousands of horses in color-ranked companies like brocade, to the emperor's delight.
entries.literal: Following the emperor on the eastern Feng sacrifice, he took tens of thousands of herd horses, each color in one company, alternating like brocade; the Son of Heaven was pleased with them.

entries.zh: 還，加開府儀同三司，自開元後，唯王仁皎、姚崇、宋璟及毛仲得之。
entries.en: On his return he received the privilege of an opening office—after Kaiyuan only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong had held it.
entries.literal: On return he was given the honor of Grand Master of the Palace with Opening an Office; after Kaiyuan only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong obtained it.

entries.zh: 陳玄禮宿衛宮禁，以淳篤自檢。
entries.en: Chen Xuanli long guarded the palace and conducted himself with plain integrity.
entries.literal: Chen Xuanli long guarded the palace precincts and restrained himself with plain sincerity.

entries.zh: 帝嘗欲幸虢國夫人第，諫曰：「未宣敕，不可輕去就。」
entries.en: When the emperor wished to visit the Lady of Guo's mansion, Xuanli warned, "Without a proclaimed edict you must not go lightly."
entries.literal: The emperor once wished to visit the mansion of the Lady of Guo; Xuanli remonstrated, "Without an announced edict, one must not lightly go or stay.

entries.zh: 帝為止。
entries.en: The emperor yielded.
entries.literal: The emperor stopped on his account.

entries.zh: 後在華清宮，正月望夜，帝將出遊，復諫曰：「宮外曠野無備豫，陛下必出遊，願歸城闕。」
entries.en: At Huaqing on the first month's full moon, as the emperor prepared an outing, he again urged, "The grounds outside are unguarded—if you must go out, return to the city."
entries.literal: Later at Huaqing Palace, on the full-moon night of the first month, when the emperor was about to go out touring, he again remonstrated, "Outside the palace is open wild without preparations; if Your Majesty must tour, I beg you return to the walled city.

entries.zh: 帝不能奪。
entries.en: The emperor could not refuse him.
entries.literal: The emperor could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 安祿山反，謀誅楊國忠闕下，不克，至馬嵬，卒誅之。
entries.en: When An Lushan rebelled he tried to kill Yang Guozhong at the gate and failed; at Mawei he finally killed him.
entries.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he plotted to kill Yang Guozhong below the palace gate but did not succeed; at Mawei he finally executed him.

entries.zh: 從入蜀。
entries.en: He followed the emperor into Shu.
entries.literal: He followed in entering Shu.

entries.zh: 還，封祭國公。
entries.en: After the return he was made Duke of Ji.
entries.literal: On return he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

entries.zh: 及李輔國遷帝西內，玄禮以老卒。
entries.en: When Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the western palace, Xuanli died in old age.
entries.literal: When Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the western inner palace, Xuanli died of old age.

entries.zh: 景雲二年，以戶部尚書罷政事。
entries.en: In Jingyun 2 he left office while serving as Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he left the government as Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 不旬月，遷吏部，拜侍中。
entries.en: In less than a month he moved to the Ministry of Personnel and was made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Within less than ten days he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 璽詔曰：「頃王室不造，中宗厭代，戚孽專亂，將隕社稷，朕與王公皆幾於難。
entries.en: An imperial edict declared: "The house has lately been afflicted: Zhongzong left the throne, vicious relatives seized power and nearly destroyed the realm, and I with the princes and officials were all but undone.
entries.literal: An imperial edict said: "Recently the royal house suffered misfortune; Emperor Zhongzong passed from the throne; wicked kin monopolized rebellion and nearly brought down the altars of state; I and the princes and ministers all came close to ruin.

entries.zh: 幽求處危思奮，翊贊聖儲，協和義士，震殄元惡。
entries.en: Youqiu rose to the crisis, backed the rightful heir, rallied loyal men, and crushed the arch-villains.
entries.literal: Youqiu, facing peril, thought to strive; he aided and supported the sacred heir, united men of righteousness, and in awe struck down the chief evil.

entries.zh: 國家之復存，繄幽求是賴，厥庸茂焉，朕用嘉之。
entries.en: The realm's survival rested on Youqiu; his service was great, and I honor it accordingly.
entries.literal: That the state was restored to life depended on Youqiu; his merit is abundant, and I therefore praise him.

entries.zh: 雖胙以土宇，而賦入未廣。
entries.en: Though he has been granted a fief, its revenue remains modest.
entries.literal: Although enfeoffed with territory, his tax income is not yet broad.

entries.zh: 昔西漢行封，更擇多戶；
entries.en: In the Western Han, new enfeoffments were often drawn from more populous districts;
entries.literal: Formerly in the Western Han, when enfeoffments were granted, households of greater number were chosen again;

entries.zh: 東京定賞，復增大邑。
entries.en: and when rewards were fixed in the Eastern Capital, large fiefs were again enlarged.
entries.literal: in the Eastern Capital when rewards were fixed, great districts were again enlarged.

entries.zh: 宜加賜實封二百戶，子子孫孫傳國無絕，特免十死，銘諸鐵券，以傳其功。」
entries.en: Let an additional two hundred taxable households be granted, the fief to pass in perpetuity, ten capital offenses remitted, and the deed engraved on an iron charter so his service may endure."
entries.literal: He should be further granted two hundred households of substantive fief, with the state transmitted without end from sons to grandsons; he is specially exempted from ten deaths; this shall be inscribed on the iron certificate to transmit his merit."

entries.zh: 先天元年，為尚書右仆射、同中書門下三品，監修國史。
entries.en: In Xiantian 1 he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, a participant in the highest council, and put in charge of compiling the national history.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiantian he became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the same rank as the Three Departments at the Secretariat Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 崔日用，滑州靈昌人。
entries.en: Cui Riyong came from Lingchang in Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Cui Riyong was a native of Lingchang in Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 擢進士第，為芮城尉。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination and became assistant magistrate of Ruicheng.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Ruicheng.

entries.zh: 大足元年，武後幸長安，陜州刺史宗楚客委以頓峙，饋獻豐甘，稱過賓使者。
entries.en: In Dazu 1, when Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Zong Chuke, prefect of Shan, put him in charge of provisioning the imperial progress; he supplied rich delicacies and surpassed the envoys of passing guests.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dazu, when Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Zong Chuke, prefect of Shan Prefecture, entrusted him with provisioning the imperial progress; he presented abundant delicacies and outdid the envoys of passing guests.

entries.zh: 楚客嘆其能，亟薦之，擢為新豐尉，遷監宗御史。
entries.en: Chuke admired his talent, quickly recommended him, made him assistant magistrate of Xinfeng, and then transferred him to investigating censor of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
entries.literal: Chuke marveled at his ability, urgently recommended him, promoted him to assistant magistrate of Xinfeng, and transferred him to investigating censor of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 陰附安樂公主，得稍遷。
entries.en: Covertly aligned with Princess Anle, he gradually rose in rank.
entries.literal: Covertly attached to Princess Anle, he gradually advanced.

entries.zh: 神龍中，鄭普思納女後宮，日用劾奏，中宗初不省，廷爭切至，普思由是得罪。
entries.en: During Shenlong, Zheng Pusi sent his daughter into the inner palace; Riyong impeached him; Zhongzong at first ignored the charge, but after fierce debate at court Pusi was punished.
entries.literal: During Shenlong, Zheng Pusi presented his daughter to the inner palace; Riyong impeached him; at first Zhongzong paid no heed, but after heated debate at court Pusi was punished on that account.

entries.zh: 時諸武若三思、延秀及楚客等權寵交煽，日用多所結納，驟拜兵部侍郎。
entries.en: At that time Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, Chuke, and others traded power and favor; Riyong cultivated many alliances and was suddenly made vice minister of war.
entries.literal: At that time the various Wu—Sansi, Yanxiu—and Chuke and others exchanged power and favor; Riyong cultivated many ties and was suddenly made vice minister of war.

entries.zh: 宴內殿，酒酣，起為《回波舞》，求學士，即詔兼脩文館學士。
entries.en: At an inner-palace banquet, when the wine was deep, he rose and danced the "Wave-Returning Dance," asked to be made a scholar, and was immediately ordered to serve concurrently as a scholar of the Xiuxian Academy.
entries.literal: At a banquet in the inner palace, when the wine had gone deep, he rose and performed the "Wave-Returning Dance," sought the title of scholar, and was immediately ordered to serve concurrently as a scholar of the Xiuxian Academy.

entries.zh: 劉鍾崔二王
entries.en: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs
entries.literal: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs

entries.zh: 中宗以嶠身宰相，乃自陳失政，丐罷官，無所嫁非，手詔詰讓。
entries.en: Emperor Zhongzong, noting that Qiao himself was chancellor, saw his confession of misgovernment and plea to resign as blaming others without cause and issued a personal edict of rebuke.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, since Qiao himself was chancellor, took his self-accusation of misgovernment and plea to resign as blaming others without basis, and issued a personal edict rebuking him.

entries.zh: 嶠惶恐，復視事。
entries.en: Qiao was alarmed and resumed his duties.
entries.literal: Qiao was fearful and resumed his duties.

entries.zh: 三年，加修文館大學士，封趙國公，以特進同中書門下三品。
entries.en: In the third year he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and granted Special Advancement with Third Grade rank equal to the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the third year he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and made Special Advancement with the rank of Third Grade, equal to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 睿宗立，罷政事，下除懷州刺史，致仕。
entries.en: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Qiao left government, was demoted to prefect of Huai, and retired.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Qiao was removed from government affairs, demoted to prefect of Huai Prefecture, and retired.

entries.zh: 初，中宗崩，嶠嘗密請相王諸子不宜留京師。
entries.en: Earlier, when Emperor Zhongzong died, Qiao had secretly urged that the Prince of Xiang's sons should not remain in the capital.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Zhongzong died, Qiao had secretly memorialized that the Prince of Xiang's sons ought not remain in the capital.

entries.zh: 及玄宗嗣位，獲其表宮中，或請誅之。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, the memorial was found in the palace and some urged his execution.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, the memorial was found in the palace and some asked that he be executed.

entries.zh: 張說曰：「嶠誠懵逆順，然為當時謀，吠非其主，不可追罪。」
entries.en: Zhang Yue said, "Qiao was indeed confused about loyalty, yet he acted as counsel for his time—a dog barks at strangers, not at its master; his offense cannot be punished retroactively".
entries.literal: Zhang Yue said: "Qiao was indeed confused about what accords and what opposes, yet he acted as counsel for his time; a dog barks not at its master—his offense cannot be pursued".

entries.zh: 天子亦顧數更赦，遂免，貶滁州別駕，聽隨子虔州刺史暢之官。
entries.en: The emperor also weighed the many amnesties and spared him, demoting him to Vice Prefect of Chu with permission to accompany his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven also considered the many amnesties and pardoned him, demoting him to Vice Prefect of Chu and permitting him to follow his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.

entries.zh: 改廬州別駕，卒，年七十。
entries.en: He was reassigned to Vice Prefect of Lu and died at seventy.
entries.literal: He was changed to Vice Prefect of Lu and died, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 蕭至忠，沂州丞人。
entries.en: Xiao Zhizhong was a native of Cheng in Yi Prefecture.
entries.literal: Xiao Zhizhong was a man of Cheng in Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 祖德言，為秘書少監。
entries.en: His grandfather Deyan served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His grandfather Deyan was Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至忠少與友期諸路，會雨雪，人引避，至忠曰：「寧有與人期可以失信？」
entries.en: As a youth Zhizhong arranged to meet a friend at a crossroads; when snow and rain came, others urged him to take shelter. He said, "How can one keep an appointment and break faith"?
entries.literal: Zhizhong in youth made an appointment with a friend at a crossroads; when snow and rain came, people urged him to take shelter. Zhizhong said: "Can one make an appointment with another and break faith"?

entries.zh: 卒友至乃去，眾嘆服。
entries.en: He left only after his friend arrived; onlookers marveled.
entries.literal: Only when his friend arrived did he leave; the crowd sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 仕為伊闕、洛陽尉。
entries.en: He served as magistrate of Yique and Luoyang.
entries.literal: In office he served as magistrate of Yique and Luoyang.

entries.zh: 遷監察御史，劾奏鳳閣侍郎蘇味道贓貪，超拜吏部員外郎。
entries.en: Promoted to investigating censor, he impeached Vice Director Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for corruption and was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor, impeached Vice Director Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for corruption, and was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 至忠長擊斷，譽聞當時。
entries.en: Zhizhong was famed for decisive judgment and won renown in his day.
entries.literal: Zhizhong excelled in decisive judgment; his reputation was known in his time.

entries.zh: 中宗神龍初，為御史中丞。
entries.en: In the early Shenlong era under Emperor Zhongzong he became Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the early Shenlong era of Emperor Zhongzong he became Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 始，至忠為御史，而李承嘉為大夫，嘗讓諸御史曰：「彈事有不咨大夫，可乎？」
entries.en: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor and Li Chengjia was chief censor, Li once rebuked the censors: "In impeachment matters, is it permissible not to consult the chief censor"?
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor and Li Chengjia was chief censor, Li once rebuked the censors, saying: "In impeachment matters, is it permissible not to consult the chief censor"?

entries.zh: 眾不敢對，至忠獨曰：「故事，臺無長官。
entries.en: None dared reply; Zhizhong alone said, "By precedent the Censorate has no chief officer.
entries.literal: None dared reply; Zhizhong alone said: "By precedent the Censorate has no chief officer.

entries.zh: 御史，天子耳目也，其所請奏當專達，若大夫許而後論，即劾大夫者，又誰白哉？」
entries.en: Censors are the emperor's eyes and ears; their memorials should reach him directly. If the chief censor must approve first, who will report the chief censor when he is impeached?"
entries.literal: Censors are the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; what they memorialize should reach him directly. If the chief censor must approve before discussion, then who will report the chief censor when he is impeached?"

entries.zh: 承嘉慚。
entries.en: Chengjia was ashamed.
entries.literal: Chengjia was ashamed.

entries.zh: 至是，承嘉為戶部尚書，至忠劾祝欽明、竇希玠與承嘉等罪，百寮震悚。
entries.en: By then Chengjia was Minister of Revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, Chengjia, and others for crimes, and the entire bureaucracy trembled.
entries.literal: By this time Chengjia was Minister of Revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, and Chengjia and others for crimes, and the hundred officials trembled in awe.

entries.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，猶兼中丞。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel while retaining the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, still also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 節湣太子以兵誅武三思而敗，宗楚客等諗侍御史冉祖雍上變，言相王與太子謀。
entries.en: When Crown Prince Jiemin raised troops to kill Wu Sansi and failed, Zong Chuke and others urged Investigating Censor Ran Zuyong to report a plot between the Prince of Xiang and the crown prince.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Jiemin used troops to kill Wu Sansi and failed, Zong Chuke and others prompted Investigating Censor Ran Zuyong to submit an accusation, saying the Prince of Xiang and the crown prince had plotted together.

entries.zh: 帝欲按之，至忠泣曰：「往者，天後欲以相王為太子，而王不食累日，獨請迎陛下，其讓德天下莫不聞。
entries.en: The emperor wished to investigate; Zhizhong wept and said, "In the past Empress Wu wanted to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, but he fasted for days and alone asked to welcome Your Majesty back—his yielding virtue was known throughout the realm.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to investigate; Zhizhong wept and said: "In the past Empress Tian wanted to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, but the prince would not eat for days and alone asked to welcome Your Majesty back—his virtue of yielding was heard by all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 陛下貴為天子，不能容一弟，受人羅織耶？
entries.en: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven yet cannot tolerate one younger brother—will you accept others' fabrications?
entries.literal: Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven yet cannot tolerate one younger brother—will you accept others' frame-ups?

entries.zh: 竊為陛下不取。」
entries.en: I cannot believe this is worthy of Your Majesty".
entries.literal: I secretly deem it unworthy of Your Majesty".

entries.zh: 帝納其言，止。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his counsel and dropped the matter.
entries.literal: The emperor accepted his words and stopped.

entries.zh: 尋授中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: He was soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 上疏陳時政曰：
entries.en: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying:
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth current affairs, saying:

entries.zh: 至忠始在朝，有風望，容止閑敏，見推為名臣。
entries.en: Early in his career Zhizhong enjoyed reputation and bearing, refined and quick in deportment, and was praised as a famed minister.
entries.literal: Zhizhong at first in court had reputation and bearing, deportment refined and quick, and was praised as a famed minister.

entries.zh: 外方直，糾擿不法，而內無守，觀時輕重而去就之。
entries.en: Outwardly upright, he impeached wrongdoing, yet inwardly he lacked constancy and shifted with the times.
entries.literal: Outwardly upright, he impeached what was unlawful, yet inwardly he had no constancy and weighed the times' shifts in going and staying.

entries.zh: 始為御史，桓彥範等頗引重。
entries.en: When he first became censor, Huan Yanfan and others greatly valued him.
entries.literal: When he first became censor, Huan Yanfan and others greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 五王失政，更因武三思得中丞，附安樂公主為宰相。
entries.en: After the Five Princes fell, he again obtained the vice censorate through Wu Sansi, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.
entries.literal: When the Five Princes lost power, he again through Wu Sansi obtained the vice censorate, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.

entries.zh: 及韋氏敗，遽發韋洵壟，持其女柩歸。
entries.en: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and took his daughter's coffin home.
entries.literal: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and took his daughter's coffin home.

entries.zh: 後依太平，復當國。
entries.en: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held power.
entries.literal: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held the government.

entries.zh: 嘗出主第，遇宋璟，璟戲曰：「非所望於蕭傅。」
entries.en: Once leaving the princess's mansion he met Song Jing, who jested, "This is not what was hoped of Master Xiao".
entries.literal: Once leaving the princess's mansion he met Song Jing; Jing jested: "This is not what was hoped of Master Xiao".

entries.zh: 至忠曰：「善乎，宋生之言。」
entries.en: Zhizhong said, "Well said, Master Song."
entries.literal: Zhizhong said: "Well said, Master Song's words."

entries.zh: 然不能自返也。
entries.en: Yet he could not turn back.
entries.literal: Yet he could not turn back.

entries.zh: 娣嫁蔣欽緒，欽緒每戒之，至忠不聽。
entries.en: His younger sister married Jiang Qinxu, who often warned him, but Zhizhong would not listen.
entries.literal: His younger sister married Jiang Qinxu; Qinxu often warned him, but Zhizhong would not listen.

entries.zh: 嘆曰：「九世卿族，一舉而滅之，可哀也已！」
entries.en: He sighed, "A ministerial clan of nine generations, destroyed in one stroke—how lamentable"!
entries.literal: He sighed: "A ministerial clan of nine generations, destroyed in one stroke—how lamentable"!

entries.zh: 不喜接賓客，以簡儉自高，故生平奉賜，無所遺施，及籍沒，珍寶不可計。
entries.en: He disliked receiving guests and prided himself on frugality, so in life he gave away nothing from his stipends; yet when his property was confiscated, treasures were beyond counting.
entries.literal: He did not like receiving guests and prided himself on simplicity and frugality, so in life his stipends and gifts were nowhere bestowed; yet when his property was confiscated, treasures were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 然玄宗賢其為人，後得源乾曜，亟用之，謂高力士曰：「若知吾進乾曜遽乎？
entries.en: Yet Emperor Xuanzong esteemed his character; later, when he obtained Yuan Qianyao, he quickly employed him and said to Gao Lishi, "Do you know how swiftly I advanced Qianyao?
entries.literal: Yet Emperor Xuanzong esteemed his character; later obtaining Yuan Qianyao, he quickly employed him and said to Gao Lishi: "Do you know how swiftly I advanced Qianyao?

entries.zh: 吾以其貌言似蕭至忠。」
entries.en: I took his appearance and manner as resembling Xiao Zhizhong".
entries.literal: I took his appearance and speech as resembling Xiao Zhizhong".

entries.zh: 力士曰：「彼不嘗負陛下乎？」
entries.en: Lishi said, "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"
entries.literal: Lishi said: "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「至忠誠國器，但晚謬爾，其始不謂之賢哉？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Zhizhong was truly a pillar of state, but erred in his later years—was he not called worthy at the start?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Zhizhong was truly an instrument of state, but erred late—was he not called worthy at the start?"

entries.zh: 尋遷侍中，舒國公。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Duke of Shu.

entries.zh: 韋後與敘昆弟，附屬籍。
entries.en: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the clan register.
entries.literal: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the clan register.

entries.zh: 武三思封戶在貝州，屬大水，刺史宋璟議免其租，巨源以為蠶桑可輸，繇是河朔人多流徙者。
entries.en: Wu Sansi's fief households in Bei Prefecture suffered great flood; Prefect Song Jing proposed remitting their rent. Juyuan held that tribute could still be delivered—hence many north of the Yellow River fled.
entries.literal: Wu Sansi's fief households were in Bei Prefecture, which suffered great flood; Prefect Song Jing proposed remitting their rent. Juyuan held that silkworms and mulberry could still be delivered—hence many north of the Yellow River fled and migrated.

entries.zh: 景龍二年。
entries.en: In the second year of Jinglong.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jinglong.

entries.zh: 韋後自言衣笥有五色雲，巨源倡其偽，勸中宗宣布天下，帝從其言，因是大赦。
entries.en: Empress Wei claimed five-colored clouds appeared in her wardrobe; Juyuan promoted the fraud and urged Zhongzong to proclaim it to the realm. The emperor complied and issued a great amnesty.
entries.literal: Empress Wei said herself that five-colored clouds appeared in her wardrobe; Juyuan led the falsehood and urged Zhongzong to proclaim it to all under Heaven. The emperor followed his words and thereby issued a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 巨源見帝昏惑，乃與宗楚客、鄭愔、趙延禧等推處祥妖，陰導韋氏行武後故事。
entries.en: Seeing the emperor benighted, Juyuan with Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others interpreted omens and secretly guided the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.
entries.literal: Juyuan saw the emperor benighted and confused; with Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others he interpreted omens and prodigies and secretly guided the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.

entries.zh: 俄遷尚書左仆射，仍知政事。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining control of government affairs.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and still directed government affairs.

entries.zh: 帝方南郊，巨源請後為亞獻，而自為終獻。
entries.en: During the southern suburb sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress serve as secondary offerer and he himself as final offerer.
entries.literal: When the emperor was at the southern suburb sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress be secondary offerer and he himself the final offerer.

entries.zh: 及臨淄王平諸韋，家人請避之，巨源曰：「吾大臣，無容見難不赴。」
entries.en: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, his family urged him to flee. Juyuan said, "I am a great minister—I cannot flee from danger".
entries.literal: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, his family asked him to avoid danger. Juyuan said: "I am a great minister—I cannot see difficulty and not go".

entries.zh: 出都街，亂兵殺之，年八十。
entries.en: He went into the capital street and was killed by mutinous troops at eighty.
entries.literal: He went out into the capital street and mutinous troops killed him, aged eighty.

entries.zh: 彥昭本以權幸進，中宗時，有巫趙挾鬼道出入禁掖，彥昭以姑事之。
entries.en: Yanzhao had advanced through power and favor; under Zhongzong a shaman Zhao practiced occult arts in the inner palace, and Yanzhao treated him with familial deference.
entries.literal: Yanzhao had originally advanced through power and favor; in Zhongzong's time a shaman Zhao practiced ghost ways and entered the inner palace. Yanzhao treated him as a paternal aunt would.

entries.zh: 嘗衣婦服，乘車與妻偕謁，其得宰相，巫力也。
entries.en: He once wore women's dress and rode with his wife to call on the shaman—it was the shaman's power that gained him the chancellorship.
entries.literal: He once wore women's dress and rode in a carriage with his wife to pay a visit together—the shaman's power gained him the chancellorship.

entries.zh: 於是殿中侍御史郭震劾暴舊惡。
entries.en: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Guo Zhen impeached him, exposing old crimes.
entries.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Guo Zhen impeached him, exposing old evils.

entries.zh: 會姚崇執政，惡其為人，貶江州別駕，卒。
entries.en: When Yao Chong held power he hated Yanzhao's character, demoted him to Vice Prefect of Jiang, and he died there.
entries.literal: When Yao Chong held government he hated Yanzhao's character and demoted him to Vice Prefect of Jiang; he died.

entries.zh: 和逢堯，岐州岐山人。
entries.en: He Fengyao was a native of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.
entries.literal: He Fengyao was a man of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 武後時，負鼎詣闕下上書，自言願助天子和飪百度。
entries.en: Under Empress Wu he carried a cauldron to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, offering to help the Son of Heaven harmonize all affairs of state.
entries.literal: In Empress Wu's time he carried a cauldron to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying himself that he wished to help the Son of Heaven harmonize the hundred duties.

entries.zh: 有司讓曰：「昔桀不道，伊尹負鼎於湯；
entries.en: The authorities rebuked him: "In old times Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;
entries.literal: The authorities rebuked him: "In old times Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;

entries.zh: 今天子聖明，百司以和，尚何所調？」
entries.en: today the Son of Heaven is sage and bright and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs harmonizing"?
entries.literal: today the Son of Heaven is sage and bright and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs harmonizing"?

entries.zh: 逢堯不能答，流莊州。
entries.en: Fengyao could not reply and was exiled to Zhuang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Fengyao could not reply and was exiled to Zhuang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十餘年，乃舉進士高第，累擢監察御史。
entries.en: After more than ten years he passed the jinshi in the top grade and rose to investigating censor.
entries.literal: After more than ten years he passed the jinshi in the top grade and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor.

entries.zh: 李蕭盧韋趙和
entries.en: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He
entries.literal: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He

entries.zh: 澣孫抗。
entries.en: Huan's grandson Kang.
entries.literal: Huan's grandson Kang.

entries.zh: 抗字遐舉，少值天寶亂，奉母夫人隱會稽。
entries.en: Kang, courtesy name Xiaju, in youth encountered the Tianbao turmoil and supported his mother in seclusion in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Kang, courtesy name Xiaju, in youth encountered the Tianbao turmoil and supported his mother in seclusion in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 壽州刺史張鎰辟署幕府。
entries.en: Shou Prefecture prefect Zhang Yi recruited him to his staff.
entries.literal: Shou Prefecture prefect Zhang Yi recruited him to his staff.

entries.zh: 抗吏事閑敏，有文雅，從鎰鎮江西。
entries.en: Kang was quick and adept in office affairs and had literary refinement. He followed Yi to garrison Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Kang was quick and adept in office affairs and had literary refinement; he followed Yi to garrison Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 及以宰相領鳳翔，奏署監察御史。
entries.en: When Yi as chief minister also held Fengxiang he memorialized to appoint Kang investigating censor.
entries.literal: When Yi as chief minister also held Fengxiang he memorialized to appoint Kang investigating censor.

entries.zh: 李楚琳亂，奔奉天，授侍御史，遷戶部員外郎。
entries.en: When Li Chulin rebelled he fled to Fengtian, was appointed attending censor, and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: When Li Chulin rebelled he fled to Fengtian, was appointed attending censor, and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 蕭復引為江淮宣慰判官。
entries.en: Xiao Fu brought him in as judge on the Jiang-Huai pacification commission.
entries.literal: Xiao Fu brought him in as judge on the Jiang-Huai pacification commission.

entries.zh: 德宗自梁、洋還，財用大屈，鹽鐵使元琇薦抗材，改倉部郎中，斡鹽利。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong returned from Liang and Yang finances were greatly strained, Salt and Iron Commissioner Yuan Xiu recommended Kang's talent. He was made director in the Granary Section and managed salt profits.
entries.literal: When Dezong returned from Liang and Yang finances were greatly strained, Salt and Iron Commissioner Yuan Xiu recommended Kang's talent; he was changed to director in the Granary Section and managed salt profits.

entries.zh: 俄為水陸運副使，護漕江淮，給京師。
entries.en: Soon he became deputy commissioner for water and land transport, supervised grain transport on the Jiang and Huai, and supplied the capital.
entries.literal: Soon he became deputy commissioner for water and land transport, supervised grain transport on the Jiang and Huai, and supplied the capital.

entries.zh: 歷諫議大夫，坐小累，為處州刺史。
entries.en: He served as grand remonstrator. For a minor offense he became prefect of Chu Prefecture.
entries.literal: He served as grand remonstrator; for a minor offense he became prefect of Chu.

entries.zh: 歷蘇州，徙潭州觀察使，召為給事中，遷河南尹，進太常卿，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: He served in Su Prefecture, was moved to investigating commissioner of Tan Prefecture, was summoned as palace attendant, transferred to intendant of Henan, advanced to chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as vice minister of the Secretariat became co-equal with the chief ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: He served in Su Prefecture, was moved to investigating commissioner of Tan Prefecture, was summoned as attendant within the palace gates, transferred to intendant of Henan, advanced to chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as vice minister of the Secretariat became co-equal with the chief ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: ◎蘇尹畢李鄭王許潘倪席齊蘇向，雍州藍田人。
entries.en: In the biographies of Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, and Qi, Su Xiang came from Lantian in Yong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, and Qi: Su Xiang was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 中明經第，調鄠尉。
entries.en: He passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as aide at Hu County.
entries.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination and was appointed aide at Hu.

entries.zh: 時李義琰為雍州長史，鄠多訟，日至長史府，恦裁決明辦，自是無訴者。
entries.en: Li Yiyan was then chief secretary of Yong Prefecture. Hu County was rife with lawsuits, and people came every day to the chief secretary's office. Xiang's rulings were lucid and decisive, and after that there were no more complainants.
entries.literal: At that time Li Yiyan was chief secretary of Yong Prefecture; Hu had many lawsuits, and people came daily to the chief secretary's office — Xiang's judgments were clear and decisive, and from then on there were no litigants.

entries.zh: 義琰異之，顧聽事曰：「此公坐也，恨吾齒晚，不及見。」
entries.en: Yiyan was struck by his ability. Glancing toward the reception hall, he said, "That is this gentleman's seat — I only wish I had not grown old so soon and could have known him earlier."
entries.literal: Yiyan marveled at him, glanced toward the hall and said, "This is the gentleman's seat; I regret my years came late and I could not meet him sooner."

entries.zh: 武在蜀頗放肆，用度無藝，或一言之悅，賞至百萬。
entries.en: In Shu, Wu was quite unrestrained. His spending knew no bounds, and sometimes a single pleasing remark would earn a reward of as much as a million cash.
entries.literal: Wu in Shu was quite unrestrained; his expenditures knew no limit, and sometimes for a single pleasing remark he would reward as much as a million.

entries.zh: 蜀雖號富饒，而峻掊亟斂，閭裏為空，然虜亦不敢近境。
entries.en: Although Shu was known as rich and fertile, he taxed it harshly and relentlessly until whole neighborhoods were drained empty. Even so, the enemy did not dare approach the border.
entries.literal: Although Shu was called rich and fertile, he harshly scraped and urgently levied taxes until neighborhoods were emptied; yet the barbarians also did not dare approach the border.

entries.zh: 梓州刺史章彜始為武判官，因小忿殺之。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, had once served as Wu's aide. Over a minor quarrel Wu had him killed.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, Prefect of Zizhou, had first served as Wu's judge; over a small grievance Wu killed him.

entries.zh: 琯以故宰相為巡內刺史，武慢倨不為禮。
entries.en: Fang Guan, a former chancellor, came as an itinerant inspector within the circuit, but Wu treated him with arrogant disrespect.
entries.literal: Fang Guan, as a former chancellor, served as an itinerant inspector within the circuit; Wu was arrogant and did not show him courtesy.

entries.zh: 最厚杜甫，然欲殺甫數矣。
entries.en: He was closest to Du Fu, yet more than once he wanted to kill him.
entries.literal: He was closest to Du Fu, yet several times he wanted to kill Fu.

entries.zh: 李白為《蜀道難》者，乃為房與杜危之也。
entries.en: Li Bai wrote "Hard Road to Shu" to warn Fang Guan and Du Fu of the danger they faced.
entries.literal: That Li Bai wrote "Hard Road to Shu" was to warn Fang and Du of danger.

entries.zh: 永泰初卒，母哭，且曰：「而今而後，吾知免為官婢矣。」
entries.en: He died at the beginning of the Yongtai era. His mother wept and said, "From now on I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant."
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he died. His mother wept and said: "From now on, I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant."

entries.zh: 年四十，贈尚書左僕射。
entries.en: He was forty years old. He was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was forty years old; posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 裴崔盧李王嚴
entries.en: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, and Yan
entries.literal: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan

entries.zh: 曜，性沉靜，資貌瑰傑。
entries.en: Yao was sedate by nature, with a splendid and commanding presence.
entries.literal: Yao — nature sedate and quiet, endowment and appearance splendid and outstanding.

entries.zh: 累從節度府辟署，破虜有功，為開陽府果毅都尉。
entries.en: He was repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs, won merit defeating the enemy, and was made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.
entries.literal: Repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs; defeated barbarians with merit; made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.

entries.zh: 至德初，推子儀功，授衛尉卿，累進太子詹事、太原郡公。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhide era (756), in recognition of Guo Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia and was later promoted to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, in recognition of Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia; promoted in succession to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 子儀專征伐，曜留治家事，少長無閑言。
entries.en: While Guo Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns, Yao remained at home to manage the household — and among the family, young and old alike, there was no gossip.
entries.literal: Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns; Yao remained to manage household affairs — among young and old, no idle talk.

entries.zh: 諸弟或飾池館，盛車服，曜獨以朴簡自處。
entries.en: Some of his brothers ornamented their pools and halls and went about in lavish carriages and robes. Yao alone lived plainly.
entries.literal: Some of his brothers ornamented pools and halls, lavish in carriages and robes; Yao alone lived in plain simplicity.

entries.zh: 子儀罷兵，遷太子少保，昆弟六人，共制拜官。
entries.en: When Guo Ziyi laid down his arms, Yao was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. The six brothers jointly regulated official appointments within the family.
entries.literal: When Ziyi laid down arms, Yao was transferred to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; six brothers jointly regulated official appointments.

entries.zh: 子儀薨，以遺命簿上四朝所賜名馬珍物，德宗復賜之，乃悉散諸弟。
entries.en: When Guo Ziyi died, his will listed the famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns. Emperor Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed everything among his brothers.
entries.literal: When Ziyi passed away, per his will the register listed famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns; Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed all to his brothers.

entries.zh: 居喪以禮，疾甚，或勸茹蔥薤，終不屬口。
entries.en: He observed mourning rites properly. When he grew very ill, some urged him to eat leeks and chives, but he never let them touch his lips.
entries.literal: He observed mourning according to rites; very ill, some urged leeks and chives — he never let them touch his lips.

entries.zh: 後盧杞秉政，忌勳族，子儀婿太僕卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰皆以次得罪。
entries.en: Later, when Lu Qi held power, he was jealous of meritorious clans. Guo Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished one after another.
entries.literal: Later Lu Qi held power, jealous of meritorious clans; Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished in turn.

entries.zh: 奸人幸其危，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜大恐，獨宰相張鎰力保護。
entries.en: Villains preyed on the family's peril and seized many estates and slaves. Yao was greatly afraid, and only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.
entries.literal: Villains preyed on their peril and seized many estates and slaves; Yao was greatly afraid — only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.

entries.zh: 德宗稍聞之，詔有司曰：「尚父子儀有大勳力，保乂王家，嘗誓山河，琢金石，許宥十世。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong gradually learned of this, he issued an edict to the offices: "Imperial Father Guo Ziyi rendered great service and preserved the imperial house. An oath sworn on mountains and rivers and carved in metal and stone granted his line exemption for ten generations.
entries.literal: Dezong gradually heard of it and issued an edict the offices, saying, "Imperial Father Ziyi had great merit, preserved and governed the royal house, once sworn on mountains and rivers, carved in metal and stone, granted exemption for ten generations.

entries.zh: 前日其家市田宅奴婢，而無賴者以尚父歿，妄論奪之，自今有司毋得受。」
entries.en: Recently his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them. From now on the offices shall not accept such claims."
entries.literal: The other day his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing the Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them — from now on the offices shall not accept such claims."

entries.zh: 建中三年，卒，贈太子太傅，諡曰孝。
entries.en: In the third year of the Jianzhong era (782) he died. He was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and granted the posthumous name Xiao.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died; posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; posthumous name Xiao.

entries.zh: 初，曜襲代國公，食二千戶。
entries.en: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 貞元初，詔減半以封晞、曖、映、曙，人二百五十戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era (785), an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu with two hundred fifty households each.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu — two hundred fifty households each.

entries.zh: 未幾，復詔四人各減五十戶，封曜子鋒、晤子鐇各百戶雲。
entries.en: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.
entries.literal: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.

entries.zh: 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟幼:明 幼明子:昕
entries.en: Guo Ziyi's sons included Yao and Xi; Xi's grandson was Chenggu. He also had a son named Ai, whose sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian, and whose grandson was Shu. His younger brother by the same mother was Youming, and Youming's son was Xin.
entries.literal: Guo Ziyi — sons: Yao; son: Xi; Xi's grandson: Chenggu; son: Ai; Ai's sons: Zhao, Cong, and Xian; Ai's grandson: Shu; uterine younger brother You: Ming; Youming's son: Xin.

entries.zh: 抱真喜士，聞世賢者，必欲與之遊，雖小善，皆卑禮厚幣數千里邀致之，至無可錄，徐徐以禮謝。
entries.en: Baozhen delighted in scholars and sought out the worthy wherever he heard of them, sending humble invitations and rich gifts across thousands of li even for modest talents. When a guest proved unworthy, he dismissed him with courtesy.
entries.literal: Baozhen delighted in scholars; hearing of worthy men of the age, he always wished to associate with them; even for small merits he used humble rites and rich gifts to invite them from thousands of li; when there was nothing worth recording, he slowly dismissed them with courtesy.

entries.zh: 會天下稍無事，乃飾台沼以自娛。
entries.en: As the realm grew quieter, he adorned terraces and ponds for his own pleasure.
entries.literal: When the empire was somewhat without affairs, he then adorned terraces and ponds for his own pleasure.

entries.zh: 好方士，謂不死可致。
entries.en: He favored Daoist adepts and believed immortality could be attained.
entries.literal: He favored alchemical masters and held that immortality could be attained.

entries.zh: 有孫季長者為治丹，且曰：「服此當仙去。」
entries.en: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixirs for him, saying, "Take this and you will ascend as an immortal."
entries.literal: There was one Sun Jichang who prepared elixir for him and said: "If you take this you ought to ascend as an immortal."

entries.zh: 抱真表署幕府。
entries.en: Baozhen had him appointed to his staff.
entries.literal: Baozhen memorialized to appoint him to the staff.

entries.zh: 嘗語左右曰：「秦、漢君不偶此，我乃得之，後升天，不復見公等矣。」
entries.en: He told his attendants, "The emperors of Qin and Han never had this opportunity—I have found it. When I ascend to heaven I shall not see you again."
entries.literal: He once told those at his side: "The rulers of Qin and Han did not chance upon this; I have obtained it; afterward I shall ascend to Heaven and will not see you gentlemen again."

entries.zh: 夜夢駕鶴，寤而刻寓鶴，衣羽服，習乘之。
entries.en: He dreamed one night of riding a crane; on waking he had a crane carved in relief, donned feather robes, and practiced mounting it.
entries.literal: At night he dreamed of riding a crane; waking, he carved a crane in relief, wore feather robes, and practiced riding it.

entries.zh: 後益惑厭勝，因疾，請降官，七讓司空，還為左僕射。
entries.en: He grew ever more absorbed in sorcery and talismans. When illness struck he asked to be reduced in rank, declining the Ministry of Works seven times until he was left as Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Later he was increasingly deluded by sorcery and talismans; because of illness he requested reduction of rank; seven times he declined the Ministry of Works and returned to Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 餌丹二萬丸，不能食，且死，醫以彘肪穀漆下之。
entries.en: He swallowed twenty thousand elixir pills, could no longer eat, and was near death. Physicians purged him with pig fat and lacquer.
entries.literal: He ingested twenty thousand pills of elixir, could not eat, and was near death; physicians used pig fat and lacquer to purge him downward.

entries.zh: 疾少間，季長曰：「危得仙，何自棄也？」
entries.en: When he briefly improved, Jichang said, "You were on the verge of immortality—why throw that away?"
entries.literal: When his illness eased slightly, Jichang said: "You were on the verge of becoming an immortal—why abandon it yourself?"

entries.zh: 益服三千丸，卒，年六十二。
entries.en: He took three thousand more pills and died at sixty-two.
entries.literal: He took three thousand more pills and died, aged sixty-two.

entries.zh: 抱真子 緘其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪，與其屬盧會昌元仲經謀，會諸將，仲經詭抱真令曰：「吾疾不任事，令緘典軍，勉佐之。」
entries.en: Baozhen's son Jian, a Palace Attendant Censor, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."
entries.literal: Baozhen's son: Jian. His son, Palace Attendant Jian, concealed the death; with his subordinate Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he plotted; they assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged Baozhen's order, saying: "My illness prevents me from managing affairs; I order Jian to command the army—strive to assist him."

entries.zh: 副使李說及諸校俯首，皆嘸曰；
entries.en: Deputy Commissioner Li Shuo and the commanders bowed their heads and murmured assent;
entries.literal: Deputy Commissioner Li Shuo and the various commanders bowed their heads; all murmured assent;

entries.en: "Agreed."
entries.literal: "Agreed."

entries.zh: 緘盛服出，眾拜之，悉發府庫勞軍。
entries.en: Jian appeared in full regalia; the officers bowed to him and the treasury was opened to reward the troops.
entries.literal: Jian came out in full dress; the masses bowed to him; the entire treasury was opened to reward the army.

entries.zh: 會昌即為抱真表，翌日，令諸將署章，請以節付緘。
entries.en: Huichang immediately sent a memorial in Baozhen's name; the next day he had the generals sign a petition asking that command be given to Jian.
entries.literal: Huichang immediately memorialized for Baozhen; the next day he had the generals sign a petition asking that the command be given to Jian.

entries.zh: 天子已聞抱真喪，遣使者馳入軍，詔以事屬大將王延貴。
entries.en: The emperor had already learned of Baozhen's death and sent an envoy racing to the army, ordering that command pass to the senior general Wang Yangui.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven had already heard of Baozhen's death and sent an envoy galloping into the army, ordering that affairs be entrusted to the great general Wang Yangui.

entries.zh: 緘謾若抱真疾，請詰朝見，凡三日，緘乃出見使者，陳兵甚嚴。
entries.en: Jian pretended Baozhen was merely ill and asked to receive the envoy the next morning. For three days he delayed; when he finally appeared before the envoy, his troops were drawn up in strict array.
entries.literal: Jian pretended as if Baozhen were ill and requested to see [the envoy] the next morning; for three days in all; only then did Jian come out to see the envoy, arraying troops very strictly.

entries.zh: 使者曰：「朝廷已知公薨，詔以兵屬延貴，君速歸發喪。」
entries.en: The envoy said, "The court already knows your father is dead. Command passes to Yangui by edict. Return at once and begin the mourning."
entries.literal: The envoy said: "The court already knows the lord has died; an edict places the troops under Yangui; sir, quickly return and begin the mourning."

entries.zh: 緘愕然，謂諸將曰：「詔不許，若何？」
entries.en: Jian was stunned. He asked the generals, "The edict forbids it—what now?"
entries.literal: Jian was startled and said to the generals: "The edict does not permit it—what then?"

entries.zh: 眾不對。
entries.en: No one answered.
entries.literal: The crowd did not answer.

entries.zh: 乃遽以印鑰上監軍，始發喪。
entries.en: He hastily surrendered the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then began the mourning rites.
entries.literal: He then hastily turned over the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then began the mourning.

entries.zh: 使者趣延貴視事，護緘赴東都，仲經逃諸外，捕殺之，會昌得不坐。
entries.en: The envoy pressed Yangui to take command and escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital. Zhongjing fled and was hunted down and killed; Huichang escaped punishment.
entries.literal: The envoy urged Yangui to take up affairs, escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital; Zhongjing fled abroad and was captured and killed; Huichang was not punished.

entries.zh: 始，緘遣將陳榮以書抵武俊，假其財。
entries.en: Earlier Jian had sent the general Chen Rong to Wang Wujun with a letter asking to borrow funds.
entries.literal: Earlier, Jian had sent the general Chen Rong with a letter to Wujun to borrow his funds.

entries.zh: 武俊怒曰；
entries.en: Wujun said in anger,
entries.literal: Wujun said in anger:

entries.zh: 「吾與乃公善者，恭王命，非同惡也。
entries.en: "I was your father's friend out of loyalty to the throne, not as a fellow rebel.
entries.literal: "I was on good terms with your father out of respect for the royal command, not as fellow evildoers.

entries.zh: 今聞已亡，誰詐其子使不俟朝制邪？」
entries.en: Now I hear he is dead—who has deceived his son into defying the court's orders?"
entries.literal: Now I hear he is already dead—who has deceived his son into not awaiting court regulations?"

entries.zh: 囚榮而讓緘焉。
entries.en: He imprisoned Chen Rong and rebuked Jian.
entries.literal: He imprisoned Rong and reproached Jian for it.

entries.zh: 詔贈抱真太保。
entries.en: An edict posthumously made Baozhen Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made Baozhen Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 路嗣恭，字懿範，京兆三原人，始名劍客，以世廕為鄴尉。
entries.en: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Originally named Jianke, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
entries.literal: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jianke; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.

entries.zh: 席豫黜陟河朔，表為蕭關令，連徙神烏、姑臧二縣，考績為天下最。
entries.en: When Xi Yu reformed official appointments in Hebei, Sigong was recommended as magistrate of Xiaoguan, then served in succession at Shenwu and Guzang; his performance reviews ranked first in the empire.
entries.literal: Xi Yu promoted and demoted officials in Hebei; [Sigong] was recommended as Magistrate of Xiaoguan, then transferred in succession to the two counties of Shenwu and Guzang; his examination record ranked highest in the empire.

entries.zh: 玄宗以為可嗣漢魯恭，因賜名。
entries.en: Xuanzong judged him a worthy successor to the virtuous Han magistrate Lu Gong and granted him the name Sigong.
entries.literal: Xuanzong deemed him able to succeed Han's Lu Gong, and therefore granted him the name [Sigong].

entries.zh: 轉渭南令，主杜化、東陽二驛。
entries.en: He was transferred to magistrate of Weinan, overseeing the Duhua and Dongyang post stations.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Weinan, in charge of the two post stations of Duhua and Dongyang.

entries.zh: 時關畿用兵，使人系道，嗣恭儲具有素，而民不擾。
entries.en: With war raging in the capital region and couriers choking the roads, Sigong had long laid up supplies, and the people were not disturbed.
entries.literal: At that time the Guan region was at war; envoys filled the roads; Sigong had long stored supplies, and the people were not disturbed.

entries.zh: 後為郭子儀朔方節度留後，大將孫守亮擁重兵，驕蹇不受制，嗣恭因稱疾，守亮至，即殺之，一軍皆震。
entries.en: Later, as acting commissioner under Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command, he faced the arrogant general Sun Shouliang, who held a large force and refused obedience. Sigong feigned illness; when Shouliang came to call, he had him killed at once, and the whole army was shaken.
entries.literal: Later he was Acting Military Commissioner of Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command; the great general Sun Shouliang held heavy troops, was arrogant and obstinate and would not accept control; Sigong therefore feigned illness; when Shouliang came, he was immediately killed, and the whole army was shaken.

entries.zh: 永泰三年，檢校刑部尚書，知省事。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongtai he was made Acting Minister of Justice with charge of court affairs.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongtai he was made Acting Minister of Justice and managed court affairs.

entries.zh: 出為江西觀察使，以善治財賦稱。
entries.en: He was sent out as observation commissioner of Jiangxi and won renown for skill in managing revenue.
entries.literal: He went out as Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi and was famed for skill in managing finances and taxes.

entries.zh: 有賈明觀者，素事魚朝恩，朝恩誅，當坐死，宰相元載納其賂，遣效力江西，將行，居民數萬懷瓦石候擊，載諭市吏禁止，乃得去。
entries.en: Jia Mingguan had long served the eunuch Yu Chaoen. When Chaoen was executed Jia deserved death, but Chancellor Yuan Zai took his bribe and sent him to serve in Jiangxi. As he was about to leave, tens of thousands of townspeople gathered with stones to kill him; only when Zai ordered the market officers to restrain them could he depart.
entries.literal: There was one Jia Mingguan who had long served Yu Chaoen; when Chaoen was executed he ought to have been put to death; Chancellor Yuan Zai accepted his bribe and sent him to serve in Jiangxi; as he was about to depart, tens of thousands of residents carried tiles and stones waiting to strike him; Zai ordered market officers to forbid it, and only then could he leave.

entries.zh: 魏少游畏載，常回容之，及嗣恭代少遊，即日杖死。
entries.en: Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
entries.literal: Wei Shaoyou feared Zai and constantly indulged him; when Sigong replaced Shaoyou, that same day he had him beaten to death.

entries.zh: 大曆八年，嶺南將哥舒晃殺節度使呂崇賁，五嶺大擾。
