entries.en: In the eighth year of Dali the Lingnan general Geshu Huang killed Military Commissioner Lü Chongbin, throwing the Five Ridges into turmoil.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Dali the Lingnan general Geshu Huang killed Military Commissioner Lü Chongbin, and the Five Ridges were greatly disturbed.

entries.zh: 詔嗣恭兼嶺南節度使，封冀國公。
entries.en: Sigong was ordered to take concurrent command of Lingnan and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
entries.literal: An edict made Sigong concurrently Military Commissioner of Lingnan and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ji.

entries.zh: 嗣恭募勇敢士八千人，以流人孟瑤、敬冕為才，擢任之。
entries.en: Sigong recruited eight thousand brave men and, recognizing talent in the exiles Meng Yao and Jing Mian, promoted them to command.
entries.literal: Sigong recruited eight thousand brave men; he deemed the exiles Meng Yao and Jing Mian talented and promoted them to office.

entries.zh: 使瑤督大軍當其沖，冕率輕兵由間道出不意，遂斬晃及支党萬餘，築屍為京觀。
entries.en: Yao led the main force against the enemy front while Mian took light troops by a hidden route to strike from behind. They beheaded Huang and more than ten thousand of his followers and built a mound of their corpses.
entries.literal: He had Yao command the great army to meet the enemy head-on; Mian led light troops by a hidden path to strike unexpectedly; they then beheaded Huang and more than ten thousand of his followers and built the corpses into a victory mound.

entries.zh: 俚洞魁宿為惡者，皆族夷之。
entries.en: The Li cave chiefs and elders who had done evil were exterminated to the last of their clans.
entries.literal: The chieftains and elders of the Li caves who had done evil were all exterminated to the clan.

entries.zh: 還為檢校兵部尚書，復知省事。
entries.en: He returned as Acting Minister of War and again managed court affairs.
entries.literal: He returned as Acting Minister of War and again managed court affairs.

entries.zh: 嗣恭起州縣吏，以課治進至顯官，及晃事株戮舶商，沒其財數百萬私有之，代宗惡焉，故賞不酬功。
entries.en: Sigong had risen from a county clerk through merit in governance to high office. In the Huang affair he executed merchant sailors wholesale and seized millions in private wealth. Daizong despised this, and Sigong's rewards never matched his achievements.
entries.literal: Sigong rose from a county and district clerk, advanced through examination of governance to eminent office; in the Huang affair he executed merchant sailors root and branch, confiscated their wealth of several million and kept it privately; Daizong detested this, and therefore rewards did not match his merit.

entries.zh: 德宗立，陰賕宰相楊炎，炎錄前效，更拜兵部尚書、東都留守。
entries.en: When Dezong succeeded, Sigong secretly bribed Chancellor Yang Yan, who cited his past service and reappointed him Minister of War and resident of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: When Dezong took the throne, [Sigong] secretly bribed Chancellor Yang Yan; Yan recorded his past merit and again appointed him Minister of War and Resident of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 俄加懷鄭汝陝河陽三城節度、東都畿觀察使。
entries.en: Soon after he was also made military commissioner of the Three Cities circuit and observation commissioner of the Eastern Capital metropolitan region.
entries.literal: Shortly he was given the additional posts of Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Huai, Zheng, Ru, Shan, and Heyang, and Observation Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Metropolitan Circuit.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈左僕射。
entries.en: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: He died, aged seventy-one; posthumously made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 子應、恕。
entries.en: His sons were Ying and Shu.
entries.literal: Sons: Ying and Shu.

entries.zh: 子 應應，字從眾，以廕為著作郎。
entries.en: His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a Gentleman Compiler.
entries.literal: Son: Ying. Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, through privilege entered office as Drafting Secretary.

entries.zh: 貞元初，出為虔州刺史，詔嗣父封。
entries.en: Early in the Zhenyuan era he was made prefect of Qianzhou and ordered to inherit his father's title.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he went out as Prefect of Qianzhou; an edict ordered him to inherit his father's enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 鑿贛石梗嶮以通舟道。
entries.en: He cut through the obstructing crags at Gan Rock to open the river route to navigation.
entries.literal: He cut through the obstructing crags of Gan Rock to open the water route for boats.

entries.zh: 德宗時，李泌為相，號得君。
entries.en: Under Dezong, Li Bi served as chancellor and was known as a favorite of the emperor.
entries.literal: In Dezong's time Li Bi was chancellor and was called one who had won the ruler.

entries.zh: 帝嘗曰：「誰於卿有恩者，朕能報之。」
entries.en: The emperor once said, "Tell me who has been kind to you, and I will repay them."
entries.literal: The emperor once said: "Whoever has shown you kindness, I can repay them."

entries.zh: 泌乃言：「曩為元載所疾，謫江西，路嗣恭與載厚，臣嘗畏之。
entries.en: Bi replied, "Long ago Yuan Zai hated me and had me demoted to Jiangxi. Lu Sigong was close to Zai, and I feared him.
entries.literal: Bi then said: "Formerly I was hated by Yuan Zai and was demoted to Jiangxi; Lu Sigong was close to Zai, and I once feared him.

entries.zh: 會與其子應並驅，馬齧其脛，臣惶恐不自安，應閟不言，勉起見父。
entries.en: Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and forced himself up to see his father.
entries.literal: It happened that I rode side by side with his son Ying; a horse bit my shin; I was fearful and ill at ease; Ying kept it secret and did not speak, then with effort rose to see his father.

entries.zh: 臣常愧其長者，思有以報。」
entries.en: I have long felt ashamed before his forbearance and wished to repay it."
entries.literal: I have often been ashamed before his magnanimity and wished to repay it."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「善。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Good."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Good."

entries.zh: 即日加應檢校屯田郎中，服金紫。
entries.en: That same day Ying was made Acting Director of the Bureau of State Farms and granted the gold-and-purple insignia of rank.
entries.literal: That same day Ying was given the additional post of Acting Director of the Bureau of State Farms and wore gold and purple.

entries.zh: 累遷宣歙池觀察使，封襄陽郡王。
entries.en: He rose to observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi and was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi and enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 李錡反，應發鄉兵救湖、常二州，以故錡不能拔。
entries.en: When Li Qi rebelled, Ying sent local militia to relieve Hu and Chang prefectures, preventing Qi from capturing them.
entries.literal: When Li Qi rebelled, Ying sent local militia to rescue the two prefectures of Hu and Chang; because of this Qi could not take them.

entries.zh: 元和六年，以疾授左散騎常侍，卒，諡曰靖。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, ill health led to his appointment as Left Regular Cavalier; he died and was given the posthumous name Tranquil.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, because of illness he was made Left Regular Cavalier; he died; posthumous title Tranquil.

entries.zh: 子 恕恕，字體仁。
entries.en: His son Shu, courtesy name Tiren.
entries.literal: Son: Shu. Shu, courtesy name Tiren.

entries.zh: 從嗣恭討哥舒晃，授檢校工部員外郎，得從便宜，擢降將伊慎用之。
entries.en: Serving under Sigong against Geshu Huang, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Works with discretionary authority and promoted the surrendered general Yi Shen to command.
entries.literal: Following Sigong in the campaign against Geshu Huang, he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Works with discretion to act as needed; he promoted the surrendered general Yi Shen and employed him.

entries.zh: 賊平，恕功多。
entries.en: When the rebellion was suppressed, Shu had earned great merit.
entries.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Shu's merit was great.

entries.zh: 嗣恭節度河陽也，恕為懷州刺史，年才三十，楊炎用捍魏博，為時嗤詆。
entries.en: When Sigong held Heyang, Shu was made prefect of Huaizhou at only thirty. Yang Yan used him to block Weibo—a appointment widely mocked.
entries.literal: When Sigong was military commissioner of Heyang, Shu was Prefect of Huaizhou, only thirty years old; Yang Yan used him to block Weibo; contemporaries mocked and reviled this.

entries.zh: 累遷鄜坊、宣歙觀察使。
entries.en: He later served as observation commissioner of Fu-Fang and of Xuan-She.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Bin and Fang, and of Xuan and She.

entries.zh: 坐事貶吉州刺史。
entries.en: For an offense he was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.
entries.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Prefect of Jizhou.

entries.zh: 以右散騎常侍致仕，卒，贈洪州都督。
entries.en: He retired as Right Regular Cavalier, died, and was posthumously made governor of Hongzhou.
entries.literal: As Right Regular Cavalier he retired from office; he died; posthumously made Governor of Hongzhou.

entries.zh: 李嗣業，字嗣業，京兆高陵人。
entries.en: Li Siye, whose courtesy name was also Siye, came from Gaoling in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Li Siye was his name, courtesy name Siye, a native of Gaoling in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 長七尺，膂力絕眾。
entries.en: He stood seven feet tall, with strength of arm unmatched among his peers.
entries.literal: He was seven chi in height, and his arm strength surpassed the multitude.

entries.zh: 開元中，從安西都護來曜討十姓蘇祿，先登捕虜，累功署昭武校尉。
entries.en: During the Kaiyuan period he served under Anxi Protector-General Lai Yao against Suluk of the Ten Surnames, scaling the heights first and taking captives; for repeated merit he was made a Defender of Zhaowu.
entries.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he followed the Protector-General of Anxi, Lai Yao, to campaign against Suluk of the Ten Surnames; he was first to scale [the heights], captured prisoners, and for accumulated merit was appointed Defender of Zhaowu.

entries.zh: 後應募安西，軍中初用陌刀，而嗣業尤善，每戰必為先鋒，所向摧北。
entries.en: He later enlisted in the Anxi forces when the mo dao was first introduced to the troops; Siye excelled with it above all, invariably leading the van in battle and breaking the enemy wherever he charged.
entries.literal: Later he enrolled in the Anxi army; the army had newly adopted the mo blade, and Siye was especially skilled; in every battle he was made vanguard, and wherever he went the enemy was crushed.

entries.zh: 馬靈察為節度，出戰必與俱。
entries.en: Under Military Commissioner Ma Lingcha, he always accompanied him on campaign.
entries.literal: When Ma Lingcha became military commissioner, whenever he went out to fight Siye went with him.

entries.zh: 高仙芝討勃律，署嗣業及中郎將田珍為左右陌刀將。
entries.en: During Gao Xianzhi's expedition against Balur, Siye and Central Regiment Director Tian Zhen were appointed commanders of the left and right mo-blade units.
entries.literal: When Gao Xianzhi campaigned against Balur, he appointed Siye and the Central Regiment Director Tian Zhen as left and right mo-blade commanders.

entries.zh: 時吐蕃兵十萬屯娑勒城，據山瀕水，聯木作郛，以扼王師。
entries.en: A Tibetan force of one hundred thousand held Suole Fort on the heights above the water, their linked timber walls blocking the imperial advance.
entries.literal: At that time a hundred thousand Tibetan troops were encamped at Suole Fort, holding the mountains and bordering the water, linking timbers to make a palisade to block the royal army.

entries.zh: 仙芝潛軍夜濟信圖河，令曰：「及午破賊，不者皆死。」
entries.en: Xianzhi stole across the Xintu River at night with his army, declaring: "Break the enemy by noon, or every man dies."
entries.literal: Xianzhi secretly led troops by night to cross the Xintu River, ordering: "By noon break the bandits, or all shall die."

entries.zh: 嗣業提步士升山，頹石四面以擊賊，又樹大旗先走險，諸將從之。
entries.en: Siye led infantry up the slope, hurling stones down on the enemy from all sides; planting his standard first over the difficult ground, the other commanders followed.
entries.literal: Siye led foot soldiers up the mountain, rolling stones down on all sides to strike the bandits; he also planted a great banner and first took the dangerous route, and the generals followed him.

entries.zh: 虜不虞軍至，因大潰，投崖谷死者十八。
entries.en: The barbarians, caught unawares, broke and fled; as much as eight in ten of those who tumbled into gullies and ravines perished.
entries.literal: The barbarians did not expect the army's arrival and so were greatly routed; eighteen-tenths of those who plunged off cliffs and into ravines died.

entries.zh: 鼓而驅至勃律，禽其主，平之。
entries.en: They beat the drums and pressed on to Balur, seized its ruler, and brought the region under control.
entries.literal: Drumming the advance they drove to Balur, captured its lord, and pacified it.

entries.zh: 授右威衛將軍。
entries.en: He was made a general of the Right Majestic Guard.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Majestic Guard.

entries.zh: 從平石國及突騎施，以跳蕩先鋒加特進。
entries.en: Serving in the subjugation of the Stone Kingdom and the Turgesh, he earned especial advancement as spearhead of the shock troops.
entries.literal: He followed in the pacification of the Stone Kingdom and the Turgesh, and as vanguard in swift assault was granted especial advancement.

entries.zh: 虜號為「神通大將」。
entries.en: The enemy styled him the "Great General of Supernatural Might."
entries.literal: The barbarians called him the "Great General of Divine Power."

entries.zh: 俄與韋見素、崔渙奉冊靈武，見肅宗，具言上皇所以傳付意，因道當時利病，箝索虜情，辭吐華暢，帝為改容。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he went with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan to Lingwu to present the imperial register to Suzong, explained Xuanzong's purpose in abdicating, analyzed current strengths and weaknesses, and laid out the rebels' position in flowing, eloquent speech that made the emperor sit up.
entries.literal: Soon with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan he bore the registers to Lingwu, met Emperor Suzong, fully explained the Retired Emperor's intent in the transmission, and thereupon set forth the advantages and harms of the time, enumerating the enemy's situation; his words flowed with brilliance and ease, and the emperor changed expression.

entries.zh: 琯既有重名。
entries.en: Guan already enjoyed great fame.
entries.literal: Guan already had a great reputation.

entries.zh: 帝傾意待之，機務一二與琯參決，諸將相莫敢望。
entries.en: The emperor leaned on him wholeheartedly, consulted him on crucial affairs, and none of the other generals or ministers could rival his standing.
entries.literal: The emperor poured out his favor on him; one or two matters of state he decided together with Guan; none of the generals or chancellors dared compare.

entries.zh: 於是，第五琦言財利幸，為江淮租庸使。
entries.en: At this point Diwu Qi, who traded on expertise in finance, won favor and was made commissioner for Jiang-Huai tax and corvée.
entries.literal: Thereupon Diwu Qi, speaking of finance and profit, won favor and became Jiang-Huai commissioner for tax and corvée.

entries.zh: 琯諫曰：「往楊國忠聚斂，產怨天下。
entries.en: Guan remonstrated: "Under Yang Guozhong the court squeezed revenue until the empire seethed with resentment.
entries.literal: Guan remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Yang Guozhong amassed exactions and produced resentment throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 陛下即位，人未見德，今又寵琦，是一國忠死，一國忠生，無以示遠方。」
entries.en: You have just taken the throne and the people have yet to see benevolent rule; if you favor Qi now, it will look as though one Guozhong has died only for another to rise—how can that reassure the provinces?"
entries.literal: Your Majesty has ascended the throne but the people have not yet seen virtue; now You again favor Qi—it is one Guozhong dead and another Guozhong born, with no way to show the distant regions."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「六軍之命方急，無財則散。
entries.en: The emperor replied: "The armies' survival hangs in the balance; without money they will scatter.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Armies' fate is urgently at stake; without funds they will disperse.

entries.zh: 卿惡琦可也，何所取財？」
entries.en: You may dislike Qi as you please, but where else will the funds come from?"
entries.literal: You may hate Qi, but where will wealth be taken from?"

entries.zh: 琯不得對。
entries.en: Guan had no answer.
entries.literal: Guan could not reply.

entries.zh: 北海太守賀蘭進明自河南至，詔攝御史大夫、嶺南節度使，入謝，帝曰：「朕語琯除正大夫，何為攝邪？」
entries.en: Helan Jinming, prefect of Beihai, arrived from Henan and was ordered to serve as acting censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Lingnan. When he came to give thanks, the emperor said, "I told Guan to appoint you full censor-in-chief—why 'acting'?"
entries.literal: Beihai prefect Helan Jinming came from Henan; he was ordered as acting censor-in-chief and Lingnan military commissioner; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "We told Guan to appoint you full grand master—why 'acting'?"

entries.zh: 進明銜之，因曰：「陛下知晉亂乎？
entries.en: Jinming took offense and said, "Does Your Majesty know how the Jin dynasty was ruined?
entries.literal: Jinming bore a grudge over this and thereupon said: "Does Your Majesty know how Jin fell into disorder?

entries.zh: 惟以尚虛名，任王衍為宰相，基祖浮華，不事天下事，故至於敗。
entries.en: They prized empty reputation, put Wang Yan in the chancellery, and built policy on showy refinement while neglecting the realm—until the state collapsed.
entries.literal: It was solely because they valued empty reputation, employed Wang Yan as chancellor, who founded his lineage in frivolity and ornament and did not attend to the realm's affairs, and therefore came to defeat.

entries.zh: 方唐中興，當用實才，而琯性疏闊，大言無當，非宰相器。
entries.en: Tang is trying to revive itself and needs practical men, but Guan is scatterbrained, full of empty talk, and unfit for the chancellery.
entries.literal: Now as Tang is reviving, solid talent should be employed; yet Guan's nature is broad and loose, his grand words ineffectual—he is not material for chancellor.

entries.zh: 陛下待之厚，然孰肯為陛下用乎？」
entries.en: You treat him generously, but who under him would truly serve you?"
entries.literal: Your Majesty treats him generously, yet who would be willing to serve Your Majesty for his sake?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「何哉？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "How so?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "How so?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「陛下頃為皇太子，太子出曰撫軍，入曰監國，而琯為聖皇建遣諸王為都統節度，乃謂陛下為元子而付以朔方、河東、河北空虛之地，永王、豐王乃統四節度。
entries.en: He replied: "When you were crown prince, a prince leaving court was styled 'military overseer' and returning 'regent of the realm.' Yet Guan, acting for the retired emperor, had the princes made overall commanders and military commissioners: he treated you as eldest son but gave you the depleted territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Princes Yong and Feng held four military commissions between them.
entries.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty was still crown prince, the prince going out was styled 'military governor' and coming in 'regent of the realm,' yet Guan, for the Retired Emperor, devised sending the princes as overall commanders and military commissioners, and thereby treated Your Majesty as eldest son while assigning You the empty territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Prince Yong and Prince Feng commanded four military commissions.

entries.zh: 此於聖皇似忠，于陛下非忠也。
entries.en: That looked loyal to the retired emperor but was not loyal to you.
entries.literal: This toward the Retired Emperor seems loyal, but toward Your Majesty it is not loyal.

entries.zh: 琯意諸子一得天下，身不失恩，又多樹私黨，以副戎權，推此而言，豈肯盡誠于陛下乎？」
entries.en: Guan meant that whichever prince won the throne, he would keep his own favor; he also built private factions to back military power. On that logic, would he ever serve you with whole-hearted loyalty?"
entries.literal: Guan's intent was that whichever son gained the realm, he himself would not lose favor; moreover he planted many private factions to support military power—pursuing this reasoning, how could he be willing to devote full loyalty to Your Majesty?"

entries.zh: 帝入其語，始惡琯。
entries.en: The emperor accepted this account and began to turn against Guan.
entries.literal: The emperor took in his words and began to dislike Guan.

entries.zh: 以進明為御史大夫、河南節度使。
entries.en: Jinming was made censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Henan.
entries.literal: Jinming was appointed censor-in-chief and Henan military commissioner.

entries.zh: 房琯，字次律，河南河南人。
entries.en: Fang Guan, whose courtesy name was Cilü, came from Henan in Henan commandery.
entries.literal: Fang Guan, styled Cilü, was a native of Henan in Henan [commandery].

entries.zh: 父融，武后時，以正諫大夫同鳳閣鸞臺平章事；
entries.en: His father Rong had served under Empress Wu as Remonstrating Grand Master and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace chancellery;
entries.literal: His father Rong, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Remonstrating Grand Master and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace Chancellery;

entries.zh: 神龍元年，貶死高州。
entries.en: In 705 he was banished and died in exile at Gaozhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was demoted and died at Gaozhou.

entries.zh: 琯少好學，風度沈整，以廕補弘文生。
entries.en: Guan had loved scholarship from boyhood, carried himself with grave composure, and entered the Hongwen Academy by hereditary privilege.
entries.literal: Guan in his youth loved learning; his bearing was grave and composed; through yin privilege he was enrolled as a Hongwen student.

entries.zh: 與呂向偕隱陸渾山，十年不諧際人事。
entries.en: He and Lü Xiang withdrew together to Mount Lu Hun and for ten years kept out of public life entirely.
entries.literal: With Lü Xiang he retired together to Mount Lu Hun; for ten years he did not engage with worldly affairs.

entries.zh: 開元中，作《封禪書》，說宰相張說，說奇之，奏為校書郎。
entries.en: During the Kaiyuan era he wrote a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices and showed it to Chancellor Zhang Yue, who was so impressed that he had Guan appointed collating editor.
entries.literal: During Kaiyuan he composed the Fengshan shu, presented it to Chancellor Zhang Yue; Yue marveled at it and memorialized him as collating editor.

entries.zh: 舉任縣令科，授盧氏令。
entries.en: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was made magistrate of Lushi.
entries.literal: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was appointed magistrate of Lushi.

entries.zh: 拜監察御史，坐訊獄非是，貶睦州司戶參軍。
entries.en: Appointed investigating censor, he was later demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou for irregularities in a trial he conducted.
entries.literal: He was appointed investigating censor; for errors in conducting an interrogation he was demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou.

entries.zh: 復為縣，所至上德化，興長利，以治最顯。
entries.en: Restored to county office, he governed wherever he was posted with moral suasion, fostered lasting public benefit, and won renown for outstanding administration.
entries.literal: Again he served as county magistrate; wherever he went he promoted virtue and transformation, developed lasting benefits, and became distinguished for the excellence of his governance.

entries.zh: 苗晉卿，字元輔，潞州壺關人，世以儒素稱。
entries.en: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; his family had long been known for plain Confucian scholarship.
entries.literal: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; his family was renowned for plain Confucian learning.

entries.zh: 擢進士第，調為修武尉，累進吏部郎中、中書舍人，知吏部選事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu, and rose through the posts of director in the Ministry of Personnel and secretariat drafter until he was put in charge of personnel selection.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu, and was successively promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Secretariat Drafter, and put in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry.

entries.zh: 選人訴索好官，厲言倨色紛於前，晉卿與相對，終日無慍顏。
entries.en: Candidates who came to complain and demand better posts pressed him with harsh words and arrogant faces; Jinqing sat opposite them all day without a trace of anger.
entries.literal: Candidates lodging complaints and demanding good posts pressed toward him with stern words and arrogant expressions; Jinqing faced them across the table all day long without a trace of anger on his face.

entries.zh: 久之，進侍郎，積寬縱，而吏下因緣作奸。
entries.en: After a long while he was promoted to vice minister; laxness accumulated, and subordinate clerks seized the opening to commit fraud.
entries.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Minister, accumulated lax indulgence, and subordinate clerks took opportunity to commit fraud.

entries.zh: 方時承平，選常萬人，李林甫為尚書，專國政，以銓事委晉卿及宋遙，然歲命它官同較書判，核才實。
entries.en: In those peaceful years selections often involved ten thousand men; Li Linfu, as minister, monopolized state affairs and entrusted the examination process to Jinqing and Song Yao, yet each year other officials were ordered to join in reviewing papers and passes to verify true ability.
entries.literal: At a time of general peace, selections often ran to ten thousand men; Li Linfu was Minister and monopolized state affairs, entrusting examination affairs to Jinqing and Song Yao—yet each year other officials were ordered to join in reviewing documents and passes to verify true talent.

entries.zh: 天寶二年，判入等者凡六十四人，分甲、乙、丙三科，以張奭為第一。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianbao, sixty-four candidates were judged to have passed, divided into three grades—A, B, and C—with Zhang Shi placed first.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, those judged to have entered the ranks totaled sixty-four persons, divided into three classes—A, B, and C—with Zhang Shi ranked first.

entries.zh: 奭，御史中丞倚之子，倚新得幸於帝，晉卿欲附之，奭本無學，故議者囂然不平。
entries.en: Shi was the son of censor-in-chief Zhang Yi, who had newly won the emperor's favor; Jinqing wished to curry favor with him, but Shi was utterly without learning, and critics erupted in outrage.
entries.literal: Shi was the son of Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi; Yi had newly won the Emperor's favor; Jinqing wished to attach himself to him; Shi was fundamentally without learning—hence critics clamored in outrage.

entries.zh: 安祿山因間言之，帝為禦花萼樓覆實，中裁十一二，奭持紙終日，筆不下，人謂之「曳白」。
entries.en: An Lushan seized the chance to bring it up; the emperor held a verification at the Hua'e Tower, and more than nine-tenths failed; Shi held his examination paper all day without setting brush to paper—people called it "dragging the blank."
entries.literal: An Lushan seized on the opening to speak of it; the Emperor held a verification at the Hua'e Tower; more than nine-tenths failed; Shi held his sheet all day without the brush descending—people called it "dragging the white."

entries.zh: 帝大怒，貶倚淮陽太守，遙武當太守，晉卿安康太守。
entries.en: The emperor was furious and demoted Yi to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and demoted Yi to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.

entries.zh: 明年，徙魏郡，即充河北采訪使。
entries.en: The following year he was transferred to Weijun and appointed regional inspector of Hebei.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Weijun and appointed concurrently Regional Inspector of Hebei.

entries.zh: 居三年，政化大行。
entries.en: After three years in office, his policies had taken deep root throughout the region.
entries.literal: After three years in office, government and transformation flourished greatly.

entries.zh: 嘗入計，謁歸壺關，望縣門輒步，吏諫止，晉卿以「公門當下，況父母邦乎」？
entries.en: Once, on returning from the capital to present accounts, he visited Huguan; whenever he saw the county gate he would dismount and walk; clerks urged him to stop, but Jinqing said, "One dismounts at the public gate—how much more in one's native home!"
entries.literal: Once when entering to render accounts he returned to visit Huguan; when he saw the county gate he would walk; clerks remonstrated and stopped him, but Jinqing said, "At the public gate one must dismount—how much more in one's parents' homeland!"

entries.zh: 郡太守迎犒，使所屬令行酒，酒至，必立飲白釂，侍老有獻，降西階拜而飲，時美其恭。
entries.en: When the commandery prefect came out to welcome and feast him, he had the subordinate magistrates pass the wine; whenever a cup arrived he would rise and drain it to the dregs; when village elders offered wine he would descend the western steps, bow, and drink—contemporaries praised his reverence.
entries.literal: When the commandery prefect came out to welcome and entertain him, he had subordinate magistrates pass the wine; whenever wine arrived he would always rise and drain a full cup; when elders of the district presented offerings he would descend the western steps, bow, and drink—contemporaries praised his respectfulness.

entries.zh: 改河東郡，兼河東采訪使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and made concurrent regional inspector of Hedong.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and concurrently made Regional Inspector of Hedong.

entries.zh: 徙撫風郡，封高平縣男。
entries.en: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.
entries.literal: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.

entries.zh: 遷工部尚書、東都留守。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of works and defender of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 召為憲部，兼左丞。
entries.en: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and made concurrent left vice director.
entries.literal: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 安祿山反，竇廷芝棄陜郡不守，楊國忠本忌其有望，即奏「東道賊沖，非大臣不可鎮遏」，授陜郡太守、陜虢防禦使，晉卿見帝，以老辭，忤旨，聽致仕於家。
entries.en: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without defending it; Yang Guozhong, who had long resented Jinqing's standing with the people, immediately memorialized that "the eastern route is where the rebels will strike—only a great minister can hold them back," and appointed him prefect of Shaan commandery and defense commissioner of Shan-Guo; when Jinqing saw the emperor he pleaded old age and declined, contravened the imperial will, and was permitted to retire at home.
entries.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without holding it; Yang Guozhong had long resented Jinqing's popular standing and immediately memorialized: "The eastern road is where bandits will strike; only a great minister can suppress them," appointing him Prefect of Shaan commandery and Defense Commissioner of Shan-Guo; when Jinqing saw the Emperor he pleaded old age in refusal, contravened the imperial intent, and was permitted to retire at home.

entries.zh: 車駕入蜀，搢紳多陷賊，晉卿間道走金州。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, most of the gentry and officials fell into rebel hands; Jinqing took hidden routes and fled to Jinzhou.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, gentry and officials mostly fell into the rebels' hands; Jinqing took bypaths and fled to Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 樞素與朱全忠相結納，故全忠聽命，修貢獻不絕。
entries.en: Shu had long been allied with Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong therefore obeyed his orders and kept tribute flowing without interruption.
entries.literal: Shu had long been bound in alliance with Zhu Quanzhong; therefore Quanzhong obeyed orders and tribute and offerings never ceased.

entries.zh: 昭宗悅，遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to vice minister of war.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 時崔胤亦倚全忠專朝柄，因與樞善。
entries.en: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power and therefore befriended Shu.
entries.literal: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power and therefore was on good terms with Shu.

entries.zh: 俄以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Before long he was made vice minister of revenue and grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: Before long he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 帝在鳳翔，貶胤官，樞亦罷為工部尚書。
entries.en: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yin was demoted and Shu was also removed to minister of works.
entries.literal: When the Emperor was at Fengxiang Yin was demoted in office and Shu was also dismissed to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 已還宮，拜檢校尚書右仆射、同平章事。
entries.en: After the emperor returned to the palace Shu was appointed acting minister of the right and concurrent councillor.
entries.literal: After returning to the palace he was appointed acting Minister of the Right and Concurrent Councillor.

entries.zh: 出為清海節度使。
entries.en: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.
entries.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

entries.zh: 全忠言樞有經世才，不宜棄外，復拜門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。
entries.en: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to govern the age and should not be cast out; Shu was again appointed vice director of the gate, councillor, and supervisor of compiling the national history.
entries.literal: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to order the age and should not be abandoned outside; he was again appointed Vice Director of the Gate, Councillor, and supervisor of compiling the national history.

entries.zh: 累進右僕射、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
entries.en: He was successively advanced to minister of the right and commissioner for salt and iron transport in all circuits.
entries.literal: He was successively advanced to Minister of the Right and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport in all circuits.

entries.zh: 哀帝嗣位，柳璨方用事，全忠以牙將張廷範為太常卿，樞以為廷範勛臣，自宜任方鎮，何用為卿，恐非王意，持不下。
entries.en: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was in power; Quanzhong wished to make his military officer Zhang Tingfan director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Shu held that as a meritorious minister Tingfan ought to hold a frontier command—what use was there in making him court director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld the appointment.
entries.literal: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was just then in power; Quanzhong wished to make his military officer Zhang Tingfan Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Shu held that Tingfan was a meritorious minister and ought to be assigned to a frontier command—what use was there in making him director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld the appointment without issuing it.

entries.zh: 全忠怒謂賓佐曰：「吾常器樞不浮薄，今乃爾。」
entries.en: Quanzhong angrily told his staff: "I always thought Shu was not shallow and frivolous—now look at him."
entries.literal: Quanzhong angrily told his guests and aides: "I always valued Shu as not shallow and frivolous—now he is like this."

entries.zh: 璨聞，即罷樞政事，拜左僕射。
entries.en: When Can heard, he immediately removed Shu from state affairs and appointed him minister of the left.
entries.literal: When Can heard, he immediately removed Shu from state affairs and appointed him Minister of the Left.

entries.zh: 俄貶登州刺史，又貶瀧州司戶參軍。
entries.en: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou, then again to revenue aide at Luzhou.
entries.literal: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou and again demoted to revenue aide at Luzhou.

entries.zh: 至滑州，全忠遣人殺之白馬驛，投屍於河，年六十五。
entries.en: When he reached Huazhou, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his body into the river; he was sixty-five.
entries.literal: When he reached Huazhou Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post Station and cast his body into the river; he was sixty-five.

entries.zh: 初，全忠佐吏李振曰：「此等自謂清流，宜投諸訶，永為濁流。」
entries.en: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said, "These men call themselves the pure stream—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and become the muddy stream forever."
entries.literal: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said: "These men call themselves the clear stream—they ought to be cast into the He, to be the muddy stream forever."

entries.zh: 全忠笑而許之。
entries.en: Quanzhong laughed and agreed.
entries.literal: Quanzhong laughed and assented.

entries.zh: 崔苗二裴呂
entries.en: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu
entries.literal: Cui, Miao, two Pei's, Lu

entries.zh: 崔光遠，系出博陵，後徙靈昌。
entries.en: Cui Guangyuan's clan came from Boling and later relocated to Lingchang.
entries.literal: Cui Guangyuan, his lineage issued from Boling, later moved to Lingchang.

entries.zh: 祖敬嗣，嗜酒摴博。
entries.en: His grandfather Jingsi was devoted to wine and games of chance.
entries.literal: His grandfather Jingsi was addicted to wine and dice gambling.

entries.zh: 中宗在房州，吏多肆慢不為禮，敬嗣為刺史，獨盡誠推奉，儲給豐衍，帝德之。
entries.en: While Emperor Zhongzong was confined at Fangzhou, local officials were mostly insolent and showed him no courtesy; Jingsi alone, as prefect, served him with wholehearted devotion and kept the stores abundantly supplied, for which the emperor was deeply grateful.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong was in Fangzhou, officials mostly were insolent and did not show ritual; Jingsi as prefect alone exhausted sincerity in supporting him, stores and supplies abundant and overflowing, the Emperor was grateful to him.

entries.zh: 及反正，有與敬嗣同姓名者，每擬官，帝輒超拜，後召見，悟非是。
entries.en: After the restoration, there was a man who shared Jingsi's name; whenever an appointment was proposed, the emperor would repeatedly promote him by special decree. When he was later summoned for an audience, the emperor realized this was not the right man.
entries.literal: When the restoration came, there was one with the same name and surname as Jingsi; whenever an office was proposed, the Emperor would repeatedly promote by special order; later summoned for audience, realized it was not so.

entries.zh: 訪真敬嗣，已死，即授其子汪五品官。
entries.en: They sought out the real Jingsi, found he was already dead, and at once granted his son Wang a fifth-rank post.
entries.literal: They sought the true Jingsi; he was already dead; at once granted his son Wang a fifth-rank office.

entries.zh: 汪生光遠，勇決任氣，長六尺，瞳子白黑分明。
entries.en: Wang fathered Guangyuan, a man bold and decisive who trusted his own force of will; he stood six feet tall, with pupils whose white and black were sharply distinct.
entries.literal: Wang bore Guangyuan, brave and decisive, trusting his spirit, six feet in height, pupils white and black clearly distinct.

entries.zh: 開元末，為唐安令，與楊國忠善，累遷京兆少尹，為吐蕃吊祭使，還，會玄宗西狩，詔留光遠為京兆尹、西京留守、采訪使。
entries.en: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he served as magistrate of Tang'an, was on good terms with Yang Guozhong, and rose repeatedly to vice governor of Jingzhao. Sent as mourning envoy to Tibet, he returned just as Emperor Xuanzong fled west; he was ordered to remain as governor of Jingzhao, custodian of the western capital, and investigation commissioner.
entries.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, he was magistrate of Tang'an, on good terms with Yang Guozhong, repeatedly rose to Vice Governor of Jingzhao, was envoy to mourn Tibet; on return, met Emperor Xuanzong's western hunt; edict left Guangyuan as Governor of Jingzhao, Western Capital Retention Custodian, Investigation Commissioner.

entries.zh: 乘輿已出，都人亂，火左藏大盈庫，爭輦財珍，至乘驢入宮殿者。
entries.en: The imperial carriage had already departed, the capital was in turmoil, fire broke out at the Left Repository of the Great Abundance Vault, and people fought over cartloads of treasure—even riding donkeys into the palace halls.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage had already gone out; the capital people were chaotic; fire at the Left Repository Great Abundance Vault; they struggled over cartloads of valuables and treasures, even to riding donkeys into the palace halls.

entries.zh: 光遠乃募官攝府、縣，誰何宮闕，斬十數人，乃定。
entries.en: Guangyuan then recruited officials to act for the prefecture and counties, posted guards at the palace precincts, and beheaded more than ten men before order was restored.
entries.literal: Guangyuan then recruited officials to act for prefecture and counties, posted guards at the palace precincts, beheaded more than ten men, then it was settled.

entries.zh: 因偽使其子東見祿山，而祿山先署張休為京兆尹，由是追休，授光遠故官。
entries.en: He therefore pretended to send his son east to see An Lushan, but Lushan had already appointed Zhang Xiu governor of Jingzhao; Xiu was recalled for this, and Guangyuan was given his former post.
entries.literal: Thereupon feigned sending his son east to see Lushan, but Lushan had already appointed Zhang Xiu as Governor of Jingzhao; for this they recalled Xiu and gave Guangyuan his former office.

entries.zh: 俄而同羅背賊，以廄馬二千出奔，賊將孫孝哲、安神威招之不得，神威憂死，官吏驚走，獄囚皆逸。
entries.en: Soon the Tongluo turned against the rebels and fled with two thousand stable horses. The rebel generals Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei could not win them over; Shenwei died of grief; officials fled in alarm, and all the prisoners escaped.
entries.literal: Soon the Tongluo turned against the rebels, with two thousand stable horses fled out; rebel generals Sun Xiaozhe and An Shenwei could not win them; Shenwei died of grief; officials fled in alarm; prison inmates all escaped.

entries.zh: 光遠以為賊且走，命人守神威、孝哲等第，斬曳落河二人。
entries.en: Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee; he had men guard the residences of Shenwei, Xiaozhe, and the others, and beheaded two Tiele guards.
entries.literal: Guangyuan thought the rebels were about to flee, ordered men to guard the residences of Shenwei, Xiaozhe, and the rest, beheaded two Tiele guards.

entries.zh: 孝哲馳白祿山，光遠懼，與長安令蘇震出開遠門，使人奔呼曰：「尹巡門！」
entries.en: Xiaozhe galloped to report to Lushan. Guangyuan was afraid; he went with Chang'an magistrate Su Zhen out through Kaiyuan Gate and had men run ahead shouting, "The governor is inspecting the gate!"
entries.literal: Xiaozhe galloped to report to Lushan; Guangyuan was afraid; with Chang'an magistrate Su Zhen he went out Kaiyuan Gate, had men run shouting: "The Governor inspects the gate!"

entries.zh: 門兵具器仗迎謁，至，皆斬之，募得百餘人，遂趨靈武。
entries.en: The gate soldiers came out with weapons to receive him; when they arrived, he beheaded them all, recruited more than a hundred men, and hastened toward Lingwu.
entries.literal: Gate soldiers equipped weapons to receive and attend; when they arrived, all were beheaded; he recruited more than a hundred men, then hastened toward Lingwu.

entries.zh: 肅宗嘉之，擢拜御史大夫，復為京兆尹，遣到渭北募僑民。
entries.en: Emperor Suzong praised this, promoted him to censor-in-chief, again made him governor of Jingzhao, and sent him north of the Wei to recruit displaced people.
entries.literal: Emperor Suzong praised this, promoted to Censor-in-Chief, again made Governor of Jingzhao, sent to north of the Wei to recruit displaced people.

entries.zh: 會賊黨剽涇陽，休祠房，椎牛呼飲。
entries.en: When rebel bands raided Jingyang, they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen, and feasted with loud shouting.
entries.literal: It happened rebel bands raided Jingyang; they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen and shouted while drinking.

entries.zh: 光遠刺知之，率兵夜趨其所，使百騎彀滿狙其前，命驍士合噪。
entries.en: Guangyuan learned of it through spies, led troops by night toward their camp, stationed a hundred horsemen with drawn bows to ambush them in front, and ordered his fiercest soldiers to shout in unison.
entries.literal: Guangyuan learned through spies, led troops by night toward their place, made a hundred horsemen with bows full to ambush before them, ordered fierce soldiers to shout together.

entries.zh: 賊醉，不能師，斬其徒二千，得馬千噭，俘一酋長以獻。
entries.en: The rebels were drunk and could not form ranks; he beheaded two thousand of their followers, took a thousand neighing horses, and presented one chieftain as prisoner.
entries.literal: The rebels were drunk, could not form ranks, beheaded two thousand of their followers, obtained a thousand neighing horses, captured one chieftain to present.

entries.zh: 自是，賊常避其鋒。
entries.en: From then on the rebels regularly avoided his sharp edge.
entries.literal: From this, rebels regularly avoided his sharp edge.

entries.zh: 扈帝還，改禮部尚書、鄴國公，封實戶三百。
entries.en: Escorting the emperor back, he was made minister of rites and Duke of Ye, with three hundred taxable households as his fief.
entries.literal: Escorting the Emperor back, changed to Minister of Rites, Duke of Ye, enfeoffed three hundred taxable households.

entries.zh: 鄧景山，曹州人。
entries.en: Deng Jingshan was a native of Caozhou.
entries.literal: Deng Jingshan, a man of Caozhou.

entries.zh: 本以文吏進，累至監察御史。
entries.en: He had originally entered through the civil-service track and rose to investigating censor.
entries.literal: Originally entered through the civil clerk track, rose repeatedly to Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 至德初，擢拜青齊節度使，徙淮南。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhide era he was promoted to military governor of Qing and Qi, then transferred to Huainan.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, promoted as Military Governor of Qing and Qi, transferred to Huainan.

entries.zh: 為政簡肅。
entries.en: His administration was simple and austere.
entries.literal: His government was simple and austere.

entries.zh: 有鼉集城門，鄧珽語景山曰：「鼉介物也。
entries.en: A crocodile gathered at the city gate. Deng Ting said to Jingshan, "The crocodile is a scaled creature.
entries.literal: A crocodile gathered at the city gate; Deng Ting said to Jingshan: "The crocodile is a scaled creature.

entries.zh: 失所次，金不從革之象。
entries.en: Out of its proper place—an omen of metal not yielding to change.
entries.literal: Out of its proper place—an image of metal not following transformation.

entries.zh: 其有兵乎？」
entries.en: Does this portend warfare?"
entries.literal: Will there be warfare?"

entries.zh: 未幾，宋州刺史劉殿反。
entries.en: Before long, Songzhou prefect Liu Zhan rebelled.
entries.literal: Before long, Songzhou Prefect Liu Dian rebelled.

entries.zh: 初，展有異志，淮西節度使王仲昇表其狀，詔遷揚州長史兼江淮都統，密詔景山執送京師。
entries.en: Earlier Liu Zhan had harbored a different intent; Huainan West military governor Wang Zhongsheng memorialized his conduct; the emperor ordered him moved to Yangzhou chief administrator and concurrent commander of Jiang-Huai, with a secret edict to Jingshan to arrest him and send him to the capital.
entries.literal: At first Zhan had a different intent; Huainan West Military Governor Wang Zhongsheng memorialized his conduct; edict moved him to Yangzhou Chief Administrator concurrent Commander of Jiang-Huai, secret edict to Jingshan to arrest and send to the capital.

entries.zh: 展知之，擁兵二萬度淮。
entries.en: Zhan learned of it and led twenty thousand troops across the Huai.
entries.literal: Zhan learned of it, led twenty thousand troops across the Huai.

entries.zh: 景山逆擊不勝，奔壽州，因引平盧節度副使田神功討展。
entries.en: Jingshan met him in attack and was defeated; he fled to Shouzhou and then brought in Pinglu deputy military governor Tian Shenggong to attack Zhan.
entries.literal: Jingshan met him in attack and was not victorious, fled to Shouzhou, then brought in Pinglu Deputy Military Governor Tian Shenggong to attack Zhan.

entries.zh: 神功兵至揚州，大掠居人，發冢墓，大食、波斯賈胡死者數千人。
entries.en: When Shenggong's army reached Yangzhou, they greatly plundered the inhabitants and opened graves; several thousand Sogdian and Persian merchants were among the dead.
entries.literal: When Shenggong's army reached Yangzhou, they greatly plundered inhabitants, opened graves; Sogdian and Persian merchant dead numbered several thousand.

entries.zh: 展叛凡三月平，追景山入朝，拜尚書左丞，以崔圓代之。
entries.en: Zhan's rebellion was pacified in about three months; Jingshan was recalled to court, appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and Cui Yuan replaced him.
entries.literal: Zhan's rebellion was pacified in about three months; Jingshan was recalled to court, appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Cui Yuan replaced him.

entries.zh: 王思禮在太原，儲廥贏衍，請輸半以實京師。
entries.en: Wang Sili was at Taiyuan with granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half the stores to fill the capital.
entries.literal: Wang Sili was at Taiyuan; granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half to fill the capital.

entries.zh: 會卒，管崇嗣代之，政弛不治，數月，為下盜費略盡。
entries.en: He soon died; Guan Chongsi replaced him; government grew slack and was not put in order; within months theft and waste by the lower ranks had nearly exhausted everything.
entries.literal: He soon died; Guan Chongsi replaced him; government grew slack and was not put in order; within months what the lower ranks stole and wasted was nearly exhausted.

entries.zh: 帝聞，即以景山為太原尹，封南陽郡公。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of this, he at once made Jingshan governor of Taiyuan and enfeoffed him as Duke of Nanyang.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard, he at once made Jingshan Governor of Taiyuan and enfeoffed him Duke of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 至則振核紀綱，檢覆幹隱，眾大懼。
entries.en: On arrival he shook up discipline and regulations and investigated concealed abuses; the masses were greatly afraid.
entries.literal: On arrival he shook up discipline and regulations, investigated concealed abuses; the masses were greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 而景山清約，子弟饌不過草具，用器止烏漆，待上賓惟豚、魚而已，取倉粟紅腐者食之，兼給麾下，麾下怨訕。
entries.en: Yet Jingshan was frugal and abstemious: his sons and brothers' meals were no more than humble fare, his vessels were only black lacquer, and for honored guests he served only pork and fish. He took red rotten grain from the granary to eat and also gave it to his subordinates, who grumbled in ridicule.
entries.literal: Yet Jingshan was frugal and abstemious; sons and brothers' meals were no more than humble fare; vessels only black lacquer; for honored guests only pork and fish; he took red rotten grain from the granary to eat and also gave to his subordinates—the subordinates grumbled in ridicule.

entries.zh: 左右白景山，景山曰：「此不食，留將安用邪？」
entries.en: His attendants informed Jingshan; Jingshan said, "If we won't eat this, what will we keep it for?"
entries.literal: Attendants informed Jingshan; Jingshan said: "If we won't eat this, what will we keep it for?"

entries.zh: 因慢罵，士皆羞忿。
entries.en: He then reviled them with contempt, and the soldiers were all ashamed and furious.
entries.literal: He then reviled them with contempt, and the soldiers were all ashamed and furious.

entries.zh: 有裨校抵死，諸將請贖，不許；
entries.en: A staff officer was guilty of a capital offense; the generals asked to redeem him—not permitted;
entries.literal: A staff officer was guilty of a capital offense; the generals asked to redeem him—not permitted;

entries.zh: 其弟請代，不許；
entries.en: his younger brother asked to take his place—not permitted;
entries.literal: his younger brother asked to take his place—not permitted;

entries.zh: 請納一馬贖，景山乃許減死。
entries.en: they asked to offer one horse in ransom; only then did Jingshan permit commutation from death.
entries.literal: they asked to offer one horse in ransom; only then did Jingshan permit commutation from death.

entries.zh: 眾怒曰：「吾屬命才一馬直乎？」
entries.en: The crowd raged, saying, "Are our lives worth only one horse?"
entries.literal: The crowd raged, saying: "Are our lives worth only one horse?"

entries.zh: 景山護失，叱遣之。
entries.en: Jingshan, protective of his error, shouted and sent them away.
entries.literal: Jingshan, protective of his error, shouted and sent them away.

entries.zh: 少將黃抱節因眾怒作亂，景山遇害，時寶應元年也。
entries.en: The junior general Huang Baojie stirred up the crowd's anger and made a revolt; Jingshan met his death—it was the first year of Baoying.
entries.literal: The junior general Huang Baojie, because of the crowd's anger, made a revolt; Jingshan met disaster—it was the first year of Baoying.

entries.zh: 肅宗以其統馭失方，不復究驗，遣使喻撫其軍，軍中請辛雲京為節度，詔可。
entries.en: Emperor Suzong, because Jingshan had lost control, did not pursue the matter further; he sent envoys to pacify the army, and the army requested Xin Yunjing as military governor—the edict approved.
entries.literal: Emperor Suzong, because he had lost control, did not pursue investigation further, sent envoys to pacify the army; the army requested Xin Yunjing as military governor; the edict approved.

entries.zh: 景山與劉晏善，其後家寒窶，晏屢經紀之，嫁其孤女。
entries.en: Jingshan was friendly with Liu Yan; afterward his family was poor and needy, and Yan repeatedly managed affairs for him and married off his orphaned daughter.
entries.literal: Jingshan was on good terms with Liu Yan; afterward his family was poor and needy; Yan repeatedly managed affairs for him and married off his orphaned daughter.

entries.zh: 謚曰敬。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Jing.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Jing.

entries.zh: 崔鄧魏衛李韓盧高
entries.en: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li, Han, Lu, and Gao
entries.literal: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li, Han, Lu, Gao

entries.zh: 裴奰者，始以蔭為京兆司錄參軍。
entries.en: Pei Yi had first entered office through hereditary privilege as recorder of the metropolitan prefecture.
entries.literal: As for Pei Yi, he first entered office by yin privilege as Recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 瑱鎮陜州，引為判官，移襄州，又為行軍司馬，遇之厚。
entries.en: When Zhen governed Shanzhou he took Yi on as aide; at Xiangzhou he made him military secretary and treated him with great favor.
entries.literal: When Zhen governed Shan Prefecture he brought him in as aide; when transferred to Xiang Prefecture he again made him Military Affairs Secretary and treated him generously.

entries.zh: 及瑱私漢上，奰欲得其處，故背瑱言狀，帝倚以圖瑱。
entries.en: When Zhen clung to his command on the Han, Yi coveted his post, turned informer against him, and won the emperor's trust for the plot to remove him.
entries.literal: When Zhen privately held the Han region, Yi wished to obtain his post and therefore turned against Zhen in his reports; the Emperor relied on him to plot against Zhen.

entries.zh: 而性輕褊少謀，師興，給用無節。
entries.en: But he was rash, petty, and shortsighted; once his campaign began, he spent supplies without restraint.
entries.literal: Yet his nature was frivolous, narrow, and short on planning; when the army marched, supplies were expended without restraint.

entries.zh: 及敗，有詔流費州，至藍田，賜死。
entries.en: After his defeat he was banished to Feizhou and ordered to die at Lantian.
entries.literal: When he was defeated, an edict banished him to Fei Prefecture; at Lantian he was granted death.

entries.zh: 田神功，冀州南宮人。
entries.en: Tian Shengong was a native of Nangong in Jizhou.
entries.literal: Tian Shengong was a man of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.

entries.zh: 天寶末，為縣史。
entries.en: Late in the Tianbao period he served as a county clerk.
entries.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he was a county clerk.

entries.zh: 會天下兵興，賊署為平盧兵馬使，率眾歸朝，從李忠臣收滄、德，攻相州，拒杏園。
entries.en: When rebellion spread, the rebels made him Pinglu military commissioner; he then led his men back to the Tang side, followed Li Zhongchen in recovering Cangzhou and Dezhou, fought at Xiangzhou, and held Xingyuan Garden.
entries.literal: When warfare arose throughout the realm, the rebels appointed him Military Commissioner of Pinglu; he led his troops back to the court, followed Li Zhongchen in recovering Cang and De, attacked Xiang Prefecture, and held Xingyuan Garden.

entries.zh: 後守陳留，戰不勝，與許叔冀降於史思明。
entries.en: Later, defending Chenliu, he was beaten and surrendered with Xu Shuji to Shi Siming.
entries.literal: Later he defended Chenliu, was defeated in battle, and with Xu Shuji surrendered to Shi Siming.

entries.zh: 思明使與南德信、劉從諫南略江淮，神功襲德信，斬之，從諫脫身走，乃並將其兵。
entries.en: Siming sent him south with Nan Dexin and Liu Congjian to overrun Jianghuai; Shengong ambushed Dexin and killed him, and when Congjian fled he absorbed both armies.
entries.literal: Siming sent him with Nan Dexin and Liu Congjian to campaign south into Jianghuai; Shengong surprised Dexin, beheaded him, Congjian escaped by himself, and he then took command of all their troops.

entries.zh: 詔拜鴻臚卿。
entries.en: The court appointed him minister of diplomatic reception.
entries.literal: An edict appointed him Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

entries.zh: 襲敬釭鄆州，不克。
entries.en: He assaulted Jing Gang at Yunzhou but failed to take the city.
entries.literal: He attacked Jing Gang at Yun Prefecture but did not overcome him.

entries.zh: 劉展反，鄧景山引神功助討，自淄青濟淮，眾不整，入揚州，遂大掠居人貲產，發屋剔窖，殺商胡波斯數千人。
entries.en: When Liu Zhan rebelled, Deng Jingshan called on Shengong. Marching from Ziqing across the Huai in disorder, he entered Yangzhou and looted the city, breaking into houses, digging out hidden stores, and slaughtering several thousand foreign merchants, including Persians.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhan rebelled, Deng Jingshan brought in Shengong to assist in the suppression. He crossed the Huai from Ziqing with his troops in disorder, entered Yang Prefecture, and plundered the residents' property on a vast scale, tearing open houses and digging out cellars; several thousand foreign merchants, including Persians, were killed.

entries.zh: 俄而禽展送京師，遷淄青節度使。
entries.en: He soon captured Zhan and sent him to the capital, and was made military governor of Ziqing.
entries.literal: Before long he captured Zhan and sent him to the capital, and was transferred to be Military Governor of Ziqing.

entries.zh: 會侯希逸入青州，更徙兗鄆。
entries.en: When Hou Xiyi took Qingzhou, his command was shifted to Yanzhou and Yunzhou.
entries.literal: It happened that Hou Xiyi entered Qing Prefecture, and he was further transferred to Yan and Yun.

entries.zh: 時賊圍宋州急，李光弼奏神功往救，賊解去。
entries.en: Rebels were pressing Songzhou hard; Li Guangbi urged that Shengong relieve the city, and the siege was raised.
entries.literal: At that time rebels were pressing Song Prefecture urgently; Li Guangbi memorialized that Shengong should go to rescue it, and the rebels lifted the siege and departed.

entries.zh: 又破法子營，復攻敬釭，降之。
entries.en: He routed Fa Zi's camp, attacked Jing Gang again, and accepted his surrender.
entries.literal: He again defeated Fa Zi's camp, again attacked Jing Gang, and received his surrender.

entries.zh: 朝義聞，乃奔下博。
entries.en: Shi Chaoyi, hearing this, fled to Xiabo.
entries.literal: When Chaoyi heard of it, he fled to Xiabo.

entries.zh: 進封信都郡王，徙河南節度、汴宋八州觀察使。
entries.en: He was advanced to prince of Xindu and made military governor of Henan and observer of the eight Bian-Song prefectures.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Prince of Xindu and transferred to Military Governor of Henan and Observation Commissioner of the eight prefectures of Bian and Song.

entries.zh: 大歷三年來朝。
entries.en: In 768 he came to court.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dali he came to court.

entries.zh: 寧本名旰，至是賜名。
entries.en: His original name was Gan; at this point the court granted him the name Ning.
entries.literal: Ning's original name was Gan; at this time he was granted the name Ning.

entries.zh: 楊子琳襲取成都，帝乃還寧於蜀。
entries.en: When Yang Zilin seized Chengdu, the emperor sent Ning back to Shu.
entries.literal: Yang Zilin surprised and seized Chengdu, and the Emperor thereupon returned Ning to Shu.

entries.zh: 未幾，子琳敗。
entries.en: Zilin was soon defeated.
entries.literal: Before long Zilin was defeated.

entries.zh: 寧見蜀地險，饒於財，而朝廷不甚有紀，乃痛誅斂；
entries.en: Seeing that Shu was rugged, wealthy, and poorly governed from afar, Ning taxed it ruthlessly;
entries.literal: Ning saw that Shu territory was perilous and rich in wealth, while the court was not very orderly, and therefore levied taxes harshly;

entries.zh: 使弟寬居京師，以賂厚謝權貴，深結元載父子，故寬驟擢御史中丞，寬兄審至給事中。
entries.en: he kept his brother Kuan in the capital to bribe the powerful and court Yuan Zai's faction, so Kuan rose swiftly to vice censor-in-chief and his brother Shen to palace attendant.
entries.literal: he had his younger brother Kuan reside in the capital, use bribes to thank the powerful and noble lavishly, and bind himself deeply to Yuan Zai father and son; therefore Kuan was suddenly promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Kuan's elder brother Shen reached Attendant within the Palace.

entries.zh: 寧在蜀久，兵浸強，而肆侈窮欲，將吏妻妾多為汙逼，朝廷隱忍，不能詰。
entries.en: Long in Shu, his army grew strong while he indulged every excess and forced himself on many officers' wives; the court looked away and dared not call him to account.
entries.literal: Ning was long in Shu, his troops gradually grew strong, and he indulged extravagance to the limit of desire; many officers' and officials' wives and concubines were forced and violated, and the court forbear and could not investigate.

entries.zh: 累加尚書左僕射。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 十四年，入朝，進檢校司空、同中書門下平章事，兼山陵使。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he came to court, was made acting minister of works and chief councilor, and appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb works.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered court, was advanced to Acting Minister of Works, Associate Director of the Secretariat with Court Session Privileges, and concurrently Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 俄以平章事為御史大夫，即建白擇御史當出大夫，不宜謀及宰相。
entries.en: Soon made grand censor while retaining his councilorship, he argued that censor appointments should rest with the censorate alone, not with the chief ministers.
entries.literal: Before long, from chief councilor he became Grand Censor, and immediately proposed that selection of censors should come from the Grand Censor and should not involve consultation with chief ministers.

entries.zh: 因奏李衡、於結等任御史，宰相楊炎怒，寢不行。
entries.en: He nominated Li Heng, Yu Jie, and others as censors; Yang Yan blocked the appointments in anger.
entries.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Li Heng, Yu Jie, and others be appointed censors; Chief Minister Yang Yan was angry and the proposal was shelved and not carried out.

entries.zh: 炎方詆劉晏，寧申救於帝，又素事元載，而炎亦出載門，故銜之，未忍發。
entries.en: As Yang Yan attacked Liu Yan, Ning pleaded for Liu at court; though both men had ties to Yuan Zai's faction, Yan resented Ning and bided his time.
entries.literal: Yan was at that time slandering Liu Yan; Ning pleaded for rescue before the Emperor; he had also long served Yuan Zai, while Yan too came from Zai's faction—therefore Yan harbored resentment but did not yet dare to strike.

entries.zh: ◎來田侯崔嚴來瑱，邠州永壽人。
entries.en: ◎ Biographies of Lai, Tian, Hou, Cui, and Yan. Lai Zhen was a native of Yongshou in Binzhou.
entries.literal: ◎ Lai, Tian, Hou, Cui, and Yan: Lai Zhen was a man of Yongshou in Bin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父曜，奮行間，開元末，持節磧西副大使、四鎮節度使，著名西邊，終右領軍大將軍。
entries.en: His father Yao had distinguished himself in arms; late in the Kaiyuan reign he served with imperial credentials as deputy commissioner of the Western Regions and military governor of the Four Garrisons, won renown on the frontier, and died as Grand General of the Right Palace Guard.
entries.literal: His father Yao was valiant in martial exploits; at the end of the Kaiyuan era he held the insignia as Deputy Commissioner of the Western Regions and Military Governor of the Four Garrisons, was famed on the western frontier, and ended as Grand General of the Right Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 瑱略知收，尚名節，崖然有大誌。
entries.en: Zhen knew something of fiscal administration, prized honor and integrity, and carried himself with stern dignity and high ambition.
entries.literal: Zhen had some knowledge of revenue administration, esteemed reputation and integrity, and stood aloof with great ambition.

entries.zh: 天寶初，從四鎮任劇職，累遷殿中侍御史、伊西北庭行軍司馬。
entries.en: Early in the Tianbao period he held demanding posts with the Four Garrisons and rose in turn to palace censor and military affairs secretary for Yixi and Beiting.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he served in the Four Garrisons in strenuous posts and was successively promoted to Censor within the Palace and Military Affairs Secretary of Yixi and Beiting.

entries.zh: 詔舉智謀果決、才堪統眾者，拾遺張鎬薦瑱能斷大事，有禦侮才，擢潁川太守，充招討使。
entries.en: When the throne sought men of decisive counsel able to lead troops, Remonstrance Official Zhang Hao urged that Zhen could settle weighty matters and repel invasion; he was made prefect of Yingchuan and appointed pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: An edict called for men of resourceful resolve fit to command armies; Remonstrance Official Zhang Hao recommended that Zhen could decide great affairs and had talent to repel insult; he was promoted to Administrator of Yingchuan and made Pacification Commissioner.

entries.zh: 會母喪免，以孝聞。
entries.en: When his mother died he left office to mourn and won a reputation for filial devotion.
entries.literal: He happened to be dismissed on account of his mother's mourning and became known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 憲宗立，以考功郎中召，知制誥。
entries.en: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, Jifu was summoned as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and entrusted with drafting edicts.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, Jifu was summoned as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and made drafter of edicts.

entries.zh: 俄入翰林為學士，遷中書舍人。
entries.en: Soon he entered the Hanlin Academy as academician and was promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Soon he entered the Hanlin Academy as academician and was promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 劉闢拒命，帝意討之，未決。
entries.en: Liu Pi defied imperial orders; the emperor wished to suppress him but had not yet made up his mind.
entries.literal: Liu Pi defied orders; the emperor intended to attack him but had not yet decided.

entries.zh: 吉甫獨請無置，宜絕朝貢以折奸謀。
entries.en: Jifu alone advised against dispatching troops and urged that court tribute be cut off to frustrate Liu Pi's designs.
entries.literal: Jifu alone requested that no troops be sent and that court tribute be cut off to thwart treacherous designs.

entries.zh: 時李錡在浙西，厚賂貴幸，請用韓滉故事領鹽鐵，又求宣、歙。
entries.en: At that time Li Qi held Zhexi, lavished bribes on the emperor's favorites, asked to take charge of the salt and iron monopoly by the precedent of Han Huang, and also sought Xuancheng and Shezhou.
entries.literal: At that time Li Qi was in Zhexi, lavishing bribes on favored courtiers, asking by the precedent of Han Huang to take charge of salt and iron, and also seeking Xuancheng and Shezhou.

entries.zh: 問吉甫，對曰：「昔韋臯蓄財多，故劉闢因以構亂。
entries.en: The emperor asked Jifu, who replied, "In the past Wei Gao amassed great wealth, and Liu Pi was thereby able to raise rebellion.
entries.literal: The emperor asked Jifu, who replied, "In the past Wei Gao amassed great wealth, and so Liu Pi was able to raise rebellion thereby.

entries.zh: 李錡不臣有萌，若益以鹽鐵之饒、采石之險，是趣其反也。」
entries.en: Li Qi already shows signs of disloyalty; if you add the wealth of the salt and iron monopoly and the strategic strongpoint of Caishi, you will push him toward rebellion."
entries.literal: Li Qi already shows the sprouts of disloyalty; if you add to him the riches of salt and iron and the strategic danger of Caishi, you will hasten his rebellion."

entries.zh: 帝寤，乃以李巽為鹽鐵使。
entries.en: The emperor saw the point and appointed Li Xun salt and iron commissioner instead.
entries.literal: The emperor awoke to this and appointed Li Xun salt and iron commissioner.

entries.zh: 高崇文圍鹿頭未下，嚴礪請出并州兵，與崇文趨果、閬，以攻渝、合，吉甫以為非是，因言：「漢伐公孫述，晉伐李勢，宋伐譙縱，梁伐劉季連、蕭紀，凡五攻蜀，繇江道者四。
entries.en: Gao Chongwen had besieged Lutou without success; Yan Li proposed sending Bingzhou troops to join Chongwen in marching on Guo and Lang to attack Yu and He. Jifu objected, saying, "When Han attacked Gongsun Shu, Jin attacked Li Shi, Song attacked Qiao Zong, and Liang attacked Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—in all five campaigns against Shu, four went by the Yangtze route.
entries.literal: Gao Chongwen had besieged Lutou without taking it; Yan Li requested to send out Bingzhou troops to join Chongwen in advancing on Guo and Lang to attack Yu and He. Jifu held this wrong and said, "When Han attacked Gongsun Shu, Jin attacked Li Shi, Song attacked Qiao Zong, and Liang attacked Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—in all five campaigns against Shu, four went by the river route.

entries.zh: 且宣、洪、蘄、鄂強弩，號天下精兵，爭險地兵家所長，請起其兵搗三峽之虛，則賊勢必分，首尾不救，崇文懼舟師成功，人有鬥誌矣。」
entries.en: Moreover the crossbowmen of Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E are reckoned the finest troops in the empire, and seizing strategic ground is what soldiers do best. Raise their forces to strike the undefended Three Gorges; the rebels will be divided and unable to aid each other, and Chongwen, fearing that the river fleet will win the glory, will fight all the harder."
entries.literal: Moreover the strong crossbows of Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E are called the finest troops in the realm; contending for strategic terrain is what soldiers excel at. I ask that their troops be raised to strike the undefended Three Gorges; then the rebels' force will surely be divided, head and tail unable to aid each other, and Chongwen, fearing that the river fleet will succeed, will have men with fighting spirit."

entries.zh: 帝從之。
entries.en: The emperor followed his advice.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this advice.

entries.zh: 礪復請大臣為節度，吉甫諫曰：「崇文功且成，而又命帥，不復盡力矣。」
entries.en: Yan Li again asked that a senior minister be made military commissioner; Jifu remonstrated, "Chongwen's victory is nearly won; if another commander is appointed over him, he will no longer give his full effort."
entries.literal: Li again requested that a great minister be made military commissioner; Jifu remonstrated, "Chongwen's achievement is nearly complete; if another commander is appointed, he will no longer exert himself fully."

entries.zh: 因請以西川授崇文，而屬礪東川，益資、簡六州，使兩川得以相制。
entries.en: He therefore proposed giving West River Circuit to Chongwen while assigning Yan Li East River Circuit with the six prefectures of Yi, Zi, and Jian added, so that the two circuits could keep each other in check.
entries.literal: He therefore asked that West River Circuit be given to Chongwen while Li was assigned East River Circuit with the six prefectures of Yi, Zi, and Jian added, so that the two circuits could check each other.

entries.zh: 由是崇文悉力。
entries.en: Thereupon Chongwen gave his full effort.
entries.literal: Thereupon Chongwen exerted himself fully.

entries.zh: 劉闢平，吉甫謀居多。
entries.en: When Liu Pi was suppressed, Jifu's counsel had played the leading part.
entries.literal: When Liu Pi was pacified, Jifu's planning had the greater part.

entries.zh: 李棲筠，字貞一，世為趙人。
entries.en: Li Qiyun, whose courtesy name was Zhenyi, came from a Zhao family of long standing.
entries.literal: Li Qiyun, courtesy name Zhenyi, was for generations a man of Zhao.

entries.zh: 幼孤。
entries.en: He lost his parents while still young.
entries.literal: Orphaned in childhood.

entries.zh: 有遠度，莊重寡言，體貌軒特。
entries.en: He possessed breadth of vision, was solemn and reticent, and cut an imposing, distinguished figure.
entries.literal: He had far-reaching vision, was grave and sparing of speech, and his physique was lofty and distinctive.

entries.zh: 喜書，多所能曉，為文章，勁迅有體要。
entries.en: He delighted in learning, mastered many subjects, and wrote prose that was vigorous, swift, and structurally sound.
entries.literal: He loved books, understood many fields, and in writing essays was forceful and swift with structural essentials.

entries.zh: 不妄交遊。
entries.en: He was careful about whom he befriended.
entries.literal: He did not make acquaintances rashly.

entries.zh: 族子華每稱有王佐才，士多慕向。
entries.en: His kinsman Li Hua often declared that he had the makings of a chief minister, and scholars flocked to admire him.
entries.literal: His clansman Li Hua often said he had the talent to assist a king; many scholars admired and turned toward him.

entries.zh: 始，居汲共城山下，華固請舉進士，俄擢高第。
entries.en: At first he lived at the foot of Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Li Hua pressed him to sit for the jinshi examination, and he soon placed at the head of the list.
entries.literal: At first he lived at the foot of Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Hua insistently urged him to enter the jinshi examination, and he soon was selected at the top rank.

entries.zh: 調冠氏主簿，太守李峴視若布衣交。
entries.en: He was posted as chief clerk of Guanshi, where Prefect Li Xian treated him as an equal friend.
entries.literal: He was appointed principal clerk of Guanshi; the prefect Li Xian treated him as a friend in plain cloth.

entries.zh: 遷安西封常清節度府判官。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as secretary in Feng Changqing's Anxi command.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be secretary in Feng Changqing's Anxi military governorship.

entries.zh: 常清被召，表攝監察御史，為行軍司馬。
entries.en: When Feng Changqing was recalled to court, he recommended Qiyun as acting investigating censor and army marshal.
entries.literal: When Changqing was summoned, he memorialized that Qiyun act as investigating censor and serve as army marshal.

entries.zh: 肅宗駐靈武，發安西兵，棲筠料精卒七千赴難，擢殿中侍御史。
entries.en: When Emperor Suzong held court at Lingwu and Anxi forces were called up, Qiyun picked seven thousand elite troops to march to the emperor's aid and was promoted to palace attendant censor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Suzong was stationed at Lingwu and Anxi troops were mobilized, Qiyun selected seven thousand crack soldiers to go to the rescue and was promoted to attendant censor in the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠辟為判官，累遷左司員外郎。
entries.en: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Zhexi, recruited him as an administrative aide, and he rose in stages to Vice Director of the Left Office.
entries.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun recruited him as administrative aide, and he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Left Office.

entries.zh: 與劉晏善，晏得罪，貶信州長史。
entries.en: He was on good terms with Liu Yan. When Yan fell from favor, Zao was demoted to chief administrator of Xin Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was friendly with Liu Yan. When Yan was convicted, [Zao] was demoted to Chief Administrator of Xin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 徙建州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to prefect of Jian Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Jian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 朱泚亂，造輒馳檄比州，發所部兵二千以待命，德宗嘉之。
entries.en: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, Zao at once sent proclamations to neighboring prefectures and mobilized two thousand troops from his command to await orders. Emperor Dezong commended him.
entries.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Zao immediately dispatched proclamations to neighboring prefectures, mobilizing two thousand troops from his jurisdiction to await orders. Dezong praised this.

entries.zh: 京師平，召還，至藍田，自以舅源休與賊同逆，上疏請罪。
entries.en: After the capital was restored he was recalled. When he reached Lantian, considering that his maternal uncle Yuan Xiu had joined the rebels in treason, he submitted a memorial asking to be punished.
entries.literal: When the capital was pacified he was summoned back. Reaching Lantian, he considered that his uncle Yuan Xiu had joined the rebels in treason and submitted a memorial requesting punishment.

entries.zh: 帝以為有禮，下詔慰勉，擢給事中。
entries.en: The emperor judged his conduct honorable, issued an edict to comfort and encourage him, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.
entries.literal: The emperor considered this proper conduct, issued an edict of comfort and encouragement, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.

entries.zh: 貞元二年，以給事中同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the second year of the Zhenyuan era he was made Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as Drafting Attendant.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, as Drafting Attendant he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 帝謂造敢言，為能立事，故不次用之。
entries.en: The emperor said that Zao spoke boldly and could get things done, and therefore promoted him ahead of the usual order.
entries.literal: The emperor said Zao dared to speak and could accomplish affairs, and therefore employed him out of turn.

entries.zh: 造久在江左，疾錢谷諸使罔上，或幹沒自私，乃建言：「天下兩稅，請委本道觀察使、刺史選官部送京師。
entries.en: Zao had long served south of the Yangzi and resented the fiscal commissioners who deceived the throne or seized funds for themselves. He proposed: "The empire's two-tax revenues should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to choose officials and deliver the receipts to the capital.
entries.literal: Zao had long been in the Jiangzuo region and resented the grain-finance commissioners who deceived the throne or embezzled for private gain. He memorialized: "The empire's two-tax revenues should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to select officials and deliver them to the capital.

entries.zh: 諸道水陸轉運使、度支巡院、江淮轉運使，請悉停，以度支鹽鐵務還尚書省，六曹皆宰相分領。」
entries.en: All circuit transport commissioners, expenditure-review patrol offices, and the Jianghuai transport commissioner should be abolished. The expenditure and salt-iron offices should be returned to the Secretariat, with the chief ministers each overseeing one of the six bureaus."
entries.literal: The various circuits' land-and-water transport commissioners, expenditure-review patrol offices, and Jianghuai transport commissioner should all be abolished. Return the expenditure and salt-iron affairs to the Secretariat, and let the chief ministers each oversee one of the six bureaus."

entries.zh: 於是齊映判兵部，李勉刑部，劉滋吏、禮二部，造戶、工二部；
entries.en: Accordingly Qi Ying took charge of the Bureau of War, Li Mian of Punishments, Liu Zi of Personnel and Rites, and Zao of Revenue and Public Works.
entries.literal: Thereupon Qi Ying oversaw the Bureau of War, Li Mian the Bureau of Punishments, Liu Zi the Bureaus of Personnel and Rites, and Zao the Bureaus of Revenue and Public Works.

entries.zh: 又以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒事，吉中孚度支諸道兩稅事。
entries.en: Yuan Xiu, Vice Director of Revenue, was also put in charge of salt, iron, and liquor monopolies for all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu was put in charge of the two-tax expenditure for all circuits.
entries.literal: Vice Director of Revenue Yuan Xiu was also assigned salt-iron and liquor monopoly affairs for all circuits, and Ji Zhongfu the expenditure affairs of all circuits' two-tax system.

entries.zh: 而浙江東、西歲入米七十五萬石，方歲饑，更以兩稅準米百萬，豪、壽、洪、潭二十萬，責韓滉杜亞漕送東渭橋。
entries.en: Zhejiang East and West had previously delivered 750,000 shi of grain each year. In a year of famine the quota was raised to the two-tax equivalent of one million shi, with Hao, Shou, Hong, and Tan together supplying 200,000. Han Huang and Du Ya were ordered to transport the grain by canal to Dongwei Bridge.
entries.literal: Zhejiang East and West had annually delivered 750,000 shi of grain. In a year of famine the quota was changed to a two-tax equivalent of 1,000,000 shi of grain, with Hao, Shou, Hong, and Tan contributing 200,000. Han Huang and Du Ya were charged to transport by canal to Dongwei Bridge.

entries.zh: 諸道有鹽鐵處，仍置巡院。
entries.en: In circuits where salt and iron were produced, patrol offices were still retained.
entries.literal: Where circuits had salt-iron [production], patrol offices were still established.

entries.zh: 歲盡，宰相計最殿以聞。
entries.en: At the end of the year the chief ministers calculated the best and worst results and reported them to the throne.
entries.literal: At year's end the chief ministers calculated best and worst grades and reported them.

entries.zh: 造厚元琇，故首命之。
entries.en: Zao was on close terms with Yuan Xiu and therefore gave him the leading appointment.
entries.literal: Zao was close to Yuan Xiu, and therefore appointed him first.

entries.zh: 時滉方領轉運，有寵於帝，朝廷仰其須。
entries.en: At the time Han Huang was still in charge of transport and enjoyed the emperor's favor; the court depended on him for supplies.
entries.literal: At the time Huang was just leading transport and was favored by the emperor; the court relied on his supplies.

entries.zh: 滉持不可改，帝重違之，復以滉滉為江淮轉運使，余如造請。
entries.en: Huang insisted the arrangement could not be changed. Unwilling to override him, the emperor restored Han Huang as Jianghuai transport commissioner, while the rest of the plan went forward as Zao had proposed.
entries.literal: Huang insisted the plan could not be changed. The emperor was reluctant to oppose him and restored Huang as Jianghuai transport commissioner; the rest followed as Zao had requested.

entries.zh: 是秋，江淮米大集，帝美滉功，以滉專領度支諸道鹽鐵、轉運等使。
entries.en: That autumn grain from the Jianghuai region poured in. The emperor praised Huang's achievement and put him in sole charge of expenditure, salt and iron, transport, and related offices for all circuits.
