entries.literal: That autumn Jianghuai grain assembled in great quantity. The emperor praised Huang's achievement and had Huang solely direct expenditure, all circuits' salt-iron affairs, transport, and other commissioners.

entries.zh: 造懼，始托疾辭位，乃罷為太子右庶子，貶琇雷州司戶參軍。
entries.en: Alarmed, Zao first pleaded illness to resign. He was removed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household, and Yuan Xiu was demoted to revenue officer of Lei Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zao feared this. He first pleaded illness to resign and was then dismissed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household; Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Lei Prefecture.

entries.zh: 於是造所請悉罷，以憂愧卒，年五十一。
entries.en: Everything Zao had proposed was then undone. He died of grief and shame at the age of fifty-one.
entries.literal: Thereupon all Zao had requested was abolished. He died of grief and shame at age fifty-one.

entries.zh: 議者謂造舉不適時，方用之乏，不能權濟大事，雖據舊典，奚能抗一切之制雲。
entries.en: Later critics said Zao's proposals came at the wrong moment: just when supplies were desperately needed, he could not maneuver flexibly on a matter of state. However sound his precedents, he was in no position to overturn a system that controlled everything.
entries.literal: Commentators said Zao's proposals were ill-timed—just when supplies were needed he could not flexibly manage great affairs. Though based on old precedents, how could he resist an all-controlling system?

entries.zh: 齊映，瀛州高陽人。
entries.en: Qi Ying was a native of Gaoyang in Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Qi Ying was a native of Gaoyang in Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 舉進士，博學宏詞，中之，補河南府參軍事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination and the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric examination, then was appointed military adjutant of Henan Prefecture.
entries.literal: He passed the Jinshi examination and the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric tests, and was appointed Henan Prefecture military adjutant.

entries.zh: 滑亳節度使令狐彰署掌書記，彰疾甚，引映托後事。
entries.en: Linghu Zhang, military commissioner of Hua and Bo, appointed him chief secretary. When Zhang fell gravely ill he entrusted his affairs after death to Ying.
entries.literal: Hua-Bo Military Commissioner Linghu Zhang appointed him chief secretary. When Zhang was gravely ill he entrusted Ying with affairs after his death.

entries.zh: 映因說彰納節，歸諸子京師。
entries.en: Ying then persuaded Zhang to surrender his command and send his sons to the capital.
entries.literal: Ying thereupon persuaded Zhang to surrender his commission and send his sons to the capital.

entries.zh: 彰從之，即以女妻映。
entries.en: Zhang agreed and gave Ying his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Zhang complied and gave his daughter to Ying in marriage.

entries.zh: 彰卒，軍亂，映間歸東都。
entries.en: When Zhang died the army mutinied, and Ying made his way back to the eastern capital.
entries.literal: When Zhang died the army mutinied, and Ying slipped away back to the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 三城使馬燧辟為判官。
entries.en: Ma Sui, commissioner of the Three Cities, recruited him as an administrative aide.
entries.literal: Three Cities Commissioner Ma Sui recruited him as administrative aide.

entries.zh: 盧杞薦授刑部員外郎。
entries.en: Lu Qi recommended him, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.
entries.literal: Lu Qi recommended him and he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.

entries.zh: 又為鳳翔張鎰判官。
entries.en: He later served as administrative aide to Zhang Yi in Fengxiang.
entries.literal: He also served as administrative aide to Zhang Yi of Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 映練軍事，論奏數稱旨，進行軍司馬。
entries.en: Ying was skilled in military affairs, and his memorials often pleased the emperor, who promoted him to army vice marshal.
entries.literal: Ying was versed in military affairs; his submitted discussions often pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Army Vice Marshal.

entries.zh: 會德宗出奉天，鎰儒緩不知兵，部將李楚琳者，素慓悍，欲介賊為亂。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Zhang Yi was a bookish man, slow-moving and ignorant of war. A subordinate general named Li Chulin was naturally fierce and unruly and wanted to join the rebels in raising trouble.
entries.literal: When Dezong fled to Fengtian, Yi was a Confucian, slow and ignorant of warfare. A subordinate general, Li Chulin, was by nature fierce and unruly and wished to collude with the rebels to raise disorder.

entries.zh: 映與齊抗請先事誅之，鎰不用，更示寬大，徐謂楚琳曰：「欲以君使外，若何？」
entries.en: Ying and Qi Kang urged that Chulin be killed first. Yi refused and instead tried a show of leniency, saying slowly to Chulin: "I would like to send you on assignment elsewhere. What do you say?"
entries.literal: Ying and Qi Kang asked to execute him preemptively. Yi did not adopt this, instead showing leniency, and slowly said to Chulin: "I wish to send you abroad on mission—what do you think?"

entries.zh: 楚琳恐，夜殺鎰以應賊，映雅為軍中慕賴，故得免。
entries.en: Chulin grew afraid. That night he killed Yi and went over to the rebels. Ying had long been respected and trusted in the army, and so he escaped unharmed.
entries.literal: Chulin feared this. By night he killed Yi to join the rebels. Ying had long been trusted and relied upon in the army, and therefore escaped harm.

entries.zh: 奔奉天，授御史中丞。
entries.en: He fled to Fengtian and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He fled to Fengtian and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 從幸梁，道險澀，常為帝禦。
entries.en: On the emperor's journey to Liang the road was dangerous and rough, and Ying constantly drove the carriage for him.
entries.literal: Following the emperor's journey to Liang, the road was treacherous and rough, and he constantly drove for the emperor.

entries.zh: 會馬駭突，帝恐傷映，詔舍轡，固不去，曰：「馬奔踶，不過傷臣；
entries.en: Once the horses bolted in fright. Fearing Ying would be hurt, the emperor told him to let go of the reins, but he refused to leave, saying: "If the horses rear and kick, they can hurt me at most.
entries.literal: When horses bolted in alarm the emperor feared Ying would be hurt and ordered him to drop the reins. He firmly would not leave, saying: "If the horses rear and kick, at most they injure your servant.

entries.zh: 舍之，或犯清蹕，臣雖死不中償責。」
entries.en: If I drop the reins they may break the imperial procession. Even if I die, that would not atone for such a fault."
entries.literal: If I abandon them they might violate the imperial procession—though your servant dies it would not repay the debt."

entries.zh: 帝嘉嘆，擢給事中。
entries.en: The emperor praised him warmly and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.
entries.literal: The emperor praised and sighed, and promoted him to Drafting Attendant.

entries.zh: 映為人白晰長大，言音鴻爽，故帝常令侍左右，或前馬臚傳詔旨。
entries.en: Ying was fair-complexioned, tall, and imposing, with a clear, ringing voice. The emperor therefore kept him close at hand and sometimes had him ride ahead as herald to proclaim edicts.
entries.literal: Ying was fair-skinned, tall, and large; his speech was resonant and clear. Therefore the emperor often had him attend at his side, sometimes riding ahead as herald to announce edicts.

entries.zh: 進中書舍人。
entries.en: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.

entries.zh: 貞元二年，以舍人同中書門下平章事，俄改中書侍郎，封河間縣男，與崔造、劉滋並輔政。
entries.en: In the second year of the Zhenyuan era he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as drafting officer. Soon he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Hejian County, and shared governance with Cui Zao and Liu Zi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, as drafting officer he became Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery. Soon he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Hejian County, and assisted in governance together with Cui Zao and Liu Zi.

entries.zh: 滋端重寡言，映謙不肯事否可，一顓於造。
entries.en: Liu Zi was grave and sparing of speech. Ying was deferential and unwilling to settle matters on his own; everything turned on Zao.
entries.literal: Zi was dignified and taciturn. Ying was modest and unwilling to decide yes or no—everything focused on Zao.

entries.zh: 會造疾，映乃當國。
entries.en: When Zao fell ill, Ying took charge of the government.
entries.literal: When Zao fell ill, Ying then controlled the state.

entries.zh: 吐蕃數入寇，關輔震騷，鹹言帝欲避狄。
entries.en: The Tibetans raided repeatedly, throwing the Guanzhong region into alarm, and rumor spread that the emperor meant to flee before the barbarians.
entries.literal: Tibet repeatedly raided inward; Guanfu was shaken with alarm, and everywhere it was said the emperor wished to flee the barbarians.

entries.zh: 映入諫曰：「戎狄不懲，臣之罪也。
entries.en: Ying went in to remonstrate, saying: "If the barbarians go unpunished, the fault is mine.
entries.literal: Ying entered to remonstrate, saying: "If the barbarians are not punished, it is your servant's fault.

entries.zh: 然內外恟恟，謂陛下具糗糧，欲治行。
entries.en: Yet inside and outside the court people are terrified, saying that Your Majesty has gathered provisions and is preparing to depart.
entries.literal: Yet inside and outside are panicked, saying Your Majesty has prepared dry rations and intends to set out on a journey.

entries.zh: 夫大幸不再，奈何不與臣等計乎？」
entries.en: Good fortune does not strike twice. Why not discuss this with us?"
entries.literal: Great fortune does not come twice—why not consult with your servants?"

entries.zh: 因俯伏流涕，天子為感寤。
entries.en: He then prostrated himself and wept, and the emperor was deeply moved.
entries.literal: He then prostrated himself weeping, and the Son of Heaven was moved to awakening.

entries.zh: 後給事中袁高忤帝旨，而映以為尚書左丞、御史大夫。
entries.en: Later, when Drafting Attendant Yuan Gao offended the emperor, Ying was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Later Drafting Attendant Yuan Gao offended the emperor's intent, and Ying was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 始，映微時，張延賞遇之善。
entries.en: In Ying's early days, when he was still unknown, Zhang Yanshang had treated him kindly.
entries.literal: Initially, when Ying was obscure, Zhang Yanshang treated him well.

entries.zh: 及映相，而延賞為左仆射，數為映畫事，又為所親求官，映不答，延賞恚。
entries.en: Once Ying became chief minister while Yanshang served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yanshang often drafted business for him and also asked favors for his friends. Ying gave no answer, and Yanshang grew furious.
entries.literal: When Ying became chief minister and Yanshang was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yanshang often drafted affairs for Ying and also sought offices for his intimates. Ying did not respond, and Yanshang was enraged.

entries.zh: 既復用，即劾映非宰相器。
entries.en: When Yanshang returned to power he at once impeached Ying as unfit for the chancellorship.
entries.literal: Once restored to power he immediately impeached Ying as unfit to be chief minister.

entries.zh: 明年，貶夔州刺史，徙衡州。
entries.en: The next year Ying was demoted to prefect of Kuizhou and later transferred to Hengzhou.
entries.literal: The next year [Ying] was demoted to Prefect of Kui Prefecture and then transferred to Heng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 久之，為桂管、江西兩觀察使。
entries.en: After some years he served as observation commissioner of Guiguan and Jiangxi.
entries.literal: After a long time he became observation commissioner of both Guiguan and Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 始，映罷不以罪，冀復進，乃掊斂獻貢，以中帝欲。
entries.en: At first Ying had not been dismissed for any crime, and he hoped to return to court. He therefore squeezed the region for tribute to satisfy the emperor's wishes.
entries.literal: Initially when Ying was dismissed it was not for crime; he hoped to advance again and therefore extorted and collected tribute to hit the emperor's desires.

entries.zh: 初，諸藩銀大瓶止五尺，李兼為江西，始獻六尺瓶，至映乃八尺雲。
entries.en: At first the great silver vases presented by the various prefectures were only five chi tall. When Li Jian governed Jiangxi he was the first to send six-chi vases; by Ying's time they had reached eight chi.
entries.literal: At first among the various prefectures silver great vases were only five chi. When Li Jian governed Jiangxi he first presented six-chi vases; by Ying's time they reached eight chi.

entries.zh: 卒，年四十八，贈禮部尚書，謚曰忠。
entries.en: He died at the age of forty-eight. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Zhong, "Loyal."
entries.literal: He died at age forty-eight. He was posthumously granted Minister of Rites; his posthumous name was Zhong.

entries.zh: 贊曰：楊綰之德，陸贄之賢，而袞、憬以為憎，何哉？
entries.en: The appraiser says: Yang Guan had virtue and Lu Zhi had talent—yet Chang Gun and Zhao Jing resented them. Why?
entries.literal: The appraiser says: Yang Guan's virtue, Lu Zhi's worthiness—yet Gun and Jing were jealous of them; why?

entries.zh: 士固蔽於娼前，然主聽不一，故乘以為奸。
entries.en: Scholars are indeed blinded before flatterers, but when the sovereign's ear is not single-minded, they seize the chance for treachery.
entries.literal: Scholars are indeed blinded before flatterers, but when the sovereign's hearing is not one, they therefore seize opportunity for treachery.

entries.zh: 昔齊桓、秦堅任管仲、王猛，興區區，霸天下，蓋不以不肖者參之。
entries.en: In former times Duke Huan of Qi and Emperor Jian of Qin entrusted Guan Zhong and Wang Meng. From a small realm each dominated the world, largely because they did not let unworthy men share in power.
entries.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi and Emperor Jian of Qin entrusted Guan Zhong and Wang Meng—with only a small realm they dominated the world, largely because they did not mix in the unworthy.

entries.zh: 君臣相諒，果難哉！
entries.en: For ruler and minister to trust each other in good faith—is it not truly hard!
entries.literal: For ruler and minister to trust each other in good faith—is it not truly hard!

entries.zh: 李常趙崔齊盧
entries.en: Li, Chang, Zhao, Cui, Qi, and Lu
entries.literal: Li, Chang, Zhao, Cui, Qi, Lu

entries.zh: 徐岱，字處仁，蘇州嘉興人，世農家子。
entries.en: Xu Dai, styled Churen, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou; his family had been farmers for generations.
entries.literal: Xu Dai, style name Churen, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou, from a farming family for generations.

entries.zh: 於學無所不通，辯論明銳，座人常屈。
entries.en: He mastered every branch of learning; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those who sat with him often yielded.
entries.literal: In learning there was nothing he did not master; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those seated with him often yielded.

entries.zh: 大歷中，劉晏表為校書郎。
entries.en: In the Dali era Liu Yan memorialized him as collator.
entries.literal: In the Dali era, Liu Yan memorialized him as collator.

entries.zh: 觀察使李棲筠欽其賢，署所居為「復禮鄉」。
entries.en: Observation commissioner Li Qiyun admired his virtue and designated the place where he lived as "Fuli Township."
entries.literal: Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun admired his virtue and designated his residence district as "Fuli Township" (Return to Rites).

entries.zh: 名達於朝，擢偃師尉。
entries.en: His fame reached the court and he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi.
entries.literal: His fame reached the court; he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi.

entries.zh: 禮儀使蔣鎮薦為太常博士，專掌禮事。
entries.en: Ritual commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, put in charge of ritual affairs.
entries.literal: Ritual Commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, exclusively overseeing ritual affairs.

entries.zh: 從德宗出奉天，以膳部員外郎兼博士。
entries.en: He followed Dezong to Fengtian and served as vice director of the Ministry of Court Revenues while also holding the doctorate.
entries.literal: He followed Dezong to Fengtian and served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Court Revenues, concurrently as doctor.

entries.zh: 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾
entries.en: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, and Yu
entries.literal: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu

entries.zh: 以兵部兼御史大夫，判度支。
entries.en: He served as Minister of War while also holding the post of Chief Censor and taking charge of the revenue commission.
entries.literal: As Minister of War he also served as Chief Censor with charge of the Commission for Public Revenue.

entries.zh: 王師討淮西，於陵用所親為供軍使，主唐、鄧，而高霞寓騰牒度支，以餉道乏。
entries.en: When imperial armies marched against Huai West, Yu Ling put a close associate in charge of army supplies for Tang and Deng prefectures. Gao Xiayu sent urgent dispatches to the revenue commission reporting that the supply lines were exhausted.
entries.literal: When imperial troops campaigned against Huai West, Yu Ling appointed a close associate as army supply commissioner in charge of Tang and Deng; Gao Xiayu sent urgent dispatches to the revenue commission complaining of exhausted supply routes.

entries.zh: 及戰敗，詔責之，指以為言。
entries.en: When the army was defeated, an edict censured him and cited this very matter as the cause.
entries.literal: When battle was lost, an edict held him responsible, citing this as the reason.

entries.zh: 帝怒，貶於陵郴州刺史。
entries.en: The emperor was enraged and demoted Yu Ling to prefect of Chenzhou.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Yu Ling to prefect of Chen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 徙原王傅，復以戶部侍郎知吏部選。
entries.en: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan and again served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of personnel selection.
entries.literal: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan and again served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of personnel selection.

entries.zh: 李師道平，詔宣慰淄青。
entries.en: After Li Shidao was pacified, an edict appointed Yu Ling commissioner of consolation to Zi and Qing.
entries.literal: When Li Shidao was suppressed, an edict ordered Yu Ling to console Zi and Qing.

entries.zh: 朝廷始議分其地，而劉悟節度滑州，未出鄆，於陵趣使上道。
entries.en: The court had just begun debating how to divide the territory. Liu Wu was military commissioner at Hua Prefecture but had not yet departed from Yan. Yu Ling pressed him to take to the road at once.
entries.literal: The court had begun discussing partition of the territory; Liu Wu held command at Hua Prefecture but had not yet left Yan. Yu Ling urged him to set out on the road.

entries.zh: 還奏，帝悅其能。
entries.en: When he returned and reported, the emperor was pleased with his competence.
entries.literal: On returning he reported; the emperor was pleased with his capability.

entries.zh: 會浙西觀察使李閹死，皇甫镈素忌於陵，薦以代翛，帝不之可。
entries.en: When Li Yan, observation commissioner of Zhexi, died, Huangfu Bo—who had long resented Yu Ling—recommended him as replacement. The emperor did not agree.
entries.literal: When observation commissioner Li Yan of Zhexi died, Huangfu Bo, who had long resented Yu Ling, recommended him to replace Xiao; the emperor did not approve.

entries.zh: 穆宗立，遷戶部尚書，為東都留守。
entries.en: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Yu Ling was promoted to Minister of Revenue and appointed garrison commissioner of the eastern capital.
entries.literal: When Muzong acceded, Yu Ling was promoted to Minister of Revenue and made eastern capital garrison commissioner.

entries.zh: 數上疏乞身，不許。
entries.en: He repeatedly memorialized asking to retire, but permission was not granted.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 授太子少傅，封弘農郡公。
entries.en: He was appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong Commandery.
entries.literal: He was granted Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong Commandery.

entries.zh: 俄以尚書左仆射致仕，詔賜實俸，讓不受。
entries.en: Before long he retired with the title Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. An edict granted him his full salary, but he declined to accept it.
entries.literal: Soon he retired as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; an edict granted him full salary but he declined to accept it.

entries.zh: 於陵器量方峻，進止有常度，節操堅明，始終不失其正，時人尊仰之。
entries.en: Yu Ling was stern and upright in bearing, measured in all he did, and firm and clear in integrity. He never lost his rectitude from first to last, and his contemporaries honored and revered him.
entries.literal: Yu Ling's bearing was stern and square; his conduct had constant measure; his integrity was firm and bright; from beginning to end he never lost his rectitude; contemporaries honored and looked up to him.

entries.zh: 太和四年卒，年七十八。
entries.en: He died in the fourth year of Taihe (830), at the age of seventy-eight.
entries.literal: He died in the fourth year of Taihe, aged seventy-eight.

entries.zh: 冊贈司空，謚曰貞孝。
entries.en: He was posthumously invested as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Upright and Filial.
entries.literal: Posthumously invested as Grand Tutor; posthumous epithet Zhenxiao (Upright and Filial).

entries.zh: 孔穆崔柳楊馬
entries.en: The Kong, Mu, Cui, Liu, Yang, and Ma Clans
entries.literal: Kong, Mu, Cui, Liu, Yang, and Ma

entries.zh: 王播，字明敭，其先太原人。
entries.en: Wang Bo, styled Mingyang, came from a Taiyuan family.
entries.literal: Wang Bo, styled Mingyang, his ancestors were men of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 父恕為揚州倉曹參軍，遂家焉。
entries.en: His father Shu served as grain-store aide in Yang Prefecture, and the family settled there.
entries.literal: His father Shu served as grain-store aide of Yangzhou, and there the family settled.

entries.zh: 播，貞元中與弟炎、起皆有名，並擢進士，而播、起舉賢良方正異等。
entries.en: During the Zhenyuan era Bo, together with his younger brothers Yan and Qi, all won renown; all three passed the jinshi examination, and Bo and Qi were also selected in the exceptional grade of the Worthy and Upright examination.
entries.literal: Bo, in the Zhenyuan era, together with his younger brothers Yan and Qi all had fame; all passed the jinshi examination, and Bo and Qi were also raised in the exceptional grade of Worthy and Upright.

entries.zh: 補盩厔尉。
entries.en: He was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi County.
entries.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zhouzhi.

entries.zh: 以善治獄，御史中丞李汶薦為監察御史。
entries.en: Because he was skilled at handling legal cases, Censor-in-Chief Li Wen recommended him for appointment as investigating censor.
entries.literal: Because he was skilled at handling cases, the censor-in-chief Li Wen recommended him as investigating censor.

entries.zh: 雲陽丞源咸季坐賕免，賂有司復得調，播劾解其官。
entries.en: Yuan Xianji, assistant magistrate of Yunyang, had been dismissed for bribery but bribed the relevant offices and secured a new appointment; Bo impeached him and had him removed from office.
entries.literal: The assistant magistrate of Yunyang, Yuan Xianji, was removed from office for bribery, bribed the relevant offices and again obtained reassignment, and Bo impeached him and stripped him of his post.

entries.zh: 歷侍御史。
entries.en: He later served as attendant censor.
entries.literal: He served successively as attendant censor.

entries.zh: 李實為京兆尹，與播遇諸衢。
entries.en: Li Shi was serving as intendant of the capital district when he encountered Bo in the street.
entries.literal: Li Shi was Jingzhao intendant, and he met Bo in the streets.

entries.zh: 故事，尹當避道揖，實不肯。
entries.en: By precedent the intendant was supposed to yield the road and bow, but Shi refused.
entries.literal: By precedent the intendant should yield the road and bow, but Shi would not.

entries.zh: 播移文詆之。
entries.en: Bo sent an official dispatch denouncing him.
entries.literal: Bo sent a dispatch denouncing him.

entries.zh: 實大怒，表播為三原令，將折之，播受命，趨府謝如禮。
entries.en: Shi flew into a rage and had Bo transferred to the post of magistrate of Sanyuan, intending to humiliate him; Bo accepted the appointment and promptly went to the intendant's office to pay his respects according to protocol.
entries.literal: Shi was greatly angered, memorialized to appoint Bo magistrate of Sanyuan intending to break him, Bo accepted the order, and hurried to the office to pay thanks according to ritual.

entries.zh: 邑中豪強犯法，未嘗輒貸，歲終課最。
entries.en: He never readily pardoned powerful local offenders, and at year's end his performance ranked first.
entries.literal: When powerful men in the district violated the law, he never readily pardoned them, and at year's end his assessment ranked highest.

entries.zh: 實重其才，更薦之，德宗將擢以要近，會母喪解。
entries.en: Shi came to respect his ability and recommended him again; Emperor Dezong was about to promote him to an important post at court when the death of his mother forced him to leave office.
entries.literal: Shi valued his talent and recommended him again; Dezong was about to promote him to an important nearby post when his mother's death obliged him to resign.

entries.zh: 還，除駕部員外郎。
entries.en: When he returned to service he was appointed outer-office member of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages.
entries.literal: When he returned he was appointed outer-office member of the Directorate of Imperial Carriages.

entries.zh: 長安令于頔奴客與民盜馬，吏系民而縱奴，播捕取，均其罰。
entries.en: A slave-guest of Yu Di, magistrate of Chang'an, and a commoner stole horses together; officials detained the commoner but let the slave go free, so Bo arrested both and imposed equal penalties.
entries.literal: The magistrate of Chang'an, Yu Di's slave-guest and a commoner stole horses; officials detained the commoner but released the slave, and Bo seized and punished both, equalizing their penalties.

entries.zh: 遷工部郎中，知御史雜事。
entries.en: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works and put in charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of Works and given charge of miscellaneous censorial affairs.

entries.zh: 刺舉不阿，有能稱。
entries.en: In investigation and impeachment he never bent to favor, and he won a reputation for ability.
entries.literal: In investigation and impeachment he did not bend, and he had a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 關中饑，諸鎮或閉糴，播以為言，三輔不乏。
entries.en: When Guanzhong suffered famine and some garrison commands hoarded grain by closing sales, Bo protested, and the Three Adjuncts did not go wanting.
entries.literal: Guanzhong suffered famine; some garrison commands closed grain sales, Bo spoke out against this, and the Three Adjuncts did not lack provisions.

entries.zh: 歷虢州刺史。
entries.en: He later served as prefect of Guo Prefecture.
entries.literal: He served successively as prefect of Guozhou.

entries.zh: 炎終太常博士。
entries.en: Yan ended as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Yan ended as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 子鐸、鐐自有傳。
entries.en: His sons Duo and Liao have their own biographies.
entries.literal: His sons Duo and Liao have their own biographies.

entries.zh: 起子龜、式。
entries.en: Qi's sons Gui and Shi.
entries.literal: Qi's sons Gui and Shi.

entries.zh: 白裴崔韋二李皇甫王
entries.en: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, the two Lis, Huangfu, and Wang
entries.literal: Bai, Pei, Cui, Wei, two Li's, Huangfu, Wang

entries.zh: 子逢，從父征伐，累功署忠武都知兵馬使。
entries.en: His son Feng campaigned with him, won repeated honors, and was appointed overall commander of the Zhongwu army.
entries.literal: His son Feng followed his father in campaigns, accumulated merit, and was appointed overall commander of Zhongwu military affairs.

entries.zh: 太和中，入為諸衛將軍。
entries.en: During the Taihe era he entered court service as a guard general.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era he entered court as a general of the guard regiments.

entries.zh: 從劉沔、石雄破回鶻於天德，有士二千人未嘗戰，欲冒賞賜，逢不與。
entries.en: He followed Liu Mian and Shi Xiong in defeating the Uyghurs at Tiande; two thousand men who had never fought demanded rewards anyway, and Feng refused.
entries.literal: Following Liu Mian and Shi Xiong he defeated the Uyghurs at Tiande; there were two thousand soldiers who had never fought yet wished to claim rewards fraudulently — Feng would not grant them.

entries.zh: 或為請之，答曰：「士奮死取賞，若無功而賞，何哉？」
entries.en: When others interceded for them he replied, "Men risk death for reward — what becomes of discipline if the idle are paid?"
entries.literal: Some pleaded for them; he answered: "Soldiers strive to death to win reward — if without merit there is reward, what then?"

entries.zh: 武宗以逢用法嚴，使宰相李德裕讓之，逢曰：「戰者，前踏白刃，不以法，人孰用命？」
entries.en: Emperor Wuzong, finding Feng too strict, had Chancellor Li Deyu rebuke him. Feng answered, "In battle men face naked steel — without discipline, who will give his life?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wuzong, because Feng applied the law strictly, had Chancellor Li Deyu reprove him. Feng said: "In battle one treads before naked blades — without law, who will stake his life?"

entries.zh: 討劉稹也，為太原道行營將，領陳許兵七千屯翼城。
entries.en: In the campaign against Liu Zhen he served on the Taiyuan front, leading seven thousand Chen-Xu troops at Yicheng.
entries.literal: Campaigning against Liu Zhen, he was a Taiyuan circuit field camp general, leading seven thousand Chen-Xu troops encamped at Yicheng.

entries.zh: 稹平，加檢校右散騎常侍。
entries.en: After Zhen's defeat he was made acting Right Gentleman for Casual Conversation.
entries.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was made acting Right Gentleman for Casual Conversation.

entries.zh: 後亦至忠武節度使雲。
entries.en: He later also rose to military commissioner of Zhongwu.
entries.literal: Later he also reached the post of Zhongwu military commissioner.

entries.zh: 劉稹阻命，詔沔南討，屯榆社。
entries.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled Mian was ordered south and encamped at Yushe.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen defied orders; an edict ordered Mian south to campaign and encamp at Yushe.

entries.zh: 沔素與張仲武不協，時方追幽州兵，故徙義成。
entries.en: Mian had long been at odds with Zhang Zhongwu; with Youzhou forces in pursuit he was shifted to Yicheng.
entries.literal: Mian had long been at odds with Zhang Zhongwu; at the time they were pursuing Youzhou troops, and therefore he was transferred to Yicheng.

entries.zh: 會王宰逗留，宰相李德裕表沔鎮河陽，以滑兵二千壁萬善，居宰肘腋下，激之俾出軍。
entries.en: When Wang Zai stalled, Li Deyu had Mian posted at Heyang with two thousand Hua troops at Wanshan to press Zai from the rear and force him forward.
entries.literal: It happened that Wang Zai lingered; Chancellor Li Deyu memorialized that Mian garrison Heyang, with two thousand Hua troops fortify Wanshan, sit under Zai's armpit, and stir him to make the army advance.

entries.zh: 稹平，進檢校司徒，徙忠武節度使。
entries.en: After Zhen's defeat he was promoted to acting Minister of Education and made commissioner of Zhongwu.
entries.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was advanced to acting Minister of Education and transferred to military commissioner of Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 以病改太子少保，不任謁，拜太子太傅致仕。
entries.en: Illness forced him to become Junior Guardian; unable to attend court he was named Grand Tutor and retired.
entries.literal: Because of illness he was changed to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, could not perform audiences, and was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

entries.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈司徒。
entries.en: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.
entries.literal: He died at age sixty-five and was posthumously made Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 武寧李彥佐討劉稹逗留，以雄為晉絳行營諸軍副使，助彥佐。
entries.en: When Li Yanzhuo of Wuning stalled in the campaign against Liu Zhen, Xiong was named vice commander of the Jin-Jiang field armies to assist him.
entries.literal: Li Yanzhuo of Wuning, campaigning against Liu Zhen, lingered; Xiong was made vice commander of the Jin-Jiang field camp armies to assist Yanzhuo.

entries.zh: 是時，王宰屯萬善，劉沔屯石會關，顧望莫先進。
entries.en: Wang Zai held Wanshan and Liu Mian held Shihui Pass; both hung back, neither willing to advance.
entries.literal: At this time Wang Zai encamped at Wanshan, Liu Mian at Shihui Pass; they looked about and none advanced first.

entries.zh: 雄受命，即勒兵越烏嶺，破賊五壁，斬獲千計，賊大震。
entries.en: Xiong took command at once, crossed Wuling, stormed five rebel forts, killed and captured by the thousands, and threw the enemy into panic.
entries.literal: Xiong received the order and immediately drove the army over Wuling, broke five rebel ramparts, beheaded and captured by the thousands, and the rebels were greatly shaken.

entries.zh: 雄臨財廉，每朝廷賜與，輒置軍門，自取一匹縑，余悉分士伍，由是眾感發，無不奮。
entries.en: Scrupulous with money, he placed every imperial gift at the camp gate, kept one bolt of silk for himself, and gave the rest to his men; the army was moved to fight with all their might.
entries.literal: Xiong in handling wealth was frugal; whenever the court bestowed gifts he placed them at the army gate, took for himself one bolt of silk, and distributed all the rest among the soldiers; from this the masses were moved and stirred, and none did not strive.

entries.zh: 武宗喜曰：「今將帥義而勇罕雄比者。」
entries.en: Emperor Wuzong said with delight, "Among today's commanders for loyalty and courage, few can match Xiong."
entries.literal: Wuzong said with pleasure: "Among commanders today who are righteous and brave, few can be compared with Xiong."

entries.zh: 就拜行營節度使，代彥佐。
entries.en: He was immediately made field camp commissioner, replacing Yanzhuo.
entries.literal: He was immediately appointed field camp military commissioner, replacing Yanzhuo.

entries.zh: 徙河中。
entries.en: He was transferred to Hedong.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Hedong.

entries.zh: 稹危蹙，其大將郭誼密獻款，請斬稹首自歸。
entries.en: Zhen was cornered; his general Guo Yi secretly offered surrender, promising to kill Zhen and submit.
entries.literal: Zhen was in dire straits; his great general Guo Yi secretly offered allegiance, requesting to behead Zhen and return in submission.

entries.zh: 眾疑其詐，雄大言曰：「稹之叛，誼為謀主。
entries.en: Some suspected a trick; Xiong declared, "Yi was the chief architect of Zhen's rebellion.
entries.literal: The masses suspected deception; Xiong spoke loudly: "In Zhen's rebellion Yi was the chief plotter.

entries.zh: 今欲殺稹，乃誼自謀，又何疑？」
entries.en: If he now wants Zhen dead, that is his own scheme — why doubt him?"
entries.literal: Now wishing to kill Zhen is Yi's own plot — what is there to doubt?"

entries.zh: 雄以七千人徑薄潞，受誼降。
entries.en: Xiong took seven thousand men straight to Lu and accepted Yi's surrender.
entries.literal: Xiong with seven thousand men pressed straight on Lu and accepted Yi's surrender.

entries.zh: 進檢校兵部尚書，徙河陽。
entries.en: He was promoted to acting Minister of War and transferred to Heyang.
entries.literal: He was advanced to acting Minister of War and transferred to Heyang.

entries.zh: 初，雄討稹，水次見白鷺，謂眾曰：「使吾射中其目，當成功。」
entries.en: Early in the campaign against Zhen he saw a white egret by the river and told his men, "If I hit its eye, we will win."
entries.literal: At first, when Xiong campaigned against Zhen, by the water he saw a white egret and told the masses: "If I shoot and hit its eye, we shall succeed."

entries.zh: 一發如言。
entries.en: One shot struck true.
entries.literal: With one shot it was as he said.

entries.zh: 帝聞，下詔褒美。
entries.en: The emperor heard and issued an edict of praise.
entries.literal: The emperor heard and issued an edict praising him.

entries.zh: 李烏王楊曹高劉石
entries.en: Li, Wu, Wang, Yang, Cao, Gao, Liu, and Shi
entries.literal: Li, Wu, Wang, Yang, Cao, Gao, Liu, Shi

entries.zh: 討劉稹也，詔宰以兵出魏博，趨磁州。
entries.en: During the campaign against Liu Zhen, the emperor ordered Zai to march from Weibo toward Cizhou at the head of his troops.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhen was being suppressed, an edict ordered Zai to lead troops out from Weibo and advance on Cizhou.

entries.zh: 當是時，何弘敬陰首鼠，聞宰至，大懼，即引軍濟漳水。
entries.en: He Hongjing was then hedging his bets in secret; when he learned Zai was coming he panicked and at once crossed the Zhang River with his army.
entries.literal: At that time He Hongjing secretly wavered like a rat; hearing Zai had arrived, he was greatly afraid and immediately led his army across the Zhang River.

entries.zh: 宰相李德裕建言：「河陽兵寡，以忠武為援，既以捍洛，則並制魏博。」
entries.en: The chief minister Li Deyu argued: "Heyang's garrison is thin; Zhongwu should reinforce it—protect Luoyang and Weibo falls into our grip as well."
entries.literal: Chief minister Li Deyu offered counsel: "Heyang has few troops; use Zhongwu as reinforcement—once Luoyang is shielded, Weibo can be controlled together."

entries.zh: 遂詔宰以兵五千椎鋒，兼統河陽行營。
entries.en: The emperor accordingly put Zai at the head of five thousand shock troops and gave him overall command of the Heyang field camp.
entries.literal: An edict then ordered Zai with five thousand troops as the vanguard and concurrently to command the Heyang field headquarters.

entries.zh: 進取天井關，賊黨離沮。
entries.en: He seized Tianjing Pass, and the rebel host broke apart in discouragement.
entries.literal: He advanced and took Tianjing Pass; the rebels' partisans scattered in dismay.

entries.zh: 德裕以宰乘破竹勢不遂取澤州，以其子晏實守磁，為顧望計，帝有詔切責。
entries.en: Zai had the momentum of a bamboo split wide open yet stalled before Zezhou while his son Yan Shi guarded Cizhou—a feint of hesitation—and the emperor sent down a stern rebuke.
entries.literal: Because Zai, though pressing with irresistible momentum, did not promptly seize Zezhou—his son Yan Shi holding Cizhou as a scheme of watchful delay—the emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking him.

entries.zh: 宰懼，急攻陵川，破賊石會關，進攻澤州。
entries.en: Frightened, Zai rushed to assault Lingchuan, stormed the rebel strongpoint at Shihui Pass, and pressed the attack on Zezhou.
entries.literal: Zai was afraid; he urgently attacked Lingchuan, broke the rebel Shi Hui Pass, and advanced to attack Zezhou.

entries.zh: 其將郭誼殺稹降。
entries.en: His subordinate Guo Yi killed Liu Zhen and capitulated.
entries.literal: His general Guo Yi killed Zhen and surrendered.

entries.zh: 宰傳稹首京師，遂節度太原。
entries.en: Zai forwarded Liu Zhen's head to the capital and was appointed military governor of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Zai sent Zhen's head to the capital and was then made military governor of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 晏實幼機警，智興自養之，故名與諸父齒。
entries.en: Yan Shi was quick-witted from boyhood; Zhixing personally reared him, so his name was placed among those of his uncles.
entries.literal: Yan Shi was clever and alert from childhood; Zhixing raised him himself, and therefore his given name ranks with those of his paternal uncles.

entries.zh: 稹平，擢淄州刺史，終天雄節度使。
entries.en: After Liu Zhen's defeat he was elevated to prefect of Zizhou and eventually finished his career as military governor of Tianxiong.
entries.literal: When Zhen was pacified he was promoted to prefect of Zizhou and ended as military governor of Tianxiong.

entries.zh: 亞自以當衡柄，悒悒不悅。
entries.en: Ya believed himself destined for the chancellorship and brooded in dissatisfaction.
entries.literal: Ya considered himself fit for the scales of power and was sullen and displeased.

entries.zh: 李棲筠風望高，時謂當宰相，故亞厚結納。
entries.en: Li Qiyun commanded high esteem and was widely tipped for the chancellery—Ya drew him into a warm alliance.
entries.literal: Li Qiyun's reputation stood high; contemporaries said he would become chief minister, and therefore Ya cultivated a close bond with him.

entries.zh: 元載得罪，亞與劉晏等劾治。
entries.en: When Yuan Zai was brought down, Ya stood with Liu Yan and others to impeach and try him.
entries.literal: When Yuan Zai fell from grace, Ya joined Liu Yan and others in impeaching and prosecuting him.

entries.zh: 載死，遷給事中。
entries.en: After Zai's death he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
entries.literal: When Zai died, Ya was transferred to Supervising Censor.

entries.zh: 常袞惡之，出為江西觀察使。
entries.en: Chang Gun, who despised him, had him posted as observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Chang Gun disliked him and sent him out as observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 德宗立，召還。
entries.en: Dezong's accession brought his recall to court.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was recalled.

entries.zh: 亞意必任臺宰，倍道進。
entries.en: Convinced he would be named chief minister, Ya hastened toward the capital at breakneck pace.
entries.literal: Ya was certain he would be appointed to the highest office of the secretariat and traveled at double speed.

entries.zh: 與人語，皆天下大政。
entries.en: Every conversation he held turned on the grand policies of the empire.
entries.literal: In speaking with people, all his topics were great affairs of the realm.

entries.zh: 或以事祈謁，輒相然可。
entries.en: Whoever came to him with a request invariably won his ready assent.
entries.literal: When someone came to petition him on some matter, he would invariably agree.

entries.zh: 帝知，不悅也。
entries.en: When the emperor learned of it, he was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor learned of this and was displeased.

entries.zh: 既又建奏疏闊，不稱旨，罷為陜虢觀察兼轉運使。
entries.en: His memorials grew diffuse and missed the mark; he was removed and made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo with concurrent charge of transport.
entries.literal: Moreover his memorials were broad and loose and did not suit the emperor's intent; he was dismissed and made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo and concurrently transport commissioner.

entries.zh: 徙河中。
entries.en: He was transferred to Hezhong.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Hezhong.

entries.zh: 劉晏抵罪，貶睦州刺史。
entries.en: When Liu Yan fell, Ya was demoted to prefect of Muzhou.
entries.literal: When Liu Yan was convicted, Ya was demoted to prefect of Muzhou.

entries.zh: 于王二杜範
entries.en: Yu, Wang, the two members of the Du clan, and Fan
entries.literal: Yu, Wang, the two Du's, and Fan

entries.zh: 會昭義監軍劉承偕慢劉悟，舉軍嘩怒，執承偕，悟拘以聞。
entries.en: The Zhaoyi army supervisor Liu Chengxie insulted Liu Wu. The whole army rose in uproar, seized Chengxie, and Wu reported the matter under restraint.
entries.literal: It happened that Zhaoyi army supervisor Liu Chengxie slighted Liu Wu; the whole army clamored in anger, seized Chengxie, and Wu detained him to report.

entries.zh: 帝怒，問度：「何施而可？」
entries.en: The emperor was furious and asked Du, "What can be done?"
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and asked Du: "What measure will do?"

entries.zh: 度頓首謝：「籓臣不與政。」
entries.en: Du kowtowed and declined. "A frontier minister does not meddle in central government."
entries.literal: Du knocked his head and declined: "A frontier minister does not participate in government."

entries.zh: 辭不對。
entries.en: He refused to answer.
entries.literal: He declined and did not answer.

entries.zh: 帝強之，度曰：「臣素知承偕怙寵，悟不能堪，嘗以書訴臣。
entries.en: The emperor pressed him. Du said, "I have long known Chengxie abused imperial favor and that Wu could not endure it. Wu once wrote to me to complain.
entries.literal: The emperor pressed him; Du said: "Your servant has long known Chengxie relied on favor, and Wu could not bear it—he once complained to your servant in a letter.

entries.zh: 是時，中人趙弘亮在行營知狀，欲持悟書以奏，陛下亦知之邪？」
entries.en: At that time the eunuch Zhao Hongliang at headquarters knew the facts and meant to present Wu's letter. Did Your Majesty know of this?"
entries.literal: At that time the inner eunuch Zhao Hongliang at the field headquarters knew the situation and wished to take Wu's letter to memorialize—does Your Majesty also know of this?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「我不及知。
entries.en: The emperor said, "I did not know.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I did not come to know of it.

entries.zh: 顧悟誠惡之，胡不自聞，何哉？」
entries.en: If Wu truly hated him, why did he not report it himself?"
entries.literal: Yet if Wu truly hated him, why did he not himself report—how so?"

entries.zh: 度曰：「雖悟得聞，恐陛下不必聽。
entries.en: Du said, "Even if Wu had reported it, I fear Your Majesty might not have listened.
entries.literal: Du said: "Though Wu could have it heard, I fear Your Majesty would not necessarily listen.

entries.zh: 且臣視天顏不咫尺，比尚未能決，千里單言，可悟聖聽哉？」
entries.en: Besides, I stand before Your Majesty face to face and still cannot always win a decision. How could a lone report from a thousand li away reach your ears?"
entries.literal: Moreover your servant views the heavenly countenance not a foot away—just now he still could not decide; a thousand li away with a single word, could it awaken the sage ear?"

entries.zh: 帝亟曰：「前語姑置，直謂今日奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor said urgently, "Leave that aside. Tell me plainly what to do today."
entries.literal: The emperor urgently said: "Set aside the earlier words for now—speak directly: what of today?"

entries.zh: 度曰：「必欲收忠義心，使帥臣死節，獨斬承偕，則四方群盜隱然破膽矣。」
entries.en: Du said, "If you wish to win loyal hearts and make commanders die for their duty, execute Chengxie alone. Rebels everywhere will lose their nerve at once."
entries.literal: Du said: "If you must win loyal and righteous hearts and make commanders die for principle, execute Chengxie alone, and the bandits everywhere will inwardly have their courage broken."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「顧太后養為子，且我何愛？
entries.en: The emperor said, "The empress dowager raised him as her son. What do I owe him?
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Considering the empress dowager raised him as a son, what love do I have for him?

entries.zh: 更言其次。」
entries.en: Tell me the next option."
entries.literal: Speak of the next option."

entries.zh: 度曰：「投諸荒裔可乎？」
entries.en: Du said, "Could he be exiled to the frontier?"
entries.literal: Du said: "Cast him to the wild borderlands—would that do?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「可。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Yes."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "It will do."

entries.zh: 悟果出承偕，昭義遂安。
entries.en: Wu released Chengxie, and Zhaoyi was pacified.
entries.literal: Wu indeed released Chengxie, and Zhaoyi was thereby settled.

entries.zh: 長慶四年，王廷湊屠元翼之家，敬宗嗟惋，歎宰輔非其人，使凶賊熾肆。
entries.en: In 824 Wang Tingcou massacred Niu Yuanji's household. Emperor Jingzong sighed in grief and lamented that his chief ministers were unworthy men who had let vicious rebels run wild.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing, Wang Tingcou slaughtered Yuanji's household; Jingzong sighed in regret and lamented that the chief ministers were not the right men, allowing fierce rebels to blaze unchecked.

entries.zh: 學士韋處厚上疏曰：「臣聞汲黯在朝，淮南寢謀；
entries.en: Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou memorialized, "I have heard that while Ji An held court office, Huainan abandoned its plots;
entries.literal: Academician Wei Chuhou sent up a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that with Ji An at court, Huainan laid its plots to rest;

entries.zh: 干木處魏，諸侯息兵。
entries.en: and while Gan Mu served in Wei, the feudal lords laid down their arms.
entries.literal: with Gan Mu in Wei, the feudal lords ceased arms.

entries.zh: 王霸之理，以一士止百萬之師，一賢制千里之難。
entries.en: The principle of true kingship is that one worthy man can halt an army of a million and master trouble across a thousand li.
entries.literal: The principle of true kingship and hegemony is that one scholar stops an army of a million, one worthy controls difficulty for a thousand li.

entries.zh: 裴度元勳巨德，文武兼備，若位岩廟，委參決，必使戎虜畏威，幽、鎮自臣。
entries.en: Pei Du is a founding minister of great virtue, skilled in both civil and military affairs. If he were placed at the summit of government and entrusted with decisions, barbarians would fear our might and You and Zhen would submit of themselves.
entries.literal: Pei Du has original merit and great virtue, combining civil and military; if placed in the lofty temple and entrusted with deliberation and decision, he will surely make barbarian enemies fear his awesomeness, and You and Zhen will submit of themselves.

entries.zh: 管仲曰：'人離而聽之則愚，合而聽之則聖。
entries.en: Guan Zhong said, 'Listen to men separately and you will be foolish; listen to them together and you will be wise.'
entries.literal: Guan Zhong said: 'If men are apart and one listens, one is foolish; if one listens together, one is sage.'

entries.zh: '治亂之本，非有他術。
entries.en: The root of order and disorder lies in nothing else.
entries.literal: The root of order and disorder has no other art.

entries.zh: 陛下當饋而歎，恨無蕭、曹，今一裴度擯棄於外，所以馮唐知漢文帝有頗、牧不能用也。」
entries.en: Your Majesty sighs at table, lamenting the lack of men like Xiao He and Cao Shen. Yet Pei Du alone has been cast aside. This is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han possessed generals like Lian Po and Li Mu yet could not use them."
entries.literal: Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen; now a single Pei Du is cast aside outside—this is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han had Lian Po and Li Mu yet could not employ them."

entries.zh: 帝感悟，謂處厚曰：「度累為宰相，而官無平章事，謂何？」
entries.en: The emperor was moved and asked Chuhou, "Du has served repeatedly as chief minister, yet his title lacks grand councillor. What does that mean?"
entries.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding and said to Chuhou: "Du has repeatedly been chief minister, yet his office lacks grand councillor—what does this mean?"

entries.zh: 處厚具道其由，帝於是復度兼平章事。
entries.en: Chuhou explained the whole story, and the emperor restored Du as grand councillor.
entries.literal: Chuhou fully explained the reason; the emperor thereupon restored Du to concurrent grand councillor.

entries.zh: 帝雖孺蒙，然注意度，中人至度所，必丁甯尉安，且示召期。
entries.en: Though the emperor was young and inexperienced, he kept his eye on Du. Whenever eunuchs visited Du's residence they reassured him and hinted when he would be recalled.
entries.literal: Though the emperor was young and unlearned, he nevertheless paid attention to Du; when inner eunuchs came to Du's place they were sure to comfort and reassure him and also show the date of summons.

entries.zh: 寶曆二年，度請入朝，逢吉黨大懼，權輿作偽謠云：「非衣小兒坦其腹，天上有口被驅逐。」
entries.en: In 826 Du petitioned to return to court. Fengji's faction was terrified. Zhang Quanyu forged a prophecy: "The child in plain clothes bares his belly; the mouth in heaven is driven away."
entries.literal: In the second year of Baoli, Du requested to enter court; Fengji's faction was greatly afraid; Quanyu fabricated a false rhyme saying: "Not-clothes, small child, belly exposed; heaven above has a mouth and is driven away."

entries.zh: 以度平元濟也。
entries.en: It alluded to Du's pacification of Wu Yuanji.
entries.literal: This referred to Du's pacification of Yuanji.

entries.zh: 都城東西岡六，民間以為乾數，而度第平樂裏，直第五岡。
entries.en: Six ridges lay east and west of the capital, which folk associated with the qian hexagram. Du's house in Pingle Ward stood directly on the fifth ridge.
entries.literal: East and west of the capital were six ridges, which the people took as the qian number; Du's residence was in Pingle Ward, directly on the fifth ridge.

entries.zh: 權輿乃言：「度名應圖讖，第據岡原，不召而來，其意可見。」
entries.en: Quanyu then said, "Du's name fulfills a prophecy. His house occupies the sacred ridge. He comes without being summoned. His intent is obvious."
entries.literal: Quanyu then said: "Du's name answers chart prophecies; his residence occupies the ridge plain; without summons he comes—his intent can be seen."

entries.zh: 欲以傾度。
entries.en: He meant to destroy Du with this.
entries.literal: He wished thereby to topple Du.

entries.zh: 天子獨能明其誣，詔復使輔政。
entries.en: The emperor alone saw through the slander and ordered Du restored to the chancellorship.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven alone could make clear the slander and ordered him again to assist in government.

entries.zh: 識，字通理，性敏悟，凡經目未始忘。
entries.en: Shi, styled Tongli, was quick-witted and never forgot anything he read.
entries.literal: Shi, courtesy name Tongli, was by nature keen and perceptive; whatever passed his eyes he never forgot.

entries.zh: 推廕補京兆參軍，擢累大理少卿。
entries.en: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a Capital staff officer and rose to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was supplemented as staff officer of the capital metropolis, was selected and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 王師討劉稹，為供軍使。
entries.en: When the court campaigned against Liu Zhen, he served as army supply commissioner.
entries.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Liu Zhen, he was supply commissioner.

entries.zh: 稹平，改司農卿，進湖南觀察使。
entries.en: After Zhen fell he was made Minister of Agriculture, then Hunan governor.
entries.literal: When Zhen was pacified, he was changed to Minister of Agriculture and advanced to Hunan observation commissioner.

entries.zh: 入拜大理卿，襲晉國公半封。
entries.en: He returned to court as chief of the Court of Judicial Review and inherited half his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Jin.
entries.literal: He entered court as chief of the Court of Judicial Review and inherited half the enfeoffment of Duke of Jin.

entries.zh: 為涇原節度使。
entries.en: He was appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan.
entries.literal: He was made military commissioner of Jingyuan.

entries.zh: 裴度子:識 諗
entries.en: Pei Du's sons were Shi and Shen.
entries.literal: Pei Du's sons: Shi and Shen.

entries.zh: 鎮州亂，殺田弘正而立王廷湊，詔愈宣撫。
entries.en: Zhenzhou rose in revolt, killing Tian Hongzheng and enthroning Wang Tingcou in his place; the court appointed Han Yu pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: Zhenzhou rebelled; they killed Tian Hongzheng and installed Wang Tingcou; [the emperor] decreed Yu as pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 既行，眾皆危之。
entries.en: After he departed, everyone feared for his safety.
entries.literal: Once he had set out, all regarded his position as perilous.

entries.zh: 元稹言：「韓愈可惜。」
entries.en: Yuan Zhen remarked, "Han Yu is too valuable to risk."
entries.literal: Yuan Zhen said: "It would be a pity to lose Han Yu."

entries.zh: 穆宗亦悔，詔愈度事從宜，無必入。
entries.en: Emperor Muzong likewise regretted the assignment and ordered Han Yu to handle matters as he saw fit, without insisting that he enter the rebel stronghold.
entries.literal: Emperor Muzong also regretted [the mission] and decreed that Yu should gauge affairs as circumstances required, without necessarily entering [Zhenzhou].

entries.zh: 愈至，廷湊嚴兵迓之，甲士陳廷。
entries.en: When Han Yu arrived, Wang Tingcou met him with troops drawn up in battle order, armored soldiers filling the hall.
entries.literal: When Yu arrived, Tingcou arrayed troops sternly to receive him, armored soldiers lining the court.

entries.zh: 既坐，廷湊曰：「所以紛紛者，乃此士卒也。」
entries.en: After they were seated, Wang Tingcou said, "These soldiers here are the cause of all the turmoil."
entries.literal: Once seated, Tingcou said: "Those responsible for all this uproar are precisely these soldiers."

entries.zh: 愈大聲曰；
entries.en: Han Yu raised his voice and said:
entries.literal: Yu said in a loud voice:

entries.zh: 「天子以公為有將帥材，故賜以節，豈意同賊反邪？」
entries.en: "The Son of Heaven believed you had the makings of a general and gave you the commander's baton—did he mean for you to side with rebels?"
entries.literal: "The Son of Heaven considered you possessed of commander talent, and therefore bestowed the staff of office—did he intend that you join the bandits in rebellion?"

entries.zh: 語未終，士前奮曰：「先太師為國擊硃滔，血衣猶在，此軍何負，乃以為賊乎？」
entries.en: Before he could finish, soldiers surged forward: "Our late Grand Tutor fought Zhu Tao for the empire—his bloody garments remain! What crime has this army committed, that you brand us rebels?"
entries.literal: Before he finished speaking, soldiers stepped forward vehemently and said: "The former Grand Tutor fought Zhu Tao for the state; his blood-stained garments are still here—what fault has this army, that you call us bandits?"

entries.zh: 愈曰：「以為爾不記先太師也，若猶記之，固善。
entries.en: Han Yu replied, "I thought you had forgotten your Grand Tutor; if you still honor his memory, all the better.
entries.literal: Yu said: "I had thought you did not remember the former Grand Tutor; if you still remember him, so much the better.

entries.zh: 天寶以來，安祿山、史思明、李希烈等有子若孫在乎？
entries.en: Since the Tianbao era, have the sons or grandsons of An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Xilie, and their kind survived among you?
entries.literal: Since the Tianbao era, have An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Xilie, and the like had sons or grandsons [among you]?

entries.zh: 亦有居官者乎？」
entries.en: Did any of them hold government posts?"
entries.literal: Have any of them held office?"

entries.zh: 眾曰：「無。」
entries.en: The soldiers answered, "None."
entries.literal: The crowd said: "None."

entries.zh: 愈曰：「田公以魏博六州歸朝廷，官中書令，父子受旗節；
entries.en: Han Yu continued, "Lord Tian surrendered Weibo's six prefectures to the court and rose to Grand Counselor; father and son both received command banners and staffs of office—
entries.literal: Yu said: "Lord Tian surrendered the six prefectures of Weibo to the court and was appointed Grand Counselor; father and son both received banners and staffs;

entries.zh: 劉悟、李祐皆大鎮。
entries.en: Liu Wu and Li You each governed major circuits.
entries.literal: Liu Wu and Li You both held great prefectures.

entries.zh: 此爾軍所其聞也。」
entries.en: These are deeds your army well knows."
entries.literal: This is what your army has surely heard."

entries.zh: 眾曰：「弘正刻，故此軍不安。」
entries.en: They replied, "Hongzheng was severe—that is why the army grew restless."
entries.literal: The crowd said: "Hongzheng was harsh, hence this army was unsettled."

entries.zh: 愈曰：「然爾曹亦害田公，又殘其家矣，復何道？」
entries.en: Han Yu said, "Yet you yourselves killed Lord Tian and destroyed his family—what excuse remains?"
entries.literal: Yu said: "Yet you yourselves also harmed Lord Tian and further ravaged his household—what more is there to say?"

entries.zh: 眾讙曰：「善。」
entries.en: The soldiers broke into an uproar, crying, "Fair enough!"
entries.literal: The crowd clamored noisily: "Good."

entries.zh: 廷湊慮眾變，疾麾使去。
entries.en: Wang Tingcou, fearing the troops might turn, quickly gestured for them to leave.
entries.literal: Tingcou feared the crowd would change, and swiftly waved them to withdraw.

entries.zh: 因曰：「今欲廷湊何所為？」
entries.en: He then asked, "What do you wish Tingcou to do now?"
entries.literal: Thereupon he said: "What now does [Wang] Tingcou wish me to do?"

entries.zh: 愈曰：「神策六軍將如牛元翼者為不乏，但朝廷顧大體，不可棄之。
entries.en: Han Yu answered, "The Shence Armies have no lack of generals like Niu Yuanyi, yet the court cares for the larger interest and cannot abandon him.
entries.literal: Yu said: "Among the Shence Six Armies, commanders such as Niu Yuanyi are not scarce, but the court regards the larger interest and cannot abandon him.

entries.zh: 公久圍之，何也？」
entries.en: Why have you besieged him so long?"
entries.literal: You have long besieged him—why?"

entries.zh: 廷湊曰：「即出之。」
entries.en: Wang Tingcou said, "I will release him forthwith."
entries.literal: Tingcou said: "I will release him at once."

entries.zh: 愈曰：「若爾，則無事矣。」
entries.en: Han Yu said, "Then all will be well."
entries.literal: Yu said: "If so, then there will be no further trouble."

entries.zh: 會元翼亦潰圍出，延湊不追。
entries.en: Just then Niu Yuanyi had already broken out of the encirclement; Wang Tingcou did not give chase.
entries.literal: It happened that Yuanyi also broke the siege and escaped; Tingcou did not pursue.

entries.zh: 愈歸奏其語，帝大悅。
entries.en: Han Yu returned and reported what had been said; the emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: Yu returned and reported his words; the emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 轉吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: [He was] transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 韓愈附:孟郊 張籍 皇甫湜 盧仝 賈島 劉乂
entries.en: Han Yu, with appended biographies: Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Huangfu Shi, Lu Tong, Jia Dao, and Liu Yi
entries.literal: Han Yu, with appended [biographies]: Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Huangfu Shi, Lu Tong, Jia Dao, Liu Yi

entries.zh: 子大夫皆識達古今，誌在康濟，造廷待問，副朕虛懷，必當箴治之闕，辨政之疵，明綱條之致紊，稽富庶之所急。
entries.en: You gentlemen all understand past and present, your hearts set on bringing peace to the realm; you come to court to await my questions and to meet my open mind — you must point out what is lacking in governance, distinguish flaws in policy, show where statutes fall into disorder, and examine what the people urgently need for prosperity.
entries.literal: You, gentlemen, all understand and penetrate past and present, your will set on bringing peace and aid; coming to court to await questioning, matching my open mind — you must admonish the gaps in governance, distinguish the flaws in policy, clarify where statutes and regulations fall into disorder, and examine what wealth and population urgently need.

entries.zh: 何施革於前弊？
entries.en: What measures will reform the abuses of the past?
entries.literal: What measures shall reform former abuses?

entries.zh: 何澤惠於下土？
entries.en: What bounty will reach the people below?
entries.literal: What bounty shall benefit the lower realm?

entries.zh: 何脩而治古可近？
entries.en: What cultivation will bring the governance of antiquity within reach?
entries.literal: What cultivation shall make governance of antiquity attainable?

entries.zh: 何道而和氣克充？
entries.en: What Way will fully fill the realm with harmonious qi?
entries.literal: What Way shall make harmonious qi fully fill?

entries.zh: 推之本源，著於條對。
entries.en: Trace each matter to its root and set it forth in your written replies.
entries.literal: Trace it to the root source and set it forth in itemized answers.

entries.zh: 至若夷吾輕重之權，孰輔於治？
entries.en: As for Guan Zhong's power to weigh light and heavy, which of these aids governance?
entries.literal: As for Guan Yiwu's power over light and heavy, which shall aid governance?

entries.zh: 嚴尤底定之策，孰葉於時？
entries.en: Yan You's policies for securing the realm — which accord with our times?
entries.literal: Yan You's policies for securing the foundation — which accord with the times?

entries.zh: 元凱之考課何先？
entries.en: In the performance review of Yuan Kai, what should come first?
entries.literal: In the performance review of Yuan Kai, what comes first?

entries.zh: 叔子之克平何務？
entries.en: In Shuzi's achievement of peace, what is the essential task?
entries.literal: In Shuzi's achievement of peace, what is the task?

entries.zh: 惟此龜鑒，擇乎中庸，斯在洽聞，朕將親覽。
entries.en: Take these as your tortoise mirrors, choose the Mean among them; this depends on thorough knowledge — I shall read your answers myself.
entries.literal: Only these tortoise mirrors — choose among the Mean; this lies in comprehensive hearing; I shall personally review.

entries.zh: 伏以聖策有思古先之治，念玄默之化，將欲通天地以濟俗，和陰陽以煦物，見陛下慮道之深也。
entries.en: I note that your sage question reflects on the governance of antiquity and the transformation of profound silence, intending to join Heaven and Earth to aid the people and harmonize yin and yang to warm all things — this shows how deeply Your Majesty ponders the Way.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself: the sage examination question thinks on the governance of antiquity, recalls the transformation of profound silence, intends to connect Heaven and Earth to aid custom, harmonize yin and yang to warm things — this shows Your Majesty's deep concern for the Way.

entries.zh: 臣以為哲王之治，其則不遠，惟致之之道何如耳。
entries.en: I believe the standard of the wise king's governance is not far off; the question is only how to attain it.
entries.literal: Your subject believes that the governance of the wise king — its standard is not far; only how the Way of attaining it is, that is all.

entries.zh: 伏以聖策有祗荷丕構而不敢荒寧，奉若謨訓而罔有怠忽，見陛下憂勞之至也。
entries.en: I note that your sage question shows you reverently bearing this great edifice without daring idleness, heeding the counsels of old without negligence — this shows the depth of Your Majesty's worry and labor.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself: the sage question reverently bears the great structure and dares not be idle, follows as if the counsels and has no negligence — this shows Your Majesty's utmost worry and labor.

entries.zh: 若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜絀左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣。
entries.en: As for employing the worthy with vigilance and rising before dawn to eat after dusk — you should dismiss the petty flatterers at your side and advance the great ministers who are your arms and thighs.
entries.literal: As for employing the worthy with vigilance, rising early and eating late — one should dismiss the petty flatterers at left and right, and advance the great ministers who are the arms and thighs.

entries.zh: 若夫追縱三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當代之成敗。
entries.en: As for following the tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and continuing your ancestors' work — you should take as your mirror the rise and fall of former ages and see clearly the successes and failures of our own day.
entries.literal: As for pursuing the tracks of the Three and Five and continuing the ancestors — one should take as mirror the rise and fall of former ages, and clarify the success and failure of the present age.

entries.zh: 心有未達，以下情蔽而不得上通；
entries.en: what the heart has not attained is because conditions below are blocked and cannot reach you;
entries.literal: what the heart has not attained — because conditions below are blocked and cannot reach above;

entries.zh: 行有未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹。
entries.en: what in conduct has not won trust is because your favor above is clogged and cannot soak the realm below.
entries.literal: what in conduct has not won trust — because favor above is clogged and cannot soak below.

entries.zh: 欲人之化，在脩己以先之；
entries.en: If you wish the people to be transformed, cultivate yourself first to lead them;
entries.literal: If you wish men to be transformed, cultivate the self first to lead them;

entries.zh: 欲氣之和，在遂性以導之。
entries.en: if you wish the vital energies to harmonize, follow their nature to guide them.
entries.literal: if you wish the qi to be harmonious, follow their nature to guide them.

entries.zh: 救災旱在致精誠，廣播殖在視食力。
entries.en: Relief from drought and disaster lies in utmost sincerity; to broaden sowing and planting, look to the people's productive strength.
entries.literal: To rescue from disaster and drought lies in extending utmost sincerity; to broaden sowing and planting lies in regarding food-producing strength.

entries.zh: 國廩罕畜，本乎冗食尚繁；
entries.en: that the state granaries seldom fill — the root cause is that redundant consumption remains too great;
entries.literal: that state granaries rarely store grain — its root lies in redundant consumption still being abundant;

entries.zh: 吏道多端，本乎選用失當。
entries.en: that official paths branch in every direction — the root cause is mistaken selection and appointment.
entries.literal: that the ways of officials are manifold — its root lies in selection and employment being wrong.

entries.zh: 豪猾逾檢，繇中外之法殊；
entries.en: that the powerful and cunning overstep bounds — because laws at court and in the provinces differ;
entries.literal: that the powerful and cunning overstep bounds — because laws within and without differ;

entries.zh: 生徒惰業，繇學校之官廢；
entries.en: that students are slack in their studies — because school officials have been neglected;
entries.literal: that students are idle in studies — because school officials are neglected;

entries.zh: 列郡幹禁，繇授任非人；
entries.en: that commanderies violate prohibitions — because the wrong men are appointed;
entries.literal: that commanderies violate prohibitions — because appointments are not the right men;

entries.zh: 百工淫巧，繇制度不立。
entries.en: that the crafts turn to extravagant artifice — because institutions are not firmly established.
entries.literal: that the hundred crafts are extravagant in artifice — because institutions are not established.

entries.zh: 伏以聖策有擇官濟治之心，阜財發號之嘆，見陛下教化之本也。
entries.en: I note that your sage question shows the heart to choose officials and aid governance, the sigh over enriching the treasury and issuing commands — this shows where Your Majesty's transforming work must begin.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself: the sage question has the heart to select officials and aid governance, the sigh over enriching wealth and issuing commands — this shows Your Majesty's root of transforming and educating.

entries.zh: 且進人以行，則枝葉安有難辨乎？
entries.en: Moreover, if you advance men by their conduct, how could branches and leaves be hard to tell apart?
entries.literal: Moreover, if you advance men by their conduct, how could branches and leaves be hard to distinguish?

entries.zh: 防下以禮，則恥格安有不形乎？
entries.en: If you guard subordinates with ritual, how could shame and restraint fail to take visible form?
entries.literal: If you guard subordinates with ritual, how could shame and regulation fail to take form?

entries.zh: 念生寡而食眾，可罷斥惰遊；
entries.en: Seeing that producers are few and consumers many, dismiss the idle and wandering;
entries.literal: Reflecting that producers are few and consumers many, dismiss the idle and wandering;

entries.zh: 念令煩而治鮮，要察其行否。
entries.en: seeing that ordinances multiply while governance grows rare, examine whether they are actually carried out.
entries.literal: reflecting that ordinances are troublesome yet governance rare, examine whether they are carried out or not.

entries.zh: 博延群彥，願陛下必納其言；
entries.en: In broadly gathering the worthies, I beg Your Majesty to accept their words;
entries.literal: Broadly extending the assembled worthies — I wish Your Majesty will surely accept their words;

entries.zh: 造廷待問，則小臣安敢愛死？
entries.en: in coming to court to await your questions, how could this petty subject dare hold back his life?
entries.literal: coming to court to await questioning — how could this petty subject dare cherish his life?

entries.zh: 伏以聖策有求賢箴闕之言，審政辨疵之令，見陛下咨訪之勤也。
entries.en: I note that your sage question calls for seeking the worthy and admonishing what is lacking, for examining governance and distinguishing flaws — this shows how diligently Your Majesty consults.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself: the sage question has words of seeking the worthy and admonishing gaps, orders to examine governance and distinguish flaws — this shows Your Majesty's diligence in consultation.

entries.zh: 遂小臣斥奸豪之誌，則弊革於前；
entries.en: if your subject then carries out his will to denounce treacherous grandees, former abuses will be reformed;
entries.literal: if this petty subject then carries out the will to denounce treacherous grandees, former abuses will be reformed;

entries.zh: 守陛下念康濟之心，則惠敷於下。
entries.en: if I hold to Your Majesty's heart set on bringing peace to the realm, bounty will spread to the people below.
entries.literal: if I keep Your Majesty's heart intent on bringing peace and aid, bounty will spread below.

entries.zh: 邪正之道分，而治古可近；
entries.en: if the paths of the wicked and the upright are divided, the governance of antiquity may be approached;
entries.literal: if the paths of perverse and upright are divided, governance of antiquity may be approached;

entries.zh: 禮樂之方著，而和氣克充。
entries.en: if the methods of ritual and music are made manifest, harmonious qi can fully fill the realm.
entries.literal: if the methods of ritual and music are made manifest, harmonious qi can fully fill.

entries.zh: 至若夷吾之法，非皇王之權；
entries.en: As for Guan Zhong's methods, they are not the authority of the sage-king;
entries.literal: As for the methods of Yiwu, they are not the authority of the sage-king;

entries.zh: 嚴尤所陳，無最上之策；
entries.en: what Yan You presented offers no policy of the highest order;
entries.literal: what Yan You presented has no policy of the highest order;

entries.zh: 元凱之所先，不若唐堯考績；
entries.en: what Yuan Kai puts first cannot match Tang Yao's performance review;
entries.literal: what Yuan Kai puts first is not equal to Tang Yao's performance review;

entries.zh: 叔子之所務，不若虞舜舞幹。
entries.en: what Shuzi makes his task cannot match Yu Shun's dancing with shields and axes.
entries.literal: what Shuzi makes his task is not equal to Yu Shun's dancing with shields.

entries.zh: 且非大德之中庸、上聖之龜鑒，又何足為陛下道之哉？
entries.en: Moreover, if they are not the Mean of great virtue or the tortoise mirror of the supreme sage, how are they worth mentioning to Your Majesty?
entries.literal: Moreover, if they are not the Mean of great virtue or the tortoise mirror of the supreme sage, how are they worth speaking of to Your Majesty?

entries.zh: 或有以系安危之機、兆存亡之變者，臣請披肝膽為陛下別白而重言之。
entries.en: If there are matters that touch the pivot of security and danger and foretoken survival or extinction, I beg to lay bare my heart and speak of them plainly and at length for Your Majesty.
entries.literal: If there are matters that bear on the pivot of security and danger, that foretoken the change of survival and extinction, your subject asks to lay bare liver and gall and for Your Majesty separately clarify and speak of them again with weight.

entries.zh: 臣前所謂「若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜絀左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣」，實以陛下憂勞之至也。
entries.en: What I meant when I said "you should employ the worthy with vigilance, rise before dawn and eat after dusk, dismiss the petty flatterers at your side, and advance your great ministers as arms and thighs" — is that Your Majesty's worry and labor have reached an extreme.
entries.literal: What your subject earlier said — "As for employing the worthy with vigilance, rising early and eating late, one should dismiss the petty flatterers at left and right and advance the great ministers who are the arms and thighs" — is in truth because Your Majesty's worry and labor reach the utmost.

entries.zh: 臣聞不宜憂而憂者，國必衰；
entries.en: I have heard that when a ruler worries over what he should not worry about, the state must decline;
entries.literal: Your subject has heard: when one worries over what one should not worry about, the state must decline;

entries.zh: 宜憂而不憂者，國必危。
entries.en: when a ruler fails to worry over what he should worry about, the state must be in peril.
entries.literal: when one does not worry over what one should worry about, the state must be in peril.

entries.zh: 陛下不以國家存亡、社稷安危之策而降於清問，臣未知陛下以布衣之臣不足與定大計耶？
entries.en: Your Majesty does not lower your clear inquiry to policies for the state's survival, the realm's security and danger — I do not know whether Your Majesty thinks a man in plain cloth insufficient to settle the great plan?
entries.literal: Your Majesty does not lower clear inquiry with policies for the state's survival or extinction, the altar of soil and grain's security or danger — your subject does not know whether Your Majesty thinks a subject in plain cloth insufficient to settle the great plan?

entries.zh: 或萬機之勤有所未至也？
entries.en: Or is it that your diligence over the myriad affairs has not yet reached everywhere?
entries.literal: Or is it that diligence over the myriad affairs has not yet reached everywhere?

entries.zh: 不然，何宜憂而不憂乎？
entries.en: If not, why do you fail to worry over what you should worry about?
entries.literal: If not, why do you not worry over what you should worry about?

entries.zh: 臣以為陛下所先憂者，宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，四海將亂。
entries.en: I believe what Your Majesty should worry over first is this: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and the four seas are about to fall into chaos.
entries.literal: Your subject believes what Your Majesty should worry over first: the inner palace is about to change, the altar of soil and grain is about to be in peril, all under Heaven is about to topple, the four seas are about to fall into chaos.

entries.zh: 此四者，國家已然之兆，故臣謂聖慮宜先及之。
entries.en: These four are omens already manifest in the state; therefore I say Your Majesty's concern should reach them first.
entries.literal: These four are already-manifest omens of the state; therefore your subject says the sage consideration should reach them first.

entries.zh: 夫帝業艱難而成之，固不可容易而守之。
entries.en: The imperial enterprise was won only with difficulty; it certainly cannot be held with ease.
entries.literal: The imperial enterprise was achieved with difficulty; it certainly cannot be guarded with ease.

entries.zh: 太祖肇其基，高祖勤其績，太宗定其業，玄宗繼其明，至於陛下，二百餘載，其間聖明相因，擾亂繼作，未有不用賢士、近正人而能興者。
entries.en: Taizu laid its foundation, Gaozu labored at its achievements, Taizong fixed its enterprise, Xuanzong continued its brilliance — down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years have passed; through that span sage rulers succeeded one another and turmoil followed in turn — never yet has a dynasty flourished without employing worthy men and drawing near the upright.
entries.literal: Taizu laid its foundation, Gaozu labored at its achievements, Taizong fixed its enterprise, Xuanzong continued its brilliance — down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years; in that interval sage brilliance succeeded one another, disturbance and chaos followed in succession — never has there been one who, without employing worthy scholars and drawing near upright men, could flourish.

entries.zh: 或一日不念，則顛覆大器，宗廟之恥，萬古為恨。
entries.en: Neglect it for a single day and the great vessel is overturned — shame upon the ancestral temples, a regret for ten thousand ages.
entries.literal: If for a single day you do not think on it, the great vessel is overturned, the shame of the ancestral temples — for ten thousand ages a regret.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》，人君之道，在體元以居正。
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: the ruler's Way lies in embodying the beginning to dwell in correctness.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: the Way of the ruler lies in embodying yuan to dwell in correctness.

entries.zh: 昔董仲舒為漢武帝言之略矣，有未盡者，臣得為陛下備論之。
entries.en: Long ago Dong Zhongshu spoke of it to Emperor Wu of Han in outline; what he left unsaid, your subject may now set forth fully for Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Formerly Dong Zhongshu spoke of it to Emperor Wu of Han in summary; what was not exhausted, your subject may fully discuss for Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 夫繼故必書即位，所以正其始也；
entries.en: In succeeding a predecessor, the Annals must record enthronement — thereby to set the beginning right;
entries.literal: In succeeding the former, one must record enthronement — thereby to correct the beginning;

entries.zh: 終必書所終之地，所以正其終也。
entries.en: At the end one must record where it ends — thereby to set the conclusion right.
entries.literal: At the end one must record the place where it ends — thereby to correct the end.

entries.zh: 故為君者，所發必正言，所履必正道，所居必正位，所近必正人。
entries.en: Therefore for a ruler: what he speaks must be upright words, what he walks must be the upright Way, where he dwells must be the upright position, and whom he draws near must be upright men.
entries.literal: Therefore for one who is ruler: what he issues must be upright words, what he treads must be the upright Way, where he dwells must be the upright position, whom he draws near must be upright men.

entries.zh: 《春秋》：「閽弒吳子余祭。」
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals records: "A gate guard murdered Prince Yuji of Wu."
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: "A gate guard murdered Prince Yuji of Wu."

entries.zh: 書其名，譏疏遠賢士，昵刑人，有不君之道。
entries.en: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, favored mutilated men, and conducted himself unlike a true ruler.
entries.literal: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, was intimate with mutilated men, and had the conduct of one who is not a ruler.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下思祖宗開國之勤，念《春秋》繼故之誡。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to reflect on the toil of the ancestors in founding the state and heed the Spring and Autumn's admonition on succeeding a predecessor.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty to think on the toil of the ancestors in founding the state, and recall the admonition of the Spring and Autumn on succeeding the former.

entries.zh: 明法度之端，則發正言，履正道；
entries.en: Clarify the foundations of law and institution, then speak upright words and walk the upright Way;
entries.literal: Clarify the beginning of laws and institutions, then issue upright words and tread the upright Way;

entries.zh: 杜篡弒之漸，則居正位，近正人。
entries.en: block the gradual advance of usurpation and regicide, then dwell in the upright position and draw near upright men.
entries.literal: block the gradual advance of usurpation and regicide, then dwell in the upright position and draw near upright men.

entries.zh: 遠刀鋸之殘，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以顓其任，庶寮得以守其官。
entries.en: Keep far from the cruelty of torture, draw near the blunt integrity of true remonstrators; then chief ministers can fully carry out their duties and the myriad offices can keep to their posts.
