entries.literal: Keep far the cruelty of blade and saw, draw near the straightness of those who are bone in the throat; then chief ministers can fully carry out their duties, and the myriad offices can keep to their posts.

entries.zh: 奈何以褻近五六人總天下大政，外專陛下之命，內竊陛下之權，威懾朝廷，勢傾海內，群臣莫敢指其狀，天子不得制其心，禍稔蕭墻，奸生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽復生於今日，此宮闈將變也。
entries.en: Yet how can five or six men of intimate proximity monopolize the great affairs of the realm — outwardly monopolizing your commands, inwardly stealing your authority, their might terrifying the court and their power overturning the empire; the ministers dare not point to their conduct, the Son of Heaven cannot control their hearts; disaster ripens within the courtyard wall and treachery arises within the curtain — I fear Cao Jie and Hou Lan are reborn in our day: this is the inner palace about to change.
entries.literal: Yet how can five or six men of intimate proximity monopolize the great affairs of all under Heaven — outwardly monopolizing Your Majesty's commands, inwardly stealing Your Majesty's authority, their might terrifying the court, their power overturning the realm; the hundred ministers dare not point to their conduct, the Son of Heaven cannot control their hearts; disaster ripens within the courtyard wall, treachery arises within the curtain — your subject fears Cao Jie and Hou Lan are reborn in our day: this is how the inner palace is about to change.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》：「定公元年春王。」
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "In spring of the first year of Duke Ding, the King."
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: "In spring of the first year of Duke Ding, the King."

entries.zh: 不言正月者，《春秋》以為先君不得正其終，則後君不得正其始，故曰「定無正」也。
entries.en: It does not speak of the first month because the Annals hold that if the former ruler could not set his end right, the later ruler cannot set his beginning right — therefore it says "Ding has no correctness."
entries.literal: It does not speak of the first month because the Spring and Autumn holds that if the former ruler could not correct his end, then the later ruler cannot correct his beginning — therefore it says "Ding has no correctness."

entries.zh: 今忠賢無腹心之寄，閽寺專廢立之權，陷先帝不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始，況太子未立，郊祀未脩，將相之職不歸，名器之宜不定，此社稷將危也。
entries.en: Now the loyal and worthy have no trust at your side; gatekeepers and eunuchs monopolize the power to depose and establish, trapping the former emperor so he could not set his end right and causing you not to set your beginning right — moreover the heir is not established, suburban sacrifices are not performed, the duties of generals and ministers do not return to their places, and titles and regalia are not fixed: this is how the altars of state are about to be endangered.
entries.literal: Now the loyal and worthy have no trust of heart and belly; gatekeepers and eunuchs monopolize the power to depose and establish, trapping the former emperor so he could not correct his end, causing Your Majesty not to correct your beginning — moreover the heir is not established, suburban sacrifices not performed, the duties of generals and ministers do not return to their places, the appropriateness of titles and vessels is not fixed: this is how the altar of soil and grain is about to be in peril.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》：「王劄子殺召伯、毛伯。」
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Prince Zha of Zhou murdered the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao."
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Prince Zha of Zhou murdered the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao."

entries.zh: 《春秋》之義，兩下相殺不書。
entries.en: The principle of the Annals: when two sides kill each other, it is not recorded.
entries.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn: when two sides kill each other, it is not recorded.

entries.zh: 此書者，重其顓王命也。
entries.en: That it is recorded here emphasizes how he monopolized the royal command.
entries.literal: That it is recorded here emphasizes how he monopolized the king's command.

entries.zh: 夫天之所授者在命，君之所存者在令。
entries.en: What Heaven bestows lies in the mandate; what the ruler preserves lies in his commands.
entries.literal: What Heaven bestows lies in the mandate; what the ruler preserves lies in commands.

entries.zh: 操其命而失之者，是不君也；
entries.en: to grasp the mandate yet lose it — that is not to be a ruler;
entries.literal: to grasp the mandate yet lose it — that is not being a ruler;

entries.zh: 侵其命而專之者，是不臣也。
entries.en: to encroach on the mandate and monopolize it — that is not to be a minister.
entries.literal: to encroach on the mandate and monopolize it — that is not being a minister.

entries.zh: 君不君，臣不臣，此天下所以將傾也。
entries.en: When the ruler is no ruler and the minister no minister — this is why the realm is about to topple.
entries.literal: The ruler not a ruler, the minister not a minister — this is why all under Heaven is about to topple.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》，晉趙鞅以晉陽之兵叛入於晉，書其歸者，能逐君側之惡以安其君，故《春秋》善之。
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion and entered Jin; the Annals record his return because he drove out the wicked at the ruler's side to secure his lord — therefore the Annals commend him.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion and entered Jin; it records his return because he was able to drive out the wicked at the ruler's side to secure his ruler — therefore the Spring and Autumn commends him.

entries.zh: 今威柄陵夷，藩臣跋扈。
entries.en: Now royal authority declines and frontier lords grow overbearing.
entries.literal: Now authority declines, frontier lords are overbearing.

entries.zh: 有不達人臣大節，而首亂者將以安君為名；
entries.en: there are those who do not comprehend a minister's great integrity, yet those who first raise chaos will take securing the ruler as their pretext;
entries.literal: there are those who do not comprehend the great integrity of a minister, yet those who first raise chaos will take securing the ruler as their name;

entries.zh: 不究《春秋》之微，稱兵者在逐惡為義。
entries.en: without investigating the subtlety of the Annals, those who raise armies will claim that driving out the wicked is righteous.
entries.literal: not investigating the subtlety of the Spring and Autumn, those who raise armies will take driving out the wicked as righteousness.

entries.zh: 則典刑不繇天子，征伐必自諸侯，此海內之將亂也。
entries.en: then canonical punishments will not come from the Son of Heaven and campaigns will necessarily come from the feudal lords — this is how the empire is about to fall into chaos.
entries.literal: then canonical punishments will not come from the Son of Heaven, campaigns and punishments will necessarily come from the feudal lords — this is how the realm within the seas is about to fall into chaos.

entries.zh: 故樊噲排闥而雪涕，袁盎當車而抗辭，京房發憤以殞身，竇武不顧而畢命，此皆陛下明知之矣。
entries.en: Therefore Fan Kuai pushed through the door with tears streaming, Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with defiant words, Jing Fang gave vent to indignation and lost his life, Dou Wu paid no heed and gave his life — all these Your Majesty clearly knows.
entries.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai pushed through the door with tears streaming, Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with defiant words, Jing Fang gave vent to indignation and lost his life, Dou Wu paid no heed and ended his life — all these Your Majesty clearly knows.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》，晉狐射姑殺陽處父，書襄公殺之者，以其君漏言也。
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin murdered Yang Chufu; the Annals record that Duke Xiang murdered him because his ruler leaked a secret.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin murdered Yang Chufu; it records that Duke Xiang murdered him because his ruler leaked words.

entries.zh: 襄公不能固陰重之機，處父所以及殘賊之禍，故《春秋》非之。
entries.en: Duke Xiang could not keep a weighty secret; Chufu therefore met a cruel end — therefore the Annals condemn it.
entries.literal: Duke Xiang could not secure the secret weighty occasion; Chufu therefore met the disaster of cruel injury — therefore the Spring and Autumn condemns it.

entries.zh: 夫上漏其情，則下不敢盡意；
entries.en: When those above leak their feelings, those below dare not speak their full intent;
entries.literal: When those above leak their feelings, those below dare not exhaust their intent;

entries.zh: 上泄其事，則下不敢盡言。
entries.en: when those above disclose their affairs, those below dare not speak their full mind.
entries.literal: when those above disclose their affairs, those below dare not exhaust their words.

entries.zh: 故《傳》有造膝詭辭之文，《易》有失身害成之戒。
entries.en: Therefore the Commentary has texts of knee-to-knee deceptive words, and the Changes warns of losing one's person and harming what is accomplished.
entries.literal: Therefore the Commentary has texts of knee-to-knee deceptive words, and the Changes has the warning of losing one's person and harming what is accomplished.

entries.zh: 今公卿大臣，非不欲為陛下言之，慮陛下不能用也。
entries.en: Now the great ministers — it is not that they do not wish to speak to you; they fear you cannot employ their words.
entries.literal: Now the great ministers and high officials — it is not that they do not wish to speak to Your Majesty; they fear Your Majesty cannot employ their words.

entries.zh: 忽而不用，必泄其言，臣下既言而不行，必嬰其禍；
entries.en: if you suddenly do not employ them, they will surely leak their words; if subordinates speak yet nothing is done, they will surely meet disaster;
entries.literal: if suddenly not employed, they will surely leak their words; if subordinates have spoken yet it is not carried out, they will surely meet with disaster;

entries.zh: 適足鉗直臣之口，而重奸臣之威。
entries.en: this only clamps shut the mouths of upright ministers and adds weight to the might of treacherous ministers.
entries.literal: this only clamps shut the mouths of upright ministers and adds weight to the might of treacherous ministers.

entries.zh: 是以欲盡其言則有失身之懼，欲盡其意則有害成之憂，裴回郁塞，以須陛下感悟，然後盡其啟沃。
entries.en: Therefore if they wish to speak fully they fear for their lives; if they wish to speak their full mind they worry of harming what is accomplished; they hesitate, depressed and blocked, awaiting your awakening — only then do they fully offer their counsel.
entries.literal: Therefore if they wish to exhaust their words they have the fear of losing their person; if they wish to exhaust their intent they have the worry of harming what is accomplished; they turn and hesitate, depressed and blocked, awaiting Your Majesty's awakening — only then do they fully offer their nourishing counsel.

entries.zh: 陛下何不聽朝之餘，時禦便殿，召當世賢相老臣，訪持變扶危之謀，求定傾救亂之術，塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵陵迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂。
entries.en: Why do you not, after court affairs, from time to time proceed to the side hall, summon the worthy chief ministers and elder statesmen of the age, inquire after plans to uphold change and support peril, seek methods to settle what topples and rescue chaos, block the paths of perverse influence, dismiss intimate favorites, restrain hearts that encroach and coerce, restore the work of sweeping clear the gates and households, warn against what should be warned, and worry over what should be worried?
entries.literal: Why does Your Majesty not, after hearing court affairs, from time to time proceed to the convenient hall, summon the worthy chief ministers and elder statesmen of the age, inquire after plans to uphold change and support peril, seek methods to settle what topples and rescue chaos, block the paths of yin perversity, dismiss intimate and familiar ministers, restrain hearts that encroach and coerce, restore the work of sweeping clear the gates and households, warn against what should be warned, worry over what should be worried?

entries.zh: 既不得治其前，當治於後；
entries.en: If you cannot set right what came before, set right what comes after;
entries.literal: If you cannot govern what came before, govern what comes after;

entries.zh: 不得正其始，當正其終。
entries.en: if you cannot set the beginning right, set the end right.
entries.literal: if you cannot correct the beginning, correct the end.

entries.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構，終任賢之效，無宵旰之憂矣。
entries.en: Then you can reverently follow the canonical counsels, fully inherit the great edifice, finally achieve the effect of employing the worthy, and be free of the worry of rising before dawn and eating after dusk.
entries.literal: Then you can reverently follow the canonical counsels, fully inherit the great structure, finally achieve the effect of employing the worthy, and be without the worry of rising early and eating late.

entries.zh: 臣前所謂陛下「心有所未達，以下情塞而不能上通；
entries.en: What I said earlier — Your Majesty, "what you intend in the heart has not been realized because conditions below are blocked and cannot reach you;
entries.literal: What your subject earlier said — Your Majesty "what the heart has not attained, because conditions below are blocked and cannot reach above;

entries.zh: 行有所未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹」；
entries.en: what you enact has not won trust because your favor above is clogged and cannot soak the realm below";
entries.literal: what in conduct has not won trust, because favor above is clogged and cannot soak below";

entries.zh: 且百姓有塗炭之苦，陛下無繇而知；
entries.en: moreover the people suffer as if in fire and coals, yet you have no means to know;
entries.literal: moreover the hundred surnames have the suffering of being in fire and coals, yet Your Majesty has no means to know;

entries.zh: 陛下有子惠之心，百姓無繇而信。
entries.en: Your Majesty has a heart of fatherly kindness, yet the people have no means to believe it.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has a heart of fatherly kindness, yet the hundred surnames have no means to believe.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》書「梁亡」不書「取」者，梁自亡也，以其思慮昏而耳目塞，上出惡政，人為寇盜，皆不知其所以，終自取其滅亡也。
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: it records "Liang perished" and does not record "taken" — Liang destroyed itself because its thought was muddled and its ears and eyes blocked, above issued wicked government and men became bandits, none knowing why — in the end it brought on its own extinction.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: it records "Liang perished" and does not record "taken" — Liang destroyed itself, because its thought was muddled and ears and eyes blocked, above issued wicked government, men became bandits and robbers, none knew why — in the end it took its own extinction and perishing.

entries.zh: 臣聞國君之所以尊者，重其社稷也；
entries.en: I have heard that what makes a ruler honored is valuing his altars of state;
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that what makes the ruler of a state honored is valuing his altar of soil and grain;

entries.zh: 社稷之所以重者，存其百姓也。
entries.en: what makes the altars valued is preserving the people.
entries.literal: what makes the altar of soil and grain valued is preserving the hundred surnames.

entries.zh: 茍百姓不存，則雖社稷不得固其重；
entries.en: If the people do not survive, then even the altars cannot secure their weight;
entries.literal: If the hundred surnames do not survive, then even the altar of soil and grain cannot secure its weight;

entries.zh: 社稷不重，則人君不得保其尊。
entries.en: if the altars are not valued, then the ruler cannot preserve his honor.
entries.literal: if the altar is not valued, then the ruler of men cannot preserve his honor.

entries.zh: 故治天下者，不可不知百姓之情。
entries.en: Therefore one who governs the realm cannot fail to know the feelings of the people.
entries.literal: Therefore one who governs all under Heaven cannot fail to know the feelings of the hundred surnames.

entries.zh: 夫百姓者，陛下之赤子，陛下宜令慈仁者視育之，如保傅焉，如乳哺焉，如師之教導焉。
entries.en: The people are Your Majesty's infants; you should have the kind and benevolent regard and nurture them — as a guardian and tutor, as nursing with milk, as a teacher's instruction and guidance.
entries.literal: The hundred surnames are Your Majesty's red infants; Your Majesty should have the kind and benevolent regard and nurture them — as a guardian and tutor, as nursing with milk, as a teacher's instruction and guidance.

entries.zh: 故人之於上也，恭之如神明，愛之如父母。
entries.en: Therefore men's attitude toward those above should be: revering them as spirits, loving them as parents.
entries.literal: Therefore men's attitude toward those above: revering them as spirits, loving them as parents.

entries.zh: 今或不然，陛下親近貴幸，分曹建署，補除卒吏，召致賓客，因其貨賄，假以聲勢；
entries.en: Now it is perhaps not so: you draw near the honored and favored, divide offices and establish bureaus, appoint and dismiss clerks, summon guests — relying on their bribes and lending them reputation and power;
entries.literal: Now it is perhaps not so: Your Majesty draws near the honored and favored, divides offices and establishes bureaus, supplements and dismisses clerks and officers, summons and receives guests — relying on their goods and bribes, lending them reputation and power;

entries.zh: 大者統藩方，小者為守牧，居上無清惠之政而有饕餮之害，居下無忠誠之節而有奸欺之罪。
entries.en: the great ones command frontier regions, the small ones serve as prefects and governors — above there is no clear and gracious government but the harm of gluttonous greed; below there is no loyalty but the crime of treachery and deceit.
entries.literal: the great ones command frontier regions, the small ones serve as prefects and governors — above there is no clear and gracious government but the harm of gluttonous beasts; below there is no integrity of loyalty but the crime of treachery and deceit.

entries.zh: 故人之於上也，畏之如豺狼，惡之如仇敵。
entries.en: Therefore men's attitude toward those above becomes: fearing them as jackals and wolves, hating them as enemies.
entries.literal: Therefore men's attitude toward those above: fearing them as jackals and wolves, hating them as enemies.

entries.zh: 今海內困窮，處處流散，饑者不得食，寒者不得衣，鰥寡孤獨不得存，老幼疾病不得養，加以國權兵柄顓於左右，貪臣聚斂以固寵，奸吏因緣而弄法，冤痛之聲，上達於九天，下入於九泉，鬼神為之怨怒，陰陽為之愆錯。
entries.en: Now the empire is distressed and impoverished, people scatter everywhere — the hungry cannot obtain food, the cold cannot obtain clothing, widowers and orphans cannot survive, the old and sick cannot be cared for; added to this, state authority and military power are monopolized by those at your side, greedy ministers gather levies to secure favor, treacherous officials seize opportunities to manipulate the law — cries of wrongful pain reach up to the nine heavens and sink down to the nine springs; spirits and ghosts are angered, yin and yang are disordered.
entries.literal: Now within the seas there is distress and poverty, everywhere scattering and dispersal — the hungry cannot obtain food, the cold cannot obtain clothing, widowers and orphans cannot survive, old and young, sick and diseased cannot be nourished; added to this, state authority and military power are monopolized by those at left and right, greedy ministers gather levies to secure favor, treacherous officials seize opportunities to manipulate the law — cries of wrongful pain reach up to the nine heavens, sink down to the nine springs; spirits and ghosts are angered by it, yin and yang are disordered by it.

entries.zh: 君門萬重，不得告訴，士人無所歸化，百姓無所歸命。
entries.en: The ruler's gate is ten thousand layers deep — they cannot lodge complaints; scholars have nowhere to turn, the people have nowhere to place their trust.
entries.literal: The ruler's gate is ten thousand layers deep — they cannot lodge complaints; scholars have nowhere to turn for transformation, the hundred surnames have nowhere to turn for their mandate.

entries.zh: 官亂人貧，盜賊並起，土崩之勢，憂在旦夕。
entries.en: Officials in chaos, people in poverty, bandits rising together — the momentum of earth collapsing, worry within morning and evening.
entries.literal: Officials in chaos, people in poverty, bandits and robbers rising together — the momentum of earth collapsing, worry within morning and evening.

entries.zh: 即不幸因之以病癘，繼之以兇荒，陳勝、吳廣不獨起於秦，赤眉、黃巾不獨生於漢，臣所以為陛下發憤扼腕、痛心泣血也。
entries.en: If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clutch my wrist in anguish, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.
entries.literal: If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why your subject for Your Majesty vents indignation, clutches his wrist, grieves to the heart and weeps blood.

entries.zh: 如此則百姓有塗炭之苦，陛下何繇而知之乎？
entries.en: If it is thus, the people suffer as if in fire and coals — how can you have means to know?
entries.literal: If it is thus, the hundred surnames have the suffering of fire and coals — how can Your Majesty have means to know?

entries.zh: 陛下有子惠之心，百姓安得而信之乎？
entries.en: Your Majesty has a heart of fatherly kindness — how can the people obtain belief in it?
entries.literal: Your Majesty has a heart of fatherly kindness — how can the hundred surnames obtain belief in it?

entries.zh: 使陛下行有所未孚，心有所未達，固其然也。
entries.en: That your conduct has not won trust and what you intend has not been realized — it is solidly so.
entries.literal: That Your Majesty's conduct has not won trust, what the heart has not attained — it is solidly so.

entries.zh: 臣聞漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美。
entries.en: I have heard that at the beginning of Emperor Yuan of Han's accession, he changed more than seventy institutions — his heart was very sincere, his reputation very fine.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that at the beginning of Emperor Yuan of Han's accession, he changed more than seventy institutions — his heart was very sincere, his reputation very fine.

entries.zh: 然紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，奸宄日強，黎元日困，繇不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。
entries.en: Yet day by day the statutes were tangled, day by day the dynastic fortune declined, day by day treacherous villains grew strong, day by day the people were distressed — because he could not select the worthy and employ them, he lost his grip on power.
entries.literal: Yet day by day the statutes were tangled, day by day the dynastic fortune declined, day by day treacherous villains grew strong, day by day the black-haired people were distressed — because he could not select the worthy and bright and employ them, he lost his grip on the handle.

entries.zh: 自陛下即位，憂勤兆庶，屢降德音，四海之內，莫不抗首而長息，自喜復生於死亡之中也。
entries.en: Since your accession, worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements — throughout the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh with relief, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.
entries.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements — within the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh long, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下慎終如始，以塞四方之望。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of the four directions.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of the four directions.

entries.zh: 誠能揭國柄以歸於相，持兵柄以歸於將，去貪臣聚斂之政，除奸吏因緣之害，惟忠賢是近，惟正直是用，內寵便僻無所聽焉。
entries.en: If you can truly return state authority to the chancellor and military authority to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy and employ only the upright — hear none of the words of inner favorites and convenient flatterers.
entries.literal: If you can truly raise the state's handle and return it to the chancellor, hold the military handle and return it to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy, employ only the upright — inner favorites and convenient flatterers, none of their words heard.

entries.zh: 選清慎之官，擇仁惠之長，敏之以利，煦之以和，教之以孝慈，導之以德義，去耳目之塞，通上下之情，俾萬國歡康，兆庶蘇息，即心無不達，而行無不孚矣。
entries.en: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with harmony, teach them filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace and the myriad masses revive and rest; then what you intend will reach everywhere and what you enact will win trust everywhere.
entries.literal: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with harmony, teach them with filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace, the myriad masses revive and rest; then what the heart intends will not fail to reach, what is enacted will not fail to win trust.

entries.zh: 臣前所謂「追縱三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當時之成敗」者。
entries.en: What I meant when I said "you should follow the tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and continue your ancestors' work — take as your mirror the rise and fall of former ages and see clearly the successes and failures of our own time."
entries.literal: What your subject earlier called "pursuing the tracks of the Three and Five, continuing the ancestors — one should take as mirror the rise and fall of former ages, clarify the success and failure of the present time."

entries.zh: 臣聞堯、禹之為君而天下大治者，以能任九官、四嶽、十二牧，不失其舉，不貳其業，不侵其職，居官唯其能，左右唯其賢，元凱在下雖微而必舉，四兇在朝雖強而必誅，考其安危，明其取舍。
entries.en: I have heard that Yao and Yu brought the realm to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — never missing the right appointment, never duplicating tasks, never encroaching on duties; in office only by ability, at their side only the worthy; worthy men below though slight were always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong were always executed; they examined security and danger and clarified what to take and what to discard.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that Yao and Yu as rulers brought all under Heaven to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties; in office only according to ability, at left and right only the worthy; the Yuan and Kai below though slight yet always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong yet always executed; examining security and danger, clarifying what to take and what to discard.

entries.zh: 至秦二世、漢元成，鹹願措國如唐、虞，致身如堯、舜，而終敗亡者，以其不見安危之機，不知取舍之道，不任大臣，不辨奸人，不親忠良，不遠讒佞也。
entries.en: As for Qin Ershi and the Han emperors Yuan and Cheng — all wished to set the state like Tang and Yu and make themselves like Yao and Shun, yet in the end were defeated and perished — because they did not see the pivot of security and danger, did not know what to take and what to discard, did not employ great ministers, did not distinguish treacherous men, did not draw near the loyal, and did not keep far from slanderous flatterers.
entries.literal: As for Qin Ershi and the Han emperors Yuan and Cheng — all wished to set the state like Tang and Yu, make their persons like Yao and Shun, yet in the end were defeated and perished — because they did not see the pivot of security and danger, did not know the Way of taking and discarding, did not employ great ministers, did not distinguish treacherous men, did not draw near the loyal and good, did not keep far from slanderous flatterers.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下察唐、虞之所以興，而景行於前；
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to examine why Tang and Yu flourished and take their bright conduct as your model;
entries.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty to examine why Tang and Yu flourished, and take their bright conduct as model before you;

entries.zh: 鑒秦、漢之所以亡，而戒懼於後。
entries.en: take as your mirror why Qin and Han perished and be warned and fearful thereafter.
entries.literal: take as mirror why Qin and Han perished, and be warned and fearful thereafter.

entries.zh: 陛下無謂廟堂無賢相，庶官無賢士，今紀綱未絕，典刑猶在，人誰不欲致身為王臣，致時為升平？
entries.en: Your Majesty must not say the court has no worthy chief minister or the offices no worthy scholar — the statutes are not yet severed and canonical punishments still exist; who among men does not wish to serve as your minister and bring the age to peace?
entries.literal: Your Majesty must not say the temple hall has no worthy chief minister, the myriad offices no worthy scholar — now the statutes are not yet severed, canonical punishments still exist; who among men does not wish to devote his person as the king's minister, devote the age to ascending peace?

entries.zh: 陛下何忽而不用邪？
entries.en: Why do you suddenly not employ them?
entries.literal: Why does Your Majesty suddenly not employ them?

entries.zh: 又有居官非其能，左右非其賢，惡如四兇，詐如趙高，奸如恭、顯，陛下何憚而不去邪？
entries.en: Moreover there are those in office beyond their ability, at your side not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why do you shrink from removing them?
entries.literal: Moreover there are those in office not according to their ability, at left and right not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why does Your Majesty shrink from removing them?

entries.zh: 神器固有歸，天命固有分，祖宗固有靈，忠臣固有心，陛下其念之哉！
entries.en: The sacred vessel has its rightful place, the mandate of Heaven has its allotment, the ancestors have their spirits, loyal ministers have their hearts — Your Majesty, think on these!
entries.literal: The sacred vessel inherently has its return, the mandate of Heaven inherently has its allotment, the ancestors inherently have their spirits, loyal ministers inherently have their hearts — Your Majesty, think on these!

entries.zh: 昔秦之亡也，失於強暴；
entries.en: Formerly Qin perished through violent severity;
entries.literal: Formerly Qin's perishing was lost through violent severity;

entries.zh: 漢之亡也，失於微弱。
entries.en: Han perished through feebleness.
entries.literal: Han's perishing was lost through feebleness.

entries.zh: 強暴則奸臣畏死而害上，微弱則強臣竊權而震主。
entries.en: Violent severity makes treacherous ministers fear death and harm their superiors; feebleness lets powerful ministers steal authority and shake their lord.
entries.literal: Violent severity then treacherous ministers fear death and harm their superiors; feebleness then powerful ministers steal authority and shake their lord.

entries.zh: 臣伏見敬宗不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌。
entries.en: I see that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's disaster, did not cut away its sprout.
entries.literal: Your subject prostrate sees that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's disaster of perishing, did not cut away its sprout.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸，則祖宗之洪業可紹，三五之遐軌可追矣。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty deeply to grieve Han's disaster and block its gradual advance — then the ancestors' great enterprise can be continued and the distant tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors can be pursued.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty deeply to grieve Han's disaster of perishing, to block its gradual advance — then the ancestors' great enterprise can be continued, the distant tracks of the Three and Five can be pursued.

entries.zh: 臣前所謂「豪猾逾檢，繇中外之法殊」者，以其官禁不一也。
entries.en: What I said about "the powerful and cunning overstepping bounds, because inner and outer law differ" — this is because official prohibitions are not one.
entries.literal: What your subject earlier called "overbearing and cunning men overstep bounds, because inner and outer laws differ" — because official prohibitions are not unified.

entries.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》，齊桓公盟諸侯不日，而葵丘之盟特以日者，美其能宣明天子之禁，率奉王官之法，故《春秋》備而書之。
entries.en: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: when Duke Huan of Qi covenanted with the feudal lords, dates were usually omitted; yet the covenant at Kuiqiu is specially dated — praising his ability to proclaim the Son of Heaven's prohibitions and lead the states in keeping to the royal laws; therefore the Annals record it in full.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: when Duke Huan of Qi covenanted with the feudal lords, dates were not given; yet the covenant at Kuiqiu is specially dated — praising his ability to proclaim and clarify the Son of Heaven's prohibitions and lead in keeping to the royal officers' laws; therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals records it in full.

entries.zh: 然則官者，五帝、三王之所建也；
entries.en: Thus offices were what the Five Emperors and Three Kings established;
entries.literal: Thus offices were what the Five Emperors and Three Kings established;

entries.zh: 法者，高祖、太宗之所制也。
entries.en: laws were what Gaozu and Taizong enacted.
entries.literal: laws were what Gaozu and Taizong enacted.

entries.zh: 法宜畫一，官宜正名。
entries.en: Laws should be unified; offices should have correct titles.
entries.literal: Laws should be drawn as one; offices should have corrected names.

entries.zh: 今又分外官、中官之員，立南司、北司之局，或犯禁於南則亡命於北，或正刑於外則破律於中，法出多門，人無所措，繇兵農勢異，而中外法殊也。
entries.en: Now again outer and inner officials are divided in posts, and Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau offices are established — violate a prohibition in the south and flee to the north; be punished outside and break the law within; laws issue from many gates and men have nowhere to turn — because military and agricultural power diverge, inner and outer law are separate.
entries.literal: Now again outer officials and inner officials are divided in posts, Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau offices are established — if one violates prohibition in the south he flees to the north; if punished outside he breaks law within; laws issue from many gates and men have nowhere to set themselves — because military and agricultural power differ, inner and outer laws are separate.

entries.zh: 臣聞古者因井田以制軍賦，間農事以脩武備，提封約卒乘之數，命將在公卿之列，故兵農一致，而文武同方，以保乂邦家，式遏亂略。
entries.en: I have heard that in antiquity the well-field system regulated military levies, agricultural seasons were interwoven with military training, fiefs were tallied for chariot and foot numbers, and commanders were appointed from among the chief ministers — thus military and agriculture were one, civil and martial shared one direction, to secure the state and check rebellion.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that in antiquity, through well-field [land] they regulated military levies, interspersed agricultural affairs to cultivate military readiness, took fiefs and reckoned chariot-and-foot numbers, and commanders were placed among dukes and ministers — therefore military and agriculture were one, civil and martial shared one direction, to secure and govern the state and family and check rebellious designs.

entries.zh: 太宗置府兵臺省軍衛，文武參掌，閑歲則櫜弓力穡，有事則釋耒荷戈，所以脩復古制，不廢舊物。
entries.en: Taizong established the fubing militia, Terrace offices, and army guards — civil and martial jointly administered; in peaceful years they sheathed bows and labored in the fields; when trouble arose they set aside plows and took up arms — thereby restoring the ancient system without abandoning the old institutions.
entries.literal: Taizong established fubing militia, Terrace offices, and army guards — civil and martial jointly administered; in idle years they sheathed bows and exerted strength at sowing; when affairs arose they set aside plows and shouldered spears — thereby restoring the ancient system without abandoning the old institutions.

entries.zh: 今則不然。
entries.en: Now it is not so.
entries.literal: Now it is not so.

entries.zh: 夏官不知兵籍，止於奉朝請；
entries.en: the Minister of War does not know the military registers, and attends court only as a formality;
entries.literal: the Minister of War does not know military registers, stopping at attending court audience;

entries.zh: 六軍不主武事，止於養階勛。
entries.en: the Six Armies do not preside over military affairs, and exist only to nurture ranks and honors.
entries.literal: the Six Armies do not preside over military affairs, stopping at nurturing ranks and merit.

entries.zh: 軍容合中官之政，戎律附內臣之職。
entries.en: military affairs are merged with inner eunuch government; military regulations are attached to inner attendants' offices.
entries.literal: military affairs merge with inner officials' government; military regulations attach to inner attendants' duties.

entries.zh: 首一戴武弁，疾文吏如仇讎；
entries.en: one head dons the military cap and hates civil officials like sworn enemies;
entries.literal: one head dons the military cap and hates civil officials like sworn enemies;

entries.zh: 足一蹈軍門，視農夫如草芥。
entries.en: one foot steps through the army gate and regards farmers as nothing.
entries.literal: one foot steps through the army gate and regards farmers like grass and husks.

entries.zh: 謀不足以翦除奸兇，而詐足以抑揚威福；
entries.en: their stratagems are insufficient to cut down treacherous villains, yet their cunning suffices to raise and lower authority and favor;
entries.literal: their stratagems are insufficient to cut down treacherous villains, yet their cunning suffices to raise and lower authority and favor;

entries.zh: 勇不足以鎮衛社稷，而暴足以侵害閭裏。
entries.en: their courage is insufficient to guard the altars of state, yet their violence suffices to prey on lanes and hamlets.
entries.literal: their courage is insufficient to guard and secure the altars of soil and grain, yet their violence suffices to invade lanes and hamlets.

entries.zh: 羈紲藩臣，幹陵宰輔，隳裂王度，汩亂朝經。
entries.en: They bind feudal ministers, overawe chief ministers, shatter the royal measure, and muddy the constants of court governance.
entries.literal: They bind feudal ministers, overawe chief ministers, shatter the royal measure, and muddy and disorder court constants.

entries.zh: 張武夫之威，上以制君父；
entries.en: They display the might of warriors to control the ruler and father above;
entries.literal: They display the might of warriors to control the ruler and father above;

entries.zh: 假天子之命，下以禦英豪。
entries.en: they borrow the Son of Heaven's command to repel heroes below.
entries.literal: they borrow the Son of Heaven's command to repel heroes below.

entries.zh: 有藏奸觀釁之心，無伏節死難之誼。
entries.en: They harbor treachery and watch for openings, but have no principle of bowing to duty and dying in hardship.
entries.literal: They have hearts that harbor treachery and watch for openings, but no principle of bowing to duty and dying in hardship.

entries.zh: 豈先王經文緯武之旨邪！
entries.en: Is this the purpose of the former kings in weaving civil and martial together!
entries.literal: Is this the purpose of the former kings in weaving civil and martial!

entries.zh: 臣願陛下貫文武之道，均兵農之功，正貴賤之名，一中外之法，還軍衛之職，脩省署之官；
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to thread civil and martial Ways together, equalize military and agricultural achievement, correct titles of noble and base, unify inner and outer law, restore the duties of army guards, and repair the provincial offices;
entries.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to thread through civil and martial Ways, equalize military and agricultural achievements, correct names of noble and base, unify inner and outer laws, restore army guards' duties, and repair provincial offices;

entries.zh: 近崇貞觀之風，遠復成周之制：自邦畿以刑下國，始天子而達諸侯，可以制猾奸之強，無逾檢之患矣。
entries.en: near at hand honor the spirit of the Zhenguan reign, far off restore the institutions of the accomplished Zhou: from the capital domain discipline the subordinate states, from the Son of Heaven down to the feudal lords — then you can restrain the strong among cunning villains, and there will be no calamity of overstepping bounds.
entries.literal: near at hand honor the wind of the Zhenguan reign, far off restore the institutions of the accomplished Zhou: from the capital domain punish the subordinate states, beginning with the Son of Heaven and reaching the feudal lords — then one can restrain the strong among cunning villains, and there will be no calamity of overstepping bounds.

entries.zh: 贊曰：漢武帝三策董仲舒，仲舒所對，陳天人大概，緩而不切也。
entries.en: The encomium says: Emperor Wu of Han thrice examined Dong Zhongshu; what Dong answered set forth the great outline of Heaven and man — leisurely and not incisive.
entries.literal: The encomium says: Emperor Wu of Han thrice examined Dong Zhongshu; what Dong answered set forth the great outline of Heaven and man — leisurely and not incisive.

entries.zh: 蕡與諸儒偕進，獨譏切宦官，然亦太疏直矣。
entries.en: Fen advanced together with the other scholars, alone speaking sharply against the eunuchs — yet he was also too blunt and direct.
entries.literal: Fen advanced together with the various scholars, alone sharply criticizing the eunuchs — yet he was also too blunt and direct.

entries.zh: 戒帝漏言，而身誦語於廷，何邪？
entries.en: He warned the emperor against leaking secrets, yet himself spoke his full mind in open court — how contradictory?
entries.literal: He warned the emperor against leaking words, yet himself declaimed his words in court — how is this?

entries.zh: 其後宋申錫以謀泄貶，李訓以計不臧死，宦者遂強，可不戒哉！
entries.en: Afterward Song Shenxi was demoted when his plot leaked, Li Xun died when his scheme failed — the eunuchs then grew strong; should this not serve as a warning!
entries.literal: Afterward Song Shenxi was demoted when the plot leaked, Li Xun died when the plan was not good — the eunuchs then grew strong; should this not be a warning!

entries.zh: 意蕡之賢，當先以忠結上，後為帝謀天下所以安危者，庶其紓患耶！
entries.en: One thinks that with Fen's talent, he ought first to win the sovereign's trust through loyalty, then counsel the emperor on what secures or endangers the realm — perhaps then he might have eased the calamity!
entries.literal: One thinks that with Fen's worth, he ought first to bind the sovereign with loyalty, then afterward plot for the emperor what brings security and danger to all under Heaven — perhaps then he could have relieved the trouble!

entries.zh: 劉蕡，字去華，幽州昌平人，客梁、汴間。
entries.en: Liu Fen, whose courtesy name was Quhua, came from Changping in Youzhou and had long resided as a guest in the Liang and Bian regions.
entries.literal: Liu Fen, styled Quhua, was a native of Changping in Youzhou, and lived as a guest in the regions of Liang and Bian.

entries.zh: 明《春秋》，能言古興亡事，沈健於謀，浩然有救世意。
entries.en: He mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, could speak at length on the rise and fall of ancient states, was steady and resolute in planning, and carried within him a vast determination to rescue the age.
entries.literal: He was versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals, could discourse on the rise and fall of states in antiquity, was composed and firm in counsel, and bore a grand resolve to save the world.

entries.zh: 擢進士第。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi civil examination.
entries.literal: He was advanced to the jinshi degree.

entries.zh: 元和後，權綱馳遷，神策中尉王守澄負弒逆罪，更二帝不能討，天下憤之。
entries.en: After the Yuanhe period the axes of power shifted violently; Wang Shoucheng, the Shence Army commandant, carried the guilt of regicide, yet two successive emperors could not bring him to account, and the empire seethed with outrage.
entries.literal: After the Yuanhe era, the pivots of power shifted rapidly; Wang Shoucheng, Commandant of the Divine Stratagem Army, bore the crime of regicide, yet through two emperors he could not be punished, and all under Heaven raged against it.

entries.zh: 文宗即位，思洗元和宿恥，將翦落支黨。
entries.en: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, he meant to wash away the old humiliation of the Yuanhe years and to cut down their factional networks.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he thought to wash away the long-standing shame of the Yuanhe era and intended to prune away their factional branches.

entries.zh: 方宦人握兵，橫制海內，號曰「北司」，兇醜朋挻，外脅群臣，內掣侮天子，蕡常痛疾。
entries.en: Meanwhile the eunuchs held the armies and lorded it over the realm under the name "Northern Office"; brutal and hideous, they swarmed in factions, outwardly intimidating the officials and inwardly restraining and humiliating the Son of Heaven — a wrong Fen felt as a constant wound.
entries.literal: At the time eunuchs held the armies and tyrannized the realm, called the "Northern Office"; vicious and ugly, they banded together in gangs, outwardly coercing the ministers, inwardly restraining and insulting the Son of Heaven — Fen was often consumed with bitter grief.

entries.zh: 開成二年，進同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In 837 he was made a co-director of the Chancellery with the title of chief minister.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he was advanced to Co-Director of the Chancellery with the designation Tong Zhongshu Menxia Pingzhangshi.

entries.zh: 而楊嗣復、李玨相次輔政，夷行介特，雅不與合，每議論天子前，往往語相侵短。
entries.en: Yang Sifu and Li Jue, however, were serving as chief ministers in succession; Yixing was stiff and independent by nature and clashed with them, and their exchanges before the emperor often turned personal.
entries.literal: But Yang Sifu and Li Jue in turn held chief ministerial power; Yixing was upright and aloof and by nature did not harmonize with them—whenever they debated before the Son of Heaven their words often cut at one another.

entries.zh: 夷行不能堪，輒引疾求去，文宗遣使者尉勞起之。
entries.en: Unable to bear the friction, Yixing repeatedly cited illness to resign, until Wenzong sent messengers to comfort him and recall him to duty.
entries.literal: Yixing could not endure it and repeatedly pleaded illness to resign; Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to console him and urge his return to office.

entries.zh: 會以王彥威為忠武節度使，史孝章領邠寧，議皆出嗣復。
entries.en: When Wang Yanwei was named military commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang was put in charge of Binning, the appointments had all been Sifu's doing.
entries.literal: It happened that Wang Yanwei was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang took charge of Binning—the deliberations all came from Sifu.

entries.zh: 及夷行對延英，帝問：「除二鎮當否？」
entries.en: At the Yanying audience Yixing was asked, "Were these two frontier appointments appropriate?"
entries.literal: When Yixing responded at the Yanying Hall, the emperor asked: "Were the appointments to the two circuits appropriate?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「茍自聖擇，無不當者。」
entries.en: He answered, "If Your Majesty chose them yourself, every appointment is fitting."
entries.literal: He replied: "If they were chosen by Your Sacred Majesty, none could be inappropriate."

entries.zh: 嗣復曰：「若用人盡出上意而當，固善。
entries.en: Sifu said, "If every choice that matches the emperor's wish is automatically right, that is well enough.
entries.literal: Sifu said: "If every appointment that accords with the sovereign's will is good, that is fine.

entries.zh: 如小不稱，下安得嘿然？」
entries.en: But if something is even slightly unsuitable, how can ministers below keep quiet?"
entries.literal: But if there is some slight unfitness, how can those below remain silent?"

entries.zh: 夷行曰：「比奸臣數幹權，願陛下無倒持大阿，以鐏授人。」
entries.en: Yixing said, "Treacherous ministers have lately seized power again and again; I beg Your Majesty not to grip the great sword by the blade and offer the hilt to someone else."
entries.literal: Yixing said: "Lately treacherous ministers have repeatedly meddled in power; I beg Your Majesty not to hold the great sword reversed and hand the pommel to others."

entries.zh: 嗣復曰：「古者任則不疑，齊桓公器管仲於讎虜，豈有倒持慮邪？」
entries.en: Sifu replied, "In antiquity to appoint was to trust; Duke Huan of Qi prized Guan Zhong though he had been his enemy's captive—where is the worry about holding the sword backward?"
entries.literal: Sifu said: "In antiquity, once a man was entrusted there was no doubting him; Duke Huan of Qi valued Guan Zhong though he had been a captive of his enemy—was there any thought of holding the sword reversed?"

entries.zh: 帝以其面相觸，頗不悅。
entries.en: The emperor, seeing them clash face to face, was deeply displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor, because their faces clashed in debate, was quite displeased.

entries.zh: 仙韶樂工尉遲璋授王府率，右拾遺竇洵直當衙論奏，鄭覃、嗣復嫌以細故，謂洵直近名。
entries.en: The Xianshao musician Yuchi Zhang was made commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested at court, but Zheng Tan and Sifu dismissed it as trivial and accused Xunzhi of seeking renown.
entries.literal: A Xianshao musician, Yuchi Zhang, was appointed commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi memorialized at court, and Zheng Tan and Sifu disliked it as a petty matter, saying Xunzhi was courting fame.

entries.zh: 夷行曰：「諫官當衙，正須論宰相得失，彼賤工安足言者？
entries.en: Yixing said, "Remonstrance officials at court ought to debate the chancellors' merits and faults—what business has a lowly musician in the matter?
entries.literal: Yixing said: "When remonstrance officials attend court, they ought precisely to discuss the chancellors' right and wrong—what is that base artisan fit to speak of?

entries.zh: 然亦不可置不用。」
entries.en: Still, he should not simply be ignored."
entries.literal: Yet he also cannot simply be set aside and unused."

entries.zh: 帝即徙璋光州長史，以百縑賜洵直。
entries.en: The emperor immediately reassigned Zhang as chief clerk of Guang Prefecture and rewarded Xunzhi with a hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: The emperor at once transferred Zhang to be Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture and gave Xunzhi a hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 進門下侍郎。
entries.en: Yixing was promoted to vice director of the Chancellery.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 陳三李曹劉
entries.en: Chen, the Three Lis, Cao, and Liu
entries.literal: Chen, Three Li's, Cao, Liu

entries.zh: 帝至自鳳翔，大赦天下，諸道皆賜詔，獨不及李茂貞。
entries.en: When the emperor returned from Fengxiang, he proclaimed a general amnesty for the empire. Every circuit received an edict except Li Maozhen.
entries.literal: When the emperor returned from Fengxiang he declared a great amnesty for all under heaven; every circuit received an edict except Li Maozhen.

entries.zh: 扆曰：「國西，鳳翔為最近，跡其罪固不可赦。
entries.en: Yi said, "To the west of the realm, Fengxiang is the nearest of the circuits. Judging by his crimes, he indeed cannot be pardoned.
entries.literal: Yi said: "West of the state, Fengxiang is nearest. Tracing his crimes he indeed cannot be pardoned.

entries.zh: 然尚修職貢，朝廷未之絕，無宜於詔書有以異也。」
entries.en: Yet he still sends his regular tribute, and the court has not severed relations with him. The amnesty edict ought not to treat him differently."
entries.literal: Yet he still sends tribute and the court has not cut him off; it is not fitting that the edict treat him differently."

entries.zh: 始，崔胤罷相，扆代之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Cui Yin was removed from the chancellorship, Yi had replaced him.
entries.literal: At first when Cui Yin was removed from the chancellorship, Yi replaced him.

entries.zh: 胤內怨望，及是議以為陰有黨附，貶沂王傅，分司東都。
entries.en: Yin harbored resentment within, and on this occasion the court concluded that Yi had secretly maintained factional ties. Yi was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Yi and assigned to the eastern capital.
entries.literal: Yin harbored resentment within, and on this occasion the discussion held that Yi secretly had factional ties; he was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Yi and assigned to the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 胤死，復授吏部尚書，從遷洛。
entries.en: After Yin died, Yi was again appointed Minister of Personnel and accompanied the court in its move to Luoyang.
entries.literal: When Yin died, Yi was again appointed Minister of Personnel and followed the move to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 柳璨始附朱全忠，謀去朝廷衣冠有望者，貶扆濮州司戶參軍，殺之白馬驛，年五十九。
entries.en: Liu Can, who had attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong, plotted to remove from court every man of standing in official dress. Yi was demoted to registrar of Pu Prefecture and then killed at Baima Post Station. He was fifty-nine.
entries.literal: Liu Can at first attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong and plotted to remove from court the gentry with standing; Yi was demoted to Registrar of Pu Prefecture and killed at Baima Post Station at age fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 扆初名允迪，後改雲。
entries.en: Yi's original name was Yundi; he later changed it to Yun.
entries.literal: Yi's original name was Yundi; later he changed it to Yun.

entries.zh: 擢國子《毛詩》博士。
entries.en: He was promoted to Doctor of the Mao Odes at the National University.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Doctor of the Mao Odes in the National University.

entries.zh: 上書言當世事，議遷都曰：「古王者不常厥居，皆觀天地興衰，隨時制事。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial on current affairs and discussed moving the capital, writing, "Ancient kings did not keep to a single residence. They all observed the rise and fall of heaven and earth and shaped policy according to the times.
entries.literal: He memorialized on current affairs, discussing moving the capital: "Ancient kings did not fix their residence; all observed heaven and earth's rise and fall and made policy according to the time.

entries.zh: 關中，隋家所都，我實因之，凡三百歲，文物資貨，奢侈僭偽皆極焉。
entries.en: Guanzhong was the capital of the Sui, and we in turn took it over. For three hundred years cultural treasures, goods, luxury, and usurpation all reached their extreme there.
entries.literal: Guanzhong was the Sui capital—we took it over; altogether three hundred years; cultural objects, goods and wealth, luxury and usurpation all reached their extreme.

entries.zh: 廣明巨盜陷覆宮闕，局署帑藏，裏闬井肆，所存十二，比幸石門、華陰，十二之中又亡八九，高祖、太宗之制蕩然矣。
entries.en: In the Guangming era the great rebel overran and destroyed the palace. Of the government offices, treasuries, lanes, and markets, only a tenth remained. After the emperor's flight to Shimen and Huayin, eight or nine tenths of even that remnant were lost. The institutions established by Gaozu and Taizong were swept away.
entries.literal: In Guangming the great bandit overthrew and buried the palace; bureau offices, treasury stores, lanes and markets—twelve parts remained. Compared with the flight to Shimen and Huayin, of the twelve eight or nine more were lost; the institutions of Gaozu and Taizong were swept away.

entries.zh: 夫襄、鄧之西，夷溫數百里，其東，漢輿、鳳林為之關，南，菊潭環屈而流屬於漢，西有上洛重山之險，北有白崖聯絡，乃形勝之地，沃衍之墟。
entries.en: West of Xiang and Deng lie several hundred li of warm frontier lands. To the east, Han Yu and Fenglin form its passes. To the south, Jutan bends and flows into the Han River. To the west stand the steep mountains of Shangluo. To the north, white cliffs link together. It is a place of strategic advantage and fertile ground.
entries.literal: West of Xiang and Deng several hundred li of level, warm land; east, Han Yu and Fenglin form its passes; south, Jutan bends and flows into the Han; west the dangerous heights of Shangluo mountains; north, white cliffs link together—advantageous terrain and fertile fields.

entries.zh: 若廣浚漕渠，運天下之財，可使大集。
entries.en: If the transport canals were broadly dredged and the wealth of the empire moved there, great resources could be gathered.
entries.literal: If widely dredging the transport canal, moving the empire's wealth, great collection can be made.

entries.zh: 自古中興之君，去已衰之衰，就未王而王。
entries.en: From antiquity, rulers who restored a dynasty have left what was already in decline and gone to a place not yet crowned with kingship.
entries.literal: From antiquity restoring-the-dynasty rulers leave the already declining and go to the not yet kingship.

entries.zh: 今南陽，漢光武雖起而未王也。
entries.en: Nanyang today is like the place where Emperor Guangwu of Han rose to power before he had yet become king.
entries.literal: Now Nanyang—Han Guangwu though risen was not yet king.

entries.zh: 臣視山河壯麗處多，故都已盛而衰，難可興已；
entries.en: Your servant has observed that majestic mountains and rivers are abundant elsewhere, while the old capital has already flourished and declined and can hardly be revived again;
entries.literal: Your servant views many places where mountains and rivers are majestic; therefore the old capital flourished then declined, hard to revive;

entries.zh: 江南土薄水淺，人心囂浮輕巧，不可以都；
entries.en: south of the Yangtze the soil is thin and the waters shallow, and the people's hearts are restless, frivolous, and clever—it cannot serve as a capital;
entries.literal: South of the Yangtze soil thin water shallow, people's hearts noisy floating and clever—cannot be capital;

entries.zh: 河北土厚水深，人心強愎狠戾，不可以都。
entries.en: north of the Yellow River the soil is thick and the waters deep, but the people's hearts are stubborn, fierce, and cruel—it too cannot serve as a capital.
entries.literal: Hebei soil thick water deep, people's hearts strong obstinate fierce cruel—cannot be capital.

entries.zh: 惟襄、鄧實惟中原，人心質良，去秦咫尺，而有上洛為之限，永無夷狄侵軼之虞，此建都之極選也。」
entries.en: Only Xiang and Deng are truly the central plains. The people there are plain and good-hearted. They lie within a stone's throw of Qin, yet Shangluo forms a natural barrier, so there would forever be no fear of barbarian raids. This is the finest possible choice for establishing the capital."
entries.literal: Only Xiang and Deng are truly central plains; people's hearts plain and good; close to Qin by a foot and Shangluo as its limit—forever no barbarian invasion worry—this is the extreme choice for establishing capital."

entries.zh: 不報。
entries.en: The throne gave no reply.
entries.literal: There was no response.

entries.zh: 中書舍人令狐渙任機巧，帝嘗欲以當國，俄又悔曰：「渙作宰相或誤國，朕當先用卿。」
entries.en: The Secretariat drafter Linghu Huan was skilled in intrigue. The emperor once wished to put him in charge of government, but soon regretted it and said, "If Huan becomes chancellor he may ruin the state. I ought to use you first."
entries.literal: Secretariat Drafter Linghu Huan was skilled in schemes; the emperor once wished to make him hold government; soon again regretted: "Huan as chancellor might ruin the state—I should first use you."

entries.zh: 辭曰：「渙再世宰相，練故事，陛下業已許之。
entries.en: Wo declined, saying, "Huan comes from two generations of chancellors and is thoroughly versed in precedent. Your Majesty has already promised him the post.
entries.literal: Wo declined: "Huan is a twice-generation chancellor, skilled in precedents; Your Majesty already promised him.

entries.zh: 若許渙可改，許臣獨不可移乎？」
entries.en: If a promise to Huan may be changed, may a promise to me alone not be changed as well?"
entries.literal: If permitting Huan can be changed, permitting your servant alone cannot be moved?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「我未嘗面命，亦何憚？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I never gave him the appointment in person. What is there to fear?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I never commanded face to face—what is there to fear?"

entries.zh: 偓因薦御史大夫趙崇勁正雅重，可以準繩中外。
entries.en: Wo then recommended Censor-in-Chief Zhao Chong, a man of stern integrity and weighty character who could serve as a standard for the court and the realm.
entries.literal: Wo thereby recommended Censor-in-Chief Zhao Chong upright, elegant, and weighty, able to be the standard inside and outside.

entries.zh: 帝知偓，崇門生也，嘆其能讓。
entries.en: The emperor knew that Wo had been Zhao Chong's student and marveled at his willingness to yield.
entries.literal: The emperor knew Wo was Chong's student and sighed at his ability to yield.

entries.zh: 初，李繼昭等以功皆進同中書門下平章事，時謂「三使相」，後稍稍更附韓全誨、周敬容，皆忌胤。
entries.en: At first Li Jizhao and the others were all promoted to Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery for their merits, and the age called them the "Three Commissioner-Chancellors." Later they gradually attached themselves to Han Quanhui and Zhou Jingrong, and all came to resent Cui Yin.
entries.literal: At first Li Jizhao and others for merit all advanced Co-Director; the time called "three commissioner-chancellors"; later gradually more attached to Han Quanhui and Zhou Jingrong—all resented Yin.

entries.zh: 胤聞，召鳳翔李茂貞入朝，使留族子繼筠宿衛。
entries.en: When Yin heard of this, he summoned Li Maozhen of Fengxiang to court and had Maozhen's clansman Li Jiyun remain behind as an inner guard.
entries.literal: Yin heard and summoned Fengxiang Li Maozhen to court, had his clan nephew Jiyun remain as inner guard.

entries.zh: 偓聞，以為不可，胤不納。
entries.en: When Wo heard of this, he regarded the plan as unwise, but Yin would not listen.
entries.literal: Wo heard, thought it impossible; Yin did not accept.

entries.zh: 偓又語令狐渙，渙曰：「吾屬不惜宰相邪？
entries.en: Wo spoke again to Linghu Huan. Huan said, "Do you think men like us do not value the chancellorship?
entries.literal: Wo again spoke to Linghu Huan; Huan said: "Our sort does not cherish the chancellorship?

entries.zh: 無衛軍則為閹豎所圖矣。」
entries.en: Without guard troops we shall be plotted against by the eunuchs."
entries.literal: Without guard troops we will be schemed against by the eunuchs."

entries.zh: 偓曰：「不然。
entries.en: Wo said, "That is not so.
entries.literal: Wo said: "Not so.

entries.zh: 無兵則家與國安，有兵則家與國不可保。」
entries.en: Without troops, both family and state may be secure; with troops, neither family nor state can be preserved."
entries.literal: Without troops then family and state are secure; with troops then family and state cannot be preserved."

entries.zh: 胤聞，憂，未知所出。
entries.en: When Yin heard this, he grew anxious and did not know what to do.
entries.literal: When Yin heard he was worried and did not know what course to take.

entries.zh: 李彥弼見帝倨甚，帝不平，偓請逐之，赦其黨許自新，則狂謀自破，帝不用。
entries.en: Li Yanbi behaved with great arrogance when he met the emperor, and the emperor was displeased. Wo asked that Yanbi be expelled and his followers pardoned on condition of reform, saying that their reckless plots would then collapse of themselves, but the emperor did not adopt the plan.
entries.literal: Li Yanbi when seeing the emperor was very arrogant; the emperor was displeased; Wo asked to expel him, pardon his faction allowing renewal, then mad plots would break themselves; the emperor did not use this.

entries.zh: 彥弼譖偓及渙漏禁省語，不可與圖政，帝怒，曰：「卿有官屬，日夕議事，奈何不欲我見學士邪？」
entries.en: Yanbi slandered Wo and Huan for leaking inner-court secrets and said they were unfit to take part in governing. The emperor grew angry and said, "You have your own officials discussing affairs day and night—why do you not wish me to see the academicians?"
entries.literal: Yanbi slandered Wo and Huan for leaking forbidden-palace speech, unfit to plan government; the emperor was angry and said: "You have official subordinates discussing affairs day and night—why do you not wish me to see the academicians?"

entries.zh: 繼昭等飲殿中自如，帝怒，偓曰：「三使相有功，不如厚與金帛官爵，毋使豫政事。
entries.en: Jizhao and the others drank freely in the hall as though it were their own house, and the emperor was furious. Wo said, "The Three Commissioner-Chancellors have rendered service. It would be better to reward them generously with gold, silk, offices, and titles, and not allow them to take part in government affairs.
entries.literal: Jizhao and others drank in the hall as they pleased; the emperor was angry; Wo said: "The three commissioner-chancellors have merit—better to give them generously gold, silk, offices and ranks, and not let them participate in government affairs.

entries.zh: 今宰相不得顓決事，繼昭輩所奏必聽。
entries.en: At present the chancellor cannot decide affairs on his own, and whatever Jizhao and his associates submit must be heard.
entries.literal: Now the chancellor cannot exclusively decide affairs; whatever Jizhao's crowd memorializes must be heard.

entries.zh: 它日遽改，則人人生怨。
entries.en: If policy is suddenly changed another day, everyone will harbor resentment.
entries.literal: If one day it is suddenly changed, then everyone will harbor resentment.

entries.zh: 初以衛兵檢中人，今敕使、衛兵為一，臣竊寒心，願詔茂貞還其衛軍。
entries.en: At first the guard troops were used to keep watch over the inner attendants. Now the edict-envoys and the guards have become one body, and I am privately filled with dread. I beg that an edict be issued ordering Maozhen to withdraw his guard troops.
entries.literal: At first guards inspected the inner attendants; now edict-envoys and guards are one—I privately feel chilled in heart and wish to edict Maozhen to return his guard army.

entries.zh: 不然，兩鎮兵鬥闕下，朝廷危矣。」
entries.en: Otherwise the armies of the two commands will fight beneath the palace gates, and the court will be in grave peril."
entries.literal: Otherwise the two commands' troops will fight below the palace gates and the court will be in peril."

entries.zh: 及胤召朱全忠討全誨，汴兵將至，偓勸胤督茂貞還衛卒。
entries.en: When Yin summoned Zhu Quanzhong to attack Quanhui and the Bian armies were about to arrive, Wo urged Yin to press Maozhen to withdraw his guard troops.
entries.literal: When Yin summoned Zhu Quanzhong to attack Quanhui, Bian troops were about to arrive; Wo urged Yin to press Maozhen to return the guard soldiers.

entries.zh: 又勸表暴內臣罪，因誅全誨等；
entries.en: He also urged that a memorial be submitted exposing the crimes of the inner attendants so that Quanhui and the others might be executed;
entries.literal: He also urged a memorial exposing the inner attendants' crimes and thereby executing Quanhui and others;

entries.zh: 若茂貞不如詔，即許全忠入朝。
entries.en: and if Maozhen did not obey the edict, then Quanzhong should be permitted to enter the capital.
entries.literal: if Maozhen did not follow the edict, then permit Quanzhong to enter court.

entries.zh: 未及用，而全誨等已劫帝西幸。
entries.en: Before these plans could be carried out, Quanhui and the others had already seized the emperor and forced him west on campaign.
entries.literal: Before this could be used, Quanhui and others had already seized the emperor on a western flight.

entries.zh: 畢崔劉陸鄭朱韓
entries.en: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, and Han.
entries.literal: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, Han.

entries.zh: 涔陽耕得古鐘，高尺餘，收扣之，曰：「此姑洗角也。」
entries.en: Plowing at Cenyang he turned up an ancient bell more than a foot high; Shou struck it and said, "This is the jue pitch of Guxian."
entries.literal: While plowing at Cenyang he unearthed an ancient bell more than a foot high; Shou struck it and said: "This is the jue of Guxian."

entries.zh: 既劀拭，有刻在兩欒，果然。
entries.en: Once scraped and cleaned, an inscription on both raised bands proved him right.
entries.literal: After it was scraped and wiped clean, there was an inscription on both raised bands, and it was indeed so.

entries.zh: 嘗言：「琴通黃鐘、姑洗、無射三均，側出諸調，由羅蔦附灌木然。」
entries.en: He once said, "The qin spans the three keys of Huangzhong, Guxian, and Wuyi; subsidiary modes branch off like bindweed clinging to shrubs."
entries.literal: He once said: "The qin connects the three keys of Huangzhong, Guxian, and Wuyi; the subsidiary modes branch out like convolvulus clinging to shrubs."

entries.zh: 時有安涚者，世稱善琴，且知音。
entries.en: At the time there was An Shu, renowned for skill on the qin and for understanding music.
entries.literal: At the time there was An Shu, whom the age called skilled at the qin and also knowledgeable in music.

entries.zh: 收問：「五弦外，其二雲何？」
entries.en: Shou asked, "Beyond the five strings, what are the other two?"
entries.literal: Shou asked: "Beyond the five strings, what are the other two?"

entries.zh: 涚曰：「世謂周文、武二王所加者。」
entries.en: Shu said, "People say Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou added them."
entries.literal: Shu said: "The age says they were added by Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou."

entries.zh: 收曰：「能為《文王操》乎？」
entries.en: Shou said, "Can you play the Ballad of King Wen?"
entries.literal: Shou said: "Can you perform the 'Ballad of King Wen'?"

entries.zh: 涚即以黃鐘為宮而奏之，以少商應大弦，收曰：「止！
entries.en: Shu at once took Huangzhong as tonic and played, answering the great string with lesser shang; Shou said, "Stop!
entries.literal: Shu immediately took Huangzhong as the tonic and played it, answering the great string with the lesser shang; Shou said: "Stop!

entries.zh: 如子之言，少商，武弦也。
entries.en: As you say, lesser shang is King Wu's string.
entries.literal: As you say, the lesser shang is the string of King Wu.

entries.zh: 且文世安得武聲乎？」
entries.en: Besides, how could King Wu's sound appear in King Wen's age?"
entries.literal: Moreover, how could there be the sound of Wu in the age of Wen?"

entries.zh: 涚大驚，因問樂意，收曰：「樂亡久矣。
entries.en: Shu was astonished and asked about musical meaning; Shou said, "Music has been lost for a long time.
entries.literal: Shu was greatly startled and then asked about musical meaning; Shou said: "Music has long been lost.

entries.zh: 上古祀天地宗廟，皆不用商。
entries.en: In high antiquity, sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples all avoided the shang mode.
entries.literal: In high antiquity, sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples all avoided shang.

entries.zh: 周人歌大呂、舞《雲門》以俟天神，歌太蔟、舞《鹹池》以俟地祇。
entries.en: The Zhou sang Dalü and danced the Cloud Gate to await the heavenly spirit, and sang Taicu and danced the Brine Pool to await the earthly spirit.
entries.literal: The Zhou people sang Dalü and danced the "Cloud Gate" to await the spirit of Heaven, and sang Taicu and danced the "Brine Pool" to await the spirit of Earth.

entries.zh: 大呂、黃鐘之合，陽聲之首。
entries.en: The pairing of Dalü and Huangzhong is the head of the yang pitches.
entries.literal: The union of Dalü and Huangzhong is the head of the yang pitches.

entries.zh: 而《雲門》，黃帝樂也；
entries.en: Yet the Cloud Gate is the Yellow Emperor's music;
entries.literal: Yet the "Cloud Gate" is the music of the Yellow Emperor;

entries.zh: 《鹹池》，堯樂也。
entries.en: the Brine Pool is Yao's music.
entries.literal: the "Brine Pool" is the music of Yao.

entries.zh: 不敢用黃鐘，而以太蔟次之。
entries.en: They dared not use Huangzhong and therefore set Taicu next instead.
entries.literal: They dared not use Huangzhong and therefore placed Taicu next.

entries.zh: 然則祭天者，圜鐘為宮，黃鐘為角，太蔟為徵，姑洗為羽；
entries.en: Thus for sacrifices to Heaven, Yuanzhong was tonic, Huangzhong jue, Taicu zhi, and Guxian yu;
entries.literal: Thus for sacrifices to Heaven, Yuanzhong served as tonic, Huangzhong as jue, Taicu as zhi, and Guxian as yu;

entries.zh: 祭地者，函鐘為宮，太蔟為角，姑洗為徵，南呂為羽。
entries.en: for sacrifices to Earth, Hanzhong was tonic, Taicu jue, Guxian zhi, and Nanlü yu.
entries.literal: for sacrifices to Earth, Hanzhong served as tonic, Taicu as jue, Guxian as zhi, and Nanlü as yu.

entries.zh: 訖不用商及二少。
entries.en: In the end shang and the two lesser pitches were never used.
entries.literal: In the end shang and the two lesser pitches were not used.

entries.zh: 蓋商聲剛而二少聲下，所以取其正、裁其繁也。
entries.en: For shang is forceful and the two lesser pitches are low—this was to keep what is correct and cut away excess.
entries.literal: For shang is a forceful pitch and the two lesser pitches are low—this was to take what is correct and trim what is excessive.

entries.zh: 漢祭天則用商，而宗廟不用，謂鬼神畏商之剛。
entries.en: The Han used shang for sacrifices to Heaven but not in the ancestral temple, saying spirits fear shang's force.
entries.literal: The Han used shang in sacrifices to Heaven but not in the ancestral temple, saying that spirits fear the force of shang.

entries.zh: 西京諸儒惑圜鐘、函鐘之說，故其自受命，郊祀、宗廟樂，唯用黃鐘一均。
entries.en: Western Capital scholars were misled by doctrines of Yuanzhong and Hanzhong, so from receiving the Mandate onward suburban and ancestral temple music used only the Huangzhong key.
entries.literal: The scholars of the Western Capital were confused by the doctrines of Yuanzhong and Hanzhong, and so from the time they received the Mandate, suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple music used only the single key of Huangzhong.

entries.zh: 章帝時，太常丞鮑業始旋十二宮。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhang, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Bao Ye first rotated the twelve keys.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhang, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Bao Ye first rotated the twelve keys.

entries.zh: 夫旋宮以七聲為均，均，言韻也，古無韻字，猶言一韻聲也。
entries.en: Rotating keys treats the seven pitches as a key; jun means rhyme—in antiquity there was no separate character for rhyme, so it is like speaking of one rhyming sound.
entries.literal: Rotating keys takes the seven pitches as a key; jun means rhyme—in antiquity there was no character for rhyme, so it is as if one spoke of a single rhyming sound.

entries.zh: 始以某律為宮，某律為商，某律為角，某律為徵，某律為羽，某律少宮，某律少徵，亦曰『變』，曰『比』。
entries.en: First one pitch serves as tonic, another as shang, jue, zhi, yu, lesser tonic, and lesser zhi—also called change and comparison.
entries.literal: First one pitch is taken as tonic, another as shang, another as jue, another as zhi, another as yu, another as lesser tonic, another as lesser zhi—also called "change" and "comparison."

entries.zh: 一均成則五聲為之節族，此旋宮也。」
entries.en: When one key is complete, the five pitches form its scale—this is key rotation."
entries.literal: When one key is complete, the five pitches form its scale degrees—this is rotating keys."

entries.zh: 乃取律次之以示
entries.en: He then arranged the pitches in order to show
entries.literal: He then arranged the pitches in order to show

entries.zh: 馬楊路盧
entries.en: Ma, Yang, Lu, and Lu
entries.literal: Ma, Yang, Lu, and Lu

entries.zh: 始，全忠擊楊行密不能克，諷荊、襄、青、徐等道請己為都統以討行密，帝猗違未報；
entries.en: Earlier Quanzhong had attacked Yang Xingmi without success and prompted the Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to ask that he be made overall commander against Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and gave no answer;
entries.literal: At first Quanzhong attacked Yang Xingmi but could not overcome him; he prompted Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to request that he be made overall commander to attack Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and did not reply;

entries.zh: 而珂與太原、鎮定等道亦請加行密都統，以討全忠。
entries.en: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits asked that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.
entries.literal: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits also requested that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.

entries.zh: 繇是兩罷之，全忠怨珂，不忘也。
entries.en: Both requests were denied. Quanzhong resented Ke and never forgot it.
entries.literal: therefore both requests were set aside. Quanzhong resented Ke and did not forget it.

entries.zh: 帝為劉季述所廢，珂憤見言色，屢陳討賊謀。
entries.en: When Liu Jishu deposed the emperor, Ke's rage showed plainly in word and face, and he repeatedly urged plans to attack the rebels.
entries.literal: When the emperor was deposed by Liu Jishu, Ke's anger showed in his words and expression; he repeatedly presented plans to attack the rebels.

entries.zh: 既反正，首獻方物，帝甚倚之。
entries.en: After the restoration he was the first to present tribute, and the emperor relied on him heavily.
entries.literal: After the restoration he was first to present local products; the emperor relied on him greatly.

entries.zh: 而全忠以克用方強，不敢加兵。
entries.en: Quanzhong, however, dared not attack while Keyong was still strong.
entries.literal: But Quanzhong, because Keyong was then strong, did not dare send troops against him.

entries.zh: 及王镕詘服，拔定州，而克用兵折，乃謂其將張存敬曰：「珂恃太原侮慢我，爾持一繩縛之。」
entries.en: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture fell, and Keyong's armies were spent, he told his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke leans on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."
entries.literal: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture was taken, and Keyong's military strength was broken, he then said to his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke relies on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."

entries.zh: 存敬以兵數萬度河，由含山襲，絳州刺史陶建釗、晉州刺史張漢瑜皆降，以何絪戍之，進攻珂。
entries.en: Cunjing crossed the river with tens of thousands of men and struck through Hanshan. The governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He left He Yin to garrison the region and marched against Ke.
entries.literal: Cunjing led tens of thousands of troops across the river, struck by way of Hanshan, and the governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He garrisoned the territory with He Yin and advanced to attack Ke.

entries.zh: 全忠率師繼進，即劾珂交構克用，為方鎮生事，不可赦。
entries.en: Quanzhong followed with his main army and immediately impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—an offense that could not be pardoned.
entries.literal: Quanzhong led his army in continued advance and at once impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—unforgivable.

entries.zh: 珂乞師太原，為絪所迮，不能進。
entries.en: Ke begged Taiyuan for troops, but Yin blocked them and they could not get through.
entries.literal: Ke begged troops from Taiyuan, but was hemmed in by Yin and they could not advance.

entries.zh: 珂急使妻遺克用書曰：「賊攻我，朝夕見俘，乞食大梁矣。」
entries.en: In desperation Ke sent his wife to Keyong with a letter: "The enemy presses me; I may be captured any day—I shall soon be begging bread in Daliang."
entries.literal: Ke in urgency sent his wife with a letter to Keyong, saying, "The rebels attack me; any day I may be captured—I shall soon be begging food in Daliang."

entries.zh: 克用答曰：「道且斷，往救必俱亡，不如歸朝廷。」
entries.en: Keyong answered, "The roads will soon be cut. If I march to save you we shall both perish. Better submit to the court."
entries.literal: Keyong replied, "The roads are about to be cut; if I go to rescue you we shall both perish. Better to submit to the court."

entries.zh: 珂窮，遣使告李茂貞曰：「上初反正，詔藩鎮無相疑。
entries.en: Cornered, Ke sent envoys to Li Maozhen: "When the emperor first restored order, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.
entries.literal: Ke, at his wits' end, sent envoys to tell Li Maozhen, "When His Majesty first restored the throne, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.

entries.zh: 而朱公不顧約，以攻弊邑。
entries.en: Yet Lord Zhu has broken the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.
entries.literal: Yet Lord Zhu disregarded the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.

entries.zh: 弊邑亡，則邠、岐非君所保，天子神器斂手付人矣。
entries.en: If my commandery falls, you cannot hold Bin and Qi, and the Son of Heaven's regalia will pass into another's hands.
entries.literal: If my commandery falls, then Bin and Qi will not be yours to protect, and the Son of Heaven's sacred regalia will pass into another's hands with folded arms.

entries.zh: 宜與華州韓公出精銳固潼關，以張兵勢。
entries.en: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending elite troops to hold Tong Pass and show military strength.
entries.literal: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending crack troops to secure Tong Pass and display military strength.

entries.zh: 仆不武，公其惠我西偏地，以為扞守。
entries.en: I am no fighter—grant me the western districts as a defensive hold.
entries.literal: I am not martial—would you grant me the western districts as a defensive hold?

entries.zh: 蒲，請公自有之。
entries.en: As for Pu, I beg you to take it for yourself.
entries.literal: As for Pu, I beg that you take it for yourself.

entries.zh: 關西安危，國祚長短，系公此舉也。」
entries.en: The fate of Guanxi—and the dynasty's future—rests on what you do now."
entries.literal: The security of Guanxi hangs in the balance; the length of the dynasty's fortune depends on this move of yours."

entries.zh: 茂貞不答。
entries.en: Maozhen did not answer.
entries.literal: Maozhen did not reply.

entries.zh: 方立倚朱全忠為助，故克用擊邢、洺、磁無虛歲，地為鬥場，人不能稼。
entries.en: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for support, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci almost every year; the land became a battlefield and farming ceased.
entries.literal: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for aid, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci year after year without pause; the land became a battleground and people could not farm.

entries.zh: 光啟二年，克修擊邢州取故鎮，進攻武安。
entries.en: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced on Wu'an.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced against Wu'an.

entries.zh: 方立將呂臻、馬爽戰焦岡，為克修所破，斬首萬級，執臻等，拔武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河。
entries.en: Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang and were routed by Kexiu; ten thousand heads were taken, Zhen and others captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe fell.
