entries.zh: 悟獨表師古子明安為朗州司戶參軍。
entries.en: Wu alone petitioned to name Shigu's son Ming'an registrar at Langzhou.
entries.literal: Wu alone memorialized to appoint Shigu's son Ming'an as registrar of Lang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 親將王承慶，承宗弟也，師道以兄女妻之，潛約左右，欲因肄兵執師道，會悟入，出奔徐州，歸朝。
entries.en: Wang Chengqing, a favored commander and younger brother of Chengzong, whom Shidao had married to his elder brother's daughter, had plotted with his men to arrest Shidao during maneuvers; when Wu stormed the city he fled to Xuzhou and defected to the court.
entries.literal: The intimate general Wang Chengqing, younger brother of Chengzong, whom Shidao had married to his elder brother's daughter, secretly agreed with those close to him to seize Shidao during drill; when Wu entered the city he fled to Xuzhou and submitted to the court.

entries.zh: 程日華，定州安喜人，始名華，德宗以其有功，益曰日華。
entries.en: Cheng Rihua, a native of Anxi in Dingzhou, was originally named Hua; Emperor Dezong, honoring his service, enlarged his name to Rihua.
entries.literal: Cheng Rihua was a man of Anxi in Ding Prefecture; his original name was Hua; Dezong, because of his merit, added the character Ri to make Rihua.

entries.zh: 父元皓為安祿山帳下，偽署定州刺史，故日華籍本軍，為張孝忠牙將。
entries.en: His father Yuanhao had served An Lushan as puppet prefect of Dingzhou; Rihua entered the home army and became a guard officer under Zhang Xiaozhong.
entries.literal: His father Yuanhao had been in An Lushan's camp and was falsely appointed prefect of Ding Prefecture; therefore Rihua was registered in the native army and served as Zhang Xiaozhong's guard officer.

entries.zh: 滄，故成德部州也，孝忠絕李惟嶽，德宗以滄畀義武。
entries.en: Cangzhou had belonged to Chengde; when Xiaozhong broke with Li Weiyue, Dezong awarded it to Yiwu.
entries.literal: Cang was formerly a prefecture of Chengde; Xiaozhong broke with Li Weiyue, and Dezong gave Cang to Yiwu.

entries.zh: 前刺史李固烈與惟嶽姻屬，即牢守。
entries.en: The outgoing prefect Li Gulie, Weiyue's kinsman by marriage, barricaded himself in the city.
entries.literal: The former prefect Li Gulie was related by marriage to Weiyue and at once held the city fast.

entries.zh: 孝忠令日華往喻之，固烈請還恒州。
entries.en: Xiaozhong sent Rihua to reason with him; Gulie agreed to withdraw to Hengzhou.
entries.literal: Xiaozhong ordered Rihua to go persuade him; Gulie asked to return to Heng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 既治裝，悉帑以行，軍中怒曰：「馬瘠，士饑死，刺史不棄豪發恤吾急，今刮地以去，吾等何望？」
entries.en: As he packed to leave with every coin he could carry, the troops raged: "Our horses are starved, our men dying of hunger, and the prefect won't spare a penny—now he strips the place bare. What hope is left for us?"
entries.literal: When he had packed, he took all his wealth with him; the army raged, saying: "The horses are lean, the soldiers starving to death—the prefect will not spare a hair to relieve our distress, yet now he scrapes the land bare and leaves—what hope have we?"

entries.zh: 遂共殺固烈，屠其家。
entries.en: They killed Gulie and massacred his family.
entries.literal: They then together killed Gulie and slaughtered his household.

entries.zh: 日華驚匿床下，將士迎出之曰：「暴吾軍者已死，何畏而亡？」
entries.en: Rihua hid under a bed in terror; the soldiers pulled him out, saying, "The man who wronged us is dead—why should you flee?"
entries.literal: Rihua in alarm hid under a bed; officers and soldiers brought him out, saying: "He who wronged our army is dead—why fear and flee?"

entries.zh: 共逼領州。
entries.en: They pressed him to take command of the prefecture.
entries.literal: Together they compelled him to take charge of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 孝忠亦以日華寬厚，遂假以刺史。
entries.en: Xiaozhong, impressed by Rihua's generous character, confirmed him as acting prefect.
entries.literal: Xiaozhong also, because Rihua was generous and mild, thereupon provisionally appointed him prefect.

entries.zh: ◎藩鎮淄青橫海李正己，高麗人。
entries.en: In the biographies of the Ziqing and Henghai buffer regions, Li Zhengji was of Koguryo descent.
entries.literal: Buffer Regions: Ziqing and Henghai. Li Zhengji was a man of Goguryeo origin.

entries.zh: 為營州副將，從侯希逸入青州，希逸母即其姑，故薦為折沖都尉。
entries.en: He had been deputy commander at Yingzhou and followed Hou Xiyi into Qingzhou; because Xiyi's mother was his aunt, Xiyi recommended him as regimental commander of the Zhechong unit.
entries.literal: He served as deputy general of Ying Prefecture, followed Hou Xiyi into Qing Prefecture; Xiyi's mother was his paternal aunt, so he was recommended as commander of the Zhechong regiment.

entries.zh: 寶應中，以軍候從討史朝義。
entries.en: During the Baoying reign (762–763), he served as a military scout in the campaign against Shi Chaoyi.
entries.literal: In the Baoying era, as a military scout he followed the campaign against Shi Chaoyi.

entries.zh: 時回紇恃功橫，諸軍莫敢抗。
entries.en: The Uyghurs, flush with their victories, threw their weight around, and no allied army dared stand up to them.
entries.literal: At that time the Uyghurs relied on their merit and acted overbearingly; none of the armies dared resist.

entries.zh: 正己欲以氣折之，與大酋角逐，眾土皆墻立觀，約曰：「後者批之。」
entries.en: Zhengji meant to humble them by sheer nerve and challenged the Uyghur chieftain to a footrace; the troops lined the walls to watch, with the wager that "whoever finished second would have his face struck."
entries.literal: Zhengji wished to break their spirit by force of will; he raced the great chieftain, and all the men stood along the wall watching, with the agreement: "Whoever comes in behind gets his face slapped."

entries.zh: 既逐而先，正己批其頰，回紇矢液流離，眾軍哄然笑。
entries.en: Though he had chased from behind, he crossed the line first and slapped the chieftain across the face; the Uyghur was left trembling and drenched in sweat, and the whole army roared with laughter.
entries.literal: Having overtaken him yet arriving first, Zhengji slapped his cheek; the Uyghur was drenched in sweat and urine, and the armies burst into laughter.

entries.zh: 酋大慚，自是沮憚不敢暴。
entries.en: The chieftain was utterly humiliated; thereafter the Uyghurs were cowed and no longer dared abuse their position.
entries.literal: The chieftain was deeply shamed; from then on he was discouraged and afraid and did not dare act violently.

entries.zh: 希逸以為兵馬使，沈毅得眾心，然陰忌之，因事解其職。
entries.en: Xiyi made him director of military affairs; his steady, resolute manner won the soldiers' loyalty, but Xiyi secretly resented him and found a pretext to strip him of his post.
entries.literal: Xiyi appointed him military commissioner; his gravity and resolution won the hearts of the troops, yet Xiyi secretly envied him and removed him from office on a pretext.

entries.zh: 軍中皆言不當廢，尋逐希逸出之，有詔代為節度使。
entries.en: The troops protested that he should never have been removed; before long they expelled Xiyi, and an imperial edict installed Zhengji as military governor in his place.
entries.literal: The army all said he should not have been dismissed; soon they drove Xiyi out, and an edict named him to replace him as military governor.

entries.zh: 本名懷玉，至是賜今名，遂有淄、青、齊、海、登、萊、沂、密、德、棣十州，與田承嗣、薛嵩、李寶臣、梁崇義輔牙相倚。
entries.en: Born Huaiyu, he now received the name Zhengji by imperial grant. He came to control ten prefectures—Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di—and stood shoulder to shoulder with the buffer lords Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, Li Baochen, and Liang Chongyi.
entries.literal: His original name was Huaiyu; at this time he was granted his present name. He then held the ten prefectures of Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di, and with Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, Li Baochen, and Liang Chongyi he leaned on one another like cheek teeth.

entries.zh: 嵩死，李靈耀反，諸道攻之，共披其地。
entries.en: After Xue Song's death, Li Lingyao rose in revolt; the allied circuits besieged him and carved up his domain among themselves.
entries.literal: When Song died, Li Lingyao rebelled; the various circuits attacked him and together stripped his territory.

entries.zh: 正己復取曹、濮、徐、兗、鄆，凡十有五州。
entries.en: Zhengji seized Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun as well, bringing his holdings to fifteen prefectures.
entries.literal: Zhengji again took Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun, fifteen prefectures in all.

entries.zh: 市渤海名馬，歲不絕，賦繇均約，號最強大。
entries.en: He bought famed Bohai horses without interruption, kept taxes and labor service fair and predictable, and was reckoned the most powerful of the buffer lords.
entries.literal: He traded for famous horses of Bohai year after year without cease; levies and corvée were even and measured, and he was called the strongest of all.

entries.zh: 政令嚴酷，在所不敢偶語，威震鄰境。
entries.en: His rule was mercilessly strict—no one in his territory dared whisper in company—and his authority terrified the neighboring provinces.
entries.literal: His government orders were harsh; within his domain no one dared speak casually in pairs, and his might awed the neighboring circuits.

entries.zh: 歷檢校司空，加同中書門下平章事，以司徒兼太子太保，封饒陽郡王。
entries.en: He rose through acting Minister of Works, was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, served as Grand Mentor while also Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang commandery.
entries.literal: He rose through acting Minister of Works, was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, served as Grand Mentor while also Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang commandery.

entries.zh: 請附屬籍，許之。
entries.en: He petitioned to be entered on the imperial clan rolls, and the court consented.
entries.literal: He requested attachment to the imperial clan register; this was granted.

entries.zh: 因徙治鄆，以子納及腹心將守諸州。
entries.en: He shifted his headquarters to Yunzhou and left his son Li Na and his closest generals to hold the outlying prefectures.
entries.literal: He therefore moved his seat of government to Yun, placing his son Na and trusted generals to guard the various prefectures.

entries.zh: 執宜死，子赤心嗣。
entries.en: When Zhuyi died, his son Chixin succeeded him.
entries.literal: Zhuyi died; his son Chixin succeeded.

entries.zh: 開成四年，回鶻徑磧口，抵榆林塞。
entries.en: In Kaicheng 4 (839) the Uyghurs marched straight through the desert pass and reached the Yulin frontier.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng the Uyghurs went straight through the desert pass and reached Yulin frontier.

entries.zh: 宰相掘羅勿以良馬三百遺赤心，約共攻彰信可汗。
entries.en: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and proposed a joint attack on Khan Zhangxin.
entries.literal: Chancellor Jueluowu sent Chixin three hundred fine horses and agreed to attack Khan Zhangxin together.

entries.zh: 可汗死，節度使劉沔以沙陀擊回鶻於殺胡山。
entries.en: After the khan's death, Military Governor Liu Mian led the Shatuo against the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.
entries.literal: When the khan died, Military Governor Liu Mian used the Shatuo to strike the Uyghurs at Shahu Mountain.

entries.zh: 久之，伐潞，誅劉稹，詔赤心率代北騎軍三千隸石雄為前軍，破石會關，助王宰下天井，合太原軍，次榆社，與監軍使呂義忠禽楊弁。
entries.en: Later, in the campaign against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai horsemen under Shi Xiong as the vanguard. They stormed Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined forces with the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and together with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.
entries.literal: After a time, campaigning against Lu to execute Liu Zhen, Chixin was ordered to lead three thousand Northern Dai cavalry under Shi Xiong as vanguard; they broke Shihui Pass, helped Wang Zai take Tianjing, joined the Taiyuan army, encamped at Yushe, and with Army Supervisor Lü Yizhong captured Yang Bian.

entries.zh: 潞州平，遷朔州刺史，仍為代北軍使。
entries.en: After Luzhou was pacified he was transferred to prefect of Shuozhou while retaining command of the Northern Dai army.
entries.literal: When Luzhou was pacified, he was moved to prefect of Shuozhou and remained Northern Dai army commander.

entries.zh: 大順初，克用自攻赫連鐸於雲州，拔東郛。
entries.en: Early in the Dashun era Keyong personally attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and captured the eastern suburb.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dashun, Keyong himself attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou and took the eastern suburb.

entries.zh: 幽州李匡威以兵三萬救之，殺其將安金俊，克用走。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand men to the rescue, killed Keyong's general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.
entries.literal: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou brought thirty thousand to rescue him, killed his general An Jinjun, and Keyong fled.

entries.zh: 鐸與匡威共建言：「山南亂，克用實首之。
entries.en: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains was chiefly Keyong's doing.
entries.literal: Duo and Kuangwei jointly memorialized: "The turmoil in the southern mountains—Keyong was truly its author.

entries.zh: 今乘其敗，可伐而取也。」
entries.en: Now that he is defeated, he can be attacked and destroyed."
entries.literal: Now, taking advantage of his defeat, he can be attacked and taken."

entries.zh: 全忠亦請與河北三鎮共討之。
entries.en: Quanzhong likewise asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.
entries.literal: Quanzhong also asked to join the three Hebei circuits in attacking him.

entries.zh: 宰相張浚是其計，乃下制削克用官爵、屬籍，以浚為兵馬招討、制置、宣慰使，京兆尹孫揆副之，樞密使駱全諲為行營都監，華州節度使韓建為行營馬步都虞候兼供軍糧料使，王镕領河東東面，全忠南面，李匡威北面，並為行營招討使。
entries.en: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan. An edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register. Zhang Jun was appointed campaign commander, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner, with Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui as deputy, Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian as campaign supervisor, and Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian as chief adjutant and provisions commissioner. Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, and Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.
entries.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jun approved the plan; an edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register; Jun was made campaign commander for horse troops, disposition commissioner, and pacification commissioner; Jingzhao Prefect Sun Kui was his deputy; Privy Councilor Luo Quanqian was campaign supervisor; Huazhou Military Governor Han Jian was campaign horse-and-foot chief adjutant and army provisions commissioner; Wang Rong commanded the eastern Hedong front, Quanzhong the south, Li Kuangwei the north—all as campaign commanders.

entries.zh: 鐸副匡威，先薄戰。
entries.en: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.
entries.literal: Duo served under Kuangwei and pressed the attack first.

entries.zh: 克用追潞兵，不肯行，共殺守將李克恭，送款於汴，南首闕下。
entries.en: Keyong pursued the Lu troops, but they refused to march, killed garrison commander Li Kejing, submitted to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.
entries.literal: Keyong pursued the Lu troops; they refused to march; together they killed the garrison commander Li Kejing, sent submission to Bian, and turned south toward the palace.

entries.zh: 更詔揆為昭義節度使，克用將李存孝邀揆長子殺之。
entries.en: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi. Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.
entries.literal: Sun Kui was reappointed military governor of Zhaoyi; Keyong's officer Li Cunxiao ambushed and killed Kui's eldest son.

entries.zh: 匡威、鐸並吐蕃、黠戛斯眾十萬攻遮虜軍，殺其將劉胡子。
entries.en: Kuangwei and Duo, with one hundred thousand Tibetan and Qarluk allies, attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.
entries.literal: Kuangwei and Duo with Tibetan and Qarluk forces numbering one hundred thousand attacked Zhelu Army and killed its commander Liu Huzi.

entries.zh: 克用乃屯渾河川，存孝與鐸戰樂安，鐸敗走。
entries.en: Keyong encamped on the Hun River. Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an and drove him off.
entries.literal: Keyong then encamped on the Hun River; Cunxiao fought Duo at Le'an; Duo was defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 浚入陰地關，壁汾、隰，薛鐵山、李承嗣營洪洞迎戰。
entries.en: Zhang Jun entered Yindi Pass and encamped at Fen and Xi. Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet him.
entries.literal: Jun entered Yindi Pass, walled at Fen and Xi; Xue Tieshan and Li Chengsi encamped at Hongdong to meet the attack.

entries.zh: 存孝次趙城，韓建夜出壯士三百乘其營，存孝伏以待，建兵大奔。
entries.en: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng. Han Jian sent three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp, but Cunxiao lay in wait and Jian's men fled in disorder.
entries.literal: Cunxiao halted at Zhaocheng; Han Jian sent out three hundred stalwarts by night to strike his camp; Cunxiao lay in ambush; Jian's troops fled in great disorder.

entries.zh: 存孝攻絳州，未下，晉州刺史張行恭棄城走，建與浚遁還。
entries.en: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou without success. Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned his city and fled. Han Jian and Zhang Jun withdrew in defeat.
entries.literal: Cunxiao attacked Jiangzhou but did not take it; Jinzhou Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled; Jian and Jun slipped back.

entries.zh: 明年，克用奉表自陳，乃復拜檢校太師、守中書令、隴西郡王。
entries.en: The following year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was restored as Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.
entries.literal: The next year Keyong memorialized in his own defense and was again appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Duke of Longxi.

entries.zh: 景福初，鎮州王镕攻堯山，克用使李嗣勛擊之，斬級三萬，克用遂拔天長，略常山，度滹沱，燔其郛。
entries.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan. Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and claimed thirty thousand heads. Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan; Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and took thirty thousand heads; Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.

entries.zh: 徇地至趙，取鼓、槁二城。
entries.en: He overran the country as far as Zhao and took the cities of Gu and Gao.
entries.literal: He overran the land to Zhao and took the two cities of Gu and Gao.

entries.zh: 赫連鐸眾八萬攻天成軍，克用飛檄發軍太原，匡威已壁雲州北郊，克用自神堆引軍夜入雲州，死戰，走之。
entries.en: Helian Duo attacked Tiancheng Army with eighty thousand men. Keyong issued urgent orders from Taiyuan while Kuangwei had already encamped at the north suburb of Yunzhou. Keyong led his men by night from Shendui into Yunzhou, fought savagely, and drove him off.
entries.literal: Helian Duo with eighty thousand attacked Tiancheng Army; Keyong sent urgent orders from Taiyuan; Kuangwei had already walled at the north suburb of Yunzhou; Keyong from Shendui led troops by night into Yunzhou, fought to the death, and drove him off.

entries.zh: 乾寧元年，克用次新城，鐸膝行詣軍門降，克用鞭而縱之。
entries.en: In Qianning 1 (894) Keyong halted at Xincheng. Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender. Keyong whipped him and let him go.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianning, Keyong halted at Xincheng; Duo came on his knees to the camp gate to surrender; Keyong whipped him and let him go.

entries.zh: 進下武州，攻新州。
entries.en: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.
entries.literal: He advanced to take Wuzhou and attacked Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 李匡籌引步騎七萬救之，克用迎戰，斬首萬級，俘少將三百，徇城下，新州降。
entries.en: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to the rescue. Keyong met him in battle, claimed ten thousand heads, took three hundred junior officers prisoner, overran the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.
entries.literal: Li Kuangchou led seventy thousand foot and horse to rescue it; Keyong met him in battle, took ten thousand heads, captured three hundred junior officers, overran below the walls, and Xinzhou surrendered.

entries.zh: 取媯州，匡籌棄幽州走。
entries.en: He took Guizhou. Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.
entries.literal: He took Guizhou; Kuangchou abandoned Youzhou and fled.

entries.zh: 明年，幽州降，克用以劉仁恭為留後，乃旋。
entries.en: The following year Youzhou surrendered. Keyong appointed Liu Rengong acting commander and returned home.
entries.literal: The next year Youzhou surrendered; Keyong made Liu Rengong acting commander and returned.

entries.zh: 光化初，帝還京師，詔克用與全忠解仇，宰相徐彥若、崔胤皆勸之。
entries.en: Early in the Guanghua era the emperor returned to the capital and ordered Keyong and Quanzhong to reconcile. Chancellors Xu Yanruo and Cui Yin both urged them to comply.
entries.literal: Early in Guanghua, the emperor returned to the capital and ordered Keyong and Quanzhong to end their feud; chancellors Xu Yanruo and Cui Yin both urged it.

entries.zh: 克用勢已折，然尚以功高位全忠上，恥先下之，時王镕方睦於汴，乃遺書镕，使為己倡。
entries.en: Keyong's strength was already broken, yet he still outranked Quanzhong by merit and was ashamed to yield first. Wang Rong was then on friendly terms with Bian, so Keyong sent him a letter asking him to take the lead on his behalf.
entries.literal: Keyong's power was already broken, yet he still outranked Quanzhong by merit and seniority and was ashamed to yield first; Wang Rong was then on friendly terms with Bian, so he sent Rong a letter asking him to take the lead for him.

entries.zh: 全忠即遣使奉書幣恭甚，克用亦報之。
entries.en: Quanzhong at once sent envoys bearing letters and gifts with great deference, and Keyong replied in kind.
entries.literal: Quanzhong at once sent envoys bearing letters and gifts with great deference, and Keyong replied in kind.

entries.zh: 然汴日益張，窮鬥不置。
entries.en: Yet Bian grew stronger by the day, and their bitter struggle did not let up.
entries.literal: Yet Bian grew stronger day by day, and their bitter struggle did not cease.

entries.zh: 王珙請汴兵攻河中，克用使李嗣昭、張漢瑜援之，汴兵走。
entries.en: Wang Gong asked Bian for troops to attack Hezhong. Keyong sent Li Cizhao and Zhang Hanyu to the rescue, and the Bian troops fled.
entries.literal: Wang Gong asked Bian for troops to attack Hezhong; Keyong sent Li Cizhao and Zhang Hanyu to aid the defense, and the Bian troops fled.

entries.zh: 葛從周取承天軍，氏叔琮取遼州、樂平，進壁榆次，克用使周德威逐出之。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou took Chengtian Army. Shi Shuzong seized Liaozhou and Leping and advanced to encamp at Yuci. Keyong sent Zhou Dewei to drive them out.
entries.literal: Ge Congzhou took Chengtian Army; Shi Shuzong took Liaozhou and Leping and advanced to encamp at Yuci; Keyong sent Zhou Dewei to drive them out.

entries.zh: 李嗣昭以步騎三萬下太行，略河內，拔懷州，進攻河陽，汴人閻寶救之，嗣昭退保懷。
entries.en: Li Cizhao descended the Taihang with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, overran Henan Interior, took Huaizhou, and advanced on Heyang. Yan Bao of Bian came to the rescue, and Cizhao withdrew to hold Huai.
entries.literal: Li Cizhao descended the Taihang with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, overran Henan Interior, took Huaizhou, and advanced on Heyang; Yan Bao of Bian came to the rescue, and Cizhao withdrew to hold Huai.

entries.zh: 天復元年，全忠取晉、絳，逼河中，王珂告急，使相望，汴人扼空道，晉兵不得前，遂虜珂。
entries.en: In Tianfu 1 Quanzhong took Jin and Jiang and pressed Hezhong. Wang Ke sent urgent appeals, envoys arriving one after another, but Bian troops blocked the open road and Jin forces could not advance. Ke was captured.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Quanzhong took Jin and Jiang and pressed Hezhong; Wang Ke sent urgent appeals, envoys stretching in sight of one another; Bian troops blocked the open road and Jin troops could not advance, and Ke was captured.

entries.zh: 珂妻，克用女，不能救，全忠遂有河中，克用朝貢道亦梗。
entries.en: Ke's wife was Keyong's daughter, yet Keyong could not save him. Quanzhong thus gained Hezhong, and Keyong's tributary route was also cut off.
entries.literal: Ke's wife was Keyong's daughter, yet he could not save her husband; Quanzhong thus gained Hezhong, and Keyong's tributary route was also blocked.

entries.zh: 沙陀，西突厥別部處月種也。
entries.en: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue people, a dependent tribe of the Western Turks.
entries.literal: The Shatuo were of the Chuyue branch among the dependent tribes of the Western Turks.

entries.zh: 始，突厥東西部分治烏孫故地，與處月、處蜜雜居。
entries.en: In the beginning, as the Eastern and Western Turks partitioned the old Wusun territories, they dwelt alongside the Chuyue and Chumi peoples.
entries.literal: At first, when the Eastern and Western Turks divided rule over the former Wusun lands, they lived intermixed with the Chuyue and Chumi.

entries.zh: 貞觀七年，太宗以鼓纛立利邲咄陸可汗，而族人步真觖望，謀並其弟彌射乃自立。
entries.en: In Zhenguan 7 (633), Emperor Taizong invested Ashina Yipiduolu as khan in the formal drum-and-banner ceremony. A clansman named Böke, resentful of the appointment, conspired to ally with his younger brother Mishe and seize power for himself.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Taizong installed Ashina Yipiduolu as khan with the drum-and-banner ceremony; the clansman Böke was discontented and plotted to join his younger brother Mishe and declare himself ruler.

entries.zh: 彌射懼，率處月等入朝。
entries.en: Fearing for his safety, Mishe led the Chuyue and other tribes to present themselves at court.
entries.literal: Mishe was afraid and led the Chuyue and others to submit to the court.

entries.zh: 而步真勢窮，亦歸國。
entries.en: Böke, his position hopeless, likewise submitted to the Tang.
entries.literal: Böke, his strength exhausted, also returned to allegiance.

entries.zh: 其留者，咄陸以射匱特勒劫越之子賀魯統之。
entries.en: Those who stayed behind were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.
entries.literal: Those who remained were placed under Helu, son of the Shegui tegin Jeučü, by Ashina Duolu.

entries.zh: 光化元年三月，天子以王兼天平軍節度使。
entries.en: In the third month of Guanghua 1 (898) the court added the Tianping command to Quanzhong's titles.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guanghua the Son of Heaven made Quanzhong concurrently military governor of the Tianping army.

entries.zh: 四月，遣葛從周攻晉之山東，取邢、洺、磁三州。
entries.en: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou into Hedong's Shandong districts and seized Xing, Ming, and Ci.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Hedong's Shandong region and took Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures.

entries.zh: 襄州趙匡凝自其父德諲時來附，匡凝又與楊行密、李克用通，而其事泄。
entries.en: Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou had been a vassal since his father Deyin's day. He was now in touch with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the traffic was discovered.
entries.literal: Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture had submitted since his father Deyin's time; Kuangning again communicated with Yang Xingmi and Li Keyong, and the matter was exposed.

entries.zh: 七月，遣氏叔琮、康懷英攻匡凝，取其泌、隨、鄧三州。
entries.en: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning and took Mi, Sui, and Deng.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying to attack Kuangning and took his Mi, Sui, and Deng prefectures.

entries.zh: 曾三異校定曰：三異案，唐書地理志：唐州，天祐三年朱全忠徙治泌陽，表更名泌州。
entries.en: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi observes that the Geography Treatise of the Tang History records Zhu Quanzhong moving Tangzhou’s seat to Biyang in Tianyou 3 and petitioning to rename it Mizhou.
entries.literal: Zeng Sanyi’s collation says: Sanyi notes that according to the Geography Treatise of the Tang History, in Tianyou 3 Zhu Quanzhong moved Tang Prefecture’s seat to Biyang and submitted a memorial changing its name to Mi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 則是天祐二年唐州舊名猶在，至三年始更為泌。
entries.en: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tangzhou was still in use; it was only in the third year that it became Mizhou.
entries.literal: Thus in Tianyou 2 the old name Tang Prefecture still remained, and only in the third year was it changed to Mi.

entries.zh: 光化之初，未當有泌州之名。
entries.en: At the beginning of Guanghua, the name Mizhou should not yet have existed.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, there should not yet have been the name Mi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 今書為泌，則誤也。
entries.en: So when the present text writes Mizhou, it is mistaken.
entries.literal: If the present text writes it as Mi, then that is an error.

entries.zh: 匡凝請和，乃止。
entries.en: Kuangning sued for peace and the campaign ended.
entries.literal: Kuangning sued for peace, and the attack stopped.

entries.zh: 十二月，李罕之以潞州來降。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi handed Luzhou over.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou.

entries.zh: 二年，幽州劉仁恭攻魏，羅紹威來求救。
entries.en: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou struck Wei, and Luo Shaowei called for help.
entries.literal: In the second year Liu Rengong of Youzhou attacked Wei; Luo Shaowei came to beg rescue.

entries.zh: 王救魏，敗仁恭于內黃。
entries.en: Quanzhong relieved Wei and beat Rengong at Neihuang.
entries.literal: Quanzhong rescued Wei and defeated Rengong at Neihuang.

entries.zh: 四月，遣氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。
entries.en: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan; the city held.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he sent Shi Shuzong to attack Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.

entries.zh: 七月，李克用取澤、潞。
entries.en: In the seventh month Li Keyong recovered Ze and Lu.
entries.literal: In the seventh month Li Keyong took Ze and Lu.
